src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment.
tgt: Maemo a Kabinete mabapi le dintlha tsa bohlokwa maemong a ha jwale.

src: Cabinet expressed concern at recent labour unrest at Lonmin’s Marikana Mine which has led to the downing of tools and a disruption of productivity.
tgt: Kabinete e hlahisitse ngongoreho ya yona mabapi le merusu ya moraorao tjena Morafong wa Lonmin o Marikana o bakileng ho nyahlatswa ha mosebetsi le tshitiso ya tlhahiso.

src: The dispute is reported as centering around issues of majority representation involving the National Union of Mineworkers and the Association for Mining and Construction Union.
tgt: Qabang ena e tlalehwa e le mabapi le dintlha tsa bongata ba boemedi bo kenyeletsang Mokgatlo wa Basebetsi wa Basebeletsi ba Merafo (NUM) le mokgatlo o mong wa Mokgatlo wa Basebeletsi ba Merafo le Kaho (AMCU).Kabinete e etsa boipiletso ho boetapele ba mekgatlo ka bobedi e leng (NUM le AMCU) hore ba rarolle qabang ya bona ka kgotso le ho beha ditabatabelo tsa naha le tsa basebetsi ka pele ho feta eng kapa eng.

src: Cabinet appeals to the leadership of both unions (NUM and AMCU) to resolve their dispute amicably and put the interests of the country and workers above everything else.
tgt: Basebetsi ba tshwanela ho lemoha hore seteraeke se sa tshireletswang se ka ba le ditlamorao tse mpe haholo e seng ho bona feela, empa le bakeng sa bokamoso ba morafo le ba mesebetsi ya bona.

src: Cabinet also appeals to Lonmin management to do everything possible to make sure that the problems are resolved as soon as possible without further damage.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e etsa boipiletso ho botsamaisi ba Lonmin hore bo etse ka hohle kamoo ho ka kgonehang ho etsa bonnete ba hore mathata a rarollwa ka potlako kamoo ho ka kgonehang pele ho senyeha dintho tse ngata ho feta.

src: It is in the best interest of the country for both unions and management at Lonmin to demonstrate required levels of leadership and industrial relations management.
tgt: Ho molemong wa bohlokwa wa naha bakeng sa hore mekgatlo ka bobedi le botsamaisi ba Lonmin ho bontsha maemo a hlokehang a boetapele le a bolaodi ba dikamano tsa mesebetsi.

src: Cabinet fully supports the preliminary findings from the investigation into the unauthorised landing of a civilian aircraft at Waterkloof Air Force Base.
tgt: Kabinete e tshehetsa ka botlalodiphihlello tsa sethathong tsa diphuputso tsa ho dumellwa ha ho tsorama ho sa dumellwang ha sefofane sa setjhaba Setsing sa Lebotho la Sesole sa Moyeng sa Waterkloof.

src: Cabinet stressed that the safety and sovereignty of South Africa is of paramount importance.
tgt: Kabinete e tobokeditse hore polokeho le boikemelo ba Aforika Borwa ke ntlha ya bohlokwa.

src: Violation of laws and rules relevant to the ports of entry and facilities of strategic national importance must be dealt with firmly and without fear or favour.
tgt: Tlolo ya melao le melawana e tsamaelanang le madiboho le ditsha tse hlokolosi tsa naha e lokela hore ho sebetsanwe le yona ka thata ntle le tshabo kapa ho ratwa.

src: Those who are found to infringe and compromise regulations must face the full might of the law.
tgt: Batho ba tla fumanwang ba tlola le ho nyenyefatsa melao ba lokelwa ke kgalefo e matla ya molao.

src: Cabinet welcomes the work by Government Departments which has been reported on by various Ministers during the departmental Budget Votes.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela mosebetsi wa Mafapha a Mmuso oo o tlalehilweng ke Matona a fapafapaneng nakong ya Dipuo tsa Ditekanyetso tsa mafapha.

src: Cabinet notes that the coverage afforded to the Budget Votes assists in empowering citizens with information and holding government accountable.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela ntlha ya hore phatlalatso e fuweng Dipuo tsa Ditekanyetso e thusa bakeng sa ho matlafatsa baahi ka tlhahisoleseding le ho etsa hore mmuso o ikarabelle.

src: Cabinet welcomes the discussions between the Department of Basic Education and the South African Democratic Teachers' Union (SADTU) which led to the suspension of protest action.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela dipuisano tsa mahareng a Lefapha la Thuto ya Motheo le Mokgatlo wa Matitjhere wa Demokrasi wa Aforika Borwa tse entseng hore diketsahalo tsa boipelaetso di fanyehuwe.

src: Cabinet calls on all stakeholders in the education sector to resolve their disputes so that education of our young people is not compromised.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho bankakarolo bohle ho tsa thuto ho rarolla diqabang tsa bona hore thuto ya batjha ba rona e se ke ya behwa tsietsing.

src: Cabinet noted the Quarterly Labour Force Survey (QLFS) which shows an increase in the unemployment rate from 24,9 per cent to 25,2 per cent.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Phuputso ya ka ha Palo ya Mesebetsi e bontshang ho phahama ha sekgahla sa tlhokahalo ya mesebetsi ho tloha ho diphesente tse 24,9 ho ya ho tse 25,2.Mmuso o potlakisa mekgwa, e jwaloka ho akofisa dikaho tsa motheo tse kgannwang ke mmuso, bakeng sa ho eketsa mesebetsi ka ho sebedisa Makala a Setjhaba hore a kenakene ntlha ena.

src: Government is accelerating measures, such as the state-led infrastructure drive, to increase employment through Public Sector interventions.
tgt: Mmuso mmoho le ba ikarabelang ho tsa mesebetsi le dikgwebo o kgakotse Tumellano ya Kahisano ya Kgiro ya Batjha ka Mmesa 2013.

src: Government together with labour and business launched the Social Accord on Youth Employment in April 2013.
tgt: Sena ho ya pele se bontsha boitlamo bo kopanetsweng ho iseng ho tobaneng le ntlha ya tlhokahalo ya mosebetsi Sena se bontsha kamoo makala ka bonngwe a etsang boitlamo ba ho lwantsha tlhoko ya mesebetsi hara batjha ka ho shebana le maikemisetso a bonahalang le dinako tseo ka tsona ba tla fihlelang seo ka katleho, ho beha leihlo le ho lekola mmoho boikenyakako bo hlwauweng.

src: It maps out individual sector pledges to contribute in fighting youth unemployment with concrete targets and time frames for successful execution, monitoring and collective evaluation of the identified interventions.
tgt: Kabinete e dutse e na le tshepo ya hore mekgwa e teng ha jwale e tla thusa naha ho hlahisa mesebetsi e metjha le ho fihlella maikemisetso a yona a ho hlahisa mesebetsi e metjha e dimilione tse hlanoka 2020.

src: Cabinet remains confident that measures already underway will assist the country to create new jobs and realise its target of five-million new jobs by 2020.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela ho tekenwa ha moralo wa tshebetso bakeng sa ho kenya tshebetsong memorandamo o bitswang Memorandamo wa Kutlwisisano Mabapi le Paballo le Tshireletso ya tsa Tlhaho pakeng tsa Aforika Borwa le Vietnam.

src: Cabinet welcomes the signing of an action plan to implement the Memorandum of Understanding on Biodiversity Conservation and Protection between South Africa and Vietnam.
tgt: Moralo wa ho Kenngwa Tshebetsong o tla tsamaya ho fihla ka 2017 mme o tla thusa mekutung ya ho lwantsha ditlolo tsa molao tse kenyeletsang Diphoofolo tse hlaha, haholoholo ho tsongwa ho seng molaong ha ditshukudu.

src: The Implementation Plan will run until 2017 and will assist efforts to combat crime involving wildlife, particularly rhino poaching.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e pheta hore Mmuso o ikemiseditse ho shebana le ntlha ya ho tsongwa ha ditshukudu ho seng molaong le ho tiisa hore disenyi di tla ahlolwa.

src: Cabinet reiterates that Government is committed to addressing the scourge of rhino poaching and reaffirms that perpetrators will be prosecuted.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela phatlalatso ya Lefapha la Merero ya Lehae ya ho qala ka mokgwa wa boitsebiso wa karete o bitswang Tshebediso ya Karete ya Boitsebiso, o matlafatsang boitsebiso ba rona ba naha le ho ntlafatsa polokeho ya setjhaba.

src: Cabinet welcomes the announcement by the Department of Home Affairs to pilot the Smart ID card system, which further consolidates our national identity and enhances national security.
tgt: Mokolokotwane ona wa bohlokwa o tshwere kgonahalo ya ho potlakisa ditshebeletso tsa mmuso, ha ka ho le leng o fokotsa botlokotsebe le bobodu bo kenyeletsang ditokomane tsa boitsebiso.

src: This key milestone holds the potential to speed up government services, while cutting down on crime and corruption involving identity documents.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa ho tshehetsa tsamaiso ena hore ka 2020 bohle re be re na le Karete ya Boitsebiso le mokgwa wa boitsebiso wa bosetšhaba.

src: Cabinet calls on South Africans to support this process so that by 2020 we are all in receipt of a Smart ID Card as a form of national identification.
tgt: Kabinete e tshwela ka mathe tlhaselo ya mokoloko wa makoloi a Matjhaba a Kopaneng ho la Abyei, Sudan, e bakileng mafu a morena wa morabe le mosebeletsi wa kgotso wa Etopia.

src: Cabinet condemns the attack on a United Nations convoy in Abyei, Sudan, which resulted in the deaths of a tribal chief and an Ethiopian peacekeeper.
tgt: Ketsahalo ena e madimabe e tshosa botsitso ba Abyei mmoho le tswelopele e fihlelletsweng haufinyana tjena ke Sudan le Sudan Borwa.

src: Cabinet denounces the attack on Syria by the Israeli security forces.
tgt: Kabinete e kgahlanong le tlhaselo ya Syria ke mabotho a polokeho a Israele.

src: Cabinet calls on the United Nations to prevail on external forces to respect the sovereignty of Syria and to allow Syrians to work together in resolving their disputes.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba a kopaneng hore o iponahatse mabothong a ka thoko bakeng sa ho hlompha boikemelo ba Syria le ho tlohella maSyria ho sebetsa mmoho bakeng sa ho rarolla diqabang tsa ona.

src: Cabinet welcomed the inauguration of Advocate Lawrence Mushwana as the new Chairperson of the International Co-ordinating Committee (ICC) of National Institutions for the Promotion and Protection of Human Rights.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho behwa setulong ha Moadfokate Lawrence Mushwana jwaloka modulasetulo wa Komiti ya Tsamaiso ya Matjhaba (ICC) ya Ditheo tsa Kgothaletso le Tshireletso ya Ditokelo tsa Botho.

src: This is the first time that Africa heads the office of the Chairperson of the ICThe position of ICC Chairperson secures increased focus on the country's human rights track record and its compliance with international human rights obligations.
tgt: Lena ke lekgetlo la pelehore Aforika e etelle pele kantoro ya Modulasetulo wa ICMaemo a Modulasetulo wa ICC a tiisetsa tsepamiso e phahameng ya maikutlo hodima nalane ya naha ya ditokelo tsa botho le ho tsamaelana ha yona le boitlamo ba ditokelo tsa botho tsa matjhaba.

src: Cabinet welcomed that the 50th anniversary of the Organisation of African Unity which will be celebrated on Africa Day, 25 May 2013.Cabinet highlighted that the solidarity of the OAU in excluding the apartheid government from its organs uplifted our struggle for freedom and attainment of democracy.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse hore ho ketekwa ha dilemo tse 50 tsa Mokgatlo wa Kopano ya Aforika (OAU) ho tla etsahala ka Letsatsi la Aforika, ka la 25 Motsheanong 2013.Kabinete e hlakisitse hore momahano ya OAU bakeng sa ho se kenyeletse mmuso wa karohano makaleng a ona ho phahamisitse boitseko ba rona bakeng sa tokoloho le phihlello ya demokerasi.

src: South Africa will join the continent in commemorating the 50th Anniversary of the African Union.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tla imatahanya le kontinente bakeng sa ho hopola hoketeka dilemo tse 50 tsa Kopano ya Aforika.

src: The activities include a month-long exhibition of contemporary visual arts in the SADC region from 24 May to 28 June 2013.
tgt: Diketsahalo di kenyeletsa dipontsho tsa kgwedi kaofela tsa bonono ba pono lebatoweng la Dinaha tsa Ntshetsopele ya Dinaha tsa Aforika e ka Borwa (SADC) ho tloha ka la 24 Motsheanong ho ya ho la 28 Phuptjane 2013.

src: The Africa Institute of South Africa will also convene the academic community and diaspora as part of the commemorations on 19-21 May 2013.
tgt: Institjute ya Aforika Borwa le yona e tla bitsa pitso ya se bitswang sehlopha sa dirutehi le ya dinaha tse ding e le karolo ya mekete ya sehopotso ka la 19-21 Motsheanong 2013.

src: Furthermore, there will be an exhibition at the Ditsong Museum (City of Tshwane) to commemorate Africa Day on 21 May 2013 under the theme “50 Years after forming the Organisation of African Union – Africa must unite or Perish”.
tgt: Ho fetafeta moo, ho tla ba le dipontsho Museamong waDitsong (Motsemoholo wa Tshwane) ho hopola Letsatsi la Aforika ka la 21 Motsheanong 2013 tlasa mookotaba o reng “Dilemo tse 50 kamora ho thehwa ha OAU – Aforika ha e Kopane kapa e Timele.”Senase tla latelwa ke konsarete ya mmino ya Letsatsi la Aforika Meahong ya Kopano ka la 25 Motsheanong 2013.

src: This will be followed by a Africa Day music concert at the Union Buildings on 25 May 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse karabelo e potlakileng ya Mopresidente Jacob Zuma bakeng sa sememo sa setho sa badudi sa ho etela badudi Eldorado Park le Kliptown e mabapi le yona, ka Labobedi la 14 Motsheanong 2013.

src: The community’s request was to discuss the escalating illegal drug trafficking and abuse problem in the area.
tgt: Kopo ya badudi e ne e le ho sekaseka ho phahama ha tsamaiso ya dithethefatsi tse seng molaong le tshebediso e mpe ya tsona sebakeng seo.

src: Government, together with the community, has committed to accelerate the intervention programme to stop the scourge that is destroying young people.
tgt: Mmuso, mmoho le badudi, o itlamme ho potlakisa mananeo a boikenyako ba ona ho thibela bothata bona bo qetang batjha.

src: Cabinet welcomed the follow up visit by Deputy President Motlanthe, accompanied by leaders of the three spheres of government, to De Doorns in the Western Cape on Saturday 11 May 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse leeto la bobedi la Motlatsa Mopresidente Motlanthe, a feleheditswe ke baetapele ba makala a mararo a mmuso, ho ya De Doorns ho la Kapa Bophirima ka moqebelo wa la 11 Motsheanong 2013.

src: The visit and dialogue with stakeholders including farmworkers stems from the initial visit of the Deputy President on 12 February 2013.
tgt: Leeto le dipuisano le bankakarolo ho kenyeletswa le basebeletsi ba mapolasi e tswetswe ke leeto la pele la Motlatsa Mopresidente ka la 12 hlakola 2013.

src: Solid progress was noted from a number of departments in improving services in the area.
tgt: Tswelopele e tsitsitseng e ile ya bonahala ho hlaha mafapheng a mangata bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa ditshebeletso sebakeng seo.

src: The commitment demonstrated by all parties lays a solid foundation for ongoing engagement toward a sustainable agrarian sector.
tgt: Boitlamo bo bontshitsweng ke makala oohle a etsa motheo o tiileng bakeng sa dipuisano tse tswellang ho isa lekaleng le tsepameng la temo.

src: Key Cabinet discussions and decisions.
tgt: Dipuisano le diqeto tsa bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet was briefed on preparations for Child Protection Week (CPW) between 27 May and 2 June 2013, under the theme: “Working together to protect children.”	The child and youth dialogues are being conducted in all provinces as a build up to the launch of Child Protection Week and the Conference.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka boitokisetso ba Beke ya Tshireletso ya Bana mahareng a la 27 Motsheanong le la 2 Phuptjane 2013, tlasa mookotaba o reng: “Ho sebetsa mmoho bakeng sa tshireletso ya bana.”Dipuisano ka ha bana le batjha di ntse di etswa diprofenseng tsohle e le boitokisetso ba ho thakgola Beke ya Tshireletso ya Bana le Khonferense.

src: As part of awareness-raising, Child Protection Week will be launched together with the orphans, vulnerable children and youth (OVCY) Conference on 27 May at the Inkosi Albert Luthuli International Convention Centre in KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Jwaloka karolo ya ho hlohleletsa temoso, Beke ya Tshireletso ya Bana e tla thakgolwa mmoho le Khonferense ya Dikgutsana, Bana ba Tsietsing le Batjha (OVCY) ka la 27 Motsheanong Setsing sa Matjhaba sa Dikhonferense sa Inkosi Albert Luthuli ho la KwaZulu Natal.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to contribute towards the protection of our children and create a safe and secure environment.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa bakeng sa ho nyehela tshireletsong ya bana ba rona le ho theha tikoloho e bolokehileng le e tshireletsehileng.

src: South Africans can visibly demonstrate their support by wearing a green ribbon as a symbol of life, growth, hope, care and support for our future leaders.
tgt: MaAforika Borwa a ka bontsha ka ho hlaka tshehetso ya oona ka ho rwala ribone e tala e le letshwao la bophelo, kgolo, tshepo, kgathallo le tshehetso bakeng sa baetapele ba rona ba kamoso.

src: The focus of Child Protection Week and the Orphans, Vulnerable Children and Youth Conference is on child participation in our society and communities so that children are heard on matters affecting them.
tgt: Maikemisetso a OVCY a tobile ho nka karolo ha bana setjhabeng le metseng ya rona hore bana batle ba mamelwe ditabeng tse ba amang.

src: Cabinet approved the National Aquaculture Policy Framework (NAPF).
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana Moralo wa Leano la Setjhaba la tsa Metsing (NAPF).

src: This policy provides a unified framework for the establishment and development of an industry that contributes towards sustainable job creation and increased investment.
tgt: Leano lena le fana ka moralo o kopanetsweng bakeng sa ho thehwa le ho ntshetswa pele ha indasteri e nyehelang bakeng sa tlhahiso ya mesebetsi e tsitsitseng le matsete a eketsehileng.

src: The NAPF was developed against the backdrop of a global aquaculture sector that has seen an increased demand for fishery products.
tgt: NAPF e hlahisitswe ho shebuwe lekala la tsa metsing tsa lefatshe le bonahetseng le bontsha tlhoko e phahameng bakeng sa dihlahiswa tsa tlhapi.

src: In South Africa, marine and freshwater aquaculture presents a good opportunity to diversify fish production to satisfy local demand, contribute to food security, job creation, economic development and rural development, and export opportunities.
tgt: Ho la Aforika Borwa, tsa metsing a lewatle le metsi a foreshe di hlahisa monyetla o motle bakeng sa ho qaqolohanya tlhahiso ya tlhapi sa ho kgotsofatsa tlhoko ya lehae, ho nyehela bakeng sa botsitso ba dijo, tlhahiso ya mesebetsi, ntshetsopele ya moruo le ntshetsopele ya dibaka tsa mahae, le menyetla ya ho rekisetsa dinaha tsa ka ntle.

src: Cabinet approved that South Africa hosts the Third Global Conference on Agriculture, Food Security and Climate Change in the fourth quarter of 2013, led by the Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana ntlha ya hore Aforika Borwa e tshware Khonferense ya Boraro ya Lefatshe ho tsa Temo, Botsitso ba Dijo le ho fetofetoha ha Tlelaemete kotareng ya bone ya 2013, e eteletsweng pele ke Lefapha la Temo, Meru le tsa Ditlhapi.

src: Food security remains a major concern and the Conference will have positive implications for how we produce, manage and utilise food.
tgt: Botsitso ba dijo e sa le taba e ngongorehisang mme Khonferense e tla tla ka dintlha tse hlwahlwa bakeng sa kamoo re hlahisang, re laolang le ho sebedisa dijo.

src: Since COP17/CMP7, South Africa has been one of the leading countries in promoting climate smart agriculture, which responds to the challenges of food security and climate change.
tgt: Ho tloha ka COP17/CMP7, Aforika Borwa e sa le e le e nngwe ya dinaha tse ka sehloohong bakeng sa ho hodisa se bitswang temo e qhekanyetsang tlelaemete e leng se arabelang diphephetso tsa botsitso ba dijo le ho fetofetoha ha tlelaemete.

src: The Global Conference aims to develop forms of growth that are socially and environmentally sustainable.
tgt: Ke sepheo sa Khonferense ya Lefatshe ho ntshetsapele mekgwa ya kgolo e tla tshwarellang bakeng sa kahisano le tikoloho.

src: Cabinet approved South Africa’s ratification of the Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) Annex to the Southern African Development Community’s Protocol on Trade and for this to be submitted to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana tumellano ya Aforika Borwa ya Tsitlallelo ya Bohlweki (SPS) ho Tumellano ya Kgwebo ya Ntshetsopele ya Kgwebo ya Ditjhaba tsa Aforika e Borwa le hore sena se hlahiswe Palamenteng.

src: The SADC Protocol on Trade to which South Africa has acceded serves to promote regional cooperation and integration amongst member states for trade in goods and services within the region, including agricultural products.
tgt: Tumellano ya Kgwebo ya SADC eo Aforika Borwa e kgemang le yona bakeng sa ho hodisa tshebedisano mmoho ya lebatowa le kopano hara mebuso ya ditho bakeng sa kgwebisano thepeng le ditshebeletsong ka hara lebatowa, ho kenyeletswa dihlahiswa tsa temo.

src: The SADC SPS Annex to the SADC Protocol on Trade provides an enabling framework for SPS cooperation.
tgt: Karolwana ya SADC SPS Annex ho Tumellano ya Kgwebo ya SADC e fana ka moralo o kgontshang shebisano mmoho ya SPHape e hodisa dikamano tse ntle tsa mekgwa ya SPS e thehilweng hodima maemo a matjhaba le ditataiso bakeng sa ho tsamaisa kgwebisano e bolokehileng le e hlokang leeme ya dihlahiswa tsa temo lebatoweng.. Kabinetee ile ya behwa sehlohlolong ka tswelopele e amanang le ho tshwarwa ha dikopano tsa Sekema sa Tsamaiso ya ho fana ka Ditifikeiti ya Kimberley (KPCS) ke Aforika Borwa ka 2013, e kenyeletsang dikopano tsa kopanelo ho la Kimberley ho tloha ka la 4 ho ya ho la 7 Phuptjane le kopano kakaretso ya KPCS ho la Gauteng ho tloha ka la 26 ho ya ho la 29 Pudungwana 2013.

src: It also promotes harmonisation of SPS measures based on international standards and guidelines in order to facilitate safe and fair trade of agriculture products in the region.
tgt: Ho tshwarwa ha dikopano tsa KPCS ho tla thusa bakeng sa ho hodisa indasteri ya taemane le bohahlaodi.

src: Cabinet was updated on progress relating to South Africa’s hosting of the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme (KPCS) meetings in 2013, which includes the Inter-sessional meeting in Kimberley from 4 to 7 June and the KPCS Plenary in Gauteng from 26 to 29 November 2013.
tgt: Maemo a Aforika Borwa jwaloka modulasetulo wa KPCS e fana ka kananelo bakeng sa karolo ya bohlokwa eo Aforika Borwa e e bapalang lekaleng la matjhaba la taemane.

src: The hosting of the KPCS meetings will contribute to the promotion of the diamond industry and tourism.
tgt: Jwaloka modulasetulo, ke sepheo sa Aforika Borwa ho matlafatsa dikamano tsa kgwebisano tsa matjhaba, ka morero wa ho matlafatsa le ho eketsa menyabuketso ya Aforika ka hara KPCS le ho nyehela bakeng sa tikoloho e bolokehilengya lefatshe.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the Restitution of Land Rights Amendment Bill 2013 and Memorandum on the Objects of the Bill, for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana phatlalatso ya Bili ya Puseletso ya Ditokelo tsa Mobu ya 2013 le Memorandamo wa Dipheo tsa Bili, bakeng sa ho tshwaela.

src: This gives effect to the President’s 2013 State of Nation Address announcement on proposed amendments to the Restitution Act.
tgt: Sena se fana ka matla ho Puo ya Mopresidente ka Maemo a Setjhaba ya 2013 moo a phatlaladitseng dintlafatso tsa Molao wa Puseletso ya Mobu.

src: This relates to extending the date for lodgment of claims for restitution, to enable those parties that did not submit claims by the closing date of 31 December 1998 or who were excluded from the process, to submit.
tgt: Sena se amana le ho eketsa nako ya ho kenya ditseko bakeng sa puseletso, ho etsa hore batho ba sa kenyang ditseko ka letsatsi la ho qetela e leng la 31 Tshitwe 1998 kapa ba neng ba sa kenyeletswa mohatong ona, hore ba kenye ditseko.

src: The re-opening of lodgment of claims is guided by the vision of the National Development Plan as well as the Comprehensive Rural Development Programme and other growth strategies intended to promote national reconciliation and social cohesion.
tgt: Ho bulwa botjha ha ho kenngwa ha ditseko ho tataiswa ke pono ya Moralo wa Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba(NDP) mmoho le Lenaneo le Akaretsang la Ntshetsopele ya Dibaka tsa Mahae le mawala a mang a kgolo ao morero a ona e leng ho hodisa poelano ya setjhaba le kopano ya kahisano.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Electronic Communication Amendment Bill to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana Bili ya Ntlafatso ya Dikgokahano tsa Elektroniki ho Palamente.

src: The amendment was necessitated by the liberalisation of the electronic communications sector and rapid technological advancements which have rendered the continued presence of some provisions in the Act redundant.
tgt: Ntlafatso e bakuwe ke ho lokollwa ha lekala la dikgokahanyo tsa elektroniki le dintlafatso tse potlakileng tsa theknoloji tse entseng hore ho dule ho na le dikarolo tse sa hlokahaleng Molaong.

src: The Amendments seeks to deal with competition promotion limitation, access to electronic communications infrastructure, communication costs as well as improving turnaround time for consultative processes.
tgt: Dintlafatso di batla ho sebetsana le phokotso ya phehisano, ho fihlella marangrang a dikgokahano tsa elektroniki, ditjeho tsa dikgokahano mmoho le ho ntlafatsa nako ya ho phethela ditsamaiso tsa dithuso.

src: The Amendment Bill aligns the Act with broad-based black economic empowerment legislation refines licensing issues improves competition provisions removes regulatory bottlenecks and provides for matters connected to this.
tgt: Bili ya Ntlafatso e matahanya Molao le Molao wa matlafatso moruong o bataletseng wa batho ba batsho se lokisa botjha phano ya dilaesense se ntlafatsa dipehelo tsa phehisano se tlosa ditiehiso tsa molao le ho sebetsana le dintlha tse tsamaelanang le sena.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA) Amendment Bill to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana pehelo ya Bili ya Ntlafatso ya Mokgatlo o Ikemetseng wa Dikgokahano wa Aforika Borwa (ICASA) Palamenteng.

src: The Amendment Bill responds to some of the issues in the National Development Plan (NDP).The amendments of the Independent Communication Authority Act No.
tgt: Bili ya Ntlafatso e arabela mabakeng a mang a ho NDP.

src: 13 of 2002 (ICASA Act) are underpinned by the need for institutional improvements to strengthen the independent Authority.
tgt: Dintlafatso tsa Molao wa ICASA wa Nomoro ya 13 wa 2002 o bitswang (Molao wa ICASA) di hlakiswa ke tlhokahalo ya dintlafatso bakeng sa ho matlafatsa Mokgatlo o ikemetseng.

src: This will be through the provision of clarity on aspects of its powers to align the Act more closely to the requirements of the Public Finance Management Act (PFMA) and to improve its efficiency.
tgt: Sena se tla hlahiswa ke pehelo ya tlhakisetso mabakeng a matla a ona bakeng sa ho matahanya Molao haufi le ditlhoko tsa Molao wa Bolaodi ba Ditjhelete tsa Setjhaba le ho ntlafatsa bohlwahlwa ba ona.

src: This is with a view to improve accountability and transparency which will contribute to sound governance practices within ICASGovernment needs to play a greater role to ensure that the electronic communications sector is regulated in a manner that supports overall national goals.
tgt: Sena ke ka morero wa ho ntlafatsa boikarabelo le ponahaletso tse tla tlisang taolo e hlwahlwa ka hara ICASA.

src: This should not be read to suggest any limitation on ICASA’s independence.
tgt: Mmuso o lokela ho bapala karolo e tomanyana ho netefatsa hore lekala dikgokahano tsa elektroniki le laolwa ka mokgwa o tshehetsang dipheo tsa setjhaba ka kakaretso.

src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment.
tgt: Maemo a Kabinete mabapi le dintlha tsa bohlokwa maemong a ha jwale.

src: Cabinet calls on communities to be vigilant against the possible resurgence of criminal violence targeting foreign nationals.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho badudi hore ba fadimehe kgahlanong le ho tsoha botjha ho ka nnang ha hlaha ha merusu ya botlokotsebe e tobileng melata.

src: Cabinet is cautious not to label this violence as xenophobia because preliminary evidence indicates that these acts may be driven primarily by criminality.
tgt: Kabinete e sedi hore e se ke ya supa merusu ena e le lehloyo la melata hobane bopaki ba sethathong bo bontsha hore diketso tsena di kgannwa haholo ke botlokotsebe.

src: Cabinet commended the law enforcement agencies for their swift and decisive action.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya thoholetsa makala a tiiso ya molao bakeng sa mosebetsi wa ona wa ka potlako le o matla.

src: Cabinet conveys its condolences to the families and friends of the young men who lost their lives as a result of inappropriate initiation ceremonies.
tgt: Kabinete e lebisa matshediso a yona ho malapa le metswalle ya bahlankana ba batjha ba lahlehetsweng ke bophelo ba bona ka lebaka la mekgwa ya mabollo e fosahetseng.

src: Cabinet endorses the call by President Jacob Zuma for swift justice and calls on traditional leaders and members of the community to be vigilant against abuse or neglect.
tgt: Kabinete e thatiselletsa kgoeletso ya Mopresidente Jacob Zuma bakeng sa toka e potlakileng le ho etsa boipiletso ho baetapele ba botjhaba le baahi hore ba fadimehe kgahlanong le tshebediso e mpe le ho se kgathalle.

src: Government fully supports the traditions and cultures of our diverse society and highlights that these must be balanced with constitutional rights.
tgt: Mmuso o tshehetsa ka botlalo meetlo le botjhaba ba naha ya rona bo fapafapaneng le ho hatella hore tsena tsohle di lokela ho ipapisa le ditokelo tsa molao wa motheo.

src: Cabinet welcomed South Africa’s participation in the recent African Union (AU) Summit, where South Africa prioritised a number of issues on the agenda of the Summit.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho nka karolo ha Aforika Borwa Sebokeng sa maobanyana mona sa Kopano ya Aforika (AU), moo Aforika Borwa e behileng dintlha tse ngatanyana ka sehloohong lenanetsamaisong la Seboka.

src: These included the Strategic Plan of the AU Commission for the period 2014-2017 and the AU Budget for 2014 the state of peace and security in Africa alternative sources of funding for the AU the post-2015 Development Agenda the meeting of the NEPAD Heads of State and Government Orientation Committee, and the African Peer Review Mechanism (APRM) Forum Summit.
tgt: Tsena di ne di kenyeleditse Moralo wa Bohlokwa wa Khomishene ya AU bakeng sa nako ya 2014-2017 le Ditekanyetso tsa AU bakeng sa 2014 maemo a kgotso le polokeho Aforika mehlodi e meng ya dithuso tsa ditjhelete bakeng sa AU Lenanetsamaiso la Ntshetsopele la ka mora 2015 kopano ya Baetapele ba Mebuso ba Bosemphato bo Botjha Bakeng sa Ntshetsopele ya Aforika le Komiti ya Mmuso Tlwaetso ya Makgulo, le Foramo ya Seboka sa Aforika sa Mokgwa wa ho Shebisana tse fetileng Mmoho.

src: Cabinet commended the Southern African Development Community (SADC) leadership for facilitating the process that led to Zimbabwe adopting a new Constitution.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholeditse boetapele ba Dinaha tse Kopaneng Bakeng sa Ntshetsopele ya Aforika e ka Borwa bakeng sa ho thusa tsamaisong e lebisitseng hore Zimbabwe e amohele Molaotheo o motjha.

src: The Zimbabwean Constitution marks a significant milestone in the successful implementation of the Global Peace Agreement.
tgt: Molaotheo wa Zimbabwe o tshwaya mokolokotwane wa bohlokwa ho kenngweng tshebetsong ha Tumellano ya Kgotso ya Lefatshe ka katleho.

src: On the eve of Youth Month Cabinet calls on all segments of society to raise the profile of programmes to fight substance abuse.
tgt: Mathuleng ana a Kgwedi ya Batjha Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho makala oohle a setjhaba ho phahamisa maemo a mananeo a ho lwantsha tshebediso e mpe ya dithethefatsi.

src: The Youth Month theme is: “Working Together for Youth Development and a Drug Free South Africa.”Government’s decisive action to address substance abuse in Eldorado Park, Gauteng, brings the people in this area closer to the realisation of a drug-free community.
tgt: Mookotaba wa Kgwedi ya Batjha o re: “Ha re Sebetseng Mmoho bakeng sa Ntshetsopele ya Batjha le Aforika Borwa e Hlokang Dithethefatsi.”Ketso e matla ya Mmuso bakeng sa ho shebana le tshebediso e mpe ya dithethefatsi ho la Eldorado Park, Gauteng, e tlisa batho ba tulo ena haufi le ho hlokomela ntlha ya sebaka se hlokang dithethefatsi.

src: Cabinet notes and welcomes the progress made by the police, community leaders and other structures in Eldorado Park under the leadership of the Gauteng Provincial Government.
tgt: Kabinete e lemoha le ho ananela tswelopele e entsweng ke sepolesa, baetapele ba badudi le makala a mang ho la Eldorado Park tlasa boetapele ba Mmuso wa Porofense wa Gauteng.

src: Together they made significant progress in fighting the scourge of substance abuse.
tgt: Mmoho ba entse kgatelopele ya bohlokwa twantshong ya kgehlepe ena ya tshebediso e mpe ya dithethefatsi.

src: Cabinet is aware that the situation in Eldorado Park is symptomatic of issues facing many communities in the rest of the country and calls on communities throughout the country to lead the fight for a “substance-free” South Africa within their respective areas.
tgt: Kabinete e a hlokomela hore maemo ho la Eldorado Park a bontsha dintlha tse tobaneng le dibaka tse ngata naheng ka bophara le ho etsa kgoeletso baduding bohle ba naha hore ba etelle pele ntwa ya Aforika Borwa e “hlokang dithethefatsi” ka hara ditulo ka ho fapana.

src: During Youth Month, let us recommit ourselves to fighting the war against substance abuse and alcoholism in all areas of the country.
tgt: Nakong ya kgwedi ya Batjha, ha re itlameng bakeng sa ho lwana ntwa e kgahlanong le tshebediso e mpe ya dithethefatsi le botahwa ditulong tsohle tsa naha.

src: Cabinet welcomes the incremental introduction of an African language in Grade R and Grade 1 where such languages are not yet offered.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho kenngwa ha puo ya seAforika ho Kereiti ya R le ho Kereiti ya 1 moo dipuo tseo di leng siyo.

src: Cabinet also commends the announcement by the University of KwaZulu-Natal to make isiZulu compulsory for undergraduate students, who are not proficient in isiZulu, to register for a course to develop conversational skills.
tgt: Kabinete hape e thoholetsa phatlalatso ya Yunivesithi ya KwaZulu-Natal ya ho etsa hore isiZulu e be setlamo ho barutwana ba qalang, ba sa tsebeng puo ya isiZulu hantle, ho ingodisa bakeng sa thuto eo ho ntshetsapele bokgoni ba ho qoqa.

src: Cabinet encourages all South Africans to learn an indigenous language as it promotes multilingualism and fosters nation-building.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa baahi bohle ba Aforika Borwa ho ithuta puo e le nngwe ya ka hara naha ka ha sena se kgothaletsa tsebo ya maleme a mangata le kaho ya setjhaba.

src: Cabinet notes that from 1 to 3 June 2013 President Jacob Zuma will pay an official visit to Japan and attend the 5th Tokyo International Conference on African Development (TICAD V).
tgt: Kabinete e ananela hore ho tloha ka la 1 ho ya ho la 3 Phuptjane 2013 Mopresidente Jacob Zuma o tla etela semmuso ho la Japan le ho kenela Khonferense ya Matjhaba ya bo hlano ya Tokyo mabapi le Ntshetsopele ya Aforika (TICAD V).

src: The theme of TICAD V in Yokohama, Japan, is: “Hand in Hand with a More Dynamic Africa.”.
tgt: Mookotaba wa TICAD V ho la Yokohama, Japan, ke: “Re tshwarisane le Aforika e Fetohelang Pele Haholo.”.

src: Cabinet is saddened by the passing of veteran journalist Vuyo Mbuli and offers condolences to the Mbuli family, friends and colleagues in the media industry.
tgt: Kabinete e maswabi ka ho hlokahala ha mokaubere wa raditaba Vuyo Mbuli le ho isa matshediso ho ba lelapa la Mbuli, metswalle le bomphato indastering ya boraditaba.

src: Mr Mbuli had contributed immensely to shaping the national discourse on key issues and his passion for his work had touched the hearts of South Africans.
tgt: Monghadi Mbuli o nyehetse haholo bakeng sa ho bopa dipuisano tsa setjhaba dintlheng tsa bohlokwa le lerato la mosebetsi wa hae le amme dipelo tsa baahi ba Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet expressed its deepest condolences to the citizens of Bangladesh and families and friends of over 1 000 garment factory workers who died when a building collapsed.
tgt: Kabinete e bontshitse matshediso a yona ho baahi ba Bangladesh le malapa le metswalle mabapi le basebeletsi ba fetang 1 000 ba feme ya masela ba hlokahetseng ha ba welwa ke moaho.

src: Our thoughts and prayers are with the people of Bangladesh.
tgt: Mehopolo le dithapelo tsa rona di na le setjhaba sa Bangladesh.

src: Cabinet is deeply saddened by the loss of lives and injuries as a result of major flooding in southern China.
tgt: Kabinete e maswabi haholo ka tahlehelo ya bophelo le ditemalo ka lebaka la dikgohola tse matla ho la China e ka borwa.

src: Cabinet also expressed deep sorrow at the death of five learners from Lwandile Village in Ngqeleni, Eastern Cape, who died in a bus accident.
tgt: Kabinete hape e bohloko haholo ka lefu la baithuti ba bahlano ba motsana wa Lwandile ho la Ngqeleni, Kapa Botjhabela, ba timetseng kotsing ya bese.

src: 30 learners were also injured during this tragic incident.
tgt: Baithuti ba 30 le bona ba ile ba lemala kotsing ena e mpe.

src: Government offers its condolences to the families, friends, fellow learners and educators of the victims.
tgt: Mmuso o isa matshediso a ona ho malapa, metswalle, baithutimmoho le matitjhere a diphofu.

src: It is a sad moment when South Africa loses future leaders.
tgt: Ho utlwisa bohloko ha Aforika Borwa e lahlehelwa ke baetapele ba kamoso.

src: Key Cabinet discussions and decisions.
tgt: Dipuisano le diqeto tsa bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved that the Green Paper on Policing be published in the Government Gazette for public comments.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana hore Pampiritshwaelo bakeng sa Tshebetso ya Sepolesa e phatlalatswe ho Kazete ya Mmuso bakeng sa hore setjhaba se tshwaele.

src: Since the establishment of the South African Police Service (SAPS) in 1994, there have been many changes in the internal and external environment that have impacted on the Service’s understanding of and response to issues of crime and safety.
tgt: Ho tloha ha ho ne ho thehwa Tshebeletso ya Sepolesa ya Aforika Borwa (SAPS) ka 1994, ho bile le diphetoho tse ngata tikolohong e ka hare le ka ntle e bileng le kgahlamelo kutlwisisong ya Tshebeletso le ho arabeleng dintlha tsa botlokotsebe le polokeho.

src: Post-1994, government was faced with addressing the twin objectives of creating a developmental state while also transforming the police into an institution of governance.
tgt: Ka mora 1994, Mmuso o ne o tobane le ho shebana le dipheo tse pedi tsa ho bopa mmuso o tswelang pele ka ho le leng o ntse o fetolela sepolesa ho institjushene ya taolo.

src: This Green Paper responds to the challenges identified following an assessment of the relevance of the 1996 Crime Prevention Strategy (NCPS) and the 1998 White paper on Safety and Security.
tgt: Pampiritshwaelo ena e arabela ho diphephetso tse hlwauweng ho latela tekolo ya kgema ha Leano la Setjhaba la Thibelo ya Botlokotsebe (NCPS) la 1996 le Pampiritemoso ya 1998 e mabapi le Paballo le Polokeho.

src: Embedded in these policies was the notion of addressing safety and security in a holistic manner through the development and implementation of integrated cross-sectoral programmes.
tgt: Setsing sa maano ana ho ne ho na le mohopolo wa ho shebana le ipaballo le polokeho ka mokgwa o batsi ka ntshetsopele le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha mananeo a akaretsang makala a fapaneng ka kopanelo.

src: Together they sought to put in place a comprehensive framework for dealing with broader issues of safety and security until 2004.The Green Paper deals with “Confronting Crime in a Democratic South Africa, Policing in South Africa, Mainstreaming Police Profssionalism and Institutional Arrangements”.
tgt: Mmoho mohopolo e ne e le ho hlahisa moralo o bataletseng bakeng sa ho sebetsana le dintlha tse batsi tsa paballo le polokeho ho fihlela ka 2004.Pampiritshwaelo e sebetsana le “Ho tobana le Botlokotsebe ho Aforika Borwa ya Demokerasi, Tshebetso ya Sepolesa ka hara Aforika Borwa, Batalatso ya Boprofeshenale le Ditlhophiso tsa Institjushene ya Sepolesa.” Sepheo sa sena ke hore qetellong ho etswe hore SAPS e arabele lepatlelo la botlokotsebe le ntseng le fetoha le ho kgotsofatsa ditlhoko tsa Mmuso o ntseng o tswelapele.

src: This aims to ultimately position the SAPS to respond to a constantly evolving criminal landscape while simultaneously meeting the needs of a developmental state.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana Moralo wa Naha wa Tshebetso bakeng sa Bana wa 2012-2017 jwaloka moralo o batsi bakeng sa ho fana ka tataiso le tshupiso ho mafapha a mmuso, badudi le bomphato ba bang lefapheng la tsa bana bakeng sa ho phethahatsa ditokelo tsa bana.

src: Cabinet approved the National Plan of Action for Children 2012-2017 as the comprehensive plan to give guidance and direction to government departments, civil society and other partners in the children’s sector towards the realisation of children’s rights.
tgt: Moralo ona o kenyeletsa Molaotheo, ditumellano tsa matjhaba le tsa lebatowa, ho hlaha ha molao bakeng sa bana ka hara Aforika Borwa, Dipheo tsa Ntshetsopele ya Mongwahakgolo le Moralo wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP) wa Pono ya 2030.Moralo ona o na le meokotaba e mehlano e ka sehloohong: ho phela ha bana (mohlala.

src: The plan embraces the Constitution, international and regional treaties, the emerging legislation on children in South Africa, Millennium Development Goals and the National Development Plan Vision 2030.The plan has five main themes: child survival (e. g. reduction of child mortality) child development (e. g. early childhood development services) child protection (e. g. protection from violence and sexual abuse) standard of living of children (e. g. conditions on accommodation for children) and child participation (e. g. children taking responsibility while enjoying their rights).This National Plan of Action for Children 2012-2017 will be further unpacked during a separate media briefing.
tgt: Phokotseho ya sekgahla sa ho shwa ha masea) kgodiso ya bana (mohlala Ditshebeletso tsa kgodiso ya bana ba sale banyane) tshireletso ya bana (mohlala tshireletso kgahlanong le merusu le tlhekefetso ka motabo) maemo a bophelo a bana (mohlala Maem a bodulo ba bana) le bonkakarolo ba bana (mohlala Bana ba be le boikarabelo ha ba sebedisa ditokelo tsa bona).Moralo ona wa Naha wa Tshebetso bakeng sa Bana wa 2012-2017 o tla ahlaahlwa ho ya pele nako e tlang ya boraditaba.

src: Cabinet approved that the Charter for African Cultural Renaissance be submitted to Parliament for approval of ratification in terms of Section 231 (92) of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana hore Tjhatara bakeng sa Ntjhafatso ya Botjhaba ba Aforika e nehelwe Palamenteng bakeng sa ho tjhaelwa monwana wa tokiso ho ya ka dipehelo tsa Karolo 231 (92) ya Molaotheo wa Rephaboliki ya Aforika Borwa.

src: The ratification of the Charter by government is a response to the Declaration on Cultural Renaissance and Shared Values of the 16th Ordinary Session of the African Union (AU) Heads of State and Government held in Equatorial Guinea, January 2011, and the Launch of the AU campaign on the Charter for African Cultural Renaissance which took place in late 2011 in South Africa.
tgt: Tokiso ya Tjhatara ke mmuso ke karabelo ho Boitlamo bakeng sa Ntjhafatso ya Botjhaba le Maitshwaro bo Tshwanang ba Tulo e Setlwaeding ya bo 16 ya Dihlooho tsa AU e neng e tshwaretswe ho la Equatorial Guinea, ka Pherekgong 2011, le Kgakolo ya letsholo la AU bakeng sa Tjhatara bakeng sa Ntjhafatso ya Botjhaba ba Aforika e neng e tshwaretswe Aforika Borwa ho ya mafelong a 2011.Tokiso ya Tjhatara e phahamisa tshireletso ya maitshwaro a botjhaba a maAforika le mafa a botjhaba mme e kgothaletsa Boikgantsho ba BoAforika.

src: Ratification of the Charter enhances protection of African cultural values and cultural heritage and promotes the spirit of Pan-Africanism.
tgt: Tjhatara e kgothaletsa kopanngo ya botjhaba, bonono, maitshwaro a botjhaba, puo, lefa mmoho le diindasteri tsa botjhaba le popo e le tsa bohlokwa bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya nako e telele.

src: This has the potential to contribute to the growth of the economy and social cohesion.
tgt: Sena se na le boleng ba ho nyehela kgolong ya moruo le kopanong ya kahisano.

src: The Charter is aligned to the New Growth Path, the National Development Plan, the White Paper on Arts, Culture and Heritage and the Mzansi Golden Economy Strategy.
tgt: Tjhatara e nyalantswe le Tsela e Ntjha ya Kgolo, NDP, Pampiritemoso mabapi le Bonono, Botjhaba le Lefa le Leano la Moruo la Gauta ya Mzansi.

src: The Minster of Arts and Culture will host a media briefing in this regard.
tgt: Letona la Bonono le Botjhaba o tla bitsa kopano ya boraditaba mabapi le sena.

src: Cabinet noted the hosting of the first Science, Technology and Innovation Summit from 20 to 21 July 2013.The planned dialogue during the Summit provides a platform to explore ways to enhance coordination between government and the private sector.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho tshwarwa ha Seboka sa pele sa Saense, Theknoloji le Ntlafatso (STI) ho tloha ka la 20 ho ya ho la 21 Phupu 2013.Dipuisano tse rerilweng nakong ya Seboka di fana ka lepatlelo la ho fatana le ditsela tsa ho ntlafatsa kgokahanyo pakeng tsa mmuso le lefapha la poraefete.

src: The Summit will enable participants to explore ways in which science, technology and innovation (STI) can play a significant role in our journey towards a knowledge-based economy and realisation of Vision Bills.
tgt: Seboka se tla kgontsha bankakarolo ho fatana le ditsela tsa kamoo STI e ka bapalang karolo ya bohlokwa leetong la rona la ho ya moruong o itshetlehileng tsebong le ho phethahatsa Pono ya Dibili.

src: Cabinet approved the proposed amendments to the Draft Public Administration Management (PAM) Bill which will now be published for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana Bili e lohothwang ya sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Moralo wa Tsamaiso ya Setjhaba (PAM) se jwale se tla phatlalatswang bakeng sa tshwaelo ya setjhaba.

src: The draft Bill seeks to create a uniform legal framework for human resources and certain organisational and governance matters in national, provincial and municipal administrations.
tgt: Bili ya moralo e batla ho hlahisa moralo wa semolao o tshwanang bakeng sa basebetsi le mabaka a itseng a tlhophiso le taolo ho tsamaiso ya naha, porofense le bomasepala.

src: This is aimed at enhancing service delivery through a uniform system of public administration, improved utilisation of staff and the creation of a single door to government services for citizens.
tgt: Sepheo sa sena ke ho ntlafatsa phano ya ditshebeletso ka mokgwa o tshwanang bakeng sa tsamaiso ya tsa setjhaba, tshebediso e ntlafetseng ya basebeletsi le ho theha kgoro e le nngwe bakeng sa ditshebeletso tsa mmuso ho baahi.

src: Cabinet approved the Public Service Commission Amendment Bill for public comment and the introduction of the Amendment Bill in Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Khomishene ya Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba bakeng sa tshwaelo ya setjhaba le ho hlahiswa ha Sehlomathiso sa Bili Palamenteng.

src: The purpose of the Amendment Bill is to align the Public Service Commission Act of 1997 with the Constitution.
tgt: Sepheo sa Sehlomathiso sa Bili ke ho matahanya Molao wa Khomishene ya Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba wa 1997 le Molaotheo.

src: It further seeks to empower the Public Service Commission to give directions relating to the principles that govern public administration.
tgt: Ho fetafeta moo se batla ho matlafatsa Khomishene ya Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba hore e fane ka tataiso e tsamaelanang le melawana e busang tsamaiso setjhaba.

src: This is in line with the strengthened role envisaged by the National Development Plan for the Commission.
tgt: Sena se tsamaelana le karolo e matlafaditsweng e labalabelwang ke NDP bakeng sa Khomishene.

src: Cabinet approved that the South African Weather Service Amendment Bill 2013 be published for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana hore Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Tshebeletso ya Tsa Boemo Ba Lehodimo ya Aforika Borwa sa 2013 se phatlalatswe bakeng sa tshwaelo ya setjhaba.

src: This Amendment Bill seeks to amend the South African Weather Services Act, 2001 (Act No.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Bili ena ke ho hlomathisa Molao wa Tshebeletso tsa Boemo ba Lehodimo, wa 2001 (Molao wa 08 wa 2001) o nehelanang ka ho thehwa, dipheo, matla le mesebetsi ya Tshebeletso ya Tsa Boemo Ba Lehodimo ya Aforika Borwa.

src: 08 of 2001) which provides for the establishment, objectives, powers and functions of the South African Weather WEBTOKEN the main the amendments will provide the South African Weather Service with a legal mandate to implement the ambient air quality information management function, and to act as a custodian of the South African Air Quality information System.
tgt: Haholoholo dihlomathiso di tla neha Tshebeletso ya Tsa Boemo Ba Lehodimo ya Aforika Borwa tumello ya molao ya ho kenya tshebetsong mosebetsi wa taolo ya boleng ba tlhahisoleseding ka moya o fetofetohang, le ho sebetsa jwaloka mohlokomedi wa Mokgwa wa Tlhahisoleseding ka Boleng ba Moya wa Aforika Borwa.

src: This contributes towards protecting and enhancing our environmental assets and natural resources.
tgt: Sena se nyehela ho tshireletseng le ho matlafatseng ha thepa ya rona ya tikoloho le mehlodi ya tlhaho.

src: Cabinet approved that the Mineral and Petroleum Resources Development Draft Amendment Bill, 2012 be submitted to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana hore Moralo wa Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Ntshetsopele ya Mehlodi ya Diminerale le Petroliamo, wa 2012 o nehelwe Palamente.

src: The Mineral and Petroleum Resources Development Draft Amendment Bill 2012 (Draft Bill) seeks to amend the Mineral and Petroleum Resources Development Act, 2002 (Act No.
tgt: Moralo wa Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Ntshetsopele ya Mehlodi ya Diminerale le Petroliamo (Bili ya Sehlomathiso) o batla ho hlomathisa Molao wa Ntshetsopele ya Mehlodi ya Diminerale le Petroliamo wa 2002 (Molao wa 28 wa 2002) jwaloka ha o hlomathisitswe ke Molao wa Ntshetsopele ya Mehlodi ya Diminerale le Petroliamo wa 2008 (Molao wa 49 wa 2008).Dipheo tse kgolo tsa moralo wa Bili ya Sehlomathiso ke, hara tse ding, ho matlafatsa phano bakeng sa ho tshwaelwa ha diminerale hore ho hodiswe indasteri le ho nyehela dipheong tsa naha tsa ho hlahisa mesebetsi le kgolo ya moruo jwaloka ha ho labalabelwa ke NDHo tla behwa nako e ikgethileng bakeng sa ntlha ena.

src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment Cabinet wishes President Nelson Mandela a speedy recovery and reassures the nation that he is receiving the best medical care.
tgt: Maemo a Kabinete mabapi le dintlha tsa bohlokwa maemong a ha jwale.

src: Cabinet is pleased that he is responding well to treatment and reiterates the request for the media and the public to respect the privacy of the former President and his family during this period.
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa Mopresidente wa mehleng Nelson Mandela ho fola ka potlako le ho netefaletsa setjhaba hore o fumana tlhokomelo e hlwahlwa ka ho fetisisa ya bongaka.

src: Cabinet commends the work of the Justice, Crime, Prevention and Security Cluster’s Anti-Corruption Task Team (ACTT) which was established by President Jacob Zuma in 2010.
tgt: Kabinete e nyakaletse hore o arabela kalafo hantle le ho pheta kopo ya yona ho boraditaba le setjhaba hore ho hlomphuwe boinotshi ba Mopresidente wa mehleng le lelapa la hae nakong ena.

src: For the first time in the history of our democracy, criminals who had abused public trust and resources were made known and held accountable for their actions publicly.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa mosebetsi wa Moifo wa Tshebetso wa Twantsho ya Bobodu wa Lekala la Toka, Thibelo ya Botlokotsebe le Polokeho o ileng wa thehwa ke Mopresidente Jacob Zuma ka 2010.

src: This aggressive stance aims to deter people in the private and public sectors from engaging in corrupt and criminal activities and is driven by our commitment to ensure that all citizens are and feel safe.
tgt: Lekgetlo la pele nalaneng ya demokerasi ya rona, ditlokotsebe tse sebedisitseng tshepo ya setjhaba hampe le mehlodi di ile tsa tsebahatswa le hore di arabelle diketso tsa tsona phatlalatsa.

src: Cabinet condemns in the strongest terms the recent acts of racism in some parts of our country.
tgt: Ho se mamelle bobodu ka ho phethahala ha Mmuso wa Aforika Borwa ho re atametsa haufi le pono ya rona bakeng sa 2030 moo setjhaba sa Aforika Borwa se tla itshupang ka maemo a phahameng a boitshwaro le tlhompho e phethahetseng.

src: There is no room for racism in our country and democracy, let alone in our schools, where the values of our Constitution ought to be promoted and defended.
tgt: Qeto ena e matla e batla ho thibela batho ba makaleng a poraefete le a setjhaba ho kena diketsahalong tsa bobodu le botlokotsebe le ho kgannwa ke boitlamo ba rona ba ho netefatsa hore baahi bohle ba bolokehile le ho ikutlwa ba bolokehile.

src: Cabinet commends the Department of Basic Education for its quick action in dealing with racism in schools and encourages all parents, pupils, and teachers to report racism and abuse at schools.
tgt: Kabinete e nyefola ka bohale diketsahalo tsa semorabe tsa haufinyana tjena dikarolong tse ding tsa naha ya rona.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to work together with government to get deal with racism whenever it occurs in our society.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa oohle ho sebetsana le bosemorabe hohle moo bo hlahellang teng setjhabeng sa rona.

src: Cabinet welcomes the visit to the Republic of South Africa by the President of the United States of America (US), Barack Obama which is part of a three-nation visit to Senegal, Tanzania and South Africa between 26 June and 3 July 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela leeto la Mopresidente wa Amerika, Barack Obama ho la Aforika Borwa, e leng karolo ya ketelo ya dinaha tse tharo e leng Senegal, Tanzania le Aforika Borwa mahareng a la 26 Phuptjane le 3 Phupu 2013.

src: Our strategic political dialogue with the United States continues to positively impact our bilateral relations.
tgt: Puisano ya rona ya maele a sepolotiki le Amerika e tswela pele ka sekgahla se setle hodima dikamano tsa bobedi ba rona.

src: The US remains an important trade, investment, tourism and technology partner.
tgt: Amerika e dula e le molekane wa bohlokwa ho tsa kgwebisano, matsete, bohahlaudi le theknoloji.

src: Cabinet commended the landmark meeting on the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme (KPCS) held between 4 and 7 June 2013 in Kimberley.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholeditse kopano ya bohlokwa mabapi le Sekema sa Setifikeiti sa Tshupo sa Kimberley (KPCS) e neng e tshwerwe mahareng a la 4 le 7 Phuptjane 2013 ho la Kimberley.

src: The Summit discussed amongst other things ways of strengthening the effectiveness of the rough diamond certification scheme.
tgt: Seboka sena se tshohlile hara tse ding ditsela tsa ho matlafatsa bohlwahlwa ba sekema sa setifikeiti sa tshupo sa taemane e tala.

src: This is to ensure that diamond trade does not finance violence by rebel movements and their allies that seek to undermine legitimate governments.
tgt: Sena ke ho netefatsa hore kgwebisano ya taemane ha e lefelle merusu ya mekgatlo ya marabele le batshehetsi ba yona ba batlang ho kgella fatshe mebuso e molaong.

src: Recommendations from this meeting will be considered at the plenary meeting of the KPCS to be held later this year.
tgt: Dikgothaletso ho tswa kopanong ena di tla sekasekwa kopanong ya seboka ya KPCS e tla tshwarwa ha morao selemong sena.

src: Cabinet noted that the commemoration of Youth Day which in 2013 marks the 37th anniversary of June 16 Soweto Uprising will be celebrated under the theme “Working together for youth development and a drug free South Africa”.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse hore ho hopolwa ha Letsatsi la Batjha leo ka 2013 le tshwayang sehopotso sa dilemo tse 37 sa Merusu ya Phutjane 16 ya Soweto se tla ketekwa tlasa mookotaba o reng “Ha re sebetseng mmoho bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya batjha le Aforika Borwa e hlokang dithethefatsi”.

src: Cabinet acknowledged the sacrifices made by the class of 1976 in turning the history of the country and setting South Africa firmly on the road to democracy.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse boinehelo bo entsweng ke sehlopha sa 1976 bakeng sa ho fetola nalane ya naha le ho tsepamisa Aforika Borwa tseleng e isang demokerasing.

src: Cabinet reiterated that, while the youth of 1976 fought for freedom and the creation of a democratic state, today’s youth activism is directed towards successfully tackling the challenges of combating poverty, unemployment, HIV and AIDS, personal development and drug abuse.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya pheta hore, ha batjha ba 1976 ba lwanetse tokoloho le ho thehwa ha mmuso wa demokerasi, tshebetso ya batjha ba kajeno ke e isang ho sebetsaneng ka katleho le diphephetso tsa bofuma, tlhoko ya mesebetsi, HIV le AIDS, bointshetsopele le tshebediso e mpe ya dithethefatsi.

src: Cabinet encourages all South Africans and organisations to work together to improve the lives of young people and fight to remove the drug dealers within our communities.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa maAforika Borwa oohle le mekgatlo ho sebetsa mmoho bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa bophelo ba batjha le ho lwanela ho tlosa barekisi ba dithethefatsi metseng ya rona.

src: The national Youth Day commemoration will take place on Sunday, 16 June 2013 in Newcastle, KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Ho hopolwa ha Letsatsi la Batjha la naha ho tla tshwarwa ka Sontaha, 16 Phuptjane 2013 ho la Newcastle, KwaZulu-Natal.

src: Cabinet congratulates the Congress of South African Students (Cosas) on its 34th anniversary, which has its roots in the Soweto 1976 struggle for free, quality and relevant education.
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa Mokgatlo wa Baithuti wa Aforika Borwa (Cosas) mahlohonolo sehopotsong sa ona sa dilemo tse 34, o nang le metso ya yona ho ntwa ya Soweto ya 1976 bakeng sa thuto e lefellweng, e nang le boleng le ho ipapisa le maemo.

src: The country joins Cosas in celebrating its remarkable achievements and in advancing quality education for all.
tgt: Naha e ikamahanya le Cosas ha e keteka diphihlello tsa yona tse babatsehang le ho kgothaletsa thuto e nang le boleng bakeng sa bohle.

src: Cabinet also commends the leadership of Cosas for taking the initiative to rally young people against drug abuse.
tgt: Kabinete hape e thoholetsa boetapele ba Cosas bakeng sa ho etsa matsapa a ho bokanya batjha kgahlanong le tshebediso e mpe ya dithethefatsi.

src: Cabinet condemns the acts of public dumping of human waste in the Western Cape by the protestors against portable bucket toilets.
tgt: Kabinete e nyefola diketso tsa ho tshollela mantle pontsheng ho la Kapa Bophirima ke baipelaetsi ba kgahlanong le matlwana a mabakete.

src: While, Government respects citizens’ right to protest, this particular form of protest is undignified and poses a serious health risk to communities and to the protesters themselves.
tgt: Le ha, Mmuso o hlompha tokelo ya baahi ya ho ipelaetsa, mokgwa o tjena wa ho ipelaetsa o hloka seriti mme o ka baka kotsi e kgolo bophelong bo botle ba badudi le ho baipelaetsi ka bo bona.

src: Cabinet calls on citizens to raise their grievances constructively and to treat public institutions with utmost respect irrespective of their grievances.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho baahi ho hlahisa dingongoreho tsa bona ka tsela e lokileng le ho hlompha ditsha tsa mmuso ho sa natswe dingongoreho tsa bona.

src: Cabinet further called on authorities to speedily address issues in a manner that is in keeping with our Constitution.
tgt: Ho fetafeta moo Kabinete e entse kgoeletso ho ba ka sehloohong hore ba sebetsane le mabaka ka potlako ka tsela e ipapisitseng le Molaotheo wa rona.9 Mmuso, tlasa boetapele ba Motlatsa Mopresidente Kgalema Motlanthe, o ile wa kopana le baetapele ba bodumedi ba emetseng Lekgotla la Aforika Borwa la Dikereke le Khonferense ya Babishopo ba Katholiki ba Aforika Borwa ho tshohla dingongoreho tsa bona tsa kamoo Projeke ya Ntlafatso ya Mebila e Bulehileng ya Gauteng e tlang ho thefula bafutsana le hore mmuso ha o kgathalle dihloko tsa ba kojwana di mahetleng.

src: Cabinet re-iterates that government has exempted registered public transport (which is largely used by the poor) from the toll tariffs on the Gauteng toll roads.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e pheta hore mmuso ha o a kenyeletsa dipalangwang tsa setjhaba tse ngodisitsweng (tse sebediswang haholo ke ba kojwana di mahetleng) ditefellong tsa mebila e lefuwang ya Gauteng.

src: Also, to address the concerns of the other motorist, government has reduced the tariffs and introduced new capped amounts for all categories of vehicles.
tgt: Hodima moo, bakeng sa ho sebetsana le dingongoreho tsa boramakoloi ba bang, mmuso o theotse ditefello le ho hlahisa ditefello tse ntjha tse nyehlisitsweng bakeng sa mekgahlelo yohle ya makoloi.

src: Cabinet encourages motorists in Gauteng to register for e-tags and to view this project as part of the country's drive to build public infrastructure.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa boramakoloi ba Gauteng ho ingodisa bakeng sa di e-tag le ho nka projeke ena jwaloka mekutu ya naha ya ho aha meralo ya motheo ya setjhaba.

src: Cabinet congratulates Bafana Bafana and Banyana Banyana Soccer Teams and the Proteas Cricket Team on their recent wins in football and cricket.
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa dihlopha tsa Bolo tsa Bafana Bafana le Banyana Banyana le Sehlopha sa Kerikete sa Diprothea mahlohonolo ka ho hlola ha bona bolong le keriketeng.

src: Cabinet congratulates the national teams on their hard-fought victories over the past week and encourages all South Africans to support our national teams.
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa dihlopha tsa setjhaba mahlohonolo bakeng sa ditlholo tsa bona tse lwanetsweng ka thata bekeng e sa tswa feta le ho kgothaletsa maAforika Borwa oohle ho tshehetsa dihlopha tsa rona tsa naha.

src: Cabinet welcomed the launch of Power FM, a new talk-radio station, as a new player in the industry.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse ho thakgolwa ha Power FM, seteishene sa radio se setjha sa dipuisano, jwaloka setlabotjha indastering ena.

src: Cabinet noted that the station will deal with politics, social issues and sport in the main and joins a list of radio platforms that can be used to inform South Africans.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse hore seteishene sena se tla sebetsana haholo le dipolotiki, mabaka a kahisano le dipapadi le ho imatahanya le letoto la mapatlelo a radio a ka sebediswang bakeng sa ho hlahlella maAforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet congratulates the Department of Health Director General, Dr Malebona Precious Matsoso, on her appointment as a member and one of the Vice chairpersons of the World Health Assembly Executive Board for a period of 3 years.
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa Motsamaisikakaretso wa Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle, Ngaka Malebona Precious Matsoso, bakeng sa ho thonngwa ha hae jwaloka setho le e mong wa Motlatsa baduladitulo ba Boto ya Phethahatso ya Seboka sa Lefatshe sa Bophelo bo Botle bakeng sa dilemo tse tharo.

src: Key Cabinet discussions and decisions Cabinet noted that the Financial Intelligence Centre of South Africa will host the 2013 Annual Plenary and General Working Group Meetings of the Egmont Group of financial intelligence units.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse hore Setsi sa Mautlwela a Ditjhelete sa Aforika Borwa se tla tshwara dikopano tsa Selemo ka seng ya 2013 le ya Seboka le Sehlopha sa Tshebetso sa Kakaretso sa Sehlopha sa Egmont sa dikarolwana tsa mautlwela a ditjhelete.

src: The Egmont Group is an organisation of financial intelligence units from 131 countries.
tgt: Sehlopha sa Egmont ke mokgatlo wa dikarolwana tsa mautlwela a ditjhelete ho tswa dinaheng tse 131.

src: They meet regularly to enable international cooperation to identify the proceeds of crime, combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism with the objective of defending the integrity of the financial system.
tgt: Di kopana kgafetsa ho kgontsha tshebedisano mmoho bakeng sa ho hlwaya dikuno tsa botlokotsebe, ho thibela ho hasanngwa ha tjhelete ho seng molaong le ho thuswa ha boferekanyi ka ditjhelete ka sepheo sa ho tshireletsa mokgwa wa tsa tshebediso ya ditjhelete o nang le seriti.

src: Cabinet noted the election of South Africa to serve on the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) for the period 2013 - 2015.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetstse ho kgethwa ha Aforika Borwa bakeng sa ho sebetsa ho Lekgotla la Matjhaba a Kopaneng la Moruo le Kahisano (ECOSOC) bakeng sa 2013 – 2015.

src: This presents an opportunity to strategically position South Africa’s leadership on development issues and reinforce the country’s role as a consistent and effective player in multilateralism.
tgt: Sena se hlahisa monyetla wa ho beha boetapele ba Aforika Borwa ka bohlale bakeng sa mabaka a ntshetsopele le ho matlafatsa karolo ya naha jwaloka sebapadi sa bohlokwa le se hlwahlwa dipuisanong le matjhabatjhaba.

src: South Africa will also ensure that ECOSOC is further strengthened and reformed to better meet evolving global challenges and the needs of developing countries.
tgt: Hape Aforika Borwa e tla netefatsa hore ECOSOC e boela e matlafaditswe le ho ahwa botjha hore e tle e kgone ho tobana le diphephetso ka bokgabane tsa lefatshe le fetofetohang le ditlhoko tsa dinaha tse ntseng di tswela pele.

src: Cabinet noted the report on South Africa’s Non-Permanent membership of the United Nations Security Council from 1 January 2011 to 31 December 2012.The report describes South Africa’s influence in the global governance system in the maintenance of international peace and security.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse tlaleho ka ha Setho se seng sa ka dinako tsohle sa Lekgotla la Matjhaba a Kopaneng la Tshireletso (UNSC) ho tloha ka la 1 Pherekgong 2011 ho isa ho la 31 Tshitwe 2012.Tlaleho ena e hlalosa kgahlamelo ya Aforika Borwa mokgweng wa taolo wa lefatshe bakeng sa ho boloka kgotso le polokeho ya matjhaba.

src: In line with its values and national interests, South Africa in the UNSC prioritised conflict resolution and peace and stability on the African Continent.
tgt: Ho ipapisitswe le mabaka a maitshwaro le dikgahleho tsa naha, Aforika Borwa ho UNSC e behile ka sehloohong tharollo ya diqabang le kgotso le botsitso Kontinenteng ya Aforika.

src: Membership of the UNSC also provided South Africa with an opportunity to strengthen relations with key developing country partners - Brazil, India, Nigeria and China - who shared Council membership with South Africa.
tgt: Setho sa UNSC hape se file Aforika Borwa monyetla wa ho matlafatsa dikamano le balekane ba bohlokwa ba dinaha tse ntseng di tswela pele – Brazil, India, Nigeria le China – tse arolelaneng setho sa Lekgotla le Aforika Borwa.

src: Bills Cabinet approved that the Disaster Management Amendment Bill be published for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana hore Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Taolo ya Dikoduwa se phatlalatswe bakeng sa maikutlo a setjhaba.

src: This Bill aims to address the challenges which are being experienced across the spheres of government after commencement of the Disaster Management Act 2002.
tgt: Sepheo sa Sehlomathiso sena ke ho tobana le diphephetso tse bonahalang di le teng ho ya le mekgahlelo ya mmuso kamora ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Molao wa Taolo ya Dikoduwa wa 2002.

src: The Amendment will re-affirm the function of district municipalities regarding the responsibility to establish capacity for the development and coordination of a disaster management plan.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sena se tla tiisetsa botjha mosebetsi wa bomasepala ba ditereke mabapi le ho thehwa ha matla bakeng sa ntshetsopele le kgokahanyo ya moralo wa taolo ya dikoduwa.

src: This includes the implementation of a disaster management function for the municipal area.
tgt: Sena se kenyeletsa ho kenngwa tshebetsong mosebetsi wa taolo ya dikoduwa bakeng sa tulo ya masepala.

src: The Disaster Management Act 2002 has a fourfold focus: It establishes an elaborate institutional framework for disaster management it entrenches a detailed policy development and strategic planning framework for disaster management.
tgt: Molao wa Taolo ya Dikoduwa wa 2002 o tobile dintlha tse nne: O theha moralo o batsi wa dibaka bakeng sa taolo ya dikoduwa o thatiselletsa ho hodiswa ha leano le keneletseng la moralo wa bohlale ba taolo ya dikoduwa.

src: The bill further provides for the classification and declaration of disaster and it deals provisionally with the funding of post-disaster recovery and rehabilitation.
tgt: Ho fetafeta moo sehlomathiso se fana ka tlhophiso le peho ya koduwa mme se bua bakeng sa nako e seng kae ka matlole boiphumano le tokiso tsa kamora koduwa.

src: It provides for disaster management volunteers and a few other ancillary matters.
tgt: Se fana ka baithaopi ba taolo ya dikoduwa le mabakanyana a mang a tlatsetso.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Local Government Municipal property Rates Amendment Bill to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana ho kenngwa ha Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Ditefello tsa thepa ya Bomasepala ba Mmuso wa Lehae Palamenteng.

src: The Local Government: Municipal Property rates Act became effective on 2 July 2005.
tgt: Mmuso wa Lehae: Molao wa Ditefello tsa Thepa ya Bomasepala o qadile ho kena tshebetsong ka la 2 Phupu 2005.

src: It was amended twice in 2008 and 2009.
tgt: O ile wa ntlafatswa botjha ka 2008 le 2009.

src: The amendments seek to remove ambiguity and provide greater legal certainty.
tgt: Sepheo sa dintlafatso botjha ke ho tlosa pherekano le ho fana ka bonnete ba molao bo utlwahalang.

src: The amendment will allow for transparency in the setting of rates for different property categories, thus enhancing property owners understanding of rating.
tgt: Ntlafatso botjha e tla dumella ponaletso bakeng sa ho beha ditefello bakeng sa mekgahlelo e fapaneng ya thepa, kahoo e ntlafatsa kutlwisiso ya borathepa ditefello.

src: The amendment will exclude certain public service infrastructure (PSI) such as roads, railways, airports aprons and runways, dams and breakwater from being rated.
tgt: Ntlafatso botjha ha e no kenyeletsa meralo e itseng ya motheo ya ditshebeletso tsa setjhaba e kang mebila, diporo, dibaka tsa maemafofane, matamo le metsi a dinoka hore di lefellwe.

src: These are publicly controlled and will not disadvantage private sectors.
tgt: Tsena di laolwa ke setjhaba mme di ke ke tsa kgathatsa makala a poraefete.

src: This would enhance economic activity across municipal boundaries.
tgt: Sena se tla eketsa diketsahalo tsa moruo ho ya le meedi ya bomasepala .

src: It would also contribute to the developmental role of SOEs by reducing their fixed costs.
tgt: Hape sena se tla nyehela karolong ya ntshetsopele ya Dikgwebo tsa Mmuso ka ho fokotsa ditjeho tsa bona tsa motjha-o-tjhele.

src: Cabinet approved a battery of Merchant Shipping Legislation for tabling in Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana letoto la Melao ya Dikepe tsa Kgwebo bakeng sa ho tshohlwa Palamenteng.

src: These Bills form part of a package of measures designed to give effect to South Africa’s obligations under the International Maritime Organisation Protocol of 1992.
tgt: Dihlomathiso tsena ke karolo ya pakana ya mekutu e reretsweng ho fana ka sekgahla ho boitlamo ba Aforika Borwa tlasa Protokhole ya Mokgatlo wa Mawatle ya Matjhaba ya Sepheo sa Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Dikepe tsa Kgwebo (Tumellano ya Boikarabelo ho Setjhaba) ke ho: kenya tshebetsong Protokhole ya Mokgatlo wa Mawatle ya Matjhaba ya 1992 le ho o fetisa e le molao wa Tumellano ya Matjhaba ho Boikarabelo ho Setjhaba bakeng sa Tshenyo ka Tshilafatso ya Oli se ntlafaditsweng botjha sa, 1969.

src: .1 The purpose of the Merchant Shipping (Civil Liability Convention) Bill is to: enact International Maritime Organisation Protocol, 1992 and to pass into law the amended International Convention on Civil Liability for Oil Pollution Damage, 1969.
tgt: Tumellano ya Boikarabelo ho Setjhaba e theha le ho laola boikarabelo ba monga sekepe ya ngodisitsweng.

src: The Civil Liability Convention establishes and regulates the liability of the registered ship owner.
tgt: Sepheo sa Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Dikepe tsa Kgwebo (Letlole la Matjhaba la Ditlhapiso tsa Tshilafatso ya Oli) ke ho: kenya tshebetsong Protokhole ya 1992 ho Tumellano ya Matjhaba bakeng sa ho Thehwa ha Letlole la Matjhaba bakeng sa Tshenyo ya Tshilafatso ka Oli, ya 1971 (Tumellano ya Letlole).Tumellano ya Letlole e theha Letlole la Matjhaba, le bitswang Letlole la Matjhaba la Ditlhapiso tsa Tshilafatso ya Oli (IOPC).

src: .2 The aim of the Merchant Shipping (International Oil Pollution Compensation Fund) Bill is to: implement the 1992 Protocol to the International Convention on the Establishment of an International Fund for Compensation for Oil Pollution Damage, 1971 (the Fund Convention).
tgt: Sepheo sa Letlole ke ho lefella ditlhapiso ho mahlatsipa a tshenyo ka tshilafatso (ka hara moelelo wa Tumellano ya Boikarabelo ho Setjhaba) moo ba sa kgonang ho thola ditlhapiso, kapa ditlhapiso ka botlalo, tlasa dipehelo tsa Tumellano ya Boikarabelo ho Setjhaba.

src: The Fund Convention establishes an international Fund, called the International Oil Pollution Compensation (IOPC) Fund.
tgt: Letlole la IOPC le fumana ditjhelete ho tswa ho beng ba thepa.

src: The purpose of the Fund is to pay compensation to victims of pollution damage (within the meaning of the Civil Liability Convention) where they have been unable to obtain compensation, or compensation in full, under the provisions of the Civil Liability Convention.
tgt: Dihlomathiso tsa Boikarabelo ho Setjhaba le Letlole la Ditumellano di sebetsana le mabaka a boikarabelo le ditlhapiso bakeng sa tahlehelo kapa tshenyo e bakilweng ke tshwaetso ka lebaka la ho tsholoha kapa ho dutla ha oli e tswang ditankeng tsa oli.

src: The Civil Liability and Fund Conventions Bills deal with questions of liability and compensation for loss or damage caused by contamination resulting from the escape or discharge of persistent oil from tankers.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Dinyehelo wa Dikepe tsa Kgwebo (Letlole la Matjhaba la Ditlhapiso tsa Tshilafatso ya Oli) le Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Tsamaiso ya Dikepe tsa Kgwebo (Letlole la Matjhaba la Ditlhapiso tsa Tshilafatso ya Oli) di fana ka ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Protokhole ya Mokgatlo wa Mawatle wa Matjhaba ya 1992 ho ntlafatsa botjha Tumellano ya Matjhaba bakeng sa ho Thehwa ha Letlole la Matjhaba bakeng sa Tshenyo ka Tshilafatso ka Oli, ke Aforika Borwa.

src: .3 The Merchant Shipping (International Oil Pollution Compensation Fund) Contributions Bill and the Merchant Shipping (International Oil Pollution Compensation Fund) Administration Bill provide for the implementation of the International Maritime Organisation Protocol of 1992 to amend the International Convention on the Establishment of an International Fund for Oil Pollution Damage, by South Africa.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa molao wa Tsamaiso se tla fana ka tumello ya molao e hlokahalang ho kgontsha ba Ditshebeletso tsa Lekeno la Aforika Borwa ho tsamaisa pokello ya lekgetho la Letlole la Matjhaba la Ditlhapiso tsa Tshilafatso ya Oli.

src: The Administration Bill will provide the necessary legislative authority to enable the South African Revenue Service (SARS) to administer the collection of the International Oil Pollution Compensation Fund Contributions levy.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Dinyehelo ke Sehlomathiso sa tjhelete se fanang ka ho behwa le pokello ya dinyehelo tse tshwanelang ho lefellwa ho Letlole.

src: Appointments Cabinet approved the appointment of seven (7) members for a period of five (5) years with effect from 12 June 2013, to serve on the Sport and Recreation Distributing Agency, in terms of the Lotteries Act (No.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana ho thonngwa ha ditho tse supileng (7) bakeng sa nako ya dilemo tse hlano (5) ho tloha ka la 12 Phuptjane 2013, ho sebetsa ho Lekala la Bophatlalatsi la Dipapadi le Boikgathollo, ho ya ka Molao wa Diloto ( wa nomoro ya 57 wa 1997).a.

src: Dr Vukile Charles Mehanab.
tgt: Ngaka Vukile Charles Mehanab.

src: Mr Thandisenzo Aleck Skhosanac.
tgt: Monghadi Thandisenzo Aleck Skhosanac.

src: Ms Muditambi Raveled.
tgt: Mofumahadi Muditambi Raveled.

src: Ms Annamarie Louise van Wieringene.
tgt: Mofumahadi Annamarie Louise van Wieringene.

src: Ms Krubavathi Jaramf.
tgt: Mofumahadi Krubavathi Jaramf.

src: Mr Ado Moloabi andg.
tgt: Monghadi Goliath Munro.

src: Mr Goliath Munro Cabinet approved the appointment of three (3) members for a period of five (5) years with effect from 12 June 2013, to serve on the Arts, Culture and National Heritage Distributing Agency in terms of the Lotteries Act (No 57 of 1997).
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana ho thonngwa ha ditho tse tharo (3) bakeng sa nako ya dilemo tse hlano (5) ho tloha ka la 12 Phuptjane 2013, ho sebetsa ho Lekala la Bophatlalatsi la Bonono, Botjhaba le Setso ho ya ka Molao wa Diloto (wa nomoro ya 57 ya 1997).a.

src: a. Ms Hellen Kentse Makgaeb.
tgt: Mofumahadi Hellen Kentse Makgaeb.

src: Ms Violet Tyamzashe andc.
tgt: Mofumahadi Violet Tyamzashe lec.

src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment Cabinet joins the nation and the international community in praying for the father of the nation, former President Nelson Mandela.
tgt: Kabinete e imatahanya le setjhaba le ba matjhabeng bakeng sa ho rapella ntate wa setjhaba, Mopresidente wa mehlengNelson Mandela.

src: At this difficult time, let us all show love and compassion and make Madiba proud.
tgt: Nakong ena e boima, ha re bontsheng lerato le kutlwelobohloko mme re etse Madiba motlotlo.

src: Cabinet noted the 58th anniversary of the signing of the Freedom Charter signed on the 26th June 1955 which is the foundation of our democracy and Constitution.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho ketekwa ha selemo sa bo 58 sa ho tekenwa ha Tjhata ya Tokoloho e neng e tekenwe ka la 26 Phuptjane 1955 e leng motheo wa demokerasi le Molaotheo wa rona.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to ‘Play Your Part’ in taking the country closer to the vision of a united, non-racial, non-sexist, democratic and prosperous South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa oohle ho ‘Bapala karolo ya lona’ mabapi le ho isa naha haufiufi le pono ya Aforika Borwa e kopaneng, e hlokang semorabe, e hlokang kgethollo ka bong, ya demokerasi le e tswetseng pele.

src: Cabinet welcomes the renewed commitment by the Department of Health, together with researchers, to confront issues that pose challenges to the collective efforts in the fight against HICabinet also welcomes preparations by the Department of Health to introduce a number of new interventions into existing structures which include increased awareness on HIV and AIDS, and measures to decrease the risk of HIV infection.
