tgt: Kabinete e amohela boitlamo bo botjha ba Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle, mmoho le bafuputsi bakeng sa ho tobana le dintlha tse hlahisang diphepetso bakeng sa mekutu e kopanetsweng ya ntwa kgahlanong le HIKabinete hape e amohela boitokisetso ba Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle ba ho hlahisa boikenyako bo atisitsweng ho mefuta e teng e kenyeletsang tlhokomediso e ekeditsweng mabapi le HIV le AIDS, le mehato bakeng sa ho fokotsa kotsi ya tshwaetso ya HIKabinete e lebisa matshediso ho Kompone ya Setjhaba e Mogadishu ho la Somalia ya Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) ho latela tlhaselo e mpe ya ka la 19 Phuptjane 2013 eo ho yona ho shweleng batho ba 15 ho kenyeletswa maAforika Borwa a mabedi.

src: We call on all political groups outside the political process in Somalia to renounce violence and raise their concerns with the Federal Somali Government in a constructive and reconciliatory manner.
tgt: Re etsa boipiletso ho dihlopha tsohle tsa dipolotiki tse ka thoko ho ditsamaiso tsa dipolotiki ho la Somalia ho nyahlatsa dikgoka le ho hlahisa ditletlebo tsa yona Mmusongwa Bofederale wa Somalia ka tsela e bopang le e nang le moya wa poelano.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to volunteer 67 minutes of their time on Nelson Mandela Day (18 July) to help change their communities and South Africa for the better.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa oohle ho ithaopa ka metsotso e 67 ya nako ya ona ka Letsatsi la Nelson Mandela (18 Phupu) bakeng sa ho thusa ho tlisa phethoho dibakeng tsa ona le Aforika Borwa bakeng sa ntlafatso ya bophelo.

src: This year’s event will take place under the theme of “Take action inspire change make every day a Mandela Day” with a focus on food security, shelter and literacy.
tgt: Ketsahalo ya selemong sena e tla tswela pele tlasa sehloho se reng “Etsa ho hong tlisa phethoho etsa letsatsi ka leng ebe Letsatsi la Mandela” maikutlo a tsepamisitswe ho hlahiso e sa haelleng ya dijo, bodulo le ho tseba ho bala.

src: Cabinet noted that as part of the Nelson Mandela Day, the phased roll-out of the Smart ID card will be launched.
tgt: Kabinete e lemohile hore, jwaloka karolo ya Letsatsi laNelson Mandela, ho tla thakgolwa mokgahlelo wa pele wa Karete ya Boitsebiso.

src: This launch is a significant break with our past and the end of the passbook era in South Africa.
tgt: Ho thakgolwa hona ke karohano ya bohlokwa mehleng ya rona e fetileng le ho qetello ya mehla ya ho jara dipasa Aforika Borwa.

src: The smart ID is a contactless card with a capability to accommodate information from various stakeholders now and in future.
tgt: Karete ya Boitsebiso ke karete e sa hlokeng ho hlahiswa mme e nang le bokgoni ba ho tshwara tlhahisoleseding e tswang ho bankakarolo ba fapafapaneng ba ha jwale le ba isao.

src: The Minister of Home Affairs will provide more details in planned briefing in due course.
tgt: Letona la Merero ya Lehae le tla fana ka dintlha tse batsi pitsong e tlang ho tshwarwa haufinyana.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch of the Department of Basic Education campaign called 94+ Projects for Madiba to celebrate Nelson Mandela’s birthday and legacy.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho thakgolwa ha letsholo la Lefapha la Thuto ya Motheo le bitswang Diprojeke tse 94+ bakeng sa Madiba ho keteka letsatsi la tswalo la Nelson Mandela le lefa la hae.

src: The campaign aims to improve infrastructure in over 94 schools to become state-of-the-art institutions of quality learning.
tgt: Sepheo sa letsholo lena ke ho ntlafatsa meralo ya motheo dikolong tse fetang 94 hore e be dibaka tsa mankgonthe tsa ho ithuta le tsa boleng.

src: The campaign gives hope and dignity to schools across the country.
tgt: Letsholo lena le fana ka tshepo le seriti dikolong ho phatlalla le naha.

src: During Mandela Month from July 2013, the department will be leading the handover of completed new schools per week as part of the commitment to improve quality basic education.
tgt: Nakong ya Kgwedi ya Mandela ho tloha ka Phupu 2013, lefapha le tla be le eteletse pele phano ya sekolo se setjha se phethetsweng beke ka nngwe e le karolo ya boitlamo ba ho ntlafatsa boleng ba thuto ya motheo.

src: Cabinet welcomes the completion and handover of the Nkosi Dalibhunga Mandela Legacy Bridge to the Mvezo community which is led by Nkosi Mandla Mandela, grandson of former President Nelson Mandela, on 18 July 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho phethelwa le phano ya Borokgo ba Lefa la Morena Dalibhunga Mandela ho badudi ba Mvezo ba eteletsweng pele ke Morena Mandla Mandela, e leng setloholo sa Mopresidente wa mehleng Nelson Mandela, ka la 18 Phupu 2013.

src: The handover will coincide with the birthday of Former President Mr Nelson Mandela, who will turn 95 years of age on this day.
tgt: Phano ena e tla tsamaelana le letsatsi la tswalo la Mopresidente wa mehleng Monghadi Nelson Mandela, eo a tla beng a qeta dilemo tse 95 ka letsatsi lena.

src: Cabinet noted South Africa’s commemoration of the United Nations International Day against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking on 26 June 2013, in Kimberley.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho hopola hwa Aforika Borwa hwa Letsatsi la Matjhaba a Kopaneng le kgahlanong le Tshebediso e mpe ya Dithethefatsi le ho Rekiswa ha batho ho seng Molaong ka la 26 Phuptjane 2013, ho la Kimberley.

src: The Day was used to emphasise the importance of dealing with challenges facing the world, including crime, HIV and AIDS, moral degeneration, domestic violence and teenage pregnancy.
tgt: Letsatsi lena le ile la sebediswa ho toboketsa bohlokwa ba ho sebetsana le diphephetso tse tobileng lefatshe, tse kenyeletsang botlokotsebe, HIV le AIDS, boitshwaro bo hlephileng, dikgoka tsa malapeng le ho ima ha barwetsana.

src: Cabinet welcomes the hosting of the Science, Technology and Innovation Summit which takes place from 20 to 21 July.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho tshwarwa ha Seboka sa Saense, Theknoloji le Ntjhafatsose tla tshwarwaho tloha ka la 20 ho ya ho la 21 Phupu.

src: The summit will address a recommendation of the Ministerial Review Committee report, improved coordination and integration within the National System of Innovation and strengthened dialogue between government, industry and academia.
tgt: Seboka se tla shebana le kgothaletso ya tlaleho ya Komiti ya Tekolo ya Matona, kgokahano e ntlafetseng le kopanelo ka hara Mokgwa wa Naha wa Ntjhafatso le dipuisano tse matlafaditsweng mahareng a mmuso, indasteri le borathuto.

src: Cabinet welcomes the report on progress made in Muyexe village in Giyani, Limpopo province in the implementation of commitments made by government to improve the lives of the people.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse tlaleho mabapi le tswelopele e entsweng motsaneng wa Muyexe ho la Giyani, Profenseng ya Limpopo, ho kenngweng tshebetsong ha boitlamo ba mmuso ba ho ntlafatsa bophelo ba batho.

src: Cabinet further echoed the President’s concern that all levels of government should speed up delivery as per the agreed plans.
tgt: Ho feta moo, Kabinete e phetile ngongoreho ya Mopresidente ya hore makala oohle a mmuso a lokela ho potlakisa phano ya ditshebeletso ho ya ka meralo eo ho dumellanweng ka yona.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch on Saturday, 29 June 2013 of SIP-18 which relates to the issues of infrastructure for the purpose of delivering on water and sanitation.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho thakgolwa ha Projeke ya Mawala a Meralo ya Motheo ya bo 18 ka Moqebelo, 29 Phupu 2013 e tsamaelanang le mabaka a meralo ya motheo bakeng sa ho fana ka metsi le bohlweki ba ona.

src: The project will ensure the provision of sustainable supply of water to meet social needs and support economic growth.
tgt: Projeke e tla netefatsa phano ya ka nako e telele ya metsi bakeng sa ho kgotsofatsa ditlhoko tsa kahisano le ho tshehetsa kgolo ya moruo.

src: Cabinet welcomed a briefing it received on cartel activities in the construction sector.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse lesedi leo e le fumaneng mabapi le diketso tsa mmomori wa lekala la tsa kaho.

src: Cabinet welcomes the outcome of the investigation that yielded evidence of pervasive price fixing, collusion and corruption in the private construction industry.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela sephetho sa diphuputso tse hlahisitseng bopaki ba ditheko tse fosahetseng, mmomori le bobodu indasteringya kaho ya poraefete.

src: The scale of the collusion warrants firm action by the competition authorities.
tgt: Sekgahla sa mmomori se batla letsoho le matla la ba ka sehloohong ho tsa phehisano.

src: Cabinet awaits the outcome of the Competition Tribunal process but notes that the evidence shows substantial damage to the public interest with inflated prices that the state paid as a result of the collusion."
tgt: Kabinete e emetse tsamaiso ya sephethosa Lekgotla la Diphehisano empa e lemohile hore bopaki bo supa hore ho bile le tshenyo e kgolo kgahlehong ya setjhaba ka lebaka la ditheko tse phahamisitsweng tseo mmuso o di lefileng ka lebaka la mmomori ona.

src: Key Cabinet discussions and decisions Cabinet approved the National Drug Master Plan (2013-2017) and its implementation over the next five years.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana Moralo wa Mankgonthe wa Naha wa Dithethefatsi (2013-2017) le hore o kenngwe tshebetsong bakeng sa dilemo tse hlano tse tlang.

src: The Plan serves as the country’s blueprint for preventing and reducing alcohol and substance abuse and its associated social and economic consequences on South African society.
tgt: Moralo o sebetsa jwaloka lewa la mmuso bakeng sa ho thibela le ho fokotsa tshebediso e mpe ya tahi le dithethefatsi le ditlamorao tse tsamaelanang le tsona tsa bophelo ba kahisano le moruo setjhabeng sa Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet approved the Hosting of the National Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment Summit in October 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana Ho tshwarwa ha Seboka sa Naha sa Matlafatso Moruong e Pharaletseng ya Batho ba Batsho ka Mphalane 2013.

src: The National Summit will showcase success stories and articulate government’s interventions in support of effective and sustainable economic participation and access for black people in the mainstream of the economy, in a way that will contribute to inclusive growth.
tgt: Seboka sa Naha se tla bontsha dipale tsa katleho le ho namalatsa boikenyako ba mmuso tshehetsong ya bonkakarolo bo hlwahlwa le phumantsho ya batho ba batsho ho tsa moruo ka hara moruo o phatlaletseng, ka tsela e tlang ho nyehela moruong o kopanetsweng.

src: Cabinet approved for South Africa to co-host the “Leading Change in the City” Conference with the United Nations Human Settlements programme (UN-HABITAT) on 5 and 6 September 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana hore Aforika Borwa e tshwarisane le Lenaneo la Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng la Bodulo ba Batho (UN-HABITAT) ka ho tshwara Khonferense ya “Ho etella pele Phethoho ya Motsemoholo”ka la 5 le 6 Loetse 2013.

src: The emphasis of the conference is on women’s participation in urban life in Africa.
tgt: Tabakgolo ya khonferense e hodima bonkakarolo ba basadi bophelong ba motsesetoropo ho la Aforika.

src: The conference will provide a platform for Africa to adequately address the challenges of urbanisation and harness urbanisation for human development.
tgt: Khonferense e tla fana ka lepatlelo bakeng sa Aforika hore e tobane ka botlalo le diphephetso tsa ho dula ditoropong le ho qhaneha ho dula ditoropong bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya batho.

src: Cabinet approved the Draft White Paper on Families and the Implementation Plan.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana Pampiri e Tshweu ya Moralo mabapi le Malapa le Moralo wa ho kenngwa Tshebetsong.

src: Draft White Paper on Families will enable Government and other stakeholders to use family as the springboard for the realisation of societal well-being.
tgt: Pampiri e Tshweu ya Moralo Mabapi le Malapa e tla kgontsha Mmuso le bankakarolo ba bang ho sebedisa lelapa e le motheo wa ho fihlella bophelo ba mankgonthe ba setjhaba.

src: The White Paper proposes three key strategic priorities, Promotion of healthy family life, Family strengthening and Family preservation.
tgt: Pampiri e Tshweu e sisinya mawala a mararo a ka sehloohong, Kgothaletso ya bophelo bo botle ba lelapa, matlafatso ya Lelapa le paballo ya Lelapa.

src: Cabinet approved the finalisation and gazetting of the second National Water Resource Strategy.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana phethelo le ho kenngwa lesedinyaneng la molao ha Lewa la bobedi la Mohlodi wa Naha wa Metsi.

src: This strategy builds on the 2004 National Water Resource Strategy.
tgt: Lewa lena le ahelletswe hodima Lewa la Mohlodi wa Naha wa Metsi la 2004.

src: The National Water Resource Strategy 2 provides an analysis on the role of water in the economy and identifies the specific challenges, development opportunities and actions which inform an agreed framework for the priority areas of the country.
tgt: Lewa la bobedi la Mohlodi wa Naha wa Metsi le fanaka mohlophollo ho karolo eo metsi a e bapalang moruong le ho hlwaya diphephetso tse teng, menyetla ya ntshetsopele le diketsahalo tse supisang moralo o dumellanweng ka ona bakeng sa dibaka tsa bohlokwa tsa naha.

src: The Strategy 2 also seeks to ensure sustainable, equitable and secure water for a better life and environment for all and that water is efficiently and effectively managed for equitable and sustainable growth and development.
tgt: Lewa la bobedi hape le batla ho netefatsa boteng ba metsi ba nako e telele, a lekanang bohle le a bolokehileng bakeng sa bophelo bo betere le tikoloho e betere bakeng sa bohle le hore metsi a laolwa hantle le ka makgethe bakeng sa kgolo e lekanang ya nako e telele le ntshetsopele.

src: Cabinet approved the report on the Outcomes of the 16th meeting of the Conference of Parties to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES CoP 16), held in Bangkok, Thailand from 3 – 14 March 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana tlaleho ka Diphetho tsa kopano ya bo 16 ya Khonferense ya Mekga bakeng sa Seboka sa Kgwebo ya Matjhaba bakeng sa Dibopuwa tse Kotsing tsa Diphoofolo le Dimela tse Hlaha (CITES CoP 16), e neng e tshwaretswe Bangkok, ho la Thailand ho tloha ka la 3 – 14 Hlakubele 2013.

src: Cabinet further approved that South Africa prepares and submits a trade proposal for consideration at CITES CoP 17 in 2016 in South Africa.
tgt: Ho feta moo Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana hore Aforika Borwa e lokise le ho kenya tshisinyo e lokelang ho tsepamisetswa maikutlo kopanong ya CITES CoP 17 ka 2016 ho la Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet accepted the invitation from the African Development Bank for South Africa to become a member of the Infrastructure Consortium for Africa (ICA) which was launched at the G8 Gleneagles Summit in 2005.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse memo e tswang ho Banka ya Ntshetsopele ya Aforika bakeng sa Aforika Borwa ya ho ba setho sa Lemulwana la Dikaho tsa Motheo bakeng sa Aforika (ICA) le ileng la thakgolwa Sebokeng sa G8 ho la Gleneagles ka 2005.

src: South Africa’s large investment in infrastructure over the medium term will be enhanced through its membership to the ICA especially in the generation of data and knowledge products and the coordination of development policies between the G20 and African countries.
tgt: Letsete le leholo la Aforika Borwa ho dikaho tsa motheo bakeng sa nako e mahareng le tla ntlafatswa ke ho ba setho sa ICA haholoholo tlhahisong ya tshedimosetsole dihlahiswa tsa tsebo le kgokahano ya maano a ntshetsopele pakeng tsa dinaha tsa G20 le tsa Aforika.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Protocol on Trade in Services to Parliament for ratification, in accordance with section 231 of the Constitution.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana ho hlahiswa ha Protokhole ya Setjhaba sa Ntshetsopele ya Dinaha tsa Borwa ba Aforika (SADC) bakeng sa Kgwebisano Ditshebeletsong Palamenteng bakeng sa tshekatsheko, ho ya ka karolo ya 231 ya Molaotheo.

src: The objectives of the Protocol are to liberalise intra-regional trade in services on the basis of equity, balance and mutual benefit.
tgt: Merero ya Protokhole ke ho lokolla kgwebo ya ditshebeletso ka hara mabatowa ho itshetlehilwe hodima tekatekano, botsitso le ho kgola molemo mmoho.

src: This Protocol also sets out a framework for the liberalisation of trade in services between SADC member states and serves as a basis for negotiations.
tgt: Protokhole ena hape e qaqisa moralo bakeng sa tokoloho ya kgwebisano ditshebeletsong pakeng tsa dinaha tseo e leng ditho tsa SADC le ho sebetsa e le motheo wa ditherisano.

src: Cabinet noted the launch of the Bachelor of Human Settlements Development Degree (BHSD) in partnership between the Department of Higher Education and Training and the Nelson Mandela Metro University.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetseho thakgolwa ha lengolo la thuto la Batjhela ya Ntshetsopele ya Dibaka tsa Bodulo tsa Batho (BHSD) kakopanelo le Lefapha la Thuto le Thupello e Phahameng le Yunivesithi ya Nelson Mandela Metro.

src: The Bachelor Degree (BHSD) is aimed at developing effective Human Settlements managers and practitioners who will possess the relevant knowledge and skills necessary to create, upgrade and speed up sustainable human settlements development in South Africa.
tgt: Lengolo lena la thuto la BHSD morero wa lona ke ho ntshetsapele balaodi le bahlanka ba hlwahlwa ba Dibaka tsa Bodulo ba tla ba le tsebo le bokgoni bo hlokahalang bakeng sa ho bopa, ho ntlafatsa le ho potlakisa ntshetsopele ya bodulo ba batho bakeng sa nako e telele Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet calls on all government departments, municipalities and parastatals operating in Gauteng to register all state vehicles for e-tags.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho mafapha oohle a mmuso, bomasepala le makala a mmuso a sebetsang Gauteng ho ngodisa dipalangwang tsohle tsa mmuso bakeng sa dipapetlwana tsa di e-tag.

src: Cabinet approved the implementation steps proposed for the establishment of a Border Management Agency (BMA).
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana mehato ya ho kenngwa tshebetsong e sisintsweng bakeng sa ho thehwa ha Lekala la Bolaodi ba Meedi (BMA).

src: The BMA would manage migration, customs and land border line control services and efficiently coordinate the service of all departments in ports of entry.
tgt: BMA e tla laola phallo, madiboho le ho laola metjha e naheng ya ditshebeletso tsa meedi le ho hokahanya tshebeletso ya mafapha oohle madibohong a ho kena.

src: The Department of Home Affairs will be the lead Department in establishing the BMCabinet approved the following Bills for submission to Parliament.
tgt: Lefapha la Merero ya Lehae e tla ba Lefapha le eteletseng pele ho thehwa ha BMKabinete e tjhaeletse monwana dibili tse latelang bakeng sa ho hlahiswa Palamenteng:.

src: Customs Control Bill (CCB), the Customs Duty Bill, 2013 (CDB) and the Customs and Excise Amendment Act, 2013 (CEAA) - The Bills provides a foundation for the facilitation of international trade and protection of the economy and society, thereby creating a balance between customs control and trade facilitation Water Research Amendment Bill - The Amendment aims to bring it in line with major changes in institutions, policy, water science and legal environment and also to increase the Water Research Commission’s contribution to the water research needs of South Africa and to ensure that the country is strategically placed to respond to the needs and challenges of an arid country like South Africa.
tgt: Bili ya Taolo ya Madiboho, Bili ya Lekgetho la Madiboho, ya 2013 le Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Madiboho le Ditefello, wa 2013 – Dibili tsena di fana ka motheo bakeng sa tsamaiso ya kgwebo ya matjhaba le tshireletso ya moruo le setjhaba, kahoo di bopa botsitso pakeng tsa taolo ya madiboho le tsamaiso ya kgwebo.

src: National Environmental Management Laws Amendment Bill, 2013 - The bill proposes amendments to certain provisions under the National Environmental Management Act, 1998 (Act No.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Diphuputso tsa Metsi – Sepheo sa Sehlomathiso sena ke ho se matahanya le diphethoho tse kgolo ho diinstitjute, leano, saense ya metsi le tikoloho ya tsa molao hape le ho eketsa nyehelo ya Khomishene ya Diphuputso tsa Metsi bakeng sa ditlhoko tsa diphuputso tsa metsi tsa Aforika Borwa le ho netefatsa hore naha e eme hantle bakeng sa ho arabela ditlhoko le diphephetso tsa naha e nang le bothata ba metsi jwaloka Aforika Borwa.

src: 107 of 1998) and further ensure that the country’s natural resources are protected for current and future generation as contemplated by the National Development Plan (NDP).
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Melao ya Naha ya Taolo ya Tikoloho, sa 2013 –Bili ena e sisinya dihlomathiso dipehelong tse itseng tlasa Molao wa Taolo ya Tikoloho, wa 1998 (Molao wa 107 wa 1998) le ho feta moo ho netefatsa hore mehlodi ya naha ya tlhaho e tshireleditswe bakeng sa moloko wa jwale le o tlang jwaloka ha ho labalabelwa ke Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha.

src: Draft National Environmental Management: Air Quality Amendment Bill, 2013 - This Bill amends certain provisions under the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act, 2004 which regulates air quality in the country to protect the environment by providing reasonable measures for the prevention of pollution and ecological degradation while promoting justifiable economic and social development.
tgt: Moralo wa Naha wa Taolo ya Tikoloho: Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Boleng ba Moya, sa 2013 – Bili ena e fetola dipehelo tse itseng tlasa Taolo ya Tikoloho ya Naha: Molao wa Boleng ba Moya, wa 2004 o laolang boleng ba moya ka hara naha bakeng sa ho tshireletsa tikoloho ka ho fana ka mekgwa e kgonehang bakeng sa thibelo ya tshilafatso le ho thefula maemo a tlhaho ho ntse ho kgothaletswa ntshetsopele e lokileng ya moruo le kahisano.

src: National Environmental Management: Waste Amendment Bill, 2013 - The Bill amends the National Environmental Management: Waste Act, 2008 (Act No.
tgt: Taolo ya Naha ya Tikoloho: Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Matlakala, sa 2013 – Bili ena e fetola Taolo ya Naha ya Tikoloho: Molao wa Matlakala, wa 2008 (Molao wa 59 wa 2008) o laolang taolo ya matlakala bakeng sa ho tshireletsa bophelo bo botle le tikoloho.

src: 59 of 2008) which regulates waste management in order to protect health and the environment.
tgt: Taolo ya Naha ya Tikoloho: Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Dibaka tse Tshireleditsweng, sa 2013 – Bili ena e fetola Taolo ya Naha ya Tikoloho: Molao wa Dibaka tseTshireleditsweng, wa 2003 (Molao wa 57 wa 2003).

src: National Environmental Management: Protected Areas Amendment Bill, 2013 - The Bill amends the National Environmental Management: Protected Areas Act, 2003 (Act No.57 of 2003).
tgt: Diphethoho di kenyeletsa taolo ya Dibaka tsa Lewatle tse Tshireleditsweng mokgweng wa taolo ya dibaka tse ding tse Tshireleditsweng le ho fana ka sefutho ho Diphatlalatso tsa Mopresidente tse arolang mesebetsi pakeng tsa mabaka a botshwasi ba ditlhapi le taolo ya tikoloho.

src: Amendments incorporate the management of Marine Protected Areas in the system of management of other Protected Areas as well as giving effect to the Presidential Proclamations separating the functions between fisheries and environmental management.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Banka ya Poso ya Aforika Borwa – Sepheo se seholo sa Molao wa Banka ya Poso ya Aforika Borwa, wa 2010 (Molao wa 9 wa 2010) ke ho theha setsha sa ditjhelete bakeng sa ho kgothaletsa batho ka bongata ho boloka le ho tsetela le ho bopa banka ya kgetho ya mantlha bakeng sa sehlopha se fumanang meputso e tlase.

src: 9 of 2010) is to establish a financial institution for mass mobilisation of savings and investment and to create a bank of first choice for the lower income group.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaeletse monwana Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Inshorense ya Tlhoko ya Mosebetsi sa 2012 bakeng sa ho nonya maikutlo a setjhaba le bakeng sa tjhebisano le Bomphato ba Kahisano ba Lekgotla la Naha la tsa Moru le Mesebetsi.

src: Cabinet approved the unemployment Insurance Amendment Bill 2012 for public comments and for consultation with NEDLAC Social Partners.
tgt: Bili ena e fetola Molao wa Inshorense ya Tlhoko ya Mosebetsi, wa 63 wa 2001.

src: This amendment addresses the issue of workers who are presently excluded in the Act and improve payment of benefits to contributors, extend the period of payment of benefits to the contributor from eight to twelve months and provides for the nomination of beneficiaries in case of death benefits.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sena se tobana le ntlha ya basebetsi bao mothating wa jwale ba teetsweng ka thoko Molaong ona le ho ntlafatsa ditefello tsa menyetla ho ba nyehelang, ho eketsa nako ya tefo ya menyetla ho ba nyehelang ho tloha dikgweding tse robedi ho ya ho tse leshome le metso e mmedi le ho fana ka kgetho ya bakgolamolemo haeba ho lokelwa ho fanwa ditlhapiso ha lefu le ka hlaha.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Electoral Amendment Bill, 2013 to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho hlahiswa ha Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Dikgetho sa 2013 Palamenteng.

src: The Amendment Bill seeks to provide for special votes in elections for the National Assembly, as well as to provide for the registration of voters who are ordinarily resident outside the Republic to enable them to cast a special vote.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Bili se batla ho fana ka dikgetho tse ikgethang dikgethong tsa Seboka sa Naha, le ho fana ka boingodiso ba bakgethi bao ka tlwaelo e leng batho ba dulang ka ntle ho Riphaboliki ho ba kgontsha ho kenya kgethoe ikgethang.

src: Appointments Cabinet concurs with the appointment Mr. Romeo Adams to the position of Deputy Director-General: Corporate Services in the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development.
tgt: Kabinete e dumellana le ho thonngwa ha MonghadiRomeo Adams maemong a Motlatsa Motsamaisi-Kakaretso: Ditshebeletsong tsa Kgwebo ho Lefapha la Toka le Ntshetsopele ya Molaotheo.

src: Cabinet concurs with the appointment Ms Irene Rofhiwa Singo to the position of Chief Financial Officer in the Department of Mineral Resources.
tgt: Kabinete e dumellana le ho thonngwa ha Mofumahadi Irene RofhiwaSingo maemong a Mohlanka ya ka Sehloohong wa Ditjhelete ho Lefapha la Mehlodi ya Diminerale.

src: Cabinet concurs with the appointment Ms Kalayvani Pillay to the position of Deputy Director-General: Legislative Development in the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development.
tgt: Kabinete e dumellana le ho thonngwa haMofumahadi Kalayvani Pillay maemong a Motlatsa Motsamaisi-Kakaretso: Ntshetsopeleng ya Theramelao ho Lefapha la Toka le Ntshetsopele ya Molaotheo.

src: Cabinet concurs with the appointment Dr Bismark Tyobeka to the position of Chief Executive Officer of the National Nuclear Regulator of South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e dumellana le ho thonngwa ha Ngaka Bismark Tyobeka maemong a Mohlanka ya ka Sehloohong wa Phethahatso wa Taolo ya Naha ya Matla a Nyutlelere ya Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet concurs with the re-appointment of Mr Tsietsi Mokhele as Chief Executive Officer of the South African Maritime Safety Authority (SAMSA) for a period of five years with effect from 1 April 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e dumellana le ho thonngwa botjha hape ha Monghadi Tsietsi Mokhele jwaloka Mohlanka ya ka Sehloohong wa Phethahatso wa Bolaodi ba Polokeho Mawatleng bakeng sa nako ya dilemo tse hlano ho tloha ka la 1 Mmesa 2013.

src: Cabinet concurs the re-appointment of the following Non-Executive members to the board of the South African National Accreditation System (SANAS), whose current term of office will expire on 30 November 2013, to serve a second term from 1 December 2013 to 30 November 2018.Vernon Roderick SeymourPhakamisa Zonke.
tgt: Kabinete e dumellana le ho thonngwa botjha hapeha ditho tseo e seng tsa phethahatso tse latelang ho boto ya Mekgwa ya Ditumello ya Naha ya Aforika Borwa, bao nako ya bona ya tshebetso e tla fela ka la 30 Pudungwana 2013, ho sebetsa lekgetlo la bobedi ho tloha ka la 1 Tshitwe 2013 ho ya ka la 30 Pudungwana 2018.• Monghadi Vernon Roderick Seymour• Monghadi PhakamisaZonke.

src: Cabinet noted the re-appointment of thirteen members to the South African Council for Space Affairs (SACSA) with effect from 24 June 2013 to 24 June 2015.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho thonngwa botjha hape ha ditho tse leshome le metso e meraro ho Lekgotla la Aforika Borwa la Merero ya Sepakapaka ho tloha ka la 24 Phuptjane 2013 ho ya ho la 24 Phuptjane 2015.

src: Cabinet also noted the appointment of representatives from the Department of Defence, Council of Scientific and Industrial Research and the Department of International Relations and Cooperation with effect from 24 June 2013 to 24 June 2015.Dr Peter MartinezMs Nomfuneko MajajaMr Kim Victor GorringeDr Sandile Bethuel MalingaMs Pontsho MarupingMs Andiswa MlisaDr Valanathan MunsamiMr Tenza ThembaMr Ron OlivierMr Linden PetzerMr Hendrik RheederAdv Phetole Patrick SekhuleDr Jo-Ansie Karina van WykNomination from the Department of DefenceNomination from the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)Nomination from the Department of International Relations and Cooperation.
tgt: Kabinete hape e ananetse ho thonngwa ha baemedi ho tswa ho Lefapha la Tshireletso, Lekgotla la Diphuputso tsa Saense le Indasteri (CSIR) le Lefapha la Dikamano le Tshebedisano ya Matjhaba ho tloha ka la 24 Phuptjane 2013 ho ya ho la 24 Phuptjane 2015.a.

src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment.
tgt: Maemo a Kabinete mabapi le dintlha tsa bohlokwa maemong a ha jwale.

src: Cabinet congratulated the people of Zimbabwe and political parties on holding successful harmonised parliamentary and local elections.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholeditse batho ba Zimbabwe le mekga ya dipolotiki ka ho tshwara dikgetho tse hlophisitsweng hantle tsa palamente le tsa dibaka.

src: Cabinet commended the efforts of President Jacob Zuma as the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Facilitator on the Zimbabwe Dialogue in ensuring that all political parties were committed to peaceful elections.
tgt: Kabinete e rorisitse matsapa a Mopresidente Jacob Zuma e le Monamodi ya emetseng Selekane sa Ntshetsopele ya Dinaha tsa Borwa ba Aforika Ditherisanong tsa Zimbabwe, ho netefatseng hore mekga yohle ya dipolotiki e ikitlaelleditse dikgetho tse nang le kgotso.

src: Cabinet condemned the bomb attack on a building housing the Turkish Embassy staff in Mogadishu, Somalia, and expressed condolences to the Governments and people of Somalia and Turkey.
tgt: Kabinete e seollotse tlhaselo ya qhomane moahong o sebediswang ke basebetsi ba Boqosa ba Turkey mane Mogadishu, Somalia, ya ba ya fetisa melaetsa ya matshediso Mebusong ya Somalia le Turkey.

src: On the eve of our 20 Years of Freedom, Cabinet joins the nation in celebrating Women’s Month under the theme “A Centenary of Working Together towards Sustainable Women Empowerment and Gender Equality”.
tgt: Selemong se etellang pele phethelo ya Dilemo tse 20 tsa Tokoloho, kabinete e ikamahanya le setjhaba ho ketekeng Kgwedi ya Basadi tlasa mookotaba o reng “Dilemokgolo tsa ho Sebetsa Mmoho Matlafatsong ya Basadi ya Nako e Telele le Tekano ya Bong.”Dilemokgolo di tlotla dintwa tsa tokoloho tse lwannweng ke basadi haesale ho tloha ha moitseki ya qollehang, Charlotte Maxeke, a ile a etella pele sehlopha sa basadi mohwantong wa Bloemfontein o neng o hanana le melao ya dipasa ka 1913.Seabo se entsweng ke basadi twantshong ya melao ya dipasa esita le dikarolong tse ding tsa ntwa ya tokoloho ke ntho ya bohlokwa ya kgothatso Kareteng ya Boitsebiso e sa tswa thakgolwa.

src: The centenary honours the struggles waged by women since the distinguished activist, Charlotte Maxeke, led a group of women on a march in Bloemfontein against pass laws in 1913.
tgt: Jwaloka ha setjhaba se keteka basadi, Kabinete e boela e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ohle ho satalla kgahlanong le tlhekefetso efe kapa efe ya basadi le bana esita le ho hlompha ditokelo tsa basadi jwaloka ha di fuperwe ke Molaotheo.

src: The contribution made by women in fighting pass laws and in other facets of the liberation struggle is an important part of the inspiration behind the recently launched Smart ID WEBTOKEN the nation celebrates women, Cabinet also calls on all South Africans to take a stand against any abuse of women and children and to respect the rights of women as enshrined in our Constitution.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya pheta teboho ya pejana ya Mopresidente Jacob Zuma setjhabeng esita le matjhabeng ka ho etsa Letsatsi la Matjhaba la Nelson Mandela hore e be letsatsi le leholohadi ho fihlela jwale la keteko ya matswalo a Madiba.

src: On July 18, thousands of people around South Africa and the world took time to roll up their sleeves and help less fortunate people.
tgt: Mohla la 18 Phupu, diketekete tsa batho Aforika Borwa ka bophara le lefatsheng di ile tsa ipha nako ya ho ya thusa batho ba sotlehang.

src: Cabinet called on South Africans to support the inaugural Nelson Mandela Sport and Culture Day at FNB Stadium, Johannesburg, on 17 August.
tgt: Kabinete e ipileditse ho maAforika Borwa ho tshehetsa tlhomamiso ya Letsatsi la Dipapadi le Botjhaba la Nelson Mandela Lebaleng la FNB, Johannesburg, mohla la 17 Phato.

src: The Springboks will play Argentina, Bafana Bafana will take on Burkina Faso and a South African Masters football side will play Italy, followed by a star-studded music concert in the evening.
tgt: Di-Springbok di tla bapala le Argentina, Bafana Bafana yona e tla thulana le Burkina Faso athe sehlopha sa bolo ya maoto sa Mekaubere sa Aforika Borwa se tla bapala le sa Italy, ho tla latela khonsarete ya mmino e tletseng dikgalala tsa dibini ka phirimana.

src: All proceeds will go to the Nelson Mandela children’s hospital project.
tgt: Tjhelete yohle e bokelletsweng moo e tla iswa projekeng ya kaho ya sepetlele sa Bana sa Nelson Mandela.

src: Cabinet reiterated the call to South Africans to “Take Action Inspire Change (and) Make Every Day a Mandela Day”.Cabinet continues to call on all South Africans to continue keeping former President Nelson Mandela in their thoughts and prayers as he responds to medical treatment.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya boela ya pheta kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa ho “Nka Kgato ho Kgothalletsa Phetoho (le) ho Etsa hore Letsatsi le leng le le leng e be Letsatsi la Mandela”.Kabinete e tswelapele ho ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ohle hore a tswelepele ho bea Mopresidente wa mehleng Nelson Mandela menahanong le merapelong ya wona jwaloka ha a ntse a hlaphohelwa tshebedisong ya meriana ya kalafo.

src: Cabinet is saddened by the passing of former Chief Justice Pius Langa who was laid to rest on 3 August 2013 during a Special Official Funeral.
tgt: Kabinete e mahlonokong ka ho hlokahala ha Moahlodi e Moholo wa mehleng Pius Langa, ya bolokilweng ka la 3 Phato nakong ya Lepato le Kgethehileng la Semmuso.

src: Cabinet offers condolences to his family, friends and colleagues.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisetsa matshediso ho lelapa la hae, metswalle le basebetsimmoho.

src: Former Chief Justice Pius Langa will be remembered for his contribution to the liberation Struggle, his defence of our constitutional democracy and, more recently, his work in the Press Freedom Commission.6 Cabinet recognises the positive developments in the education sector, in particular the strengthening of the Curriculum Assessment Policy Statements (CAPS) and the continued support from teachers in its implementation.
tgt: Moahlodi e Moholo wa mehleng Pius Langa o tla hopolwa ka seabo sa hae Ntweng ya tokoloho, tshireletso ya hae ya demokrasi ya rona e tataiswang ke molaotheo, athe morao tjena, le ka mosebetsi wa hae Khomisheneng ya Bolokolohi ba Ditaba.

src: Cabinet welcomed the establishment of the Task Team assigned to manage the implementation of the South African Sign Language (SASL) curriculum in 2014 from Grades R to 12, in line with the President’s call to have the sign language declared as official.
tgt: Kabinete e hlokomela boteng ba dikgatelopele tse ntle lekaleng la thuto, haholoholo matlafatsong ya Setatemente sa Leano la Kharikhulamo le Tekanyetso esita le tshehetso e ntseng e tswelapele ya matitjhere ho kenngweng tshebetsong ha sona.

src: The new curriculum will provide greater access to education opportunities for all.7 Cabinet calls on the 2013 matriculants to register now at tertiary institutions for 2014 in line with the Department of Higher Education and Training’s Apply Now!
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse ho thewa ha Setlamo sa Tshebetso se filweng mosebetsi wa ho tsamaisa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha kharikhulamo ya Puo ya Matsoho ya Aforika Borwa ka 2013 ho tloha Kereiting ya R ho isa ho ya 12, ho ya ka kgoeletso ya Mopresidente ya hore puo ya matsoho e ananelwe e le ya semmuso.

src: Learners are encouraged to carefully consider their career choices and assess their financial requirements.
tgt: Baithuti ba kgothalletswa ho ba sedi ha ba kgetha seo ba batlang ho ithutela sona, ba be ba sekaseke ditlhoko tsa bona tsa ditjhelete.

src: Learners are reminded about government’s National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS) which provides financial aid to academically deserving and financially needy students.8 Cabinet congratulates the launch of the 24-hour television news channel by the South African Broadcasting Corporation which responds to the ever-increasing demand for up-to-date news broadcasts on events of national and international importance and gives a voice and platform to all South Africans.9 Cabinet congratulates swimmers Cameron van der Burgh, Chad le Clos and Giulio Zorzi who made the country proud by winning medals at the 15th International Swimming Federation (FINA) World Championships in Barcelona.10 Cabinet extended its well wishes to the Muslims of South Africa as they celebrate Eid.
tgt: Baithuti ba hopotswa ka Sekema sa Setjhaba sa Thuso ya Baithuti ka Ditjhelete, se fanang ka thuso ya ditjhelete ho ba tshwanelehileng ho ya ka mesebetsi ya bona e metle dithutong esita le baithuti ba hlokang ditjhelete.

src: Cabinet also wishes the South African Jewish Community a happy month of Elul.2 Key Cabinet discussions and decisions.1 Cabinet approved the commencement of the consultation process for the National Water Policy Positions by the Department of Water Affairs.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa thakgolo ya kanale ya ditaba tsa thelevishene tsa ka nako tsohle ya Lekgotla la Kgaso la Aforika Borwa e rarollang tlhokeho e dulang e eketseha ya kgaso ya ditaba tsa moraorao diketsahalong tsa bohlokwa tsa naha le tsa matjhaba ebile e fa maAforika Borwa ohle lepatlelo la ho hlahisa maikutlo.

src: The Policy aims to holistically align and address the various issues relating to intellectual property, which cut across various disciplines, including: trade, science, agriculture and health.
tgt: Sepheo sa tjhebolobotjha ya leano lena ke ho fumana le ho lokisa ditlamorao dife kapa dife tse sa rerwang esita le dikgeo maanong a jwale a metsi.

src: This lays the foundation for incorporating citizen-based monitoring into government’s monitoring WEBTOKEN this framework, citizen-based monitoring describes an approach to monitoring government performance that focuses on the experiences of ordinary citizens in order to strengthen public accountability and drive service delivery improvements.4 Cabinet approved the Principles of Public Administration and Financial Management Delegations.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse phatlalatso ya Leano la Naha la Boithuelo ba Thepa, bakeng sa tshwaelo ya setjhaba ka nako ya matsatsi a 30.Leano le habile ho amanya le ho rarolla kahohlehohle dintlha tse fapafapaneng tse amanang le boithuelo ba thepa, bo phopholetsang hohle dinthong tse fapafapaneng, ho akga: kgwebisano, saense, temo le bophelo bo botle.

src: The Principles provide a guide to how the powers of an Executive Authority are delegated to an Accounting Officer and further to lower structures as prescribed in the Public Service Act (PSA) and the Public Financial Management Act (PFMA).The Principles make the process of delegating powers easier, which will promote more efficient and effective service delivery.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse moralo wa leano bakeng sa tiso eo motheo wa yona e leng baahi ka sehlooho se reng “Moralo wa ho Matlafatsa dilekane tsa Baahi le Mmuso bakeng sa Tiso Phanong ya Ditshebeletso tsa Mantlha”.Mafapha a mmuso a amehang phanong ya ditshebeletso setjhabeng, a lebelletswe ho fetofetola tiso ya wona le meralo ya tlhahlobo ho kenyelletsa mekgwa ya ho kopanya maikutlo le malebela a baahi phanong ya ditshebeletso.

src: The Convention provides a legal framework for regional cooperation amongst States concerned to undertake collaborative actions towards solving interlinked problems of the coastal and marine environment that they share.
tgt: Sena se rala motheo wa ho kopanya tiso eo motheo wa yona e leng baahi le mokgwa wa tiso wa mmuso.

src: They were further apprised on the outstanding matters that still require WEBTOKEN of 31 July 2013 the credit balance was R.3bn compared to an overdraft of R1, 7b when it went under administration in December 2011.Having appreciated the corrective measures put in place in the five departments that are under administration, Cabinet approved that the Ministerial Committee can commence the six month transitional process of handing over the administration of Limpopo to the Premier and his new Executive.
tgt: Kabinete e se e ananetse ditumellano tse latelang hore di amohelwa Palamenteng ho ya ka Karolo ya 231 ya Molaotheo wa Aforika Borwa: Ya pele, phihlello ya Aforika Borwa Tumellanong ya ho thewa ha Khomishene ya Tjhuna Lewatleng la India (IOTC), Ya bobedi ke Seboka se Seholo sa Poloko ya Tuna ya Bluefin ka Borwa (CCSBT) le Ya boraro, e leng Mokgatlo wa Dijo le Temo (FAO) wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng Tumellanong ya Mekgwatsamaiso ya Lediboho la Naha ho Thibela, ho se Kgothalletse le ho Fedisa Botshwasi ba Ditlhapi bo seng Molaong, bo sa Tlalehwang bo bile bo sa Laolwe (IUU).Letona la Temothuo, Meru le tsa Ditlhapi le lona le se le ikamahantse le kopano ena e le ho thatoloha ka boleng bo tla tliswa ke sena indastering ya botshwasi ba ditlhapi le seabo sa yona ho hodiseng moruo wa rona.

src: Cabinet agreed that further investigations should continue on matters that seek to establish irregularities and where people are found to have flouted procurement procedures the due disciplinary process will take effect.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse hore Aforika Borwa e tla tshwara Seboka sa 11 sa Mekgatlo (COP) se hlahlamang Seboka se seholo sa Abidjan Cape Town ho tloha mohla la 24-28 Hlakubele 2014.Seboka se seholo sa Abidjan ke se seng sa tse 18 tsa Diboka tse Kgolo tsa Mabatowa a Mawatleng moo merero ya Tshebetso e ileng ya thewa ke Lenaneo la Tikoloho la Matjhaba a Kopaneng e le karolo ya ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Lenanetsamaiso la Stockholm la 1972.Seboka se Seholo se fana ka moralo wa molao bakeng sa tshebedisano mmoho ya mabatowa Dinaheng tse amehang ho ikatlaelletsa tshebetso e kopanetsweng mabapi le ho rarolla mathata a nyalanang a tikoloho ya mabopo le mawatle ao di abelanang ka wona.

src: A fuller briefing by the Ministerial Committee will take place at an appropriate time.3 Bills.1 Cabinet approved the introduction of the Legal Metrology Bill to Parliament.
tgt: Setheo se hodimodimo sa Seboka se Seholo sa Abidjan se etsang diqeto, ke COP, e leng kopano ya ka morao a dilemo tse pedi e kgobokanyang Matona a Tikoloho le ditsebi tsa dintho tse sa utlwisiseheng habobebe tse tswang mekgatlong e Dumellanang, esita le dinaha tsa bolemohi, dieijensi tse ding tsa Matjhaba a Kopaneng le mekgatlo eo e seng ya mmuso.

src: The Bill is meant to guide all measurement made by industry when trading using scales, meters and other measuring equipment are accurate.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya kumelwa ka tlaleho ya seabo sa borumuwa ba Aforika Borwa Mmokeng wa 57 wa Khomishene ya Matjhaba a Kopaneng ho tsa Maemo a Basadi, o neng o tshwerwe ho tloha ka la 4 ho isa ho la 15 Hlakubele 2013.Mmoka wa 57 o ne o tshwaretswe Ntlokgolo ya Matjhaba a Kopaneng New York, mme mookotaba o ka sehloohong e ne e le “Phediso ya Dikgoka kgahlanong le Basadi le Banana.”Boitlamo bo tomanyana bo ile ba etswa ba ba ba ananelwa ke ba neng ba nka seabo phedisong ya dikgoka kgahlanong le basadi le banana.

src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment.
tgt: Maemo a Kabinete mabapi le dintlha tsa bohlokwa maemong a ha jwale.

src: Cabinet welcomed the public launch of the sixth edition of the Development Indicators by the Minister in the Presidency for Performance Monitoring and Evaluation.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse ho kgakolwa phatlalatsa ha kgatiso ya botshelela ya Matshwao a Ntshetsopele ke Letona la Bopresidenteng la Bodisa le Tlhahlobo ya Tshebetso.

src: As the nation prepares to celebrate 20 Years of Freedom, South Africans should be proud that life has changed for the better since 1994.The indicators show improvement in key areas and simultaneously point to the hard work still required to deal with some of our more persistent challenges.
tgt: Jwaloka ha setjhaba se hlophisetsa ho keteka Dilemo tse 20 tsa Tokoloho, maAforika Borwa a tshwanela ho ba motlotlo ka hore bophelo bo fetohile ba ba ba ntlafala haesale ho tloha ka 1994.Matshwao a bontsha ntlafalo dinthong tsa bohlokwa athe a boela a supa mosebetsi o boima o ntseng o tshwanela ho etswa ho sebetsana le tse ding tsa diphephetso tsa rona tse ntseng di iphetapheta.

src: Furthermore, the indicators encourage debate on the challenges our country faces and act as markers along our journey of socio-economic progress.
tgt: Ho feta moo, matshwao a kgothalletsa ngangisano ka diphephetso tseo naha ya rona e tobaneng le tsona mme a boela a sebetsa ho thusa leetong la rona la kgatelopele ya moruo le phedisano.

src: Cabinet commended the 41% (115) of municipalities that received unqualified financial statements on the 2011/2012 financial audits.
tgt: Kabinete e rorisitse 41% (115) ya bomasepala ba fumanweng ba se na diphoso ditsamaisong tsa ditjhelete ha ho ne ho etswa bahlahlobi ba dibuka tsa ditjhelete ba 2011/2012.

src: It further acknowledged the improvement made by the 21 municipalities that previously received the adverse or disclaimed opinions in the previous year.
tgt: E boetse ya ananela ntlafalo e entsweng ke bomasepala ba 21 bao nakong e fetileng ba ileng ba fumana ditsheollo tse amanang le selemo se fetileng.

src: Cabinet appreciates the work done by the Auditor General in assisting the municipalities to improve on the governance compliance requirements.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela mosebetsi o entsweng ke Kantoro ya Mohlakisi Kakaretso ka ho thusa bomasepala ho ntlafatsa ditlhoko tsa bona tsa boikamahanyo pusong.

src: It also acknowledged the commitment made by the municipality leadership to continue to work on further improving the areas highlighted by the Auditor General.3 Cabinet thanked all South Africans for their support of the Nelson Mandela Sport and Cultural Day hosted in aid of the Nelson Mandela Children's Hospital project.
tgt: E ile ya boela ya ananela boikitlaetso bo entsweng ke boetapele ba bomasepala hore ba tswele pele ho sebeletsa ntlafalo dinthong tse hlakisitsweng ke Kantoro ya Mohlakisi Kakaretso.3 Kabinete e lebohile maAforika Borwa ohle ka ho tshehetsa Letsatsi la Dipapadi le Botjhaba la Nelson Mandela le neng le tshwaretswe ho thusa projeke ya Sepetlele sa Bana sa Nelson Mandela.

src: South Africans are encouraged to continue working in communities and partnering with government to improve the lives of citizens and bring to life the ideals to which Madiba dedicated his life.4 Cabinet noted the upcoming visit of President Jacob Zuma to the Russian Republic.
tgt: MaAforika Borwa a kgothalletswa ho tswelapele ho sebetsa dibakeng tsa bona le ho sebedisana le mmuso ho ntlafatsa maphelo a baahi esita le ho kenya tshebetsong mehopolo eo Madiba a ileng a nyehela bophelo ba hae ka lebaka la yona.4 Kabinete e nketse hloohong leeto le tlang la Mopresidente Jacob Zuma la ho ya Rephaboliking ya Russia.

src: He will be attending the Group of 20 (G20) Summit in St Petersburg on 5 and 6 September 2013 as part of promoting South Africa’s political and economic interests.
tgt: O tla be a ya Sebokeng sa Setlamo sa 20 (G20) St Petersburg mohla la 5 le 6 Loetse 2013 e le karolo ya ho phahamisa ditabatabelo tsa Aforika Borwa tsa sepolotiki le tsa moruo.

src: South Africa continues to support the G20’s development agenda that advances global economic stability and long-term sustainable growth and job creation.5 Cabinet commended the first meeting of the Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa (BRICS) Business Council, which saw business leaders from these countries converge in South Africa.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tswelapele ho tshehetsa morero wa G20 wa ntshetsopele o ntshetsang pele botsitso ba moruo lefatsheng esita le kgolo le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi tse tla itjara ka nako e telele.5 Kabinete e rorisitse kopano ya pele ya Lekgotla la Kgwebo la Brazil, Russia, India, China le Aforika Borwa (BRICS), moo baetapele ba kgwebo ho tswa dinaheng tsena ba neng ba kgobokana Aforika Borwa.

src: The meeting was also attended by prominent business leaders from 19 other African countries.6 Cabinet welcomed the assurance given at the 12th annual African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) Forum to renew AGOA before it expires in 2015.
tgt: Kopanong ena ho ile ha boela ha eba teng baetapele ba bohlokwa ba kgwebo ba tswang dinaheng tse ding tse 19 tsa Aforika.6 Kabinete e amohetse tiisetso e fanweng Foramong ya bo12 ya Molao wa Kgolo le Monyetla wa Aforika (AGOA) ya ho ntjhafatsa AGOA pele e fellwa ke nako ka 2015.

src: AGOA has benefited both the United States and the African continent and has underpinned a growing and relatively balanced bilateral trade relationship between South Africa and the United States (US).SA believes AGOA offers an appropriate framework to build stronger, mutually beneficial bilateral trade and investment relations and strengthen cooperation between the US and the broader African continent.7 As part of the nationwide celebration of Women’s Month, Deputy President Kgalema Motlanthe will on Friday, 23 August 2013 visit Gombani Village in Mutale Municipality, Limpopo, to hand over houses to the community.
tgt: AGOA e foletse molemo ho tswa nahakgolo ya Amerika le ya Aforika ya ba ya tshehetsa kgwebisano ya naha tse pedi dipakeng tsa Aforika Borwa le Amerika e ntseng e hola ebile e tsitsa.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch of the Public Service Charter and commends public service unions and the State as the employer on the commitments made through this Charter.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho thakgolwa ha Tokomane ya Tshebetso ya Setjhaba ebile e thoholetsa mekgatlo ya basebetsi tshebeletsong ya setjhaba esita le Mmuso e le mohiri boikitlaetsong bo entsweng Tokomaneng ena.

src: The Charter introduces service standards within the public service with public service unions pledging their commitment to support the service standards.
tgt: Tokomane e teka maemo a tshebeletso kahara tshebeletso ya setjhaba moo mekgatlo ya basebetsi tshebeletsong ya setjhaba e itlamang ho tshehetsa maemo a tshebeletso.

src: Cabinet notes that many sectors are currently or have been engaged in wage negotiations.
tgt: Kabinete e hlokomela hore hajwale makala a mangata a kene kapa a ile a kena ditherisanong tsa meputso.

src: Cabinet welcomes settlements that have been reached in some sectors and takes note of continuing negotiations in others.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ditumellano tse fihlelletsweng makaleng a mang mme e a tseba ka ditherisano tse ntseng di tswelapele makaleng a mang.

src: Cabinet recognises that in a democracy, workers have the right to strike.
tgt: Kabinete e a ananela hore moo demokrasi e leng teng, basebetsi ba na le tokelo ya ho ipelaetsa.

src: Cabinet emphasises that such right must be exercised in a non-violent manner and in full compliance with the law.
tgt: Kabinete e thasisetsa hore tokelo e jwalo e tlameha ho etswa ka mokgwa o se nang dikgoka ebile e le o ikamahanyang le molao ka hohlehohle.

src: There is a responsibility on trade union leaders, employers and the state’s security services to ensure that the law is upheld, that provocative actions are avoided and that industrial action is conducted in a peaceful manner.
tgt: Ho na le boikarabelo baetapeleng ba mekgatlo ya basebetsi, bahiri le ditshebeletso tsa naha tsa tshireletso ho netefatsa hore molao ha o tlolwe, ho qojwa diketso tsa ho e lata letailana le hore mehwanto e etswe ka kgotso.

src: Cabinet calls on all parties to use their efforts to settle negotiations as soon as possible and to avoid protracted disputes.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa mekgatlong yohle ho sebedisa matsapa a yona ho phethela ditherisano kapelepele esita le ho qoba diqhwebeshano tsa nako e telele.

src: Such expeditious settlements will help to reduce the costs to the economy and promote the achievement of the county’s jobs and growth goals.
tgt: Ditumellano tseo tsa kapelepele di tla thusa ho fokotsa ditjeo moruong di be di kgothaletse katleho ya naha sepheong sa mesebetsi le kgolo.

src: Cabinet acknowledged the second Annual Mining Lekgotla that was held last week.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Lekgotla la bobedi la Merafo la Selemo le selemo le neng le tshwerwe bekeng e fetileng.

src: The Lekgotla presented another opportunity for the key role players in the mining industry to continue engaging in finding lasting solutions to the challenges that afflict this sector.
tgt: Lekgotla le hlahisitse monyetla o mong bakeng sa ba ka sehloohong ba amehang indastering ya merafo ho tswelapele ho fumaneng ditharollo tsa nako e telele diphephetsong tse thefulang lekala lena.

src: Under the leadership of the Deputy President Kgalema Motlanthe government also continues to support the framework agreement and its implementation for a sustainable and stable mining sector.
tgt: Tlasa boetapele ba Motlatsi wa Mopresidente Kgalema Motlanthe, mmuso le wona o tswelapele ho tshehetsa tumellano ya moralo esita le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha lekala la merafo le nang le boitjaro ba nako e telele le bile le tsitsitse.

src: In the build-up to the 20 Years of Freedom on the 27 April 2014, Cabinet calls on all South Africans to commemorate our history and celebrate our diverse cultures during Heritage Month.
tgt: Ditokisetsong tsa Tokoloho ya Dilemo tse 20 mohla la 27 Mmesa 2014, Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ohle ho hopola nalane ya rona le ho keteka botjhaba ba rona bo kopaneng ka ho se tshwane nakong ya Kgwedi ya Letlotlo la Setjhaba.

src: This year’s celebrations will be marked under the theme: “Reclaiming, Restoring and Celebrating Our Living Heritage”.The Heritage Day celebrations will take place at Sisa Dukashe Stadium in Mdantsane, Buffalo City Metro Municipality, Eastern Cape province on 24 September WEBTOKEN part of the 20 Years of Freedom campaign, the national communication partnership will see the launch of ‘Freedom Friday’ on 20 September 2013, which will provide a platform for South Africans to cherish our hard-fought freedom to ensure that future generations are able to benefit from our developmental democracy.
tgt: Mekete ya monongwaha e tla tshwauwa tlasa mookotaba o reng: “Ho tseka botjha, ho Kgutlisa le ho Keteka Letlotlo la rona la Setjhaba le Phelang”.Mekete ya Letsatsi la Letlotlo la Setjhaba e tla tshwarelwa Lebaleng la Dipapadi la Sisa Dukashe le Mdantsane, Masepaleng wa Toropokgolo ya Buffalo, Porofenseng ya Kapa Botjhabela mohla la 24 Loetse 2013.E le karolo ya Dilemo tse 20 tsa Tokoloho, selekane sa dikgokahanyo tsa naha se tla etella pele ho kgakolwa ha ‘Labohlano la Tokoloho’ mohla la 20 Loetse 2013, se tla fanang ka lepatlelo ho maAforika Borwa ohle ho baballa tokoloho e lwanetsweng ka thata, ho netefatsa hore meloko e tlang e kgona ho fola molemo demokrasing ya rona e ntseng e hola.

src: During September, in support of our domestic tourism efforts, Cabinet encourages South Africans to visit heritage sites to remind us of our journey to freedom.
tgt: Nakong ya Loetse, ho tshehetsa matsapa a bahahlaudi ba rona ba kahare, Kabinete e kgothalletsa maAforika Borwa ho etela ditsha tsa Letlotlo la naha ho re hopotsa ka leeto la rona la ho ya tokolohong.

src: Also, to support our natural heritage by visiting national parks free of charge from 9 to 13 September 2013 as part of the 8th annual South African National Parks (SANParks) Week.
tgt: Hape, ho tshehetsa letlotlo la rona la tlholeho ka ho etela dipaka tsa naha mahala ho tloha mohla la 9 ho ya ho la 13 Loetse 2013 e le karolo ya borobedi ya selemo le selemo ya Beke ya Dipaka tsa Naha tsa Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet encourages all parents and guardians to support their children in the preparation for the upcoming Annual National Assessments (ANA) in literacy and numeracy that takes place between 10 and 13 September 2013.Parents and guardians must ensure that they engage with the 2013 ANA results as this serves as an important diagnostic tool of learners’ strengths and WEBTOKEN preparation for the upcoming ANA parents, guardians and learners are urged to use the tools provided by the Department of Basic Education.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa batswadi le bahlokomedi bohle ho tshehetsa bana ba bona ditlhophisetsong tse tlang tsa Ditekolo tsa Naha tsa Selemo le Selemo (ANA), mokgahlelong wa ho bala le ho ngola esita le dipalo, tse tla tshwarwa dipakeng tsa mohla la 10 le 13 Loetse 2013.Batswadi le bahlokomedi ba tlameha ho netefatsa hore ba henahenana le diphetho tsa ANA tsa 2013 jwaloka ha di sebetsa e le sesebediswa sa bohlokwa sa tlhahlobo ya baithuti ya moo ba leng matla kapa moo ba fokolang teng.

src: These can be accessed on the Department's website.
tgt: Tsena di ka fumanwa websaeteng ya Lefapha (WEBTOKEN).

src: Cabinet extends a message of support to the South Africa National Defence Force soldiers deployed in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo for the period 13 June 2013 to 31 March 2014.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisa molaetsa wa tshehetso masoleng a Lebotho la Naha la Tshireletso la Aforika Borwa, a isitsweng Rephaboliking ya Demokrasi ya Congo nakong ya la 13 Phuptjane 2013 ho ya ho 31 Hlakubele 2014.

src: South Africans are called upon to support and give recognition to these soldiers who are instrumental is realising South Africa’s commitment to peace, stability and the strengthening of democracy in the African continent.
tgt: MaAforika Borwa a kopjwa ho tshehetsa le ho ananela masole ana a etsang mosebetsi wa bohlokwa o phethahatsang boikitlaetso ba Aforika Borwa ba kgotso, botsitso le matlafatso ya demokrasi kontinenteng ya Aforika.

src: Cabinet congratulates the presidential appointments of Mr Mxolisi Sandile Oliver Nxasana as the National Director of Public Prosecutions and Vasantrai Soni (SC) as the Head of Special Investigative Unit .
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa dikgiro tsa Mopresidente tsa Ntate Mxolisi Sandile Oliver Nxasana e le Motsamaisi e Moholo Botjhotjhising ba Setjhaba ba Naha le Vasantri Soni (SC) e le Hlooho ya Yuniti e Ikgethileng ya Dipatlisiso.

src: Cabinet wishes the Jewish community of South Africa a very happy Rosh Hashanah (5 to 6 September 2013).
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa setjhaba sa Majuda a Aforika Borwa Rosh Hashanah e monatenate (5-6 Loetse 2013).

src: Rosh Hashanah has profound significance for the Jewish Community in that it marks the beginning of a process of self-examination and reflection culminating in Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement.
tgt: Rosh Hashanah e na le tshusumetso ya bohlokwa setjhabeng sa Majuda hobane e bontsha qalo ya mosebetsi wa boitlhahlobo le boitekolo eo sethatho sa yona e leng Yom Kippur, Letsatsi la Tshwarelano.

src: Cabinet expresses its condolences to Minister Mthethwa and his family on the passing away of his mother Ms Nurse Gumbi on 3 September 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisa molaetsa wa matshediso ho Letona Mthethwa le ba lelapa labo ka ho hlokahallwa ke mmae, Mme Nurse Gumbi ka la 03 Loetse Dipuisano le diqeto tsa bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet received a report on the results of the Management Performance Assessments Tool (MPAT) of national and provincial departments for the 2012/13 financial year.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse tlaleho ka diphetho tsa Sesebediswa sa Ditekolo tsa Tshebetso ya Bolaodi (MPAT) sa mafapha a naha le a diporofense bakeng sa selemo sa ditjhelete sa 2012/13.

src: The report is another tool that seeks to improve the quality of services provided by the departments.
tgt: Tlaleho ke sesebediswa se seng se habileng ho ntlafatsa boleng ba ditshebeletso tseo mafapha a fanang ka tsona.

src: It assesses the four broad management areas namely supply chain management human resource management strategic planning and service delivery improvement.
tgt: E lekola dibaka tse nne tse batsi tsa bolaodi e leng bolaodi ba phano ya disebediswa bolaodi ba basebetsi merero ya mawa mmoho le ntlafatso ya phano ya ditshebeletso.

src: The assessment is done on three levels, self-assessment then a moderated process by the internal audit and finally moderated by a team of independent moderators.
tgt: Tekolo e etswa mehatong e meraro, boitekolo ka bowena ho latele tlhahlobo ya mosebetsi ya bohlakisi ba kahare ba dibuka tsa ditjhelete ho qetelwe ka ya ho lekolwa ke sehlopha se ikemetseng sa balekodi.

src: The report will be further unpacked by the Department of Performance Monitoring and Evaluation during a scheduled launch of the MPAT next week in Cape Town.
tgt: Tlaleho e tla boela e tsenkollwa ke Lefapha la Bodisa le Tlhahlobo ya Tshebetso nakong ya ho thakgolwa ho seng ho hlophisitswe ha MPAT bekeng e tlang Cape Town.

src: Cabinet received and approved the first quarter reports for 2013/14 on the implementation of Delivery Agreements for the Outcomes.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse ya ba ya ananela ditlaleho tsa kotare ya pele ya 2013/14 ho kenngweng tshebetsong ha Ditumellano tsa Phano bakeng sa Diphetho.

src: These reports will be unpacked during a planned series of media briefings for each of the 12 Outcomes.
tgt: Ditlaleho tsena di tla tsenkollwa nakong ya lethathamo le rerilweng la dipuisano le ba mehlodi ya ditaba bakeng sa se seng le se seng sa Diphetho tse Kabinete e bone tlaleho e tswang ho ‘Projeke ya ho Tloswa ha Lesedi le Lebe la Sekoloto’ mme ya ananela ditshisinyo tsa Komiti e Kgethehileng ya Kgwebisano le Dikamano tsa Matjhaba.

src: Cabinet noted the report from the ‘Removal of Adverse Credit Information Project’ and approved the recommendations of the Select Committee on Trade and International Relations.
tgt: Sena se habile ho rarolla qaka ya phihlello ya sekoloto ho maAforika Borwa ao a ka kgonang sekoloto.

src: This seeks to address the issue of access to credit to those South Africans that can afford credit.
tgt: Bana ke bareki bao e ka nnang yaba ba qetile ho lefa dikoloto tsa bona ka botlalo mme ba boemong boo ba ka kgonang sekoloto empa hajwale, phihlello ya bona e hakureditswe ke lesedi le lebe la sekoloto direkotong tsa bona.

src: These are consumers who may have paid their debts in full and are in a position to afford credit but whose access is currently impeded by negative credit information on their record.
tgt: Sena se habile ho netefatsa hore Molao wa Naha wa Sekoloto (Molao 34 wa 2005) o sebetsa ho ya kamoo o rerilweng ka teng ho netefatsa hore bareki ba ka kgonang sekoloto ba se ke ba kolotelwa.

src: Inaccessible or expensive credit hinders growth.
tgt: Sekoloto se sa fihlelleheng kapa se turang se sithabetsa kgolo.

src: Access to sustainable credit market is essential to all developmental goals.
tgt: Phihlello mmarakeng wa sekoloto wa nako e telele e a hlokeha sepheong sohle sa ntshetsopele.

src: Cabinet approved the White Paper on Remand Detention and its introduction to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Pampiri e Tshweu ya ho Busetsa Ditlamong esita le ho tekwa ha yona Palamenteng.

src: The draft White Paper seeks to improve the management of awaiting trial detention system in South African prisons.
tgt: Moralo wa nakwana wa Pampiri e Tshweu o habile ho ntlafatsa ho laolwa ha mokgwatshebetso wa ho emela ho bua nyewe motho a le ditlamong ditjhankaneng tsa Aforika Borwa.

src: The paper outlines the principles that will drive the detention management of remand detention.
tgt: Pampiri e hlakisa mekgwatshebetso e tla susumetsa bolaodi ba ditlamong ba ho busetsa ditlamong.

src: The report will be released through the Parliamentary process.
tgt: Tlaleho e tla ntshuwa ho ya ka metjha ya Palamente.

src: Cabinet approved that the Convention of Cluster Munitions be sent to Parliament for ratification.
tgt: Kabinete e dumetse hore Mmoka wa Sehlopha sa Dihlomo o romelwe Palamenteng bakeng sa kananelo.

src: Cabinet supports the destruction of cluster munitions stocks in compliance with this WEBTOKEN November 2006 a United Nations (UN) conference could not reach agreement on how the adverse humanitarian impact of these weapons should be addressed.
tgt: Kabinete e tshehetsa ho senngwa ha thepa ya sehlopha sa dihlomo e le ho ikamahanya le Mmoka ona.

src: This led to a group of 46 countries, including South Africa, embarking on a process outside the UN, the so-called Oslo Process, to ban cluster munitions.
tgt: Ka Pudungwana ya 2006 seboka sa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) ha se a ka sa fihlella tumellano ya kamoo sefutho sa botho sa ho rarolla bothata ba dihlomo tsena se leng kateng.

src: South Africa together with 93 other States signed the Convention in December 2008.
tgt: Sena se ile sa lebisa moo sehlopha sa dinaha tse 46, ho akga le Aforika Borwa, se ileng sa eba motjheng o mong o kathoko ho UN, o bitswang Mosebetsi wa Oslo, ho kwala sehlopha sa dihlomo.

src: On 1 August 2010 the Convention entered into force.
tgt: Mohla la 1 Phato 2010 Mokgwatshebetso o ile wa kenngwa tshebetsong.

src: The Convention bans the use, production, stockpiling and transfer of certain category of cluster munitions.
tgt: Mokgwatshebetso o kwala tshebediso, tlhahiso, poloko ya thepa le phetiso ya mofuta o itseng wa sehlopha sa dihlomo.

src: The ratification of the Convention is in line with South Africa’s commitments to upholding human rights and humanitarian law when engaging in war fare.
tgt: Kananelo ya Mokgwatshebetso e tsamaisana le boikitlaetso ba Aforika Borwa ba ho boloka ditokelo tsa botho le molao wa botho ha e sebetsana le dintwa.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the report on the Audit of Registered State Land and a desktop analysis of Private Land Ownership in South Africa, by the Chief Surveyor-General to WEBTOKEN information is critical to the success of all land developments in the country.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha tlaleho ya Tlhahlobo ya Dibuka tsa Ngodiso ya Mobu wa Mmuso le tshekatsheko e sa tebang ya Boithuelo ba Poraefete ba Mobu Aforika Borwa, e entsweng ke Mohlahlobikakaretso e Moholo wa tsa Mobu, Palamenteng.

src: The purpose of the audit of registered state land is to determine how much land is owned by the state, what it is used for and who the occupants/users are.
tgt: Sepheo sa tlhahlobo ya dibuka tsa ngodiso ya mobu wa mmuso ke ho fumana hore na mmuso o na le mobu o mokae, o sebedisetswa eng le hore na basebedisi ba wona ke bomang.

src: This will be used to enhance the integrity of the land register, which would serve as the basis for enhanced land planning and administration, including other functions relating to property portfolio management and improved delivery of services.
tgt: Sena se tla sebedisetswa ho ntlafatsa botshepehi ba rejistara ya mobu, e tla sebetsa e le motheo bakeng sa thero le tsamaiso tsa mobu tse ntlafaditsweng, ho akga le mesebetsi e meng e amanang le bolaodi ba tshebetso ya thepa esita le phano e ntlafaditsweng ya ditshebeletso.

src: Cabinet approved the South African Mint Company’s designs for the 2013 R2 (1/4 oz) commemorative 24 ct gold coin series and the 2013 R1 (1/10 oz) commemorative 24 ct gold coin series.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse metako ya Khamphane ya Popo ya Tjhelete Aforika Borwa bakeng sa lethathamo la sehopotso sa tjhelete e lewana ya 24 ct ya kgauta ya R2 ya 2013 (1/4 oz) le lethathamo la sehopotso sa tjhelete e lewana ya 24 ct ya kgauta ya R1 (1/10 oz).Motako wa tjhelete e lewana ya kgauta ya R2 ya 2013 o tla ngolwa ka puo ya Sekgothu athe motako wa tjhelete e lewana ya kgauta ya R1 ya 2013 e tla ba tlhoka ya boraro – Mohlampepe wa Ditholwana.

src: The design of the 2013 R2 gold coin will feature the San language and the design of the 2013 R1 gold coin will be the 3rd pollinator – the Fruit Bat.
tgt: Metako ya tjhelete e lewana mmoho le Mahlalosi a tsona di tla hatiswa Koranteng ya Melawana ya Mmuso.

src: The coin designs together with their Proclamations will be printed in the Government Gazette.
tgt: Kamorao ho moo, di tla etswa mme di rekiswe ka metjha e tlwaelehileng.

src: Cabinet approved the submission to the United Nation Committee on the Rights of the Child and African Union Expert Committee the 3 reports relating to the progress made in securing the rights and wellbeing of children.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha ditlaleho tse tharo tse amanang le kgatelopele e entsweng tshireletsong ya ditokelo le bophelo bo botle ba bana Komiting ya Matjhaba a Kopaneng ya Ditokelo tsa Ngwana le Komiti ya Boqhetseke ya Kopano ya Aforika.

src: The reports provide a transparent and critical opportunity for South Africa to assess the progress it has made in these areas:a) Country Report on the Optional Protocol on the Sale of Children, Child Prostitution and Child Pornographyb) the combined second, third and fourth report on the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Childc) the African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child: First Country report to the African Union Expert Committee on the Rights and Welfare of the Child.
tgt: Ditlaleho di fana ka monyetla wa bohlokwa o nang le ponaletso bakeng sa Aforika Borwa ho sekaseka kgatelopele eo e seng e e entse dintlheng tsenaa) Tlaleho ya Naha ka Prothokhole e sa Tlameng ka Thekiso ya Bana, Bootswa ba Bana le ho Nyweka ha Bana.

src: Cabinet thanks the range of committed civil society organisations and international partners who partnered with government in realising the commitments made to children in our Constitution.
tgt: Kabinete e leboha lethathama la mekgatlo ya setjhaba ka boikitlaetso esita le balekane ba matjhaba ba ikopantseng le mmuso ka ho hlokomela boikitlaetso bo entsweng ke Molaotheo wa rona baneng.

src: Bills.
tgt: Dibili.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Restitution of Land Rights Amendment Bill to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha Bili ya Sehlomathiso ya Pusetso ya Ditokelo tsa Mobu Palamenteng.

src: The Bill amends the Restitution Act to extend the date for the lodging of claims for restitution to 31 December 2018 the criminalisation of the lodgement of a fraudulent claim the simplification of the procedure for the appointment of Judges to the Land Claims Court and the amendment of certain provisions aimed at promoting the effective implementation of the Act.
tgt: Bili e hlomathisa Molao wa Pusetso ho eketsa letsatsi la ho qetela bakeng sa ho kenngwa ha ditseko tsa pusetso ya mobu ho ya fihla ho la 31 Tshitwe 2018 ho etsetsa hore e be tlolo ya molao ho kenngwa ha tseko ka bolotsana nolofatso ya tsamaiso bakeng sa ho kgethwa ha Baahlodi Lekgotleng la Ditseko tsa Mobu esita le ho hlomathiswa ha dikarolwana tse itseng tse reretsweng ho kgothalletsa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Molao ka bokgabane.

src: The re-opening of lodgment of claims is guided by the vision of the National Development Plan as well as the Comprehensive Rural Development Programme and other growth strategies intended to promote national reconciliation and social cohesion.
tgt: Ho bulwa botjha ha ho kenngwa ha ditseko ho tataiswa ke tjhebelopele ya Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP) esita le Lenaneo le Phethahetseng la Ntshetsopele ya Dibaka tsa Mahaeng le mawa a mang a kgolo a reretsweng ho kgothalletsa poelano ya setjhaba le momahano ya setjhaba.

src: Cabinet approved the introduction of the Science and Technology Laws, Amendment Bill, 2013 to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha Bili ya Sehlomathiso ya Melao ya Saense le Theknoloji, 2013 Palamenteng.

src: The Amendment Bill deals with amendments to a battery of Acts which govern the operations of entities (science councils) that were established in terms of the said Acts.
tgt: Bili ya Sehlomathiso e sebetsana le dihlomathiso tsa lethathama la Melao e laolang tshebetso ya ditheo (makgotla a saense) tse neng di thewe ho ya ka Melao eo.

src: The Bill seeks to streamline the process for the nomination and appointment of members as well as the filling of vacancies to the Boards or Councils of such entities.
tgt: Bili e habile ho nolofatsa mosebetsi wa ho thonngwa le ho kgethwa ha ditho esita le ho kwalwa ha dikgeo Dibotong kapa Makgotleng a ditheo tseo.

src: The Bill enhances efficiency and consistency in the operations and governance of public entities reporting to the Minister of Science and WEBTOKEN strengthening Parliament’s oversight role, the Bill seeks to release Parliament from certain executive responsibilities relating to the appointment of members and filling of vacancies to such Boards or Councils.
tgt: Bili e ntlafatsa tshebetso e ntle le tshwano mosebetsing le taolong ya ditheo tsa setjhaba tse tlalehang ho Letona la Saense le Theknoloji.

src: The Bill makes statutory provisions for the recognition of the Khoi-San and also addresses limitations of existing legislation relating to traditional leadership and governance.
tgt: Ho matlafatseng seabo sa tekolo sa Palamente, Bili e habile ho lokolla Palamente boikarabelong bo itseng ba phethahatso bo amanang le ho kgethwa ha ditho esita le ho kwalwa ha dikgeo Dibotong tseo kapa Makgotleng ao.

src: The Bill will contribute to the National Development Plan’s key target relating to the broadening of social cohesion and unity while addressing the inequities of the past.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho phatlalatswa ha Bili ya Ditaba tsa Setso Koranteng Melawana ya ya Mmuso bakeng sa ditshwaelo tsa setjhaba.

src: Cabinet approved the National Credit Act Policy Review Framework and the National Credit Amendment Bill for introduction to Parliament.
tgt: Bili e fana ka dintlha tsa molao bakeng sa kananelo ya Bakgothu ebile e rarolla bothata ba ho kgoneha molaong o seng o le teng o amanang le boetapele ba setso le puso.

src: The National Credit Act, 2005 (Act 34 of 2005) came into full effect on 1 June 2007 introducing a new era of credit regulations into the South African legal system.
tgt: Haesale ho tloha ka 1994 mmuso o ile wa nkela hloohong diphephetso tse amanang le Bakgothu, haholoholo kananelo ya setjhaba sa bakgothu le baetapele.

src: The Bill aims to strengthen the capacity of the National Credit Regulator (NCR) to address certain challenges especially around court processes and to strengthen enforcement and implementation of the provisions of the National Credit Act 34 of 2005.The Department of Trade and Industry (the dti) also concluded that the policy framework on Consumer Credit, on which the National Credit Act 34 of 2005 is founded, is sound and relevant.
tgt: Bili e tla thusa pehelong ya bohlokwa ya NDP e amanang le ho etswa batsi ha momahano ya setjhaba le kopano, ha ka lehlakoreng le leng e ntse e rarolla bothata ba nako e fetileng ba ho se lekane.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Determination of Remuneration of Members of Constitutional Institutions Matters Amendment Bill, 2013.The Bill aims to create uniformity in respect of the determination of remuneration, allowances and other terms and conditions of employment of members from the Chapter 9 Institutions, thereby enhancing efficiency and consistency in the operations and governance of these key institutions.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Moralo wa Tjhebobotjha ya Leano la Molao wa Naha wa Sekoloto le Bili ya Sehlomathiso ya Naha ya Sekoloto bakeng sa ho tekwa Palamenteng.

src: Cabinet approved the appointment of Mr Mokutule Joseph Kgobokoe to the post of Deputy Director-General: Food Security and Agrarian Reform at the Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries.
tgt: Sepheo sa Bili ke ho matlafatsa bokgoni ba Molaodi wa Naha wa Sekoloto (NCR) ho rarolla diphephetso tse itseng haholoholo mabapi le mesebetsi ya lekgotla la dinyewe esita le ho matlafatsa ho qobella le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha dikateng tsa Molao wa Naha wa Sekoloto wa 34 wa 2005.Lefapha la Kgwebisano le Indasteri (dti) le lona le qetile ka hore moralo wa leano wa Sekoloto sa Bareki, moo Molao wa Naha wa Sekoloto wa 34 wa 2005 o fumanweng teng, o motle ebile o nepahetse.

src: Cabinet approved with the appointment of Ms Zandile Yvonne Mathe to the post of Deputy Director-General: National Water Resource Infrastructure at the Department of Water Affairs.
tgt: Sena se latela tjhebobotjha e phethahetseng ya 2012, e entsweng ke dti.

src: Cabinet approved the appointment of the following people as board members to the Cooperative Banks Development Agency:a) Sethe Patricia Makhesha (Chairperson)b) Peter Koch (re appointment to Deputy Chairperson)c) Venete Jarlene Kleind) Lufuno Nevondwee) Thabo Vaughan Shenxanef) Samuel Senalor Akrongg) David Ginsburgh) Renganayagee Kisten.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha Bili ya Sehlomathiso ya ho Nka Qeto ka Tefo ya Meputso ya Ditho tsa Ditaba tsa Ditheo tsa Molaotheo, 2013.Sepheo sa Bili ke ho thea tshwano mabapi le ho nka qeto ka tefo ya meputso, melemo e fumanwang mosebetsing le melawana e meng le dipehelo tsa kgiro ya ditho tsa ditheo tsa Kgaolo ya 9, moo e matlafatsang tshebetso e ntle le tshwano mesebetsing ya puso ditheong tsena tsa bohlokwa.

src: Cabinet approved the appointment of the following members to the Agricultural Research Council in terms of section 9(1) of the Agricultural Research Act, 1990 Act No.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse kgiro ya Ntate Mokutule Joseph Kgobokoe mosebetsing wa Motlatsi wa Motsamaisi e Moholo: Hlahisong e sa Kgaelleng ya Dijo le Ntlafatso ya Temo Lefapheng la Temo, Meru le Botshwasi ba Ditlhapi.

src: a) Mr Jonathan Winston Alexander Godden (reappointment)b) Prof Michael Jeffrey Kahn (reappointment)c) Prof Sibusiso Vil-Nkomo (reappointment)d) Dr Joyce Chitja (reappointment)e) Ms Wilna Jansen Van Rijssen (reappointment)f) Ms Dudu Msomi (reappointment)g) Mr Mzolisi Dyasi (reappointment)h) Prof Frans J.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse kgiro ya batho ba latelang e le ditho tsa boto tsa Eijensi ya Ntshetsopele ya Dibanka tse Kopaneng:a) Sethe Patricia Makhesha (Modulasetulo)b) Peter Koch (kgiro hape e le Motlatsi wa Modulasetulo)c) Venete Jarlene Kleind) Lufuno Nevondwee) Thabo Vaughan Shenxanef) Samuel Senalor Akrongg) David Ginsburgh) Renganayagee Kisten.

src: C Swanepoel (reappointment)i) Mr Gerard John Martinj) Ms Dora Ndabak) Mr. Ismail Cassim Motalal) Ms Muhle Joyce Mashitengm) Ms. Rowen Graham Nicholisn) Mr. Clive Douglas Knealeo) Prof Louw Hoffmanp) Mr. Allen Henry Bishop.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse kgetho ya ditho tse latelang Lekgotleng la Diphuphutso tsa Temo ho ya ka karolo 9(1) ya Molao wa Diphuphutso tsa Temo, 1990 Molao wa 86 wa 1990 nakong e sa feteng dilemo tse tharo.

src: Cabinet concurred with the appointment of the following persons to the Council Of The Private Security Industry Regulatory Authority, for a period not exceeding three years:a) Mr Daniel Claude Mojalefa Rathebe (Vice-Chairperson)b) Brigadier Cynthia Lindiwe Philison (councillor)c) Mr Benjamin Somangamane Ntuli (councillor)d) Ms. Nontokoza Mthembu (councillor).
