tgt: a) Ntate Jonathan Winston Alexander Godden (o kgirilwe hape)b) Moprofesara Michael Jeffrey Kahn (o kgirilwe hape)c) Moprofesara Sibusiso Vil-Nkomo (o kgirilwe hape)d) Ngaka Joyce Chitja (o kgirilwee hape)e) Mme Wilna Jansen Van Rijssen (o kgirilwe hape)f) Mme Dudu Msomi (o kgirilwe hape)a) Ntate Mzolisi Dyasi (o kgirilwe hape)b) Moprofesara Frans J.

src: Cabinet approved the extension of the employment contract of Dr Vuyelwa Nhlapo as the Chief Executive Officer of ` the National Development Agency, for a 2 year term with effect 1 September 2013 to 31 August 2015.
tgt: C Swanepoel (o kgirilwe hape)c) Ntate Gerard John Martind) Mme Dora Ndabae) Ntate Ismail Cassim Motalaf) Mme Muhle Joyce Mashitengg) Mme Rowen Graham Nicholish) Ntate Clive Douglas Knealei) Moprofesara Louw Hoffmanj) Ntate Allen Henry Bishop.

src: Cabinet approved the appointment of Mr Mokadi Max Mathye as the Chief Executive Officer for the Food and Beverage Sector Education and Training Authority.
tgt: Kabinete e dumellana le ho kgethwa ha batho ba latelang Lekgotleng la Matla a Taolo ya Indasteri ya Tshireletso ya Poraefete, nakong e sa feteng dilemo tse tharo:a) Ntate Daniel Claude Mojalefa Rathebe (Motlatsi wa Modulasetulo)b) Brigadier Cynthia Lindiwe Philison (Molekgotla)c) Ntate Benjamin Somangamane Ntuli (Molekgotla)d) Mme Nontokoza Mthembu (Molekgotla).

src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment.1 Under President Jacob Zuma’s leadership, government is rolling out the country’s multitrillion-rand public infrastructure programme aimed at unlocking job opportunities and bringing services to all South Africans.
tgt: 23 Sep Maemo a Kabinete mabapi le dintlha tsa bohlokwa maemong a ha jwale.1 Tlasa boetapele ba Mopresidente Jacob Zuma, mmuso o sebetsa ka lenaneo la naha la meralo ya motheo ya setjhaba la ditrilione tse ngata ngata tsa diranta le reretsweng ho utolla menyetla ya mesebetsi le ho tlisa ditshebeletso ho maAforika Borwa ohle.

src: Through these programmes government is delivering on its commitment to create more jobs.
tgt: Ka mananeo ana, mmuso o tsitlallela boikitlaetsong ba wona ba ho thea mesebetsi e mengata le ho feta.

src: Since the adoption of the New Growth Path employment has increased by 750 000, with just under half of these jobs, having been generated in the public service, especially amongst the ranks of health workers, teachers and the police.
tgt: Haesale ho tloha kananelong ya Mokgwa o Motjha wa Kgolo mesebetsi e eketsehile ka 750 000, mme katlasenyana ho halofo ya mesebetsi ena e hlahisitswe tshebeletsong ya setjhaba, haholoholo basebetsing ba tsa bophelo bo botle, matitjhere le mapolesa.

src: These programmes prioritise small business development which is an important component for unlocking economic opportunities.
tgt: Mananeo ana a bea ntshetsopele ya dikgwebo tse nyenyane ka sehloohong, e leng ntho ya bohlokwa ya ho utolla menyetla ya moruo.

src: Cabinet expresses its gratitude to those sectors who are partnering with government to implement this massive infrastructure development drive and calls for further collaboration in fast-tracking efforts to create employment and transform the economy and our WEBTOKEN part of the public infrastructure roll-out President Jacob Zuma will on 20 September 2013 open the Grootvlei Power Station and inspect the railway line construction site in Mpumalanga.
tgt: Kabinete e leboha makala ao a ikamahanyang le mmuso ho kenya tshebetsong lenaneo lena le leholohadi la ntshetsopele ya meralo ya motheo mme e etsa kgoeletso tshebedisanong ya ho potlakisa matsapa a ho thea mesebetsi le ho fetola moruo esita le setjhaba sa habo rona.

src: Cabinet welcomed the construction of the new Sol Plaatjie University in Kimberley, Northern Cape which is expected to start before the end of September 2013.
tgt: Mopresidente Jacob Zuma o tla bula Seteishene sa Motlakase sa Grootvlei ka la 20 Loetse 2013 a be a hlahlobe le setsha sa kaho ya seporo sa terene kwana Mpumalanga, e le karolo ya boikitlaetso ba neelano ya meralo ya motheo ya setjhaba.

src: The development of the new university has been identified and prioritised within the Strategic Integrated Projects (SIP 14) by the Presidential Infrastructure Coordinating Committee (PICC).2 President Jacob Zuma together with his Cabinet will be honouring senior citizens of South Africa at Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria on 29 September 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse kaho ya Yunivesithi e ntjha ya Sol Plaatjie Kimberly, Kapa Leboya, e lebeletsweng ho qala pele ho mafelo a Loetse 2013.

src: This forms part of celebrating the contribution by our senior citizens to the development of our communities and country.
tgt: Ena ke katleho e kgolo kgolong le ntshetsopeleng ya lekala la thuto e phahameng Aforika Borwa.

src: This will mark the start of the Older Persons Week, ending on 6 October, which is Grandparents Day.3 President Jacob Zuma will address the General Debate of the 68th Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA68) in New York on 24 September 2013.This year’s theme is: “The Post-2015 Development Agenda: Setting the Stage!” and focusses on the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) target date of 2015, as well the Development Agenda going forward.
tgt: Kaho ya yunivesithi e ntjha e ile ya hlwauwa yaba ya bewa ka sehloohong kahara Diprojeke tsa Lewa le Momahantsweng (SIP 14) ke Khomishene ya Mopresidente e Hlophisang Dikaho tsa Motheo (PICC).2 Mopresidente Jacob Zuma hammoho le Kabinete ya hae ba tla be ba tlotla metsofe ya Aforika Borwa Tlung ya Baeti ya Mopresidente ya Sefako Makgatho e Pretoria ka la 29 Loetse 2013.

src: UNGA68 provides South Africa with a platform to advance our strategic approach towards achieving the MDGs and the Post-2015 Development Agenda.
tgt: Sena se bopa karolo ya ho keteka seabo sa metsofe ya rona ntshetsopeleng ya setjhaba sa habo rona esita le ya naha.

src: Our participation will also be informed by South Africa’s national interest and priorities, as well as our regional and continental commitments.4 Cabinet condemns in the strongest terms the sabotage to the electricity grid by illegal strikers that resulted in power outages in parts of Johannesburg.
tgt: Sena e tla be e le sesupo sa qalo ya Beke ya Batho ba Baholo, e tla fela ka la 6 Mphalane, e leng Letsatsi la Bonkgono le Bontatemoholo.3 Mopresidente Jacob Zuma o tla tshetleha puo Ngangisanong e Akaretsang ya Phutheo ya bo68 ya Sebokakakaretso sa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UNGA68) New York ka la 24 Loetse 2013.

src: Such acts at the time when the country is moving towards stabilising its electricity supply cannot be ignored and must be dealt with to the full extent of the law.5 The release of South Africa’s annual 2012/13 National Crime Statistics reaffirms our conviction that working together we will reach our goal of a society that is free from crime, that attracts investment that ensure peace and stability in our communities.
tgt: Mookotaba wa monongwaha ke: “Lenanetsamaiso la Ntshetsopele la Kamora 2015: Ho Bula Sebaya!” mme o habile nakong e beilweng ya 2015 ya Maikemisetso a Ntshetsopele ya Dilemokete (MDGs), esita le Lenanetsamaiso la Ntshetsopele kamorao ho moo, ho ya pele.

src: Crime statistics are also used daily as a management tool to guide operational plans for the South African Police Service (SAPS).Cabinet commends the tireless efforts of the South African Police Service and all organised and community bodies which have partnered with government in the fight against crime.
tgt: Seabo sa rona se tla boela se susumetswa ke ditabatabelo le dintho tse ka sehloohong tsa Aforika Borwa, esita le boikitlaetso ba rona ba lebatowa le ba kontinente.4 Kabinete e seolla kahohlehohle ditshitiso tsa marangrang a motlakase, tse entsweng ke batho ba neng ba le seteraekeng se seng molaong, tse ileng tsa baka ho kgaoha ha phepelo ya motlakase dikarolong tsa Johannesburg.

src: Working together we will ensure a South Africa were South African feel safe and secure.6 Cabinet expressed its grave concern at the recent spate of gruesome road traffic accidents.
tgt: Diketso tse jwalo di ke ke tsa tlodiswa mahlo hodimo nakong ena eo naha e hahamallang botsitsong ba phepelo ya yona ya motlakase, mme di tlameha ho thibelwa kahohlehohle ka tshebediso ya molao.5 Ho ntshuwa ha Dipalopalo tsa selemo le selemo tsa 2012/13 tsa Ditlolo tsa Molao Aforika Borwa ho boela ho thasisetsa boitshepo ba rona ba hore ha re sebetsa mmoho re tla fihlella sepheo sa rona sa setjhaba se sa angweng ke ditlolo tsa molao, se hohelang matsete a netefatsang kgotso le botsitso dibakeng tsa rona.

src: Such accidents have left some families destitute and they also have a serious negative impact on the economy.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho bohle ba amehang ho tshohla ka botebo diphumano tsena ka moya o motle.

src: Cabinet calls upon all motorists to ensure that their vehicles are roadworthy and they take responsibility when get behind the wheel.
tgt: Mmuso o ntsha dipalopalo tsena hang ka selemo ka sepheo sa ho fa setjhaba lesedi la moraorao twantshong ya ditlolo tsa molao, esita le ho sheba botjha mawa a jwale a ho lwantsha ditlolo tsa molao.

src: To that extent Cabinet calls upon road traffic authorities to continue to main a zero tolerance towards unroadworthy vehicles and drank driving.
tgt: Dipalopalo tsa ditlolo tsa molao di boela di sebediswa kamehla e le sesebediswa sa ho tataisa merero ya ho sebetsa ya Tshebeletso ya Sepolesa sa Aforika Borwa (SAPS).Kabinete e thoholetsa matsapa a matla a SAPS le mekgatlo yohle e ipopileng esita le setjhaba ka ho sebedisana le mmuso twantshong ya ditlolo tsa molao.

src: Cabinet also calls upon pedestrians to respect the traffic laws.7 Cabinet calls on all South Africans to celebrate Heritage Day, 24 September 2013 by visiting various sites of our rich and diverse heritage across the country in celebrating our 20 Years of Freedom.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa ohle ho ikamahanya le twantsho ya ditlolo tsa molao.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to support our disabled athletes who continue to make our country proud by delivering a world-class performance and inspiring all of us to reach greater heights.9 Cabinet welcomes the National Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment (BBBEE) Summit which will take place from 3 to 5 October 2013 under the theme: “A Decade of Economic Empowerment”.The policy instrument of Black Economic Empowerment is essentially a growth strategy aimed at broadening the economic base of the country by targeting inequality which remains the weakest point of the South African economy.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e ipiletsa ho ditaaso ho hlompha melao ya tsela.7 Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ohle ho keteka Letsatsi la Letlotlo la Botjhaba, 24 Loetse 2013, ka ho etela dibaka tse fupereng letlotlo la botjhaba bo sa tshwaneng naha ka bophara e le ho keteka Dilemo tse 20 tsa Tokoloho ya rona.

src: The Summit will assess the progress of the implementation of BBBEE following the 10 year anniversary since the enactment of the BBBEE Act in 2003.
tgt: Ho kopjwa maAforika Borwa ohle, dikolo, dikgwebo le dibaka tsohle ho phahamisa folakga ya rona e le sesupo sa rona sa ho keteka Dilemo tse 20 tsa Tokoloho esita le ho tshehetsa letsholo la ‘Bolabohlano ba Tokoloho’ le kgakolwang ka la 20 Lwetse 20.8 Kabinete e thoholetsa Lucas Sithole ka ho hapa papadi e bapalwang ka bonngwe ke ba sebedisang dituloteti ya Thonamente ya Tenese ya Amerika New York.

src: Corporate stakeholders, trade union representatives, political parties and civil society organisations will participate in charting South Africa’s third iteration of black economic empowerment with the amended BBBEE Act and refined BBBEE Codes of Good Practice.10 Cabinet applauds the Department of Social Development on their new service delivery improvement strategy called Project Mikondzo which will extend the reach of social services to the poor and vulnerable in every corner of South Africa.
tgt: Maemo a Sithole a lefatshe a nyolohile ka kgato e le nngwe hore e be wa bobedi kamora tlholo ena, eo e neng e le ya pele ya maemo a hodimo ya Setlamo sa Tenese ya Matjhaba bakeng sa moAforika ebile e le moAforika Borwa.

src: During Social Development Month, the Department of Social Development together with its entities, the South African Social Security Agency and the National Development Agency, will continue to roll out Project Mikondzo in the 1 300 poorest wards in 23 District Municipalities as identified and prioritised by Cabinet.11 Cabinet encourages South Africans to participate in the upcoming Imbizo Focus Week between 7 and 13 October 2013.Following the success of the June 2013 National Imbizo Focus Week, this second Focus Week will provide a platform for the Political Principals to further engage with the public.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ho tshehetse baatlelete ba rona ba holofetseng, ba tswelang pele ho etsa hore naha ya rona e be motlotlo ka ho intsha sehlabelo le ho re kgothatsa bohle hore re fihlelle ditabatabelo tsa rona.9 Kabinete e ananela Seboka sa Naha sa Motheo o Batsi wa Matlafatso ya ba Batsho Moruong (BBBEE) se tla tshwarwa ho tloha ka la 3 ho ya ho la 5 Mphalane tlasa mookotaba o reng: “Selemoshome sa Matlafatso Moruong”.Sesebediswa sa leano la Matlafatso ya ba Batsho Moruong hantlentle ke lewa la kgolo le reretsweng ho etsa hore motheo wa moruo wa naha o be batsi ka ho tsepamisa maikutlo tlhokehong ya tekano, e leng bofokodi bo boholo ba moruo wa Aforika Borwa.

src: This period provides another avenue for citizens to engage face-to-face with Members of the Executive, to celebrate successes and to address challenges on implementation of government programmes.
tgt: Seboka se tla sekaseka kgatelopele ya ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha BBBEE kamora ho ketekwa ha dilemo tse 10 haesale ha na ho kgakolwa Molao wa BBBEE ka 2003.

src: Key Cabinet discussions and decisions.1 Cabinet approved the National Policy on Food and Nutrition Security, the Household Food and Nutrition Security Strategy and the Fetsa Tlala Food Production intervention.
tgt: Setlamo sa ba amehang, baemedi ba mekgatlo ya basebetsi, mekga ya dipolotiki le mekgatlo ya setjhabeng ba tla ba le seabo ho kutlweng ha thasisetso ya boraro ya matlafatso ya ba batsho moruong ya Aforika Borwa, ka Molao wa BBBEE o hlomathisitsweng le Mekgwa e ntlafaditsweng ya Tshebetso e Ntle.10 Kabinete e thoholetsa Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba leanong la lona le letjha le ntlafaditsweng la phano ya ditshebeletso le bitswang Projeke ya Mikondzo, le tla atolla phihlello ya ditshebeletso tsa setjhaba ho ya bafutsaneng esita le bao ba kotsing dikgutlwaneng tsohle tsa Aforika Borwa.

src: It is supported by specific intervention strategies to tackle the challenges of household food shortages as well as increase food production, so as to end hunger by 2030.
tgt: Dipuisano le diqeto tsa bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.1 Kabinete e ananetse ho kena dipakeng ha Leano la Naha Tshireletsong ya Dijo le Phepo, Lewa la Tshireletso ya Dijo le Phepo ya Malapeng esita le ho kena dipakeng ha Tlhahiso ya Dijo ya Fetsa Tlala.

src: The Strategy and the Fetsa Tlala Food production are Inter-Departmental programmes that underpin the Policy.
tgt: Leano la Naha le habile ho arabela diphephetsong tse ngata tse amanang le ho se be teng ha tshireletso ya dijo Aforika Borwa.

src: A launch will be conducted to unpack the Policy and Programmes.2 Cabinet approved the Framework for South Africa’s engagement with the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) for the period 2013/14-2016/17.South Africa seeks to utilise this relationship to achieve three key objectives i) higher, inclusive economic growth, a prerequisite for addressing unemployment, poverty and inequality ii) a skilled and capable workforce, to support the delivery of the national development targets and iii) Advancing the African agenda, where South Africa will seek to exert greater influence of the global agenda from which African economies can derive benefit.
tgt: Le tsheheditswe ke mawa a totobetseng a ho kena dipakeng e le ho rarolla diphephetso tsa dikgaello tsa dijo malapeng hammoho le ho eketsa tlhahiso ya dijo, ka sepheo sa ho fedisa tlala ka 2030.

src: OECD countries remain key trade and investment partners for South Africa.
tgt: Lewa mmoho le Tlhahiso ya Fetsa Tlala ke mananeo a ho matlafatsa Leano a Kopanetsweng ke Mafapha.

src: It is estimated that OECD countries contributed more than 65% to global GDP in 2011.The approach provides a framework for government departments to manage their respective engagements with the OECThis enhanced coordination in government would enable optimal benefits to be derived from the partnership.
tgt: Kgakolo e tla etsuwa ho qhoqholla Leano le Mananeo.2 Kabinete e ananetse Moralo wa dipuisano tsa Aforika Borwa le Mokgatlo wa Ntshetsopele ya Tshebedisanommoho Moruong (OECD) bakeng sa nako ya 2013/14-2016/17.Aforika Borwa e habile ho sebedisa selekane sena ho fihlella dipheo tse tharo tsa bohlokwa:i) kgolo ya moruo e phahameng e kenyeletsang bohle, e leng tlhokeho e kgolo ya ho rarolla tlhokeho ya mesebetsi, bofuma le ho hloka tekatekanoii) basebetsi ba nang le boqhetseke le bokgoni, ho tshehetsa neelano ya dipehelo tsa ntshetsopele ya naha leiii) ho Ntshetsapele lenanetsamaiso la Aforika moo meruo ya Aforika e ka folang molemo.

src: The incentive is one among many that will fall under the umbrella of Government’s youth employment strategy and will complement existing government programmes.
tgt: Mokgwa ona o fana ka moralo bakeng sa mafapaha a mmuso ho laola dipuisano tsa wona le OECTlhophiso ena e ntlafaditsweng mmusong, e tla thusa hore ho folwe melemo e metle ka ho fetisisa selekaneng sena.

src: The youth employment tax incentive targets young people entering the labour market and earning below the personal income tax threshold.
tgt: Dibili.1 Kabinete e ananetse Bili ya Meropotso ya Lekgetho la Mesebetsi e tla ntshwa hore setjhaba se tshwaele ka yona.

src: In doing so, it targets lower skill, lower wage individuals who have low prospects of finding a job.
tgt: Bili e teka meropotso haholoholo ka sepheo sa ho kgothaletsa bahiri ho hira batjha ba tsomang mesebetsi ba bile ba se na boiphihlelo bo bokaalo.

src: The incentive will create conditions conducive to job creation and improve employment prospects for such marginalised workers.
tgt: Moropotso ke enngwe ya dintho tse ngata tse welang tlasa bonamelo ba lewa la Mmuso la mesebetsi ya batjha mme le tla thusa ho tshehetsa maano a mmuso.

src: A planned briefing will be undertaken to unpack the Bill.2 Cabinet approved the Draft Land Management Commission Bill, 2013 to be released for public comments.
tgt: Meropotso ya lekgetho la mesebetsi ya batjha e tobile batho ba batjha ba qalang ho sebetsa mme ba amohela meputso e katlase ho sekepele sa lekeno la motho ka mong le pukutlwang lekgetho.

src: Amongst others the Land Management Commission Bill, 2013 seeks to establish the Land Management Commission.
tgt: Ho tla tshwarwa pontshano e reretsweng ho qhaqholla Bili.2 Kabinete e ananetse Bili ya Moralo wa Khomishene ya Bolaodi ba Mobu, 2013, e tla ntshuwa bakeng sa hore setjhaba se tshwaele ka yona.

src: The Land Management Commission will be required to adjudicate land ownership disputes in respect of which two or more title deeds may have been issued on the same land parcel.
tgt: Ho tse ding, Bili ya Khomishene ya Bolaodi ba Mobu, 2013, e habile ho thea Khomishene ya Bolaodi ba Mobu.

src: The Commission will also be required to establish and maintain a government wide database of all state land registered in the name of a department including any surveyed unregistered state land.3 Cabinet approved the submission of the Legal Aid Bill, 2013 to Parliament.
tgt: Khomishene ya Bolaodi ba Mobu e tla lebellwa ho diya kahlolo qhwebeshanong ya boithuelo ba mobu moo e ka nnang ya ba mangolo a mabedi kapa a fetang bobedi a boithuelo ba thepa a ntshitswe bakeng sa setsha se le seng.

src: The Bill is intended to repeal the Legal Aid Act, 1969 (Act no.22 of 1969) in accordance with prevailing circumstances, particularly the new constitutional dispensation, and to streamline its application.
tgt: Khomishene e tla boela e lebellwa ho thea le ho boloka lesedi la motheo le batsi la mmuso la mobu ohle o ngodisitsweng e le wa mmuso lebitsong la lefapha, ho akga le mobu ofe kapa ofe o hlahlobilweng wa mmuso mme o sa ngodiswa.3 Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha Bili ya Dithuso tsa Molao, 2013, Palamenteng.

src: The Bill is intended to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of Legal Aid South Africa, which, in turn will have positive knock-on effects for society as a whole.
tgt: Bili e reretswe ho hlakola Molao wa Dithuso tsa Molao, 1969 (Molao wa 22 wa 1969) ho ya ka maemo a renang, haholoholo tshebetso e ntjha ya molaotheo, esita le ho ntlafatsa tshebediso ya wona e ntle.

src: It can be linked to the key targets of entrenching a social security system with social protection for the poor and other groups in need, and the realisation of a developmental, capable and ethical state that treats its citizens with dignity.4 Cabinet approved the publication of the International Health Regulations Bill, 2013 in the Government Gazette for public comments.
tgt: E ka nna ya amanngwa le dipehelo tsa mokgwa wa tshireletso ya setjhaba ka kakaretso le tshireletso ya setjhaba bakeng sa bafutsana le dihlophana tse ding tse e hlokang ka sebele, le kelohloko ya naha e ntseng e thuthua, e nang le bokgoni le boitshwaro bo botle ebile e tshwara baahi ba yona ka seriti.4 Kabinete e ananetse phatlalatso ya Bili ya Ditaolo tsa Matjhaba ho tsa Bophelo bo Botle, 2013, Koranteng ya Mmuso bakeng sa hore setjhaba se tshwaele ka yona.

src: The Bill seeks to repeal the International Health Regulations Act, 1974 (Act No.
tgt: Bili e habile ho hlakola Molao wa Ditaolo tsa Matjhaba ho tsa Bophelo bo Botle, 1974 (Molao wa 28 wa 1974) esita le ho kenyeletsa Ditaolo tsa Matjhaba ho tsa Bophelo bo Botle, 2005, ketsong ya melao ya naha.

src: 28 of 1974) as well as to incorporate the International Health Regulations, 2005 into national legislation.
tgt: Ditaolo tsa Matjhaba ho tsa Bophelo bo Botle (2005) ke molao wa matjhaba o thusang dinaha ho sebedisana e le ho pholosa maphelo le boiphediso kgahlanong le diketsahalo tse bakwang ke ho phasalla ha malwetse le dikotsi tse ding tsa bophelo bo botle matjhabeng.5 Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha Bili ya Sehlomathiso sa Meriana le Meriana e Meng e Jwalo ka Yona, 2012, Palamenteng.

src: The International Health regulations (2005) is international law which helps countries collaborate to save lives and livelihoods from events caused by the international spread of diseases and other health risks.5 Cabinet approved the introduction of the Medicines and Related Substances Amendment Bill, 2012 to Parliament.
tgt: Bili ya Sehlomathiso e hlomathisa Molao wa Meriana le Meriana e Meng e Jwalo ka Yona, 1965 (Molao wa 101 wa 1965) jwaloka ha o hlomathisitswe ke Molao wa 72 wa 2008.Phihlello merianeng ya boleng, e fihlellehang ebile e bolokehile mmoho le disebediswa tse thusang ho ntlafatsa bophelo bo botle ke tshiya ya bohlokwa bophelong bo botle ba setjhaba, mme e thusa ka ho kenya letsoho phihlellong ya maikemisetso a Mmuso a ho eketsa tebello ya ho phela halelele ha maAforika Borwa.6 Kabinete e ananetse ho phatlalatswa ha Bili ya Taolo ya Thekiso ya Dino tse Tahang, 2013, Koranteng ya Mmuso bakeng sa hore setjhaba se tshwaele ka yona.

src: Access to quality, affordable and safe medicines and medical devices is a critical pillar of public health and contributes to the attainment of Government’s goal of increasing the life expectancy of South Africans.6 Cabinet approved the publication of the Control of Marketing of Alcoholic Beverages Bill, 2013 in the Government Gazette for public comment.
tgt: Leha e le hore mmuso o ke ke wa kwala thekiso ya jwala, o boela o ke ke wa dumella kgothaletso ya ho nowa ha jwala ka ho dumella setjhaba, haholoholo batjha, ho dumela hore maphelo a bona a ka ntlafala haele hore bonneteng ho tla ba le ditlamorao tse mpe ho ba bangata.

src: Alcohol is a major impediment to reaching government’s outcome of a long and healthy life for all.
tgt: Ho kena dipakeng hona ha ho a tlameha ho bonwa e le pudumo ya seemanosi, empa e le karolo ya mekgwa e momahantsweng ke mmuso ho fokotsa thefuleho e amanang le jwala.

src: The Bill seeks to reduce alcohol related harm through control of marketing of alcoholic beverages.
tgt: Ho tla tshwarwa pontshano e reretsweng ho qhaqholla Bili.7 Kabinete e ananetse ho phatlalatswa ha Dibili tse pedi, tseo ka bobedi ba tsona di hlomathisang Molao wa Bana, 2005 (Molao wa 38 wa 2005) jwaloka ha o hlomathisitswe ke Molao wa 41 wa 2007 ho ya ka Karolo ya 75 ya Molaotheo le Karolo ya 76, hore setjhaba se tshwaele ka tsona.

src: While government cannot ban alcohol it also cannot ethically permit encouragement of alcohol consumption by allowing the public and especially the youth to believe that their life will be enhanced when in fact for many it will have the opposite impact.
tgt: Bili e habile ho kenya tlhaloso ya tlolo ya molao ya motabo ho netefatsa hore motho ofe kapa ofe ya tshwaretsweng tlolo efe kapa efe ya molao ya motabo jwaloka ha e hlalositswe Sehlomathisong sa Molao wa Ditlolo tsa Molao (Ditlolo tsa Molao tsa Motabo le dintho tse Amanang le tsona), wa 32 wa 2007, o nkuwa a sa tshwaneleha ho sebetsa le bana.

src: This intervention should not be seen in isolation but as part of comprehensive measures by government to reduce alcohol-related harm.
tgt: Bili e boetse e amanya Molao le kahlolo ya Lekgotla la Molaotheo e le ho fana ka tjhebobotjha ya molao ya qeto ya ho tlosa le ho bea ngwana tlhokomelong e bolokehileng ya nakwana ho le teng kapa ho le siyo taelo ya lekgotla la dinyewe ka nakwana e totobaditsweng.

src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment.
tgt: 10 Oct Maemo a Kabinete mabapi le dintlha tsa bohlokwa maemong a ha jwale.

src: Cabinet welcomes President Jacob Zuma’s signing into law the Transport Laws and Related Matters Amendment Bill as well as the Supreme Court of Appeal’s dismissal of an appeal by the Opposition to Urban Tolling Alliance (Outa) in its e-toll challenge against the South African National Roads Agency Limited (Sanral).Cabinet believes these developments now allow the people of Gauteng and South Africans in general to focus on the benefits we have already gained - and still stand to gain - from improvements to the freeways in the economic hub of South and Southern Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho tekenwa ha Bili ya Tlhomathiso ya Melao ya Dipalangwang le Dintho tse Amanang le Yona hore e be molaong, esita le ho qhalwa ha maipiletso a e-toll (tefiso ya tshebediso ya mebila) a Setlamo se Hanyetsanang le Tefiso ya Tshebediso ya Mebila Ditoropong (Outa) kgahlanong le Eijensi ya Mebila ya Naha ya Aforika Borwa (Sanral) ho entsweng ke Lekgotla le Phahameng la Maipiletso.

src: The e-tolling system is one aspect of the Gauteng Freeway Improvement Project which has enhanced the movement of people and goods and will make the provincial and national economy more efficient into the future.
tgt: Kabinete e kgolwa hore jwale dikgatelopele tsena di dumella batho ba Gauteng le maAforika Borwa ka kakaretso ho tsepamiso maikutlo melemong eo re seng re e fumane – esita le eo re leng boemong ba ho e fumana – dintlafalong tsa mebila e meholo kgubung ya moruo wa Aforika Borwa le Aforika e ka Borwa.

src: E-toll tariffs have been reduced in response to public comment poor passengers have been taken care of through the exemption of public transport operators from paying toll fees a monthly payment cap has been introduced, and a rebate system exists for transport companies.
tgt: Mokgwa wa tefiso mebileng ke ntho e le nngwe ya Projeke ya Ntlafatso ya Mebila e Meholo Gauteng e nolofaditseng ho tsamaya ha batho le thepa mme e tla etsa hore moruo wa porofense le wa naha o sebetse hantle kamoso.

src: Cabinet calls on users of Gauteng’s freeways to abide by the law, demonstrate good citizenship and make their contribution to a better South Africa by registering for e-tags and paying for use of these world-class roads.
tgt: Ditefiso tsa mebileng di fokoditswe ka lebaka la ditshwaelo tse entsweng ke setjhaba bapalami bao e leng bafutsana ba nketswe hloohong ka hore beng ba dipalangwang tsa setjhaba ba teelwe ka thoko ditefisong tsa mebileng sekepele sa tefiso ya kgwedi le kgwedi se se se entswe, mme ho teng mokgwa wa phokoletso bakeng sa dikhamphane tsa dipalangwang.

src: Cabinet urges South Africans to pull together and work together to make the Gauteng Freeway Improvement Project a success and to appreciate the remarkable growth of modern infrastructure in the country.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho basebedisi ba mebila e meholo ya Gauteng ho ikamahanya le molao, ho bontsha moya o motle wa boahi le ho kenya letsoho ntlafatsong ya Aforika Borwa ka ho ingodisetsa ditekete tsa boitsebahatso mme ba lefelle tshebediso ya mebila ena ya maemo a hodimo.

src: Cabinet urges all the motorists who frequently use the Gauteng freeways to register on the system and purchase their e-tag so as to enjoy the discounted tariffs.2 Cabinet applauds the continued rollout, under President Jacob Zuma’s leadership, of the multitrillion-rand public infrastructure programme, which includes the recent launch of the R71 and R81 to connect Polokwane to the town of Giyani and the opening of Bridge City and Rail Link project in KwaZulu-Natal on the 19 October 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e kopa maAforika Borwa ho hulela hlakoreng le le leng esita le ho sebetsa mmoho ho etsa hore Projeke ya Ntlafatso ya Mebila e Meholo Gauteng e be katleho, mme ba tsebe ho leboha kgolo e babatsehang ya kaho ya meralo ya motheo ya sejwalejwale naheng.

src: An integrated road network is the key factor in attracting investment into the country and the WEBTOKEN we modernise roads around the country, Cabinet calls on all users to exercise caution when using the roads.
tgt: Letona la Dipalangwang le tla etsa tsebiso ka letsatsi leo tefiso ya mebileng e tla qala ka lona.

src: Cabinet is concerned about the increase in incidents involving pedestrians on highways.
tgt: Kabinete e kopa beng ba makoloi bohle ba sebedisang mebila e meholo ya Gauteng kgafetsa ho ingodisa tsamaisong esita le ho reka ditekete tsa boitsebahatso ho etsetsa hore ba be boemong bo botle ba ho fumana ditheolelo.

src: Cabinet applauds the continued achievements of the Partnership against HIV and AIDS, which celebrated its 15th anniversary on 9 October 2013.South Africa is currently implementing the largest antiretroviral treatment programme in the world.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa ohle ho ba le seabo Bekeng ya Tsepamiso ya Maikutlo ya Imbizo eo ha jwale e tswelang pele, ho fihlela ka la 13 Mphalane 2013.

src: President Jacob Zuma will receive President Francois Hollande of the Republic of France for a State Visit at the Union Buildings from 14 to 15 October 2013.The State Visit will deepen our bilateral political and economic relations with France strengthen North-South cooperation as well as further our African Agenda.
tgt: Kabinete e rorisa dikatleho tse ntseng di tswelapele tsa Selekane se kgahlanong le HIV le AIDS, se ketekileng sehopotso sa bo 15 ka la 9 Mphalane 2013.Ha jwale Aforika Borwa e kenya tshebetsong lenaneo le leholohadi lefatsheng la kalafo ya diantiretrovaerale.

src: The ICN Cartel Workshop enables an exchange of views and networking on issues relating to cartels among its participating members and Non-Governmental Agencies around the world.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa moya oo ditherisano tsa meputso di neng di tshwerwe tsa ba tsa phethelwa ka wona makaleng ao a amehileng, moo ditharollo tsa kutlwisisano ebile e le tsa ka potlako di ileng tsa fihlellwa.

src: Bills.1 Cabinet approved the publication of the Draft Extension of Security of Tenure Amendment Bill for public comment.
tgt: Dipuisano le diqeto tsa bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.1 Kabinete e ananetse Melawana ya Setekhinikale ya ho Fuputsa le ho Honya Peteroliamo e tla phatlalatswa koranteng ya Mmuso bakeng sa ditshwaelo.2 Kabinete e ananetse ho tshwarwa ha Wekshopo ya Setlamo sa Neanotaba ya Tlhodisano ya Matjhaba (ICN) ke Khomishene ya Tlhodisano ya Aforika Borwa ho tloha ka la 16 ho ya ho la 18 Mphalane, Motsekapa.

src: The Amendment Bill amends the Extension of Security of Tenure Act, 1997 (Act No 62 of 1997) in order to strengthen, clarify and protect the tenure rights of occupiers (farm dwellers).The Bill aims to find a sustainable solution to tenure insecurities by combining land redistribution measures with effective legal protection and dispute resolution mechanisms.
tgt: Wekshopo ya Setlamo ya ICN e thusa ka phapanyetsano ya maikutlo le neanotaba dinthong tse amanang le ditlamo hara ditho tsa yona tse nkang seabo le Dieijensi tseo e Seng tsa Mmuso lefatshe ka bophara.3 Kabinete e ile ya bewa sehlohlolong sa ditaba ka kgatelopele e entsweng kotareng ya pele ya 2013/14 ka Selekane sa Kgiro ya Batjha se tekennweng ka la 18 Mmesa 2013.Dintho tse tsheletseng tse ka sehloohong tsa Selekane sena ke (1) thuto le thupelo, (2) malebela a mosebetsi, (3) mekgatlo ya batjha, (4) pehelo ya batjha e teetsweng ka thoko, (5) bohwebi le dikoporasi tsa batjha esita le (6) dikgato tse nkwang ke lekala la poraefete.

src: The Bill seeks to improve the rights of farm workers and dwellers.
tgt: Katleho e kgolokgolo bakeng sa kotare ya pele e fupere tlhahlobo ya sethathong ya dibuka tsa ditjhelete ya diketsahalo le dikgato tsa batjha tse nkilweng ho phunyeletsa le naha yohle esita le kgato enngwe e nkuwang lekaleng la poraefete.

src: Secondary farm dwellers are mostly women and children.2 Cabinet approved the publication of the Draft Amendment Bill of the Mine Health and Safety Act, 2013 in the Government Gazette, for public comments.
tgt: Dibili.1 Kabinete e ananetse ho phatlalatswa ha Moralo wa Bili ya Tlhomathiso ya wa Katoloso ya Netefaletso ya Bodudi bakeng sa hore setjhaba se tshwaele.

src: The Bill seeks to amend the Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996 so as to review the enforcement provisions, simplify the fine system and strengthen WEBTOKEN improving the health and safety of mine employees, the Draft Amendment Bill also seeks to maintain a healthy and safe mine environment with a positive impact on environmental sustainability and resilience in line with the National Development Plan.
tgt: Bili ya Tlhomathiso e fetola Molao wa Katoloso ya Netefaletso ya Bodudi, 1997, (Molao wa 62 wa 1997) ho matlafatsa, ho hlakisa le ho tshireletsa ditokelo tsa bodudi tsa ba dulang sebakeng seo (badudi ba mapolasing).Sepheo sa Bili ke ho fumana tharollo ya nako e telele ditlhokehong tsa tshireletso ya bodudi ka ho kopanya mekgwa ya kabobotjha ya mobu le tshireletso ya molao, esita le mekgwa ya tharollo ya dikgohlano.

src: Cabinet held its ordinary meeting in Cape Town on 23 October Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment.1 Cabinet welcomed the progress we are seeing in the country’s public infrastructure roll-out campaign coordinated by the Presidential Infrastructure Coordinating Commission.
tgt: 24 Oct 2013Kabinete e ile ya tshwara kopano ya yona e tlwaelehileng Motse Kapa ka la 23 Mphalane Maemo a Kabinete mabapi le dintlha tsa bohlokwa maemong a ha jwale.

src: President Jacob Zuma recently launched a number of completed projects as part of the Infrastructure Development programme.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse kgatelopele eo re e bonang letsholong la kaho ya meralo ya motheo ya setjhaba e hlophiswang ke Khomishene ya Moporesidente ya Tlhophiso ya Meralo ya Motheo (PICC).

src: These include work on the R81 and R71 roads in Limpopo, the Bridge City train station that will service Umlazi in Durban and the sod-turning ceremony at De Beers’ Venetia Mine in Vhembe, Limpopo.
tgt: Tsena di akga mosebetsi o entsweng mebileng ya R81 le R71 Limpopo, seteishene sa terene sa Bridge City se tla thusa batho ba Umlazi, Durban, esita le mokete wa setletle o neng o le Morafong wa De Beers wa Venetia o Vhembe, Limpopo.

src: The President is also due to launch other infrastructure programmes such as the Saldanha Bay Industrial Development Zone (IDZ) in the Western Cape pay a site visit to the De Hoop Dam, Limpopo, launch the first automotive wagons built in South Africa in the Eastern Cape, and officially open the Ladybrand Hospital in the Free State.
tgt: Moporesidente o boetse o mathuleng a ho kgakola mananeo a mang a meralo ya motheo a kang Lebatowa la Ntshetsopele ya Diindasteri le Koung ya Saldanha (IDZ) Kapa Bophirima ho etela setsha sa Letamo la De Hoop, Limpopo, ho kgakola makoloi a pele a entsweng Aforika Borwa kwana Kapa Botjhabela, le ho bula semmuso Sepetlele sa Ladybrand Foreistata.

src: Cabinet also welcomed the progress on the Johannesburg, Tshwane, Cape Town and Rustenburg Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) systems.
tgt: Kabinete e boetse ya amohela kgatelopele ya mekgwatsamaiso ya Dipalangwang tsa Dibese tse Potlakang (BRT) Johannesburg, Tshwane le Rusternburg.

src: This countrywide multi-trillion rand infrastructure programme is reshaping the economy and the transport system in our country.
tgt: Lenaneo lena la meralo ya motheo la diterilioneterilione tsa diranta le bopa botjha moruo le mokgwatsamaiso wa dipalangwang naheng ya rona.

src: These projects have had the effect of poising the economy for a higher growth trajectory and will continue to contribute to economic development and job creation.2 Cabinet welcomes the Medium Term Budget Policy Statement presented by the Minister of Finance.
tgt: Diprojeke tsena di bile le sephetho sa ho bea moruo motjheng wa kgolo e hodimo mme di tla tswelapele ho kenya letsoho ntshetsopeleng ya moruo le tlhahisong ya mesebetsi.2 Kabinete e amohela Pehelo ya Leano la Ditekanyetso tsa Nako e Bohareng e takilweng ke Letona la tsa Ditjhelete.

src: Cabinet supports the austerity measures propose for government.
tgt: Kabinete e tshehetsa mehato e matla ya tokiso e sisintsweng bakeng sa mmuso.

src: These measures will go a long way in reducing any wastage in government spending.
tgt: Mehato ena e tla thusa ka nako e telele phokotsehong ya tshenyo efe kapa efe tshebedisong ya tjhelete ya mmuso.

src: Such measures will ensure that government uses its resources effectively and efficiently.
tgt: Mehato eo e tla netefatsa hore mmuso o sebedisa disebediswa tsa wona ka bokgabane.

src: Cabinet calls on all national and provincial departments, municipalities, public entities and constitutional institutions to implement these measures.3 Cabinet joined President Jacob Zuma and the South African public in condemning abuse, violence and neglect against children.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho mafapha ohle a naha le a diporofense, bomasepala, ditheo tsa setjhaba le ditheo tsa molaotheo ho kenya mehato ena tshebetsong.3 Kabinete e ikamahantse le Moporesidente Jacob Zuma mmoho le setjhaba sa Aforika Borwa ho seolleng tlhekefetso, dikgoka le ho se tsotelle bana.

src: Cabinet commended the law enforcement agencies for their swift action in recently reported WEBTOKEN we mark National Children’s Day on 2 November, Cabinet urges all South Africans to protect children as they are our future leaders.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholeditse sepolesa ka mekgahlelo ya sona ka ho nka dikgato tse potlakileng ditlolong tsa molao tse sa tswa tlalehwa haufinyane.

src: Cabinet also calls on communities to continue to work with law enforcement agencies in fighting crime within communities.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e etsa kgoeletso setjhabeng ho tswelapele ho sebedisana le sepolesa twantshong ya ditlolo tsa molao kahara WEBTOKEN tshwanela le ho ba sedi ka taba ya hore tshireletso ya bana ke boikarabelo ba batswadi le setjhaba.

src: We should offer assistance to mothers who needs help to raise their children.4 Cabinet welcomed the announcement by Umalusi that the country is ready for the National Senior Certificate examinations from 28 October to 29 November 2013.
tgt: Re tshwanela ho thusa bomme ba hlokang thuso ya ho hodisa bana ba bona.4 Kabinete e amohetse tsebiso e entsweng ke Umalusi ya hore naha ke malalaalaotswe bakeng sa ditlhahlobo tsa Materiki ho tloha ka la 28 Mphalane ho sia ho la 29 Pudungwana 2013.

src: Cabinet wishes all 707 136 candidates, including 130 000 part-time learners, well in their examinations.
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa baithuti bohle ba 707 136, ho akga le baithuti ba nakwana ba 130 000, katleho ditlhahlobong tsa bona.

src: Parents and guardians are urged to support their children as they prepare for their examinations.
tgt: Batswadi le bahlokomedi ba kopjwa ho tshehetsa bana ba bona jwaloka ha ba ntse ba itlhophisetsa ditlhahlobo.

src: Cabinet calls on the Class of 2013 to make the country proud.5 Cabinet welcomed the launch of Fetsa Tlala (End Hunger) food security programme by President Jacob Zuma in Kuruman in Northern Cape on 24 October 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho Sehlopha sa 2013 ho etsa naha hore e be motlotlo.5 Kabinete e ananetse ho kgakolwa, ke Moporesidente, ha lenaneo la tshireletso ya dijo la Fetsa Tlala Kuruman Kapa Leboya ka la 24 Mphalane 2013.

src: The programme will assist communities to produce food on communal and other under-utilised land.
tgt: Lenaneo le tla thusa setjhaba ho hlahisa dijo mobung wa setjhaba esita le o mong o sa sebedisweng hakaalo.

src: It will support smallholder farmers with infrastructure, development of agro-processing and the development of new markets, including state procurement.6 Cabinet welcomes the inaugural African Maritime Indaba which will take place in Sandton, Johannesburg, on 24 and 25 October 2013.
tgt: E tla tshehetsa borapolasi ba banyenyane ka meralo ya motheo, kaho ya disebediswa tsa tlhahiso ya dihlahiswa tsa temo esita le kaho ya mebaraka e metjha, ho akga le phumantsho ya mmuso.6 Kabinete e ananela ho hlomamiswa ha Indaba ya Mawatleng a Aforika e tla ba Sandton, Johannesburg, ka la 24 le 25 Mphalane 2013.

src: The Indaba will be hosted by the South African Maritime Safety Authority and the maritime industry.
tgt: Indaba e tla be e tshwerwe ke Lekgotla la Polokeho ya Mawatleng la Aforika Borwa esita le indasteri ya mawatleng.

src: The conference will provide a platform for various role-players to craft a development path for Africa’s maritime industries and establish a Pan-African Partnership for the development of Africa’s blue economy.7 Cabinet noted the coming State Visit by President Zuma to the Democratic Republic of Congo on October 29 and 30 2013.
tgt: Seboka se tla fana ka lepatlelo bakeng sa banka karolo ba fapafapaneng ho kutla tsela ya ntshetsopele bakeng sa diindasteri tsa mawatleng a Aforika se be se thee Selekane sa Dinaha Tsohle tsa Aforika bakeng sa kaho ya moruo o tswetseng pele wa Aforika.7 Kabinete e tsebile ka Ketelo ya ho Emela Naha ya Moporesidente Zuma ya ho ya Rephaboliki ya Demokrasing ya Congo (DRC) ka la 29 le la 30 Mphalane 2013.

src: The visit will strengthen our bilateral political and economic relations with the DRC and further enhance our commitment to peacekeeping efforts and the Post-Conflict Reconstruction and Development (PCRD) programme in that country.8 Cabinet calls on all South Africans to support National Disability Rights Awareness Month from 3 November to 3 December 2013, which also marks International Day of Persons with Disabilities.
tgt: Ketelo e tla matlafatsa maemo a rona a sepolotiki sa naha tse pedi le dikamano tsa moruo le DRC, ho feta moo e ntlafatse boikitlaetso ba rona ba matsapa a ho boloka kgotso esita le lenaneo la Kahobotjha le Ntshetsopele Kamora Dikgohlano (PCRD) naheng eo.8 Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa ohle ho tshehetsa Kgwedi ya Naha ya Tlhokomediso ya Ditokelo tsa ba Holofetseng ho tloha ka la 3 Pudungwana ho ya ho la 3 Tshitwe, e boelang e ba Letsatsi la Matjhabatjhaba la Batho ba Holofetseng.

src: The month will be celebrated under the theme: “Break barriers, open doors: for an inclusive society for all”.9 Cabinet noted with concern the resurgence of violence and hostilities in the Republic of Mozambique.
tgt: Kgwedi e tla ketekwa tlasa mookotaba o reng: “Tlosa ditshita, bula menyetla: bakeng sa setjhaba se kenyeletsang bohle”.9 Kabinete e tsebile ya ba ya ngongorehiswa ke tsosoloso ya merusu le dikgoka Rephaboliking ya Mozambique.

src: Cabinet wishes to underscore that Mozambique has a legitimate government and that any insurgency undermines the sovereignty of the Mozambican government and its people.
tgt: Kabinete e batla ho thasisetsa hore Mozambique e na le mmuso o molaong mme ho tsohela matla hofe kapa hofe ho nyatsa boipuiso ba mmuso wa Mozambique le batho ba yona.

src: Key Cabinet discussions and decisions.1 Cabinet approved the ratification of the Doha Amendment to the Kyoto Protocol.
tgt: Kabinete e seolla kahohlehohle ditlhaselo tsa ho tsohela mmuso matla.2 Dipuisano le diqeto tsa bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.1 Kabinete e ananetse kamohelo ya Sehlomathiso sa Doha ho Porothokhole ya Kyoto.

src: These amendments form part of the 2013-2020 global gas emission reduction efforts that set out to avert dangerous climate change while protecting the developmental priorities of developing countries.2 Cabinet approved that South Africa’s Combined Initial and Periodic Reports under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights be submitted to the United Nations.
tgt: Dihlomathiso tsena di bopa karolo ya matsapa a phokotso ya ho kunkela ha gase lefatsheng a reretsweng ho thibela phetoho e kotsi ya tlelaemete ha ka ho le leng di tshireletsa dintho tse ka sehloohong tsa ntshetsopele dinaheng tse ntseng di thuthua.2 Kabinete e ananetse hore Ditlaleho tsa Sethathong tse Kopantsweng tsa ba tsa Hakuretswa tsa Aforika Borwa tlasa Selekane sa Matjhabatjhaba Ditokelong tsa Setjhaba le tsa Sepolotiki di fetisetswe Matjhabeng a Kopaneng.

src: The report is an evaluation of achievements and challenges associated with giving effect to civil and political rights contained in the Covenant and our Constitution.
tgt: Tlaleho ke tshekatsheko ya dikatleho le diphephetso tse amanang le ho fanwa ha sephetho ditokelong tsa setjhaba le tsa sepolotiki tse fuperweng ke Selekane esita le Molaotheo wa rona.

src: It has a particular focus on human dignity and the right to equality since the dawn of democracy in Bills.1 Cabinet approved publication of the draft Promotion and Protection of Investment Bill, 2013 for public comments.
tgt: E tsepamisitse maikutlo seriting sa botho le tokelo ya tekano haesale ho tloha qalong ya demokrasi ka 1994.3 Dibili.1 Kabinete e ananetse ho phatlalatswa ha moralo wa Bili ya Kgothaletso le Tshireletso ya Matsete, ya 2013, bakeng sa ditshwaelo tsa setjhaba.

src: The bill provides a legal framework for investments and addresses the legal protection of all investors in line with Constitutional requirements.
tgt: Bili e fana ka moralo wa molao bakeng sa matsete ebile e bua ka tshireletso ya molao ya boramatsete bohle ho ya ka ditlhoko tsa Molaotheo.

src: The envisioned Act will enhance our ability to attract foreign investment and export growth to promote sustainable growth and development in South Africa.
tgt: Molao o lohothwang o tla ntlafatsa bokgoni ba rona ba ho hohela matsete a tswang kantle esita le kgolo ya diyantle le ho kgothaletsa kgolo ya nako e telele ya ntshetsopele Aforika Borwa.

src: The draft Bill therefore seeks to achieve several balances between the rights and obligations of all investors in South Africa, the need to provide adequate and equal protection of foreign and domestic investors.2 Cabinet approved the introduction of the Rental Housing Amendment Bill, 2013 to Parliament.
tgt: Moralo wa Bili, kahoo, o habile ho fihlella botsitso bo itseng dipakeng tsa ditokelo le ditlamo tsa boramatsete bohle Aforika Borwa, tlhokeho ya ho fana ka tshireletso e lekaneng ebile e le e lekanang ya boramatsete ba tswang kantle ho naha esita le ba lapeng.2 Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha Bili ya Sehlomathiso ya ho Rentwa ha Matlo Palamenteng.

src: The Bill addresses certain interpretation and implementation issues which surfaced since the promulgation of the Rental Housing Act, 1999 (Act No.
tgt: Bili e rarolla dintho tse ding tsa ho hlakisa le ho kenya tshebetsong tse ropohileng haesale ho tloha ka tsebiso ya Molao wa ho Rentwa ha Matlo, wa 1999 (Molao wa Nomoro ya 50 wa 1999) (jwaloka ha o hlomathisitswe ka 2008).

src: The legislation aims to promote a stable and growing market which progressively meets the latent demand for affordable rental housing amongst persons historically disadvantaged by unfair discrimination.3 Cabinet approved the introduction of the Attorney’s Amendment Bill, 2013 to Parliament.
tgt: Sepheo sa ketso ya molao ke ho kgothaletsa mmaraka o tsitsitseng o bile o hola mme o kgahlanyetsana le tlhokeho e kubutehileng ya matlo a fihlellehang a rentwang bathong ba neng ba kotetswe ke kgethollo e leeme.3 Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha Bili ya Sehlomathiso Bontamolane, ya 2013, Palamenteng.

src: The Bill amends the Attorneys Act, 1979 (Act 53 of 1979), as an interim measure, pending the enactment and implementation of the Legal Practice Bill.
tgt: Bili e hlomathisa Molao wa Bontamolane wa 1979 (Molao wa 53 wa 1979), e le mohato wa nakwana, ho emetswe ho tekwa le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Bili ya Tshebetso ya Molao.

src: It addresses disparities in relation to attorneys and candidate attorneys and also does away with law societies created in terms of jurisdictional boundaries of the defunct homeland system (Transkei, Bophuthatswana, Ciskei and Venda).
tgt: E rarolla ho se lekane ho amanang le bontamolane esita le bomaithutwana ba bontamolane ebile e nyahlatsa mekgatlo ya tsa molao e theilweng ho ya ka meedi ya boahlodi mokgwatsamaiso wa mahae a seng a fedisitswe (Transkei, Bophuthatswana, Ciskei le Venda).

src: The amendments will ensure the uniform regulation of the attorneys’ profession throughout the country and will strengthen governance of the legal profession in the mentioned areas.4 Cabinet approved the introduction of the State Attorney Amendment Bill, 2013 to Parliament.
tgt: Dihlomathiso di tla netefatsa boteng ba taolo e tshwanang ya porofeshene ya bontamolane naha ka bophara ebile di tla matlafatsa taolo ya porofeshene ya tsa molao dibakeng tse phanyaotsweng.4 Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha Bili ya Sehlomathiso Ntamolane e Moholo wa Mmuso, ya 2013 Palamenteng.

src: The aim of the Bill is to amend the State Attorney Act, 1957 (Act 56 of 1957).
tgt: Sepheo sa Bili ke ho hlomathisa Molao wa Ntamolane e Moholo wa Mmuso, wa 1957 (Molao wa 56 wa 1957).

src: The amendments provide strategic leadership for the management of and oversight over State Legal Services.
tgt: Dihlomathiso di fana ka lewa la boetapele bakeng sa bookamedi le tekolo tsa Ditshebeletso tsa Molao tsa Mmuso.

src: It aims to facilitate the appointment of a Solicitor-General who will be in charge of all the State Attorneys and provide for related matters, as an initial step in the implementation of the Policy Framework for the Transformation of State Legal Services.5 Cabinet approved the submission of the Draft Property Valuation Bill, 2013 to Parliament.
tgt: Sepheo sa Bili ke ho nolofatsa ho thonngwa ha Ntamolane-Kakaretso ya tla tshwara Bontamolane bohle ba Mmuso a be a fane ka dintho tse amanang le hoo, e le kgato ya pele ho kenngweng tshebetsong ha Moralo wa Leano bakeng sa Phetoho ya Ditshebeletso tsa Molao tsa Mmuso.5 Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha moralo wa Bili ya Tekolo ya Boleng ba Thepa ya 2013 Palamenteng.

src: The Bill makes provision for the establishment of a Valuer-General’s Office.
tgt: Bili e hlekela ho thewa ha Kantoro ya Molekodi-Kakaretso wa Thepa.

src: This office will provide a valuation service for property that has been identified for expropriation and land reform purposes, as well as voluntary property valuation service to departments that may request the office to perform such valuations.6 Cabinet approved the revised draft of the Infrastructure Development Bill to Parliament.
tgt: Kantoro ena e tla fana ka tshebeletso ya tekolo ya boleng bakeng sa thepa e hlwaetsweng mabaka a kamoho ya thepa molemong wa setjhaba le kabobotjha ya mobu, esita le tshebeletso ya boithaopo ya tekolo ya boleng ba thepa mafapheng a ka nnang a kopa kantoro ho etsa ditekolo tse jwalo tsa boleng.6 Kabinete e ananetse ho shejwa botjha ha moralo wa Bili ya Kaho ya Meralo ya Motheo Palamenteng.

src: The Bill establishes in law the Presidential Infrastructure Coordinating commission (PICC) and the National Infrastructure Plan as key mechanisms to coordinate and drive infrastructure development in South Africa.
tgt: Bili e thea ka ho ya ka molao, PICC le Morero wa Naha wa Meralo ya Motheo e le mekgwa ya bohlokwa ho hlophisa le ho sututsa kaho ya meralo ya motheo Aforika Borwa.

src: The Infrastructure Development Bill provides a legal framework for the build programme and helps improve its developmental outcomes and effectiveness.7 Cabinet approved the Draft Women Empowerment and Gender Equality Bill, 2013 for tabling in Parliament.
tgt: Bili ya Kaho ya Meralo ya Motheo e fana ka moralo wa molao bakeng sa lenaneo la kaho ebile e thusa ho ntlafatsa diphetho tsa yona tsa ntshetsopele le ho sebetsa ka bokgabane.7 Kabinete e ananetse moralo wa Bili ya Matlafatso ya Basadi le Tekano ya Bong, 2013, bakeng sa hore o hlahiswe Palamenteng.

src: The Bill seeks to establish a legislative framework for the values of non-racialism, non-sexism and equality as contemplated in the Constitution.
tgt: Bili e habile ho thea moralo wa ketso ya molao bakeng sa boleng bo sa kgetholleng mmala, bo sa kgetholleng bong mme e le ba tekano jwaloka ha ho thasiseditswe ho Molaotheo.

src: It also seeks to promote the empowerment of women, their equal representation in decision-making structures and their protection and advancement as envisaged in Section9 (2) of the Constitution.8 Cabinet approved the submission of the Public Administration Management Bill, 2013 to Parliament.
tgt: E boetse e habile ho kgothaletsa matlafatso ya basadi, boemedi ba bona bo lekanang ditheong tsa ketso ya diqeto esita le tshireletso ya bona jwaloka ha ho utollwa ho Karolo ya 9 (2) ya Molaotheo.8 Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha Bili ya Bolaodi ba Tsamaiso ya Setjhaba ya 2013, Palamenteng.

src: The Bill is the framework that seeks to provide for the promotion of basic values and principles referred to in section 195(1) of the Constitution in the public administration provide for the transfer and secondment of employees in public administration regulate the prohibition of employees to conduct business with the state provide for ethics and integrity measures which includes the establishment of a Public Administration Ethics, Integrity and Disciplinary Technical Assistance Unit.
tgt: Bili ke moralo o habileng ho fana ka kgothaletso ya boleng ba mantlha le mekgwatsamaiso eo ho buuwang ka yona karolong ya 195 (1) ya Molaotheo tsamaisong ya setjhaba ho lokisetsa phetiso ho ya mafapheng a mang esita le kgiro ya basebetsi tsamaisong ya setjhaba ho laola thibelo ya basebetsi hore ba se ke ba etsa kgwebo le mmuso Ho fana ka mekgwa ya boitshwaro bo botle le seriti e akgang ho thewa ha Yuniti ya Boitshwaro bo Botle, Seriti le Thuso ya Sethekgeniki ya Kgalemo Tsamaisong ya Setjhaba.

src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment.1 Cabinet welcomed the Goldman Sachs report, Two Decades of Freedom, which is a detailed account of 10 areas in which South Africa has made structural advances since 1994 and 10 areas in which the country has to take decisive action.
tgt: 07 Nov Maemo a Kabinete mabapi le dintlha tsa bohlokwa maemong a ha jwale.1 Kabinete e amohetse tlaleho ya Goldman Sachs, Dilemoshome tse Pedi tsa Tokoloho, e leng tlhakisetso e tebileng ya dibaka tse leshome tseo Aforika Borwa e entseng dikgatelopele tse bonahalang haesale ho tloha ka 1994, esita le dikarolo tse 10 moo naha e tshwanelang ho nka dikgato ho tsona.

src: The report is welcome confirmation of government’s own assessment of the performance of the country and it affirms the priorities for the future set out in the National Development Plan.
tgt: Tlaleho ena ke tiiso ya kamohelo ya boitekolo ba mmuso ba tshebetso ya naha ebile e ananela dintlha tse ka sehloohong bakeng sa bokamoso, bo tekilweng Morerong wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha.

src: The report is a source of hope and inspiration and is an important contribution to public discourse at a time when South Africa has begun celebrating 20 Years of Freedom.
tgt: Tlaleho ena ke mohlodi wa tshepo le kgothatso mme ke seabo sa bohlokwa puisanong le setjhaba ka nako ena eo Aforika Borwa e seng e qadile ho keteka Dilemo tse 20 tsa Tokoloho.

src: Government urges South Africans to work together and work hard to make South Africa even more successful and to concentrate their energies and conversations on these issues.
tgt: Mmuso o kopa maAforika Borwa ho sebetsa mmoho le ho sebetsa ka thata ho etsa hore Aforika Borwa e atlehe le ho feta, esita le ho tsepamiso maikutlo le dipuisano tsa bona mehopolong ena.2 Kabinete e ananela ho thewa ha diyunivesithi tse ntjha tse pedi Kapa Leboya le Mpumalanga, tsa pele tsa ho ahwa haesale ho thewa demokrasi.

src: The Mpumalanga University will open in January 2014.
tgt: Yunivesithi ya Mpumalanga e tla bulwa ka Pherekgong ya 2014.

src: This achievement reflects the importance government and all South Africans attach to education as part of the nation’s development.
tgt: Katleho ena e bontsha bohlokwa boo mmuso le maAforika Borwa ohle a e beang thutong e le karolo ya ntshetsopele ya naha.

src: The new campus will also make it possible for Mpumalanga students to study close to home and will generate a range of economic activities centered on servicing the university and its population.
tgt: Khamphase ena e ntjha e tla thusa baithuti ba Mpumalanga ka ho ithuta haufi le mahabo bona mme e tla hlahisa menyetla e mengatanyana ya moruo e tla be e reretswe ho sebeletsa yunivesithi le setjhaba sa yona.

src: South Africa has made great advances in providing services and new institutions to the marginalized and needy communities.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e entse dikgatelopele tse kgolo phanong ya ditshebeletso le ditheo tse ntjha setjhabeng se kotetsweng ebile e le se hlokang haholo.

src: The destruction of these institutions reverses the significant gains we have all achieved during our new democracy.3 Cabinet further welcomes the announcement that Eskom’s power plants Kusile and Medupi will deliver electricity in 2014.
tgt: Tshenyo ya ditheo tsena e kgutlisetsa morao dikatleho tsa bohlokwa tseo bohle re di fihlelletseng nakong ya demokrasi ya rona e ntjha.3 Kabinete e boela e ananela tsebiso ya hore ditsi tsa motlakase tsa Eskom, e leng Kusile le Medupi, di tla fepela motlakase ka 2014.Ho fehlwa ha motlakase ke ditsi tsa motlakase tsa Kusile le Medupi isao e tla ba katleho e kgolo ntshetsopeleng ya naha mme e tla bontsha katleho ya mmuso ya ho kenya tshebetsong lenaneo la kaho ya meralo ya motheo e meholo, e bopang botjha moruo le setjhaba sa rona.

src: The generating of electricity next year by Kusile and Medupi power plants will be another major milestone for the country’s development and will demonstrate government’s success in implementing a large-scale infrastructure development programme which is reshaping our economy and society.
tgt: Motlakase o itjarang ka nako e telele o bohlokwa bakeng sa bareki ba malapeng le ba diindasteri mme o bula menyetla bakeng sa ho hodisa moruo – e leng ntlha e bileng ka sehloohong haesale ho tloha ka 2009.

src: Sustainable energy is vital for domestic and industrial customers and opens up new possibilities for growing the economy – which has been a priority for this administration since 2009.
tgt: Ka diprojeke tse ngata hakaalo tsa mofuta ona tse ntseng di tswelapele naha ka bophara, Aforika Borwa e se e nkile dikgato tse ngatanyana tsa bohlokwa tseleng ya yona e ntjha ya kgolo, kahoo maAforika Borwa ohle a tshwanela ho keteka dikatleho tsa rona.4 Kabinete e thoholetsa ho tekenwa ha Selekane sa Projeke e Kgolo ya Inga ya Phehlo ya Motlakase, nakong ya Ketelo ya moraorao ya Mopresidente Jacob Zuma Rephaboliking ya Demokrasi ya Congo.

src: With so many projects of this kind in progress around the country, South Africa has taken a number of important steps along its new growth path, and all South Africans should celebrate our accomplishments.4 Cabinet lauds the signing of the Treaty on the Grand Inga Hydropower Project, during the recent State Visit by President Jacob Zuma to the Democratic Republic of Congo.
tgt: Projeke ena e tla atolla phihlello ya motlakase Aforika e be e fane ka menyetla e metle haholo ya temo, merafo le Makala a mang lebatoweng la Dinaha tse Tswelang pele tsa Aforika e ka Borwa (SADC).Hang ha ho se ho phethetswe mekgahlelo yohle, projeke ena e tla tlisa phepelo e ntjhafatsehang ya motlakase kontinenteng ya Aforika.

src: This project will extend energy access in Africa and present immense benefits for agriculture, mining and other sectors in the SADC region.
tgt: Projeke ena e tla qholotsa tlhahiso ya mesebetsi, ntshetsopele ya bokgoni le phetisetso ya theknoloji dinaheng tse nang le seabo mme e tla thusa basebedisi ba malapeng le ba diindasteri.

src: Cabinet encourages all South Africans, especially young and first-time voters, to exercise their democratic right by taking the first step of registering to vote on 9 and 10 November 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e hopotsa balefi ba lekgetho ba ntseng ba lokela ho kenya dipusetso tsa bona tsa lekgetho hore mohla la 22 Pudungwana 2013 ke letsatsi la ho qetela la ho kenya dipusetso ka mokgwa wa elektroniki bakeng sa pusetso ya motho ka mong ya selemo sa ditjhelete sa 2012/13, mme letsatsi leo le ntse le atamela ka potlako.7 Kabinete e tshwela ka mathe sewa sa moraorao sa merusu, tshenyo ya thepa ya poraefete le ya setjhaba esita le ho hapa thepa ka mahahapa Gauteng, Kapa Botjhabela le Kapa Bophirima.

src: Cabinet’s position on prominent issues in the current environment.
tgt: 21 Nov Maemo a Kabinete mabapi le dintlha tsa bohlokwa maemong a ha jwale.

src: Cabinet welcomes the high number of eligible voters who heeded the call to register during the initial registration period of 9 and 10 November 2013.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela lenane le leholo la bakgethi ba tshwanelehileng ba ileng ba sekehela tsebe kgoeletso ya ho ingodisa nakong ya boingodiso ba pele ba mohla la 9 le 10 Pudungwana 2013.

src: Eligible voters who have not yet registered are reminded that the period of registration continues up until the announcement of the date for the next national elections.
tgt: Bakgethi ba tshwanelehileng ba e so ka ba ingodisa ba hopotswa hore nako ya boingodiso e tswelapele ho fihlela tsebisong ya letsatsi la dikgetho tse latelang tsa naha.

src: Cabinet commends the work of the Independent Electoral Commission, and calls on all South Africans to exercise their democratic right to vote, which came about as a result of our struggle for freedom and democracy.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa mosebetsi wa Khomishene e Ikemetseng ya Dikgetho, mme e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ohle ho nka monyetla wa tokelo ya bona ya demokrasi ya ho kgetha, e bileng teng ka lebaka la ntwa ya rona ya tokoloho le demokrasi.

src: The 16 Days Activism Campaign of No Violence against Women and Children will take place from 25 November to 10 December 2013 under the theme: “VIKELA MZANSI – Kwanele: Communities united in preventing violence against women and children.”Cabinet calls on all South Africans to use this period to renew our commitment, to end brutal and dehumanising behaviour by some in our society and to recommit our country to the inalienable rights of women and children.
tgt: Letsholo la Boitseki la Matsatsi a 16 la Phediso ya Dikgoka kgahlanong le Basadi le Bana le tla qala mohla la 25 Pudungwana ho ya ho la 10 Tshitwe tlasa mookotaba o reng: VIKELA MZANSI – Kwanele: Ditjhaba di kopane ho thibela dikgoka kgahlanong le basadi le bana”.Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ohle ho sebedisa nako ena ho ntjhafatsa boikitlaetso ba rona, ho fedisa boitshwaro bo soto bo bile bo hlabisa dihlong bo etswang ke ba bang setjhabeng sa rona re be re tsosolose boitlamo ba naha ya rona ditokelong tse ke keng tsa phephetswa tsa basadi le bana.

src: Deputy President Kgalema Motlanthe will lead the World AIDS Day commemoration in Mkhondo, Gert Sibande District, Mpumalanga, on 1 December 2013 under the theme: “Get wise.
tgt: Motlatsi wa Mopresidente, Ntate Kgalema Motlanthe o tla etellapele sehopotso sa Letsatsi la Lefatshe la AIDS Mkhondo, Seterekeng sa Gert Sibande, Mpumalanga, ka la 1 Tshitwe 2013 tlasa mookotaba o reng: “Hlalefa.

src: Get tested.
tgt: Etsa diteko.

src: Get circumcised.”The platform will be used to apprise the nation on government efforts to fight the epidemic, to increase awareness, and to intensify efforts to scale up interventions to curtail the epidemic.
tgt: Pukutlwa leeko.”Lepatlelo le tla sebedisetswa ho tsebisa setjhaba ka matsapa a mmuso a ho lwantsha sewa sena, ho eketsa tlhokomediso, esita le ho tiisa matsapa a ho matlafatsa bokena dipakeng ba ho kgina sewa sena.

src: This is aligned to the National Strategic Plan for HIV and AIDS 2012-2016.This World AIDS Day will also be used to revitalise the HIV Counselling and Testing (HCT) campaign and to launch the Medical Male Circumcision campaign.
tgt: Sena se amana le Morero wa Lewa la Naha wa HIV le AIDS wa 2012-2016.Letsatsi lena la Lefatshe la AIDS le tla boela le sebediswa ho tsosolosa letsholo la Ho Thoba Maikutlo le Diteko tsa HIV (HCT) le ho thakgola letsholo la Pukutlo ya Leeko Ditsing tsa Bophelo bo Botle.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to practise safe sex to get tested for HIV at least once per year in order to make informed decisions on preventative measures, treatment, care and support and for men and boys to take up medical male circumcision services.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ohle ho etsa thobalano e bolokehileng ho etsa diteko tsa HIV bonnyane hanngwe ka selemo e le ho etsa diqeto tse susumetswang ke thuo ya lesedi ka mehato ya thibelo, kalafo, tlhokomelo le tshehetso le hore banna le bashanyana ba ikakgele ka setotswana ditshebeletsong tsa pukutlo ya leeko ditsing tsa bophelo bo botle.

src: South Africans must play their part and integrate the ABC (Abstinence, be faithful, use a condom) strategy as a way of life.
tgt: MaAforika Borwa a tlameha ho ba le seabo ba kopanye lewa la ho se Ikamahanye, ho tshepahala, ho sebedisa khondomo (ABC).

src: Cabinet highlighted the strict enforcement of traffic offences as part of the Festive Season Campaign - Arrive Alive - under the theme ‘Together We Can Save Millions of Lives’, and calls on all road users to adopt a more responsible attitude that fully understands that vehicle crashes destroy lives.
tgt: Kabinete e hlakisitse qobello e matla ya melao ya sephethephethe e le karolo ya Letsholo la Sehla sa Keteko ya Mafelo a Selemo – Arrive Alive – tlasa mookotaba o reng: ‘Mmoho re ka Boloka Dimilione tsa Maphelo’, mme e ipiletsa ho basebedisi bohle ba tsela ho ipopela tlwaelo e nang le kutlwisiso e phethahetseng ya hore ho swahlamana ha makoloi ho ruthutha maphelo.

src: Cabinet commends the progress made through the multi-agency approach which was adopted in response to the Presidential intervention in May 2013 at Eldorado Park, to tackle drug and gang violence and related socio-economic challenges.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa kgatelopele e entsweng, ka mokgwa wa dieijensi tse ngata, e ileng ya ananelwa mabapi le bokena dipakeng ba Mopresidente ka Motsheanong 2013 Eldorado Park, ho lwantsha dikgoka tse bakwang ke dithethefatsi le dihlopha tsa dinokwane esita le diphephetso tse amanang le moruo setjhabeng.

src: This has since seen the arrest of 1 431 people, of which 1 098 are awaiting trial 1 095 received bail, three are still in custody and 289 were convicted on criminal charges.
tgt: Sena se bakile ho tshwarwa ha batho ba 1 431, ba 1 098 ba bona ba emetse ho bua dinyewe ba 1 095 ba fuwe beili, ba bararo ba ntse ba kwalletswe mme ba 289 ba ile ba fumanwa ba le molato diqosong tsa ditlolo tsa molao.

src: Cabinet appeals to communities to refrain from the practice of punishing crimes or seeking justice outside of the legal system, as this is illegal and contributes to criminal behaviour.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa setjhabeng hore se tlohele ho inkela molao matsohong kapa ho ipatlela toka ka thoko ho tsamaiso ya molao, kaha sena se se molaong se bile se na le seabo boitshwarong ba ditlolo tsa molao.

src: Cabinet encourages communities to work with the police to root out drug lords and dealers who exacerbate criminal activities.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa setjhaba ho sebedisana le sepolesa ho fothola dikokonono le barekisi ba dithethefatsi ba mpefatsang diketsahalo tsa ditlolo tsa molao.

src: Cabinet expressed condolences to the family and friends of those who died as a result of the collapsed construction site in Tongaat, KwaZulu-Natal and wishes a speedy recovery to those who were injured.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisitse matshediso ho beng le metswalle ya bao ba hlokahetseng ka lebaka la ho heleha ha moaho o ntseng o ahwa setsheng se Tongaat, KwaZulu-Natal mme e lakaletsa bao ba lemetseng hore ba fole ka potlako.

src: Cabinet emphasised that there are labour laws which protect the rights of workers and condemned those responsible for the disaster.
tgt: Kabinete e thasiseditse hore ho na le melao ya tsa mesebetsi e tshireletsang ditokelo tsa basebetsi ya ba ya seolla bao ba ikarabellang koduweng eo.

src: Cabinet insisted that the matter be followed up rigorously.
tgt: Kabinete e qobelletse hore taba eo e salwe morao ka hloko.

src: Cabinet welcomed the opening of the Nelson Mandela Centre of Memory.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse ho bulwa ha Setsi sa Sehopotso sa Nelson Mandela.

src: The centre houses some of the most important heritage resources that chronicle the life and times of Tata Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela.
tgt: Setsi se bolokile tse ding tsa disebediswa tsa bohlokwahlokwa tsa letlotlo la botjhaba tse phetang ka bophelo le dinako tsa Ntate Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela.

src: These resources are an integral part of our nation’s heritage, in particular our liberation heritage.
tgt: Disebediswa tsena ke karolo ya bohlokwa ya letlotlo la botjhaba la naha ya rona.

src: They are our nation’s treasures and need to be preserved.
tgt: Ke matlotlo a naha ya rona mme a tshwanela ho bolokwa.

src: Government will continue to honour Nelson Mandela and his generation of leaders for the massive contribution they made to our liberation.
tgt: Mmuso o tla tswelapele ho tlotla Ntate Nelson Mandela le baetapele ba moloko wa hae ka seabo se seholo seo ba se entseng tokolohong ya rona.

src: Cabinet applauds the continued rollout of the multitrillion-rand public infrastructure programme by the Presidential Infrastructure Coordinating Commission led by President Jacob Zuma.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa kaho ya lenaneo la meralo ya motheo ya setjhaba ya diterilione tsa diranta e etswang ke Khomishene ya Tlhophiso ya Meralo ya Motheo ya Mopresidente e etelletsweng pele ke Mopresidente Jacob Zuma.

src: The opening of Spring Grove Dam by the President is designed to contribute to expanding water supply to six municipalities, namely eThekwini Metropolitan, uMgungundlovu District, Msunduzi Local, Ugu Local, and Sisonke and iLembe Local Municipalities.
tgt: Pulo ya Letamo la Spring Grove ka Mopresidente e raletswe ho thusa phepelong e ntseng e ata ya metsi ho ya bomasepaleng ba tsheletseng, e leng Toropokgolo ya eThekwini, Setereke sa uMgungundlovu, Masepala wa Sebaka sa Mmeunduzi, wa Sebaka sa Ugu, esita le Bomasepala ba Dibaka tsa Sisonke le iLembe.

src: Government has invested more than R1 billion in the project, which is also designed to create jobs.
tgt: Mmuso o tsetetse tjhelete e fetang bilione e le nngwe ya diranta projekeng, e boelang e reretswe ho thea mesebetsi.

src: During construction of the dam a total of 960 people were employed.
tgt: Nakong ya kaho ya letamo, ke batho ba 960 ba ileng ba hirwa.

src: President Jacob Zuma will visit King Sabatha Dalindyebo Municipality, Eastern Cape Province, on 22 November 2013 as part of the Siyahlola Presidential Monitoring Programme.
tgt: Mopresidente Jacob Zuma o tla etela Masepala wa King Sabata Dalindyebo, Profenseng ya Kapa Botjhabela, ka la 22 Pudungwana 2013 e le karolo ya Lenaneo la Bodisa la Mopresidente la Siyahlola.

src: This will include a visit to Mthatha to assess the airport improvements and other presidential infrastructure projects in the area.
tgt: Sena se tla akga le ketelo Mthatha ho ya lekola dintlafatso tsa boemafofane le diprojeke tse ding tsa meralo ya motheo ya mopresidente tikolohong eo.

src: Mthatha was declared a Rapid High Impact Presidential Intervention Node in 2009 and the interventions are intended to address infrastructure backlogs and service delivery challenges, in order to fully revitalise Mthatha.
tgt: Mthatha e ile ya etswa Sebaka se Thefulehileng sa Bokena dipakeng bo Potlakileng ba Mopresidente ka 2009, mme bokenadipakeng bo reretswe ho rarolla diphephetso tsa tshallomorao ya kaho ya meralo ya motheo le phano ya ditshebeletso, ka sepheo sa ho ntjhafatsa Mthatha kahohlehohle.

src: The President will also assess first-hand the progress made on government’s infrastructure projects with regard to the provision of water, electricity and roads in the area.
tgt: Mopresidente o tla boela a sekaseka ka boyena kgatelopele e entsweng diprojekeng tsa meralo ya motheo ya mmuso mabapi le phumantsho ya metsi, motlakase le mebila tikolohong eo.

src: The switch-on by President Jacob Zuma at the Thornhill substation will provide the network capacity to address the backlog of about 25 000 households.
tgt: Ho kgantshwa ho tla etswa ke Mopresidente Jacob Zuma ha seteishenana sa motlakase sa Thornhill ho tla fana ka bokgoni ba marangrang a ho rarolla tshallomorao ya malapa a ka bang 25 000.

src: President Jacob Zuma will undertake a State Visit to Accra, Ghana, from 26 to 27 November 2013.
tgt: Mopresidente Jacob Zuma o tla kena Leetong la ho Emela Naha Accra, Ghana, ho tloha ka la 26 ho isa ho la 27 Pudungwana 2013.

src: The visit will deepen our existing strong bilateral relationship with Ghana and advance intra-trade on the continent.
tgt: Leeto le tla tiisa dikamano tsa rona tse matla le Ghana le be le ntshetsepele kgwebisano e momahaneng kontinenteng.

src: President Jacob Zuma is scheduled to chair the South Africa-Botswana Bi-National Commission (BNC) on 21 November 2013.
tgt: Mopresidente Jacob Zuma o bile modulasetulo wa Khomishene ya Dinahapedi tsa Aforika Borwa le Botswana (BCN) ka la 21 Pudungwana 2013.

src: This will enhance bilateral relations and co-operation between the two neighbouring countries.
tgt: Sena se tla ntlafatsa dikamano le tshebedisano mmoho dipakeng tsa dinaha tse pedi tse ahisaneng.

src: This annual BNC at the level of Heads of State was established last year to elevate the status of the Joint Permanent Commission for Cooperation and the Joint Permanent Commission for Cooperation on Defence and Security.
tgt: BNC ena ya selemo le selemo boemong ba Dihlooho tsa Dinaha e ile ya thewa ngwahola ho phahamisa boemo ba Khomishene ya Moshwelella ya Kopanelo bakeng sa Tshebedisanommoho le Khomishene ya Moshwelella ya Kopanelo bakeng sa Tshebedisanommoho ya Tshireletso.

src: Cabinet welcomes South Africa’s election to the United Nations Human Rights Council (on 12 November 2013).
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho kgethwa ha Aforika Borwa Lekgotleng la Ditokelo tsa Botho la Matjhaba a Kopaneng (ka la 12 Pudungwana 2013).

src: Our term starts on 1 January 2014 which coincides with the country’s celebration of 20 Years of Freedom.
tgt: Sehla sa rona se qala ka la 1 Pherekgong 2014 mme se tjhaisana le keteko ya naha ya Dilemo tse 20 tsa Tokoloho.

src: This reaffirms our commitment to the achievement of human rights for all our citizens, the citizens of the African continent and the citizens of the world.
tgt: Sena se netefatsa botjha boikitlaetso ba rona phihlellong ya ditokelo tsa botho bakeng sa baahi bohle, baahi ba kontinente ya Aforika esita le baahi ba lefatshe lohle.

src: Cabinet joins the international community in expressing heartfelt appreciation to those Non-Governmental Organisations who have contributed to the international emergency aid relief for those affected by Typhoon Haiyan in the Philippines.
tgt: Kabinete e ikamahanya le baahi ba matjhaba ka ho ntsha maikutlo a kutlwelobohloko thorisong ya Mekgatlo eo e seng ya Mmuso, e kentseng letsoho thusong ya matjhaba ya tshohanyetso bakeng sa bao ba anngweng ke Lehodiotswana la Haiyan kwana Phillipines.

src: The spirit of Ubuntu will contribute to easing the grief of the Philippine people during this difficult time.
tgt: Moya wa Botho o tla thusa ho kokobetsa mahlonoko a batho ba Phillipines nakong ena ya mathata.

src: Cabinet welcomes the announcement of yet another milestone in the life of the Gauteng Freeway Improvement Project, with tolling on the designated sections of Gauteng Highways commencing on 3 December 2013.Motorists who have not registered for e-tolling are encouraged to do so, to ensure that they qualify for the discounted rates.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela tsebiso ya katleho e nngwe hape botenng ba Projeke ya Ntlafatso ya Mebilaphara ya Gauteng, moo ditefello tsa mebila dikarolong tse kgethilweng tsa Mebila e Meholo ya Gauteng di qalang ka la 3 Tshitwe 2013.Beng ba makoloi ba e so kang ba ingodisetsa ditefello tsa mebila ba kgothalletswa ho etsa jwalo, ho netefatsa hore ba lokelwa ke ditheolelo.

src: Cabinet commends the Departments of Science and Technology and Higher Education and Training as well as the Cape Peninsula University of Technology for making history with the launch of the country’s first CubeSat, today, 21 November 2013, in Russia.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Mafapha a Saense le Theknoloji le Thuto le Thupelo e Phahameng hammoho le Yunivesithi ya Theknoloji ya Hlohleng ya Kapa ka ho etsa nalane ka ho thakgola CubeSat ya pele ya naha ena, kajeno, mohla la 21 Pudungwana 2013, kwana Russia.

src: The satellite, which will provide valuable space weather data, demonstrates South Africa’s capability in the field of space science and technology.
tgt: Satalaete ena, e tla fana ka lesedi la bohlokwa la maemo a lehodimo sepakapakeng, e bontsha bokgoni ba Aforika Borwa lekaleng la saense le theknoloji ya sepakapakeng.

src: Cabinet welcomed the election of Minister of Basic Education Angie Motshekga as Chairperson of the Southern and Eastern Africa Consortium for Monitoring Education Quality (SACMEQ) during the 37th UNESCO General Conference this bolsters confidence in our education system and institutions.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho kgethwa ha Letona la Thuto ya Motheo Mme Angie Motshekga e le modulasetulo wa Sehlopha sa Aforika e ka Borwa le e ka Botjhabela ya Bodisa ba Thuto ya Boleng (SACMEQ) nakong ya Seboka Kakaretso sa bo37 sa UNESCO sena se matlafatsa boitshepo mokgweng wa thuto ya rona le ditheo tsa rona.

src: The objective of SACMEQ is to undertake integrated research and training activities that will expand opportunities for educational planners and researchers to receive training in the technical skills required to monitor, evaluate, and compare the general conditions of schooling and the quality of basic education.
