src: The tournament will be officially opened by President Jacob Zuma and seeks to promote karate as a sport to the youth given its benefits in instilling self-discipline, self-defence, focus and also in promoting social crime prevention.
tgt: Thonamente e tla bulwa semmuso ke Moporesidente Jacob Zuma mme sepheo sa yona ke ho kgothaletsa karate jwalo ka papadi ya batjha ha ho shejwa melemo ya yona ya ho ruta boitshwaro bo botle ba botho, boitshireletso, tsepamiso ya maikutlo mme hape le ho kgothaletsa thibelo ya botlokotsebe.

src: The Competition Commission will convene the Eighth Annual Conference and Fifteen-Year Celebration from 4 – 5 September 2014.
tgt: Khomishene ya Ditlhodisano e tla bitsa Seboka sa Borobedi sa Selemo ka seng le keteko ya Dilemo tse Leshome le Metso e Mehlano ho tloha ka la 4 – 5 Loetse 2014.

src: The conference will be officially opened by Minister Ebrahim Patel welcoming delegates, including those from competition agencies around Africa and one regional competition agency, the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa Competition Commission.
tgt: Seboka se tla bulwa semmuso ke Letona Ebrahim Patel a amohela baemedi, ho kenyeletswa le ba tswang makaleng a ditlhodisano ho potoloha Aforika le lekala le le leng la lebatowa la ditlhodisano, Mmaraka wa Kopanelo bakeng sa Khomishene ya Ditlhodisano ya Aforika e ka Botjhabela le e ka Borwa.

src: Appointments.
tgt: Dithonyo.

src: Cabinet’s position on current issues.
tgt: Maemo a Kabinete mabapi le dintlha tsa hajwale.

src: LesothoCabinet appreciated the initiative by President Zuma together with SADC to restore peace in Lesotho.
tgt: LesothoKabinete e ananetse boikitlaetso ba Moporesidente Zuma mmoho le Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba ya Aforika e ka Borwa (SADC) ba ho kgutlisetsa kgotso Lesotho.

src: Cabinet supports the recent Summit’s resolutions which mandated the Deputy President of the Republic of South Africa, The Honourable Cyril Ramaphosa, supported by the Secretariat and a team of experts from Troika Member States, to act as SADC Facilitator to the Kingdom of Lesotho.
tgt: Kabinete e tshehetsa ditumellano tsa Seboka sa haufinyane tjena se rommeng Motlatsi wa Moporesidente wa Rephaboliki ya Aforika Borwa, Mohlomphehi Cyril Ramaphosa, a tsheheditswe ke Sekrethariate le moifo wa ditsebi ho tswa ho Ditho tsa Mebuso tsa Troika, ho sebetsa jwalo ka Mothusi wa SADC ho Naha ya Borena Lesotho.

src: The Deputy President, Secretariat and experts have clear Terms of Reference to facilitate the restoration of political and security stability in the Kingdom of Lesotho, in the short and long term.
tgt: Motlatsi wa Moporesidente, Sekrethariate le ditsebi ba na le Dipehelo tse hlakileng tsa Tshebetso ho thusa ka ho kgutlisetsa botsitso ba dipolotiki le polokeho ka hara Naha ya Borena ya Lesotho, bakeng sa nako e kgutshwanyane le e telele.

src: South African companies exhibition in RussiaCabinet congratulates the South African companies that were awarded the best standing at the World Food Show in Moscow.
tgt: Dipontsho tsa Dikhamphani tsa Aforika Borwa RussiaKabinete e lebohela dikhamphani tsa Aforika Borwa tse ileng tsa putswa ka maemo a phahameng a bokgabane ho World Food Show ho la Moscow.

src: Working with the Department of Trade and Industry South Africa’s local Food Products have been well received amongst Russian Food importers.
tgt: Di sebetsa le Lefapha la Kgwebisano le Indaseteri, Dihlahiswa tsa Dijo tsa lehae tsa Aforika Borwa di amohetswe hantle hara bareki ba Dijo tsa ka ntle ba Russia.

src: This international accolade comes against the backdrop of President Zuma’s recent visit to the Russian Republic.
tgt: Thoholetso ena ya matjhaba e tla kamora leeto la Moporesidente Zuma la moraorao tjena Rephaboliking ya Russia.

src: This year 3 000 exhibitors showcased their produce.
tgt: Selemong sena bapepesi ba 3 000 ba bontshitse dihlahiswa tsa bona.

src: Under the Export Marketing and Investment Assistance (EMIA) scheme, 21 South African companies showcased the agro processing sector.
tgt: Tlasa sekema sa Thekiso ya Ka Ntle le Thuso ya Matsete (EMIA), dikhamphani tse 21 tsa Aforika Borwa di bontshitse lekala la tsona la ho sebetsana le dihlahiswa tsa temo.

src: Essay competition on Nat Nakasa and Freedom and Democracy achievements Cabinet congratulates the winners of the inaugural essay competition on the life of Nat Nakasa, a prominent journalist whose remains returned to South Africa after fifty years on 19 August 2014.
tgt: Tlhodisano ya Moqoqo ka Nat Nakasa le Diphihlello tsa Tokoloho le DemokerasiKabinete e lebohela bahlodi ba tlhodisano ya moqoqo wa pele ka bophelo ba Nat Nakasa, raditaba ya itlhommeng pele eo masalla a hae a kgutletseng Aforika Borwa kamora dilemo tse 50 ka la 19 Phato 2014.

src: This initiative by the Department of Arts and Culture reminds our young generation about our struggle for freedom and exposes them to the history of writing and journalism in South Africa.
tgt: Boikitlaetso bona ba Lefapha la Bonono le Botjhaba bo hopotsa moloko wa rona wa batjha ka ntwa ya rona ya tokoloho le ho ba hlahisetsa nalane ya ho ngola le tsa boqolotsi ba ditaba ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: The journalism students Sbongakonke Mbatha, Qiniso Mbili and Nkamogeleng Lebeloane each won an internship placement and a laptop.
tgt: Baithuti ba bongodi le ba boqolotsi ba ditaba Sbongakonke Mbatha, Qiniso Mbili le Nkamogeleng Lebeloane ka bonngwe ba bona ba hapile ho kenela thupello ya mosebetsi le lepthopo.

src: Another category was the learners’ debate which reflected on the achievements attained through Freedom and Democracy.
tgt: Mokgahlelo o mong e ne e le wa dingangisano tsa baithuti tse neng di bontsha diphihlello tse fihlelletsweng ka Tokoloho le Demokerasi.

src: Competition objectives included creating awareness on the role of journalists during the liberation struggle in South Africa.
tgt: Dipheo tsa dingangisano di ne di kenyeletsa ho hlahisa tsebo ka seabo sa baqolotsi ba ditaba nakong ya ntwa ya tokoloho ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: The winners Mfundo Radebe, Dumisa Nzama, Danielle Dallas, Olivia Habonimana, Faith Marthinussen and Cebisa Ncube each won a laptop.
tgt: Bahlodi Mfundo Radebe, Dumisa Nzama, Danielle Dallas, Olivia Habonimana, Faith Marthinussen le Cebisa Ncube ba hapile lepthopo motho ka mong.

src: Key Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Transfer of Department of Health Shares in Biovac CompanyCabinet approved the transfer of Department of Health‘s shares in the Biological and Vaccines Institute (Biovac) of Southern Africa to the Department of Science and Technology.
tgt: Phethisetso ya Diabo tsa Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle ho Khamphani ya BiovacKabinete e tjhaelletse monwana phethisetso ya diabo tsa Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle ka hara Setsha sa Kalafo le Diente (Biovac) sa Aforika e ka Borwa ho ya ho Lefapha la Saense le Thekenoloji.

src: Biovac is a public-private partnership between the South African Government and the Biovac Consortium.
tgt: Biovac ke bomphato ba setjhaba le poraefete pakeng tsa Mmuso wa Aforika Borwa le Mokgatlo wa Biovac.

src: The South African Government shares comprised of 12, 5% owned by Department of Science and Technology and 35% owned by Department of Health.
tgt: Diabo tsa Mmuso wa Aforika Borwa e ne e le tsa 12,5% tse neng di tshwerwe ke Lefapha la Saense le Thekenoloji mme 35% e ne e le ya Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle.

src: The transfer of shares is a response to the concerns raised by the World Health Organisation (WHO) and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) that Department of Health in the current arrangement may be conflicted as it acted as a shareholder and a buyer.
tgt: Phethisetso ya diabo ke karabelo ho dingongoreho tse hlahisitsweng ke Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Bophelo bo Botle (WHO) le Letlole la Bana la Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (Unicef) hore Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle ho ya ka ditlhophiso tsa jwale le ka baka dikgohlano ka ha le ne le sebetsa jwalo ka radiabo le moreki.

src: The WHO requires the regulatory authority (in this case the Medicines Control Council which is part of the Department of Health) and its oversight role be separated from that of any manufacturer of medicine – in this, Biovac.
tgt: WHO e batla hore ba ka taolong (tabeng ena Lekgotla la Taolo ya Meriana e leng karolo ya Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle) le karolo ya lona ya bodisa di arohanngwe le tsa mohlahisi wa meriana – mona ke, Biovac.

src: The transfer of Department of Health shares to Science and Technology, will enable Biovac to export its manufactured products to countries benefitting from the WHO and UNICEF vaccines programmes.
tgt: Phethisetso ya diabo tsa Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle ho ya ho la Saense le Thekenoloji, e tla thusa Biovac ho rekisa dihlahiswa dinaheng tsa ka ntle tse kgolang molemo mananeong a WHO le Unicef a kentelo.

src: Biovac is a company that supplies high-quality, safe and effective vaccines to the public sector, and is a leading supplier of paediatrics vaccines to government's Expanded Programme on Immunisation (EPI).
tgt: Biovac ke khamphani e fanang ka diente tsa boleng bo hodimo, tse bolokehileng le ho ba hlwahlwa ho lekala la setjhaba, mme ke mofani ya ka sehloohong wa diente tsa bana ho Lenaneo la mmuso la Katoloso ya Kentelo.

src: Through the Department of Science and Technology, government will now own 47,5% of Biovac shares while % will be held by the Biovac Consortium.
tgt: Ka Lefapha la Saense le Thekenoloji, jwale mmuso o tla ba le diabo tsa 47,5% ho tsa Biovac ha % di tla tshwarwa ke Mokgatlo wa Biovac.

src: EskomAs announced this past weekend, Cabinet has approved a package of measures to secure the sustainability of the electricity industry, strengthen Eskom’s finances, and ensure that the energy security of the country is maintained.
tgt: ESKOMJwalo ka ha ho tsebisitswe mafelong a beke e fetileng, Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana pakana ya mekgwa ya ho boloka boteng ba indaseteri ya motlakase, ho matlafatsa ditjhelete tsa Eskom, le ho nnetefatsa hore polokeho ya eneji ya naha e hlokomelehile.

src: All of this will have to be done in a manner that does not add further pressure to the nation’s finances.
tgt: Sena sohle se lokela ho etswa ka mokgwa o sa tlo eketsa kgatello le ho feta ditjheleteng tsa setjhaba.

src: At the same time, government would like to ensure that poor households are cushioned as far as fiscal resources allow from the impact of the tariff adjustment.
tgt: Ka ho tshwana, mmuso o batla ho nnetefatsa hore malapa a futsanehileng a tshireleditswe ho ya ka moo mehlodi ya ditjhelete e dumelang ho tswa ho kgahlamelo ya ho lokiswa ha ditefello.

src: The Cabinet decision is based on the recommendations of an Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) which reviewed an extensive set of options available to ensure energy security.
tgt: Qeto ya Kabinete e itshetlehile hodima dikgothaletso tsa Komiti ya kopanelo ya Matona (IMC) e lekotseng botjha maikgethelo a mangata a teng bakeng sa polokeho ya eneji.

src: The IMC will continue to monitor the industry closely.
tgt: IMC e tla tswela pele ho beha indaseteri ena leihlo le bohale.

src: Details of the package can be accessed via the National Treasury WEBTOKEN summary the package consists of, among others, an injection by government of additional equity into Eskom to help the utility strengthen its balance sheet, enabling it to borrow more from financial markets.
tgt: Ka bokgutshwanyane pakana e kenyeletsa, hara tse ding, thuso ya mmuso ya tekatekano e eketsehileng ho Eskom ho thusa kgwebo ho matlafatsa ditjhelete tsa yona, bakeng sa ho e thusa ho kadima haholwanyane ho tswa mebarakeng ya ditjhelete.

src: To ensure that government’s financial resources are not strained, the equity injection will be funded by leveraging non-strategic government assets.
tgt: Ho nnetefatsa hore mehlodi ya ditjhelete ya mmuso ha e kene tlasa kgatello, thuso ya tekatekano e tla thuswa ka ditjhelete ka ho matlafatsa thepa ya mmuso eo e seng ya bohlokwa.

src: Further details in this regard will be provided when the Minister of Finance tables the Medium Term Budget Policy Statement (MTBPS) on 22 October.
tgt: Dintlha tse ding tabeng ena ho tla fanwa ka tsona ha Letona la Ditjhelete le hlahisa Pehelo ya Leano la Ditekanyetso tsa Nako e Bohareng (MTBPS) ka la 22 Mphalane.

src: Other elements of the package include: a strong improvement in Eskom’s operational efficiencies which will reduce costs a R50 billion increase in debt raised by Eskom which will be supported by the existing government guarantees government support for Eskom’s application to NERSA for an adjustment to the tariff, which is in line with normal regulatory processes demand management measures refinements to energy policy and the expansion of the independent power producer WEBTOKEN terms of cushioning poor households, government will strengthen oversight of the free basic electricity grant.
tgt: Dikarolo tse ding tsa pakana di kenyeletsa: ntlafatso e matla bokgabaneng ba Eskom ba tshebetso bo tla fokotsa ditjeho nyollo ya R50 bilione ya sekoloto se entsweng ke se tla tshehetswa ke ditiisetso tsa hajwale tsa mmuso tshehetso ya mmuso bakeng sa kopo ya Eskom ho Bolaodi ba Eneji ba Naha ba Aforika Borwa (NERSA) bakeng sa ho nyoloha ha ditefello, e tsamaelanang le ditsamaiso tsa taolo mekgwa ya taolo ya tseko tokiso ya leano la eneji le katoloso ya lenaneo la mohlahisi ya ikemetseng wa matla a motlakase.

src: This will ensure that allocations are used effectively as well as to encourage municipalities to improve the efficiency with which they maintain their networks and supply power to consumers.
tgt: Mabapi le ho bebofatsa mathata a malapa a futsanehileng, mmuso o tla matlafatsa peho leihlo ho dithuso tsa motlakase wa motheo wa mahala.

src: These measures are necessary for South Africa to raise economic growth to a rate which is sufficient to create more jobs, reduce poverty and inequality.
tgt: Mekgwa ena e a hlokahala bakeng sa hore Aforika Borwa e phahamise kgolo ya moruo ho ya maemong a loketseng bakeng sa ho hlahisa mesebetsi e mengata, ho fokotsa bofuma le ho se lekalekane.

src: Transfer of administrative functions to the Office of Chief JusticeCabinet was briefed on the commencement of the initial phase of the transfer of administrative functions and staff relating to the Superior Courts from the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development to the Office of the Chief Justice.
tgt: Phethisetso ya mesebetsi ya tsamaiso ho ya ho Kantoro ya Moahlodi e MoholoKabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka qalo ya mokgahlelo wa pele wa phethisetso ya mesebetsi ya tsamaiso le basebeletsi mabapi le Makgotla a Maholo a Dinyewe ho tloha ho Lefapha la Toka le Ntshetsopele ya Molao wa Motheo ho ya ho Kantoro ya Moahlodi e Moholo.

src: This gives effect to the Constitution Seventeenth Amendment Act, 2012 and the Superior Courts Act, Act No.
tgt: Sena se fana ka matla ho Sehlomathiso sa Boleshome le metso e supileng sa Molao wa Motheo sa Molao wa 2012, le Molao wa Makgotla a Dinyewe a Maholo, Molao wa bo 10 wa 2013.Molao wa Makgotla a Maholo a Dinyewe o ntlafatsa tsamaiso ya bo makgiseterata ka ho beha bomakgiseterata ka hara Karolo ya Lekgotla le Phahameng la Dinyewe le ka tlasa taolo ya Moporesidente wa Boahlodi wa Karolo e amehang.

src: The Superior Courts Act enhances the administration of the magistracy by placing magistrates in every Division of the High Court under the control of the Judge President of the Division concerned.
tgt: Molao o fana ka matla le mesebetsi ho Kantoro ya Moahlodi e Moholo e ileng ya thehwa jwalo ka setsha se arohaneng sa puso se tshwanang le lefapha ho ya ka Kgoeletso ya Moporesidente ka 2010.

src: The Act assigns powers and functions to the Office of the Chief Justice which was established as a separate state institution equivalent to a department by a Presidential Proclamation in 2010.
tgt: Sena se tiisa boitlamo ba Mmuso bakeng sa boikemelo ba Makgotla a Dinyewe jwalo ka ha ho hlahella ho Molao wa Motheo.

src: This affirms the Government’s commitment to the independence of the Judiciary as espoused in our Constitution.
tgt: Ho thehwa ha kantoro ya bolaodi ba diporojeke bakeng sa Boikitlaetso ba ho akofisa Dikaho tsa Motheo tsa BoporesidenteKabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho thehwa ha Kantoro ya Bolaodi ba Diporojeke bakeng sa Boikitlaetso ba ho Akofisa Dikaho tsa Motheo tsa Boporesidente tsa Kopano ya Aforika bo eteletsweng pele ke Moporesidente Zuma.

src: Establishment of project management office for Presidential Infrastructure championingCabinet approved the establishment of the Project Management Office for African Union Presidential Infrastructure Championing Initiative which is led by President Zuma.
tgt: Lena ke lenaneo le tsamaiswang ke Aforika la dikaho tsa motheo le reretsweng ho akofisa diporojeke tse tshelang madiboho tse tla bula bokgoni ba moruo ba kontinente le ho fana ka menyetla ya ntshetsopele bakeng sa badudi, metsemeholo le mabatowa.

src: This is an African-driven infrastructure programme meant to champion cross boarder infrastructure projects that will unlock the economic potential of the continent and provide development opportunities for communities, cities and regions.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho thehwa ha Kantoro ya Bolaodi ba Diporojeke bakeng sa Boikitlaetso ba ho Akofisa Dikaho tsa Motheo tsa Boporesidente ka tshehetso ya mafapha a mmuso a amehang.

src: Cabinet approved the establishment of the Presidential Infrastructure Championing Initiative Project Management Office with the support of relevant government departments.
tgt: Kantoro ya Bolaodi ba Diporojeke e tla tshehetswa ke ho thehwa ha IMC mabapi le Boikitlaetso ba ho Akofisa Dikaho tsa Motheo ba Boporesidente ka AU ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: The Project Management Office will be supported by the establishment of an Inter-Ministerial Committee on AU Presidential Infrastructure Championing Initiative in South Africa.
tgt: Komiti e tla ba tlasa bodulasetulo ba Letona Kantorong ya Moporesidente bakeng sa Merero, Bodisa le Tlhatlhobo ya Tshebetso.

src: The Committee will be chaired by the Minister in the Presidency for Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation.
tgt: Ho thehwa ha mohlodi wa Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba wa ditsebi ho tsa molao le ho tsa merero ya mesebetsiKabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho thehwa ha mohlodi wa Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba wa ditsebi ho tsa molao le ho tsa mesebetsi ya ka hare ho sebetsana le tshallomorao ya dinyewe tsa tsebiso ya ho fanyehwa mosebetsing ka hara tshebeletso ya setjhaba.

src: Establishment of Public Service pool of legal and labour relation specialistCabinet approved the establishment of an internal Public Service pool of legal and labour relations specialists to deal with the backlog of pending precautionary suspension cases in the public service.
tgt: Dipheo tsa boitshunyako bona ke ho bona hore Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba e sebetsa ka bokgabane le bohlwahlwa ho feta ka ho fokotsa nako ya ditsamaiso tsa kgalemo, haholoholo moo basebeletsi ba fanyehilweng mosebetsing ba ntseng ba amohela mekgolo ya bona e felletseng.

src: The intervention aims to get the Public Service to operate more efficiently and effectively by reducing the period for completing disciplinary processes, especially where personnel are suspended on full pay.
tgt: Ho fetafeta moo, boikitlaetso bona bo nnetefatsa bolaodi bo nepahetseng ba kgalemo ka ho kenya tshebetsong boholo nako ya dikgwedi tse tharo (matsatsi a 90) a ho phethela dinyewe.

src: The legal and labour relations specialists’ pool will comprise Public Service officials who are experts in this field, including investigators, prosecutors and presiding officers to ensure that the full labour relations value chain is optimal.
tgt: Mohlodi wa ditsebi ho tsa molao le ho tsa mesebetsi di tla eketsa Bahlanka ba Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba bao e leng ditsebi lehlakoreng lena, ho kenyeletswa bafuputsi, batjhutjhisi le batsamaisi ho nnetefatsa hore ketane ya boleng ya dikamano tsa basebetsi e sebetsa ka botlalo.

src: Bills.
tgt: Dibili.

src: Cabinet approved the tabling in Parliament of Disaster Management Amendment Bill, 2002 (Act No.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho hlahiswa Palamenteng ha Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Taolo ya Dikoduwa, 2002 (Molao wa bo 57 wa 2002).

src: Key Cabinet decisions.1 Cabinet approved the publication of the draft National Learner Transport Policy for public comments in the Government Gazette for 21 days.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana phatlalatso ya moralo wa Leano bakeng sa Dipalangwang tsa Naha tsa Baithuti Koranteng ya Mmuso bakeng sa matsatsi a 21.Leano lena le ntlafatsa phumantsho ya thuto e nang le boleng ka ho fana ka dipalangwang tsa baithuti tse bolokehileng, tse shebahalang, tse hlwahlwa, tse momahantsweng le ho ba tsa moshwelella, haholoholo dibakeng tsa metse ya mahae moo dipalangwang di sitisang phumantsho ya thuto.

src: The policy improves access to quality education by providing safe, decent, effective, integrated and sustainable learner transport, especially in rural communities where transportation challenges hinder access to education.
tgt: Leano le shebana le karohano ya dibaka le ho hlophisa botjha ditshebetso tse amang boleng ba dipalangwang tsa setjhaba.

src: The policy addresses spatial challenges and re-organisation of operations which impact on the quality of public transport.
tgt: Hape le fana ka tsamaiso ya moralo o kopanetsweng le maemo a tshwanang a bolaodi.

src: It also provides for an integrated planning system and uniform standards of management.
tgt: Ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha leano lena ho tla fana ka tikoloho e bolokehileng le ho tshireletseha bakeng sa baithuti ka tshebedisanommoho le momahano le bolaodi ba thibelo ya tlolo ya molao.

src: Implementation of this policy will provide a safe and secure transport environment for learners through cooperation and collaboration with law enforcement authorities.2 Cabinet approved the Directive on Compulsory Development, Mandatory Training Days and Minimum Entry Requirements to the levels of Senior Management Service as determined in terms of Section 3(2) of the Public Service Act, 1994.This promotes skills development so as to respond to the National Development Plan objective of building a capable and developmental state for the benefit of improved service delivery.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Tshupiso mabapi le Ntshetsopele e Qobellang, Matsatsi a laetsweng a Thupello le Ditshwanelo tse tlase tse hlokahalang tsa ho kena maemomg a Tshebeletso e ka Sehloohong ya Bolaodi jwaloka ha e tekilwe ho ya ka Karolo 3(2) ya Molao wa Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba, 1994.Sena se susumetsa ntshetsopele ya bokgoni hore ho arabelwe ho sepheo sa Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP) wa ho aha puso e kgonang le e tswelang pele molemong wa phano ya ditshebeletso e ntlafetseng.

src: The directive is a long-term skills development strategy that will enhance the quality of human resources which is critical to government’s capacity to deliver on its mandate.
tgt: Tshupiso ena ke lewa la nako e telele la ntshetsopele ya bokgoni le tla ntlafatsa boleng ba basebeletsi le hlokolosi ho bokgoni ba mmuso ho fana ka ditshebeletso ho ya ka thomo ya ona.

src: All departments in the Public Service will be required to adopt a consistent approach to promote relevant and mandatory skills development within the Senior Management Service.3 Cabinet approved for the Department of Performance Monitoring and Evaluation to present the draft Discussion Document on Performance Monitoring and Evaluation Principles and Approach to Parliament’s Portfolio Committee on Public Service Administration and Planning Monitoring and Evaluation.
tgt: Mafapha ohle a Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba a tla tshwanela ho rua katamelo e tsitsitseng bakeng sa ho kgothaletsa ntshetsopele ya bokgoni bo tsamaelanang le bo batlehang ka hara Tshebeletso ya Bolaodi e ka Sehloohong.

src: The document proposes a set of basic principles and an approach to Performance Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) that is intended to result in continuous improvement in government performance and increased accountability.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana bakeng sa Lefapha la Bodisa le Tlhatlhobo ya Tshebetso ho fana ka moralo wa Tokomane ya Puisano mabapi le Dipehelo le Katamelo tsa Bodisa le Tlhatlhobo ya Tshebetso ho di behela Komiti ya Potefolio ya Palamente mabapi le Tsamaiso ya Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba le Meralo, Bodisa le Tlhatlhobo.

src: Its key objective is to build consensus on the objectives of M&E, and how it should be implemented.
tgt: Tokomane e sisinya pokello ya dipehelo tsa mantlha le katamelo ho Lefapha la Bodisa le Tlhatlhobo ya Tshebetso (M&E) e reretsweng ho baka hore ho be le ntlafatso e tswellang tshebetsong ya mmuso le boikarabelo bo eketsehileng.

src: This contributes to the implementation of the National Development Plan (NDP) in relation to building a capable and developmental state as well as promoting an active citizenry and strong leadership.
tgt: Sepheo sa yona se seholo ke ho aha tumellano mabapi le dipheo tsa M&E, le kamoo e tshwanetseng ho kenngwa tshebetsong.

src: M&E competencies are part of the core managerial competencies that are required for a capable and developmental state.4 Cabinet approved South Africa’s negotiating positions for Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals (CMS COP11) which will be held in Quinto, Ecuador, from 4 to 9 November 2014.South Africa’s active participation in addressing challenges of climate change and the conservation of nature and associated species is based on the principle of sustainable development and environmental sustainability, and is in line with the requirements of Section 24 of the Bill of Rights.5 Cabinet approved the negotiating mandate that will serve as the basis for South Africa’s engagement at the 20th session of the Conference of Parties to the UNFCCC (COP 20), and the 10th Conference of Parties serving as the meeting of Parties to the Kyoto Protocol (CMP 10), from 1 to 12 December 2014, in Lima Peru.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana maemo a Aforika Borwa a ho kena ditherisanong bakeng sa Paballo ya Mefuta e Fallang ya Diphoofolo tse Hlaha (CMS COP11) e tla tshwarelwa Quinto, ho la Ecuador, ho tloha ka la 4 ho ya ho la 9 Pudungwana 2014.Bonkakarolo bo matla ba Aforika Borwa tabeng ya ho shebana le diphephetso tsa ho fetofetoha ha tlelaemete le paballo ya tlhaho le mefuta e amehang bo itshetlehile hodima pehelo ya ntshetsopele ya moshwelella le tikoloho ya moshwelella, mme bo tsamaelana le ditlhoko tsa Karolo 24 ya Bili ya Ditokelo.

src: South Africa’s position is in line with the country’s national interest, and the implications for South Africa’s further engagement in the international climate change negotiations as outlined in the National Development Plan.6 Cabinet approved a submission of the Cape Town Agreement of 2012 on the implementation of the provisions of the Torremolinos Protocol of 1993 relating to the International Convention for the Safety of Fishing Vessels, 1977 for ratification by Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana thomo ya ho kena ditherisanong e tla sebetsa e le motheo bakeng sa hore Aforika Borwa e kene ho tulo ya bo 20 ya Seboka sa Mekgatlo ho UNFCCC (COP 20), le Seboka sa Mekgatlo ya bo 10 e sebetsang jwaloka kopano ya Mekgatlo ho Porotokhole ya Kyoto (CMP 10), ho tloha ka la 1 ho ya ho la 12 Tshitwe 2014, ho la Lima, Peru.

src: The Torremolinos Convention and its Protocol of 1993 lay down safety standards, such as life-saving appliances, radio communication, fire protection, machinery and electrical installations, as well as specific requirements for seagoing fishing vessels of 24 metres and longer.
tgt: Maemo a Aforika Borwa a tsamaelana le dikgahleho tsa naha, le dikateng bakeng sa ho kena ha Aforika Borwa ditherisanong tsa matjhaba tsa ho fetofetoha ha tlelaemete jwaloka ha di tekilwe ho NDKabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho tekwa ha Tumellano ya Motse Kapa ya 2012 mabapi le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha dipehelo tsa Porotokhole ya Torremolinos ya 1993 e mabapi le Seboka sa Matjhaba bakeng sa Polokeho ya Dikepe tsa Botshwasi ba Ditlhapi, ya 1977 bakeng sa ho sekaseka ke Palamente.

src: This binding international safety regime will contribute to improving safety standards in order to reduce the number of fatalities at sea, estimated at 24 000 annually worldwide.
tgt: Seboka sa Torremolinos le Porotokhole ya sona ya 1993 di hlahisa maemo a polokeho, a kang disebediswa tse bolokang bophelo, dikgokahanyo ka radio, tshireletso mollong, ho kenngwa ha metjhini le kgokelo tsa motlakase, mmoho le ditlhoko tse itseng bakeng sa dikepe tsa botshwasi ba ditlhapi tse lebang metsing tsa bolelele ba dimithara tse 24 le ho feta.

src: South Africa’s fishing vessels will be subject to the provisions of the protocol when in the waters of a State party to the 1993 Torremolinos protocol.
tgt: Tumellano ena e tlamang ya polokeho ya matjhaba e tla nyehela bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa maemo a polokeho ho fokotsa palo ya mafu lewatleng, e akanyetswang ho mafu a 24 000 ka selemo lefatsheng ka bophara.

src: This is in line with Operation Phakisa’s objectives of developing an institutional framework for the management of South Africa’s ocean space, improving the protection of South Africa’s oceans, particularly around critically endangered ecosystems, and addressing the skills gap, amongst others.7 Cabinet approved for South Africa to accede to the International Convention on Standards of Training, Certification and Watch-keeping for Fishing Vessel Personnel, 1995 (STCW-F).This is the first attempt to establish international mandatory training standards for the crews of seagoing fishing vessels of 24 metres or more in length.
tgt: Dikepe tsa Aforika Borwa tsa botshwasi ba ditlhapi di tla sebetsa ho ya ka dipehelo tsa porotokhole ha di le metsing a mokgatlo wa Puso o teng ho porotokhole ya Torremolinos ya 1993.Sena se tsamaelana le dipheo tsa Operation Phakisa tsa ho ntshetsapele moralo wa mmuso bakeng sa bolaodi ba sebaka sa lewatle sa Aforika Borwa, ho ntlafatsa tshireletso ya mawatle a Aforika Borwa, haholoholo ditheong tsa tlhaho tse tsietsing ka tsela e hlokolosi, le ho shebana le sekgeo sa bokgoni, hara tse ding.

src: This will improve the safety of life and property at sea, as well as to prevent pollution of the marine environment by the fishing WEBTOKEN the past, extended periods of sea service were seen as the way to acquire experience and appropriate skills.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana bakeng sa Aforika Borwa ho dumellana le Seboka sa Matjhaba mabapi le Maemo a Thupello, Phano ya ditifikeiti le Peho-leihlo bakeng sa Basebeletsi ba Dikepe tsa Botshwasi ba Ditlhapi (STWC-F), ya 1995.Sena ke boiteko ba pele ba ho theha maemo a matjhaba a tlamang a thupello bakeng sa meifo ya dikepe tsa botshwasi ba ditlhapi tse yang lewatleng tsa bolelele ba dimithara tse 24 kapa ho feta.

src: This system of on-the-job training has not produced a quality outcome for the skills of the crew.
tgt: Mokgwa ona wa ho rupellwa ka hara mosebetsi ha o so hlahise sephetho sa boleng bakeng sa bokgoni ba moifo o motjha.

src: The new system is built around a combination of reduced experiential training with upgraded and more structured education for enhancing knowledge.
tgt: Mokgwa o motjha o ahilwe ho potoloha motswako wa ho fokotsa thupello ya boiphihlelo ka thuto e ntlafaditsweng le ho hlophiswa hantle bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa tsebo.

src: This will make it possible for fishers to progress over time from small vessels to large fishing vessels and eventually internationally trading vessels.8 Cabinet approved for the following 2015 commemorative coin designs by the South African Mint Company, to be promulgated in a Government Gazette.
tgt: Sena se tla etsa hore ho kgonahale bakeng sa batshwasi ho tswela pele hanyane-hanyane ho tloha dikepeng tse nyane ho ya ho tse kgolo mme qetellong ho ya ho dikepe tse hwebang matjhabeng.

src: The Protea Coin Series: “The Life of a Legend: NR Mandela” The Natura Coin Series: “Nocturnal Hunters – The Black Backed Jackal” R1 Gold Coin Series: “South African Reptiles – The Nile crocodile” R2 Gold Coin Series: “UNESCO Project: Man and Biosphere” Crown and Tickey Silver Coin Series: “Trains of South Africa” and The Sterling Silver Coin Series: “Marine Protected Areas of South Africa”1.9 Cabinet was briefed on the Rationalisation of Magisterial Districts and Areas of Jurisdiction of the Divisions and Local Seats of the High Court of South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana bakeng sa moralo wa dikhoine tse latelang tsa sehopotso tsa 2015 ke Khamphani ya Aforika Borwa ya Mente, hore o phatlalatswe Koranteng ya Mmuso.

src: It establishes a blueprint which will guide all affected departments, law enforcement agencies and justice institutions to align their operations accordingly.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka Tokisobotjha ya Makgotla a Bomasepala a Ditereke le Dibaka tsa Bolaodi tsa Dikarolo le dibaka tsa Bodulo tsa Lehae tsa Lekgotla le Phahameng la Aforika Borwa.

src: Previously marginalised communities living in the former homelands, self-governing states and rural villages will now benefit from the outcomes of the rationalisation process.
tgt: Porojeke ya tokisobotjha ya makgotla a dinyewe e busetsa morao lefa la ho hloka tekatekano le toka.

src: They will be able to access courts at reduced WEBTOKEN providing access to justice, it is necessary to rationalise the old apartheid-drawn areas of jurisdiction of all the courts, including their composition and structure.
tgt: E theha mohlala o tla tataisa mafapha ohle a amehang, makala a thibelo ya ditlolo tsa molao le ditsha tsa toka bakeng sa ho momahanya ditshebetso tsa ona ka tshwanelo.

src: The rationalisation process ensures that there is an equitable distribution of the courts in the country, to enhance access to courts, which is a fundamental human right enshrined in Section 34 of the Bill of Right in the Constitution.
tgt: Badudi ba neng ba tinngwe menyetla pele dibakeng tsa mehleng tsa mahae, dipuso tse neng di ipusa le metsana ya mahae jwale di tla kgola molemo ho tswa ho diphetho tsa tsamaiso ya tokisobotjha.

src: The amendments alleviate the challenges, legal and administrative, experienced by maintenance beneficiaries, who are mostly women and children.
tgt: Bakeng sa ho fana ka phumantsho ho tsa toka, ho a hlokahala ho lokisa botjha dibaka tsa bolaodi ba makgotla a dinyewe tse neng di thehilwe ke mmuso wa kgethollo, ho kenyeletswa le popo le sebopeho sa ona.

src: This links directly to the key targets of the National Development Plan on economic transformation and social protection.
tgt: Tsamaiso ya tokiso botjha e netefatsa hore ho na le karolelano e lekalekanang ya makgotla a dinyewe ka hara naha, bakeng sa ntlafatso ya ho fihlella makgotla a dinyewe, e leng tokelo ya motheo ya botho jwaloka ha e hlahella ho Karolo 34 ya Bili ya Ditokelo ka hara Molao wa Motheo.

src: The Amendment Bill proposes amendments to the Auditing Profssion Act, 2005, to regulate candidate auditors and to update references to the Companies Act, 1973 so as to align the Auditing Profssion Act with the Companies Act 2008 (Act No.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho hlahiswa ha Maintenance Amendment Bill (Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Tlhokomelo), ya 2014 Palamenteng.

src: 71 of 2008).The aim is to bring aspiring auditors (candidate auditors), before registration, under the Auditing Profssion Act, 2005 so that they are regulated by the Independent Regulatory Board for Auditors, in the same way that registered auditors are regulated, and to make significant amendments required by the Companies Act 2008.
tgt: Bili e fetola Maintenance Act (Molao wa Tlhokomelo), wa 1998 (Molao 99 wa 1998) ho ntlafatsa tsamaiso ya Tlhokomelo le ho ntlafatsa phumantsho ya toka bakeng sa basadi le bana.

src: The Bill proposes the repeal of 16 defence laws that are obsolete and further proposes the amendment of one Act, which does not comply with Section 9 of the Constitution (equality clause).
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho tekwa ha Agrément South Africa Bill (Bili ya Tumellano ya Aforika Borwa) le Memorandamo mabapi la Dipheo tsa Bili Palamenteng.

src: This will bring the defence laws in line with the current constitutional ethos by eliminating discriminatory provisions from the statue book.
tgt: Ho thehwa ha Tumellano ya Aforika Borwa, jwaloka ha ho sisintswe ho Bili ya Tumellano ya Aforika Borwa, ya 2014 ho tla nyehela bakeng sa tswalo ya lekala le matla le ntjhafatsang la kaho le tla amang ka tshwanelo tlhahiso ya mesebetsi ha le nyehela ho merero ya Mmuso ya dikaho tsa motheo.

src: Implementation of Key Government Programmes.1 Cabinet joins South Africans in the celebration of Media Freedom Day on the 19th of October 2014 when President Jacob Zuma hosted veteran journalists and editors as part of celebrating 20 years of press freedom in South Africa.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Bili se sisinya diphethoho ho Auditing Profession Act (Molao wa Lekala la Bohlakisi), wa 2005, ho laola baiketi ba bohlahlobi le ho ntlafatsa tjhebo ho Companies Act (Molao wa Dikhamphani), wa 1973 hore Molao wa Lekala la Bohlakisi o ipapise le Molao wa Dikhamphani wa 2008 (Molao wa 71 wa 2008).Sepheo ke ho tlisa ba lakatsang ho ba bahlahlobi (bahlahlobi ba iketang), pele ho boingodiso, tlasa Molao wa Lekala la Bohlakisi, wa 2005 hore ba tle ba laolwe ke Boto e Ikemetseng bakeng sa Bahlahlobi, ka tsela e tshwanang le eo bahlahlobi ba ngodisitsweng ba laolwang ka yona, le ho etsa diphetho tse bonahalang tse batlwang ke Molao wa Dikhamphani wa 2008.

src: The forum reflects all stakeholders’ collective commitment to the future of mining in South Africa, and to the creation and maintenance of an equitable balance between socio-economic imperatives and investment objectives.
tgt: Khomishene e laetswe ho etsa tlhatlhobo ya melao yohle ya Aforika Borwa bakeng sa ho eletsa mabapi le ho fetolwa ha dipehelo tse sa hlokahaleng, ho batleha kapa tse sa tsamaelaneng le molao wa motheo.

src: Work streams will over a six-week period explore the sector and develop delivery plans which will be released to the public once completed.5 Cabinet received the Medium Term Budget Policy Statement (MTBPS), which provides a summary of the expenditure framework within which national and provincial budgets are being prepared.
tgt: Ho Kenngwa Tshebetsong ha Mananeo a Bohlokwa a Mmuso.1 Kabinete e imatahanya le maAforika Borwa moketeng wa Letsatsi la Tokoloho ya Bophatlalatsi ka la 19 Mphalane 2014 ha Moporesidente Jacob Zuma a memme mekaubere ya boraditaba le bahlophisi jwaloka karolo ya ho keteka dilemo tse 20 tsa tokoloho ya bophatlalatsi ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet reassures South Africans that even in this tough economic climate government will continue to fund its social programmes, infrastructure investments and incentives to support important industries.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela boitlamo bo botjha ho Moralo wa Tumellano bakeng sa Indaseteri ya merafo ya Moshwelella le ho fumana ditharollo tsa nako e telele tsa diphephetso tse tobileng indaseteri ena.4 Kabinete e amohela tsebiso ya Moporesidente Jacob Zuma ka kgatelo pele e entsweng ka Operation Phakisa ho bula bokgoni ba moruo ba mawatle a Aforika Borwa ka tsela ya moshwelella.

src: Cabinet’s Position on Current Issues.1 Cabinet welcomes measures put in place by the Department of Energy to improve the country’s energy security, meet the needs of the economy and create much-needed jobs.
tgt: Moralo wa phano wa Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o re atametsa haufi le ho fihlelleng melemo ya moruo wa mawatle, e ka nyehelang R177 bilione ho Dihlahiswa Kaofela tsa Naha Selemong le ho hlahisa mesebetsi e ka bang milione.

src: The signed agreements add to the pool of nuclear suppliers from which the country can choose for its nuclear procurement programme and mark another milestone in the country’s prioritisation of energy security.
tgt: Makala a tshebetso nakong ya beke tse tsheletseng a tla shebisisa lekala lena le ho ntshetsapele meralo ya phano e tla lokollelwa setjhaba hang feela hae phethetswe.5 Kabinete e amohetse Pehelo ya Leano la Ditekanyetso tsa Nako e Bohareng (MTBPS), e fanang ka kgutsufatso ya moralo wa ditjeho eo ka hara ona ditekanyetso tsa naha le tsa diporofense di lokiswang.

src: This process moves the country a step closer to graduating from the existing nuclear energy plant in Koeberg to a more comprehensive, self-sufficient nuclear industry which is expected to contribute GW of electricity to the national grid.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela mekgwa e phatlaladitsweng ka hara MTBPS ho thibela tshebediso ya ditjhelete ka hara Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba.

src: The National Development Plan commits the country to explore all available energy options to secure our future energy supply.
tgt: Kabinete e rata ho tiisetsa maAforika Borwa botjha hore le ka hara maemo a thata a moruo mmuso o tla tswela pele ho tshehetsa mananeo a setjhaba ka matlole, matsete a dikaho tsa motheo le ditsiane tsa ho tshehetsa diindaseteri tsa bohlokwa.

src: Cabinet supports the efforts by the World Health Organisation in establishing Ebola treatment centres and strengthening capacity for laboratory testing, contact tracing, social mobilisation, safe burials and non-Ebola health care in West Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela mekgwa e kentsweng tshebetsong ke Lefapha la Eneji bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa polokeho ya eneji, ho mekamekana le ditlhoko tsa moruo le ho hlahisa mesebetsi e hlokehang haholo.

src: Government is seized with this issue and will not hesitate act more effectively to combat this scourge.5 Trade and Investment South Africa (TISA), a division of the Department of Trade and Industry (the dti), last week received an award at the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development’s World Investment Forum in Geneva for the promotion of sustainable investment.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela le ho thoholetsa mekgatlo yohle ka ho bula botjha Palamente ya Lesotho ka katleho bekeng e fetileng ho ipapisitswe le Tumellano ya Bonamodi ya Maseru e tsamaiswang ke Motlatsi wa Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa.

src: This was for the work undertaken by TISA in supporting the establishment of Unilever’s Indonesia plant in Ethekwini, which was opened by the Minister of Trade and Industry during South Africa’s hosting of the COP .6 Cabinet received an update on the collapse of the building in Nigeria.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e pheta hore Aforika Borwa e thehile mekgwa e hlokahalang bakeng sa ho thibela Ebola ho nama ka hara naha.

src: Upcoming events.1 President Jacob Zuma will deliver the opening keynote address under the theme “The World as one Big Emerging Market”, at the innovaBRICS & Beyond Conference in London on 27 October 2014.The conference convenes government leaders and businesses with operations or interest in emerging markets, to explore and discuss investment opportunities and challenges within these markets.
tgt: Kabinete e tshehetsa mekutu ya Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Bophelo bo Botle wa ho theha ditsha tsa phekolo ya Ebola le ho matlafatsa bokgoni ba diteko tsa laboratori, ho latela mohlala wa kopano, tsebiso ya setjhaba, dipoloko tsa bafu tse bolokehileng le tlhokomelo ya kalafo eo e seng ya Ebola ho la Aforika Bophirima.

src: Cabinet welcomes the innovaBRICS & Beyond Conference as an opportunity to profile South Africa as an investment destination to United Kingdom-based businesses and other emerging markets.2 President Zuma will receive Burundian President Pierre Nkurunziza on 4 November in Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete hape e ipiletsa ho batho ka bo mong le borakgwebo ka lefatshe lohle ho nyehela ho Letlole la Karabelo ya Ebola le thehilweng ho thusa dinaha tsa Aforika Bophirima tse amehang ntweng ya tsona kgahlanong le lefu lena le kotsi.

src: The visit will deepen our existing strong bilateral relationship with Burundi and advance intra-trade on the continent.3 The Department of Water and Sanitation, in partnership with the African Ministers' Council on Water (AMCOW), the Water Research Commission of South Africa, SADC and Women for Water Partnership, will host the Gender, Water and Development Conference in East London from 3 to 7 November 2014 under the theme: “Gender, Water & Development – the untapped connection”.The agenda of the conference will be set by the AMCOW Policy and Strategy for Mainstreaming Gender in the Water Sector in Africa, which has seven objectives focussing on policy, resources, strategic research, capacity building, cooperation and monitoring and evaluation, to reach the overall objective of gender equality in water policy.4 Cabinet wishes all learners well as they prepare for their year-end examinations.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho tshwarwa ha batho ba tsheletseng ba amahanngwang le boshodu ba dikheibole bo bakileng ho hlokahala ha metsi dikarolong tsa Gauteng.

src: Cabinet also urges parents and guardians to support the 2015 School Governing Body Election from 6 to 28 March 2015 either by standing as candidates or by voting.5 Cabinet calls on all South Africans to support National Disability Rights Awareness Month between 3 November and 3 December 2014 under the theme: “Celebrating 20 years of the rights of persons with disabilities in our Democracy”.Since 1994 we have made major strides in advancing the rights and quality of life of people with disabilities through legislation, policies and social interventions.
tgt: Mmuso o ngongorehile ke taba ena mme o keke wa qeaqea ho sebetsa ka matla ho lwantsha ketso ena.5 Setheo sa Kgwebo le Matsete sa Aforika Borwa (TISA), e leng karolo ya Lefapha la Kgwebo le Indaseteri (dti), bekeng e fetileng le amohetse kgau Sebokeng sa Matjhaba a Kopaneng se mabapi le Kgwebo le Ntshetsopele ya Foramo ya Lefatshe ya Matsete Geneva bakeng sa tshutshumetso ya matsete a moshwelella.

src: According to the Twenty Year Review 1994 – 2014, the Office on the Status of People with Disabilities was established, Integrated National Disability Strategy adopted, and free healthcare, social assistance and inclusive education provided for people with disabilities.
tgt: Sena ke bakeng sa mosebetsi o entsweng ke TISA ka ho tshehetsa ho thehwa ha polante ya Unilever Indonesia ho la Ethekwini, e ileng ya bulwa ke Letona la Lefapha la Kgwebo le Indaseteri nakong ya ho tshwarwa ha COP 17 ke Aforika Borwa.6 Kabinete e behilwe sehlohlolong ka ho putlama ha moaho ho la Nigeria.

src: Key Cabinet decisions Cabinet approved the 16 Days of Activism Campaign under the theme “Count Me In: Together Moving a Non-Violent South Africa forward”.This year (2014) marks the 16th anniversary of this campaign which aims to continue generating awareness on the protection of women and children with more focus on mobilising men and partnering with them to also assist in the fight against this scourge of violence on women and children.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Letsholo la Matsatsi a 16 la Boitseko bo Matla tlasa mokotaba “Nkenyeletse: Mmoho re Ntshetsa Aforika Borwa e Hlokang Dikgoka pele.”Selemo sena (2014) se tshwaya kgopotso ya bo16 ya letsholo lena leo sepheo sa lona e leng ho tswela pele ho fehla temoso mabapi le tshireletso ya basadi le bana ho tsepamisitswe maikutlo haholo ho sebedisweng ha banna le ho ba etsa balekane hore le bona ba thuse ntweng e kgahlanong le leru lena le letsho la dikgoka ho basadi le bana.

src: The campaign will be launched on 25th of November until the 10th December 2014.
tgt: Letsholo le tla thakgolwa ka la 25 Pudungwana ho fihla ka la 10 Tshitwe 2014.

src: Beyond the 16 Days of Activism, there is a year-long programme which will monitor and evaluate the extent to which lives have improved through the implementation of laws and programmes aimed at eradicating violence against women and children.
tgt: Ka nqane ho Matsatsi a 16 a Boitseko bo matla, ho na le lenaneo la selemo kaofela le tla beha leihlo le ho lekola kamoo bophelo bo ntlafetseng ka ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha melao le mananeo ao sepheo sa ona e leng ho fedisa dikgoka kgahlanong le basadi le bana.

src: Cabinet was briefed on the progress report on developing a model for Citizen-based Monitoring.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka tlaleho ya kgatelopele mabapi le ho ntshetsapele mokgwa wa Tlhatlhobo o thehilweng hodima bonkakarolo ba baahi.

src: A pilot project focuses on building the capacity of government to elicit the views of citizens as part of its monitoring mechanism.
tgt: Porojeke ya teko e tsepamisitse maikutlo hodima kaho ya bokgoni ba mmuso ba ho hlakisa maikutlo a baahi jwaloka karolo ya ona ya mekgwa ya tlhatlhobo.

src: The pilot will use existing programmes such as the Community Works Programme and the Community Development Workers programme to upscale the citizen-based monitoring over the Medium Term Strategic Framework period.
tgt: Teko ena e tla sebedisa mananeo a ntseng a le teng a kang Lenaneo la Mesebetsi ya Badudi le lenaneo la Basebeletsi ba Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba ho hodisa tlhatlhobo e thehilweng hodima bonkakarolo ba baahi bakeng sa nako ya Moralo wa Lewa la Nako e Bohareng (MTSF).Teko e ne e tobisitswe ho makala a mafapha a bohlokwa a latelang: Tshebeletso ya Sepolesa sa Aforika Borwa (SAPS), Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle le la Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba le Lekala la Tlhokomelo ya Setjhaba sa Aforika Borwa.

src: This will be extended to other sectors over the course of the Medium Term Strategic Framework period.
tgt: Sena se tla atolosetswa ho makala a mang ha MTSF e ntse e tswela pele.

src: Cabinet approved the deployment of 140 members of the South African Police Service (SAPS) to the Kingdom of Lesotho for the initial period of ninety days with an extension should it be required.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho romelwa ha ditho tse 140 tsa SAPS Naheng ya Lesotho bakeng sa matsatsi a 90 a tumellano a ka eketswang ha ho hlokahala.

src: Immediate SADC intervention was required in the Kingdom of Lesotho following the escalating tensions and the subsequent deterioration of political and security situation in August 2014.
tgt: Boitshunyako bo potlakileng ba Ntshetsopele ya Dinaha tsa Borwa ba Aforika (SADC) bo ne bo hlokahala ka hara Naha ya Lesotho ho latela ditsitsipano tse matla le ho putlama ha maemo a dipolotiki le polokeho tse ileng tsa latela ka la 21 Phato 2014.

src: The SADC intervention is aimed in particular at the attainment of long term political and security stability.
tgt: Boitshunyako ba SADC bo reretswe haholoholo ho fihlellwa ha botsitso ba dipolotiki le polokeho ba nako e telele.

src: The SADC Troika on Politics, Defence and Security of which South Africa is the Chair requested the South African government to support the implementation of the Roadmap of the kingdom of Lesotho.
tgt: Mokgatlo wa Troika wa SADC ho tsa Dipolotiki, Tshireletso le Polokeho moo Aforika Borwa e leng Modulasetulo o ile wa kopa mmuso wa Aforika Borwa ho tshehetsa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Morero wa naha ya Lesotho wa ho ya botsitsong.

src: The deployment of 140 SAPS members commenced on 2 September 2014 and is expected to end on 30 November 2014, should no extension be required.
tgt: Ho romelwa ha ditho tse 140 tsa SAPS ho qadile ka la 2 Loetse 2014 mme ho lebeletswe ho emisa ka la 30 Pudungwana 2014, haeba ho sa hlokahale ho eketswa.

src: South Africa deployed the Police in Lesotho in terms of the South African Police Service Act 1995 (Act No.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e rometse Mapolesa Lesotho ho ya ka Molao wa Tshebeletso ya Sepolesa sa Aforika Borwa wa 1995 (Molao wa bo68 wa 1995) o reng Mokhomishenara wa Naha wa SAPS a ka romela ditho tsa sepolesa kantle ho meedi ya Rephaboliki, ka tumello ya Letona.

src: 68 of 1995) provides that the National Commissioner of the South African Police Service may deploy police members outside the borders of the Republic, with the permission of the Minister.
tgt: Kaha ditho di tla romelwa tlasa thomo ya SADC ho keke ha ba le Memorandamo wa Kutlwanelo pakeng tsa Aforika Borwa le Mmuso wa Lesotho.

src: Since the members will be deployed under the SADC mandate there will be no Memorandum of Understanding between South Africa and the Government of Lesotho.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana thomo ya ditherisano bakeng sa baromuwa ba Aforika Borwa ba tla kenela Seboka se Kopanetsweng sa Mekgatlo (COP) ya bo10 ho Kopano ya Vienna ya bo26 Kopano ya Mekgatlo (MOP) ho Porothokhole ya Montreal mabapi le Dinthwana tse Senyang Moalo wa Ozouno (COP10-MOP26), ya la 17-21 Pudungwana 2014 ho la Paris, Fora.

src: Cabinet approved the negotiating mandate for the South African delegation attending the Joint 10th Conference of the Parties (COP) to the Vienna Convention and the 26th Meeting of the Parties (MOP) to the Montreal Protocol on Substance that Deplete the Ozone Layer (COP10-MOP26), 17-21 November 2014 in Paris, France.
tgt: Kopano ya Vienna le Porothokhole ya Montreal di thehilwe ke Lenaneo la Matjhaba a Kopaneng la Tikoloho ka Sepheo sa ho tshireletsa Moalo wa Ozouno.

src: The Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol were established by the United Nations Environment Programme with the objective of protecting the Ozone layer.
tgt: Tshireletso ya tikoloho bakeng sa meloko ya hajwale le e tlang ke ntlha e ka sehloohong mmoho le tshireletso ya Moalo wa Ozouno.

src: The protection of the environment for present and future generations is a priority and also the protection of the ozone layer.
tgt: Sepheo sa mantlha ke ho sebeletsa ho fihlella taolo e hlwahlwa ya dikhemikhale ka mokgwa wa moshwelella.

src: The primary aim is to work towards environmentally sound management of chemicals in a sustainable manner.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho thehwa ha Lekgotla la Tjhata la Ntshetsopele e batsi ya matlafatso ya batho ba batsho Lekala la Dipalangwang bakeng sa ho beha leihlo le ho lekola ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha dipheo tsa Matlafatso ya Batho ba Batsho Moruong.

src: Implementation of Key Government Programmes.
tgt: Ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Mananeo a Bohlokwa a Mmuso.

src: Cabinet welcomed President Jacob Zuma’s Siyahlola Service Delivery Monitoring Visit to the Mopani District, Giyani in Limpopo Province.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Leeto la Siyahlola la Tlhatlhobo ya Phano ya Ditshebeletso la Moporesidente Jacob Zuma Seterekeng sa Mopani, ho la Giyane Porofenseng ya Limpopo.

src: Service delivery programmes resulted in water being provided to 55 villages in this district and the refurbishment of the Giyani Water Treatment Works, which increased capacity to an additional Megalitres per day.
tgt: Mananeo a phano ya ditshebeletso a ile a baka hore ho fanwe ka metsi metsaneng e 55 ka hara setereke le tlhabollo ya Tshebetso ya Tokiso ya Metsi ya Giyane, e phahamiseditseng mothamo wa metsi ho ya ho dimekalitha tse ka letsatsi.

src: This provision of water will improve sanitation and consequently have a positive impact on the health and wellbeing of residents.
tgt: Phano ena ya metsi e tla ntlafatsa tsamaiso ya dikgwerekgwere mme kahoo e be le kgahlamelo e ntle ho bophelo bo botle ho badudi.

src: Cabinet welcomed the initiative led by Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa that brought together the constituency of National Economic Development and Labour Council on 4 November 2014 to find amicable solutions to workplace conflict at the Labour Relations Indaba.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse boikitlaetso bo eteletsweng pele ke Motlatsi wa Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa bo kopantseng baemedi ba Ntshetsopele ya Naha ya Moruo le Lekgotla la Basebetsi ka la 4 Pudungwana 2014 ho fihlella ditharollo tsa kgotso dikgohlanong tsa dibaka tsa tshebetso ho Indaba ya Dikamano tsa Basebetsi.

src: The delegates attending the Indaba declared as follows, “that constituencies recognise the challenges of unemployment, poverty and inequality facing the South African economy and society.
tgt: Baromuwa ba neng ba kenetse Indaba ba itlamme, “ka hore baemedi ba ananela diphephetso tsa tlhoko ya mesebetsi, bofuma le ho se lekalekane tse tobileng moru le setjhaba sa Aforika Borwa."

src: Notwithstanding any challenges which may constrain current social dialogue, the Nedlac constituencies recognise Nedlac as the key structure under which social dialogue is conducted, and therefore the custodian of any processes that may follow the Labour Relations Indaba (Indaba).The indaba social partners that it will be a launch of a process of engagement, through task teams, that will identify ways of addressing the key challenges considered during the Indaba.
tgt: Ho sa kgathaletsehe diphephetso dife kapa dife tse kginang puisano ya hajwale ya setjhaba, baemedi ba Nedlac ba ananela Nedlac jwaloka sebopeho seo tlasa sona ho etswang dipuisano tsa setjhaba, mme kahoo ke mohlokomedi wa ditsamaiso dife kapa dife tse ka latelang Indaba ya Dikamano tsa Basebetsi.

src: A detailed roadmap of the process will be developed within two months of the Indaba, and the deliberations will begin during January 2015.Cabinet is confident that such engagements between government, business, labour and civil society will contribute to higher economic growth.
tgt: Basemphato ba setjhaba ba indaba ba tla sibolla ho thakgolwa ha tsamaiso ya kopano ka meifo ya tshebetso, e tla hlwaya ditsela tsa ho sebetsana le diphephetso tsa bohlokwa tse ileng tsa elwa hloko nakong ya Indaba.

src: Cabinet welcomed the Deputy President Cyril Ramphosa’s intervention in the reported eviction in the Western Cape farms.
tgt: Morero wa dintlha tse batsi tsa tsamaiso o tla ntshetswapele nakong ya dikgwedi tse pedi tsa Indaba, mme dipuisano di tla qala kgweding ya Pherekgong 2015.Kabinete e na le tshepo ya hore dikopano tse jwalo pakeng tsa mmuso, dikgwebo, basebetsi le badudi di tla nehela kgolong e phahameng ya moruo.

src: The programme, which included the innovaBRICS Conference and Chatham House in London, provided government and South African business leaders with an opportunity to promote South Africa as a prime business destination.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse boitshunyako ba Motlatsi wa Moporesidente Cyril Ramphosa mabapi le ho ntshuwa ha batho ka sheshe matlong mapolasing a Kapa Bophirima.

src: Cabinet welcomed the Auditor General briefing on the audit outcomes of the National and provincial government 2013/14 as this is part of government’s efforts to ensure good governance.
tgt: Dikopano tsa hae le borapolasi le basebeletsi di hlahisitse ditholwana tabeng ena.

src: The South Africa Economic Update, released on Tuesday, 04 November 2014, found that SA’s fiscal policies are cutting the rates of poverty and inequality, and that tax and social benefits are effectively redistributing income from rich to poor.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse tsebiso ya Mohlakisikakaretso wa Ditjhelete mabapi le diphetho tsa tlhatlhobo ya Mmuso wa Naha le wa Diporofense ya 2013/14 kaha sena ke karolo ya mekutu ya mmuso ya ho netefatsa puso e ntle.

src: The report showed that fiscal policy is very progressive in South Africa as it benefits the poor.
tgt: Mmuso o tla nka mehato bakeng sa mosebetsi wa tokiso moo ho hlwailweng bofokodi ke hlakiso.

src: Cabinet reassures South Africans that addressing unemployment remains government’s top priority.
tgt: Kabinete e rata ho netefaletsa maAforika Borwa hore ho etswa tsohle ho sebetsana le mathata ana.

src: While Public Employment Programmes continue to yield results, Cabinet calls on all the social partners to work with government to intensify efforts to create jobs and finding short and long term solutions to the challenge of unemployment.
tgt: Kabinete e lemohile Tekolo ya Kotara ka nngwe ya Basebetsi e bontshitseng tlhoko ya semmuso ya mesebetsi kotareng ya boraro ya selemong sena ho 25.4% ho tloha ho 24.7% nakong e tshwanang selemong se fetileng le ho hlakisa tlhokeho ya tshebetso e matla ka ho fetisisa hore re kgone ho sebetsana le diphephetso tse tharo tsa tlhoko ya mesebetsi, bofuma le ho se lekalekane.

src: Cabinet welcomed the recent rating upgrade of the Industrial Development Cooperation (IDC) by the Fitch Ratings Agency.
tgt: Kabinete e netefaletsa maAforika Borwa hore ho sebetsana le tlhoko ya mesebetsi e dula e le ntlha e ka sehloohong ya mmuso.

src: Cabinet conveys its condolences to the government and people of the Republic of Zambia following the passing of President Michael Chilufya Sata.
tgt: Ha Mananeo a Kgiro ya Setjhaba a tswela pele ho hlahisa ditholwana, Kabinete e ipiletsa ho basemphato bohle ba setjhaba ho sebetsa le mmuso ho matlafatsa mekutu ya ho hlahisa mesebetsi le ho fumana ditharollo tsa nako e kgutshwane le e telele bakeng sa phephetso ya tlhoko ya mesebetsi.

src: Cabinet is saddened by the death of four of the country’s sporting stars and conveys its condolences to the families and friends of professional boxer Phindile Mwelase, Olympic gold medallist Mbulaeni Mulaudzi, former Springbok player Tinus Linee and Bafana Bafana captain Senzo Meyiwa.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse tekolo ya ntlafatso ya haufinyane tjena ya Koporasi ya Ntshetsopele ya Diindaseteri (IDC) ka Lekala la Ditekolo la Fitch.

src: Cabinet also applauded the speedy arrest of one suspect by the South African Police Service last week in the murder of Bafana Bafana captain Senzo Meyiwa and also urge communities to continue working with the Police to bring all suspects to book.
tgt: Kabinete e lebisa matshediso a yona ho mmuso le batho ba Rephaboliki ya Zambia kamora ho hlokahala ha Moporesidente Michael Chilufya Sata.

src: Cabinet welcomes the nine life sentences meted out to Ntokozo Hadebe for his heinous crimes against three young girls in Diepsloot, Johannesburg, as well as the 315-year prison sentence given to Mhlonishwa Elias Mathebula for his reign of terror in Kwazulu Natal.
tgt: Kabinete e utlwisitswe bohloko ke mafu a dikgalala tsa dipapadi tse nne tsa naha mme e fetisa matshediso a yona ho ba malapa le metswalle ya maditebele wa porofeshenale Phindile Mwelase, Mohlodi wa metale wa gauta wa diolimpiki Mbulaeni Mulaudzi, sebapadi sa mehleng sa di-Springbok Tinus Linee le Mokapoteni wa Bafana Bafana Senzo Meyiwa.

src: From 2008 - 2013, Mathebula accosted females on the South Coast, mainly Umzinto, Hibberdene, Dududu and Msinsi by stalking and raping 18 victims, aged from 14 to 40.These sentences send a strong message to criminals that acts of criminality will not be tolerated.
tgt: Tshehetso ya Setjhaba bakeng sa ditshebeletso tsa sehopotso le ho ntshuwa ha maikutlo a tswang botebong di ile tsa re kopanya bohlokong ba rona ha re hopola bahale ba rona ba dipapadi.

src: Cabinet assures South Africans that government is doing everything possible to keep everyone safe and calls on communities to assist the police by reporting criminal activities in their area.
tgt: Kabinete hape e thoholeditse ho tshwarwa ka potlako ha e mong wa babelaellwa ke SAPS polaong ya mokapotene wa Bafana Bafana Senzo Meyiwa mme e kopa badudi ho tswela pele ho sebetsa mmoho le sepolesa ho tshwara babelaellwa kaofela.

src: Cabinet reiterates that the health and port authorities remain on high alert to identify and contain Ebola.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela dikahlolo tsa bophelo bohle tjhankaneng tse robong tse filweng Ntokozo Hadebe bakeng sa botlokotsebe bo sehloho kgahlanong le bananyana ba bararo ba banyenyane ho la Diepsloot, Johannesburg, mmoho le kahlolo ya dilemo tse 315 tsa ho hlola tjhankaneng e filweng Mhlonishwa Elias Mathebula bakeng sa ho hlorisa batho Kwa-zulu Natal.

src: Cabinet congratulates H. Ms Dilma Rousseff, of the Workers Party on her successful re-election as President of the Federative Republic of Brazil following the successful elections in 26 October 2014.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Motlotlehi Moporesidente Moleftenente Mokgenerale Ian Khama Seretse Khama, Moetapele wa Botswana Democratic Party, mabapi le ho kgethwa hape jwaloka Moporesidente wa Rephaboliki ya Botswana, ho latela dikgetho tse atlehileng tsa la 24 Mphalane 2014.

src: Cabinet wishes the new Governor of the South African Reserve Bank, Lesetja Kganyago well as he assumes his position on 9 November 2014.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Motlotlehi Mofumahadi Dilma Rousseff, wa Mokgatlo wa Basebetsi ka ho kgethwa hape ka katleho jwaloka Moporesidente wa Rephaboliki ya Bofederale ya Brazil ho latela dikgetho tse atlehileng tsa la 26 Mphalane 2014.

src: Cabinet also expresses its gratitude to the outgoing Governor Gill Marcus for steering monetary policy well in difficult economic times.
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa mahlohonolo Mmusisi e motjha wa Banka ya Resefe ya Aforika Borwa, Lesetja Kganyago jwaloka ha a tla qala ka mosebetsi wa hae ka la 9 Pudungwana 2014.

src: Cabinet congratulates Chad Le Clos as one of the two overall winners of the FINA (Fédération Internationale de Natation) Swimming World Cup Series which ended in Singapore.
tgt: Kabinete hape e hlahisa teboho ya yona ho Mmusisi ya tlohelang mosebetsi Gill Marcus bakeng sa ho tsamaisa leano la ditjhelete hantle dinakong tse boima tsa moruo.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: President Jacob Zuma will attend the G20 Summit in Brisbane, Australia, from 15 to 16 November 2014.
tgt: Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o tla kenela Seboka sa G20 ho la Brisbane, Australia, ho tloha ka la 15 ho ya ho la 16 Pudungwana 2014.

src: As the only African country represented in the G20, South Africa’s membership provides an opportunity to influence key international policies that could have an impact on our economy, the region and the continent.
tgt: Jwaloka naha e le nngwe e emetseng Aforika ho G20, botho ba Aforika Borwa bo fana ka monyetla wa ho susumetsa maano a bohlokwa a matjhaba a ka bang le kgahlamelo moruong wa rona, lebatowa le kontinente.

src: The SADC facilitator and Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa will pay a visit to Lesotho from 5 – 6 November as part of efforts to consolidate peace and security in the Kingdom.
tgt: Motsamaisi wa SADC le Motlatsi wa Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa o tla etela Lesotho ho tloha ka la 5 – 6 Pudungwana jwaloka karolo ya boitshunyako ba ho tlisa kgotso le polokeho ka hara Mmuso.

src: This follows the recent signing of the Maseru facilitation declaration and the Maseru security accord which lays a basis for the return of Lesotho to political normalcy and the stabilisation of the security situation in the country.
tgt: Sena se latela ho saenwa ha Tumellano ya Bonamodi ya Maseru le kgotso le polokeho Maseru e behang motheo wa ho kgutla ha dipolotiki tse tlwaelehileng tsa Lesotho le maemo a tsitsitseng a polokeho ka hara naha.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch of Operation Phakisa 2: Scaling up Ideal Clinic Realisation and Maintenance Programme.
tgt: Ho Kenngwa Tshebetsong ha Mananeo a Bohlokwa a Mmuso Kabinete e amohela ho thakgolwa ha Operation Phakisa 2: Ho hodiswa ha Lenaneo la Phihlello ya Ditliliniki le Tokiso.

src: This follows Operation Phakisa 1 which focused on unlocking the economic potential of South Africa's oceans.
tgt: Sena se latela Operation Phakisa 1 e neng e tsepamisitse maikutlo ho bulweng ha bokgoni ba mawatle a Aforika Borwa ho tsa moruo.

src: Operation Phakisa 2 seeks to improve the quality of care provided in 3 500 Primary Health Care facilities, consisting of government clinics and Community Health Centres.
tgt: Operation Phakisa 2 e batla ho ntlafatsa boleng ba tlhokomelo eo ho fanwang ka yona ditsheng tse 3 500 tsa tlhokomelo ya Mantlha tsa Kalafo, tse akgang ka hare ditliliniki tsa mmuso le Ditsi tsa Kalafo tsa Badudi.

src: The expected outcomes entails transformation of the existing clinics and Community Health Centres into centres of excellence, which will be used by all South Africans, due to the enhanced quality of services they will provide.
tgt: Diphetho tse lebeletsweng di kenyeletsa ho fetolwa ha ditliliniki tse ntseng di le teng le Ditsi tsa Kalafo tsa Badudi ho ba tsa boqhetseke, tse tla sebediswa ke maAforika Borwa kaofela, ka lebaka la boleng ba ditshebeletso tse ntlafaditsweng tseo di tla fanang ka tsona.

src: Cabinet congratulates the winners of the Batho Pele Excellence Awards, which was held on 14 November 2014.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa bahlodi ba Dikgau tsa Boqhetseke tsa Batho Pele, tse neng di tshwerwe ka la 14 Pudungwana 2014.

src: These awards entrench professionalism and recognise excellence in the public service.
tgt: Dikgau tsena di kgothaletsa boporofeshenale le ho lemoha boqhetseke ka hara tshebeletso ya setjhaba.

src: Cabinet noted that Minister of Sport and Recreation, Minister Fikile Mbalula will host the 2014 South African Sport Awards at the Sandton Convention Centre on 30 November 2014.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse hore Letona la Dipapadi le Boikgathollo, Fikile Mbalula le tla tshwara mokete wa Dikgau tsa Aforika Borwa tsa Dipapadi wa 2014 Setsing sa Seboka sa Sandton ka la 30 Pudungwana 2014.

src: Cabinet encourages sport loving South Africans to be part the South African Sports Awards by voting for the Sports Star of the Year.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa barati ba dipapadi ba Aforika Borwa ho ba karolo ya mokete wa Dikgau tsa Dipapadi tsa Aforika Borwa ka ho kgetha Kgalala ya Dipapadi ya Selemo.

src: Information is available on WEBTOKECabinet congratulates our national sporting teams Bafana Bafana, the Springboks and the Proteas for flying the flag high with their strong performances over the weekend and making South Africa proud.
tgt: Tlhahisoleseding e teng ho WEBTOKEKabinete e thoholetsa dihlopha tsa rona tsa dipapadi Bafana Bafana, di-Springbok le di-Protea ka ho phahamisa folakga ya naha ka tshebetso e matla mafelong a beke le ho etsa Aforika Borwa motlotlo.

src: The naming of Mr AB de Villiers as the International Cricket Council's One Day International (ODI) Cricketer of the Year for scoring 7 000 ODI runs, is commendable.
tgt: Ho kgethwa ha Monghadi AB de Villiers jwaloka Sebapadi sa Kirikete sa Selemo ke Lekgotla la Matjhaba la Kirikete ya Letsatsi le le Leng (ODI) ka ho fihlella dirane tse 7 000 tsa ODI, ho a babatseha.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch of the A Re Yeng Bus Rapid Transport (BRT) service in Tshwane, which started operating from Monday, 17 November 2014.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho thakgolwa ha ditshebeletso tsa Dipalangwang tsa Dibese tsa Potlako tsa A Re Yeng (BRT) ho la Tshwane, ho qadileng ho sebetsa ho tloha ka Mantaha wa la 17 Pudungwana 2014.

src: The A Re Yeng, like other BRT services around the country, forms part of a strategic public transport network that will improve the lives of commuters by providing them with fast, safe, affordable and comfortable urban mobility.
tgt: A Re Yeng, jwaloka ditshebeletso tse ding tsa BRT naha ka bophara, e etsa karolo ya mawala a marangrang a dipalangwang tsa setjhaba a tla ntlafatsa bophelo ba bapalami ka ho ba neha mokgwa wa ho tsamaya o potlakang, o bolokehileng, o kgonehang le o phuthulohileng ditoropong.

src: The construction of these services forms part of government’s infrastructure roll-out programme, which intends to develop a world class infrastructure in South Africa, while creating jobs.
tgt: Kaho ya ditshebeletso tsena e etsa karolo ya phano ya lenaneo la mmuso la dikaho tsa motheo, leo morero wa lona e leng ho ntshetsapele dikaho tsa motheo tsa maemo a hodimo ka hara Aforika Borwa, ha ka ho le leng ho hlahiswa mesebetsi.

src: Key Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved implementation of a comprehensive program to ensure compliance with existing localisation procurement leverage policies and regulations.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha lenaneo le phatlaletseng ho netefatsa boimatahanyo le maano le melawana e ntseng e le teng ya matlafatso ya theko ya dihlahiswa tsa lehae.

src: This includes a policy alignment process to review and strengthen the Preferential Procurement Policy Framework Act, extending the Competitive Supplier Development Program to all strategic State-Owned Companies as well as strengthening departmental regulations (particularly the mining charter) to enable local procurement.
tgt: Sena se kenyeletsa tsamaiso ya ho matahanngwa ha leano la ho sheba botjha le ho matlafatsa Molao wa Moralo wa Leano la Ditheko tse Kgothaletswang, ka ho atolosa Lenaneo la Ntshetsopele ya Bafani ba Phehisanang ho Dikhamphani tsa Mmuso mmoho le ho matlafatsa melawana ya mafapha (haholoholo tjhata ya merafo) ho thusa thekong ya dihlahiswa tsa lehae.

src: This is a powerful instrument for industrialisation which will enhance the competitiveness of national industry, enable the development of new national industrial and technological capabilities, increase exports and achieve deeper black economic empowerment.
tgt: Sena ke sesebediwa se matla bakeng sa diindaseteri tse tla matlafatsa phehisano ya diindaseteri tsa naha, ho thusa kgodiso ya bokgoni ho tsa diindaseteri le thekenoloji, ho eketsa diyantle le ho fihlella matlafatso ya batho ba batsho moruong o tebileng.

src: Cabinet was appraised on the Presidential Local Government Summit, and approved the Back to Basics Programme for Local Government, which is based on building a responsive, caring and accountable local government sector.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa mabapi le Seboka sa Boporesidente sa Mebuso ya Lehae, mme ya tjhaella monwana Lenaneo la ho Boela ho tsa Motheo bakeng sa Mebuso ya Lehae, le itshetlehileng hodima ho aha lefapha la mmuso wa lehae le arabelang, le tsotellang, le le ikarabellang.

src: The Back to Basics Programme will focus planning and operations of all municipalities on the effective delivery of basic municipal services and regular communication with residents.
tgt: Lenaneo la ho Boela ho tsa Motheo le tla tsepamisa maikutlo hodima ho etsa meralo le ditshebetso tsa bomasepala bohle hodima phano e hlwahlwa ya ditshebeletso tsa motheo tsa bomasepala le ho buisana kgafetsa le badudi.

src: The aim is to move from intent to action.
tgt: Sepheo ke ho tloha ho maikemisetso ho ya ho tshebetso.

src: Improvements in the performance of municipalities will improve the living conditions of all South Africans that depend on well-functioning municipalities to lead dignified lives.
tgt: Dintlafatso tshebetsong ya bomasepala di tla ntlafatsa maemo a bodulo a maAforika Borwa ohle a itshetlehileng hodima bomasepala ba sebetsang hantle bakeng sa ho phela ka hlompho.

src: Since 1994, local government has been a primary site for the delivery of service.
tgt: Ho tloha ka 1994, mmuso wa lehae esale e le sebaka sa mantlha sa phano ya tshebeletso.

src: While there has been unprecedented progress in delivering water, electricity, sanitation and refuse removal at local levels, in areas where service delivery is failing we need to put people and their concerns first.
tgt: Ha ho ntse ho na le kgatelopele e sa kgolahaleng ya phano ya metsi, motlakase, tsamaiso ya dikgwerekgwere le ho tloswa ha matlakala boemong ba lehae, dibakeng moo phano ya ditshebeletso e hlolehang re lokela ho beha batho le ditletlebo tsa bona pele.

src: This requires that we move away from the outdated top down service delivery to a culture of Batho Pele and serving communities.
tgt: Sena se batla hore re suthe mokgweng wa rona wa kgale wa ho qala hodimo ebe re ya tlase wa phano ya ditshebeletso ho ya tlwaelong ya Batho Pele le ho sebeletsa badudi.

src: Crucial to this new approach is a system of reporting on, and being accountable for performance.
tgt: Se hlokolosi ka katamelo ena e ntjha ke mokgwa wa ho tlaleha, le ho ikarabella bakeng sa tshebetso.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of South Africa’s Biennial Update Report on Emission Reductions, inclusive of the Final 2000-2010 National Green House (GHG) Inventory, to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa ha Tlaleho ya Habedi ka Selemo ya Pehosehlohlolong ka Diphokotso Tsa Tlhahiso ya Dikgase Moyeng, ho kenyeletswa Dikateng tsa Naha tsa Kgase ya Sepakapakeng (GHG) ya ho qetela ya 2000-2010, ho Seboka sa Matjhaba a Kopaneng sa Meralo e mabapi le ho Fetofetoha ha Tlelaemete (UNFCCC).

src: It provides an overview and analysis of South Africa’s GHG emissions profile and key drivers of change in emissions.
tgt: E fana ka kgutsufatso le tlhatlhobo ya Aforika Borwa mabapi le ho hlahella ha dikgase tsa GHG le ba ka sehloohong ba diphethoho tabeng ya dikgase.

src: It also highlights the comprehensive suite of climate change measures as part of the transition to a low-carbon economy.
tgt: E boetse e hlakisa mokgwa o phatlaletseng wa ditsela tsa ho fetofetoha ha tlelaemete jwaloka karolo ya phethoho ho ya ho moruo wa khabone e fokotsehileng.

src: These include defining desired emission reduction outcomes promoting innovation and investment in renewable energy encouraging energy efficiency creating a national system for greenhouse gas data collection and other instruments such as Carbon Tax.
tgt: Tsena di kenyeletsa ho hlalosa diphetho tsa phokotseho ya dikgase e lebeletsweng ho kgothaletsa ntlafatso le matsete ho eneji e ka hlabollwang botjha ho kgothaletsa tshebediso e hlwahlwa ya eneji ho hlahisa mokgwa wa ho bokella dintlha tsa kgase ya Kgase ya Sepakapakeng le mekgwa e meng e kang Lekgetho la Khabone.

src: This also forms part of South Africa’s international reporting obligation under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).
tgt: Sena hape se etsa karolo ya mosebetsi wa Aforika Borwa wa matjhaba wa ho tlaleha tlasa UNFCCKabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho thehwa ha sehlopha sa tshebetso sa mafapha tlasa Lekala la Tshebedisano ya Matjhaba, Lekala la Kgwebisano le Polokeho ho disa ho kenngwa tshebetsong Tumellano ya Tsamaiso ya Kgwebo ya Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Kgwebo (WTO).Boemo ba Aforika Borwa ke ho sebetsa le dinaha tse ding tsa Aforika ho netefatsa hore ho amohelwa le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Tumellano ya Tsamaiso ya Kgwebo ha bo etse hore Dinaha tsa Aforika di dumele boitlamo boo di hlokang bokgoni ba ho bo jara mme seo se ba kenye diphephetsong ho tsa molao.

src: Cabinet approved the establishment of an inter-departmental task team under the International Cooperation, Trade and Security Cluster to oversee the implementation of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) Trade Facilitation Agreement.
tgt: Ha Aforika Borwa e dutse e itlamme ka ditherisano le mebuso e mengata tlasa Lekgotla la Doha, taba ya rona ke ho batla sephetho se tla boloka sebaka sa rona sa ho latela maano a tshehetsang ntshetsopele ya diindaseteri le phumantsho ya mesebetsi tseo e leng tsona motso wa dipheo tse tekilweng ka hara Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP).Aforika Borwa e tiisitse bohlokwa ba dikatamelo tsa mebuso e mengata tse kenyeletsang ka botlalo ho tshebetso ya mabaka a WTO a loketseng hantle diphetho tse tsitsitseng, tse lekalekanang tse kgotsofatsang ditabatabelo tsa ditho tsa ona kaofela.

src: South Africa’s position is to work with other African countries to ensure that the adoption and implementation of the Trade Facilitation Agreement does not require African countries to accept obligations they do not have the capacity to meet and that expose them to legal challenges.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya behwa sehlohlolong ka Mmaraka wa Kopanelo bakeng sa Aforika e ka Botjhabela le e ka Borwa – Badudi ba Aforika e Botjhabela – Mokgatlo wa Ntshetsopele ya Dinaha tse Aforika e Borwa (COMESA-EAC-SADC) Tumellano ya Kgwebo e Lokolohileng ya Dinaha tse Tharo (TFTA) le hape ho tjhaella monwana boemo ba Aforika Borwa mabapi le TFTBoikitlaetso ba Dinaha tse Tharo ke porojeke ya bohlokwa e eteletsweng pele ke Aforika ka sepheo sa ho susumetsa meruo ya tekano, ho thusa phehisano, phapano ya dihlahiswa, ho kgothaletsa dikgwebo tsa lebatowa, kgwebisano le matsete ka hara mabatowa, le dikaho tsa motheo ho parola le madiboho.
