src: South Africans are reminded that the National Heritage Resources Act of 1999 outlines the consultative processes that should be followed in the case of a removal and or relocation of a statue.
tgt: Leeto la Puso la Zimbabwe.1 Kabinete e amohela leeto la puso la Zimbabwe le neng le eteletswe pele ke Moporesidente Robert Gabriel Mugabe.

src: South Africa and Zimbabwe, have and long history of regional affiliation and cultural ties.
tgt: Aforika Borwa le Zimbabwe, di na le nalane e telele ya bosemphato ba lebatowa le maqhama a botjhaba.

src: The people of Zimbabwe have played a significant historical role in supporting the liberation struggle in South Africa.
tgt: Batho ba Zimbabwe ba bapetse karolo ya bohlokwa nalaneng ya ho tshehetsa ntwa ya tokoloho ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: The visit elevated the bilateral relations with the establishment of the Bi-National Commission as well as the signing of three agreements and two Memoranda of Understanding.
tgt: Leeto le ntlafaditse dikamano tsa dinaha ka bobedi ka ho theha Khomishene ya Naha tse pedi mmoho le ho saena ditumellano tse tharo le Dimemorandamo tse pedi tsa Kutlwisisano (MoU).Tumellano mabapi le Theho ya Khomishene ya Naha tse pedi e ntlafatsa tshebedisano ya rona ho ya maemong a phahameng ka ho fetisisa ka ho kopana ha Dihlooho tse pedi tsa Puso bakeng sa ho sheba botjha kgatelopele mabapi le ditumellano tsa bobedi bona tsa tshebedisanommoho tse ananetsweng.

src: The Agreement on the Establishment of the Bi-National Commission elevates our structured bilateral engagement to the highest level with the two Heads of State meeting to review the progress on the agreed bilateral cooperation agreementsThe Agreement on Cooperation on Water Resources Management and the establishment and functioning of the Joint Water Commission will enhance cooperation in water resources planning, development and management in the spirit of mutual understanding and benefit.
tgt: Tumellano mabapi le Tshebedisanommoho ho Bolaodi ba Mehlodi ya Metsi le ho thehwa le ho sebetsa ha Khomishene e Kopanetsweng ya Metsi e tla ntlafatsa tshebedisanommoho meralong ya mehlodi ya metsi, ntshetsopele le bolaodi ka moya wa kutlwano le molemo.

src: The two countries will jointly undertake a study to understand the water resources potential of the river basins in Zimbabwe to supply water to the Republic South Africa and jointly establish water projects, which will have spin-offs in terms of job creation, economic transformation and skills development and transfer.
tgt: Dinaha tsena tse pedi ka kopanelo di tla etsa diphuputso mabapi le ho utlwisisa bokgoni ba ditsi tsa metsi ho la Zimbabwe bakeng sa ho fana ka metsi ho Rephaboliki ya Aforika Borwa mme ka kopanelo di thehe diporojeke tsa metsi, tse tla bang le molemo mabapi le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi, diphethoho ho tsa moruo le ntshetsopele ya bokgoni le phethisetso.

src: The Agreement Regarding Mutual Assistance between Customs Administrations - Lays the basis for establishing a one-stop border post.
tgt: Tumellano mabapi le Thusano pakeng tsa Ditsamaiso tsa Madiboho- E ala motheo bakeng sa ho theha lediboho le nang le tsohle.

src: This is a standard international model advocated by the World Customs Organisation.
tgt: Sena ke boemo ba motheo wa matjhaba o kgothaletswang ke Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Madiboho.

src: The purpose is to enable the two administrations to exchange information, support each other with technical assistance, and undertake surveillance, visits and investigations together and to co-operate towards enhancing the efficiency of operations.
tgt: Sepheo ke ho kgontsha ditsamaiso tse pedi tsena ho fapanyetsana ka tlhahisoleseding, ho tshehetsana ka thuso ya setekginiki, le ho sebetsa ka peho-leihlo, maeto le diphuputso mmoho le ho sebedisana mmoho mabapi le ho ntlafatsa bohlwahlwa ba ditshebetso.

src: The Memorandum of Understanding on Diplomatic Consultations will establish a mechanism for regular diplomatic talks on issues in Africa and other issues of mutual interest.
tgt: MoU mabapi le Dipuisano tsa Bodipolomate o tla theha mokgwa bakeng sa dipuisano tsa kamehla tsa bodipolomate mabapi le dintlha tse ka hara Aforika le dintlha tse ding tsa dikgahleho tse tshwanang.

src: The key objective of this MoU is to establish a mechanism for regular diplomatic consultations on issues of strengthening bilateral relations, security and cooperation in Africa.
tgt: Sepheo se seholo sa MoU ke ho theha mokgwa bakeng sa dipuisano tsa bodipolomate kamehla mabapi le dintlha tsa ho matlafatsa dikamano tsa bobedi bona, tshireletso le tshebedisanommoho ka hara Aforika.

src: The Memorandum of Understanding on Trade Cooperation aims to provide a platform for the two countries to consult and share experiences towards boosting economic development.
tgt: MoU mabapi le Tshebedisanommoho ya Kgwebisano o reretswe ho fana ka lepatlelo bakeng sa dinaha tse pedi ho buisana le ho arolelana diphihlello mabapi le ho hodisa ntshetsopele ya moruo.

src: The parties agreed to cooperate through trade promotion, resolution of impediments to trade and building of technical capacity in various areas identified as well as general skills developments.
tgt: Bobedi bona bo dumellane ka ho sebedisana mmoho ka kgodiso ya kgwebisano, tharollo ya ditshita tsa ho hweba le ho ahuwa ha bokgoni ba setekginiki dibakeng tse hlwauweng mmoho le ntshetsopele ya bokgoni le boitsebelo.

src: Sefako Makgatho Health Sciences University.
tgt: Yunivesithi ya Disaense tsa Kalafo ya Sefako Makgatho (SMU)4.1 Kabinete e amohela ho thakgolwa ha SMU ke Moporesidente Jacob Zuma Ga-Rankuwa, ho la Gauteng ka la 14 Mmesa 2015.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch of the Sefako Makgatho Health Sciences University (SMU) by President Jacob Zuma in Ga-Rankuwa, Gauteng on 14 April 2015.
tgt: Yunivesithi ena, e kenyeletsang khamphase ya mehleng ya MEDUNSA ya Yunivesithi ya Limpopo, e qadile selemo sa yona sa pele sa dithuto ka selemo sa 2015 ka baithuti ba 5 000.Ho thehwa ha SMU ho fana ka monyetla o hlwahlwa bakeng sa ntshetsopele le thupello ya moloko o motjha wa ditsebi ho tsa kalafo o tla fanang ka kgahlamelo e kgabane bophelong le boitekanelong ba maAforika Borwa a mangata a ntseng a kotetswe ke bofuma le kgaello ya ho fihlella ditshebeletso tsa kalafo.

src: This university, which incorporates the former MEDUNSA campus of the University of Limpopo, started its first academic year in 2015 with 5 000 students.
tgt: SMU ke yunivesithi ya pele e ikemetseng ya tsa kalafo ya ho thehwa ka hara naha.

src: Government will continue to invest in education and skills development as a key driver to economic growth and development.
tgt: Mmuso o tla tswela pele ho tsetela thutong le ntshetsopeleng ya bokgoni jwaloka mokgwa wa bohlokwa wa ho hotetsa kgolo ya moruo le ntshetsopele.

src: Cabinet expressed its gratitude to all South Africans who came out in numbers to participate in direct engagement with public representatives during the National Imbizo Focus Week themed “Together we move South Africa Forward”.
tgt: Beke ya Naha ya Imbizo ya Tsepamiso ya Maikutlo.1 Kabinete e hlahisitse teboho ya yona ho maAforika Borwa oohle a tlileng ka bongata bakeng sa ho nka karolo dipuisanong tse otlolohileng le baemedi ba setjhaba nakong ya Beke ya Naha ya Imbizo ya Tsepamiso ya Maikutlo eo mookotaba wa yona e neng e le “Mmoho re ntshetsa Aforika Borwa pele”.

src: This is a demonstration of a maturing democracy where citizens actively participate in initiatives aimed at making government accountable as envisioned in the National Development Plan.
tgt: Sena ke pontsho ya demokerasi e holang moo baahi ba nkang karolo ka matla boikitlaetsong boo sepheo sa bona e leng ho etsa hore mmuso o ikarabelle jwaloka ha ho lebeletswe ho ya ka Morero wa Naha wa Ntshetsopele.

src: Political principals interacted with communities and unpacked the pronouncements made by President Jacob Zuma during the 2015 State of the Nation Address.
tgt: Boradipolotiki ba ka sehloohong ba ile ba buisana le badudi le ho phahlolla ditsebiso tse entsweng ke Moporesidente Jacob Zuma nakong ya Puo ya Pulo ya Palamente ya 20.2 Imbizo hape e fane ka monyetla ho boradipolotiki ba ka sehloohong ho arolelana le badudi merero ya mmuso ya ho ntlafatsa phano ya ditshebeletso le ho mamela dintlha tse tobileng badudi.

src: Over 70 Izimbizo events took place from the 7 April to 12 April 2015.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse fetang 70 tsa di-Imbizo di etsahetse ho tloha ka la 07 Mmesa ho ya ka la 12 Mmesa 2015.

src: The events culminated on the 12 April, with an innovative “Imbizo Lounge”, which was hosted simultaneously by three political principals in three provinces.
tgt: Diketsahalo di fihlile sehlohlolong ka la 12 Mmesa, ka ntjhafatso ya “Imbizo Lounge”, e neng e tshwerwe ka nako e le nngwe ke boradipolotiki ba bararo ba ka sehloohong diporofenseng tse tharo.

src: Cabinet welcomes the results of research conducted on 161 091 complaints and queries received by the Presidential Hotline from its inception to end of March 2013.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.1 Kabinete e amohela diphetho tsa diphuputso tse entsweng mabapi le ditletlebo le dipatlisiso tse 161 091 tse amohetsweng ho Mohala wa Boporesidente ho tloha esale o thehwa mafelong a Hlakubele 2013.

src: The research established the nature of the cases logged by citizens, identified emerging themes and systemic issues across government.
tgt: Diphuputso di hlahlobile mofuta wa dinyewe tse kentsweng ke baahi, tsa hlwaya meokotaba e hlahellang le mekgwa ya tsamaiso ho parola le mafapha oohle a mmuso.

src: The findings identified a number of issues of concern to citizens that are common across government.
tgt: Diphuputso di hlwaile dintlha tse ngatanyana tse ngongorehisang baahi tse tshwanang ho parola jwalo le mafapha a mmuso.

src: The findings of the research will assist departments in better understanding the issues that concern communities, and the relevant information required by communities.
tgt: Diphetho tsa diphuputso di tla thusa mafapha ho utlwisisa betere dintlha tse ngongorehisang badudi, le tlhahisoleseding e hlokahalang e batlwang ke badudi.

src: Cabinet received an update report on the analysis of the payment of suppliers within 30 days from receipt of a legitimate invoice.
tgt: Boitshunyako bona bo tla ntlafatsa mokgwa oo re sebeletsang badudi ka ona.2 Kabinete e fumane tlaleho ya moraorao mabapi le mohlophollo wa tefo ya bafani ba ditshebeletso nakong ya matsatsi a 30 a ho thola setlankana se molaong sa tefo.

src: Cabinet has noted the progress made, but raised concerns on some of the departments that still face challenges.
tgt: Kabinete e lemohile kgatelopele e entsweng, empa e ile ya hlahisa dingongoreho mabapi le mafapha a mang a ntseng a tobane le diphephetso.

src: A comparative analysis of the National Departments between 2013 January to October and 2014 January to October 2014 showed an improvement of 39% on the average number of invoices paid within 30 days and a 32% improvement on the average number of invoices that were paid after the 30 days.
tgt: Mohlophollo wa papiso mabapi le Mafapha a Naha pakeng tsa 2013 Pherekgong ho ya ho Mphalane le 2014 Pherekgong ho ya ho Mphalane o bontshitse ntlafalo ya 39% mabapi le palohare ya palo ya dintlankana tsa tefo tse lefilweng nakong ya matsatsi a 30 le ntlafalo ya 32% mabapi le palohare ya palo ya ditlankana tsa tefo tse lefilweng kamora matsatsi a 30.Mafapha a Naha a tlalehile ditlankana tsa tefo tse 155 572 tsa boleng ba R3,8 bilione tse lefilweng kamora matsatsi a 30 mme ka nako eo, ditlankana tsa tefo tse 62 887 tsa boleng ba R2,1 bilione tse fetang matsatsi a 30 di ne di so lefuwe.

src: National departments reported 155 572 invoices worth R3,8 billion which were paid after 30 days at the same time, 62 887 invoices worth R2,1 billion invoices older than 30 days had not been paid.
tgt: Mafapha a diporofense bakeng sa nako e tshwanang a bontsha ntlafalo e seng kae ya 5% ho palohare ya palo ya ditlankana tsa tefo tse lefilweng nakong ya matsatsi a Diporofense di tlalehile ditlankana tsa tefo tse 241 332 tsa boleng ba R13,4 bilione tse lefilweng kamora matsatsi a 30 ditlankana tsa tefo tse 356 079 tsa boleng ba R21,8 bilione tse fetang matsatsi a 30 tse neng di so lefuwe.

src: Provincial departments for the same period reveal a marginal improvement of 5% in the average number of invoices paid within 30 days.
tgt: Sena ke putlamo ya 52% ho palohare ya palo ya ditlankana tsa tefo tse fetang matsatsi a 30 le tse neng di so lefuwe.

src: This is a 52% regression in the average number of invoices that is older than 30 days and which have not been WEBTOKEN order to assist departments that are still struggling, Cabinet approved the establishment of a special unit within the Department for Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation to follow up with persistently struggling departments.
tgt: Bakeng sa ho thusa mafapha a ntseng a sokola, Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho thehwa ha lekala le ikgethang ka hara Lefapha la Merero, Bodisa le Tlhatlhobo ya Tshebetso ho shebana le mafapha a ntseng a tswella ho sokola.

src: The Unit will work collaboratively with National Treasury and the Department of Public Service and Administration (DPSA).In addition a national hotline will be publicised that will be available to suppliers to log instances of delayed payment.
tgt: Lekala lena le tla sebetsa mmoho le Lefapha la Matlotlo a Setjhaba le Lefapha la Tshebeletso ya Mmuso le Taolo (DPSA).Ho phaella hodima moo ho tla phatlalatswa mohala wa naha o tla ba teng bakeng sa bafani ba ditshebeletso ho tlaleha maemo moo ditefello di diehisitsweng.

src: This will be taken up with the relevant department and responses will be reported on.
tgt: Sena se tla iswa ho lefapha le amehang mme dikarabelo di tla tlalehwa.3 Kabinete e lemohile tlaleho mabapi le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Lenaneo la Ditsiane la Tlhatlhobo ya Thekiso ya ka Ntle le Thuso ya Matsete (EMIA) le ho boela e amohela karabelo le moralo wa bolaodi wa Lefapha la Kgwebo le Diindaseteri.

src: Cabinet noted the report on the Implementation Evaluation of the Export marketing and Investment Assistance (EMIA) Incentive Programme and further welcomed the management response and improvement plan by the Department of Trade and Industry.
tgt: Sena se entse karolo ya Morero wa Naha wa Tlhahlobo wa 2013/14 ho lekola bohlwahlwa ba Lenaneo bakeng sa ho tshehetsa bahlahisi ba Aforika Borwa le ba romelang thepa mafatsheng a ka ntle.

src: This formed part of the 2013/14 National Evaluation Plan to assess the effectiveness of the Programme in supporting South African manufacturers and exporters.
tgt: EMIA e thusitse dikgwebo tse 6 766 tse romelang thepa mafatsheng a ka ntle ho parola le diporofense le ho ho lefa ditseko tsa palo ya boleng ba R510 milione ho tloha ka 2009/10 ho ya ka 2012/13.

src: These supported enterprises have created 24 802 jobs.
tgt: Dikgwebo tsena tse tsheheditsweng di hlahisitse mesebetsi e 24 802.

src: The survey of EMIA participants suggests significant usage of the EMIA incentives by mostly Historically Disadvantaged Individuals and women-owned firms.
tgt: Tekolo ya bankakarolo ba EMIA e bontsha tshebediso e kgabane ya ditsiane tsa EMIA ke bongata ba batho ba neng ba Tinngwe Menyetla ho ya ka Nalane le difeme tseo beng ba tsona e leng basadi.4 Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana moralo wa Tokomane ya Leano la Naha la ho Betjha e tla phatlalatswa ho Koranta ya Mmuso bakeng sa dipuisano tse pharaletseng le setjhaba.

src: Cabinet approved for the draft National Gambling Policy Document to be published in the Government gazette for wider public consultation.
tgt: Sepheo sa yona ke ho ntlafatsa bohlwahlwa ba ho laola ho betjha, ho ntlafatsa kgokahano le tshebedisanommoho le diporofense le ho fetola maemo botjha a Boto ya Naha ya ho Betjha jwaloka molaodi bakeng sa sebetsana ka bokgabane le ho betjha ho seng molaong.5 Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana phatlalatso ya moralo wa Leano la Tahi bakeng sa dipuisano tse pharaletseng le setjhaba.

src: It aims to improve effectiveness in regulating gambling, improve coordination and cooperation with provinces and repositions the National Gambling Board as a regulator to deal more effectively with illegal gambling.
tgt: Moralo wa Leano la Tahi o tla ntlafatsa bohlwahlwa ba ho laola kgwebo ya tahi le ho thibela kgwebo e seng molaong.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the draft Liquor Policy for wider public consultation.
tgt: Hara dintlha tse ding, ditshisinyo di tobane le kgahlamelo ya tahi ho moruo wa kahisano le ditholwana tsa tshebediso e mpe ya tahi mmoho le diphethoho indasetering ya tahi.6 Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka diphetho tsa tlhatlhobo e tebileng ya Ntlafatso ya Kgodiso ya Bana moo ditlhatlhobo tse tebileng di ileng tsa etswa bakeng sa Kereiti ya R le boitshunyako ba tsa phepo bakeng sa bana ba ka tlasa dilemo tse hlano.

src: Cabinet was briefed on the outcomes of a diagnostic evaluation of Early Childhood Development where detailed evaluations were undertaken for Grade R and nutrition interventions for children under five.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ntshetsopele ya Moralo o Kopanetsweng wa Naha wa Phepo bakeng sa Aforika Borwa, oo ka kakaretso o sebetsanang le phepo, ho kenyeletsa nako ya pele ho tswalo, matsatsi a 1 000 a pele a ho phela, ntlafatso ya kgodiso ya bana le Kereiti ya Moralo wa ntlafatso ho tloha ho tekolo mabapi le “Kgahlamelo ya ho Hlahiswa ha Kereiti ya R hodima Diphetho tsa ho Ithuta” o toboketsa ho ntlafatswa ha boleng ba Kereiti ya R bakeng sa ho phahamisa kgahlamelo ya ona ho bana ba futsanehileng le diporofense tse sa sebetseng hantle.

src: Cabinet approved the development of an integrated National Nutrition Plan for South Africa, which holistically addresses nutrition, including the pre-conception period, the first 1 000 days of life, early childhood development and Grade The improvement plan from the evaluation on “The Impact of the Introduction of Grade R on Learning Outcomes” emphasises improving the quality of Grade R to maximise its impact on poor children and in poorly performing provinces.
tgt: Sena se kenyeletsa thupello le ntshetsopele ya matitjhere a Kereiti ya R le ho nkela hloohong thonyo ya batho ba nang le mangolo a phahameng (maemo a NQF a bo5) a amehang bakeng sa morero ona.

src: This includes the training and development of Grade R teachers and consideration for the appointment of individuals in possession of the relevant higher certificate qualification (NQF level 5) for this purpose.
tgt: Dibili.1 Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho lokollwa ha Bili ya Inshorense, ya 2015 bakeng sa dipuisano le setjhaba.

src: The Bill is aligned to the National Development Plan, ensures a sound and well-regulated insurance sector, and promotes financial stability that will support sustainable economic growth by giving effect to higher prudential standards that have been developed in light of the 2008 financial crisis.
tgt: Bili ena e matahantswe le Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha, e netefatsa lekala le hlwahlwa le laolwang hantle la inshorense, le ho hodisa botsitso ho tsa ditjhelete bo tla tshehetsa kgolo ya moruo ya moshwelella ka ho fana ka kgahlamelo ho maemo a phahameng a toka a hlahisitsweng ha ho shejwa koduwa ya ditjhelete ya 2008.

src: It gives effect to a new prudential framework for the insurance sector.
tgt: E fana ka kgahlamelo ho moralo o lokileng o motjha bakeng sa lekala la inshorense.

src: The Solvency Assessment and Management regime seeks to introduce a new, forward-looking risk-based approach to insolvency by aligning the capital requirements with the underlying risks of an insurer.
tgt: Bolaodi ba Tekolo ya Bokgoni ba Paballo ya Tjhelete le Taolo bo batla ho hlahisa katamelo e ntjha, e nang le tjhebelopele e itshetlehileng hodima dikotsi tsa ho tjhona ka ho matahanya ditlhoko tsa tjhelete tse teng le dikotsi tsa ya fanang ka inshorense.

src: It also provides incentives to insurers to adopt more sophisticated risk monitoring and management tools.
tgt: Hape e fana ka ditsiane ho beng ba inshorense ho imatahanya le mekgwa e hlwahlwa ya ho beha leihlo le ho laola.

src: These measures seek to ensure better protection of policyholders and beneficiaries and contribute to financial stability.
tgt: Mekgwa ena e batla ho netefatsa tshireletso e betere ya beng ba dipholisi le bakgolamolemo le ho nyehela ho botsitso ho tsa ditjhelete.2 Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana phatlalatso ya moralo wa Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Setsi sa Merero ya Mautlwela a tsa Ditjhelete, sa 2014 bakeng sa dipuisano le setjhaba.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the draft Financial Intelligence Centre Amendment Bill, 2014 for public comment.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Bili se sisinya dihlomathiso ho Molao wa Setsi sa Merero ya Mautlwela a tsa Ditjhelete (Molao wa 38 wa 2001).

src: The Amendment Bill proposes amendments to the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (Act No.
tgt: Sena ke ho sebetsana le ditshoso tsa botsitso ba tsamaiso ya rona ya tsa ditjhelete tse hlahiswang ke dikadimo tse bohlaswa tsa ditjhelete le thuso ya boferekanyi ka ditjhelete ka ho netefatsa boimatahanyo le mekgwa ya matjhaba le dipehelo, ka hara moralo wa melao ya Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet noted with concern a sharp increase in road fatalities during the Easter weekend, which saw 208 accidents that resulted in 287 deaths, compared to last year’s number of fatalities, which stood at 193 deaths from 148 accidents.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.1 Kabinete e ananetse hore Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o tla be a araba dipotso Palamenteng ka Labone, 16 Mmesa 20.2 Kabinete e amohela Leeto la Puso ho ya Jakarta, Indonesia la Moporesidente Jacob Zuma ho tloha ka la 19 ho isa ho la 21 Mmesa 2015, le tla sheba botjha maemo a dikamano tsa bobedi bona ho netefatsa phihlello ya dilemo tse hlano tsa ‘Morero wa Tshebetso’, jwaloka ha o ile wa tshohlwa ke mahlakore ka bobedi Pretoria ka Pudungwana 2014.Moporesidente Jacob Zuma hape o tla kenela Seboka sa Asia-Aforika mahareng a la 22 ho isa ho la 23 Mmesa ho la Jakarta, se tla matlafatsa tshebedisanommoho ya dinaha tse ka borwa ba ekhweita e tla lebisa kgolong ya moruo wa kahisano bakeng sa mabatowa ka bobedi.

src: Road safety is the responsibility of all South Africans and the success of our road safety campaigns depend on all road users doing their part.
tgt: Leeto lena le tla phethelwa ka Sehopotso sa bo60 sa Seboka sa Bandung sa 1955 le Sehopotso sa bo10 sa Bosemphato se Setjha sa Mawala (NAASP) ka la 24 Mmesa 2015, se tla tshwarwa Bandung, ho la West Java.

src: Drivers must obey the rules of the road, not drink and drive, keep to the speed limit and ensure that their vehicles are roadworthy.
tgt: E ne e le Bandung moo baetapele ba mokgatlo wa rona e leng Moses Kotane le Maulvi Cachalia ba ileng ba tlisa dipehelo tsa ho hloka semorabe le boikemelo lenaneong la lefatshe.3 Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa oohle ho kenela Mekete ya Kgwedi ya Tokoloho, e tlisang dilemo tse mashome a mararo tsa tokoloho ka ho kgothaletsa seriti sa botho le ho tsitlallela mohopolo o tshwanang o tla lebisa kahong ya Aforika Borwa e kopaneng le ho atleha.

src: On behalf of the South African people, Cabinet, expresses its deepest condolences to the government and the people of the Republic of Kenya, especially families of the victims who died in the senseless attack at Garissa University College on 2 April 2015.Cabinet joins President Jacob Zuma in condemning this act of terror and reiterates that South Africa supports Kenya and the international community's efforts at peacekeeping, stability, democracy and nation-building in Somalia.3 Cabinet congratulates the people of Nigeria for conducting a peaceful, transparent credible, free and fair election on the 28 March 2015, as declared by the Independent National Elections Commission of Nigeria.
tgt: Mokete wa rona wa naha o tla phethelwa ka Letsatsi la Tokoloho, 27 Mmesa 2015 tlasa mookotaba: “Re Keteka Qalo ya Dilemo tse Mashome a Mararo tsa Tokoloho ya rona ka ho Akofisa Diphethoho tse Matla tsa Moruo”.MaAforika Borwa a boela a hopotswa ka ho intsha sehlabelo ka matla ha batho ba bo rona le basadi ntweng kgahlanong le tsamaiso e soto ya kgethollo hore re tle re thabele tokoloho eo re nang le yona kajeno.

src: On behalf of South Africans, Cabinet congratulates General Muhammad Buhari on his election as the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.4 Cabinet congratulates Marlene van Niekerk for becoming the first South African to be shortlisted for the Man Booker International Prize.
tgt: Bakeng sa ho hlompha maAforika Borwa a nyehetseng ntshetsopeleng ya demokerasi ya rona, Moporesidente Jacob Zuma ka Letsatsi la Tokoloho o tla fana ka Dikgau tsa Naha moketeng o tla beng o tshwaretswe Meahong ya Kopano.

src: Recent attacks on foreign nationals.
tgt: Ditlhaselo tsa moraorao tjena tsa melata.

src: Cabinet welcomes the peace and calm that has begun to prevail in communities that were affected by the recent attacks on foreign nationals.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela kgotso le kgutso e bonahalang e leng teng metseng e neng e anngwe ke ditlhaselo tsa moraorao tjena tsa melata.

src: Cabinet commended the departments that worked through the National Joint Operation Centre to stop the acts of violence that took place in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholeditse mafapha a sebeditseng ka Setsi sa Naha sa Tshebetso sa Kopanelo bakeng sa ho fedisa diketso tsa merusu tse etsahetseng KwaZulu-Natal le Gauteng.

src: Cabinet commended the provincial and municipal leaders in affected areas for their role in providing relief and leading the process of reintegration of foreign nationals into communities.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholeditse baetapele ba diporofense le bomasepala dibakeng tse neng di amehile bakeng sa karolo ya bona ya ho fana ka pebofaletso le ho etella pele morero wa ho kopanya botjha melata le badudi.

src: In the past week, President Jacob Zuma convened stakeholder meetings with the representatives of business, religious group, labour, civil society and foreign nationals.
tgt: Bekeng e fetileng, Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o ile a bitsa dikopano tsa bankakarolo le baemedi ba dikgwebo, dihlopha tsa bodumedi, mekgatlo ya basebetsi, ya setjhaba le ya melata.

src: The engagements were constructive to assist in taking the process forward.
tgt: Dipuisano e ne e le tse ahang bakeng sa ho thusa tabeng ya ho ntshetsa tsamaiso ena pele.

src: All participants were unanimous in expressing their condemnation of these attacks and committed to work with government in finding a lasting solution.
tgt: Bankakarolo bohle ba ile ba dumellana ka lentswe le le leng tabeng ya ho hlahisa ho tshwela ka mathe ditlhaselo tsena le ho itlama ho sebetsa le mmuso ho fumaneng tharollo ya moshwelella.

src: The recently appointed Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) on Migration is working to find a lasting solution to issues raised by communities and foreign nationals.
tgt: Komiti e Kopanetsweng ya Matona (IMC) e thontsweng moraorao tjena mabapi le Bofalli e sebetsa bakeng sa ho fumana tharollo ya moshwelella mabapi le dintlha tse hlahisitsweng ke badudi le melata.

src: Key Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet was briefed on the progress made on the Immovable Asset Register of the National Government.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka kgatelopele e entsweng mabapi le Rejisetara ya Thepa e sa Sutheng ya Mmuso wa Naha.

src: A Real Estate Registry Services Division has been established with effect from 1 April 2015.
tgt: Lekala la Ditshebeletso tsa Boingodiso ba Matlo le se le thehilwe ho tloha ka la 01 Mmesa 2015.

src: The division will be managed within the Property Management Trading Entity and will oversee State immovable assets.
tgt: Lekala lena le tla laolwa ka hara Setheo sa Bolaodi ba Kgwebisano ya Thepa ya Bodulo mme le tla okamela thepa ya Puso e sa sutheng.

src: It will serve as a single repository of State immovable assets, and will provide an oversight, regulatory and monitory structure the State Immovable Asset Register.
tgt: Le tla sebetsa jwaloka setsi sa poloko se le seng sa thepa e sa sutheng ya Puso, mme le tla fana ka bodisa, bolaodi le peho-leihlo ya Rejisetara ya Thepa e sa Sutheng ya Mmuso.

src: Cabinet approved the release of the Draft Policy on the Customary Practice of Initiation for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho lokollwa ha Moralo wa Leano mabapi le Lebollo la Setso bakeng sa hore setjhaba se tshwaele ka ona.

src: The policy seeks to protect, promote and regulate initiation by proposing acceptable norms and standards and also provide for structures at national and provincial level.
tgt: Morero wa leano lena ke ho batla ho tshireletsa, ho kgothaletsa le ho laola lebollo ka ho sisinya mekgwa le maemo a amohelehang mme hape le ho qala mekgatlo boemong ba naha le ba diporofense.

src: It will ensure the initiations take place in a controlled environment.
tgt: Le tla netefatsa hore mabollo a etsahala ka hara tikoloho e laolehang.

src: This forms part of the steps that government is taking to reinforce appropriate, acceptable customs practices and restore an acceptable level of accountability that sustained the practice over many years.
tgt: Sena se etsa karolo ya mehato e nkuwang ke mmuso ho hatella mekgwa e nepahetseng, e amohelehang ya mesebetsi ya setso le ho busetsa maemo a amohelehang a boikarabello ao esale a sebediswa bakeng sa dilemo tse telele.

src: Cabinet approved the intergovernmental Human Settlement Programme for the Nelson Mandela Bay Municipality which will use the Housing Development Agency as the implementing agent.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Lenaneo le kopanetsweng la mmuso la Bodulo ba Batho bakeng sa Masepala wa Nelson Mandela Bay le tla sebedisa Lekala la Ntshetsopele ya Matlo jwaloka motjha wa ho kenya mesebetsi ya lona tshebetsong.

src: Cabinet approved the hosting of the International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions Annual World Library Information Congress in Cape Town from 15 to 21 August 2015 under the theme "Dynamic Libraries: Access, Development and Transformation".
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho tshwarwa ha Seboka sa Matjhaba sa Mekgatlo ya Dilaeborari le Ditheo tsa Seboka sa Selemo le Selemo sa Tlhahisoleseding ya Dilaeborari tsa Lefatshe ho la Motse Kapa ho tloha ka la 15 ho isa ho la 21 Phato 2015 tlasa mookotaba "Dilaeborari tse Hlwahlwa: Phihlello, Ntshetsopele le Diphethoho".

src: Cabinet approved the tabling of the Protocol to Eliminate Illicit Trade on Tobacco Products.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho tekwa ha Tumellano ya ho Fedisa Kgwebo e seng Molaong ya Dihlahiswa tsa Kwae.

src: This is in accordance with the World Health Organization Framework Convention on Tobacco Control which South Africa ratified in April 2005.
tgt: Sena ke ho ya ka Seboka sa Moralo wa Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Bophelo bo Botle mabapi le Taolo ya Kwae oo Aforika Borwa e o tjhaelletseng monwana ka Mmesa 2005.

src: The protocol will assist countries to take global action against the illicit trade in tobacco products especially on countries that are signatories to the Protocol.
tgt: Tumellano e tla thusa dinaha ho nka mehato ya lefatshe kgahlanong le kgwebo eo e seng molaong ya dihlahiswa tsa kwae haholoholo dinaheng tse saenetseng Tumellano.

src: Cabinet’s position on current issues.
tgt: Maemo a Kabinete mabapi le dintlha tsa hajwale.

src: Cabinet expressed its condolences to the families of those who died in recent public transport accidents which included a collision of two busses in Johannesburg last week and a collision of trains this week at Denver Station south of Johannesburg.
tgt: Kabinete e hlahisitse matshediso a yona ho malapa a bao ba hlokahalletseng dikotsing tsa dipalangwang tsa moraorao tjena tse ileng tsa kenyeletsa ho thulana ha dibese tse pedi Johannesburg bekeng e fetileng le ho thulana ha diterene bekeng ena Seteisheneng sa Denver ka borwa ho Johannesburg.

src: Cabinet is confident the investigation by the relevant departments will establish the causes of these accidents and ensure such accident do not happen.
tgt: Kabinete e tshepa hore dipatlisiso ka mafapha a amehang di tla fatolla disosa tsa dikotsi tsena le ho netefatsa hore dikotsi tse kang tsena ha di etsahale.

src: Cabinet joins President Zuma in conveying its condolences to the family, friends and entire football fraternity on the passing of former Bafana Bafana football legend John “Shoes” Moshoeu who was buried on Monday, 27 April 2015.
tgt: Kabinete e imatahanya le Moporesidente Zuma ka ho fetisa matshediso a yona ho lelapa, metswalle le ho barati bohle ba bolo ya maoto ka ho hlokahala ha qhoku ya mehleng ya Bafana Bafana John “Shoes” Moshoeu ya bolokuweng ka Mantaha, 27 Mmesa 2015.

src: He will always be remembered as a supremely talented footballer who played a central role in our triumph at the 1996 Africa Cup of Nations.
tgt: O tla dula a hopolwa jwaloka sebapadi sa bolo se neng se na le talente e babatsehang haholo se bapetseng karolo ya bohlokwa tlholong ya rona ya Mohope wa Dinaha tsa Aforika wa 1996.

src: Cabinet joins President Zuma in conveying condolences to the Government and people of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal, following a massive earthquake on Saturday, 25 April 2015, that claimed thousands of lives.
tgt: Kabinete e imatahanya le Moporesidente Zuma ka ho fetisa matshediso ho Mmuso le batho ba Rephaboliki ya Demokerasi ya Bofederale ya Nepal, ho latela ho reketla ha lefatshe ho matla ka Moqebelo, 25 Mmesa 2015, ho nkileng maphelo a batho ba dikete.

src: Cabinet commends the South African non-governmental organizations who have already dispatched humanitarian aid to Nepal.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa mekgatlo eo e seng ya mmuso ya Aforika Borwa eo e seng e rometse dithuso tsa botho Nepal.

src: Cabinet expressed its deepest condolences to the family of Brigadier General Bita who died at the age of 75 in Tanzania.
tgt: Kabinete e hlahisitse matshediso a tebileng ho lelapa la Moborikadiri Mokgenerale Bita ya hlokahetseng a le dilemo tse 75 ho la Tanzania.

src: Brig-Gen Bita served as the Executive Secretary of the Liberation Committee of the then Organization of African Unity (OAU).
tgt: Moborikadiri Mokgenerale Bita o sebeditse jwaloka Mongodi wa Phethahatso wa Komiti ya Tokoloho ho Mokgatlo wa Kopano ya Aforika (OAU) wa mehleng.

src: He was the recipient of the Order of the Companions of OR Tambo in Gold, the highest honor that South Africa bestows on foreign nationals.
tgt: E ne e le moamohedi wa Kgau ya Metswalle ya O. Tambo ya Gauta, e leng tlhompho e kgolohadi eo Aforika Borwa e fanang ka yona ho melata.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: President Zuma will attend the 70th Anniversary of the Victory of the Great Patriotic War (World War II) at Red Square in Moscow on 9 May 2015.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla kenela Sehopotso sa bo70 sa Tlholo e Kgolo ya Ntwa ya Lerato la Naha (Ntwa ya Lefatshe ya II) Red Square ho la Moscow ka la 9 Motsheanong 2015.

src: He will also have a bilateral engagement with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
tgt: O tla boela a tshware dipuisano tsa dinaha ka bobedi le Moporesidente wa Russia Vladimir Putin.

src: This visit will build on our current bilateral relations with the Russian Federation to further advance cooperation in a number of fields.
tgt: Leeto lena le tla ahella hodima dikamano tsa hajwale tsa bobedi bona le Mokgatlo wa Russia bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa ho ya pele tshebedisanommoho dintlheng tse ngatanyana.

src: In the celebration of Workers’ Day tomorrow (1st May 2015), Cabinet calls on all workers to unite and build South Africa’s economy, and contribute to the continent and the world.
tgt: Bakeng sa ho keteka Letsatsi la Basebetsi (1 Motsheanong 2015), Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho basebetsi bohle ho kopana le ho aha moruo wa Aforika Borwa, le ho nehela ho kontinente le lefatshe.

src: Since 1994 government has advanced workers’ rights which resulted in workers benefitting from the generation of progressive labour and social protection benefits.
tgt: Ho tloha ka 1994 mmuso o ntsheditse pele ditokelo tsa basebetsi e leng se bakileng hore basebetsi ba kgole molemo ho tloha tlhahisong ya basebetsi ba tswelang pele le tshireletso ya melemo ya kahisano.

src: National departments will present their budget votes to Parliament between 5th and 21st May 2015 to highlight their priority activities for the current financial year.
tgt: Mafapha a Naha a tla teka dipuo tsa ona tsa ditekanyetso Palamenteng mahareng a la 5 le la 21 Motsheanong 2015 ho hlakisa mesebetsi ya ona e ka sehloohong bakeng sa selemo sa hajwale sa ditjhelete.

src: Cabinet calls on South Africans to follow the budget votes on various media platforms to better understand when Ministers outline plans for Governments Programme of Action (PoA).
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa oohle ho latela dipuo tsa ditekanyetso mapatlelong a fapafapaneng a boraditaba hore a tle a utlwisise betere ha Matona a hlahisa meralo bakeng sa Lenaneo la Tshebetso la Mmuso (PoA).

src: The Department of Tourism and South African Tourism will hold INDABA 2015 from 9 to 11 May 2015 at the Inkosi Albert Luthuli International Convention Centre in Durban.
tgt: Lefapha la Bohahlaodi mmoho le ba Bohahlaodi ba Aforika Borwa ba tla tshwara INDABA 2015 ho tloha ka la 9 ho isa ho la 11 Motsheanong 2015 Setsing sa Matjhaba sa Dikopano sa Inkosi Albert Luthuli ho la Durban.

src: This Pan-African event is a critical platform to promote our tourism products to the international market.
tgt: Ketsahalo ena ya seAforika ke lepatlelo le hlokolosi bakeng sa ho hodisa dihlahiswa tsa rona tsa bohahlaodi mmarakeng wa matjhaba.

src: It also supports the strategic vision of the National Tourism Sector Strategy to grow international arrivals to 15 million by 2020 and therefore create 225 000 new jobs.
tgt: Hape e tshehetsa pono ya mawala a Lekala la Naha la Mawala a Bohahlaodi bakeng sa ho hodisa palo ya baeti ba matjhaba ba kenang ka hara naha ho ya ho 15 milione ka 2020 mme kahoo ho hlahiswe mesebetsi e 225 000 e metjha.

src: Cabinet welcomes the 5th Gender Summit Africa, the first to be held on the African continent.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela Seboka sa bo5 sa Bong sa Aforika, e leng sa pele ho tshwarelwa kontinenteng ya Aforika.

src: The summit took taking at the Cape Town International Convention Centre.
tgt: Seboka se tshwaretswe Setsing sa Matjhaba sa Dikopano ho la Motse Kapa.

src: The summit is a platform for groups and organizations across all levels of scientific research to address gender issues of mutual concern.
tgt: Seboka ke lepatlelo bakeng sa dihlopha le mekgatlo ho parola le maemo oohle a diphuputso tsa saense bakeng sa ho sebetsana le dintlha tsa bong tse amang bohle.

src: The summit hosted by the Human Sciences Research Council strengthens Africa’s research agenda so that science, technology, infrastructure, capital, skills and data can better support the development of the continent.
tgt: Seboka sena se tshwarweng ke Lekgotla la Diphuputso tsa Disaense tsa Botho se matlafatsa lenaneo la Aforika la diphuputso hore saense, thekenoloji, dikaho tsa motheo, tjhelete, bokgoni le tlhahisoleseding di kgone ho tshehetsa betere ntshetsopele ya kontinente.

src: The Department of Water and Sanitation will mark Sanitation and Hygiene Week from 11 to 15 May 2015 under the theme “It’s not all about flushing”.The week, which was first introduced at the Global WASH Forum held in Dakar, Senegal in 2004, aims to raise awareness on the importance of sanitation and promotes sanitation best practices.
tgt: Lefapha la Metsi le Tsamaiso ya Dikgwerekgwere le tla tshwaya Beke ya Tsamaiso ya Dikgwerekgwere le Bohlweki ho tloha ka la 11 ho isa ho la 15 Motsheanong 2015 tlasa mookotaba “Ha se feela ka ho folasha”.Beke ena, e ileng ya kgakolwa la pele Foramong ya Global WASH e neng e tshwaretswe Dakar, ho la Senegal ka 2004, e reretswe ho hlahisa temoso ka bohlokwa ba tsamaiso ya dikgwerekgwere le ho hodisa ditshebetso tse hlwahlwa tsa tsamaiso ya dikgwerekgwere.

src: Since 1994 government has made great strides in the provision of access to water and sanitation.
tgt: Ho tloha ka 1994 mmuso o entse menyabuketso e meholo bakeng sa phano ya ho fihlella metsi le tsamaiso ya dikgwerekgwere.

src: Key issues in the environment.
tgt: Dintlha tsa Bohlokwa ka hara tikoloho.

src: President Jacob Zuma will lead the Africa Day celebrations under the theme: “We are Africa – Opening the doors of learning and culture from Cape to Cairo” on 24 May 2015 at the Mamelodi campus of the University of WEBTOKEN the spirit of Africa Day, Cabinet encourages South Africans, especially the youth, to work together to strengthen their participation in the affairs of our country.
tgt: Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o tla etella pele mekete ya Letsatsi la Aforika tlasa mookotaba: “Re Aforika – Re bula mamati a ho ithuta le botjhaba ho tloha Kapa ho ya Cairo” ka la 24 Motsheanong 2015 khemphaseng ya Mamelodi ya Yunivesithi ya Pretoria.

src: Africa Month is a platform to promote unity amongst African nations and our fellow African brothers and sisters residing in South Africa.
tgt: Ka moya wa Letsatsi la Aforika, Kabinete e kgothaletsa maAforika Borwa, ka ho qolleha batjha, ho sebetsa mmoho bakeng sa ho matlafatsa bonkakarolo ba bona mererong ya naha ya rona.

src: The unity of the continent is driven through the African Union’s programmes to attain its vision as articulated in the Agenda 2063.
tgt: Kgwedi ya Aforika ke lepatlelo la ho hodisa kopano hara ditjhaba tsa Aforika le bana ba bo rona ba dulang ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: The continent, guided by its citizens, will strive for an integrated, prosperous and peaceful WEBTOKEN Day also presents an opportunity for South Africans to reconnect and recommit themselves in support of all government interventions to develop a better Africa and a better world.
tgt: Kontinente, e tataiswa ke baahi ba yona, e tla tsitlallela Aforika e momahaneng, e tswetseng pele le e nang le kgotso.

src: The Africa Month theme, “We are Africa”, is a declaration and celebratory statement of pride that fosters inclusivity from all role players and stakeholders.
tgt: Letsatsi la Aforika hape le hlahisa monyetla bakeng sa maAforika Borwa hore a tsebane botjha le ho itlama botjha bakeng sa ho tshehetsa boitshunyako bohle ba mmuso ho ntshetsapele Aforika e betere le lefatshe le betere.

src: It is also a call to action for individuals and groups from all backgrounds and walks of life to join the movement for change.
tgt: Mookotaba wa Kgwedi ya Aforika, “Re Aforika”, ke pehelo ya tiisetso le ya keteko ya boikgantsho bo kgothaletsang kenyeletso ho tswa ho bankakarolo bohle.

src: Cabinet welcomes Operation Fiela\Reclaim 2015, which is a multidisciplinary operation by various state entities to ensure strict compliance with the various laws and regulations governing our society.
tgt: Hape ke kgoeletso ho batho ka bo mong le dihlopha ho tswa ka makgalo oohle a bophelo ho itahlela ka setotswana mohoong wa diphethoho.

src: This operation aims to deal with issues of criminality such as illegal weapons, drug dens, prostitution rings and other illegal activities.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela welcomes Operation Fiela\Reclaim 2015, e leng tshebetso ya dintlha tse ngatanyana ka dipopeho tse fapafapaneng tsa mmuso ho netefatsa ho imatahanya ka matla le melao e fapafapaneng le melawana e laolang setjhaba sa rona.

src: Cabinet reiterates that this operation is not targeted at foreign nationals, but at the criminality within our country as unmasked through a series of consultations with communities.
tgt: Sepheo sa tshebetso ena ke ho sebetsana le dintlha tsa botlokotsebe tse kang dibetsa tse seng molaong, mahaha a dithethefatsi, maqulwana a bootswa le mesebetsi e meng ya botlokotsebe.

src: To this effect, Cabinet dismisses in the strongest terms the assertion that this operation is targeted at foreign WEBTOKEN a country that prides itself with having the best and the most liberal Constitution in the world, we have taken a centre stage on human rights issues, as such we cannot authorise an operation that will violate the human rights of any individuals or groups.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa hore tshebetso ena ha e ya lebiswa ho melata, empa diketsong tsa botlokotsebe ka hara naha ya rona jwaloka ha di utulutswe ka letoto la dipuisano le badudi.

src: Cabinet is happy with the progress made through Operation Fiela, which has since its inception resulted in a number of arrests in various raids of trouble hotspots across the country.
tgt: Kabinete e thabetse kgatelopele e entsweng ka Operation Fiela, eo esale e thakgolwa e entseng hore ho be le ho tshwarwa ho ho ngatanyana matsholong a ho kgwasa dibaka tse nang le mathata haholo ho parola le naha.

src: Cabinet welcomes the response from community members who are partnering with law-enforcement officers in making sure that all are and feel safe in the country.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela karabelo ho tswa ho setjhaba se imatahantseng le bahlanka ba molao bakeng sa ho etsa bonnete ba hore bohle ba bolokehile le ho ikutlwa ba bolokehile ka hara naha.

src: This operation, which intensifies the fight against crime, also assists to promote and create a safer and more secure South Africa.
tgt: Tshebetso ena, e matlafatsang ntwa kgahlanong le botlokotsebe, e thusa hape ho hodisa le ho bopa Aforika Borwa e batlang e bolokehile le ho tshireletseha.

src: The Inter-Ministerial Committee on Migration will brief the media this weekend to give an update on all its work, including Operation Fiela.
tgt: Komiti e Kopanetsweng ya Matona ya Bofalli e tla kopana le boraditaba ho ba beha sehlohlolong ka mosebetsi wa yona ohle, ho kenyeletswa le Operation Fiela.

src: Implementation of key government programmes.
tgt: Ho Kenngwa Tshebetsong ha Mananeo a Bohlokwa a Mmuso.

src: Cabinet welcomes the budget votes of various departments and is pleased with the extensive reports provided by Ministers on the progress they have made in improving the lives of the people.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela dipuo tsa ditekanyetso tsa mafapha a fapafapaneng le ho thabela ditlaleho tse tebileng tseo Matona a fanneng ka tsona mabapi le kgatelopele eo a e entseng bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa bophelo ba batho.

src: The briefings further expanded on the plans of their respective departments for this current financial year.
tgt: Ditsebiso di ile tsa hlalosa ho ya pele ka meralo ya mafapha a bona ka ho fapana bakeng sa selemo sena sa ditjhelete.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch of the Moetapele Initiative by the Department of Home Affairs at its Edenvale office on 12 May 2015.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela ho thakgolwa ha Boikitlaetso ba Moetapele ke Lefapha la Merero ya Lehae kantorong ya lona ya Edenvale ka la 12 Motsheanong 2015.

src: This initiative aims to turn some of the offices into ‘model offices’ as incubators of best practice.
tgt: Sepheo sa Boikitlaetso bona ke ho fetolela tse ding tsa dikantoro ho ‘dikantoro tsa popota’ jwaloka dithuthuhiso tsa mosebetsi o hlwahlwa ka ho fetisisa.

src: This will boost the provision of critical services to South Africans and enable them to access government services efficiently.
tgt: Sena se tla matlafatsa phano ya ditshebeletso tse hlokolosi ho maAforika Borwa le ho ba thusa ho fumantshwa ditshebeletso tsa mmuso ka bokgabane.

src: Cabinet also welcomes the inaugural South African Migrants Awards which will honour outstanding migrants in South Africa and South Africans working in African countries.
tgt: Kabinete hape e ananela ho thakgolwa ha Dikgau tsa Bofalli tsa Aforika Borwa tse tla tlotla bafalli ba hlahelletseng ka mahetla ka hara Aforika Borwa le maAforika Borwa a sebetsang dinaheng tsa Aforika.

src: Cabinet calls on communities to nominate those who embody the spirit of Ubuntu and are dedicated to the development of the African continent via email through EMAILTOKEN close on 20 May 2015 and the winners will be announced on Africa Day (25 May).
tgt: Kabinete e ipeletsa ho badudi ho kgetha ba ba nang le moya wa Botho e bile ba inehetse ntshetsopeleng ya kontinente ya Aforika ka ho romela imeile ho EMAILTOKEN di kwalwa ka la 20 Motsheanong 2015 mme bahlodi ba tla tsebiswa ka Letsatsi la Aforika (25 Motsheanong).

src: One of the most exciting categories of this awards will recognise a South African community which has succeeded in integrating foreign nationals within itself and live together peacefully.
tgt: Mokgahlelo o kgahlisang ka ho fetisisa wa dikgau tsena ke o tla ananela badudi ba Aforika Borwa ba atlehileng ho amohela melata ka hara bona le ho phela mmoho ka kgotso.

src: Cabinet welcomes the rolling out of mobile land claims offices throughout the country to enable all qualifying persons to lodge land claims.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela ho ntshwa ha dikantoro tsa hloma-o-hlomolle naheng ka bophara bakeng sa ho thusa bohle ba lokelang ho kenya dittseko tsa bona tsa mobu.

src: This is in addition to the 14 lodgment offices situated in all provinces.
tgt: Sena ke tlatsetso ya dikantoro tse 14 tsa ditseko tse teng diporofenseng kaofela.

src: This process forms part of a comprehensive national communication outreach which implements the Restitution of Land Rights Amendment Act of 2014, signed into law by President Zuma.
tgt: Tsamaiso ena ke karolo e pharaletseng ya dikgokahanyo tsa naha tsa ho fihlella bohle ya ho kenya tshebetsong Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Tlhabollo ya Ditokelo tsa Mobu wa 2014, se saennweng ho ba molao ke Mopresidente Zuma.

src: The Restitution of Land Rights Amendment Act provides for restitution or equitable redress to persons and communities who were dispossessed of land rights after 19 June 1913.All qualifying South Africans who missed the initial 31 December 1998 deadline to lodge land claims have an extended opportunity until 30 June 2019 to do so.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Tlhabollo ya Ditokelo tsa Mobu se fana ka puseletso kapa tlhabollo e lekalekanang ho batho le badudi ba ileng ba nkelwa ditokelo tsa mobu kamora 19 Phuptjane 1913.MaAforika oohle a nang le tokelo a fetilweng ke nako ya letsatsi le neng le behilwe e le la ho qetela la 31 Tshitwe 1998 bakeng sa ho kenya ditseko a na le monyetla o atolositsweng ho fihla ka la 30 Phuptjane 2019.

src: Cabinet welcomes the meeting of the Minister of Mineral Resources with the mining industry representatives and stakeholders to discuss the outcome of the Mining Charter 2014 Assessment Report.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela kopano ya Letona la Mehlodi ya Diminerale le baemedi ba indaseteri ya merafo le bankakarolo ba bang ho tshohla sephetho sa Tekolo ya Tlaleho ya Tjhata ya Merafo ya 2015.

src: This report measures the progress of the nine key elements of the Mining Charter.
tgt: Tlaleho ena e metha kgatelopele ya dintlha tse robong tsa bohlokwa tsa Tjhata ya Merafo.

src: The Mining Charter was developed with the view of driving the transformational agenda in the critical sector of the economy of the country.
tgt: Tjhata ya Merafo e ile ya hlahiswa ka morero wa ho kganna lenaneo la diphethoho ka hara lekala le hlokolosi la moruo wa naha.

src: The elements to be measured seek to redress the imbalances of the past both in the sharing of the wealth with the previously disadvantaged people and the development of the human resource and ownership of the mines.
tgt: Dintlha tse tshwanetseng ho methwa di tobile ho hlabolla ho se lekalekane ha nako e fetileng ka bobedi karolelanong ya leruo le ba neng ba tinngwe menyetla pele le ntshetsopele ya mehlodi ya batho le thuo ya merafo.

src: Key Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved the hosting of the 25th International Railway Safety Council Meeting to be held from 4 to 9 October 2015 at the Sandton International Convention Centre, Johannesburg.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho tshwarwa ha Kopano ya Lekgotla la Matjhaba la Boipaballo Diporong la bo-25 e tla tshwarwa ho tloha ka la 4 ho isa ka la 9 Mphalane 2015 Setsing sa Matjhaba sa Dikopano sa Sandton, Johannesburg.

src: This international forum brings together railway safety professionals from all over the world to exchange information, experiences, lessons and best practices for improving railway WEBTOKEN this event has the potential to attract foreign investment, which can boost the economy and accelerate public infrastructure investment.
tgt: Foramo ena ya matjhaba e bokanya mmoho ditsebi ho tsa boipaballo diporong ho tswa lefatsheng ka bophara ho kgaogana tlhahisoleseding, diphihlello, dithuto le ditshebetso tse hlwahlwa ka ho fetisisa bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa boipaballo diporong.

src: This is given further impetus by South Africa’s recent investments in the passenger and freight rail sectors, which have made the country attractive for investments.
tgt: Ho tshwarwa ha ketsahalo ena ho na le monyetla wa ho hohela matsete a dinaheng tsa ka ntle, a ka matlafatsang moruo le ho akofisa matsete a dikaho tsa motheo tsa setjhaba.

src: Cabinet approved that the African Maritime Transport Charter be submitted to Parliament for ratification.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Tjhata ya Dipalangwang tsa Mawatle a Aforika hore e tliswe ka hara Palamente bakeng sa ho amohelwa.

src: This is an international agreement that provides for the harmonisation of policies, in order to promote sustained growth and development of African merchant fleets.
tgt: Sena ke tumellano ya matjhaba e fanang ka ho tsamaelana ha maano, bakeng sa ho hodisa kgolo ya moshwelella le ntshetsopele ya lethathama la dikepe tsa kgwebo tsa Aforika.

src: It will also encourage intra-Africa trade to facilitate economic and socio-economic integration on the continent.
tgt: Hape e tla kgothaletsa kgwebisano e kopanetsweng ya Aforika ho thusa bakeng sa momahano ho tsa moruo le moruo wa kahisano kontinenteng.

src: Cabinet approved submission of the Amendment to the Agreement of the International Telecommunications Satellite Organization (ITSO) to Parliament for ratification.
tgt: Kabinete tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa ha Sehlomathiso ho Tumellano ya Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba wa Dikgokahanyo tsa Mehala ya Disathalaete (ITSO) Palamenteng bakeng sa ho amohelwa.

src: ITSO is an intergovernmental organisation that ensures that Intelsat Ltd, a satellite operator, provides public telecommunications services – including voice, data and video – on a global and non-discriminatory basis.
tgt: ITSO ke mokgatlo o kopanetsweng wa mmuso o netefatsang hore Intelsat Ltd, e leng motsamaisi wa disathalaete, e fana ka ditshebeletso tsa dikgokahanyo tsa mehala tsa setjhaba – ho kenyeletsa mantswe, tshedimoso le dividio – ka mokgwa o kenyeletsang bohle le o hlokang kgethollo.

src: The amendment protects the long-term viability of the Common Heritage of Parties, and ensures the continuity of global coverage and global connectivity.
tgt: Sehlomathiso se tshireletsa tshebetso e hlwahlwa ya nako e telele ya Lefa le Tshwanang la Mekgatlo, le ho netefatsa kakaretso ya dikgokahanyo le lefatshe.

src: Ratification is also part of South Africa’s international priorities to contribute to a better world and to the development of Africa.
tgt: Ho tjhaellwa monwana hape ke karolo ya dintlha tse ka Sehloohong tsa Aforika Borwa bakeng sa ho nyehela lefatsheng le betere le ho ntshetsopele ya Aforika.

src: Cabinet’s position on current issues.
tgt: Maemo a Kabinete Mabapi le Dintlha tsa Hajwale.

src: Cabinet is saddened by the passing of Seaparankwe, Dr Ruth Segomotsi Mompati and extends condolences to her family and friends.
tgt: Kabinete e utlwisitswe bohloko ke lefu la Seaparankwe, Ngaka Ruth Segomotsi Mompati mme e fetisa matshediso a yona ho lelapa la hae le metswalle.

src: Dr Mompati dedicated her life to the struggle for freedom and was involved in various initiatives including the historic Women`s March of August WEBTOKEN 1954, she joined the African National Congress (ANC) and was elected to the National Executive Committee (NEC) of the ANC Women’s League.
tgt: Ngaka Mompati o nehetse bophelo ba hae bakeng sa ntwa ya tokoloho mme o ne a le teng ka hara mekutu e fapafapaneng ho kenyeletsa le Mohwanto wa Basadi wa hisetori wa Phato 1956.Ka 1954, o ile a kenela mokgatlo wa African National Congress (ANC) mme o ile a kgethwa ho Komiti ya Naha ya Phethahatso (NEC) ya Liki ya Mafumahadi a ANO ile a ya palehong ka 1962 moo a ileng a rupellwa ho tsa sesole mme e le mongodi le hlooho ya karolo ya basadi ya ANC, Tanzania.

src: She went into exile in 1962 where she underwent military training and held office as secretary and head of the women’s section of the ANC in WEBTOKEN the chief representative of the ANC in the United Kingdom she became part of the delegation that opened talks with the then South African government at Groote Schuur in 1990.
tgt: Jwaloka moemedi ya ka sehloohong wa ANC ho la United Kingdom e ile ya ba karolo ya kemedi e ileng ya bula dipuisano le mmuso wa nako eo wa Aforika Borwa Groote Schuur ka 1990.

src: In August 1992, she addressed the United Nations (UN) Special Committee against Apartheid in New York on the subject of women.
tgt: Ka Phato 1992, o ile a tshetlehela puo Komiti e Ikgethang ya Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) kgahlanong le mmuso wa Kgethollo ho la New York mabapi le ntlha ya basadi.

src: The day was then declared by the UN as an International Day of Solidarity with Women in South WEBTOKEN a true servant of the people, she played an indelible role in the development of our country serving as a Member of Parliament, South Africa’s Ambassador to Switzerland from 1996 to 2000 and the Mayor of Vryburg (Naledi) in North West.
tgt: Letsatsi leo le ile nkuwa e le Letsatsi la Matjhaba la Kopano le Basadi ka hara Aforika Borwa ke UN.

src: She devoted her life to the liberation of our country and showed an unwavering determination to serve her people.
tgt: Jwaloka mosebeletsi wa nnete wa batho, o bapetse karolo e kekeng ya hlakoha ntshetsopeleng ya naha ya rona a sebetsa jwaloka Setho sa Palamente, Moambasatara wa Aforika Borwa ho la Switzerland ho tloha ka 1996 ho fihlela ka 2000 le Meyara wa Vryburg (Naledi) ho la Leboya Bophirima.

src: Cabinet is saddened by the passing of Lieutenant General Bongani Isidore Mbatha and extends condolences to his family and friends.
tgt: O nehetse bophelo ba hae bakeng sa tokoloho ya naha ya rona le ho bontsha maikemisetso a sa thekeseleng a ho sebeletsa batho ba habo.

src: General Mbatha joined Umkhonto we Sizwe, the military wing of the ANC in 1978 and then served in various capacities, including the head of the WEBTOKEN 1994, General Mbatha was integrated into the South African National Defence Force (SANDF) where he underwent extensive training in various disciplines.
tgt: Kabinete e utlwisitswe bohloko ke lefu la Moleftenente Mokgenerale Bongani Isidore Mbatha mme e fetisa matshediso a yona ho ba lelapa la hae le metswalle.

src: He moved through the ranks within the SANDF, serving in a number of positions until he was promoted to a Lieutenant General responsible for Logistics in 2014, the position he occupied until his death.
tgt: Mokgenerale Mbatha o kenetse Umkhonto we Sizwe, e leng karolo ya sesole ya ANC ka 1978 mme a sebetsa maemong a fapafapaneng, ho kenyeletswa le ho ba hlooho ya tsamaiso le tlhophiso ya thepa.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse Tlang.

src: President Zuma will attend the coronation of the King of AmaXhosa, His Majesty King Mpendulo Calvin Sigcawu (Ah!
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla kenela ho behwa setulong ha Morena wa AmaXhosa, Motlotlehi Morena Mpendulo Calvin Sigcawu (Ah!

src: Zwelonke) at Nqadu Great Place in Willowvale, Eastern Cape on 15 May 2015.Cabinet congratulates King Sigcawu on his coronation and looks forward to working with the AmaGcaleka Kingdom in building vibrant, equitable and sustainable rural communities.
tgt: Zwelonke) Motseng wa Borena wa Nqadu, Willowvale, Kapa Botjhabela ka la Motsheanong 2015.Kabinete e thoholetsa Morena Sigcawu ka ho behwa ha hae boreneng mme e ikemiseditse ho sebetsa le Borena ba AmaGcaleka bakeng sa ho aha metse e kganyang, e lekalekanang le ya moshwelella ya dibaka tsa mahae.

src: Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa will attend the Alternative Sanitation Indaba taking place on 15 May 2015 under the theme: “It is not all about flushing”.
tgt: Motlatsi wa Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa o tla kenela Indaba ya Mekgwa e meng ya Tsamaiso ya Dikgwerekgwere e tla dula ka la 15 Motsheanong 2015 tlasa mookotaba: “ha se feela ka ho folaša”.

src: The Indaba will also provide an opportunity for service providers of alternative sanitation technology to showcase their products.
tgt: Indaba hape e tla fana ka monyetla bakeng sa bafani ba ditshebeletso ba thekenoloji ya dikgwerekgwere mabapi le mekgwa e meng ya thekenoloji ho bapatsa dihlahiswa tsa bona.

src: The Department of Social Development, in partnership with the South African Social Security Agency and National Development Agency, will launch Child Protection Week at the Franklin Sports Ground in Kokstad, KwaZulu-Natal on 25 May 2015 under the theme: “Working together to protect children”.
tgt: Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba, ka tshebedisano mmoho le Lekala la Tshireletso ya Setjhaba la Aforika Borwa (SASSA) le Lekala la Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDA), le tla thakgola Beke ya Tshireletso ya Bana Lebaleng la Dipapadi la Franklin Kokstad, KwaZulu-Natal ka la 25 Motsheanong 2015 tlasa mookotaba: “Re sebetsa mmoho ho tshireletsa bana”.

src: The week will conclude on 31 May 2015 in Gauteng.
tgt: Beke ena e tla fella ka la 31 Motsheanong 2015 Gauteng.

src: This awareness campaign aims to mobilise all sectors of society to care for and protect children.
tgt: Letsholo lena la temoso le reretswe ho fihlella makala oohle a setjhaba bakeng sa ho hlokomela le ho tshireletsa bana.

src: Moreover, it intends to make adults and children aware of the statutory protection a child enjoys under the Constitution, legislations, policies and international instruments.
tgt: Ho fetafeta moo, le rerile ho lemosa batho ba baholo le bana ka tshireletso ya molao e fuwang bana tlasa Molaotheo, melao, maano le disebediswa tsa matjhaba mabapi le sena.

src: Cabinet calls on parents and guardians to always put the safety of their children first and ensure that they are taken care of by responsible adults.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho batswadi le bahlokomedi hore kamehla ba behe tshireletso ya bana ba bona pele le ho netefatsa hore ba hlokometswe ke batswadi ba nang le boikarabelo.

src: Parents and guardians are encouraged to teach children to be aware of potentially dangerous situations, including unacceptable behavior or actions by adults.
tgt: Batswadi le Bahlokomedi ba kgothaletswa ho lemoha dibaka tse kotsi, ho kenyeletsa boitshwaro kapa diketso tsa batho ba baholo tse sa amoheleheng.

src: It is the responsibility of parents and guardians to know the whereabouts of their children and to take reasonable precautions to ensure their safety and protection.
tgt: Ke boikarabelo ba batswadi le bahlokomedi ho tseba moo bana ba bona ba leng teng le ho nka mehato e bonahalang ho netefatsa polokeho le tshireletso ya bona.

src: The Minister of Telecommunications and Postal Services, Dr Siyabonga Cwele, will hold an Imbizo at the Nelson Mandela Museum in Qunu, Eastern Cape to celebrate the World Telecommunication and Information Society Day on 17 May 2015.
tgt: Letona la Lefapha la Dikaho tsa Motheo tsa Dikgokahano le Ditshebeletso tsa Poso, Ngaka Siyabonga Cwele, le tla tshwara Imbizo Musiamong wa Nelson Mandela Qunu, Kapa Botjhabela ho keteka Letsatsi la Setjhaba la Lefatshe la Dikaho tsa Motheo tsa Dikgokahano le Tlhahisoleseding ka la 17 Motsheanong 2015.

src: The event is held to encourage people to increasingly use technology to improve their lives.
tgt: Ketsahalo ena e tshwarwa ho kgothaletsa batho ho eketsa ho sebedisa tshekenoloji bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa bophelo ba bona.

src: The Minister will detail what government is doing to use technology to improve service delivery to all South Africans, especially those who live in rural areas.
tgt: Letona le tla fana ka dintlha tse batsi mabapi le seo mmuso o se etsang ho sebedisa thekenoloji bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa phano ya ditshebeletso ho maAforika Borwa oohle, ka ho qolleha a dulang dibakeng tsa mahae.

src: The Imbizo is held in partnership with the Eastern Cape Provincial Government, traditional leaders and the South African Communications Forum.
tgt: Imbizo e tshwarwa ka semphato le Mmuso wa Porofense wa Kapa Botjhabela, baetapele ba botjhaba le Foramo ya Dikgokahanyo ya Aforika Borwa.

src: Annually, 17 May marks the anniversary of the signing of the first International Telegraph Convention and the creation of the International Telecommunication Union.
tgt: Selemo ka seng, 17 Motsheanong e tshwaya sehopotso sa ho saenwa ha Seboka sa pele sa Matjhaba sa Mehala le ho thehwa ha Kopano ya Matjhaba ya Dikaho tsa Motheo tsa Dikgokahano.

src: The purpose of this event is to help raise awareness of the possibilities that the use of the Internet and other information and communications technologies can bring to societies and economies, and ways to bridge the digital divide.
tgt: Sepheo sa ketsahalo ena ke ho thusa ho hlahisa temoso ka dikgonahalo tseo tshebediso ya inthanete le dithekenoloji tse ding tsa tlhahisoleseding le dikgokahanyo di ka di tlisang ho setjhaba le meruo, le ditsela tsa ho ngotla ho se lekalekane ho tsa dijithale.

src: AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: DithonyoDithonyo kaofela di tla lokelwa ke ho netefatswa ha mangolo a thuto le tumello e amehang.

src: Adv Motlatjo Josephine Ralefatane as the Chairperson of the Board of .zaDNDr Thomas Kwadwo Gyedu-Ababio as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Inkomati-Usuthu Catchment Management Agency.
tgt: Moatefokate Motlatjo Josephine Ralefatane jwaloka Modulasetulo wa Boto ya ZADNNgaka Thomas Kwadwo Gyedu-Ababio jwaloka Mohlanka e Moholo wa Phethahatso (CEO) ya Lekala la Bolaodi ba Mokgamo wa Metsi la Inkomati-Usuthu.

src: Africa Day.
tgt: Letsatsi la Aforika.

src: Cabinet would like to thank all South Africans who participated in the Africa Day 2015 celebrations, which reflected our commitment to build a united, peaceful and prosperous Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e leboha maAforika Borwa kaofela a ileng a nka karolo meketeng ya Letsatsi la Aforika 2015, le bontshitseng boitlamo ba rona ba ho aha Aforika e kopaneng, ya kgotso le tswelopele.

src: Cabinet reiterates the call by President Jacob Zuma to all South African institutions and companies to fly the African Union (AU) flag with the South African flag.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa boipiletso ba Moporesidente Jacob Zuma ho dikaho le dikhamphani kaofela tsa Aforika Borwa ho fofisa folakga ya Kopano ya Aforika (AU) mmoho le ya Aforika Borwa.

src: This is in keeping with the need to embrace the vision of a united, prosperous and peaceful Africa.
tgt: Sena se tsamaelana le tlhokeho ya ho imatahanya le pono ya Aforika e kopaneng, ya tswelopele le kgotso.

src: Implementation of key government programmes.
tgt: Ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha mananeo a bohlokwa a mmuso.

src: Cabinet reminds South Africans and foreign nationals travelling with children that the Passport and Travel Documents Act will come into effect from 1 June 2015.
tgt: Kabinete e hopotsa maAforika Borwa le melata e etang le bana hore Molao wa Dipaseporoto le Ditokomane tsa Maeto o tla qala ho sebetsa ho tloha ka la 1 Phuptjane 2015.

src: Under the new legislation, parents travelling with children under the age of 18 are required to produce their unabridged birth certificates.
tgt: Tlasa molao o motjha, batswadi ba etang le bana ba ka tlase ho dilemo tse 18 ba tshwanela ho hlahisa mangolo a bona a tlhaho a sa kgutsufatswang.

src: This is part of government’s commitment to safeguard the best interests of children and prevent child trafficking.
tgt: Sena ke karolo ya boitlamo ba mmuso ho tshireletsa dikgahleho tsa bana le ho thibela kgwebisano ka bana.

src: Key Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved the National Learner Transport Policy, which provides guidelines in providing effective, efficient and safe learner public transport services.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Leano la Naha la Dipalangwang tsa Baithuti, le fanang ka ditataiso mabapi le phano ya ditshebeletso tsa dipalangwang tsa setjhaba tse hlwahlwa, tse kgabane le ho bolokeha bakeng sa baithuti.

src: Its implementation will result in an integrated learner transport service that provides the standards of the kind of vehicles to be used and the tariff structures for the usage of scholar transport services.
tgt: Ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha lona ho tla baka tshebeletso e kopanetsweng ya dipalangwang tsa baithuti e fanang ka maemo a mefuta ya dipalangwang tse lokelang ho sebediswa le dibopeho tsa ditefello tse tla sebediswa ho ditshebeletso tsa dipalangwang tsa baithuti.

src: The policy is also aligned with the South African Schools Act, 1996 (Act 84 of 1996).
tgt: Leano lena hape le matahantswe le Molao wa Dikolo wa Aforika Borwa, 1996 (Molao 84 wa 1996).

src: Cabinet approved the submission of South Africa’s 1994 to 2014 Report on the Progress in the Implementation of the African Union Heads of States’ Solemn Declaration on Gender Equality in Africa to the AU Secretariat.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa ha Tlaleho ya Aforika Borwa ya 1994 ho isa ho 2014 mabapi le Kgatelopele ya ho Kenngwa tshebetsong ha Boitlamo bo Kgethehileng ba Dihlooho tsa Dipuso tsa Kopano ya Aforika (AU) mabapi le Tekatekano ya Bong ka hara Aforika ho Bongodi ba ATlaleho ena ke boitokisetso ba Seboka sa Dihlooho tsa Dipuso tsa AU se tla tshwarwa ka Phuptjane 2015.Tlaleho ena, e akaretsang nako ya ho tloha ka 1994 ho isa ho 2014, e hlahloba le ho lekola bohlwahlwa ba melao ya rona, maano le mananeo a ileng a hlahiswa bakeng sa ho eketsa boemedi, phano ya ditshebeletso tsa mantlha, tlhahiso ya mesebetsi, phokotso ya bofuma, phediso ya dikgoka, le tshireletso ya ditokelo tsa botho tsa basadi le banana.

src: Cabinet approved the National Youth Policy 2020 (NYP2020).
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Leano la Batjha la Naha la 2015-2020 (NYP2020).

src: The policy replaces the National Youth Policy 2009-2014 which has since expired.
tgt: Leano lena le nkile sebaka sa Leano la Batjha la Naha la 2009-2014 leo nako ya lona e seng e fedile.

src: The policy was developed after an extensive consultation process with the youth of South Africa from all the nine provinces.
tgt: Leano lena le ile la hlahiswa kamora ditsamaiso tsa ditherisano tse matla le batjha ba Aforika Borwa ho tswa diporofenseng kaofela tse robong.

src: It will form the basis for the development of an integrated Youth Development Strategy.4 Cabinet was briefed on the progress made in setting up the Property Management Trading Entity (PMTE).
tgt: Le tla bopa motheo bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya Lewa la Ntshetsopele ya Batjha le kopanetsweng.

src: The entity ensures efficiencies and cost-effectiveness in the management of the State property portfolio.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka kgatelopele e entsweng bakeng sa ho theha Mokgatlo wa Bolaodi ba Kgwebisano ya Thepa (PMTE).

src: Cabinet is satisfied with the development and the refinement of the PMTE business model, which will improve the quality of public buildings.
tgt: Mokgatlo ona o netefatsa bokgabane le bohlwahlwa ho tsa ditjeho bolaoding ba dipotefolio tsa thepa ya Puso.

src: Cabinet further approved the secondment for Mr P Serote to serve as head of the PMTE, Mr M Govender as head of Facilities and Real Estate Management and Ms BS Mathews as head of Real Estate Registry Services.
tgt: Kabinete e kgotsofetse ka ntshetsopele le ho lokiswa botjha ha motlolo wa kgwebo wa PMTE, o tla ntlafatsa boleng ba meaho ya setjhaba.

src: South Africa will host the AU Summit at the Sandton Convention Centre from 7 to 15 June 2015 under the theme: “Year of Women Empowerment and Development towards Africa’s Agenda 2063”.
tgt: Kabinete hape e tjhaelletse monwana botlatsetsi ba Monghadi P Serote ho sebetsa jwaloka hlooho ya PMTE, Monghadi M Govender jwaloka hlooho ya Dikaho le Bolaodi ba Meaho le Mofumahadi BS Mathews jwaloka hlooho ya Ditshebeletso tsa Boingodiso ba Meaho.

src: The week’s activities will conclude with the Assembly of Heads of State from 14 to 15 June 2015.The Republic of Zimbabwe, as chair of the AU for 2015, will chair the summit and its related meetings.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tla tshwara Seboka sa AU Setsing sa Dikopano sa Sandton ho tloha ka la 7 ho isa ka la 15 Phuptjane 2015 tlasa mookotaba: “Selemo sa Matlafatso ya Basadi le Ntshetsopele ho lebisa ho Lenane la Aforika la 2063”.

src: It will focus on the implementation of decisions taken at the January 2015 Summit, which includes Agenda 2063 and its First 10-Year Implementation Plan State of Continental Peace and Security, including Terrorism Women’s Empowerment and Development Alternative Sources of Funding the AU Continental integration and operationalising the African Centre for Disease Control and Prevention by 2015.President Zuma will attend the inauguration of Nigeria’s President-elect Mohammadu Buhari in Abuja, Nigeria on 29 May 2015.
tgt: Diketsahalo tsa beke di tla qetella ka Kopano ya Dihlooho tsa Dipuso ho tloha ka la 14 ho isa ka la 15 Phuptjane 2015.Riphaboliki ya Zimbabwe, jwaloka ka modulasetulo wa AU bakeng sa 2015, e tla ba modulasetulo wa seboka le dikopano tsa yona tse amehang.

src: The World Economic Forum on Africa will take place in Cape Town from 3 to 5 June 2015 under the theme: “Then and Now: Reimagining Africa’s Future.”Cabinet welcomes all political and business leaders from across the African continent and other parts of the world as the meeting marks 25 years of change in Africa.
tgt: Se tla tsepamisa maikutlo ho kenngweng tshebetsong ha diqeto tse nkilweng sebokeng sa Pherekgong 2015, tse kenyeletsang Lenane la 2063 le Moralo wa ho le kenya Tshebetsong la dilemo tse 10 tsa Pele Maemo a Kgotso le Tshireletso a Kontinente, ho kenyeletswa Boferekanyi Matlafatso ya Basadi le Ntshetsopele Mehlodi e fapaneng ya Dithuso tsa Ditjhelete bakeng sa AU Kopano ya kontinente le ho etsa hore Setsi sa Aforika sa Taolo ya Mahloko le Thibelo se be se sebetsa ka 2015.Moporesidente Zuma o tla kenela ho behwa setulong ha Moporesidente ya sa tswa kgethwa wa Nigeria Moporesidente Mohammadu Buhari Abuja, Nigeria ka la 29 Motsheanong 2015.

src: Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa, as the Chair of the South African National AIDS Council, will address the opening of the 7th South African AIDS Conference at the Inkosi Albert Luthuli International Convention Centre in Durban from 9 to 12 June 2015 under the theme: “Reflection, Refocus and Renewal”.This conference, which is held every two years, has become a barometer for government and South Africans to track advances made in controlling HIV infections.
tgt: Foramo ya Moruo wa Lefatshe mabapi le Aforika e tla tshwarwa Motse Kapa ho tloha ka la 3 ho isa ho la 5 Phuptjane 2015 tlasa mookotaba: “Maoba le Kajeno: Re Hopola Botjha Bokamoso ba Aforika.”Kabinete e amohela baetapele bohle ba dipolotiki le kgwebo ho tswa kontinenteng ya Aforika ka bophara le dikarolong tse ding tsa lefatshe jwaloka ha kopano e tshwaya dilemo tse 25 tsa diphethoho ka hara Aforika.

src: South Africa has the largest antiretroviral (ARV) programme in the world, with three million people on ARVs as of December 2014.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e na le lenaneo le leholohadi la ARV lefatsheng, ka batho ba dimilione tse tharo ba sebedisang di-ARV ho tloha ka Tshitwe 2014.

src: This has significantly contributed to reducing new HIV infections and mortality from AIDS, and ensured child survival and prolonged life.
tgt: Sena se nyehetse ka matla bakeng sa ho fokotsa ditshwaetso tse ntjha tsa HIV le ho hlokahala ka lebaka la AIDS, le ho netefatsa ho pholoha ha bana le bophelo bo bolelele.

src: Diligent planning is a major part of the success of this flagship programme, which ensures adequate availability of ARVs at every public health facility.
tgt: Meralo e hlwahlwa ke karolo e kgolo ya katleho ya lenaneo lena le tswang pele, le netefatsang ho ba teng ho lekaneng ha di-ARV dikahong tsa setjhaba tsa kalafo.

src: South Africa, through the Department of Science and Technology (DST), has been investing in HIV research for many years.
tgt: Aforika Borwa, ka Lefapha la Saense le Thekenoloji (DST), esale e tsetela diphuputsong tsa HIV ka dilemo tse ngata.

src: The DST's investment in HIV research began in 1999 when together with the Department of Health, we established the South African AIDS Vaccine WEBTOKEN 2009, the DST’s support for HIV research was expanded to include other interventions such as diagnostics, ARVs, microbicides, in addition to vaccines.
tgt: Ho tsetela ha DST diphuputsong tsa HIV ho qadile ka 1999 ha mmoho le Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle, re thehile Boikitlaetso ba Aforika Borwa ba Kentelo ya AIDS.

src: We created the South African HIV Research and Innovation Platform (SHARP) to fund pioneering HIV and AIDS research and facilitate the development of innovative solutions to the epidemic.
tgt: Ka 2009, tshehetso ya DST bakeng sa diphuputso tsa HIV di ile tsa atoloswa hore di kenyeletse boitshunyako bo bong bo kang dipopolo, di-ARV, dibolaya dikokwanahloko, ho phaella hodima diente.

src: We are currently supporting a number of HIV-related projects at various stages of development through a programme called the Strategic Health Innovation Partnership, which incorporates SHARP under the auspices of the South African Medical Research Council.
tgt: Re hlahisitse Lepatlelo la Ntlafatso le Diphuputso tsa HIV la Aforika Borwa (SHARP) bakeng sa ho tshehetsa ka matlole diphuputso tsa ho qala tsa HIV le AIDS le ho thusa ka ntshetsopele ya ditharollo tse ntlafetseng bakeng sa sewa sena.

src: The role of this programme is to facilitate the interaction of South African HIV and AIDS researchers, and to create a National Network of Collaborating Research Centres in HIV and AIDS.
tgt: Hajwale re tshehetsa diporojeke tse ngatanyana tse amanang le HIV mehatong e fapafapaneng ya ntshetsopele ka lenaneo le bitswang Bomphato ba Lewa la Ntlafatso ya Kalafo, bo kenyeletsang SHARP tlasa bodisa ba Lekgotla la Diphuputso tsa Kalafo la Aforika Borwa.

src: Currently, a number of multi-institutional, multidisciplinary, product development projects covering diagnostics, vaccines and microbicides are being pursued to advance the objectives of SHARSouth Africa attaches particular importance to the fight against AIDS, with prevention at the heart of the country’s National Strategic Plan for HIV, STIs and TB (2012-2016).4 Environment Month ProgrammeIn June South Africa will celebrate key environment days.
tgt: Mosebetsi wa lenaneo lena ke ho thusa ka ho kopanya bafuputsi ba Aforika Borwa ba HIV le AIDS, le ho hlahisa Ditsi tsa Naha tsa Marangrang a Tshebedisano mmoho a Diphuputso mabapi le HIV le AIDS.

src: Led by the Department of Environmental Affairs, on 5th June, we will celebrate the World Environment Day in Kimberley, Northern Cape.
tgt: Hajwale, palo e ngata ya dikaho tse fapaneng, mekgatlo e fapaneng, diporojeke tsa ntshetsopele tse akaretsang mesebetsi ya ho popola, diente le dibolaya dikokwanahloko di a latelwa bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa dipheo tsa SHARAforika Borwa e behile bohlokwa bo itseng bakeng sa ho lwantsha AIDS, mme thibelo e le motsong wa Moralo wa Lewa la Naha bakeng sa HIV, di-STI le TB (2012-2016).
