tgt: Lewa le habile ho eketsa seabo sa tsa tlhaho ho Palo yohle ya Dihlahiswa tsa Naha (GDP), ha le ntse le baballa tikoloho ya naha.

src: Cabinet approved the publishing for public comments of the draft framework and approach for the formulation of South Africa’s Intended Nationally Determined Contribution for consultation with stakeholders ahead of its submission to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).The framework once fully consulted will form of the legal agreement under the UNFCCC, which will be adopted in Paris, France in December BillsCabinet approved the publishing of the following Bills for public comments:.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho hatiswa ha ditshwaelo tsa setjhaba tsa moralo wa nakwana le mokgwatsamaiso bakeng sa ho etswa ha Seabo sa Aforika Borwa se Reretsweng ho Lekolwa boemong ba Naha bakeng sa dipuisano le ba amehang pele e isuwa Selekaneng sa Moralo wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng Phetohong ya Tlelaemete (UNFCC).Moralo ona, ha ho se ho buisanwe ka ona ka botlalo, o tla bopa karolo ya tumellano ya molao tlasa UNFCC, e tla ananellwa Paris, France ka Tshitwe DibiliKabinete e ananetse ho hatiswa ha Dibili tse latelang bakeng sa ditshwaelo tsa setjhaba:.

src: Border Management Agency (BMA) Bill, 2015, which seeks to establish the BMA that will balance secure cross-border travel, trade facilitation and national security imperatives, within the context of South Africa’s regional, African and international obligations.
tgt: Bili ya Lekgotla la Taolo ya Meedi (BMA), 2015, e batlang ho bopa BMA e tla tsitsisa ho eta ho bolokehileng mahlakoreng ohle a meedi, nolofatso ya kgwebisano le dintho tsa bohlokwa tsa tshireletso ya naha, ka ho ya ka boemo ba lebatowa la Aforika Borwa, ditlamo tsa Aforika le tsa matjhaba.

src: This single authority for border law enforcement provides the potential for more cost- effective services as well as enhanced security and management of the border environment.
tgt: Bolaodi bo le bong ba tshebediso ya molao meeding bo fana ka kgonahalo ya ditshebeletso tse baballang ditjeo haholwanyane esita le tshireletso le taolo tse matlafaditsweng tsa tikoloho ya meeding.

src: Refugees Amendment Bill, 2015, which seeks to create a more efficient and effective functioning application process for asylum seekers.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Baphaphathehi, 2015, e batlang ho thea mokgwatsamaiso wa ho etsa kopo o sebetsang ka bokgabane le ho feta bakeng sa ba batlang tjako.

src: Cabinet further approved the submission of the following Bills to Parliament:.
tgt: Kabinete e boetse ya ananela ho tliswa ha Dibili tse latelang Palamenteng:.

src: Local Government: Municipal Electoral Amendment Bill, 2015, which amends the Local Government: Municipal Electoral Act, 2000 (Act 27 of 2000).The amendments address issues with a view to ensuring smooth preparation and execution of the 2016 local government elections.
tgt: Mmuso wa Dibaka: Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Dikgetho tsa Bomasepala, 2015, e hlomathisang Mmuso wa Dibaka: Molao wa Dikgetho wa Bomasepala, 2000 (Molao wa 27 wa 2000).Dihlomathiso di hlaola dintho ka maikutlo a ho netefatsa tlhophiso le tshebediso e ntle ya dikgetho tsa 2016 tsa mmuso wa dibaka.

src: Unemployment Insurance Amendment Bill, 2014.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Inshorense ya Batho ba Fellwetsweng ke Mesebetsi, 2014.

src: This is the second amendment to the Unemployment Insurance Act, 2001 (Act 63 of 2001).Once the Bill is passed, it will amongst others extend the period of payments of benefits to the contributor from eight to 12 months and extend the period in which a contributor can lodge a claim from six months to 12 months.
tgt: Sena ke sehlomathiso sa bobedi sa Molao wa Inshorense ya Batho ba Fellwetsweng ke Mesebetsi wa 2001 (Molao wa 63 wa 2001).Hang ha Bili e se e atlehisitswe, ho tse ding e tla atolla nako ya ho lefa melemo ho motsetedi ho tloha dikgweding tse robedi ho ya ho tse 12 le ho atolla nako eo motsetedi a ka etsang tseko ka yona ho tloha dikgweding tse tsheletseng ho ya ho tse Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: Cabinet approved the 2015 Women’s Month theme: “Women, United in Moving South Africa Forward” and calendar of activities for Women’s Month, which leads to a year-long programme.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse mokotaba wa Kgwedi ya Basadi ya 2015: “Basadi ba Kopane ho Ntshetsa Aforika Borwa Pele” le almanaka ya diketsahalo tsa Kgwedi ya Basadi, e lebisang lenaneong la bolelele ba selemo.

src: The Women’s Day event on 9 August 2015 will take place at Sasolburg, Free State, which will also be marked by President Jacob Zuma’s release of the first Status of Women Report.2015 also marks the 59th anniversary of the Women’s March to the Union Buildings against pass laws, kick-starting the build-up to the 60th anniversary in 2016.
tgt: Ketsahalo ya Letsatsi la Basadi ka la 9 Phato 2015 e tla ba Sasolburg, Freistata, athe e tla boela e tshwauwa ke ho ntshuwa ha Tlaleho ya pele ya Maemo a Basadi ke Moporesidente Jacob Zuma.

src: The Minister of Science and Technology, Ms Naledi Pandor, will launch National Science Week (NSW) taking place from 1 to 8 August 2015 at North-West University's (NWU) Mafikeng Campus on 1 August.
tgt: Selemo sa 2015 se boela hape se tshwaya la sehopotso sa bo59 sa Mohwanto wa Basadi o neng o leba Union Buildings kgahlanong le melao ya dipasa, empa seo sa qala ho itukisetsa sehopotso sa bo60 sa 2016.

src: She will be accompanied by the North West MEC for Education, Ms Maphefo Matsemela, and the NWU’s Vice Chancellor, ProfDan Kgwadi.
tgt: Letona la Saense le Theknoloji, Mofumahadi Naledi Pandor, o tla thakgola Beke ya Naha ya Saense (NSW) e tla nka sebaka (ho tloha ka la 1 ho ya ho la 8 Phato 2015) Yunivesithing ya Leboya Bophirimela (NWU) Khamphaseng ya Mafikeng ka la 1 Phato.

src: The event will be attended by thousands of learners, university students, scientists and members of the community.
tgt: O tla felehetswa ke Setho sa Lekgotla la Phethahatso (MEC) wa Thuto wa Leboya Bophirimela, Mofumahadi Maphefo Matsemela, le Motlatsi wa Motjhanselara wa NWU, Moporofesara Dan Kgwadi.

src: The theme for NSW 2015 is “International Year of Light and Light-based Technologies”.
tgt: Mokotaba wa NSW wa 2015 ke “Selemo sa Matjhaba sa Kganya le Dithekenoloji tse itshetlehileng ka Kganya.” Kganya le bohlokwa ba yona ho ntlafatseng maphelo ho tla bontshwa ka mekgwa e fapaneng e kang ho sebediswa ha leisara ho tsa bophelo bo botle, sejareng ya mahlo, tlhahiso diindastering, ho tjheseletsa makoloi mmoho le mabone a tshireletso bakeng sa ho tshosa mashodu.

src: Light and its significance in improving lives will be showcased in different forms such as the application of laser in health, cataract surgery, industry manufacturing, car welding and security beams for deterring burglary.
tgt: Lefapha la Saense le Thekenoloji, ka Lekgotla la Saense le Diphuputso tsa Diindasteri (CSIR), le tsetetse ho saense ya maqhubu a kganya – saense ya thekenoloji ya kganya ya ho fehla, ho laola le ho fofonela maqhubu a kganya le boseberwana ba kganya.

src: The Department of Science and Technology has, through the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), invested in photonics – the science of light technology of generating controlling and detecting light waves and particles of light.
tgt: Ho tse ding, sena se lebisitse tshibollong ya pele ya lefatshe ya thekenoloji ya leisara ya dijithale.

src: This has led among other things, to the world’s first breakthrough in digital-laser technology.
tgt: Tshibollo ena ya CSIR e emetse mokgwa o motjha wa ho nahana ka thekenoloji ya leisara mme e ka ba lepatlelo leo dithekenoloji tsa kamoso di ka ahwang ho lona.

src: The breakthrough at the CSIR represents a new way of thinking about laser technology and could be a platform on which future technologies are built.
tgt: DithonyoDithonyo kaofela di tla lokelwa ke ho netefatswa ha mangolo a thuto le tumello e amehang.

src: Mr Stavros Nicolaou as the alternate National Economic Development and Labour Council member to the Special Economic Zones Advisory Board.
tgt: Monghadi Stavros Nicolaou e le setho se lehlakoreng sa Lekgotla la Naha la Ntshetsopele ya Moruo le Merero ya Mesebetsi ho Boto e Ikgethileng ya Boeletsi ba Moruo wa Dizounu.

src: Land Bank:a) Mr Bafana Patrick Mathidi – (re-appointment as Non-Executive Director)b) Adv.
tgt: Banka ya Mobu:a) Monghadi Bafana Patrick Mathidi – (o thontswe botjha e le Mookamedi eo e seng wa Phethahatso)b) Ntamolane Sandra Julie Hester Coetzee – (Mookamedi eo e seng wa Phethahatso)c) Mofumahadi Mathane Eveline Makgatho – (Mookamedi eo e seng wa Phethahatso) led) Monghadi Bennie van Rooy – (Mohlanka e Moholo wa tsa Ditjhelete e le Mookamedi wa Phethahatso).

src: Sandra Julie Hester Coetzee – (Non-Executive Director)c) Ms Mathane Eveline Makgatho – (Non-Executive Director) andd) Mr Bennie van Rooy – (Chief Financial Officer as Executive Director).
tgt: Lekgotla la Khansele ya Naha ya Boingodiso ba Baahi ba Matlo:a) Monghadi Abbey Chikane (Modulasetulo)b) Mofumahadi JuliekaBayatc) Mofumahadi Xoliswa Eunice Dakud) Monghadi Themba Thomas Cyril Dlaminie) Mofumahadi Hlaleleni Kathleen Dlepuf) Leqosa Segogwane Samuel Kotaneg) Monghadi Phetola Nailana Solomon Makgatheh) Mofumahadi Mankwana Christinah Mohalei) Mofumahadi Busisiwe Nwabisa Nzoj) Monghadi Alvin Phumudzo Rapeak) Monghadi Goolam Hoosen Manack (moemedi wa Lefapha la Matlotlo a Naha)l) Monghadi Obed Lucas Molotsi (moemedi wa Lefapha la Mesebetsi ya Setjhaba) lem) Monghadi Lulama Andisa Potwana (moemedi wa Lefapha la Kgwebisano le Indasteri).

src: Council of the National Home Builders Registration Council:a) Mr Abbey Chikane (Chairperson)b) Ms Julieka Bayatc) Ms Xoliswa Eunice Dakud) Mr Themba Thomas Cyril Dlaminie) Ms Hlaleleni Kathleen Dlepuf) Ambassador Segogwane Samuel Kotaneg) Mr Phetola Nailana Solomon Makgatheh) Ms Mankwana Christinah Mohalei) Ms Busisiwe Nwabisa Nzoj) Mr Alvin Phumudzo Rapeak) Mr Goolam Hoosen Manack (National Treasury representative)l) Mr Obed Lucas Molotsi (Department of Public Works representative) andm) Mr Lulama Andisa Potwana (Department of Trade and Industry representative).
tgt: Ngaka Muzamani Charles Nwaila e le Motsamaisi e Moholo wa Lefapha la Merero ya Setso – (Katoloso ya konteraka bakeng sa dilemo tse tharo.).

src: Dr Muzamani Charles Nwaila as Director-General (DG) for the Department of Traditional Affairs – (Extension of the contract for three years.).
tgt: Ngaka Bongani Douglas Ngqulunga e le Motlatsi wa Motsamaisi e Moholo: Kantorong ya Poraefete ya Moporesidente Kantorong ya Mopresidenteng.

src: Cabinet welcomes the progress of Project Mikondzo, a service-delivery initiative aimed at expanding the reach of social services in the poorest communities of the country.
tgt: Ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha mananeo a bohlokwa a mmuso Kabinete e amohela kgatelopele ya Porojeke ya Mikondzo, e leng boikitlaetso ba phano ya ditshebeletso bo reretsweng phihlello ya ditshebeletso tsa kahisano dibakeng tse futsanehileng ka ho fetisisa tsa naha.

src: This was demonstrated at De Doorns in the Western Cape, where aid is being provided to 4 021 families whose breadwinners are mostly seasonal farmworkers.
tgt: Sena se bonahetse De Doorns ho la Kapa Bophirima, moo ho ntseng ho fanwa ka thuso ho malapa a 4 021 ao dihlooho tsa ona boholo e leng basebeletsi ba dihla ba mapolasing.

src: The assistance include, among other things, the supply of seed and seedlings for family gardens and funding for the establishment of community-based organisations and cooperatives.
tgt: Thuso e kenyeletsa, hara tse ding, phano ya peo le sethopo bakeng sa ditshingwana tsa malapa le thuso ya ditjhelete bakeng sa ho theha mekgatlo le dikoporasi tsa badudi.

src: The Department of Social Development is also using De Doorns to develop a policy on seasonal WEBTOKEN addition, the South African Social Security Agency rolled out an extensive Social Relief of Distress programme to provide food and other necessities such as school uniforms for children from indigent families.
tgt: Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba hape le sebedisa De Doorns ho ntshetsapele leano mabapi le basebeletsi ba dihla.

src: A grant of R1 083 160 from the National Development Agency supports 11 non-centre based Early Childhood Development (ECD) playgroups, with 975 children now attending ECD centres in the area and 789 of them benefiting from government’s ECD subsidy.
tgt: Hodima moo, Lekala la Aforika Borwa la Tshireletso ya Setjhaba (SASA) le ile la tla ka lenaneo le matla la Pebofatso ya Mathata ho tsa Kahisano bakeng sa ho fana ka dijo le ditlhoko tse ding tse kang diaparo tsa sekolo bakeng sa bana ba malapa a sokolang.

src: Cabinet commends the ongoing successes of Operation Fiela, the most recent being in the Northern Cape where the integrated operation by the South African Police Service (SAPS), government departments, and provincial and municipal law-enforcement agencies went further in ensuring that people are and feel safe.
tgt: Thuso ya tjhelete ya R1 083 160 ho tswa ho Lekala la Naha la Ntshetsopele le tshehetsa dihlopha tse 11 tse sa keneleng ditsheng tsa Thuto ya Ntshetsopele ya Bana (ECD), moo bana ba 975 jwale ba kenang ditsheng tsa ECD tulong eo mme ba 789 ba bona ba kgola molemo ho tswa tshehetsong ya mmuso ya ditjhelete ya ECKabinete e thoholetsa dikatleho tse ntseng di tswela pele tsa Operation Fiela, e leng ya moraorao tjena Kapa Leboya moo tshebetso e kopanetsweng ke Tshebeletso ya Sepolesa ya Aforika Borwa (SAPS), mafapha a mmuso, le makala a tiisetso ya molao a porofense le a bomasepala a ileng a tswela pele ho netefatsa hore batho ba bolokehile le ho ikutlwa ba le jwalo.

src: The Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) on Migration will hold a media briefing next week to provide a detailed update.
tgt: Komiti e Kopanetsweng ya Matona mabapi le Bofalli (IMC) e tla tshwara kopano ya boraditaba bekeng e tlang ho fana ka dintlha tse batsi tsa moraorao tjena.

src: Cabinet commends unions and mining houses for working with government to reviltalise the mining sector, which is the backbone of our economy and urges all parties to implement commitments.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa mekgatlo ya basebetsi le dikhamphani tsa merafo mabapi le ho sebetsa mmoho le mmuso ho tsoseletsa lekala la merafo, e leng mokokotlo wa moruo wa rona mme e kgothaletsa bankakarolo bohle ho kenya tshebetsong boitlamo bona.

src: Government, together with business and labour, have been striving to improve decent housing and living conditions in mining towns.
tgt: Mmuso, mmoho le dikgwebo le basebetsi, esale o tsitlallela ho ntlafatsa bodulo bo hlwahlwa le maemo a bophelo ditoropong tsa merafo.

src: Overall R18 billion has been dedicated to ongoing work in distressed mining communities, the bulk of which is from government with mining companies contributing approximately a third of the funding.
tgt: Ka kakaretso R18 bilione e behetswe ka thoko bakeng sa mosebetsi o ntseng o tswela pele dibakeng tsa merafo tse sokolang, eo boholo ba yona bo tswang mmusong moo dikhamphani tsa merafo di nyehalang ho ka etsang nngwe-borarong ba dithuso tsa ditjhelete.

src: Cabinet approved the inclusion of the Security Cluster Ministers to the Inter-ministerial committee (IMC) on Immigration which was announced by President Zuma.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenyeletswa ha Moifo wa Matona a Tshireletso ho Komiti e Kopanetsweng ya Matona mabapi le Bofalli (IMC) ho ileng ha tsebiswa ke Moporesidente Zuma.

src: The IMC, led by Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa, will examine and solve the potential and unintended consequences of the new immigration regulations on various sectors, including tourism and investment.
tgt: IMC, e eteletsweng pele ke Motlatsi wa Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa, e tla hlahloba le ho rarolla ditlamorao tse ka bang teng ntle le maikemisetso tsa melawana ya bofalli makaleng a fapafapaneng, ho kenyeletsa bohahlaudi le matsete.

src: The IMC will comprise of the Ministers of Tourism Home Affairs Trade and Industry Social Development Small Business Development, and the Security Cluster.
tgt: IMC e tla boptjwa ka Matona a Bohahlaudi Merero ya Lehae Kgwebo le Indaseteri Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba Ntshetsopele ya Dikgwebo tse Nyenyane, le Moifo wa Tshireletso.

src: Cabinet’s position on key issues in the environment.
tgt: Maemo a Kabinete mabapi le dintlha tsa bohlokwa ka hara tikoloho.

src: Cabinet welcomed the Women’s Day celebrations that took place in Sasolburg in the Free State under the theme: “Women United in Moving South Africa Forward”.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse mekete ya Letsatsi la Basadi le o neng o tshwaretswe Sasolburg ho la Foreisetata tlasa mookotaba: “Basadi ba Kopane bakeng sa ho Ntshetsa Aforika Borwa Pele”.

src: Thousands of women gathered at the Harry Gwala Stadium in Sasolburg to recognise the important role that political activism by women played during the struggle for liberation against colonialism and apartheid.
tgt: Dikete tsa basadi di ne di bokane Lebaleng la Dipapadi la Harry Gwala Sasolburg ho ananela karolo ya bohlokwa e bapetsweng ke basadi nakong ya boitseko ba tokoloho kgahlanong le bokoloniale le kgethollo.

src: Cabinet calls on all sectors of society to sustain the theme of Women’s Month and to continue working towards ensuring that all women, particularly the girl child, are empowered and freed from societal prejudices so that we can address gender equality in the WEBTOKEN addition, President Zuma also released a first-of-its-kind report on the Status of Women in South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho makala kaofela a setjhaba ho tsitlallela mookotaba wa Kgwedi ya Basadi le ho tswela pele ho sebeletsa ho netefatsa hore basadi kaofela, haholoholo bana ba banana, ba a ntlafatswa le ho lokollwa leemeng la setjhaba hore re tle re sebetsane le tekatekano ya bong ka hara naha.

src: The report notes, great strides made in the country since 1994 to improve the status of women.
tgt: Hodima moo, Moporesidente Zuma hape o lokolotse tlaleho ya pele ya mofuta wa yona e mabapi le Maemo a Basadi ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: This report was compiled by the Department of Women after hosting dialogues across the country between March and June this year (2015).
tgt: Tlaleho e ananela, menyabuketso e meholo e entsweng ka hara naha esale ho tloha ka 1994 bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa maemo a basadi.

src: This report serves as a baseline document for the promotion of women’s socio-economic empowerment, gender equality and human rights.
tgt: Tlaleho ena e sebetsa jwaloka tokomane ya motheo bakeng sa kgothaletso ya matlafatso ya basadi, tekatekano ya bong le ditokelo tsa botho.

src: Government will use the remainder of the month to profile women achievers and their participation in the economy, especially in areas where they are under-represented.
tgt: Mmuso o tla sebedisa karolo e setseng ya kgwedi ena bakeng sa ho hlophisa diporofaele tsa basadi ba fihlelletseng tse kgolo le bonkakarolo ba bona ka hara moruo, haholoholo moo ba hlokang boemedi bo bonahalang.

src: These include the Women in Science Awards (13 August) and Women in Water and Sanitation Awards (23 August).
tgt: Tsena di kenyeletsa Dikgau tsa Basadi ho tsa Saense (13 Phato) le Dikgau tsa Basadi ho tsa Metsi le tsamaiso ya Dikgwerekgwere (23 Phato).

src: Cabinet commends the Proteas for making South Africa proud at the Netball World Cup in Sydney, Australia.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa DiProtea bakeng sa ho etsa Aforika Borwa motlotlo ho Mohope wa Lefatshe wa Netebolo Sydney, ho la Australia.

src: The South African team is on the verge of qualifying for the semi-finals of the World Cup after having played rigorous and tough games thus far.
tgt: Sehlopha sa Aforika Borwa se mathuleng a ho kenela seka makgaolakgang a Mohope wa Lefatshe kamora ho bapala ka matla le dipapadi tse boima ho fihlela mona.

src: According to the International Netball Federation, South Africa is now ranked number five in the world.
tgt: Ho ya ka Federeishene ya Matjhaba ya Netebolo, Aforika Borwa jwale e behilwe maemong a bohlano lefatsheng.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to support the Proteas as they continue in the conquest at the World Cup.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa oohle ho tshehetsa DiProtea ha di ntse di tswela pele tlholong ya tsona Mohopeng wa Lefatshe.

src: Cabinet has joined President Zuma in conveying its condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of the murdered members of the SAPSuch senseless killings should be condemned by all South Africans.
tgt: Kabinete e ipapisitse le Moporesidente Zuma bakeng sa ho fetisa matshediso ho malapa, metswalle le basebetsi mmoho ba ditho tse bolailweng tsa SAPDipolao tsena tse hlokang kelello di lokelwa ke ho tshwelwa ka mathe ke maAforika Borwa kaofela.

src: Policemen and policewomen are central in protecting communities from criminal elements in our society.
tgt: Mapolesa a banna le a basadi a bohlokwa haholo bakeng sa ho tshireletsa badudi ho ditlokotsebe ka hara setjhaba.

src: The senseless murders not only rob the country and society of law-enforcement officers, but they also deprive families of husbands, wives, brothers, sisters and parents.
tgt: Dipolao tsena tse hlokang kelello ha di hlothele feela naha le setjhaba bahlanka ba tiisetso ya molao, empa di boela di tima malapa banna, basadi, dikgaitsedi le batswadi.

src: Cabinet calls on those with information about these senseless murders to come forward and work with law-enforcement agencies to ensure that those responsible are arrested and face the full might of the law.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho bohle ba nang le tlhahisoleseding ka dipolao tsena tse hlokang kelello ho hlahella le ho sebetsa mmoho le makala a tiisetso ya molao bakeng sa ho netefatsa hore ba nkang boikarabelo ba a tshwarwa le ho tobana le letsoho le matla la molao.

src: Cabinet congratulates Team South Africa on their outstanding performance at the 16th FINA (International Swimming Federation) World Championship in Kazan, Russia during which they won two gold and three silver medals.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Sehlopha sa Aforika Borwa mabapi le tshebetso ya sona e hlwahlwa ho Bompodi ba Lefatshe ba bo-16 ba FINA (Federeishene ya Matjhaba ya Disesi) Kazan, ho la Russia moo se hapileng dimedale tse pedi tsa gauta le tse tharo tsa silifera.

src: Key Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved the release for public consultation of the Green Paper on National Rail Policy, which addresses freight and passenger rail transportation.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho lokollelwa setjhaba ha Pampiri e Tala Mabapi le Leano la Naha la Diterene, le shebaneng le maeto a diterene a thepa le bapalami.

src: This policy, which is aligned to the work of the Presidential Infrastructure Coordinating Commission, enables the revitalisation of the railway industry through strategic investment-led policy interventions that are aligned to the National Development Plan (NDP).The aim is to create an efficient transport system that is able to compete locally and internationally, and reduce transportation costs.
tgt: Leano lena, le imatahantseng le Khomishene ya Kantoro ya Moporesidente e mabapi le Dikgokahano tsa Dikaho tsa Motheo, e thusa bakeng sa tsoseletso ya indaseteri ya diterene ka leano le itshetlehileng hodima boitshunyako ba mawa a matsete bo imatahantseng le Morero wa Naha wa Ntshetsopele (NDP).Sepheo ke ho aha tsamaiso ya dipalangwang e kgabane e kgonang ho phehisana le ditshebeletso tse ding ka hara naha le matjhabeng, le ho fokotsa ditjeho tsa dipalangwang.

src: This will encourage the use of appropriate technologies to increase productivity and acquisition of much-needed skills in the economy.
tgt: Sena se tla kgothaletsa tshebediso ya dithekenoloji tse nepahetseng bakeng sa ho phahamisa bokgoni ba tlhahiso le phumantsho ya maitsebelo a batlehang haholo ka hara moruo.

src: It also improves rural access, increased mobility and job creation.
tgt: Hape le ntlafatsa phihlello ya dibaka tsa mahae, motsamao o eketsehileng le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi.

src: Cabinet approved the circulation of the “National Skills Development Strategy and Sector Education and Training Authorities beyond 2016 within the context of an integrated, differentiated post-school education and training system” document for public consultation.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana potolohiso ya tokomane ya “Lewa la Naha la Ntshetsopele ya Maitsebelo le Lekala la Bolaodi ba Thuto le Thupello ho ya ka nqane ho 2016 ka hara moelelo wa tsamaiso ya thuto le thupello ya kamora sekolo o kopanetsweng, o tswakatswakaneng” hore setjhaba se tshwaele.

src: The document addresses the efficiency and effectiveness of skills development institutions and their integration into the broader post-school education and training WEBTOKEN particular, it proposes for the next National Skills Development Strategy to prioritise occupations that have been identified as being in high demand for the implementation of national priority programmes.
tgt: Tokomane ena e shebana le bohlwahlwa le bokgabane ba ditsha tsa ntshetsopele ya maitsebelo le ho kenyeletswa ha tsona ho tsamaiso ya thuto le thupello e phatlaletseng ya kamora sekolo.

src: It also addresses the efficiency and effectiveness of governance matters of sector education and training authorities in the issuing of grants for priority occupations.
tgt: Haholoholo, e sisinya hore Lewa la Naha la Ntshetsopele ya Maitsebelo le latelang le behe ka sehloohong mesebetsi e hlwailweng e le e hlokahalang ka ho fetisisa bakeng sa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha mananeo a ka sehloohong a naha.

src: This is in line with government priorities relating to Operation Phakisa on growing the Oceans Economy.
tgt: Hape e shebana le bohlwahlwa le bokgabane ba dintlha tsa tsamaiso ya lekala la bolaodi ba thuto le thupello mabapi le ho ntsha dithuso tsa ditjhelete bakeng sa mesebetsi e ka sehloohong.

src: This will result in relocating manganese operations from the ports of Port Elizabeth and Saldanha to the Port of Ngqura.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho ntshuwa ha laesense ya tshebetso ya ka nako tsohle ho Theminale ya Maemakepe ya Transnet bakeng sa ho sebetsana le theminale ya dikhontheinara tsa mankanisi e Boemakepeng ba Ngqura, bo fumanehang lebopong le ka botjhabela la Aforika Borwa, dikilomitara tse 20 leboya botjhabela ho Port Elizabeth le ho batla ho fihla mahareng a Durban le Motse Kapa.

src: Cabinet approved for South Africa to accede to the International Convention on Liability and Compensation for Damage in Connection with Carriage of Hazardous and Noxious Substances by Sea, 2010.The convention ensures compensation for damage to persons and property, cost of clean-up and reinstatement measures, and economic losses resulting from the maritime transport of hazardous and noxious substances that may pollute the ocean.
tgt: Sena se tsamaelana le merero e ka sehloohong ya mmuso e amanang le Operation Phakisa bakeng sa ho hodisa Moruo wa Mawatle.

src: South Africa will be able to access the fund to assist in hazardous and noxious substances incidents once all the parliamentary processes to domesticate this convention have been completed.
tgt: Sena se tla baka hore ditshebetso tsa mankanisi di tloswe maemakepeng a Port Elizabeth le Saldanha ho ya Boemakepeng ba Ngqura.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Films and Publications Amendment Bill, 2015 to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa ha Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Difilimi le Diphatlalatso, ya 2015 ho Palamente.

src: The Bill amends the Films and Publications Act, 1996 (Act 65 of 1996).
tgt: Bili e hlomathisa Molao wa Difilimi le Diphatlalatso, wa 1996 (Molao 65 wa 1996).

src: The amendments provide for technological advances, especially online and social-media platforms, in order to protect children from being exposed to disturbing and harmful media content in all platforms (physical and online).The Bill strengthens the duties imposed on mobile networks and Internet service providers to protect the public and children during usage of their services.
tgt: Dihlomathiso di fana ka dintshetsopele tsa thekenoloji, haholoholo mapatlelong a tsa inthanete le mekgwa ya dikgokahanyo ya kahisano, bakeng sa ho tshireletsa bana kgahlanong le ho pepesetswa dikateng tsa mekgwa ya dikgokahanyo e sitisang maikutlo le ho ba kotsi mapatlelong oohle (a tshwarehang le a inthanete).Bili e matlafatsa makgetho a behilweng hodima marangrang a dikgokahanyo le ho bafani ba tshebeletso ba Inthanete bakeng sa ho tshireletsa setjhaba le bana nakong ya tshebediso ya ditshebeletso tsa bona.

src: The Independent Communications Authority of South Africa will not issue licences or renewals without confirmation from the Film and Publication Board of full compliance with its legislation.
tgt: Bookamedi bo Ikemetseng ba Dikgokahanyo ba Aforika Borwa bo keke ba fana ka dilaesense kapa ho fana botjha ntle le tiisetso ho tswa ho Boto ya Difilimi le Diphatlalatso bakeng sa boimatahanyo bo felletseng le molao.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: President Zuma will attend the 35th Ordinary Summit of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Heads of State from 17 to 18 August 2015 in Gaborone, Botswana.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla kenela Seboka se Tlwaelehileng sa bo-35 sa (SADC) sa Dihlooho tsa Mebuso ho tloha ka la 17 ho isa ho la 18 Phato 2015 Gaborone, ho la Botswana.

src: At the summit, the President will hand over the chairpersonship of the SADC Organ on Politics, Defence and Security Cooperation.
tgt: Sebokeng sena, Moporesidente o tla fana ka marapo a bodulasetulo ba Lekala la Dipolotiki la SADC, Tshireletso le Tshebedisano-mmoho ho tsa Polokeho.

src: In this role, South Africa has led six SADC Electoral Observation Missions, which certified that all the elections were peaceful and credible.
tgt: Mosebetsing ona, Aforika Borwa e ile ya etella pele Merero e tsheletseng ya SADC ya Tekolo ya Dikgetho, e tiiseditseng hore dikgetho kaofela e ne e le tsa kgotso tse nang le botshepehi.

src: Deputy President Ramaphosa will undertake a Working Visit to Japan from 24 to 25 August 2015.
tgt: Motlatsi wa Moporesidente Ramaphosa o tla nka Leeto la Tshebetso ho ya Japan ho tloha ka la 24 ho isa ho la 25 Phato 2015.

src: This visit includes a courtesy call to Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and participation in the South Africa-Japan External Trade Organisation Business Seminar.
tgt: Leeto lena le kenyeletsa leeto la tlhompho ho Tonakgolo Shinzo Abe le ho nka karolo ho Seminara ya Aforika Borwa-Japan ya Mokgatlo wa Dikgwebo tsa ka Ntle.

src: Cabinet welcomes the working visit to Japan, which will strengthen the friendship and mutual understanding that exists between the two countries.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela leeto la Tshebetso la ho ya Japan, le tla tiisa setswalle le kutlwisisano e teng pakeng tsa dinaha tsena tse pedi.

src: South Africa and Japan also share similar views on the importance of multilateralism and the need to reform the United Nations (UN) Security Council and UN system at the 70th UN General Assembly meeting next month.
tgt: Aforika Borwa le Japan hape di arolelana ditjhebo mabapi le bohlokwa ba ditherisano tsa bongata le tlhokeho ya ho hlabolla tsamaiso ya Lekgotla la Tshireletso la Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) kopanong ya bo-70th ya Kopano ya Kakaretso ya UN kgweding e tlang.

src: President Zuma will undertake a Presidential Imbizo to Eersterust, Pretoria on 21 August 2015 to address issues related to substance abuse.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla kenela Imbizo ya Kantoro ya Moporesidente Eersterust, ho la Pretoria ka la 21 Phato 2015 ho bua ka dintlha tse amanang le tshebediso e mpe ya dithethefatsi.

src: The National Drug Master Plan, 2013-2017, coordinates government’s efforts in the fight against alcohol and substance abuse.
tgt: Moralo wa Naha wa Mankgonthe mabapi le Dithethefatsi, 2013-2017, o hokahanya mekutu ya mmuso ntweng e kgahlanong le tshebediso e mpe ya jwala le dithethefatsi.

src: Cabinet calls on communities to work with government and law-enforcement agencies to rid our society of substance abuse, which is the cause of numerous social problems, including violence against women and child abuse.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho badudi ho sebetsa le mmuso le makala a tiisetso ya molao ho fedisa tshebediso e mpe ya dithethefatsi ka hara setjhaba sa rona, e leng sesosa sa mathata a mangata a kahisano, ho kenyeletsa dikgoka kgahlanong le basadi le tlhekefetso ya bana.

src: Parents and guardians have a critical role to play in ensuring that children are protected and nurtured.
tgt: Batswadi le bahlokomedi ba na le mosebetsi o hlokolosi oo ba lokelang ho o etsa bakeng sa ho netefatsa hore bana ba tshireletsehile le ho hodiswa hantle.

src: Cabinet welcomes the opening of the newly upgraded Makgatho Lewanika Mandela Primary School in Mvezo in the Eastern Cape on 25 August 2015 by President Zuma.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela ho bulwa ha Sekolo sa Poraemari sa Makgatho Lewanika Mandela se ntlafaditsweng botjha Mvezo ho la Kapa Botjhabela ka la 25 Phato 2015 ke Moporesidente Zuma.

src: The school is part of government’s ongoing work to restore dignity to learners and provide schools in rural areas with more modern facilities.
tgt: Sekolo sena ke karolo ya mosebetsi o ntseng o tswela pele wa mmuso bakeng sa ho kgutlisetsa seriti ho baithuti le ho fana ka dikolo dibakeng tsa mahae tse nang le disebediswa tsa sejwalejwale.

src: Through the Department of Basic Education’s Accelerated Schools Infrastructure Delivery Initiative (ASIDI), government has eradicated a number of poorly constructed schools and created a more conducive learning environment.
tgt: Ka Boikitlaetso ba Lefapha la Thuto ya Motheo ba Phano e Potlakisitsweng ya Dikaho tsa Motheo tsa Dikolo (ASIDI), mmuso o fedisitse palo e itseng ya dikolo tse ahilweng hampe le ho bopa tikoloho e batlang e loketse ho ithuta.

src: So far, ASIDI has completed 116 schools and provided water to 499 schools, sanitation to 425 and electricity to 298.
tgt: Ho fihlela mona, ASIDI e se e phethetse dikolo tse 116 le ho fana ka metsi ho dikolo tse 499, tsamaiso ya dikgwerekgwere ho tse 425 le motlakase ho tse 298.

src: Deputy President Ramaphosa will attend the International Federation of Library Associations’ World Library and Information Congress taking place at the Cape Town International Convention Centre from 15 to 21 August 2015 under the theme: “Dynamic Libraries: Access, Development and Transformation”.
tgt: Motlatsi wa Moporesidente Ramaphosa o tla kenela Seboka sa Federeishene ya Matjhaba ya Mekgatlo ya Lefatshe ya Dilaeborari le Tlhahisoleseding e tla tshwarwa Setsing sa Matjhaba sa Dikopano sa Motse Kapa ho tloha ka la 15 ho isa ka la 21 Phato 2015 tlasa mookotaba: “Dilaeborari tse Hlwahlwa: Phihlello, Ntshetsopele le Diphethoho”.

src: The congress coincides with government’s roll-out of more than 1 000 school libraries across the country between 18 July 2015 and 18 July 2016 to encourage more learners to read.
tgt: Seboka se kopana le phano ya mmuso ya dilaeborari tsa dikolo tse fetang 1 000 ho phatlalla le naha mahareng a 18 Phupu 2015 le 18 Phupu 2016 ho kgothaletsa baithuti ba bangata ho bala.

src: The Department of Basic Education is also lobbying various private business organisations and non-governmental organisations to support the campaign by donating books and establishing libraries, among other things.
tgt: Lefapha la Thuto ya Motheo le boetse le qholotsa mekgatlo e fapafapaneng ya dikgwebo tsa poraefete le mekgatlo eo e seng ya mmuso ho tshehetsa letsholo lena ka ho nyehela ka dibuka le ho theha dilaeborari, hara tse ding.

src: Cabinet appeals to parents and teachers to endeavour to make books accessible to young people, and calls on communities to donate books and establish reading clubs because a reading nation is a winning nation.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho batswadi le matitjhere ho etsa boiteko ba hore bana ba fihlella dibuka, le ho ipiletsa ho badudi ho nyehela ka dibuka le ho theha dihlopha tsa ho bala hobane setjhaba se balang ke setjhaba se hlolang.

src: Tourism Minister Derek Hanekom will launch Tourism Month on 16 August 2015 at Euphoria Golf Estate, Mookgophong in Limpopo under the theme: “A Million new opportunities Await”, which is derived from World Tourism Day (27 September) theme: “1 Billion Tourists – 1 Billion Opportunities”.
tgt: Letona la Bohahlaudi Derek Hanekom le tla thakgola Kgwedi ya Bohahlaudi ka la 16 Phato 2015 Euphoria Golf Estate, Mookgophong ho la Limpopo tlasa mookotaba: “Menyetla e metjha e Milione e re Emetse”, o nkuweng ho tswa ho mookotaba wa Letsatsi la Lefatshe la Bohahlaudi (27 Loetse) o reng: “Bahahlaudi ba Bilione – Menyetla e Bilione”.

src: The international and local themes aim to make tourists aware of the importance of responsible tourism.
tgt: Meokotaba ya matjhaba le ya lehae e reretswe ho lemosa bahahlaudi ka bohlokwa ba bohahlaudi bo nang le boikarabelo.

src: As part of this, tourists are encouraged to respect cultures, protect heritage, save energy and water, and most importantly, buy regional products to support local jobs.
tgt: Jwaloka karolo ya sena, bahahlaudi ba kgothaletswa ho hlompha meetlo, ho tshireletsa lefa, ho boloka eneji le metsi, mme ka ho fetisisa, ba reke dihlahiswa tsa lebatowa bakeng sa ho tshehetsa mesebetsi ya lehae.

src: Cabinet encourages South Africans to explore our fascinating and beautiful country, and by doing so help maintain jobs and support local products.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa maAforika Borwa ho tseba naha ya rona e makatsang le ho ba ntle, mme ka seo ba thusa ho baballa mesebetsi le ho tshehetsa dihlahiswa tsa lehae.

src: The departments of sport and recreation and of women have partnered with G-Sport in honouring South African women who participate in sport.
tgt: Mafapha a dipapadi le boithapollo le a basadi a ikopantse le G-Sport mabapi le ho tlotla basadi ba Aforika Borwa ba nkang karolo dipapading.

src: The Department of Sport and Recreation and G-Sport will bestow honours on deserving women athletes and administrators who strove against all forms of oppression to raise the flag of this country.
tgt: Lefapha la dipapadi le Boithapollo le G-Sport a tla fana ka dikgau ho basadi ba lokelang ho tsa mabelo le batsamaisi ba ikitlaeditseng kgahlanong le ditsela tsohle tsa kgatello bakeng sa ho phahamisa folakga ya naha ena.

src: The department remains conscious of the work needed in advancing the agenda for equality of all women involved in sport, both in administration and in participation.
tgt: Lefapha le dula le fadimehetse mosebetsi o hlokahalang bakeng sa ho ntshetsapele lenaneo la tekatekano ya basadi bohle ba itahletseng ka setotswana dipapading, ka bobedi ho tsa tsamaiso le ho nka karolo.

src: While the department recognises that more work still needs to be done in this regard, it is committed to joining hands with those who are determined to make a difference in the plight of women.
tgt: Ha lefapha le sa lemohile hore ho na le mosebetsi o mongata o lokelang ho etswa tabeng ena, le itlamme ho kopanya matsoho le ba ikemiseditseng ho etsa phapang bothateng ba basadi.

src: Cabinet encourages all South Africans to nominate recipients for the 2016 National Orders Awards, which are the highest awards that South Africa bestows on its citizens and eminent foreign nationals who have contributed towards the advancement of democracy and who have made a significant impact on improving the lives of South Africans.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa maAforika Borwa kaofela ho kgetha baamohedi bakeng sa Dikgau tsa Tlotlo tsa Naha tsa 2016, tseo e leng dikgau tse phahameng ka ho fetisisa tseo Aforika Borwa e di abelang baahi ba yona le melata e hlahelletseng ka mahetla e nyehetseng bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya demokerasi le ba entseng kgahlamelo ya bohlokwa bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa bophelo ba maAforika Borwa.

src: The six National Orders are the Order of Mendi for Bravery, the Order of Ikhamanga, the Order of the Baobab, the Order of Luthuli, the Order of Mapungubwe, and the Order of the Companions of OR Tambo.
tgt: Dikgau tsa Tlotlo tsa Naha tse tsheletseng ke Tlotlo ya Mendi bakeng sa ho bontsha Sebete, Tlotlo ya Ikhamanga, Tlotlo ya Baobao, Tlotlo ya Luthuli, Tlotlo ya Mapungubwe, le Tlotlo ya Metswalle ya OR Tambo.

src: The closing date for nominations is 31 August 2015.
tgt: Letsatsi la ho qetela bakeng sa dikgetho ke la 31 Phato 2015.

src: Nomination forms can be downloaded from WEBTOKEN and must be accompanied by a one-page motivation for the nominated person.
tgt: Diforomo tsa dikgetho di ka hulwa ho tswa ho WEBTOKEN mme di lokela ho tsamaiswa le kgothaletso ya leqephe le le leng bakeng sa motho ya kgethilweng.

src: AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.

src: Cabinet welcomed Unit 6 of Medupi Power Station in Lephalale, Limpopo coming into full commercial operation and contributing 800 megawatts (MW) power into the national grid.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse hore Yuniti 6 ya Seteishene sa Matla a Motlakase sa Medupi Lephalale, ho la Limpopo e sebetsa ka botlalo le ho nyehela ka dimekawate tse 800 (MW) tsa matla a motlakase ho marangrang a naha.

src: The Medupi Power Station Project is a greenfield coal-fired power plant comprising six units rated in total at 4 764 MW installed capacity.
tgt: Porojeke ya Seteishene sa Matla a Motlakase sa Medupi ke polante ya moya o hlwekileng e besetswang ka mashala e nang le diyuniti tse tsheletseng tse akanyetswang kaofela ho palo ya 4 764 MW ya bokgoni bo ka hokelwang.

src: President Jacob Zuma will launch this unit on 30 August WEBTOKEN of the Medupi Power Station started in May 2007 and all six units are expected to be operational in the first half of 2019.
tgt: Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o tla thakgola yuniti ena ka la 30 Phato 2015.Kaho ya Seteishene sa Matla a Motlakase sa Medupi e qadile ka Motsheanong 2007 mme diyuniti kaofela tse tsheletseng di lebeletswe hore di be di sebetsa halofong ya pele ya 2019.

src: Once completed, it will be the fourth largest coal-fired plant and the largest dry-cooled power station in the world.
tgt: Hang ha se se se phethetswe, e tla be e le polante ya bone e kgolo ka ho fetisisa e besetswang ka mashala le ho ba e omiswang ka moya lefatsheng.

src: The planned operational life of the power station is 50 years.
tgt: Nako ya tshebetso ya seteishene sena sa motlakase e reretswe ho ba dilemo tse 50.Yuniti 6 e qadile ho hokelwa ho marangrang a naha ka la 2 Tlhakubele selemong sena mme e ne e ntse e fana ka motlakase ho marangrang a naha ka diqonwanaqonwana ha e ne e ntse e le tlasa diteko nako le nako tsa hore e ka sebetsa ka botlalo.

src: Unit 6 was first synchronised to the national grid on 2 March this year and has been supplying electricity to the national grid intermittently whilst undergoing regular optimisation tests.
tgt: Nakong ena Yuniti 6 e kgonne ho bebofatsa kgatello hodima tsamaiso ya motlakase wa naha, e thusa ho phema ho kgaoha ha motlakase kapa ho fokotsa sekgahla sa kgaoho.

src: During this period Unit 6 has been able to alleviate pressure on the national electricity system, helping to either avoid load-shedding altogether or minimise its severity.
tgt: Tshebetso ya tsa moruo ya yuniti e fihlelletswe, hantle ka hara nako eo e neng e e behetswe ya dikgwedi tse tsheletseng kamora hoba e hokelwe.

src: The unit’s commercial operation has been achieved, well within the normally stipulated period of six months after first synchronisation.
tgt: Tshebetso ya tsa moruo ya Yuniti 6 ya Seteishene sa Matla a Motlakase sa Medupi ke mokolokotwane o hlokolosi mekutung ya rona ya aha bokgoni bo botjha ba ho fehla motlakase.

src: The commercial operation of Unit 6 of the Medupi Power Station is a critical milestone in our effort to build new generating capacity.
tgt: Ho fetafeta moo Kabinete e ananetse diqaka tsa hajwale tseo naha e ntseng e tobane le tsona mabapi le phano ya motlakase.

src: Cabinet further appreciated the current constraints the country still faces on the power supply.
tgt: Ha ho kgaoha ha motlakatse e le ntho e sa kgahliseng, Eskom e ikemiseditse ho etsa ditokiso tse hlokehang bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa bokgoni ba dipolante tsa rona ka ditshitiso tsa amohelehang.

src: Next Monday (31 August), Unit 2 of the Koeberg Power Station in the Western Cape will be shut down for planned maintenance.
tgt: Ka Mantaha o tlang (31 Phato), Yuniti 2 ya Seteishene sa Matla a Motlakase sa Koeberg ho la Kapa Bophirima e tla kwalwa bakeng sa ditokiso tse rerilweng.

src: The unit is expected to return to service after three months.
tgt: Yuniti e lebeletswe ho boela tshebetsong kamora dikgwedi tse tharo.

src: The scheduled shutdown of Koeberg Unit 2 is part of Eskom’s overall maintenance programme for its fleet of power stations.
tgt: Ho kwalwa ho rerilweng ha Yuniti 2 ya Koeberg ke karolo ya lenaneo ka kakaretso la ditokiso la Eskom bakeng sa lethathama la yona la diteishene tsa motlakase.

src: Every 16 to 18 months, each of the two units at Koeberg is shut down for refueling, inspection and maintenance.
tgt: Dikgweding tse ding le tse ding tse 16 ho isa ho tse 18, yuniti ka nngwe ya tse pedi tsa Koeberg e a kwalwa bakeng sa ho tshela mafura, tlhatlhobo le ditokiso.

src: The routine shutdowns are scheduled so as to avoid having both units out of service at the same time and to avoid the winter months in each year.
tgt: Ho kwalwa ho setlwaeding ho reretswe bakeng sa hore ho seke ha etsahala hore diyuniti ka bobedi di seke tsa sebetsa ka nako e le nngwe le ho phema dikgwedi tsa mariha selemong ka seng.

src: Whilst we continue to make progress in improving our electricity generation capacity, Cabinet calls on South Africans to continue using electricity sparingly.
tgt: Leha re tswela pele ho etsa kgatelo pele bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa bokgoni ba rona ba ho fehla motlakase, Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ho tswela pele ho sebedisa motlakase ka paballo.

src: Summit of Heads of State and Government.
tgt: Seboka sa Dihlooho tsa Dipuso le Mmuso.

src: Cabinet welcomed the outcomes from the 35th Ordinary Southern African Development Community (SADC) Summit of Heads of State and Government, wherein President Zuma led the South African delegation.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse diphetho ho tswa ho Seboka sa bo-35 se Tlwaelehileng sa (SADC) sa Dihlooho tsa Dipuso le Mmuso, moo Moporesidente Zuma a neng a eteletse pele kemedi ya Aforika Borwa.

src: The summit adopted the revised Regional Indicative Strategic Development Plan 2015-2020.
tgt: Seboka se amohetse Moralo wa Lewa la Pontsho ya Ntshetsopele ya Lebatowa wa 2015-2020.

src: The summit further signed three agreements/protocols that will enable the region to address its key challenges of unemployment and poverty eradication in a sustainable way.
tgt: Ho fetafeta moo seboka se saenne ditumellano/diporothokhole tse tla kgontshang lebatowa ho sebetsana le diphephetso tsa lona tse ka sehloohong tsa tlhoko ya mesebetsi le phediso ya bofuma ka tsela ya moshwelella.

src: Agreement amending the Protocol on Politics, Defence and Security Cooperation (Protocol) and Agreement amending the Treaty of the SADC (Treaty).
tgt: Tumellano e hlomathisang Porothokhole ya Tshebedisano-mmoho ho Dipolotiki, Tshireletso le Polokeho le Tumellano e hlomathisang Tumellano ya SADDitumellano tsena di tla dumella Komiti ya Tshireletso le Polokeho ya Dipuso tse Kopanetsweng tsa Tshebedisano-mmoho tsa Lekala la Dipolotiki, Tshireletso le Polokeho ho sebetsa jwaloka foramo e hokahanyang bakeng sa Dihlooho tsa Tlhabollo ya Batshwaruwa le Ditjhankane ka hara Aforika e Borwa.

src: These agreements will allow the Inter-State Defence and Security Committee of the Organ on Politics, Defence and Security Cooperation to serve as a coordinating forum for the Chiefs of Corrections and Prisons in Southern Africa.
tgt: Boitlamo mabapi le Ntshetsopele le Matlafatso ya Batjha e hohela tsepamiso ya maikutlo ho maemo a potlakileng a ntshetsopele ya batjha le matlafatso mabapi le tshebedisano-mmoho, momahano, ntshetsopele le kgotso, le polokeho ka hara lebatowa.

src: Declaration on Youth Development and Empowerment draws attention to the urgency of youth development and empowerment in the context of regional cooperation, integration, development and peace, and security in the region.
tgt: Porothokhole mabapi le Ditshebeletso tsa Kgwebo bakeng sa ho lokolla ditshebeletso tsa kgwebo tsa ka hare tsa SADC ka morero wa ho bopa mmaraka o le mong bakeng sa ditshebeletso ka hara lebatowa.

src: Protocol on Trade Services to liberalise intra-SADC trade in services with a view to creating a single market for services in the region.
tgt: Ho amohelwa ha Moralo o Shebilweng botjha wa Lewa la Pontsho ya Ntshetsopele ya Lebatowa 2015-2020 ebile mokolokotwane o ka sehloohong maitekong a SADC a ho hodisa kgwebo e kopanetsweng ya lebatowa.

src: The adoption of the Revised Regional Indicative Strategic Development Plan 2015-2020 was a major milestone in SADC’s endeavors to promote intra-regional trade.
tgt: Kabinete hape e amohetse qeto ya kopano ya Boraro Bo Menahaneng ba SADC, o neng o tshwerwe mthuleng a Seboka sa SADC se neng se kenetswe ke Motlatsi wa Moporesidente le Mothusi wa SADC Cyril Ramaphosa, ho thathiselletsa maemo a hajwale a ditherisano bakeng sa Khomishene ya Dipatlisiso ya SADC tabeng ya Mmuso wa Lesotho.

src: Visit to Japan by Deputy President.
tgt: Leeto la ho ya Japan la Motlatsi wa Moporesidente.

src: Cabinet welcomed the successful visit of Deputy President Ramaphosa to Japan.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse leeto le atlehileng la Motlatsi wa Moporesidente la ho ya Japan.

src: He was accompanied by a high-level ministerial and business delegation to promote South Africa as a preferred investment destination.
tgt: O ne a feleheditswe ke kemedi ya maemo a hodimo ya matona le borakgwebo bakeng sa ho kgothaletsa hore Aforika Borwa e be sebaka se labalabelwang sa matsete.

src: The Deputy President reassured Japanese investors that South Africa was open for business and briefed them on the country’s sound macro-economic stability and conducive business environment for investment, particularly in ventures that create jobs.
tgt: Motlatsi wa Moporesidente o tiiseditse batsetedi ba Japan hore Aforika Borwa e bulehile bakeng sa kgwebo le ho ba tsebisa ka botsitso ba moruo wa dikgwebo tse kgolo le maemo a lokileng tikolohong ya kgwebo bakeng sa matsete, haholoholo maitekong a ho hlahisa mesebetsi.

src: Deputy President Ramaphosa also used the visit to secure commitments from Japan to partner with South Africa in its efforts to combat the scourge of HIV and AIDS, TB and Malaria.
tgt: Motlatsi wa Moporesidente Ramaphosa hape o sebedisitse leeto lena ho fumana boitlamo ho tswa Japan ho theha semphato le Aforika Borwa mekutung ya yona ya ho lwantsha bothata ba HIV le AIDS, TB le Malaria.

src: Key Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved the bid of South Africa and the City of Durban to host the 2022 Commonwealth Games.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana boiketo ba Aforika Borwa le Motsemoholo wa Durban ho tshwara Dipapadi tsa Commonwealth tsa 2022.

src: This is the first time that Africa will host the Commonwealth Games and will position South Africa as a sport tourism destination and also provide opportunities for Team South WEBTOKEN will also make use of the infrastructure legacy of the 2010 FIFA World Cup™.The 2022 Commonwealth Games is expected to deliver up to R20 billion in output to the economy, translating into an additional R11 billion GDP growth.
tgt: Sena ke lekgetlo la pele la hore Aforika e tshware Dipapadi tsa Commonwealth mme se tla beha Aforika Borwa maemong a matle a ho ba sebaka sa bohahlaudi le hape ho fana ka menyetla ho Sehlopha sa Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of South Africa’s 5th Periodic Report (2009-2014) on the Implementation of the Convention on the Elimination of all Forms of Discrimination against Women in the Government Gazette, for public comment.
tgt: Ho tshwara dipapadi tsena hape ho tla sebedisa lefa la meralo ya motheo la Mohope wa Lefatshe wa FIFA wa 2010.Dipapadi tsa 2022 tsa Commonwealth di lebeletswe ho fana ka ho fihla ho R20 bilione ya lekeno ho moruo, e leng se tla fetohang tlatsetso ya R11 bilione kgolong ya GDP.. Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana phatlalatso ya Tlaleho ya Nako (2009-2014) ya bo-5th ya Aforika Borwa mabapi le ho Kenngwa Tshebetsong ha Khonvenshene e mabapi le ho Fediswa ha Mekgwa yohle ya Kgethollo kgahlanong le Basadi Koranteng ya Mmuso, bakeng sa ho tshwaela ha setjhaba.

src: The report provides an overview of the effectiveness of the range of laws, policies and programmes implemented in South Africa and highlights the achievements the country has made on women’s empowerment and gender equality.
tgt: Tlaleho e fana ka kakaretso ya bohlwahlwa ba letoto la melao, maano le mananeo a kentsweng tshebetsong ka hara Aforika Borwa le ho pepesa diphihlello tseo naha e di entseng mabapi le matlafatso ya basadi le tekatekano ya bong.

src: The report also recognises the persistent challenges and barriers to overcoming inequality and discrimination in the country.
tgt: Tlaleho hape e lemoha diphephetso le dithibelo tsa dulang di le teng tabeng ya ho hlola ho se lekalekane le kgethollo ka hara naha.

src: Cabinet approved for South Africa to join the Advisory Centre on World Trade Organisation (WTO) Law in Geneva.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana hore Aforika Borwa e kenele Setsi sa Boeletsi mabapi le Molao wa Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Kgwebo (WTO) ho la Geneva.

src: This is an international organisation that provides legal advice on WTO law, support in WTO dispute settlement proceedings and training in WTO law to developing and least developed WEBTOKEN a member South Africa will be able to source advice on the compatibility of trade measures of other countries that affect South African exports and of trade measures that South Africa wants to introduce.
tgt: Ona ke mokgatlo wa matjhaba o fanang ka keletso ya semolao ho molao wa WTO, o fana ka tshehetso ditsamaisong tsa ditharollo tsa diqaka tsa WTO le thupello ya molao wa WTO bakeng sa ho ntshetsapele dinaha tsa ntseng di le morao ntshetsopeleng.

src: The centre can also assist South Africa in WTO dispute settlement cases.
tgt: Jwaloka setho Aforika Borwa e tla kgona ho fumana keletso mabapi le boimatahanyo ho mekgwa ya kgwebo ya dinaha tse ding tse amang thepa e rekisetswang dinaha tsa ka ntle ya Aforika Borwa le mekgwa ya kgwebo eo Aforika Borwa e batlang ho kena ho yona.

src: Cabinet was briefed on the Minister of Finance, Mr Nhlanhla Nene, assuming the Presidency of the Council of Ministers of the Eastern and Southern Africa Anti-Money Laundering Group, for a year.
tgt: Kabinete e tsebisitswe ka ho nka marapo ha Letona la Ditjhelete, Monghadi Nhlanhla Nene, jwaloka Moporesidente wa Lekgotla la Matona a Aforika e ka Botjhabela le e ka Borwa a Sehlopha se Kgahlanong le Phapanyetsano ya Ditjhelete e seng Molaong, bakeng sa selemo.

src: As a result the Minister will host the 2015 annual meeting of the council.
tgt: Ka lebaka leo Letona le tla tshwara kopano ya lekgotla ya selemo ka seng ya 2015.Setheo sena sa mebuso e kopanetsweng ya lebatowa se kgothaletsa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ho sa fetofetoheng ha mekgwa ya ho lwantsha phapanyetsano e seng molaong ya ditjhelete le tshehetso ya ditjhelete bakeng sa boferekanyi ho phatlalla le lebatowa la Aforika e ka botjhabela le e ka borwa.

src: The regional intergovernmental body promotes consistent implementation of measures to combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism across the southern and eastern Africa region.
tgt: Sepheo sa botho ba Aforika Borwa ke ho matlafatsa mekgwa e kgahlanong le phapanyetsano ya ditjhelete e seng molaong le tshehetso ya ditjhelete ya boferekanyi ka hara lebatowa, e leng se kgothaletsang polokeho ya naha bobedi ka hara naha le ka hara lebatowa.

src: Cabinet continues to condemn the senseless killing of police officers.
tgt: Kabinete e tswela pele ho tshwela ka mathe dipolao tse hlokang kelello tsa bahlanka ba sepolesa.

src: Cabinet calls on members of public to work with the police in assisting to arrest the perpetrators of these killings.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho setjhaba ho sebetsa mmoho le sepolesa ho thusa ho tshwara baetsi ba dipolao tsena.

src: The law-enforcement agencies are working round the clock to ensure all the perpetrators of these criminal acts are apprehended.
tgt: Makala a tiisetso ya molao a sebetsa bosiu le motsheare ho netefatsa hore baetsi ba diketso tsena tsa botlokotsebe ba a tshwarwa.

src: Cabinet thanks the members of the public who contributed to the arrest of the three people linked to police killings.
tgt: Kabinete e leboha ditho tsa setjhaba tse nyehetseng bakeng sa ho tshwarwa ha batho ba bararo ba amahanngwang le dipolao tsa mapolesa.

src: Bills.
tgt: Dibili.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Foreign Service Bill, 2015 to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa ha Bili ya Tshebeletso ya Matjhaba, ya 2015 Palamenteng.

src: The Bill provides for a single Foreign Service system and creates an enabling legislative framework through which the current Foreign Service will be managed and regulated by the Department of International Relations and Cooperation.
tgt: Bili e fana ka tsamaiso e le nngwe ya Tshebeletso ya Matjhaba le ho bopa moralo wa molao o kgontshang Tshebeletso ya Matjhaba ya hajwale hore e tle e laolwe le ho hlophiswa ke Lefapha la Dikamano tsa Matjhaba le Tshebedisano-mmoho.

src: The Bill will be operationalised in the context of the Constitution, existing legislations applicable to the Public Service, security services and it is aligned to the NDP in enhancing service delivery.
tgt: Bili e tla kenngwa tshebetsong ho ya ka dipehelo tsa Molaotheo, melao e teng ka hara Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba, ditshebeletso tsa tshireletso mme e matahantswe le NDP bakeng sa ho matlafatsa phano ya ditshebeletso.

src: This will enhance efficiency, accountability and cost-effectiveness of capitalizing on opportunities abroad to advance South Africa’s foreign policy and developmental agenda.
tgt: Sena se tla phahamisa bohlwahlwa, boikarabelo le paballo ya ditjeho tsa ho nka monyetla wa menyetla ya dinaheng tsa ka ntle bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa leano la Aforika Borwa la matjhabeng le lenaneo la ntshetsopele.

src: Cabinet approved the tabling of the Traditional and Khoisan Leadership Bill, 2015 in Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho tekwa ha Bili ya Boetapele ba Setso le ba Makhoisan, ya 2015 Palamenteng.

src: The Bill contributes to the NDP’s key target of broadening social cohesion and unity while addressing the inequalities of the past by providing for the statutory recognition of the Khoisan communities and WEBTOKEN proposes the establishment of an Advisory Committee on Khoisan matters which will assist government with the recognition process relating to Khoisan communities and leaders.
tgt: Bili e nyehela ho maikemisetso a bohlokwa a NDP a ho pharalatsa momahano le bonngwe ba kahisano ha e ntse e sebetsana le ho se lekalekane ha mehleng ka ho fana ka kananelo ya semolao ya badudi ba Makhoisan le baetapele.

src: The Bill also consolidates existing national traditional leadership legislation which will result in the repeal of the National House of Traditional Leaders Act, 2009 (Act 22 of 2009) and the Traditional Leadership and Governance Framework Act, 2003 (Act 41 of 2003).
tgt: E sisinya ho thehwa ha Komiti ya Boeletsi e mabapi le ditaba tsa Makhoisan e tla thusa mmuso ka tsamaiso ya kananelo e amanang le badudi ba Makhoisan le baetapele.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: President Zuma will launch the War on Water Leaks project, announced in his 2015 State of the Nation Address, in Port Elizabeth on 28 August 2015, as part of government’s programme to address water loss from leaks.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla thakgola porojeke ya Ntwa ya ho Dutla ha Metsi, e tsebisitsweng ho Puo ya hae ka Maemo a Setjhaba ya 2015, Port Elizabeth ka la 28 Phato 2015, jwaloka karolo ya mananeo a mmuso a ho sebetsana le tahlelo ya metsi ka lebaka la ho dutla.

src: The project will train 15 000 young people as artisans and plumbers to fix leaks within their communities it will give them skills to start their own businesses or find suitable employment.
tgt: Porojeke e tla rupella batho ba batjha ba 15 000 jwaloka ditsebi le ba lokisang dipeipi ho lokisa ho dutla ho teng ka hara metse ya bona e tla ba neha maitsebelo a ho iqalla dikgwebo tsa bona kapa ba fumana mesebetsi e loketseng.

src: The first intake of 3 000 is being recruited for the current financial year.
tgt: Batjha ba pele ba ntseng ba thaothwa ba 3 000 bakeng sa selemo sa hajwale sa ditjhelete.

src: Water leaks account for nearly 40 per cent of the nation’s water loss and costs the country R7 billion a year.
tgt: Metsi a dutlang a akanngwa bakeng sa diphesente tse 40 tsa tahlehelo ya naha ya metsi mme di ja naha R7 bilione ka selemo.

src: President Zuma will attend the 70th Anniversary of the End of the Occupation of China and World War II in the People’s Republic of China (PRC) from 2 to 4 September 2015, and will have a bilateral engagement with President Xi Jinping.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla kenela Sehopotso sa bo-70 sa Qetello ya Kgapo ya China le Ntwa ya Bobedi ya Lefatshe ka hara Riphaboliki ya Setjhaba ya China (PRC) ho tloha ka la 2 ho isa ka la 4 Loetse 2015, mme o tla ba le ditherisano tsa ka bobedi le Moporesidente Xi Jinping.

src: South Africa’s relations with the PRC is at the level of a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership underpinned by the Beijing Declaration on the Establishment of a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, which covers all relations between the two countries.
tgt: Dikamano tsa Aforka Borwa le PRC di maemong a Lewa la Semphato se Pharaletseng tse itshetlehileng hodima Boitlamo ba Beijing mabapi le ho Thehwa ha Lewa la Semphato se Pharaletseng, le akaretsang dikamano tsohle pakeng tsa dinaha tsena tse pedi.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to celebrate our history and diverse cultures as the country marks Heritage Month in September under the theme: “Our indigenous knowledge, our heritage: Towards the identification, promotion and preservation of South African’s living heritage”.This year’s commemoration will take the format of a cultural fair and communities are encouraged to use their living heritage such as food, craft, dance and music to promote cultural diversity, human rights, nation-building and economic development.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa kaofela ho keteka nalane ya rona le botjhaba bo fapafapaneng ha naha e tshwaya Kgwedi ya Lefa ka Loetse tlasa mookotaba: “Tsebo ya rona ya tsa lapeng, lefa la rona: Re lebisa boitsebisong, kgothaletso le paballong ya lefa le phelang la Aforika Borwa”.Sehopotso sa selemong sena se tla latela mokgwa wa meketjana ya boithabiso mme badudi ba kgothaletswa ho sebedisa lefa la bona le phelang le kang dijo, bonono ba boiqapelo, motjeko le mmino ho kgothaletsa phapang ya botjhaba, ditokelo tsa botho, kaho ya setjhaba le ntshetsopele ya moruo.

src: South Africa will also celebrate Tourism Month in September, which is an opportune time for families to visit the country’s heritage sites to reconnect with our past.
tgt: Aforika Borwa hape e tla keteka Kgwedi ya Bohahlaudi ka Loetse, e leng nako e lokileng bakeng sa malapa ho etela dibaka tsa lefa hore re ikgokahanye le bophelo ba rona ba mehleng.

src: During Heritage Month, the Department of Arts and Culture will undertake a sod turning on the National Heroes Acre in Pretoria to signal the start of construction of a national monument that will depict the pre-colonial era, liberation struggle and the different heroes who fought for social progress.
tgt: Nakong ya Kgwedi ya Lefa, Lefapha la Bonono le Botjhaba le tla hlophisa ho phetholwa ha lekote ho Sebaka sa Bahale Pretoria ho tshwaya qalo ya kaho ya monyumente wa naha o tla bontshang nako ya pele ho bokoloniale, ntwa ya tokoloho le bahale ba fapaneng ba lwanetseng kgatelopele ya kahisano.

src: The annual South African Police Service (SAPS) National Commemoration Day on 6 September 2015 at the Union Buildings in Pretoria will celebrate the courage and dedication of officers who paid the ultimate price to protect communities.
tgt: Letsatsi la selemo ka seng la Sehopotso sa Naha sa Tshebeletso ya Sepolesa ya Aforika Borwa (SAPS) ka la 6 Loetse 2015 Meahong ya Kopano Pretoria le tla keteka kgothalo le boitelo ba bahlanka ba lefileng ka bophelo ba bona bakeng sa ho tshireletsa badudi.

src: Through the SAPS recruitment campaign an additional 6 252 members will be enlisted during the 2015/16 financial year to enhance detective services, visible policing, crime intelligence, forensic services, including protection and security services.
tgt: Ka letsholo la ho thaotha la SAPS ditho tsa tlatsetso tse 6 252 di tla ngodiswa nakong ya selemo sa ditjhelete sa 2015/16 ho hodisa ditshebeletso tsa bofokisi, sepolesa se bonahalang, mautlwela a botlokotsebe, ditshebeletso tsa forensiki, ho kenyeletswa ditshebeletso tsa le tshireletso le polokeho.

src: Cabinet calls on our youth to consider a career in the SAPS, which offers numerous opportunities.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho batjha ba rona ho nahana ka mosebetsi ka hara SAPS, e fanang ka menyetla e batlang e le mengata.

src: More information can be obtained on WEBTOKEThe annual Public Service Month will take place across the Public Service in September under the theme “Moving South Africa forward: Taking the Public Service to the people”.The month will highlight government services, dedication, commitment and excellence in public service delivery.
tgt: Tlhahisoleseding e batsi e ka fimanwa ho WEBTOKEKgwedi ya selemo ka seng ya Tshebeletso ya Mmuso e tla ketekwa ho phatlalla le Tshebeletso ya Mmuso ka Loetse tlasa mookotaba “Re ntshetsa Aforika Borwa pele: Re isa Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba bathong”.Kgwedi ena e tla pepesa ditshebeletso tsa mmuso, boikemisetso, boitelo le boqhetseke ka hara phano ya ditshebeletso tsa setjhaba.

src: Feedback will be provided on progress made following the 2014 public service-wide consultative meetings and engagements with frontline public servants on “reinventing the way public servants work”.
tgt: Diphetho di tla fanwa mabapi le kgatelopele e entsweng ho latela dikopano tsa dipuisano tse phatlaletseng le ditherisano tsa phano ya ditshebeletso tsa 2014 ka basebeletsi ba ka sehloohong ba mmuso mabapi le ho “sibolla botjha tsela eo tshebeletso ya mmuso e sebetsang kateng”.

src: An efficient public service is a key requirement to deliver on the NDP and Cabinet calls on public servants to recommit to the Batho Pele principles by delivering high quality, cost-effective and efficient services to all South Africans.
tgt: Tshebeletso ya setjhaba e hlwahlwa ke tlhokeho ya bohlokwa bakeng sa ho nehela ho NDP mme Kabinete e ipiletsa ho basebeletsi ba setjhaba ho itlama botjha ho dipehelo tsa Batho Pele ka ho fana ka ditshebeletso tsa maemo a hodimo, tse bolokang ditjeho le ho ba hlwahlwa ho maAforika Borwa oohle.

src: Cabinet was briefed on progress made for hosting the XIV World Forestry Congress of the Food and Agriculture Organisation to be held from 7 to 11 September 2015 in the Inkosi Albert Luthuli Convention Centre, KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Kabinete e tsebisitswe ka kgatelopele e entsweng bakeng sa ho tshwara ha Seboka sa bo- XIV sa Meru sa Lefatshe sa Mokgatlo wa Dijo le Temo se tla tshwarwa ho tloha ka la 7 ho isa la 11 Loetse 2015 Setsing sa Dikopano sa Inkosi Albert Luthuli, KwaZulu-Natal.

src: The theme “Forests and People: Investing in a Sustainable Future” reflects people-centered forestry, forestry’s role in socio-economic development, needs and opportunities for investments, and the role of forests in economic development.
tgt: Mookotaba “Meru le Batho: Ho tsetela ho Bokamoso ba Moshwelella” o bontsha tsa meru tse tobileng batho, mosebetsi wa meru ho ntshetsopele ya moruo wa kahisano, ditlhoko le menyetla bakeng sa matsete, le mosebetsi wa meru ho ntshetsopele ya moruo.

src: This relates directly to government’s priorities on poverty eradication, rural development and job creation.
tgt: Sena se amana ka kotloloho le merero e ka sehloohong ya mmuso mabapi le phediso ya bofuma, ntshetsopele ya dibaka tsa mahae le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi.

src: The congress will also focus on water scarcity and climate change.
tgt: Seboka hape se tla tsepamisa maikutlo ho kgaello ya metsi le phethoho ya tlelaemete.

src: This is the first World Forestry Congress to be held in Africa and provides an opportunity to profile the continent on the global forestry stage.
tgt: Sena ke Seboka sa pele sa Meru ya Lefatshe sa ho tshwarelwa Aforika le ho fana ka monyetla wa ho beha kontinente hantle lepatlelong la lefatshe la meru.

src: An outreach programme will inform the public, including vulnerable groups, about possible participation.
tgt: Lenaneo la phihlello le tla tsebisa setjhaba, ho kenyeletswa dihlopha tse hlokang menyetla, ka kgonahalo ya ho nka karolo.

src: The congress will follow National Arbor Week (1 to 7 September) under the theme “Here’s to a new Forest” and appeals to South Africans to plant just one tree today and help invest in a sustainable future.
tgt: Seboka se tla latela Beke ya Naha ya Tjalo ya Difate (1 ho isa 7 Loetse) tlasa mookotaba “Ha re thabeng bakeng sa moru o motjha” mme o ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ho jala sefate se le seng feela kajeno le ho thusa ho tsetela bokamosong ba moshwelella.

src: Congratulatory message.
tgt: Melaetsa ya ditakaletso tse molemo.

src: Cabinet wishes success to the country’s athletes competing in the 15th World Championships in Athletics currently taking place in Beijing, China and those participating in the 11th All-Africa Games between 4 and 19 September 2015 in Brazzaville, Congo.
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa baatlelete ba naha katleho ba tla beng ba phehisana ho Bompodi ba Lefatshe ba Diatleletiki ba bo-15 bo tswelang pele hajwale Beijing, ho la China le ba nkang karolo ho Dipapadi tsa bo-11 tsa All-Africa mahareng a la 4 le 19 Loetse 2015 Brazzaville, ho la Congo.

src: Cabinet calls on South Africans to unite behind our athletes as they fly our flag high and make the nation proud.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa kaofela ho ipopa ho tshehetsa baatlelete ba rona ha ba fofisetsa folakga ya rona hodimo le ho etsa setjhaba motlotlo.

src: Cabinet joins President Zuma in congratulating the SABC journalists Dennis Tshetlhane and Sam Msibi for winning the Television Category of the SADC Media Awards, and high-school learner Imbelani Matibe for winning the SADC Essay School Category Competition.
tgt: Kabinete e ipapisa le Moporesidente Zuma bakeng sa ho thoholetsa boraditaba ba SABC Dennis Tshetlhane le Sam Msibi bakeng sa ho hapa Mokgahlelo wa Thelevishene wa Dikgau tsa SADC tsa Boraditaba, le moithuti wa sekolo se phahameng Imbelani Matibe bakeng sa ho hlola Phehisanong ya Mokgahlelo wa Moqoqo wa Dikolo ya SADKabinete e leboha maAforika Borwa kaofela a ileng a kenela mekete ya Kgwedi ya Basadi.

src: Cabinet thanks all the South Africans that joined in the celebrations of the Women’s Month.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse neng di tshwerwe ke mekgatlo e fapafapaneng le mmuso tse neng di keteka katleho eo re e entseng mabapi le ho sebetsana le ho se lekalekane ho tsa bong ka hara setjhaba sa rona.

src: The events that were held by various organisations and government which celebrated the success we have made in addressing the gender disparities in our society.
tgt: Kgwedi ena e sebedisitswe ho lekola diphephetso tseo re ntseng re shebane le tsona mabapi le tlhekefetso ya basadi le bana.

src: Cabinet wishes Health Minister Aaron Motsoaledi, who was admitted over the weekend to the Steve Biko Academic Hospital in Pretoria, a speedy recovery.
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa pholo e potlakileng ya Letona la Bophelo bo Botle Aaron Motsoaledi, ya neng a amohetswe mafelong a beke Sepetlele sa Thuto sa Steve Biko Pretoria.

src: He has since been discharged and is recuperating at home.
tgt: O se a bile a lokolotswe mme o ntse a folla lapeng.

src: AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: DithonyoDithonyo kaofela di tla lokela ke ho netefatswa ha mangolo a thuto le tumello e amehang.

src: Implementation of key government programmes.
tgt: Ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha mananeo a bohlokwa a mmuso.

src: Cabinet reiterates President Jacob Zuma’s call for all sectors of society to work together to support the economy and save jobs in the current tough economic environment.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa kgoeletso ya Moporesidente Jacob Zuma ho makala kaofela a setjhaba ya ho sebetsa mmoho bakeng sa ho tshehetsa moruo le ho baballa mesebetsi tikolohong ya hajwale ya maemo a boima a moruo.

src: The pact between government, mining houses and labour unions demonstrates the commitment across all sectors to save jobs and reduce the impact of job losses.
tgt: Tumellano pakeng tsa mmuso,beng ba merafo le mekgatlo ya basebetsi e bontsha boitlamo ho phatlalla le makala oohle ba ho baballa mesebetsi le ho fokotsa kgahlamelo ya tahlehelo ya mesebetsi.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to rally behind the implementation of the agreement.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa oohle ho ema nokeng ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha tumellano ena.

src: The pact serves as a blueprint for all sectors that face hurdles to save jobs.2 Cabinet received the Quarterly Outcomes Reports for the period 1 April to 30 June 2015.
tgt: Tumellano e sebetsa jwaloka moralo ho makala oohle a tobaneng le ditshitiso bakeng sa ho baballa mesebetsi.

src: This schedule will be communicated at a later stage.3 Cabinet received a briefing on the G20 meeting held in Ankara, Turkey from 3 to 5 September 2015.
tgt: Kabinete e thotse Ditlaleho tsa Kotara ka nngwe tsa Diphetho bakeng sa nako ya la 1 Mmesa ho isa ka la 30 Phuptjane 2015.Kabinete e thabiswa ke kgatelopele e entsweng mme e lemohile le dibaka tse hlokang boitshunyako.

src: The meeting was attended by the Ministers of Finance and Labour and the Governor of the South African Reserve Bank.
tgt: Lefapha la Tsamaiso ya Dikgokahanyo le Tlhahisoleseding ya Mmuso (GCIS) le tla hokahanya dikopano le boraditaba bakeng sa ho arolelana tlhahisoleseding mabapi le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha mananeo a mmuso.

src: The G20 also welcomed the positive outcome of the Addis Ababa Conference on Financing for Development in which South Africa played a critical role as chair of the G77 plus China.5 Cabinet welcomes the inauguration and electricity switch-on of the Kouga Wind Farm in the Eastern Cape on 4 September 2015.The Kouga Wind Farm will provide about 300 gigawatt-hours of clean electricity annually.
tgt: Kabinete e fumane tsebiso ka kopano ya G20 e neng e tshwaretswe Ankara, ho la Turkey ho tloha ka la 3 ho isa la 5 Loetse 2015.

src: Earlier this year, the Department of Energy expanded opportunities for the private sector to contribute to the production of power by approving 13 new renewable Independent Power Producers that will add 5 243 megawatts to the national grid.6 Cabinet has noted the migration developments in Europe which highlight the complexity of the migration management and its relationship with foreign policies of the respective countries.
tgt: Kopano ya Matona a Ditjhelete le Balaodi ba Dibanka tsa Resefe e ne e tsepamisitse maikutlo hodima, hara tse ding, moruo wa lefatshe moralo bakeng sa kgolo ya moshwelella le e lekalekanang matsete le meralo ya motheo dintlha tsa matjhaba tsa lekgetho, tshehetso ka ditjhelete bakeng sa ntshetsopele, le ho fetofetoha ha tlelaemete.

src: Cabinet has expressed deep concern about some political parties which have launched an attack on the MDB that seeks to undermine its independence and legitimacy in the eyes of the public.
tgt: G20 hape e ananetse sephetho se kgabane sa Khonferense ya Addis Ababa ya tshethetso ya Ditjhelete bakeng sa Ntshetsopele moo Aforika Borwa e bapetseng karolo e hlokolosi jwaloka modulasetulo wa G77 le China.

src: There are other avenues provided in law to challenge the decisions of the MDB.8 The Employment Equity (EE) reporting season opened on 1 September 2015 for both manual and online reporting, which closes on 1 October 2015 (manual) and 15 January 2016 (online) respectively.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho thakgolwa le ho hotetswa ha motlakase ha Polasi ya Motlakase o Fehlwang ka Moya ya Kouga Kapa Botjhabela ka la 4 Loetse 2015.Polasi ya Motlakase ya Kouga e tla fana ka ho ka etsang dihora tse 300 tsa dikikawate tsa motlakase o hlwekileng selemo ka seng.

src: Cabinet approved the recommendation by the Minister of Transport to provide urgent lease agreement to the Tag Yachts (PTY) Ltd .
tgt: Kabinete e babatsa mosebetsi wa Boto ya Tsheho ya Meedi ya Bomasepala (MDB) eo haufinyane e phethetseng ho tiisetswa le ho tiisetswa botjha ha meedi e batlang e ba ka thoko ya bomasepala ka hara diporofense tse robedi ho phatlalla le naha.

src: Its objective is to initiate manufacturing of high end composite catamarans in the Port Elizabeth Habour.
tgt: MDB e e ntse mosebetsi wa yona ho ya ka thomo ya molao le ho sebedisa dipehelo tse ka hara matla a yona tsa ho etsa diqeto tsa ho qetela.

src: This is to effect the assigned responsibility for the marine manufacturing Delivery Unit under the Operation Phakisa initiatives to establish a composite Boat-Building Cluster in the Eastern Cape.
tgt: Kabinete e hlahisitse ngongoreho e tebileng mabapi le mekga e meng ya dipolotiki e thakgotseng tlhaselo ho MDB e batlang ho nyenyefatsa boikemelo le matla a yona a semolao mahlong a setjhaba.

src: The charter is a policy framework for the development of statistics in Africa, which sets out the professional principles governing the production and management of statistics at national, regional and continental levels.
tgt: Lefapha la Mesebetsi le hlophisa matsholo a dipontsho tsa ho haola le naha tlasa mookotaba: “Phethoho – e etsa kelello kgwebong” ho matlafatsa ho kenngwa tshebetsong le ho netefatsa boimatahanyo.

src: Cabinet approved that the Department of Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation (DPME) takes forward the Twende Mbele Programme in order to invest in collaboration around monitoring and evaluation across Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka Tlaleho ya ho Qetela ya Dipheo tsa Ntshetsopele tsa Dilemokete (di-MDG) bakeng sa Aforika Borwa.

src: The Twende Mbele Programme will assist South Africa to build on and formalise existing informal partnerships, which may include bilateral agreements.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana moralo wa tlaleho ya ho qetela mabapi le MDG e tla hlahiswa ho Lekgotla la Matjhaba a Kopaneng hamorao selemong sena.

src: This supports the struggle for a better life in South Africa, which is linked with the pursuit of a better Africa in a better world.
tgt: Ho ya ka tlaleho, kamora dilemo tse 20 tsa ntshetsopele, kgatelopele ya bohlokwa e se e entswe bakeng sa phano ya ditshebeletso tsa bohlokwa ka hara naha le ho fokotsa maemo a mabe a bofuma.

src: The amendments, which are from the Land Tenure Security and Evictions Policies in Commercial Framing Areas, aim to find a solution to tenure insecurities by combining land redistribution measures within effective legal protection and dispute-resolution mechanisms.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana kgothaletso ya Letona la Dipalangwang ya ho fana ka tumellano e potlakileng ya kgiriso ho Tag Yachts (PTY) Ltd. Sepheo sa yona ke ho qala ho hlahisa diketswana tsa maemo a hodimo Boemakepeng ba Port Elizabeth.
