tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa Amajimbos tse molemo jwaloka ha ba le phehisanong ya Mohope wa Lefatshe wa FIFA wa U-17 FIFA Chile ho tloha ka la 17 Mphalane ho isa ka la 8 Pudungwana 2015.Kabinete e thoholetsa Orlando Pirates bakeng sa ho fihlella makgaolakgang a Mohope wa 2015 Orange CAF Confederation le Banyana Banyana bakeng sa ho atleha ho kenela Dipapadi tsa Diolimpiki tsa 20.6 Kabinete hape e fetisetsa matshediso ho lelapa le metswalle ya CEO ya mehleng ya Komiti ya Lehae ya Ditlhophiso ya Mohope wa Dinaha tsa Aforika (Afcon) wa 2013 le Bompodi ba Dinaha tsa Aforika (Chan) hape e ne e le Mohlanka wa Phethahatso wa SABC‚ Mvuzo Mbebe ya hlokahetseng bosiung ba Mantaha.7 Kabinete e utlwisitswe bohloko haholo ka ho hlokahala ha Mlungisi Sisulu, mora wa bobedi wa Walter le Albertina Sisulu, mme e fetisetsa matshediso a yona ho lelapa le metswalle.

src: Cabinet joins President Jacob Zuma in conveying condolences to the family and friends of one of South Africa’s finest actors, Sammy Moeti who passed away on Monday, 13 October 2015, after a long illness.8 Cabinet discussed extensively the recent student protests against university fee increases for 2016 academic year.
tgt: Monghadi Sisulu o bapetse karolo e matla makaleng a ANC a bokgukguni dilemong tsa bo 1980, a patile diyuniti tsa Umkhonto weSizwe lebenkeleng la hae le lenyenyane la Soweto‚ le neng le tsejwa e le Shop 7‚ a behile bophelo ba hae kotsing e kgolo.

src: Cabinet sympathizes with the concerns of the students who find the cost for higher education too expensive and inaccessible to the students coming from poor families.
tgt: Kabinete e ipapisa le dingongoreho tsa baithuti ba bonang ditjeho tsa thuto e phahameng di bitsa ho feta tekano le ho se kgone ho fihlellwa ke baithuti ba tswang malapeng a futsanehileng.

src: Education is one of the core elements to reduce the current challenges of poverty, inequalities and unemployment the country is facing.
tgt: Thuto ke e nngwe ya dintlha tsa bohlokwa bakeng sa ho fokotsa diphephetso tsa hajwale tsa bofutsana, ho se lekalekane le tlhokeho ya mosebetsi tseo naha e tobaneng le tsona.

src: Our Constitution provides that everyone has the right to basic education and further education, which the State through reasonable measures must make available and accessible.
tgt: Molaotheo wa rona o fana ka taba ya hore mang le mang o na le tokelo ya thuto ya motheo le thuto e tswelang pele, eo Puso ka mekgwa e utlwahalang e lokelang ho etsa hore e be teng le ho tholahala.

src: The current government has since 1994, made access to education a priority focus area.
tgt: Mmuso wa hajwale esale ho tloha ka 1994, o entse hore phumantsho ya thuto e be ntlha e ka sehloohong.

src: The National Student Fund Aid Scheme (NSFAS) which has contributed to the needy students has increased over the years from R300m to R9, 5bn.
tgt: Sekema sa Naha sa Dithuso tsa Letlole la Baithuti (NSFAS) se nyehetseng ho baithuti ba hlokang se phahame ka ho ya le dilemo ho tloha ho R300 milione ho ya ho R9,5 bilione.

src: In this academic year, government is supporting 45 000 poor and academically deserving students.
tgt: Selemong sena sa dithuto, mmuso o tshehetsa baithuti ba 45 000 ba futsanehileng le ba tshwanelwang ke tshehetso.

src: Cabinet was briefed by the Minister of Higher Education and training on the current interaction he is having with all the relevant stakeholders to find a solution to the fees increases.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ke Letona la Thuto e Phahameng ka dipuisano tseo a keneng ho tsona hajwale le bankakarolo bohle ba amehang ho fumana tharollo ya ho nyollwa ha ditefello.

src: Cabinet was also appraised on the work that is been done towards improving the management of NSFAThe recommendations are to be tabled to Cabinet in its next cycle.
tgt: Kabinete hape e ile ya behwa sehlohlolong ka mosebetsi o ntseng o etswa bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa botsamaisi ba NSFADikgothaletso di lebeletswe ho tekelwa Kabinete kopanong ya yona e latelang.

src: Cabinet further noted the recently established Presidential Task Team which has been mandated to look into the escalating university fees.
tgt: Kabinete e boetse e lemohile ka Moifo wa Tshebetso wa Boporesidente o sa tswa thehwa haufinyana o romilweng ho shebana le ditefello tsa diyunivesithi tse ntseng di phahama.

src: This team comprises of representatives of students, University Councils and the Department.
tgt: Moifo ona o bopilwe ka baemedi ba baithuti, Makgotla a Diyunivesithi le Lefapha.

src: The team is expected to finalize its work and report as soon as it has concluded its task.
tgt: Moifo o lebeletswe ho phethela mosebetsi wa yona le ho tlaleha hang feela ha e phethetse mosebetsi wa yona.

src: Cabinet believes that the efforts led by both the President and Minister of Higher Education have and will go a long way in addressing the concerns of students.
tgt: Kabinete e dumela hore mekutu e etellwang pele ka bobedi ke Moporesidente le Letona la Thuto e Phahameng e tla tswela pele ho sebetsana le dingongoreho tsa baithuti.

src: The seriousness with which the government looks at the grievance of the students, has led the President to call the leaderships of the students and university today so as to get to the depth of the issues with a view to finding a solution.
tgt: Bohlokolosi boo mmuso o shebang ditletlebo tsa baithuti ka bona, bo entse hore Moporesidente a bitse diketapele tsa baithuti le diyunivesithi kajeno hore ho fihlwe botebong ba dintlha ka morero wa ho fumana tharollo.

src: The President will brief the nation later as this matter is of national importance.
tgt: Moporesidente o tla tsebisa setjhaba ha mmamorao kaha taba ena e le ya bohlokwa setjhabeng.9 Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka kgatelopele e mabapi le Komiti ya ka hare ya Matona (IMC) ya Melawana ya Bofalli e neng e eteletswe pele ke Motlatsi wa Moporesidente.

src: Cabinet was briefed on the progress on the Inter- ministerial committee on Immigration Regulations which was led by the Deputy President.
tgt: Moporesidente o thehile IMC ena ka morero wa ho batlisisa ditlamorao tse neng di sa lebellwa tse ileng tsa hlahiswa ke bankakarolo ba lekaleng la bohahlaudi.

src: Having investigated and explored areas that can be adjusted to deal with both the security consideration and the unintended consequences the IMC made the following recommendations.
tgt: Kamora ho etsa dipatlisiso le ho sekaseka dintlha tse lokiswang ho sebetsana le bobedi dintlha tsa polokeho le ditlamorao tse neng di sa lebellwa IMC e entse dikgothaletso tse latelang:Ho etsa kopo ka bowena:Ditumello tse tla qala ho sebetsa nakong ya dikgwedi tse 3 tse tlang.

src: Countries where no South African missions exist, the Department of Home Affairs (DHA) will accept applications sent by post.
tgt: Dinaha moo ho se nang dikantoro tsa Aforika Borwa, Lefapha la Merero ya Lehae (DHA) le tla amohela dikopo tse rometsweng ka poso.

src: Thereafter, the biometrics and photos of those travellers will be captured on arrival at ports of entry.
tgt: Kamora moo, dintlha tsa motho le dinepe tsa batsamai bao di tla nkuwa ha ba fihla madibohong.

src: This concession will only be applicable to visitors/medical Visa.
tgt: Tumello ena e tla sebetsa feela ho di-visa tsa baeti/ba tlileng ka mabaka a kalafo.

src: The DHA will implement the biometrics (including fingerprints and photos) at ports of entry starting.
tgt: DHA e tla kenya tshebetsong dintlha tsa motho (ho kenyeletswa dikgatiso tsa menwana le dinepe) madibohong.

src: The pilot sites will be at OR Tambo Airport King Shaka Airport and Cape Town International Airport.
tgt: Dibaka tsa diteko e tla ba Boemafofane ba OR Tambo Boemafofane ba King Shaka le Boemafofane ba Matjhaba ba Motse Kapa.

src: DHA will introduce an Accredited Tourism Company (ATC) Programme for China, India and Russia with possible extension to other visa requiring countries.
tgt: DHA e tla hlahisa Lenaneo la Khamphani ya Bohahlaudi le Ngodisitsweng (ATC) bakeng sa China, India le Russia ka kgonahalo ya ho atolosetswa dinaheng tse ding tse batlang di-visa.

src: DHA will continue to issue a long-term Multiple Entry Visa to frequent travellers.
tgt: DHA e tla tswela pele ho ntsha Di-visa tsa ho kena hangata tsa nako e telele ho batsamai ba kamehla.

src: This will be valid for a period exceeding 3 months but not exceeding 3 years.
tgt: Sena se tla sebetsa bakeng sa nako e fetang dikgwedi tse 3 empa e sa feteng dilemo tse 3.Ditumello tse tla qala ho sebetsa nakong ya dilemo tse 3 ho ya ho selemo se le seng.

src: DHA will increase Visa Facilitation Centres (VHC) in China, India, United Kingdom, Nigeria Democratic Republic of Congo, Angola, Ghana, Kenya and Uganda.
tgt: DHA e tla eketsa Ditsi tsa Phano ya Di-visa (VHC) China, India, United Kingdom, Nigeria, Riphaboliki ya Demokerasi ya Congo, Angola, Ghana, Kenya le Uganda.

src: The DHA will fast-track the opening of VFC in Zimbabwe, UAE and Botswana.
tgt: DHA e tla potlakisa ho bulwa ha VFC Zimbabwe, UAE le Botswana.

src: Concessions that will be effected beyond one year.
tgt: Ditumello tse tla qala ho sebetsa nako ya ho ho feta selemo.

src: The DHA will install systems for pre-flight checks (including operation-centres) at international airports.
tgt: DHA e tla kenya mekgwa ya ho lekola batsamai pele ba fofa (ho kenyeletswa le ditsi tsa tshebetso) maemafofaneng a matjhaba.

src: The DHA will upgrade Advance Passenger Processing (APP) systems and implement a Passenger Name Record (PNR) to enhance risk assessment.
tgt: DHA e tla ntlafatsa mekgwa ya Ho sebetsana le Bapalami pele ba Palama (APP) le ho kenya tshebetsong Rekoto ya Mabitso a Bapalami (PNR) ho ntlafatsa tekolo ya dikotsi.

src: The DHA will finalise the automation of the visa and permitting system.
tgt: DHA e tla phethela tsamaiso ya ho sebedisa metjhini e itshebetsang bakeng sa ho ntsha di-visa le diphomete.

src: Child-travel requirements: South African WEBTOKEN respect of South African children (outbound travel) the IMC accepted the implementation of the current child-travel requirements, including the parental consent affidavits as these seek to protect children.
tgt: Ditlhoko tsa ho eta le bana: Bana ba Aforika Borwa:Bakeng sa bana ba Aforika Borwa ba etang (ba etelang ka ntle) IMC e amohetse ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha ditlhoko tsa ho eta ha bana tsa hajwale, ho kenyeletswa diafidaviti tsa tumello ya batswadi kaha tsena di batleha bakeng sa ho tshireletsa bana.

src: Concessions to be effective within the next 3 WEBTOKEN principals will issue letters confirming the permission for children to travel on school tours.
tgt: Ditumello tse tla qala ho sebetsa nakong ya dikgwedi tse 3 tse tlang.

src: This authority will also be extended to include registered sports bodies.
tgt: Dihlooho tsa dikolo di tla ntsha mangolo a tiisetsang tumello ya hore bana ba tsamaye ka maeto a sekolo.

src: The validity of the Parental Consent Affidavit will be extended to a period no longer than 6 months.
tgt: Ho sebetsa ha Afidaviti ya Tumello ya Batswadi e tla atoloswa bakeng sa nako e sa feteng dikgwedi tse 6.Ditumello tse tla qala ho sebetsa nakong ya dikgwedi tse 3 tse tlang ho isa selemong.

src: The term “Unabridged Birth Certificate” will be changed to “Birth Certificate containing parental details”Details of parents will be printed in passports, so that parents whose particulars are printed would therefore not be required to carry birth certificates.
tgt: Mantswe “Lengolo la Tswalo le sa Kgutsufatswang” le tla fetolelwa ho ba “Lengolo la tswalo le nang le dintlha tsa batswadi.”Dintlha tsa batswadi di tla hatiswa diphasepotong, hore batswadi bao dintlha tsa bona di hatisitsweng diphasepotong ba se tlamehe ho tsamaya ba jere mangolo a tswalo.

src: Child-travel requirements: foreign WEBTOKEN respect of inbound travellers, the IMC took the position that where visas are required, provision of original birth certificates or certified copies of required documents should continue during the visa application process as this is in line with practise in many other WEBTOKEN respect of children from visa-exempt countries, the IMC recommended a dispensation in terms of which:Travellers will be strongly advised to bring along proof of the relation and consent from the absent parent/s or guardian/sAll the other administrative issues affecting the relevant departments will be resolved through inter-departmental engagements.
tgt: Bakeng sa batsamai ba ka hara naha, IMC e nkile boemo ba hore moo di-visa di batlehang, phano ya mangolo a tswalo a mantlha kapa dikhopi tsa ditokomane tse batlehang di tla tswela pele ho sebetsa nakong ya ho etsa kopo ya visa kaha sena se tsamaelana le ditshebetso dinaheng tse ding tse ngata.

src: Cabinet endorsed these recommendations and believes these will address the unintended consequences that were raised and also the safety of the children will not in any way be compromised.
tgt: Bakeng sa bana ba tswang dinaheng tse kotetsweng bakeng sa di-visa, IMC e kgothaleditse tsamaiso eo ka yona:Batsamai ba tla eletswang ka matla hore ba tle le bopaki ba dikamano le tumello ho tswa ho mo/batswadi/mo/bahlokomedi ba sa tsamayeng le bana.

src: Implementation of key government programmes.
tgt: Ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha mananeo a bohlokwa a mmuso.

src: Cabinet welcomes the R20-million Enterprise Development pilot project.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela porojeke ya diteko ya Ntshetsopele ya Dikgwebo ya R20 milione.

src: This two-year pilot programme aims to revitalise South Africa’s industrial parks, establish specialised industrialised facilities and support the integration of local economic development in order to bolster the small business sector.
tgt: Lenaneo lena la diteko la dilemo tse pedi le rerile ho ntjhafatsa dibaka tsa diindaseteri tsa Aforika Borwa, ho theha dibaka tse ikgethang tsa diindaseteri le ho tshehetsa kopanelo ya ntshetsopele ya moruo wa lehae bakeng sa ho matlafatsa lekala la dikgwebo tse nyenyane.

src: The project is a partnership with departments of trade and industry, small business development, National Treasury, and the Middle Income Grant of the African Development Bank.
tgt: Porojeke ena ke semphato le Lefapha la Kgwebisano le Indaseteri, Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Dikgwebo tse Nyenyane, Lefapha la Matlotlo a Naha, le Thuso ya Ditjhelete ya ba Fumanang Lekeno le Mahareng ya Banka ya Ntshetsopele ya Aforika.

src: The project envisages to contribute towards job creation, reduce poverty in depressed communities, and improve access to technology and skills for small, medium and micro enterprises (SMMEs).The initiative will offer support to the SMME sector until December 2017.
tgt: Porojeke e lakatsa ho nyehela ho tlhahiso ya mesebetsi, ho fokotsa bofuma ho badudi ba hatellehileng, le ho ntlafatsa phumantsho ya thekenoloji le boitsebelo bakeng sa dikgwebo tse nyenyane, tse mahareng le tse kgolwanyane (di-SMME).Boikitlaetso bona bo tla fana ka tshehetso lekaleng la SMME ho fihlela ka Tshitwe 2017.

src: Based on its successes, government will consider rolling it out across the country.
tgt: Ho itshetlehilwe hodima dikatleho tsa bona, mmuso o tla lohotha ho fana ka bona naheng ka bophara.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch by President Jacob Zuma of the Joint Operation Centre in Skukuza.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho thakgolwa ha Setsi se Kopanetsweng sa Tshebetso ke Moporesidente Jacob Zuma ho la Skukuza.

src: This centre will coordinate operations against the scourge of rhino poaching in that area.
tgt: Setsi sena se tla hokahanya ditshebetso kgahlanong le bothata ba ho tsoma ditshukudu ntle le molao tulong eo.

src: Key Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved the Black Industrialists Policy, which is part of the Industrial Policy Action Plan (IPAP).
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Leano la Boradiindaseteri ba Batho ba Batsho, e leng karolo ya Moralo wa Leano la Tshebetso la Diindaseteri (IPAP).

src: This policy is in line with the National Development Plan and the Nine-Point Plan announced by President Zuma in the 2015 State of the Nation Address.
tgt: Leano lena le kgema le Lewa la Naha la Ntshetsopele le Moralo wa Dintlha tse Robong o tsebisitsweng ke Moporesidente Zuma ha a ne a tshetleha Puo ka Maemo a Naha ya 2015.Hape ke karolo ya boikitlaetso ba mmuso bo pharaletseng ba ho thehwa ha diindaseteri bakeng sa ho atolosa motheo wa diindaseteri le ho kenya ho fetofetoha ho hotjha ha boetapele ba dikgwebo moruong.

src: It is also part of government’s broad industrialization initiatives to expand the industrial base and inject new entrepreneurial dynamism in the economy.
tgt: Sena se hloka boitshunyako bo batlang bo tletse sebete lehlakoreng la mmuso le ho hodisa moruo ka tshehetso e nang le boitelo ho boradiindaseteri ba batho ba batsho jwaloka ha ho hlakisitswe ho IPAP.

src: It calls for bolder policy interventions on the part of the State to expand the industrial base of the country and grow the economy through dedicated support to black industrialists as highlighted in the IPAP.
tgt: Leano lena le tla tsepamisa maikutlo hodima kgolo le bophehisani ba lefatshe ba dikgwebo tseo e leng tsa batho ba batsho.

src: This policy will focus on the growth and global competitiveness of black-owned enterprises.
tgt: Sepheo ke ho nyehela ho phethoho ya maemo le dikateng tsa setjhaba tsa lekala la diindaseteri la Aforika Borwa le ho kenyeletsa boradiindaseteri ba batho ba batsho, ba nkuwang e le mohlodi o sa sebedisweng ka toka wa mesebetsi, lekeno, makgetho le ntlafatso.

src: The intention is to contribute towards shifting the demographic composition of South Africa’s industrial sector and engage black industrialists, who are regarded as the underused sources of jobs, revenue, taxes and innovation.
tgt: Leano le tla thusa ka bonkakarolo bo hlwahlwa ba dikhamphani tseo e leng tsa batho ba batsho le ho laolwa ke bona lethathameng la dikgwebo tsa boleng lekaleng la diindaseteri tsa moruo wa naha.

src: The Minister of Trade and Industry will hold a separate media briefing to unpack this policy.
tgt: Letona la Dikgwebo le Diindaseteri le tla tshwara kopano e ka thoko le boraditaba ho manolla leano lena.

src: Cabinet approved South Africa’s Third National Report on the Implementation of the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety, for submission to the Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Tlaleho ya Naha ya Aforika Borwa ya Boraro mabapi le ho Kenngwa Tshebetsong ha Porothokhole ya Cartagena ya Paballo ya tsa Tlhaho, bakeng sa ho fuwa Bongodi ba Khonvenshene ya Diphapano tsa Tlhaho.

src: The protocol governs the movements of Living Modified Organisms, also known as Genetically Modified Organisms resulting from modern biotechnology, from one country to another.
tgt: Porothokhole ke yona e laolang metsamao ya Diphedi tse Lokisitsweng, e tsejwang hape jwaloka Diphedi tse Lokisitsweng ka Dijeni tse hlahiswang ke thekenoloji ya sejwalejwale ya tsa tlhaho,ho tloha naheng e nngwe ho ya ho e nngwe.

src: South Africa is the ninth largest producer of genetically modified crops in the world and remains the pioneer for the adoption of genetically modified crops.
tgt: Aforika Borwa ke mohlahisi e moholo ka ho fetisisa wa borobong wa dimela tse lokisitsweng ka dijeni lefatsheng le ho dula e le moetapele bakeng sa ho amohelwa ha dimela tse lokisitsweng ka dijeni.

src: This is aligned to Section 24 of the Constitution, which advocates for sustainable use of biodiversity.
tgt: Sena se matahantswe le Karolo 24 ya Molaotheo, e kgothaletsang tshebediso ya moshwelella ya tswakatswakano ya tsa tlhaho.

src: Cabinet approved South Africa’s initial services offer in terms of the decision of the 9th World Trade Organization’s (WTO) Ministerial Conference to grant preferential treatment to Least Developed Countries (LDCs).South Africa is committed to implement the WTO agreement, which provides preferential support to the LDCs.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana boikemisetso ba Aforika Borwa ba ho nehelana ka ditshebeletso tsa qalo ho ya ka qeto ya Seboka sa Matona sa borobong sa Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Kgwebo (WTO) ho fana ka tshwaro e tlang pele ho Dinaha tseo Ntshetsopele ya tsona e leng e Tlase (di-LDC).Aforika Borwa e entse boitlamo ba ho kenya tshebetsong tumellano ya WTO, e fanang ka tshehetso e tlang pele ho di-LDHara dinaha tse 34 tse nkuwang e le di- LDC, tse 25 ke tsa Aforika.

src: Of the 34 countries classified as LDCs, 25 are from Africa.
tgt: Boikemisetso ba qalo ba Aforika Borwa e tla ba ho makala a ditshebeletso tsa ditjhelete, dikgokahanyo tsa mehala, bohahlaudi le dipalangwang.

src: South Africa’s initial offering will be in services in the financial services, telecommunications, tourism and transport sectors.
tgt: Nehelano e kang ena e etsa karolo ya ho bebofatsa ho kenella mebarakeng bakeng sa ditshebeletso le bafani ba ditshebeletso ka hara mebaraka eo e seng ya di-LDKabinete e tjhaelletse monwana moputso o lekotsweng botjha wa ho hlopha botjha tjhelete e phedisang ya 5.5% e lokelang ho lefuwa ditho tsa Khomishene ya Ditokelo tsa Botho ya Aforika Borwa (SAHRC) ho tloha ka la 1 Mmesa 2015.

src: This is in line with Section 9(1) of the SAHRC Act, 2013 (Act 40 of 2013).
tgt: Sena se imatahantse le Karolo 9(1) ya Molao wa SAHRC, wa 2013 (Molao 40 wa 2013).

src: Cabinet approved the submission of South Africa’s combined Second Periodic Report under the African Charter on Human and People’s Rights and the Initial Report under the Protocol to the African Charter on the Rights of Women in Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa ha Tlaleho ya Dinako tse itseng e Kopanetsweng ya Bobedi tlasa Tjhata ya Aforika e mabapi le Ditokelo tsa Batho le tsa Botho le Tlaleho ya Qalo tlasa Porothokhole ya Tjhata ya Aforika e mabapi le Ditokelo tsa Basadi ka hara Aforika.

src: The report to the African Union (AU) Commission is an evaluation of achievements and challenges in giving effect to civil, political, socio-economic and cultural rights.
tgt: Tlaleho e isitsweng ho Khomishene ya Kopano ya Aforika (AU) ke thlathlobo ya diphihlello le diphephetso tsa ho fana ka kgahlamelo ho ditokelo tsa badudi, sepolotiki, moruo wa kahisano le tsa botjhaba.

src: This is in line with South Africa being party to the AU Protocol to the African Charter on Human and People’s Rights on the Rights of Women in Africa.
tgt: Sena se kgema le ho ba karolo ha Aforika Borwa ho Porothokhole ya AU ho Tjhata ya Aforika e mabapi le Ditokelo tsa Botho le Batho hodima ditokelo tsa Basadi ka hara Aforika.

src: Cabinet approved the introduction of a Lesotho dispensation to commence from 1 February 2016.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho tsebiswa ha Tsamaiso ya Lesotho hore e qale ho tloha ka la 1 Tlhakola 2016.

src: This follows the special dispensation that was granted to Zimbabwe in 2010, which has subsequently been extended.
tgt: Sena se latela tsamaiso e ikgethang e ileng ya fuwa Zimbabwe ka 2010, eo kamora moo e ileng ya atoloswa.

src: This dispensation will assist in better management of the labour flow of Lesotho nationals who come to South Africa in violation of the current immigration mechanisms.
tgt: Tsamaiso ena e tla thusa ka taolo e betere ya motsamao wa basebetsi bao e leng baahi ba Lesotho ba tlang Aforika Borwa ba tlola melao ya mekgwa ya hajwale ya bofalli.

src: The Minister of Home Affairs will provide more details at a media briefing at a later stage.
tgt: Letona la Merero ya Lehae le tla fana ka dintlha tse batsi kopanong ya boraditaba hamorao.

src: The Minister of Finance briefed Cabinet on the implementation of the Taxation Laws Amendment Act of 2013 and 2014 to take effect 1 March 2016.
tgt: Letona la Ditjhelete le tsebisitse Kabinete ka ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Sehlomathiso sa Melao ya Lekgetho ya 2013 le 2014 se tla qala ho sebetsa ho tloha ka la 1 Tlhakubele 2016.

src: These reforms are aimed at harmonizing and simplifying the taxation of retirement contributions and benefits.
tgt: Dintlafatso tsena di reretswe ho lokisa le ho nolofatsa dinyehelo tsa lekgetho tsa ho beha meja fatshe le dikuno.

src: Extending the tax benefit to cover members’ provident funds will enable over one million workers to enjoy a higher take-home salary.
tgt: Katoloso ya kuno ya lekgetho bakeng sa ho tshireletsa matlole a ho beha meja fatshe e tla thusa basebetsi ba fetang milione ho ba le mokgolo o batlang o phahame oo ba o isang lapeng.

src: This will also prevent tax avoidance practices by higher-income earners to a maximum of per cent of remuneration or taxable income up to R350 000.The Minister also briefed Cabinet on the principle of annuitisation for all retirement funds, whereby those benefitting from the tax deduction also have to annuitise part of their savings at retirement.
tgt: Sena hape se tla thibela mekgwa ya ho iphapanya ho lefa lekgetho ha batho ba mekgolo e phahameng ho fihla ho 27.5% tsa mokgolo kapa lekeno le tshwanelwang ke lekgetho la ho fihla ho R350 000.Letona hape le tsebisitse Kabinete ka pehelo ya ho etsa hore matlole a ho beha meja fatshe a lefuwe nako e telele, moo ba kgolang molemo ho tswa phokoletsong ya lekgetho le bona ba tla lokela hore ba lefuwe nako e telele jwaloka karolo ya dipoloko tsa bona ha ba beha meja fatshe.

src: These reforms are being implemented after extensive consultations with all stakeholders within and outside the National Economic Development and Labour Council, with at least 33 meetings held with labour and industry since 2012.
tgt: Dintlafatso tsena di kenngwa tshebetsong kamora ditherisano tse tebileng le bankakarolo kaofela ka hare le ka ntle ho Lekgotla la Naha la Ntshetsopele ya Moruo le Mesebetsi, moo ho ileng ha tshwarwa dikopano tse bonyane 33 le basebetsi le boradiindaseteri ho tloha ka 2012.

src: The overwhelming majority of stakeholders have indicated their full support for proceeding with the reforms on 1 March Bills.
tgt: Bongata bo boholo ba bankakarolo bo bontshitse tshehetso ya bona e tletseng bakeng sa ho tswela pele ka dintlafatso ka la 1 Hlakubele Dibili.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Broadcasting Amendment Bill of 2015 to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa ha Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Kgaso sa 2015 Palamenteng.

src: The Bill amends the Broadcasting Act, 1999 (Act 4 of 1999) so as to develop and implement a stable corporate governance model that ensures long-term stability and sustainability of the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC).Government is committed to a strong, independent and relevant public broadcaster, which is accountable to the shareholder, the public and Parliament.
tgt: Bili e hlomathisa Molao wa Kgaso, 1999 (Molao 4 wa 1999) e le ho ntshetsapele le ho kenya tshebetsong mmotlolo o tsitsitseng wa taolo ya kgwebo o netefatsang botsitso ba nako e telele ba Lekgotla la Kgaso la Aforika Borwa (SABC).Mmuso o itlamme bakeng sa kgaso ya setjhaba e matla, e ikemetseng le ho ba le boimatahanyo, e ikarabellang ho radiabo, setjhaba le Palamente.

src: The ability to discharge its mandate is dependent on the optimal performance of the SABC Board in providing strategic direction to the public broadcaster.
tgt: Bokgoni ba ho phetha thomo ya ona ho itshetlehile hodima tshebetso e phethahetseng ya Boto ya SABC ka ho fana ka lewa la tshupiso ho kgaso ya setjhaba.

src: Cabinet approved for the Insurance Bill of 2015 to be introduced in Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana bakeng sa hore Bili ya Inshorense ya 2015 e hlahiswe ho Palamente.

src: The Bill provides a consolidated legal framework for the prudential supervision of the insurance sector that is consistent with international standards for insurance regulation.
tgt: Bili e fana ka moralo o matlafaditsweng wa semolao bakeng sa taolo e hlwahlwa ya lekala la inshorense e kgemang le maemo a matjhaba bakeng sa bolaodi ba inshorense.

src: The Bill enhances the current risk management, capital and governance requirements.
tgt: Bili e matlafatsa ditlhokeho tsa hajwale tsa taolo ya dikotsi, tjhelete le tlhatlhobo.

src: It replaces and consolidates substantial parts of the Long-term Insurance Act, 1998 (Act 52 of 1998) and the Short-term Insurance Act, 1998 (Act 53 of 1998) relating to prudential supervision.
tgt: E suthisa le ho matlafatsa dikarolo tsa bohlokwa tsa Molao wa Inshorense wa Nako e Telele, 1998 (Molao 52 wa 1998) le Molao wa Inshorense ya Nako e Kgutshwane, 1998 (Molao 53 wa 1998) o tsamaelanang le taolo e hlwahlwa.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the Draft African Exploration Mining and Finance Bill in the Government Gazette, for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho phatlalatswa ha Bili ya Moralo wa ho Kenella ho Merafo ya Aforika le Ditjhelete Koranteng ya Mmuso bakeng sa tshwaelo ya setjhaba.

src: The Bill establishes the African Exploration Mining and Finance Corporation through legislation.
tgt: Bili e theha Koporasi ya ho Kenella ho Merafo ya Aforika le Ditjhelete ka molao.

src: It also defines its mandate and strategic objectives.
tgt: Hape e hlalosa thomo ya yona le dipheo tsa lewa la yona.

src: It strengthens the governance and oversight of the entity.
tgt: E matlafatsa taolo le ho behwa leihlo ha setheo sena.

src: Cabinet approved the introduction of the Protected Disclosures Amendment Bill of 2015 in Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho hlahiswa ha Bili ya Dipepeso tse Tshireleditsweng tsa 2015 ho Palamente.

src: The Bill extends the application of the Protected Disclosures Act, 2000 (Act 26 of 2000) beyond the traditional employer and employee relationship.
tgt: Bili e atolosa ho sebetsa ha Molao wa Dipepeso tse Tshireleditsweng, 2000 (Molao 26 wa 2000) ho feta ka nqane ho dikamano tsa tlwaelo tsa mohiri le mosebeletsi.

src: The amendments regulate joint liability, introduce a duty to investigate disclosures, provide for immunity against civil and criminal liability in certain circumstances and criminalise intentional false disclosures.
tgt: Dihlomathiso di laola boikarabelo bo kopanetsweng, di hlahisa tokelo ya ho batlisisa dipepeso, di fana ka ho kotelwa kgahlanong le boikarabelo ba badudi le botlokotsebe mabakeng a itseng le ho etsa hore dipepeso tse etswang ka boomo e be tlolo ya molao.

src: The Bill contributes to government’s commitment to fight fraud and corruption by strengthening the protection of whistleblowers.
tgt: Bili e nyehela ho boitlamo ba mmuso ba ho lwantsha boqhekanyetsi le bobodu ka ho matlafatsa tshireletso ya dimpimpi.

src: Cabinet approved the introduction of the Administrative Adjudication of Road Traffic Offences Amendment Bill of 2015 in Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho hlahiswa ha Bili ya Tsamaiso ya Boahlodi ba Ditlolo tsa Molao tsa Sephethephethe sa Mebileng ya 2015 ho Palamente.

src: The Bill amends the Administrative Adjudication of Road Traffic Offences Act, 1998 (Act 46 of 1998).The Bill will assist the Road Traffic Infringement Agency and the issuing authorities to be financially stable, and it also introduces efficiencies in serving notices to infringers.
tgt: Bili e hlomathisa Molao wa Tsamaiso ya Boahlodi ba Ditlolo tsa Molao tsa Mebileng, 1998 (Molao 46 wa 1998).Bili e tla thusa Lekala la Ditlolo tsa Molao wa Sephethephethe sa Mebileng le ho etsa hore balaodi ba tsitse ho tsa ditjhelete, mme hape e hlahisa bohlwahlwa ba ho fana ka ditsebiso ho batlodi ba molao.

src: President Zuma will attend the G20 Summit on 15 and 16 November 2015 in Antalya, Turkey, where the focus will be on inclusive and robust growth through collective action.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang Moporesidente Zuma o tla kenela Seboka sa G20 ka la 15 le 16 Pudungwana 2015 Antalya, ho la Turkey, moo ho tla be ho tsepamisitswe maikutlo hodima kgolo e kenyeletsang le e matla ka tshebetso e kopanetsweng.

src: Leaders at the summit will discuss inclusiveness, implementation and investment to achieve strong, sustainable and balanced growth at a global level.
tgt: Baetapele sebokeng sena ba tla tshohla kenyeletso, ho kenngwa tshebetsong le matsete bakeng sa ho fihlella kgolo e matla, ya moshwelella le e tsitsitseng maemong a lefatshe.

src: President Zuma will undertake an Official Visit to Berlin, Germany on 10 November 2015, where he will be hosted by Chancellor Angela Merkel.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla nka Leeto la Semmuso la ho ya Berlin, ho la Jeremane ka la 10 Pudungwana 2015, moo a tla amohelwa ke Mokanseliri Angela Merkel.

src: The President will also pay a courtesy call to President Joachim Gauck.
tgt: Moporesidente hape o tla nka leeto la hlompho ho ya ho Moporesidente Joachim Gauck.

src: During the visit the two countries will reconfirm their commitment to further enhance bilateral and economic relations.
tgt: Nakong ya leeto lena dinaha ka bobedi di tla tiisetsa botjha boitlamo ba tsona ba ho tswella ho matlafatsa dikamano tsa bobedi bona le tsa kgolo.

src: President Zuma will receive Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte at the Union Buildings on 17 November 2015.Following this, Prime Minister Rutte will lead a business delegation to Johannesburg and Cape Town which will focus on agriculture, healthcare, transport, infrastructure, water and energy.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla amohela Tonakgolo ya Netherlands Mark Rutte Meahong ya Kopano ka la 17 Pudungwana WEBTOKEN tla latela sena, ke hore Tonakgolo Rutte o tla etella pele kemedi ya dikgwebo Johannesburg le Motse Kapa e tla tsepamisa maikutlo hodima Temo, tlhokomelo ya kalafo, dipalangwang, meralo ya motheo, metsi le eneji.

src: South Africa will host the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation Summit in Johannesburg on 4 and 5 December 2015.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tla tshwara Seboka sa Foramo ya Tshebedisano-mmoho ya China-Aforika ho la Johannesburg ka la 4 le 5 Tshitwe 2015.

src: The objectives of the summit are to profile the 5-10 Year Strategic Programme for Cooperation between South Africa and China (2015-2024) and to promote bilateral agreements between the two countries.
tgt: Dipheo tsa seboka ke ho hlophisa Lenaneo la Lewa la Tshebedisano-mmoho la Dilemo tse the 5-10 pakeng tsa Aforika Borwa le China (2015-2024) le ho hodisa ditumellano tsa bobedi bona pakeng tsa dinaha tsena tse pedi.

src: Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa will lead a high-level delegation on an Official Visit to the Islamic Republic of Iran from 7 to 9 November 2015, to further bilateral political and economic relations between the two countries.
tgt: Motlatsi wa Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa o tla etella pele kemedi ya maemo a hodimo Leetong la Semmuso la ho etela Riphaboliki ya Mamoseleme ya Iran ho tloha ka la 7 ho isa ka la 9 Pudungwana 2015, bakeng sa ho hodisetsa pele dikamano tsa bobedi bona tsa sepolotiki le moruo pakeng tsa dinaha tsena tse pedi.

src: President Zuma will on 6 November 2015 conduct a Siyahlola monitoring visit to Bushbuckridge in Mpumalanga, which will focus on water and sanitation.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma ka la 6 Pudungwana 2015 o tla hlophisa leeto la tlhatlhobo la Siyahlola Bushbuckridge ho la Mpumalanga, le tla tsepamisa maikutlo hodima metsi le tsamaiso ya dikgwerekgwere.

src: A total of 16 600 households are benefitting from Phase 1 of government’s water project in the area, which delivers water to 24 villages in the Bushbuckridge Local Municipality.
tgt: Palo e etsang malapa a 16 600 e kgola molemo ho tswa ho Mokgahlelo 1 wa porojeke ya metsi ya mmuso ka hara tulo ena, e fanang ka metsi metsaneng e 24 ka hara Masepala wa Lehae wa the Bushbuckridge.

src: Government remains committed to ensuring that all South Africans have access to basic services.
tgt: Mmuso o dula o itlamme ho netefatsa hore maAforika kaofela a fumantshwa ditshebeletso tsa motheo.

src: Between 2002 and 2014, the percentage of households that have access to water increased from 80 per cent to 86 per cent, while sanitation increased from 62 per cent to 80 per cent.
tgt: Mahareng a 2002 le 2014, diphesente tsa malapa a fumantshitsweng metsi di nyolohile ho tloha ho 80% ho ya ho 86%, ha tsamaiso ya dikgwerekgwere e nyolohile ho tloha ho 62% ho ya ho 80%.

src: President Zuma will attend the inauguration of the President-elect of the United Republic of Tanzania, His Excellency Mr John Pembe Magufuli, on 5 November Congratulatory message.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla kenela ho behwa setulong ha Moporesidente ya sa tswa kgethwa wa Riphaboliki e Kopaneng ya Tanzania, Mohlomphehi Monghadi John Pembe Magufuli, ka la 5 Pudungwana Molaetsa wa Ditakaletso tsa Mahlohonolo.

src: Cabinet congratulates the public servants who were nominated in the 3rd National Batho Pele Excellence Awards.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa basebeletsi ba setjhaba ba kgethilweng ho Dikgau tsa Boraro tsa Naha tsa Boqhetseke tsa Batho Pele.

src: The awards take place on 13 November 2015 at Emperor’s Palace, Gauteng under the theme: “Batho Pele – Putting People First”.
tgt: Mokete wa Dikgau o tshwarwa ka la 13 Pudungwana 2015 Emperor’s Palace, ho la Gauteng tlasa mookotaba: “Batho Pele – Re beha Batho Pele”.

src: They reward best practice, good performance and gauge citizens’ satisfaction towards government performance.
tgt: Di putsa tshebetso e kgabane ka ho fetisisa, tshebetso e ntle mme di metha kgotsofalo ya baahi ho tshebetso ya mmuso.

src: Cabinet congratulates the government and the people of both the Republic of Côte d’Ivoire and the United Republic of Tanzania for holding peaceful elections.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa mmuso le batho ka bobedi ba Riphaboliki ya Côte d’Ivoire le Riphaboliki e Kopaneng ya Tanzania ka ho tshwara dikgetho tse nang le kgotso.

src: The massive participation by the Ivoirians and Tanzanians in the general elections reflects their understanding of the importance of exercising their civic duty and fundamental rights.
tgt: Ho nka karolo ka bongata ha setjhaba sa Côte d’Ivoire le sa Tanzania dikgethong tsa kakaretso ho bontsha kutlwisiso ya bona ya bohlokwa ba ho etsa mosebetsi wa bona wa setjhaba le ho sebedisa ditokelo tsa bona tsa motheo.

src: It is an indication of the maturation of the democratization process on the continent.
tgt: Ke sesupo sa kgolo ya tsamaiso ya ho kenya demokerasi tshebetsong ka hara kontinente.

src: Cabinet congratulates the Springbok team for their performance in the International Rugby Board 2015 World Cup.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa sehlopha sa Springbok ka tshebetso ya sona ho Mohope wa Lefatshe wa Boto ya Matjhaba ya Rakbi wa 2015.

src: The team brought home the bronze medal.
tgt: Sehlopha se tlile lapeng le medale wa boronse.

src: Cabinet congratulates the South African swimming team for concluding the FINA/airweave Swimming World Cup in Doha, Qatar.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa sehlopha sa Aforika Borwa sa disesi ka ho phethela Mohope wa Lefatshe wa Disesi wa FINA Doha, ho la Qatar.

src: Cameron van der Burgh won a gold medal in the 100 metres breaststroke race, Chad le Clos in the 100 metres butterfly also managed a fourth place finish in the 200 metres backstroke win.
tgt: Cameron van der Burgh o hapile medale wa gauta ho dimithara tse 100 tsa lebelo la ho sesa ka difuba, Chad le Clos ho dimithara tse 100 tsa serurubele hape o kgonne ho qetella maemong a bone a ho sesa ka ho hapa ho sesa ka mokokotlo tlholong ya dimithara tse 200.

src: Michael Meyer won silver in the 200 metres individual medley.
tgt: Michael Meyer o hapile silivera ho dimithara tse 200 tsa lebelo la motswako la bo mong.

src: Douglas Erasmus won a bronze medal in the fast pace 50 metres freestyle.
tgt: Douglas Erasmus o hapile medale wa boronse ho lebelo la boikgethelo le potlakileng la dimithara tse Kaylene Corbett e bile wa borobedi ho lebelo la makgaolakgang la dimithara tse 50 la ho sesa ka mokokotlo ha Calvyn Justus le yena a phethetse borobeding ho lebelo la dimithara tse 200 la boikgethelo.

src: Conferences.
tgt: Dikhonferense.

src: Cabinet welcomes delegates attending the 4th BRICS International Competition Conference from 12 to 13 November 2015 at the Inkosi Albert Luthuli Convention Centre, Durban under the theme: “Competition and Inclusive Growth”.This brings together experts in competition law to explore how competition policy can contribute to inclusive growth and economic development in BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa) countries.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela kemedi e kenetseng Khonferense ya BRICS ya Bone ya Matjhaba ya Phehisano ho tloha ka la 12 ho isa ka la 13 Pudungwana WEBTOKENtsing sa Dikopano sa Inkosi Albert Luthuli, ho la Durban tlasa mookotaba: “Phehisano le Kgolo e Kenyeletsang”.Sena se bokanya mmoho ditsebi ho tsa molao wa phehisano bakeng sa ho sekaseka kamoo leano la phehisano le ka nyehelang ho kgolo e kenyeletsang le ntshetsopele ya moruo ka hara dinaha tsa BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China le Aforika Borwa).Taolo e matla ya diphehisano ya Aforika Borwa e kgontsha baahi ho nka karolo ka ho hloka leeme moruong wa naha.

src: South Africa’s strong competition regulation enables citizens to participate fairly in the national economy.
tgt: E kgothaletsa ho itahlela ka setotswana ha batho ba batlang ba le bangata makaleng a tlhahiso a moruo le ho fedisa ho se utlwane ka hara dikgwebo.

src: It promotes the involvement of more people in the productive sectors of the economy and levels the playing field in business.
tgt: Taolo ya diphehisano ya Aforika Borwa e nyehela bonkakarolo bo batlang bo phahame ba baahi mme e entse menyabuketso e bonahalang bakeng sa ho lwantsha maqulwana le ho henahenana le ditheko.

src: South Africa’s competition regulation contributes to greater citizen participation and it has made material strides in combating cartels and price-fixing.
tgt: E nkile ketapele bakeng sa ho sebedisa ditabatabelo tse mabapi le dimatahanyo le diphumantsho.

src: Transport Minister Dipuo Peters will attend the Second Global Conference for Ministers of Transport from 18 to 20 November 2015 in Brazil, where South Africa will table its Mid-Term Country Report of progress made on the implementation of the United Nations Decade of Action for Road Safety 2011-2020 Global Plan.
tgt: Letona la Dipalangwang Dipuo Peters le tla kenela Khonferense ya Bobedi ya Lefatshe ya Matona a Dipalangwang ho tloha ka la 18 ho isa ho la 20 Pudungwana 2015 ho la Brazil, moo Aforika Borwa e tla teka Tlaleho ya Nako e Bohareng ya Naha mabapi le kgatelopele e entsweng bakeng sa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Moralo wa Lefatshe wa Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng wa Dilemo tse Leshome tsa ho Sebetsana le Boipaballo Mebileng wa 2011-2020.Aforika Borwa e itlamme ho fokotsa dikotsi tsa mebileng ka 50% ho tloha ho tse 13 967 ho ya ho tse ka tlase ho 7 000 ka 2020.

src: South Africa committed itself to reduce road carnage by 50 per cent from 13 967 to below 7 000 by 2020.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e etsa menyabuketso ya bohlokwa bakeng sa ho fihlella dipheo tsa yona jwaloka ka ha di hlahella ho Moralo wa Lefatshe wa Dilemo tse Leshome tsa ho Sebetsana le Boipaballo Mebileng wa 2011-2020, ho sa natswe diphephetso tseo hajwale naha e tobaneng le tsona.

src: South Africa is making significant strides in achieving the targets as set out in the Decade of Action for Road Safety 2011-2020 Global Plan, despite challenges currently facing the country.
tgt: Maemo a Kabinete Mabapi le Dintlha tsa Bohlokwa Maemong a Hajwale Ho sebetsana le ditshita tsa tlhahiso ya mesebetsi e dula e le ntlha e ka sehloohong bakeng sa mmuso.

src: The Medium Term Budget Policy Statement highlighted a global economic growth that has slowed, with depressed commodity prices and increased unemployment in many parts of the world.
tgt: Leano la Pehelo ya Ditekanyetso tsa Nako e Bohareng le hlakisitse kgolo ya moruo ya lefatshe e tsamayang butle, ka ditheko tsa thepa tse tlasa kgatello le tlhokeho ya mesebetsi e phahameng dikarolong tse ngata tsa lefatshe.

src: This was reflected in the Quarterly Labour Force Survey, which for the third quarter of 2015 recorded unemployment at per cent, marginally up from per cent in the same quarter last year.
tgt: Sena se ile sa bonahala ho Diphuputso tsa Kotara ka nngwe tsa Lebotho la Basebetsi, tseo bakeng sa kotara ya boraro ya 2015 di ngodisitseng tlhokeho ya mosebetsi ho 25.5%, haholo ho phahama ho tloha ho 25.4% kotareng e tshwanang selemong se fetileng.

src: This underscores the need for all sectors to work with government in support of the country’s initiatives to create employment opportunities and get more South Africans into work.
tgt: Sena se hlakisa tlhokeho ya hore makala kaofela a sebetse le mmuso bakeng sa ho tshehetsa boikitlaetso ba naha ba ho hlahisa menyetla ya mesebetsi le ho etsa hore maAforika Borwa a mangata a sebetse.

src: Government, through the Nine-Point Plan, is working to ignite growth and create jobs by unlocking new opportunities in strategic economic areas.
tgt: Mmuso, ka Moralo wa Dintlha tse Robong, o sebetsa ho hotetsa kgolo le ho hlahisa mesebetsi ka ho bula menyetla e metjha dibakeng tsa mawa a moruo.

src: Cabinet welcomes the announcement by President Zuma of a zero-percent increase at tertiary institutions for the 2016 academic year.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela tsebiso ya Moporesidente Zuma ya ho se nyolle ditefello ditheong tsa thuto e phahameng bakeng sa selemo sa dithuto sa 2016.

src: This decision brings much needed monetary relief, especially to the poor, working class and lower middle class families with university students.
tgt: Qeto ena e tlisitse kimoloho e batlehang haholo ya ditjhelete, haholoholo ho ba fumanehileng, ba sebetsang le sehlopha sa malapa a mahareng a nang le baithuti.

src: Cabinet further welcomes the decision by the President to establish a commission to look into all the issues raised by the students.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e amohela qeto ya Moporesidente ya ho theha khomishene e tla shebana le dintlha tsohle tse hlahisitsweng ke baithuti.

src: The President will be announcing the commission together with its terms of reference in due course.
tgt: Moporesidente o tla tsebisa ka khomishene mmoho le dintlha tsa yona tsa tshebetso ha mmela o ntse o puta.

src: Cabinet welcomes the interventions by the Department of Water and Sanitation to assist communities in KwaZulu-Natal and the Free State affected by the recent drought.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela boitshunyako ba Lefapha la Metsi le Dikgwerekgwere bakeng sa ho thusa badudi ho la KwaZulu-Natal le Foreistata ba anngweng ke komello ya moraorao tjena.

src: Areas that are supplied by the country’s larger regional water supply dams and schemes remain water secure as these systems are currently in a positive water balance with a national average dam storage at 66 per cent full.
tgt: Dibaka tse fepelwang ke matamo a maholwanyane a lebatowa a naha le dikema di dutse di ntse di bolokehile kaha ditsamaiso tsena hajwale di na le botsitso bo botle ba palohare ya poloko ya metsi a tletseng ka 66%.Kabinete e amohela ho thehwa ha Komiti e Kopanetsweng ya Matona (IMC) e mabapi le Polokeho ya Metsi bodulasetulong ba Letona la Kopanelo ya Puso le Merero ya Botjhaba Pravin Gordhan.

src: Cabinet welcomes the establishment of an Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) on Water Security chaired by Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs Minister Pravin Gordhan.
tgt: IMC e bopilwe ka Matona a Ntshetsopele ya Dibaka tsa Mahae le Puseletso ya Mobu Metsi le Tsamaiso ya Dikgwerekgwere, le Temo, Meru le Ditlhapi.

src: The IMC consists of Ministers of Rural Development and Land Reform Water and Sanitation, and Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries.
tgt: Komiti e tla tshohla le ho sisinya boitshunyako bo bong ho badudi ba anngweng haholo ke komello.

src: Cabinet noted developments in Nigeria regarding MTN’s US$5.2 billion fine by the Nigerian Communications Commission.
tgt: Kabinete e lemohile se ntseng se etsahala ho la Nigeria mabapi le kotlo ya MTN ya US$5.2 bilione ke Khomishene ya Dikgokahanyo ya Nigeria.

src: Cabinet trusts that the discussions underway between MTN and Nigerian authorities will result in the speedy resolution of the disputes so as to ensure MTN continues its business of investing in the Nigerian economy.
tgt: Kabinete e tshepa hore dipuisano tse ntseng di tswela pele pakeng tsa MTN le ba ka sehloohong ba Nigeria di tla baka hore ho be le tharollo e potlakileng ya ho se utlwane hore ho tle ho netefatswe hore MTN e tswela pele ka kgwebo ya yona ya ho tsetela ka hara moruo wa Nigeria.

src: Cabinet was saddened about the untimely death of Chumani Nqakula, the son of Defence and Military Veterans Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula and Charles Nqakula, a Member of Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e utlwisitswe bohloko ke lefu la tshohanyetso la Chumani Nqakula, mora wa Letona la Tshireletso le Mekaubere ya Ntwa Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula le Charles Nqakula, e leng Setho sa Palamente.

src: Cabinet conveys its sincerest condolences to the Nqakula family and friends.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisa matshediso a yona a tebileng ho lelapa la Nqakula le metswalle.

src: Cabinet extends its heartfelt condolences to the family and relatives of Public Service and Administration Minister Ngoako Ramatlhodi, on the passing of his 95-year-old mother, Mmatlou Elizabeth Ramatlhodi.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisa matshediso a yona a tebileng ho lelapa le ba leloko la Letona la Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba le Tsamaiso Ngoako Ramatlhodi, ka ho hlokahala ha mme wa hae ya dilemo tse 95, Mmatlou Elizabeth Ramatlhodi.

src: AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: DithonyoDithonyo kaofela di tla lokelwa ke ho netefatswa ha mangolo a thuto le tumello e amehang.

src: Mr Mogojare Richard Seleka as the Director-General (DG) in the Department of Public Enterprises and.
tgt: Monghadi Mogojare Richard Seleka jwaloka Motsamaisi e Moholo (DG) ho Lefapha la Dikgwebo tsa Setjhaba le.

src: Cabinet commends the progress made by the Department of Human Settlements in the Savanna City Integrated Human Settlements project in the Sedibeng District Municipality.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Lefapha la Bodulo ba Batho bakeng sa ho fana ka matlo porojekeng ya Bodulo ba Batho e Kopanetsweng ya Savanna City ka hara Masepala wa Setereke wa Sedibeng ho dihlopha tse dikojwana di mahetleng.

src: Completion of the sustainable and integrated, new town development project, in ten years, will provide 18 399 Integrated housing units which include “Breaking New Ground Houses” and bonded houses, educational facilities, clinics, crèches, churches and retail sitesSince the beginning of construction early this year over 1 000 of the 18 399 houses are being built with over 100 completed.
tgt: MaAforika Borwa a itlhommeng pele a ile a ikopanya le bankakrolo ba diindaseteri, ho kenyeletswa le bomeyara le bahlanka ba tswang Masepaleng wa Setereke wa Sedibeng, mabapi le ho penta matlo a phethetsweng mmoho le ho thusa ka ditshingwana nakong ya ho thakgolwa.

src: Prominent South Africans joined industry stakeholders, including mayors and officials from the Sedibeng District Municipality, in working on three houses for the oldest beneficiaries.
tgt: Ho ahilwe matlo a ka bang 18 000, a tswetseng molemo maqheku, batho ba qhwadileng, le malapa ao dihlooho tsa ona e leng bana le basadi.

src: Cabinet welcomes the upgrading of the R25 (P6-1) road, a 42-kilometre road that links Gauteng and Limpopo.
tgt: Kabinete e boetse e amohela tsebiso ya hore selemong se tlang lefapha le tla thakgola porojeke, e tla etsa hore ho ahuwe matlo a 60 000.

src: The project, which stretches between Bapsfontein and Bronkhorstspruit, has employed more than 200 people.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela kgatelopele e entsweng ke porojeke ya Tshepo 10 000, e thusang ho fedisa tlhokeho ya mesebetsi bakeng sa batjha ka hara Motsemoholo wa Tshwane.

src: The visit aims to finalise the China-South Africa 5-10 Year Framework on Cooperation that will further entrench the implementation of our agreements since the conclusion of the Beijing Declaration in 2010.
tgt: Kabinete e tsebisitswe ke Lefapha la Saense le Thekenoloji, le tla tshwara beke ya saense ya setjhaba e kgolo: Foramo ya Saense ya Aforika Borwa 2015 tlasa mookotaba: “Re hotetsa moqoqo ka saense” ho tloha ka la 8 ho isa ka la 9 Tshitwe 2015, ho la Pretoria.

src: It will further deepen and expand on the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership that the two countries share.
tgt: Ketsahalo ena e neha bankakarolo ba tswang Aforika Borwa, ka hara kontinente le bomphato ba matjhaba lepatlelo bakeng sa dingangisano le ho ithuta ka maano mabapi le ho tsamaelana pakeng tsa saense le setjhaba.

src: South Africa’s relations with China remain central to realising its developmental agenda through its foreign policy as it increases efforts to implement the NDP, collaborate in agriculture, environmental affairs, trade and industry and finance as the country continues to drive the agenda of moving South Africa forward.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana hore Ketsahalo ya Letsatsi le Tsamaelanang le tsa Mawatle ya Lefatshe ya Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba wa Mawatle (IMO) e tshwarelwe Aforika Borwa ka 2020.

src: It is also provides an opportunity to review progress on existing areas of trade and cooperation between the two nations, and to expedite and finalise new areas of cooperation.
tgt: Lefapha la Dipalangwang ha ho le jwalo le tla fetisetsa qeto ena ya Kabinete ho kopano ya Lekgotla ya IMO e reretsweng ho etsahala ho tloha ka la 23 Pudungwana ho isa ka la 04 Tshitwe Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: President Zuma will lead a delegation to the 21st session of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the 11th Session of the Conference of Parties serving as the Meeting of Parties to the Kyoto Protocol (CMP11) to be held from 30 November to 11 December 2015 in Paris, France.
tgt: Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o tla amohela wa mphato wa hae wa China Xi Jinping bakeng sa Leeto la Semmuso la matsatsi a mabedi ho tloha ka la 2 ho isa ka la 3 Tshitwe.

src: In line with South Africa’s national interest as an African and developing country that will require post-2020 support, South Africa will continue to defend the UNFCCC’s core principles of equity and WEBTOKEN the Group of 77+China meeting, South Africa will seek to maintain and strengthen the unity of developing countries to obtain a Paris Agreement that is fair, ambitious, science-based and that produces the development space of developing countries.
tgt: Sepheo sa leeto ke ho phethela Moralo wa Tshebedisanommoho wa Dilemo tse 5-10 wa China-Aforika Borwa o tla thatiselletsa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha ditumellano tsa rona esale ho phethelwa Boitlamo ba Beijing ka 2010.

src: President Zuma will launch the 16 Days of Activism Campaign for No Violence against Women and Children campaign on 25 November 2015 in Naauwpoort, Mahikeng under the theme: “Count Me In: Together Moving a Non-Violent South Africa Forward”.
tgt: Dikamano tsa Aforika Borwa le China e dula e le bohare ba ho fihlella lenaneo la yona la ntshetsopele ka leano la yona la matjhabeng kaha le eketsa mekutu ya ho kenya tshebetsong Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP), tshebedisanommoho ho tsa temo, merero ya tsa tikoloho, kgwebisano le diindaseteri le tsa ditjhelete jwaloka ha naha e tswela pele ho kganna lenaneo la ho ntshetsa Aforika Borwa pele.

src: This campaign is commemorated as part of the 365 Days of Activism, which is a continuous campaign that raises awareness on violence against women and children, and mobilises individuals to be counted in the year long activism.
tgt: Hape le fana ka monyetla wa ho sheba botjha kgatelopele mabakeng a hajwale a kgwebisano le tshebedisanommoho pakeng tsa dinaha ka bobedi, le ho potlakisa le ho phethela dibaka tse ntjha tsa tshebedisanommoho.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to support this campaign and to use this period to mobilise communities and partner with government to end violence against women and children - #CountMeIn.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla etella pele Kemedi e tla kenela ho dula ha bo-21 ha Khonferense ya Mekga ho Seboka sa Meralo ya Phethoho ya Tlelaemete sa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UNFCCC) le ho dula ha bo-11 ha Khonferense ya Mekga e sebetsang jwaloka Kopano ya Mekga ho Porothokhole ya Kyoto (CMP11) e tla tshwarwa ho tloha ka la 30 Pudungwana ho isa ka la 11 Tshitwe 2015 Paris, ho la Fora.

src: Deputy President Ramaphosa will lead a government delegation in its regular engagement with the South African National Editors’ Forum on 21 November 2015 as part of government’s commitment and ongoing programme to strengthen relations with the media.
tgt: Ditherisano tsa matjhaba bakeng sa tumellano e ntjha ya semolao e tla hlophisa karabelo ho phethoho ya tlelaemete, e tla qala ho sebetsa ho tloha ka 2020 ho ya pele.

src: Government will brief editors on key issues and upcoming plans while affording the editors an opportunity to raise areas of interest with government.
tgt: Ho imatahantswe le ditabatabelo tsa naha tsa Aforika Borwa jwaloka naha ya Aforika e tswelang pele e tla batla tshehetso ya kamora 2020, Aforika Borwa e tla tswela pele ho tshireletsa dipehelo tsa mantlha tsa UNFCCC tsa tekatekano le phapantsho.

src: South Africa will mark World AIDS Day under a theme - “Towards an HIV-Free Generation: RISACPROTECZERO" – which is a call to action by communities.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla thakgola Letsholo la Matsatsi a 16 bakeng sa thibelo ya Dikgoka kgahlanong le Basadi le Bana ka la 25 Pudungwana 2015 Naauwpoort, ho la Mahikeng tlasa mookotaba: “Mpalle le nna: Mmoho re Ntshetsapele Aforika Borwa e hlokang Dikgoka.” Letsholo lena le hopolwa jwaloka karolo ya Matsatsi a 365 a Twantsho, leo e leng letsholo le tswellang le lemosang ka dikgoka kgahlanong le basadi le bana, le ho elellwisa batho hore ba balellwe twantshong ya selemo ho pota.

src: This year’s theme is informed by the United Nations World AIDS Day theme for 2011 to 2015 is: “Getting to Zero”.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa kaofela ho tshehetsa letsholo lena le ho sebedisa nako ena bakeng sa ho elellwisa badudi le ho imatahanya le mmuso ho fedisa dikgoka kgahlanong le basadi le bana - #Count me In.

src: The 2015 World AIDS Day will further strengthen the dialogue around stigma and discrimination, and mobilise communities to respond to and expand access to prevention, treatment and support services.
tgt: Motlatsi wa Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa o tla etella pele kemedi ya mmuso dipuisanong tsa yona tse setlwaeding le Foramo ya Bahlophisi ba Boraditaba ba Naha ya Aforika Borwa ka la 21 Pudungwana 2015 jwaloka boitlamo ba mmuso le lenaneo le tswellang la ho tiisa dikamano le boraditaba.

src: The main event to commemorate World AIDS Day will be held in KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Mmuso o tla tsebisa bahlophisi ka dintlha tsa bohlokwa le meralo e motjheng ha ho ntse ho fuwa bahlophisi monyetla wa ho hlahisa dibaka tsa kgahleho le mmuso.

src: This will set the tone for South Africa’s hosting of the 21st International AIDS Conference at the Inkosi Albert Luthuli International Convention Centre in Durban from 17 to 22 July 2016.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tla tshwaya Letsatsi la Lefatshe la AIDS tlasa mookotaba - “Ho isa Molokong o Hlokang HIV: PHAHAMSEBETSTSHIRELETSLETHO – e leng kgoeletso ya ho sebetsa ho setjhaba.

src: South Africa continues to make progress in the fight against HIV and AIDS, having expanded the country’s HIV treatment programme, with over three million people on antiretroviral treatment, further reducing mother-to-child transmission and recording improved tuberculosis indicators.
tgt: Letsatsi la Lefatshe la AIDS la 2015 le tla boela le matlafatsa puisano ka sekodi le kgethollo, le ho elelliswa ha badudi ka hore ba arabele le ho hodisa phumantsho ya thibelo, kalafo le tshehetso ya ditshebeletso.

src: Cabinet encourages South Africans to participate in the Izimbizo events planned across the country during National Imbizo Focus Week from 30 November to 6 December 2015.
tgt: Ketsahalo e kgolo ya ho hopola Letsatsi la Lefatshe la AIDS e tla tshwarelwa KwaZulu-Natal.

src: National Imbizo Focus Week will take place under the theme: “Together we move South Africa forward” and will update communities on government’s implementation of the Nine-Point Plan towards igniting economic growth and creating jobs, as outlined by President Zuma in his February 2015 State of the Nation Address.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tswella ho etsa kgatelopele ho ntwa kgahlanong le HIV le AIDS, ebile e se e atolositse lenaneo la naha la kalafo ya HIV, moo batho ba dimilione di le tharo ba tholang kalafo ya meriana ya HIV, e le mohato wa ho fokotsa tshwaetso ya ho tloha ho mme ho ya ho lesea le ho rekota matshwao a ntlafetseng a lefuba.

src: Members of the Executive will also use the opportunity to galvanise community participation in tackling various social ills, including matters relating to violence against women and children.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa maAforika Borwa ho nka karolo diketsahalong tsa di-Imbizo tse rerilweng ho phatlalla le naha nakong ya Beke ya Imbizo ya Naha ya ho Tsepamisa Maikutlo ho tloha ka la 30 Pudungwana ho isa ka la 6 Tshitwe 2015.

src: December is Reconciliation Month and South Africa will mark Reconciliation Day on 16 December in Port Elizabeth, Eastern Cape under the theme: “Bridging the divide: Building a common South African nationhood towards a national developmental state”.
tgt: Beke ya Imbizo ya Naha ya ho Tsepamisa Maikutlo e tla tshwarwa tlasa mookotaba: “Mmoho re ntshetsa Aforika Borwa pele” mme e tla beha badudi sehlohlolong ka ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Moralo wa Dintlha tse Robong ke mmuso bakeng sa ho hotetsa kgolo ya moruo le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi, jwaloka ha o tekilwe ke Moporesidente Zuma Puong ya hae ka Maemo a Setjhaba ya Tlhakola 2015.

src: The month has a special significance for the nation as it promotes reconciliation, peace and social cohesion on which the country’s new democratic dispensation was founded.
tgt: Ditho tsa Phethahatso di tla boela di sebedise monyetla ona ho kgothaletsa bonkakarolo ba badudi bakeng sa ho sebetsana le mathata a fapafapaneng a setjhaba, ho kenyeletswa dintlha tse tsamaelanang le dikgoka kgahlanong le basadi le bana.

src: Cabinet encourages all South Africans to use the month to reach out to one another as the nation continues to work together to build a united and prosperous nation.
tgt: Tshitwe ke Kgwedi ya Poelano mme Aforika Borwa e tla tshwaya Letsatsi la Poelano la 16 Tshitwe Port Elizabeth, ho la Kapa Botjhabela tlasa mookotaba: “Re ngotla karohano: Re aha bosetjhaba bo tshwanang ba Aforika Borwa ho isa pusong ya naha e tswelang pele”.

src: Cabinet thanks all taxpayers for partnering with government in providing much-needed services that help improve the lives of thousands of communities across the country.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa maAforika Borwa kaofela ho sebedisa kgwedi ena bakeng sa ho atamelana ha naha e ntse e tswella ho sebetsa mmoho bakeng sa ho aha setjhaba se le seng se atlehileng.

src: Cabinet congratulates the Department of Social Development’s Gender-Based Violence Command Centre (GBVCC) for winning the Global Best Contact Centre Award in Las Vegas, USA, on Thursday, 5 November 2015.
tgt: Kabinete e hopotsa balefi ba lekgetho ba so kang ba kenya ditokomane tsa bona tsa lekgetho bakeng sa selemo sa 2014/15 sa lekgetho hore letsatsi la ho qetela la ho kenya ditokomane ke la 27 Pudungwana 2015.

src: The GBVCC is a 24-hour call centre dedicated to providing support and counselling to victims of gender- based violence.
tgt: Kabinete e leboha balefi kaofela ba lekgetho bakeng sa ho imatahanya le mmuso mabapi le ho fana ka ditshebeletso tse hlokahalang ka matla tse thusang ho ntlafatsa bophelo ba diketekete tsa badudi ho phatlalla le naha.

src: This is another success story that shows a caring government that is resolute in the fight to stop Gender based violence.
tgt: Kabinete thoholetsa Setsha sa Mehala sa Bolaodi ba Dikgoka tse Amanang le Bong sa Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba (GBVCC) ka ho hapa Kgau ya Lefatshe ya Setsha sa Mehala se Hlwahlwa ka ho Fetisisa Las Vegas, ho la Amerika, ka Labone, la 5 Pudungwana 2015.

src: Cabinet congratulates Eskom for operating 100 days without cutting power supply (load-shedding).
tgt: GBVCC ke setsi sa mehala se sebetsang bosiu le motshehare se reretsweng ho fana ka tshehetso le boeletsi ho diphofu tsa dikgoka tse amanang le bong.

src: Eskom reached this milestone on Tuesday, 17 November 2015.
tgt: Eskom e fihletse mokolokotwane ona ka Labobedi, la 17 Pudungwana 2015.

src: The 100 days of uninterrupted electricity supply does not suggest we must be complacent.
tgt: Matsatsi a 100 a phepelo ya motlakase e sa sitisehang ha ho bolele hore re ka qhanolla.

src: Instead, Cabinet calls on communities to continue observing the energy saving interventions.
tgt: Empa, Kabinete e ipiletsa ho badudi ho tswella ho lekola boishunyako ba ho baballa eneji.

src: Cabinet congratulates nominees of the 2015 SA Sport Awards to be held on 22 November 2015 at the Sand du Plessis Theatre in Mangaung, Free State.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa bakgethwa ba Dikgau tsa Dipapadi tsa Aforika Borwa tsa 2015 tse tla tshwarwa ka la 22 Pudungwana 2015 Theatereng ya Sand du Plessis Mangaung, ho la Foreisetata.

src: The awards, convened under the theme: “Excellence is not being your best it is doing your best”, celebrates 10 years of recognising and honouring individuals and teams who have excelled both on and off the field.
tgt: Dikgau tsena, tse hlophisitsweng tlasa mookotaba: “Boqhetseke ha se ho ba hlwahlwa ho fetisisa ke ho etsa ho fetisisang”, di keteka dilemo tse 10 tsa ho ananela le ho hlompha batho ba sebeditseng ka bokgabane ka hare le ka ntle ho mabala a dipapadi.

src: South Africans are encouraged to support the event by voting for the 2015 Sports Star of the Year.
tgt: MaAforika Borwa a kgothaletswa ho tshehetsa ketshalo ena ka ho kgetha Naledi ya Selemo ya Dipapadi ya Maemo a Kabinete Mabapi le Dintlha tsa Bohlokwa Maemong a Hajwale.

src: Cabinet joined President Zuma and the international community in strongly condemning the recent terrorist attacks that took place in Beirut (Lebanon), Baghdad (Iraq), Yola (Nigeria) and Paris (France), which resulted in the loss of innocent lives and destruction of property.
tgt: Kabinete e imatahantse le Moporesidente Zuma le badudi ba matjhabeng ka ho tshwela ka mathe ka matla ditlhaselo tsa boferekanyi tsa moraorao tjena tse etsahetseng Beirut (Lebanon), Baghdad (Iraq), Yola (Nigeria) le Paris (Fora), tse bakileng tahlehelo ya bophelo ba batho ba se nang molato le tshenyo ya thepa.

src: South Africa stands firm in its condemnation of all attacks targeting innocent civilians and reiterates its stance that terrorism, in whatever form and from whichever quarter, cannot be condoned.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e ema e tiile ho tshweleng ka mathe ha yona ha ditlhaselo kaofela tse tobileng badudi ba se nang molato mme e boeletsa mmono wa yona wa hore boferekanyi, ka sebopeho sefe kapa sefe le hore bo tswa hokae, bo keke ba amohelwa.

src: Cabinet supports the actions of the Government Committee of Ministers on Water Scarcity and Drought to mitigate the effects of the drought and urges communities to use water sparingly in order to secure future supply.
tgt: Kabinete e tshehetsa diketso tsa Komiti ya Matona a Mmuso e mabapi le Kgaello ya Metsi le Komello bakeng sa ho bebofatsa kgahlamelo ya komello le ho kgothaletsa badudi ho sebedisa metsi ka polokeho bakeng sa ho tiisetsa phepelo ya kamoso.

src: Government has added R96,6 million to the initial R352,6 million set aside to support the country’s drought relief efforts.
tgt: Mmuso o ekeditse ka R96,6 milione ho R352,6 milione ya sethathong ho tshehetsa mekutu ya naha ya ho imolla mathata a komello.

src: This includes the purchase of 45 water tankers for the distribution of water to affected areas, borehole drilling and rehabilitation, water conservation and demand management, and water source augmentations.
tgt: Sena se kenyeletsa ho rekwa ha ditanka tsa metsi tse 45 bakeng sa ho fuwa dibaka tse amehileng, ho epa dipetse le tlhabollo, papallo ya metsi le ho laola tlhokeho, le ho thusa ka mehlodi.

src: The Department of Rural Development and Land Reform will in the worst affected regions allow the relocation of livestock onto state-owned land where there is still better pasture.
tgt: Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Dibaka tsa Mahae le Tlhabollo ya Mobu le tla dumella hore ho falliswe mehlape ho tloha dibakeng tse thefulehileng ka ho fetisisa ho iswa mobung oo e leng wa mmuso moo ho ntseng ho na le makgulo a betere.

src: In addition the Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs has coordinated with Mayors to implement various water saving measures under the guidance of the Department of Water and Sanitation.
tgt: Hodima moo, Lefapha la Kopanelo ya Puso le Merero ya Botjhaba le hokahane le Bomeyara bakeng sa ho kenya tshebetsong ditsela tse fapafapaneng tsa ho baballa metsi tlasa tataiso ya Lefapha la Metsi le Tsamaiso ya Dikgwerekgwere.

src: These include introducing water restrictions monitoring adherence to water restrictions applying penalties where necessary prioritising the repair of water leaks promoting water-efficient technologies such as low-flush toilet cisterns rainwater harvesting and the use of grey water for irrigation.
tgt: Tsena di kenyeletsa ho hlahisa dithibelo tsa tshebediso ya metsi ho disa boimatahanyo le dithibelo tsa tshebediso ya metsi ho fana ka dikotlo moo ho hlokahalang ho beha ka sehloohong tokiso ya ho dutla ha metsi ho kgothaletsa dithekenoloji tse hlwahlwa tse jwaloka matlwana a sa sebediseng metsi a mangata ha a hulelwa ho bokella metsi a pula le ho sebedisa metsi a sebeditseng bakeng sa ho nosetsa.

src: President Jacob Zuma led the South African delegation to the G20 Leaders Summit in Antalya, Turkey from 15 to 16 November 2015.
tgt: Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o ile a etella pele kemedi ya Aforika Borwa ho Seboka sa Baetapele ba G20 Antalya, ho la Turkey ho tloha ka la 15 ho isa ka la 16 Pudungwana 2015.

src: The theme of the summit was inclusiveness, investment and implementation.
tgt: Mookotaba wa seboka e ne e le kenyeletso, matsete le ho kenngwa tshebetsong.

src: South Africa is among 51 countries that signed the Agreement on Automatic Exchange to Tax Information in Berlin, Germany in October 2015.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e hara dinaha tse 51 tse saenneng Tumello ya Phapanyetsano ya Tlhahisoleseding ya Lekgetho Berlin, ho la Jeremane ka Mphalane 2015.

src: Countries will begin exchanging information in 2017, which will be underpinned by legislation currently before Parliament.
tgt: Dinaha di tla qala ho fapanyetsana tlhahisoleseding ka 2017, e tla hlakiswa ke molao oo hajwale o tekilweng ka hara Palamente.

src: President Zuma welcomed the conclusion of the 15 action items of the G20/Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development Base Erosion and Proft Shifting project, which were critical to ensuring fairness and securing sub-Saharan Africa’s revenue base.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o amohetse qeto ya dintlha tsa tshebetso tse15 tsa G20/Mokgatlo bakeng sa porojeke ya Tshebedisanommoho le Kgoholeho ya Motheo wa Ntshetsopele le ho Suthiswa ha Phaello, tseo di neng di le hlokolosi bakeng sa ho netefatsa ho hloka leeme le ho tiisetsa motheo wa lekeno wa dinaha tse ka Borwa ho Sahara.

src: Members of the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) Council of Ministers met on 11 November 2015 in Windhoek, Namibia on the eve of the inauguration of the SACU headquarters and the informal discussion by the SACU Heads of State and Government.
tgt: Ditho tsa Lekgotla la Matona a Kopano ya Makgetho a Madiboho a Aforika e Borwa (SACU) di kopane ka la 11 Pudungwana 2015 Windhoek, ho la Namibia letsatsing le eteletseng pele ho bulwa ha ntlokgolo ya SACU le dipuisano tseo e seng tsa semmuso tsa Dihlooho tsa Dipuso tsa SACU le Mmuso.

src: The council used the opportunity to reflect on the progress made on the Six-Point Plan since their last meeting and re-emphasized their commitment to SACThe council agreed that SACU should move beyond revenue-sharing to a developmental initiative that will support integration in the region.
tgt: Lekgotla le sebedisitse monyetla ona bakeng sa ho thuisa kgatelopele e entsweng mabapi le Moralo wa Dintlha tse Tsheletseng esale ho tshwere kopano ya ho qetela le ho toboketsa botjha boitlamo ba bona ho SACLekgotla le dumellane hore SACU e tshwanela ho sebetsa ho fihlella ka nqane ho karolelano ya lekeno ho ya boikitlaetsong ba ntshetsopele bo tla tshehetsa kopanelo ka hara lebatowa.

src: Members also adopted a roadmap and work plan towards the summit that will be held in June 2016.
tgt: Ditho hape di amohetse mmapa le moralo wa dtshebetso o tla lebisa ho seboka se tla tshwarwa ka Phuptjane 2016.

src: Cabinet welcomes the 2014-15 Audit Outcomes of national and provincial government.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela Diphetho tsa Tlhatlhobo tsa 2014-15 tsa mmuso wa naha le wa porofense.

src: The report shows consistent improvement in almost all aspects of national and provincial government audit outcomes.
tgt: Tlaleho e bontsha ntlafalo e tsitsitseng mabakeng kaofela a diphetho tsa ditlhatlhobo tsa mmuso wa naha le wa porofense.

src: It points to a steady trend towards good governance and sound financial management and reinforces good governance as more departments have received clean audits.
tgt: Di bontsha ho lebisa mokgweng o motle wa bolaodi le taolo e imametseng ya ditjhelete le ho matlafatsa bolaodi bo botle ka ha mafapha a mangatanyana a fumane ditlhatlhobo tse hlwahlwa.

src: The improvement further shows that government is working hard to ensure accountability in all areas of its work.
tgt: Ntlafalo ena e boela e supa hore mmuso o sebetsa ka thata bakeng sa ho netefatsa boikarabelo dibakeng tsa ona tsohle tsa mosebetsi wa ona.

src: Despite this improvement, government has resolved to continue supporting departments with negative findings and to ensure that the whole government machinery is functioning optimally.
tgt: Ntle le ntlafalo ena, mmuso o entse qeto ya ho tswella ho tshehetsa mafapha a nang le diphuputso tse sa kgahliseng le ho netefatsa hore mafapha oohle a mmuso a sebetsa ho ya ka tebello.

src: Cabinet welcomes the appointment by President Zuma of Judge Mandisa Muriel Maya as the Deputy President of the Supreme Court of Appeal in terms of section 174(4) of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996 and Justice Nonkosi Zoliswa Mhlantla as a judge of the Constitutional Court in terms of Section 174(3) of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996 respectively.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho thonngwa ha Moahlodi Mandisa Muriel Maya jwaloka Motlatsi wa Moporesidente wa Lekgotla le Phahameng la Maipiletso ke Moporesidente Zuma ho ya ka karolo 174(4) ya Molaotheo wa Riphaboliki ya Aforika Borwa wa the 1996 le Moahlodi Nonkosi Zoliswa Mhlantla jwaloka moahlodi wa Lekgotla la Dinyewe la Molaotheo ho ya ka Karolo 174(3) ya Molaotheo wa Rephaboliki ya Aforika Borwa wa 1996 ka tatelano.

src: The appointments strengthens South Africa’s commitment to gender equality at the highest level and advances the transformation of the judiciary.
tgt: Dithonyo tsena di matlafatsa boitlamo ba Aforika Borwa ba tekatekano ya bong maemong a phahameng ka ho fetisisa le ho akofisa phethoho ya makgotla a dinyewe.

src: Cabinet congratulates both judges and wish them all the best in the execution of this critical responsibility in the South African Judiciary.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa baahlodi ka bobedi le ho ba lakaletsa tse molemo mabapi le ho phethahatsa boikarabelo bona bo hlokolosi ka hara Makgotla a Dinyewe a Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet congratulates Dr S’thembile Ngidi who made history when she graduated from the College of Medicine South Africa as KwaZulu-Natal's first black female oncologist and only the second in the country.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Ngaka S’thembile Ngidi ya entseng nalane ka ho fumana mangolo a thuto ho tswa ho Koletjhe ya tsa Kalafo ya Aforika Borwa jwaloka ngaka ya pele e alafang mofetshe ya mosadi ho tswa KwaZulu-Natal ebile e le wa bobedi feela ka hara naha.

src: Cabinet commends South African filmmaker Reina-Marie Loader whose documentary ‘Horn’ received many accolades, including a nomination for the Rhino Conservation Awards 2015 in July in the category Best Awareness, Education and Funding, and winning the award for the Best Conservation Film at the 2015 International Film Festival in New York City, USCabinet extends its condolences to the family and friends of the Deputy Minister of Water and Sanitation, Ms Pamela Tshwete, on the loss of her mother, Mama Ruth Nomzi Zondeki.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Moetsi wa difilimi wa Aforika Borwa Reina-Marie Loader eo tlhakisetso ya hae ‘Horn’ e fumaneng dithoholetso, ho kenyeletsa ho kgethwa bakeng sa Dikgau tsa Paballo ya Ditshukudu tsa 2015 ka Phupu mokgahlelong wa kgau ya Temoso, Thuto le Merero ya Ditjhelete e Hlwahlwa ka ho Fetisisa, le ho hapa kgau bakeng sa Filimi e Hlwahlwa ka ho Fetisisa ya Paballo ya Tlhaho ho Mokete wa Difilimi tsa Matjhaba wa 2015 New York City, ho la Amerika.

src: Cabinet extends its condolences to the government of New Zealand , family, friends and the New Zealand Rugby Union on the loss of the rugby superstar, Jonah Tali Lomu, who has made a huge impact on the game.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisa matshediso a yona ho lelapa le metswalle ya Motlatsi wa Letona la Metsi le Tsamaiso ya Dikgwerekgwere, Ms Pamela Tshwete, ka ho lahlehelwa ke mme wa hae, Mama Ruth Nomzi Zondeki.

src: AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: DithonyoDithonyo kaofela di tla lokelwa ke ho netefatswa ha mangolo a thuto le tumello e amehang.

src: Extension of the Contract for five years of Mr Maswahle Diphofa – Director-General (DG): Department of Public Service and Administration.
tgt: Katoloso ya Konteraka bakeng sa dilemo tse hlano ya Monghadi Maswahle Diphofa – Motsamaisi Kakaretso (DG): Lefapha la Tshebeletso le Tsamaiso ya Setjhaba.

src: Extension of the Contract for twelve months of Ms Nonkululeko Sindane – DG: Department of Justice and Constitutional Development.
tgt: Katoloso ya Konteraka bakeng sa dikgwedi tse leshome le metso e mmedi ya Mofumahadi Nonkululeko Sindane – DG: Lefapha la Toka le Ntshetsopele ya Molaotheo.

src: Mr Livhuwani Tommy Makhode as the Deputy DG: Institutional Planning and Support in the Department of Science and Technology.
tgt: Monghadi Livhuwani Tommy Makhode jwaloka Motlatsi wa Motsamaisi Kakaretso (DDG): Meralo ya Ditheo le Tshehetso ka hara Lefapha la Saense le Thekenoloji.

src: Mr Rory Gallocher as the Chief Executive Officer of the Social Housing Regulatory Authority.
tgt: Monghadi Rory Gallocher jwaloka Mohlanka e Moholo wa Phethahatso (CEO) wa Bolaodi ba Taolo ya Matlo a Kahisano.

src: Dr Pradish Rampersadh as the new Executive Director for the South African Council for Natural Scientific Profssions.
tgt: Ngaka Pradish Rampersadh jwaloka Molaodi wa Phethahatso e motjha bakeng sa Lekgotla la Aforika Borwa la Diporofeshene tsa Saense ya Tlhaho.

src: Mr Mark Barnes as the Group Chief Executive Officer of the South African Post Office.
tgt: Monghadi Mark Barnes jwaloka CEO wa Sehlopha sa Kantoro ya Poso ya Aforika Borwa.

src: Board of the Development Bank of Southern Africa:i. Mr Jabulani Philip Moleketi – (re-appointment and Chairperson)ii.
tgt: Boto ya Banka ya Ntshetsopele ya Aforika e Borwa:i. Monghadi Jabulani Philip Moleketi – (o thontswe hape e le Modulasetulo)ii.

src: Mr Msokoli Frans Baleni – (re-appointment and Deputy Chairperson)iii.
tgt: Monghadi Msokoli Frans Baleni – (o thontswe hape e le Motlatsi wa Modulasetulo)iii.

src: Ms Martie Janse van Rensburg – (Non-Executive Director)iv.
