tgt: Mofumahadi Martie Janse van Rensburg – (Molaodi eo e seng wa Phethahatso)iv.

src: Implementation of key government programmes.
tgt: Ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha mananeo a bohlokwa a mmuso.

src: Cabinet welcomed the signing of 26 agreements to the value of R94 billion during the recent State Visit by Chinese President Xi Jinping.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetswe ho saenwa ha ditumellano tse 26 tsa boleng ba R94 bilione nakong ya Leeto la Puso la haufinyane tjena la Moporesidente wa China Xi Jinping.

src: The signed agreements included R12 billion to build a car-manufacturing plant in South Africa, a US$500 million loan facility to Eskom for infrastructure development and a US$2.5 billion funding guarantee for Transnet from the China Development Bank.
tgt: Ditumellano tse saennweng di kenyeleditse R12 bilione bakeng sa ho aha polante ya tlhahiso ya makoloi ka hara Aforika Borwa, thuso ya kadimo ya US$500 milione ho Eskom bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya meralo wa motheo le tiisetso ya thuso ya ditjhelete ya US$2.5 bilione bakeng sa Transnet ho tswa ho Banka ya Ntshetsopele ya China.

src: As part of the 2nd Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC), President Xi Jinping pledged US$60 billion for development in Africa.
tgt: Jwaloka karolo ya Foramo ya bo-2 e mabapi le Tshebedisano-mmoho ya China-Aforika (FOCAC), Moporesidente Xi Jinping o entse boitlamo ba US$60 bilione bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya Aforika.

src: The adoption of a new Declaration and Plan of Action (2016-2018) at FOCAC consolidates the growing mutual partnership between Africa and China, which will unlock new trade and investment opportunities to help stimulate economic growth.
tgt: Kamohelo ya Tumellano le Moralo wa Tshebetso wa (2016-2018) ho FOCAC o matlafatsa bosemphato bo ntseng bo hola ba kutlwano pakeng tsa Aforika le China, bo tla bula menyetla e metjha ya kgwebisano le matsete bakeng sa ho rotetsa kgolo ya moruo.

src: The economy further received an economic boost with South Africa’s BMW Group announcing an investment of R6 billion at its plant in Rosslyn, Pretoria, which bears testament to the important partnership that exists between business and government, and the role that business is playing in the development of the economy.
tgt: Moruo o boetse o fumane matlafatso ya moruo ka tsebiso ya Mokgatlo wa BMW wa Aforika Borwa ya matsete a R6 bilione polanteng ya ona e Rosslyn, ho la Pretoria, e leng bopaki ba semphato sa bohlokwa se teng pakeng tsa dikgwebo le mmuso, le karolo e bapalwang ke dikgwebo ntshetsopeleng ya moruo.

src: On Tuesday, 8 December, President Zuma bestowed National Orders to South African citizens and eminent foreign nationals who have contributed to the upliftment of humanity.
tgt: Ka Labobedi la, 8 Tshitwe, Moporesidente Zuma o abile Ditlotlo tsa Naha ho baahi ba Aforika Borwa le melata e hlahelletseng ka mahetla ba nyehetseng bakeng sa matlafatso ya batho.

src: The National Orders are a moment of great reflection, celebration and pride for our people.
tgt: Ditlotlo tsa Naha ke motsotso wa ho sheba morao ho matla, ho keteka le ho ba motlotlo ka batho ba rona.

src: They celebrate human achievement, human sacrifice and human endeavours that make our country a better place.
tgt: Di keteka phihlello ya botho, ho intsha sehlabelo ha botho le maiteko a botho tse etsang hore naha ya rona e be tulo e betere.

src: We salute the recipients of the 2015 National Orders.
tgt: Re hlompha baamohedi ba Ditlotlo tsa Naha ba 2015.

src: Cabinet appeals to all South Africans to use water sparingly.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa kaofela ho sebedisa metsi ka paballo.

src: This is in support of a number of measures taken to alleviate the water shortages, which have been exacerbated by the heatwave the country has experienced in the past weeks.
tgt: Sena ke bakeng sa ho tshehetsa mekgwa e nkuweng bakeng sa ho fedisa dikgaello tsa metsi, tse mpefaditsweng ke leqhubu la motjheso le fihlelletsweng ke naha dibekeng tse fetileng.

src: Whilst the recent rainfalls in some parts of the country provided some relief, the country’s water shortage remains a real challenge and requires all of us to use water sparingly and responsibly.
tgt: Ha dipula tsa moraorao tjena dikarolong tse ding tsa naha di fane ka kimoloho e itseng, kgaello ya metsi ya naha e dula e le phephetso mme e batla hore bohle re sebedise metsi ka paballo le ka boikarabelo.

src: Cabinet expressed its appreciation to all South Africans for participating in this year’s 16 Days of Activism for No Violence against Women and Children campaign, which ended yesterday.
tgt: Kabinete e hlahisitse kananelo ya yona ho maAforika Borwa kaofela bakeng sa ho nka karolo ho letsholo la Matsatsi a 16 la Thibelo ya Merusu Kgahlanong le Basadi le Bana la selemong sena, le neng le fela ka la 10 Tshitwe 2015.

src: Recent research indicates high numbers of new HIV infections, particularly among young women and girls in Africa between 15 and 24 years of age.
tgt: Diphuphutso tsa moraorao di bontsha dipalo tse phahameng tsa ditshwaetso tse ntjha tsa HIV, haholoholo ka hara basadi ba batjha le banana ka hara Aforika ba mahareng a dilemo tse 15 le tse 24.MaAforika Borwa a kgothaletswa ho tswela pele ka tshebetso ya twantsho ena letsatsi ka leng jwaloka karolo ya ho ba le kgahlanong le Merusu ho Basadi le Bana ya #365 Days Campaign le ya #CountMeIn le tla tswela pele ho phatlalla le selemo se tlang.

src: South Africans are encouraged to take forward their activism into everyday action as part of the #365 Days Campaign of No Violence Against Women and Children and the #CountMeIn campaign that unfolds throughout the year ahead.
tgt: Ka ho sebedisa #365 Days Campaign le #CountMeIn, naha e hloka ho tswela pele ho ngoka ditho tsa setjhaba, haholoholo banna, hore ba kopanye matsoho le mmuso bakeng sa ho sebetsana le koduwa WEBTOKEN boikarabelo ba setjhaba, bobedi ka bonngwe le ka kopanelo, ho kgina ho ata ha kokwanahloko ka ho ela hloko bophelo ba rona bo botle le ba ba bang.

src: Through the #365 Days Campaign and #CountMeIn, the country needs to continue mobilising members of society, especially men, to join hands with government in dealing with this scourge.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse kgatelopele e seng e entswe ke Lekgotla la Diphuputso tsa Saense le Indaseteri bakeng sa ho ntshetsapele tsamaiso ya tlhahiso ya tsa tlhaho ya masole a lwantshang HIV.

src: This brings the health industry a step closer to an economically viable preventative treatment.
tgt: Sena se tlisa indaseteri ya kalafo haufi le pheko ya thibelo e sa bitsing tjhelete e ngata.

src: Whilst the country still struggles to find the cure for HIV and AIDS, South Africans are still expected to practice safe sex and observe the ABC (Abstain, Be faithful and Condomise) principles of preventing new infections.
tgt: Ha naha e ntse e sokola ho fumana pheko ya HIV le AIDS, maAforika Borwa a ntse a lebeletswe ho etsa thobalano e bolokehileng le ho tsitlallela dipehelo tsa ABC (Abstain, Be faithful and Condomise) bakeng sa ho thibela ditshwaetso tse ntjha.

src: Cabinet commends all learners, students, teachers, lecturers, schools and institutions of higher learning on concluding a successful academic year, despite the challenges experienced during the year.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa kaofela baithuti, barutwana, matitjhere, barupelli, le dikolo le ditheo tsa thuto e phahameng ka ho phethela selemo se atlehileng sa dithuto, ho sa natswe diphephetso tse fihlelletsweng hara selemo.

src: Cabinet also wishes those who agreed to postpone examinations rescheduled for 2016 well in their coming examinations.
tgt: Kabinete hape e lakaletsa tse molemo ditlhatlhobong tse tlang tsa 2016 ho ba dumetseng hore ditlhatlhobo di tjhetjhiswe.

src: The Department of Social Development, in collaboration with Department of Defense and National Youth Development Agency, will hold its 6th National Youth Camp.
tgt: Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba, ka tshebedisano-mmoho le Lefapha la Tshireletso le Lekala la Naha la Ntshetsopele ya Batjha (NYDA), le tla tshwara Kampo ya Batjha ya bo-6.

src: This is a youth leadership development programme that seeks to change behaviour, attitudes and empower the youth about opportunities at their disposal.
tgt: Sena ke lenaneo la ntshetsopele ya boetapele ba batjha le rerileng ho fetola boitshwaro, mmono wa bophelo le ho matlafatsa batjha ka menyetla e teng eo ba ka e tholang.

src: The camp also assists with mentoring and teaching young boys to grow into men who value and respect women.
tgt: Kampo e thusa hape ka ho lekola le ho ruta bashemane ba batjha ho hola hore e be banna ba ananelang le ho hlompha basadi.

src: A joint agreement signed between the Minister of Higher Education and Training Minister, Dr Blade Nzimande, and BRICS partners – Brazil, Russia, India and China – is aimed at developing a framework for future cooperation in education.
tgt: Tumellano e saenetsweng ka kopanelo pakeng tsa Letona la Thuto e Phahameng le Thupello, Ngaka Blade Nzimande, le bomphato ba BRICS – Brazil, Russia, India le China – e reretswe ho ntshetsapele moralo bakeng sa tshebedisano ya bokamoso thutong.

src: The agreement covers general education, educational policy strategy, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) colleges and higher education.
tgt: Tumellano e akaretsa thuto ya kakaretso, lewa la leano la thuto, Dikoletjhe tsa Thuto le Thupello ya Tekginiki le Mesebetsi (TVET) le thuto e phahameng.

src: TVET colleges hold the potential to unlock economic opportunities for our young people, while addressing the challenges of unemployment, inequality and poverty affecting communities.
tgt: Dikoletjhe tsa TVET di na le bokgoni ba ho bula menyetla ya moruo bakeng sa batho ba batjha, ha ho ntse ho sebetsanwa le diphephetso tsa tlhokeho ya mesebetsi, ho se lekalekane, le bofuma bo amang badudi.

src: The agreement, which will improve the quality of teaching and teachers’ education, also commits BRICS universities to support joint research projects, encourage collaborative programmes at postgraduate, doctoral and postdoctoral levels and the co-publishing of scientific results.
tgt: Tumellano ena, e tla ntlafatsa boleng ba thuto le thuto ya matitjhere, hape e tlama diyunivesithi tsa BRICS ho tshehetsa diporojeke tse kopanetsweng tsa diphuputso, ho kgothaletsa mananeo a tshebedisano-mmoho maemong a dithuto tsa kamora yunivesithi, a bongaka le a dithuto tsa kamora bongaka le ho phatlalatsa mmoho diphetho tsa merero ya tsa saense.

src: The Department of Science and Technology hosted the Science Forum South Africa under the theme “Igniting conversations about science”.
tgt: Lefapha la Saense le Thekenoloji le ne le tshwere Foramo ya Saense ya Aforika Borwa tlasa mookotaba “Re hotetsa dipuisano ka saense”.

src: Over 45 countries participated in debates on the interface between science, technology and innovation and society, specifically in the context of development.
tgt: Dinaha tse fetang 45 di ile tsa kenela dingangisano tse mabapi le tshebedisano mahareng a saense, thekenoloji le ntlafatso le setjhaba, haholoholo ntlheng ya ntshetsopele.

src: The forum also served to strengthen South Africa’s strategic international science, technology and innovation partnerships.
tgt: Foramo hape e sebeditse bakeng sa ho matlafatsa lewa la saense, thekenoloji le semphato sa ntjhafatso la matjhaba la Aforika Borwa.

src: South Africa will be represented in the Council of International Maritime Organisation.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tla emelwa ho Lekgotla la Matjhaba la Mokgatlo wa Mawatle.

src: This is a major step towards realising the country and the continent’s potential in the maritime sector.
tgt: Sena ke mohato wa bohlokwa ho isa moo re tla bonang bokgoni ba naha le kontinente lekaleng la tsa mawatle.

src: The organisation is responsible for adopting decisions on global maritime affairs, ranging from the Oceans Economy, rescue initiatives and safety and security matters at sea.
tgt: Mokgatlo ona o ikarabella bakeng sa ho amohela diqeto tse mabapi le merero ya lefatshe ya tsa mawatle, ho tloha ho Moruo wa Mawatle, boikitlaetso ba pholoso le mabaka a polokeho le tshireletso lewatleng.

src: The participation in this body will support government’s programme of unlocking the country’s maritime potential through the Blue Oceans Economy Strategy and Operation Phakisa, which aims to create over one million jobs by 2033.
tgt: Bonkakarolo setheong sena bo tla tshehetsa lenaneo la mmuso la ho bula bokgoni ba naha ka Lewa la Moruo wa Mawatle le Operation Phakisa, tse rerileng ho hlahisa mesebetsi e fetang milione ka 2033.‎.

src: The South African National Defence Force commenced in the past week a process to upgrade Salisbury Island Naval Station in Durban into a fully functional naval base.
tgt: Lebotho la Naha la Aforika Borwa le qadile ka tsamaiso ya ho hlabolla Seteishene sa Sehlekehleke sa Lebotho la Lewatle sa Salisbury se Durban ho ba kampo ya lebotho la lewatle e sebetsang ka botlalo.

src: The upgrading of facilities will improve defence capabilities and also contribute towards the ocean economy.
tgt: Thlabollo ya dibaka tsena e tla ntlafatsa bokgoni ba tshireletso le ho nyehela bakeng sa moruo wa mawatle.

src: The Department of Health, in partnership with Soul City and Times Media, launched a dedicated health and lifestyle channel The Good Life Network on DStv channel 199.
tgt: Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle, ka kopanelo le Soul City le Times Media, le thakgotse kanale e reretsweng tsa bophelo bo botle le mokgwa wa bophelo ya Good Life Network ho DStv kanaleng ya 199.

src: The channel offers diverse, entertaining and original home-grown content on nutrition, health and fitness, human rights, youth sexuality, HIV and TB, as well as consumer and gender rights.
tgt: Kanale ena e fana ka dikateng tse fapafapaneng, tse thabisang le ho ba tse hlahisitsweng lapeng mabapi le phepo, bophelo bo botle le ho kwena, ditokelo tsa botho, tsa motabo ho batjha, HIV le TB, mmoho le ditokelo tsa bareki le tsa bong.

src: Cabinet calls on South Africans to watch the channel.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ho boha kanale ena.

src: Key Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the White Paper on the National Health Insurance (NHI) for South Africa, for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho phatlalatswa ha Pampiri e Tshweu ya Inshorense ya Naha ya Bophelo bo Botle (NHI) ya Aforika Borwa, hore setjhaba se tshwaele.

src: The NHI is part of government’s major health sector reforms.
tgt: NHI ke karolo ya mmuso ya ho etsa diphetho tse kgolo ho tsa kalafo.

src: The policy proposes government’s ability to offer medical services to all who visit its health facilities.
tgt: Leano lena le sisinya bokgoni ba mmuso ba ho fana ka ditshebeletso tsa bongaka ho bohle ba etelang dikaho tsa kalafo.

src: It will be funded through a central fund that will also be made available to private medical practitioners who want to participate in the scheme.
tgt: Le tla tshehetswa ka ditjhelete ka letlole la bohareng leo hape le tla ba teng ho dingaka tsa poraefete tse batlang ho nka karolo sekemeng sena.

src: Once finalised, the policy will be phased in over the years and focus mainly on commencing in underserviced areas.
tgt: Hang ha ho se ho phethetswe tsohle, leano le tla kenngwa tshebetsong ho ya jwalo le dilemo le ho tsepamisa maikutlo haholo hore le qale dibakeng tse fumanang ditshebeletso tse nyane.

src: The Minister of Health, Dr Aaron Motsoaledi, will today brief the media on the roll-out of the NHCabinet approved the National Integrated Early Childhood Development (ECD) Policy.
tgt: Letona la Bophelo bo Botle, Ngaka Aaron Motsoaledi, kajeno le tla tsebisa boraditaba ka phano ya NHKabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Leano le Kopanetsweng la Naha la Ntshetsopele ya Thuto ya Qalo ya Bana (ECD).Leano lena le hlahisitswe ka ditherisano le bankakarolo ba fapafapaneng ka hara lekala lena.

src: This integrated ECD policy will ensure all young children and their caregivers are able to access comprehensive quality ECD services from conception to Grade The policy extends the service to eight-year-old children with developmental difficulties.
tgt: Le ile la sekasekwa ka ditherisano le setjhaba ka Tlhakola 2015.Leano le kopanetsweng la ECD le tla netefatsa hore bana bohle ba banyenyane le bahlokomedi ba bona ba kgona ho fihlella ditshebeletso tse pharalletseng tsa ECD ho tloha tswalong ho fihla ho Kereiti ya Leano lena le atolosetsa tshebeletso ho bana ba dilemo tse robedi ba nang le mathata a kgolo.

src: The policy further provides a monitoring and evaluation framework to ensure it is effectively implemented to all children irrespective of race, gender or religion.
tgt: Leano ho ya pele le fana ka moralo wa peho leihlo le tekolo ho netefatsa hore le kenngwa tshebetsong ka bokgabane ho banabohle ho sa kgathallwe morabe, bong kapa bodumedi.

src: Cabinet has approved the White Paper on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and its Implementation Matrix.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Pampiri e Tshweu ya Ditokelo tsa Batho ba phelang ka Boqhwala le Moralo wa ho kenngwa tshebetsong.

src: This is aligned to the disability-inclusive Sustainable Development Goals, adopted by the United Nations (UN) General Assembly (UNGA) in September 2015.
tgt: Sena se matahantswe ho Merero ya Ntshetsopele ya Moshwelella e kenyeletsang ya boqhwala, e amohetsweng ke Kopano Kakaretso (UNGA) ya Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) ka Loetse 2015.Leano le tla akofisa diphethoho le ditokiso tse mabapi le kenyeletso e tletseng, kopanelo le tekatekano bakeng sa batho ba phelang ka boqhwala.

src: The policy will accelerate transformation and redress regarding full inclusion, integration and equality for persons with disabilities.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana phatlalatso ya Leano la Naha la Dikgwerekgwere bakeng sa tshwaelo ya setjhaba.

src: The policy places the well-being of people at the centre of development by striking a balance between allocating financial resources to support investments in higher levels of service, providing services to underserved households, while also maintaining and refurbishing existing sanitation infrastructure.
tgt: Leano lena le beha ho phela hantle ha setjhaba bohareng ba ntshetsopele ka ho tlisa botsitso mahareng a ho aba mehlodi ya ditjhelete bakeng sa ho tshehetsa matsete ho tshebeletso e phahameng, phano ya ditshebeletso ho malapa a sa sebeletsweng hantle, ha ka nqa e nngwe ho baballwa le ho ntlafatsa meralo ya motheo e ntseng e le teng.

src: Cabinet approved for the submission to Parliament of South Africa’s 5th Periodic Report (2009-2014) on the Implementation of the Convention on the Elimination of all Forms of Discrimination against Women.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana bakeng sa ho kenngwa Palamenteng ha Tlaleho ya Dinako tse itseng ya bo-5 ya Aforika Borwa (2009-2014) ya ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Khonvenshene e mabapi le Phediso ya Mefuta yohle ya Kgethollo kgahlanong le Basadi.

src: The report provides an overview on the effectiveness of the range of laws, policies and programmes implemented and highlights the country’s achievements on women’s empowerment and gender equality.
tgt: Tlaleho ena e fana ka kakaretso ya bohlwahlwa ba letoto la melao, maano le mananeo a kentsweng tshebetsong le ho hlakisa diphihlello tsa naha mabapi le matlafatso ya basadi le tekatekano ya bong.

src: The report also recognises that there are persistent challenges and barriers to overcoming inequality and discrimination in the country.
tgt: Tlaleho hape e ananela hore ho na le diphephetso le ditshita tse ntseng di le teng bakeng sa ho hlola ho se lekalekane le kgethollo ka hara naha.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the Draft National Action Plan to Combat Racism, Racial Discrimination, Xenophobia and Related Intolerance, for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana phatlalatso ya Moralo wa Naha wa Tshebetso bakeng sa ho Lwantsha Bomorabe, Kgethollo ya Merabe, Lehloyo la Melata le ho hloka mamellano, bakeng sa hore setjhaba se tshwaele.

src: The plan is an integrated and systematic national strategy aimed at combating racism and building a truly non-racist and non-sexist democratic South WEBTOKEN provides a framework for sustained and coordinated measures to be undertaken by the country as a whole to deal with the legacy of racism and racial discrimination.
tgt: Moralo ona ke lewa le kopanetsweng le ho hlohlomiswa ka morero wa ho lwantsha bomorabe le ho aha Aforika Borwa ya demokerasi ya nnete e hlokang bomorabe le kgethollo ka bong.

src: This assists South Africa to meet its international, regional and national obligations, specifically the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action adopted by the UN at the World Conference against Racism in 2001.
tgt: E fana ka moralo bakeng sa mekgwa ya moshwelella o hokahantsweng o lokelang ho etswa ke naha ka bophara ho sebetsana le lefa la bomorabe le kgethollo ya merabe.

src: Cabinet was briefed on progress made on the digital migration programme.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka kgatatelopele e seng e entswe mabapi le lenaneo la ho fallela ho mokgwa wa dijithale.

src: It approved the commencement of the dual-illumination period for the digital broadcasting signal in South Africa on 1 February 2016.
tgt: E tjhaelletse monwna qalo ya nako ya ho kgantshwa habedi ha tumello ya kgaso ya dijithale ka hara Aforika Borwa ka la 1 Tlhakola 2016.Ho falla ho tloha ho ditshebeletso tsa kgaso tsa analoko ho ya ho tsa kgaso ya dijithale ho lokolla mokgwa o batlehang haholo wa maqhubu a radio a loketseng bakeng sa phano ya ditshebeletso tsa kgaso tse phatlaletseng.

src: The migration from analogue to digital broadcasting services releases the much-needed radio frequency spectrum suitable for the provision of mobile broadband services.
tgt: Sena se tla eketsa bophehisani ba moruo wa Aforika Borwa ka ho tsoseletsa indaseteri ya kgaso, ho matlafatsa diindaseteri tse hlahisang disebediswa tsa elektroniki, ho hlahisa mesebetsi, le ho ntshetsapele dikateng tsa kgaso tsa lehae le tse fapafapaneng.

src: This will increase the competitiveness of the South African economy by revitalising the broadcasting industry, strengthening the electronics manufacturing industry, creating jobs, and developing more local and diverse broadcast content.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka diphihlello tsa Tlaleho ya Matshwao a Ntlafatso ya Aforika Borwa ya Saense le Thekenoloji ya 2014 tse ntseng di etsahala tshebetsong ya Tshebeletso ya Naha ya Ntlafatso (NSI), e hlahiswang selemo ka seng ke Lekgotla la Naha la Boeletsi ka Ntlafatso.

src: Cabinet was briefed on the findings of the 2014 South African Science, Technology and Innovation Indicators Report and the trends in the performance of the National System of Innovation (NSI), produced annually by the National Advisory Council on Innovation.
tgt: Tlaleho e sebedisa matshwao a hlokolosi bakeng sa ho lekola tshebetso le nyehelo ya NSI ho dintlha tse ka sehloohong tsa naha jwaloka ha di hlahisitswe ho Morero wa Naha wa Ntshetsopele (NDP) le ditokomaneng tse ding tsa leano tse nyehelang ho ntshetsopele ya moruo wa kahisano.

src: The report uses critical indicators to assess the performance and contribution of the NSI to key national priorities articulated in the National Development Plan (NDP) and other policy documents which contribute to socio-economic development.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho hlophiswa botjha ha ditereke tsa bomakgiseterata bakeng sa Limpopo le Mpumalanga, le ho theha Lekgotla la Dinyewe la Makgiseterata la Lephalale jwaloka tulo ya Karolo ya Lekgotla le Phahameng la Limpopo, jwaloka mokgwa wa nakwana ho fihlela ho ahuwa Karolo ya tulo ya moshwelella sebakeng seo.

src: Cabinet approved the rationalisation of magisterial districts for Limpopo and Mpumalanga, and the designation of the Lephalale Magistrate’s Court as a local seat of the Limpopo Division of the High Court, as an interim measure until a separate permanent local seat of the Division is built in the area.
tgt: Ho hlophiswa botjha ha ditereke tsa bomakgiseterata le dibaka tsa tshebetso tsa Dikarolo tsa Lekgotla le Phahameng la Dinyewe ke karolo ya ho fetola maano ka morero wa lokisa botjha lefa la ho hloka toka la mehleng la ho aha dibaka tsa bodulo.

src: The rationalisation of magisterial districts and areas of jurisdiction of the Divisions of the High Court is part of the policy reform aimed at redressing the legacy of spatial injustices of the past.
tgt: Hape ke karolo ya tshwanelo ya diphethoho tse pharaletseng bakeng sa ho matlafatsa phumantsho ya toka, e matahantsweng le Molaotheo wa Aforika Borwa wa 1996.

src: It is also part of the broader transformation imperative to enhance access to justice, which is aligned to the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana tlaleho ya kgatelopele mabapi le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha ditaelo tsa Kabinete Limpopo ho ya ka Karolo ya 100 (1)

src: Cabinet approved the withdrawal of Section 100 (1)
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho hulwa ha Karolo 100 (1)

src: by 31 March 2016 in the following Limpopo provincial departments: Health Transport Public Works Roads and Infrastructure and Treasury.
tgt: ka 31 Tlhakubele 2016 mafapheng a porofense a Limpopo a latelang: Bophelo bo Botle Dipalangwang Mesebetsi ya Setjhaba Ditsela le Meralo ya motheo le la Matlotlo.

src: Cabinet also approved the conditional withdrawal of Section 100 (1)
tgt: Kabinete hape e tjhaelletse monwana ho hulwa ntle le dipehelo ha Karolo 100 (1)

src: in Education to pave the way for the Provincial Treasury to effectively implement Section 18 of the Public Finance Management Act, 1999 (Act 1 of 1999) in the Limpopo Department of Education, with support from national government.
tgt: ho Lefapha la Thuto bakeng sa ho betla tsela bakeng sa lefapha la Matlotlo la Porofense ho kenya tshebetsong ka bokgabane Karolo 18 ya Molao wa Bolaodi ba Ditjhelete tsa Setjhaba, 1999 (Molao 1 wa 1999) ho Lefapha la Thuto la Limpopo, ka tshehetso e tswang ho mmuso wa naha.

src: Cabinet approved the following directives to the Premier and the MECs for Finance and of Education:a) Capacitating the provincial departments by recruiting competent personnelb) Finalising the appointment of senior management positions andc) Dealing decisively with leadership failure and corruption.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ditaelo tse latelang ho Tonakgolo le diMEC tsa Ditjhelete le Thuto:a) Matlafatso ya mafapha a porofense ka ho thaotha basebeletsi ba hlwahlwab) Ho phethela ho thonngwa ha batho bakeng sa mesebetsi ya batsamaisi ba ka sehloohong lec) Ho sebetsana ka matla le ho hloleha ha boetapele le bobodu.

src: Cabinet approved for South Africa to host the high level Anti-Drugs Dialogue Conference from 11 to 12 March 2016, which will be under the auspices of the African Union.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana hore Aforika Borwa e tshware Khonferense ya Dipuisano tse Kgahlanong le Dithethefatsi ya maemo a hodimo ho tloha ka la 11 ho isa ka la 12 Tlhakubele 2016, e tla ba tlasa bolaodi ba Kopano ya Aforika.

src: This serves as a follow-up session of the Russia-Africa Anti-Drugs Dialogue, which aims to present a consolidated position regarding countering the world drug problem.
tgt: Sena se sebetsa jwaloka kopano ya ho tswellisa Dipuisano tse Kgahlanong le Dithethefatsi tsa Russia le Aforika, ka morero wa ho fana maemo a kopanetsweng mabapi le ho lwantsha bothata ba lefatshe ba dithethefatsi.

src: This will be tabled at the UNGA Special Session in April 2016.
tgt: Sena se tla tekwa ho Kopano e Ikgethang ya UNGA ka Mmesa 2016.Ntwa kgahlanong le dithethefatsi tse seng molaong e tsamaellana le NDP mme Dipuisano di tla fana ka lepatlelo la ho tswela pele ho matlafatsa Moralo Wa Naha o ka Sehloohong wa Dithethefatsi wa (2013-2017).

src: The fight against illicit drugs is in line with the NDP and the Dialogue will provide a platform to further enhance the National Drug Master Plan (2013-2017).
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana hore Lefapha la Bodulo ba Batho le tshware mmoho le Lenaneo la UN la Bodulo ba Batho Khonferense ya “Re etella pele Diphethoho ka hara Motsemoholo: Ho tloha Bodulong bo Bohlaswa ho ya ho Bodulo ba Batho bo kenyeletsang, bo bolokehileng, bo Hlwahlwa le ba Moshwelella”, ka Tlhakubele 2016.Khonferense e tshehetsa ka bobedi lenaneo la matjhaba la ntshetsopele le la ntshetsopele ya lehae ka ho matlafatsa tshehetso bakeng sa Morero 11 wa Merero ya Ntshetsopele ya Moshwelella: Ho etsa metsemeholo le bodulo ba batho hore e be e kenyeletsang, e bolokehileng, e hlwahlwa le ho ba ya moshwelella.

src: Cabinet approved for the Department of Human Settlements to co-host the “Leading Change in the City: From Slums to Inclusive, Safe, Resilient and Sustainable Human Settlements” Conference with the UN Human Settlements Programme, in March 2016.The conference supports both the international development agenda and the domestic development agenda by strengthening support for Goal 11 of the Sustainable Development Goals: Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable.
tgt: Khonferense e etsa karolo ya dipuisano tse mabapi le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Lenaneo la Ntshetsopele la UN la kamora 2015 le “Lenaneo le Letjha la Metse ya Ditoropo” le tla amohelwa ke UN ka 2016.

src: Cabinet approved for the Agricultural Research Council to host the 3rd Global Conference on Agricultural Research for Development in April 2016.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana hore Lekgotla la Diphuputso tsa Temo le tshware Khonferense ya bo-3 ya Lefatshe ya Diphuputso tsa Temo bakeng sa Ntshetsopele ka Mmesa 2016.

src: The conference will identify: international research and innovation priorities as well as needs in national innovation systems so as to achieve future development goals, in particular for family farmers and poor communities.
tgt: Khonferense e tla hlwaya: dintlha tse ka sehloohong tsa diphuputso tsa matjhaba le tsamaiso ya ntlafatso hore ho tle ho fihlellwe merero ya ntshetsopelo ya bokamoso, haholoholo ho borapolasi ba malapa le metseng e futsanehileng.

src: Bills.
tgt: Dibili.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the Marine Spatial Planning Bill of 2015 for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana phatlalatso ya Bili ya Meralo ya Tlhophiso ya Mawatleng ya 2015 bakeng sa hore setjhaba se tshwaele.

src: The Bill provides a legal framework to unlock ocean economic potential by promoting cooperative spatial planning.
tgt: Bili e fana ka moralo wa semolao wa ho bula bokgoni ba moruo wa Mawatle ka ho kgothaletsa moralo o kopanetsweng.

src: The Bill will assist the already existing Operation Phakisa institutional structures.
tgt: Bili e tla thusa dibopeho tsa dikaho tse teng tsa Operation Phakisa.

src: It seeks to promote collaboration and responsible ocean governance arrangement.
tgt: E batla ho kgothaletsa tshebedisano le taolo ya tlhophiso e nang le boikarabelo ya mawatle.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: President Zuma will lead the country’s Reconciliation Day celebration on 16 December in Port Elizabeth, Eastern Cape under the theme: “Bridging the divide: Building a common South African nationhood towards a national developmental state”.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla etella pele mekete ya Letsatsi la Poelano ka la 16 December Port Elizabeth, ho la Kapa Botjhabela tlasa mookotaba: “Re ngotla karohano: Re aha bosetjhaba ba Aforika Borwa bo tshwanang ho ya ho puso ya naha e tswelang pele”.

src: The Minister of Telecommunications and Postal Services, Dr Siyabonga Cwele, will lead the South African delegation at the UNGA on the World Summit on the Information Society (WSIS) from 15 to 16 December 2015, where South Africa’s country position, contributing to the WSIS+10 Non-Paper will be presented.
tgt: Letona la Dikgokahanyo tsa Mehala le Ditshebeletso tsa Poso, Ngaka Siyabonga Cwele, o tla etelle pele kemedi ya Aforika Borwa ho UNGA mabapi le Seboka sa Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Tlhahisoleseding (WSIS) ho tloha ka la 15 ho isa ka la 16 Tshitwe 2015, moo maemo a Aforika Borwa a naha, a nyehelang ho WSIS+10 a tla hlahiswa ka ntle le Pampiri.

src: Cabinet’s position on key issues in the environment South Africa successfully hosted the 7th Africities Summit of cities and local governments of Africa in Johannesburg from 29 November to 3 December 2015.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tshwere ka katleho Seboka sa bo-7 sa Africities sa metsemeholo le mebuso ya lehae ya Aforika Johannesburg ho tloha ka la 29 Pudungwana ho isa ka la 3 Tshitwe 2015.

src: Under the theme: “Shaping the future of Africa with the people: the contribution of African local authorities to agenda 2063 of the African Union”, the summit, which attracted 15 000 mayors and 500 000 councilors, is one of the most concrete initiatives for building African unity.
tgt: Tlasa mookotaba: “Re bopa bokamoso ba Aforika le batho: nyehelo ya mebuso ya mahae ya Aforika ho lenaneo la 2063 la Kopano ya Aforika”, seboka sena, se hohetseng bomeyara ba 15 000 le makhanselara a 500 000, ke se seng sa boikitlaetso bo tiileng ba ho aha Kopano ya maAforika.

src: The summit focused on strengthening local government across the African continent, particularly financial management and establishing a secure revenue base, towards the attainment of Agenda 2063 – the Africa we want.
tgt: Seboka se ne se tsepamisitse maikutlo hodima ho matlafatsa mebuso ya lehae ho phatlalla le kontinente ya Aforika, haholoholo tsamaiso ya ditjhelete le ho theha motheo o tiileng wa lekeno, bakeng sa ho fihlella Lenaneo la 2063 – Aforika eo re e batlang.

src: The summit supports the goals of the NDP in which cities and local government play an important role in our overall development.
tgt: Seboka sena se tshehetsa merero ya NDP eo ho yona metsemeholo le mebuso ya mahae e bapalang karolo ya bohlokwa ntshetsopeleng ya rona ka kakaretso.

src: Cabinet remains confident that as negotiations unfold at the 21st session of the Conference of the Parties (COP21) to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), a fair and binding agreement will be reached.
tgt: Kabinete e dula e na le boitshepo ba hore ha ditherisano di ntse di tswela pele ho Tulo ya bo-21 ya Khonferense ya Mekga (COP21) ho Khonvenshene ya Meralo ya UN e mabapi le ho Fetofetoha ha Tlelaemete (UNFCCC), ho tla fihlellwa tumellano e hlokang leeme le e tlamang.

src: Climate change is a global problem requiring a global solution, which can only be effectively addressed multilaterally, under the broad-based legitimacy of the UNFCCC and with all parties making a contribution.
tgt: Ho fetofetoha ha tlelaemete ke bothata ba lefatshe bo batlang tharollo ya lefatshe, boo ho ka sebetsanwang le bona feela ka kopanelo, tlasa tumello e phatlaletseng ya UNFCCC mme le mekga kaofela e etsa nyehelo.

src: In South Africa, we can proudly say that we have put in place progressive, innovative and proactive policies, and plans to deal with an ever-changing climate.
tgt: Ka hara Aforika Borwa, re ka bua ka motlotlo hore re na le maano a tswetseng pele, a ntlafatsang le ho ba hlwahlwa, le meralo ya ho sebetsana le tlelaemete e dulang e fetofetoha.

src: These policies are guided by the overarching principle of sustainable development, which is the cornerstone of Vision 2030 as contained in the NDBeing the last Cabinet meeting for 2015, Cabinet extends its best wishes to all South Africans for the upcoming festive season.
tgt: Maano ana a tataiswa ke pehelo e akaretsang ya ntshetsopele ya moshwelella, e leng lejwe la motheo la Pono ya 2030 jwaloka ha e hlahella ho NDKa ha sena ke kopano ya ho qetela ya Kabinete bakeng sa 2015, Kabinete e fetisetsa ditakaletso tse molemo ho maAforika Borwa kaofela bakeng sa sehla sa mekete e tlang.

src: In the spirit of the season and in keeping with the spirit of Ubuntu, Cabinet calls on all South Africans to assist needy individuals and families in their community.
tgt: Ka moya wa sehla sena mme re ntse re imatahantse le moya wa Ubuntu, Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa kaofela ho thusa batho le malapa a hlokang ka hara metse ya bona.

src: We are a nation that cares for one another, respects each other and supports those who are less fortunate.
tgt: Re setjhaba se kgathallanang, se hlomphanang le ho tshehetsa ba seng lehlohonolo bophelong.

src: The coming New Year offers all of us the possibility to recommit ourselves to work for a better future for all.
tgt: Selemo se setjha se tlang se re tlela bohle ka kgonahalo ya hore re itlame botjha bakeng sa ho sebeletsa bokamoso bo betere bakeng sa bohle.

src: Cabinet extends its condolences and sympathies to the family and friends of Mohamed Ismail (“Issy”) Dinat, who passed on Tuesday, 8 December.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisetsa matshediso le kutlwelobohloko ho lelapa le metswalle ya Mohamed Ismail (“Issy”) Dinat, ya hlokahetseng ka Labobedi, la 8 Tshitwe.

src: His selflessness and involvement in the Struggle contributed to our freedom.
tgt: Ho itela ha hae le ho nka karolo Ntweng kgahlanong le kgethollo di nyehetse bakeng sa tokoloho ya rona.

src: Ms Thulisile Glory Manzini as DDG: Administration at the DTPIn conclusion, Cabinet extends its gratitude to those South Africans who complied by submitting their tax returns resulting in a total of 5.94 million tax returns received for non-provisional taxpayers.
tgt: Mofumahadi Thulisile Glory Manzini jwaloka DDG: Tsamaiso ho DTPS.

src: This is 11.52 per cent higher than in 2014, and the compliance for taxpayers filing on time exceeded 90 per cent for the third consecutive year.
tgt: Qetellong, Kabinete e fetisetsa teboho ya yona ho maAforika Borwa a imatahantseng le ho kenya ditokomane tsa ona tsa lekgetho tse bakileng ho kgutlisetswa kaofela ha ditokomane.

src: This high level of compliance enables government to deliver services that improve the quality of life of all its citizens.
tgt: Boemo bona bo hodima ba boimatahanyo bo thusa mmuso ho fana ka ditshebeletso tse ntlafatsang boleng ba bophelo ba baahi bohle ba ona.

src: During this festive period, government is implementing various campaigns which require all South Africans and visitors to play their part in ensuring that the festive period is enjoyed in a safe and secure environment.
tgt: Nakong ena ya ho keteka, mmuso o kenya tshebetsong matsholo a fapafapaneng a batlang hore maAforika Borwa kaofela le baeti ba bapale karolo ya bona ya ho netefatsa hore nako ya mekete e thabelwa ka hara tikoloho e bolokehileng le ho tshireletseha.

src: Cabinet calls on all to work with the South African Police Service and to report any criminal activities in our homes and communities.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho bohle ho sebetsa le Tshebeletso ya Sepolesa ya Aforika Borwa le ho tlaleha diketso dife kapa dife tsa botlokotsebe ka hara malapa a rona le ka hara setjhaba.

src: In order to accommodate the influx of cross-border travellers, all government departments at ports of entry will from 10 December 2015 to 14 January 2016 extend their operating hours.
tgt: Bakeng sa ho mekamekana le tshubuhlellano ya batsamai ba tshelang madiboho, mafapha kaofela a mmuso a sebetsanang le madiboho a tla atolosa dinako tsa ona tsa tshebetso ho tloha ka la 10 Tshitwe 2015 ho isa ka la 14 Pherekgong 2016.

src: These include Health, Agriculture, Police, Home Affairs and South African Revenue Service).
tgt: Ana a kenyeletsa la Bophelo bo Botle, Temo, Sepolesa, Merero ya Lehae le Tshebeletso ya Lekgetho ya Aforika Borwa).

src: Economy.
tgt: Moruo.

src: Cabinet met to deliberate on the state of the economy and budget related matters.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya kopana ho sekaseka maemo a moruo le dintlha tse amanang le ditekanyetso tsa ditjhelete.

src: Cabinet noted a number of factors impacting on the economy of the country.
tgt: Kabinete lemohile dintlha tse ngatanyana tse nang le kgahlamelo moruong wa naha.

src: The global outlook has deteriorated in recent months.
tgt: Tjhebahalo ya lefatshe e theohile dikgweding tse sa tswa feta moraorao tjena.

src: Slower global growth reflects, in particular, weaker performance and higher risks in several important developing countries, including China.
tgt: Kgolo e batlang e tsamaya butle ya moruo wa lefatshe e bontsha, ka ho qolleha, tshebetso e batlang e fokola le dikotsi tsa ho thefuleha ha moruo tse batlang di phahame ka hara dinaha tse itseng tse ntseng di tswela pele, ho kenyeletswa le China.

src: The welcomed recovery expected in the USA is likely to result in rising global interest rates.
tgt: Ho iphumana ho lemohilweng ho lebeletsweng ka hara Amerika ho ka nna ha baka ho phahama ha sekgahla sa tswala sa lefatshe.

src: Depressed trade volumes and turbulence in global capital markets underscore the need for nations to build resilience and act cautiously in the period ahead.
tgt: Methamo ya kgwebisano e tetebetseng le ho tsukutleha ho teng ka hara mebaraka ya lefatshe ya ditjhelete e hlakisa tlhokeho ya ho aha botsitso le ho sebetsa ka hloko bakeng sa nako ena eo re e tobileng ka pele ho rona.

src: Cabinet further noted that there were some benefits from the low price of crude oil.
tgt: Kabinete e boetse e lemohile hore ho ne ho na le melemo e itseng ho tswa ho theko e tlase ya oli e tala.

src: As a major commodity exporter, South Africa is concerned about the continued weakness in commodity prices.
tgt: Jwaloka moreki e moholo wa thepa e tswang mafatsheng a ka ntle, Aforika Borwa e ngongorehile ka ho fokola ho ntseng ho tswela dithekong tsa thepa.

src: Government continues to build on the country’s diverse economic structure, and export earnings continue to depend to a great extent on metals and semi processed raw materials.
tgt: Mmuso o tswelapele ho ahella hodima sebopeho sa naha se tswakatswakaneng sa moruo, mme kuno ya dihlahiswa tse romellwang dinaheng tsa ka ntle e tswela pele ho itshetleha haholo hodima ditshepe le thepa e tala e song ho lokiswe ka botlalo.

src: The fall in commodity prices is unlikely to reverse speedily.
tgt: Ho wa ha ditheko tsa thepa ha ho bonahale e le ntho e tla tjhetjhang ka potlako.

src: This will have sustained consequences for the South African economy and many of our partners on the African continent.
tgt: Sena se tla ba le ditlamorao tsa nako e telele bakeng sa moruo wa Aforika Borwa le ho balekane ba rona kontinenteng ya Aforika.

src: The depreciation of the Rand over the last few years offers much better prospects for export growth and, combined with a lower global oil price, has helped to relieve pressure on the current account.
tgt: Ho fokola ha Ranta dilemong tse mmalwa tse fetileng ho fana ka menyetla e batlang e ba betere bakeng sa kgolo ya thomello ya ka ntle ya thepa le, ha re kopanya le theko e batlang e ba tlase ya oli ya lefatshe, ho thusitse ho imolla kgatello hodima akhaonte ya rona ya hajwale ya matjhaba.

src: However, weaker growth in South Africa’s major trading partners has meant subdued demand for South African products abroad.
tgt: Leha ho le jwalo, kgolo e fokolang ho balekane ba ka sehloohong ba kgwebisano ba Aforika Borwa ho bolela tlhoko e fokotsehileng ya dihlahiswa tsa Aforika Borwa mose.

src: The global environment is regarded as particularly challenging for emerging markets, with lower commodity prices and tightening of monetary policy in the USA putting pressure on capital flows and growth expectations.
tgt: Tikoloho ya matjhabeng e nkuwa e le e nang le phephetso e matla bakeng sa dimmaraka tse ntseng di thuthua, ka ditheko tse tlase tsa thepa le ho tiisa lebanta ha leano la ditjhelete la Amerika ho beha kgatello ho phallo ya ditjhelete le ditebello tsa kgolo.

src: This has translated into significant volatility in capital markets.
tgt: Sena se fetohetse ho tlhokahalo ya bohlokwa ya botsitso dimmarakeng tsa ditjhelete.

src: The South African Rand, which is amongst the most traded emerging market currencies, has been particularly hard-hit in recent WEBTOKEN this difficult global context, in which all economies face difficult challenges, Cabinet reaffirmed the need for government to intervene strategically and more decisively to restore the momentum of economic growth.
tgt: Ranta ya Aforika Borwa, eo e leng hara ditjhelete tse sebediswang haholo bakeng sa kgwebisano dimmarakeng tse ntseng di thuthua, e thefulehile haholo dibekeng tsa moraorao tjena.

src: Government will reach out to social partners, particularly business and organised labour, to build consensus on the collective actions required to stabilise the economy, build confidence, raise the level of investment and return South Africa to a path of inclusive economic growth.
tgt: Ka hara maemo ana a thata a lefatshe, moo meruo kaofela e tobaneng le diphephetso tse boima, Kabinete e tiisitse botjha tlhokahalo ya mmuso ya ho tla ka mawa a boitshunyako le ho etsa ka matla hore e busetse morao lebelo la kgolo ya moruo.

src: Cabinet endorsed stronger measures to restore a sustainable fiscal path, taking account of the weakened outlook for the global economy and its domestic consequences.
tgt: Mmuso o tla ikopanya le balekane ba kahisano, haholoholo dikgwebo le mekgatlo ya basebetsi, bakeng sa ho aha kutlwano mabapi le diketso tse kopanetsweng tse batlehang bakeng sa ho tlisa botsitso moruong, ho aha tshepo, ho phahamisa maemo matsete le ho kgutlisetsa Aforika Borwa motjheng wa kgolo ya moruo o kenyeletsang.

src: Finance Minister Pravin Gordhan will unveil the measures when he presents the national budget on 24 February Higher Education fundingCabinet approved amendments to national budget allocations that would shift resources to fund universities without breaching previously announced spending limits.
tgt: Kabinete e thathiselleditse mekgwa e batlang e le matla bakeng sa ho busetsa morao motjha wa tshebediso ya matlotlo a mmuso wa moshwelella, ho ntse ho hlokometswe tjhebahalo e fokolang ya moruo wa lefatshe le ditlamorao tsa ona ka hara naha.

src: President Jacob Zuma and Higher Education and Training Minister Blade Nzimande recently indicated that these allocations would cover the zero-fee increment agreed for the current academic year, clear accumulated debt owed by the National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS) students and prevent the accumulation of such debt over the medium term.
tgt: Letona la Ditjhelete Pravin Gordhan le tla kgakola mekgwa e tla nkuwa ha a tla be a teka ditekanyetso tsa naha ka la 24 Tlhakola Matlole bakeng sa Thuto e PhahamengKabinete e tjhaelletse monwana dihlomathiso ho dikabo tsa ditekanyetso tsa naha tse tla suthisa mehlodi ya ho thusa diyunivesithi ka matlole ntle le ho tlola meedi ya tshebediso ya tjhelete e phatlaladitsweng pejana.

src: The Minister of Higher Education and training with his management team has held a number of meetings with SASCO leadership, all Student Representative Councils, University South Africa Forum , South African Union of Students, the CEO’s of SETA’s , Higher Education Transformation Network and the Parliamentary committee responsible for higher education.
tgt: Moporesidente Jacob Zuma le Letona la Thuto e Phahameng le Thupello Blade Nzimande haufinyana tjena ba tshwaile hore dikabo tsena di tla akaretsa ho se nyolohe ha ditefello hoo ho dumellanweng ka hona bakeng sa selemo sa hajwale sa dithuto, ho tlosa mokitlane oo esale o bokellana o kolotwang ke baithuti ba Sekema sa Naha sa Dithuso tsa Ditjhelete tsa Baithuti (NSFAS) le ho thibela ho bokellana ha mokitlane o jwalo bakeng sa nako e bohareng.

src: The President also met with the leadership of the students and has announced the setting up of the Commission to look into the issues raised in Higher Education.
tgt: Mekgwa ena ya boitshunyako ke karabelo ho ditherisano tse ngatanyana tse qadileng ka Phato2015 mme di ntse di tswella.

src: These engagements are still continuing as we believe as government we do want to work towards finding a lasting solution.
tgt: Dipuisano tsena di ntse di tswela pela kaha re dumela jwaloka mmuso hore re lokela ho sebeletsa ho fumana tharollo ya moshwelella.

src: The demands of the students are in line with the objectives of the programme of government in respect of education.
tgt: Ditseko tsa baithuti di imatahantse le morero wa lenaneo la mmuso le mabapi le thuto.

src: As an immediate measure, R.33 billion has been allocated to resolve the shortfall in operational funding for universities as a result of the agreement on a 0% fee increment for In the 2016/17 financial year, government has reprioritized R.543 billion of State funding to be allocated to NSFAS to provide loans to assist 71 753 identified students who qualified for NSFAS funding but were either partially or not funded at all over the past three academic years.
tgt: Jwaloka mokgwa o potlakileng, R.33 bilione e abilwe bakeng sa ho rarolla kgaello e mabapi le matlole a tshebetso a diyunivesithi ka lebaka la tumellano ya keketseho ya ditefello tsa 0% bakeng sa Selemong sa ditjhelete sa 2016/17, mmuso o phetile botjha ho beha ka sehloohongR.543 bilione ya matlole a mmuso a tla abelwa NSFAS bakeng sa ho fana ka dikadimo ho thusa baithuti ba 71 753 ba hlwailweng ho tshwanelwa ke dithuso tsa NSFAS empa ka mohlomong ba ile ba thola thuso e haellang kapa ba sa e tholang ho hang dilemong tse tharo tse fetileng tsa dithuto.

src: This means that these deserving students will not be prevented from continuing with their studies for owing universities outstanding fees.
tgt: Sena se bolela hore baithuti bana ba tshwanelwang ke thuso ba keke ba thibelwa ho tswela pele ka dithuto tsa bona hobane ba kolota diyunivesithi ditjhelete tse saletseng morao.

src: A further R.039 billion will be allocated to NSFAS in the 2016/17 financial year to support unfunded or under-funded students still in the university system in 2016 to complete their qualifications.
tgt: Tlatsetso ya R.039 bilione e tla abelwa NSFAS selemong sa dithuto sa 2016/17 ho tshehetsa baithuti ba sa tholang thuso kapa ba thotseng thuso e haellang ba ntseng ba le ka hara tsamaiso ya diyunivesithi ka 2016 bakeng sa ho phethela mangolo a bona a thuto.

src: These funds are additional to the R10 billion that NSFAS will administer in the 2016 academic year.
tgt: Matlole ana ke tlatsetso ya R10 bilione eo NSFAS e tla e laolang selemong sa dithuto sa 2016.Mmuso o itlamme bakeng sa ho fana ka thuto ya kamora sekolo bakeng sa baithuti kaofela ba tshwanelehang e sa lefellweng moo e fuwang ba futsanehileng le ba sebetsang mesebetsi e tlase, ka hara meedi ya ditjhelete tsa mmuso ya moshwelella.

src: Government is committed to providing post-school education for all academically deserving students that is free at the point of delivery for the poor and the working class, within fiscally sustainable limits.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho baithuti bohle, basebetsi, dirutehi le batsamaisi ba diyunivesithi ho sebetsa mmoho le mmuso bakeng sa ho fihlella sepheo sena.

src: Cabinet calls on students, workers, academics and university administrators to work together with government to achieve this goal.
tgt: Diketso tse sitisang ho ithuta kapa tse bakang ditebello tse hlokang kellello le ho sa fihlellehe ha bonolo ha di na molemo wa letho.

src: Actions that disrupt learning or create unreasonable and practically unachievable expectations are counterproductive.
tgt: Dikgoka le ditshoso ha di batlehe.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to recognize that there are challenging circumstances in the period ahead.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho MaAforika Borwa oohle ho ananela hore ho na le maemo a phephetso nakong eo re lebaneng le yona.

src: Global economic conditions have weakened.
tgt: Maemo a moruo wa lefatshe a se a fokola.

src: The impact of lower commodity prices is already being felt in South Africa.
tgt: Kgahlamelo ya ditheko tsa thepa tse theohileng e se e utlwahala ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: Domestic constraints such as insufficient electricity supply are still with us.
tgt: Mathata a ka hara naha a jwaloka motlakase o sa le lekanang a ntse a le teng ka hara rona.

src: The severe drought is causing hardships in several provinces.
tgt: Komello e matla e baka mathata diporofenseng tse ding.

src: Cabinet is confident that South Africans remain as a resilient nation that knows the value of working together in peace and harmony.
tgt: Kabinete e na le tshepo ya hore MaAforika Borwa a dula e le setjhaba se tsitsitseng se tsebang molemo wa ho sebetsa mmoho ka kgotso le kutlwano.

src: The recent exposure of individuals with racist’s beliefs has strengthen our collective commitment to build a nonracial, nonsexist and prosperous society.
tgt: Ho pepeswa ha moraorao tjena ha batho ba nang le ditumelo tsa bosemorabe ho matlafaditse boitlamo ba rona bo kopanetsweng ba ho aha setjhaba se hlokang kgethollo ya merabe, kgethollo ya bong le se tswetseng pele.

src: AppointmentsCabinet approved the following appointments:.
tgt: DithonyoKabinete e tjhaelletse monwana dithonyo tse latelang:.

src: Mr Shonisani Mathews Munzhedzi as Deputy Director-General (DDG): Biodiversity and Conservation in the Department of Environmental Affairs.
tgt: Monghadi Shonisani Mathews Munzhedzi jwaloka Motlatsi wa Molaodi Kakaretso (DDG): Metswako ya tsa Tlhaho le Paballo ka hara Lefapha la Merero ya Tikoloho.

src: Ms Siphokazi Ndudane as DDG: Fisheries Management in the Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries.
tgt: Mofumahadi Siphokazi Ndudane jwaloka DDG: Bolaodi ba Ditlhapika hara Lefapha la Temothuo, Meru le tsa Ditlhapi.

src: Implementation of key government programmes.
tgt: Ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha mananeo a bohlokwa a mmuso.

src: Cabinet welcomed President Jacob Zuma’s State of the Nation Address delivered on Thursday, 11 February.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Puo ya Maemo a Setjhaba ya Moporesidente Jacob Zuma eo a e entseng ka Labone, 11 Hlakola.

src: The speech set the strategic path for the implementation of government’s Programme of Action.
tgt: Puo ena e tekile motjha wa lewa la ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha lenaneo la tshebetso la mmuso.

src: The President has called on government, labour and business to work together to find solutions for a sustainable economic growth.
tgt: Moporesidente o ipileditse ho mmuso, basebetsi le borakgwebo ho sebetsa mmoho bakeng sa ho fumana ditharollo bakeng sa kgolo ya moruo ya moshwelella.

src: Cabinet supports the cost-cutting measures announced by the President, which will be elaborated by the Minister of Finance on 24 February.
tgt: Kabinete e tshehetsa mekgwa ya ho fokotsa ditjeho e phatlaladitsweng ke Moporesidente, e tla hlaloswa ho ya pele ke Letona la Ditjhelete ka la 24 Hlakola.

src: The 2016/17 Budget Speech will further map out the allocation of resources to the various government programmes as emphasised by the President.
tgt: Puo ya Ditekanyetso ya 2016/17 e tla boela e fana ka moralo wa ho abuwa ha mehlodi ho mananeo a fapafapaneng a mmuso jwaloka ha Moporesidente a tobokeditse.

src: Cabinet welcomed the successful Mining Indaba, which was held in Cape Town from 8 to 11 February.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Indaba ya Merafo e atlehileng, e neng e tshwaretswe Motse Kapa ho tloha ka la 8 ho isa ka la 11 Hlakola.

src: Leading representatives from the mining sector and several governments from Africa shared their insights into how the sector can drive investments and capitalise on the opportunities available in Africa.
tgt: Baemedi ba ka sehloohong ho tswa ho lekala la merafo le mebuso e seng mekae ho tswa Aforika ba ile ba arolelana mehopolo ya bona ya kamoo lekala lena le ka kgannang matsete le ho sebedisa lesoba la menyetla e teng ka hara Aforika.

src: Cabinet appreciated the commitment made by the Japanese government to increase its investment in South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e kgahlisitswe ke boitlamo bo entsweng ke mmuso wa Japane ba ho eketsa matsete ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet reaffirmed its commitment to a stable and flourishing mining sector.
tgt: Kabinete e tiiseditse botjha boitlamo ba yona ba lekala la merafo le tsitsitseng le ho atleha.

src: The Framework Agreement for a Sustainable Mining Industry supports the mining industry in this current difficult environment.
tgt: Moralo wa Tumellano bakeng sa Indaseteri ya Merafo ya Moshwelella e tshehetsa indaseteri ya Merafo tikolohong ena ya hajwale e boima.

src: Government continues to provide a regulatory certainty and will ensure the finalisation of the Mineral and Petroleum Resources Development Bill, which is before Parliament.
tgt: Mmuso o tswela pele ho fana ka bonnete ba taolo mme o tla netefatsa ho phethelwa ha Bili ya Ntshetsopele ya Taolo ya Mehlodi ya Diminerale le Peterole, e tekilweng ka pela Palamente.

src: Key Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved the final National Gambling Policy, which addresses challenges hampering the effectiveness of the National Gambling Act, 2004 (Act 7 of 2004).
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Leano la ho Kembola la ho qetela, le shebaneng le diphephetso tse sitisang bohlwahlwa ba Molao wa Naha wa ho Kembola, 2004 (Molao 7 wa 2004).

src: The policy proposes amendments to the regulatory structural framework of the gambling boards and strengthens the control mechanisms to minimize the abuse of gambling.
tgt: Leano lena le sisinya dihlomathiso ho meralo ya dibopeho tsa taolo ya diboto tsa ho kembola le ho matlafatsa mekgwa ya taolo bakeng sa ho fokotsa tshebediso e mpe ya ho kembola.

src: It is applicable to casinos, bingo, limited payout machines and betting on horseracing.
tgt: E sebetsa ho dikhasino, bingo, metjhini e lekanyeditsweng tjhelete le ho dipetjho tsa mejaho ya dipere.

src: The policy will replace the National Gambling Board with a National Gambling Regulator that will directly report to the Department of Trade and Industry (the dti).
tgt: Leano le tla kena bakeng sa Boto ya Naha ya ho Kembola le Bolaodi ba Naha ba ho Kembola bo tla tlaleha ka ho otloloha ho Lefapha la Dikgwebo le Diindaseteri.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Report on the Review of the Minimum Age of Criminal Capacity to Parliament, which is required in terms of the Child Justice Act, 2008 (Act 75 of 2008).
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa ha Tlaleho ya Tjhebo botjha ya Dilemo tsa ho Lokelwa ho Tshwarelwa Botlokotsebe ho Palamente, e batlehang ho ya ka Molao wa Toka wa Bana, 2008 (Molao 75 wa 2008).

src: The report recommends that the country adopts the international and regional obligations regarding the minimum age of criminal capacity of children who are in conflict with the law.
tgt: Tlaleho e kgothaletsa hore naha e amohele ditshwanelo tsa matjhaba le tsa lebatowa tse mabapi le dilemo tsa ho lokelwa ho tshwarelwa botlokotsebe ha bana ba tlolang molao.

src: Cabinet approved the gazetting of Renewable Energy Development Zones (REDZ).
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa koranteng ya mmuso ha Dibaka tsa Ntshetsopele ya Eneji e ka Hlabollwang Botjha (REDZ).

src: These will streamline the regulatory process, identify geographical areas where wind and solar Photovoltaic technologies can be incentivised and where ‘deep’ grid expansion can be directed.
tgt: Tsena di tla tsamaisa mekgwa ya taolo ka motjha o le mong, ho hlwaya dibaka tsa tlhaho moo dithekenoloji tsa ho sebedisa matla a moya le a letsatsi bakeng sa motlakase di ka qalwang le moo katoloso ya marangrang a ‘tebileng’ a ka lebiswang teng.

src: These REDZ will ensure a transition to a low carbon economy, accelerate infrastructure development, and contribute to a more coherent and predictable regulatory framework that reduces bureaucracy related to the cost of compliance.
tgt: DiREDZ di tla netefatsa ho fetohela ho moruo wa khabone e tlase, ho akofisa ntshetsopele ya meralo ya motheo, le ho nyehela ho moralo wa taolo o kopaneng le ho kgonahala o tla fokotsa bolaodi bo tomanyana bo amanang le ditjeho tsa boimatahanyo.

src: Cabinet was briefed on the findings of the 2014 South African Science, Technology and Innovation Indicators Report of the National Advisory Council on Innovation.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka diphihlello tsa Tlaleho ya Ditshupane tsa 2014 tsa Saense, Thekenoloji le Dintjhafatso tsa Lekgotla la Naha la Boeletsi la Ntjhafatso.

src: The report provides the trends in the performance of the National System of Innovation (NSI).
tgt: Tlaleho e fana ka diketsahalo ho tshebetso ya Tsamaiso ya Naha ya Dintlafatso (NSI).

src: It assesses the performance and contribution of the NSI to key national priorities articulated in the National Development Plan (NDP).
tgt: E hlahloba tshebetso le nyehelo ya NSI ho dintlha tsa bohlokwa tse ka sehloohong tse tekilweng ho Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP).

src: Cabinet approved the use of retired and in-serving public servants as lecturers in the National School of Government (NSG).The NSG was launched in 2013, replacing the Public Administration Leadership and Management Academy (PALAMA), and is mandated to promote the progressive realisation of the values and principles governing public administration and enhance the quality, extend and impact of the development of human resource capacity in institutions.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana tshebediso ya basebeletsi ba mmuso ba behileng meja fatshe le ba ntseng ba sebetsa jwaloka barupelli ho Sekolothupello sa Naha sa Mmuso (NSG).NSG e ile ya thakgolwa ka 2013, e nka sebaka sa Akhademi ya Boetapele ba Tsamaiso ya Setjhaba le Bolaodi (PALAMA), mme e romilwe ho hodisa temoho e tswetseng pele ya boleng le dipehelo tse laolang tsamaiso ya setjhaba le ho matlafatsa boleng, bophara le kgahlamelo ya ntshetsopele ya mehlodi ya bokgoni ba batho dikahong tsa mmuso.

src: This initiative will be piloted with the implementation of the Compulsory Induction Programme for public servants.
tgt: Boikitlaetso bona bo tla lekwa ka ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Lenaneo le Tlamang la ho Rutwa Mosebetsi bakeng sa basebeletsi ba mmuso.

src: This approach enables public servants to add value to the public service.
tgt: Katamelo ena e thusa basebeletsi ba setjhaba ho eketsa boleng ho tshebeletso ya setjhaba.

src: They will impart their experience, expertise, skills and knowledge to mentor and coach the public servants.
tgt: Ba tla fana ka boiphihlelo ba bona, botsebi, maitsebelo le tsebo ya ho tataisa le ho kwetlisa basebeletsi ba setjhaba.

src: This initiative will further improve in an efficient and cost effective manner the quality of the services we give to the public.
tgt: Boikitlaetso bona bo tla ntlafatsa ho ya pele ka tsela e hlwahlwa e fokotsang ditjeho tsa boleng ba ditshebeletso tseo re di nehang setjhaba.

src: Cabinet approved South Africa’s Final Phase 3 Country Report on the Implementation of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) (Anti-Bribery Convention).
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Tlaleho ya Qetelo ya Mokgahlelo 3 ya Aforika Borwa ya Naha ya ho Kenngwa Tshebetsong ya Mokgatlo wa Tshebedisano-mmoho le Ntshetsopele (OECD) (Khonvenshene e Kgahlanong le Tjotjo).Tlaleho e lokela ho kenngwa ho Sehlopha sa Tshebetso sa OECD sa Tjotjo.

src: The report is to be submitted to the OECD Working Group on Bribery.
tgt: Tlaleho e hlakisa kgatelopele e entsweng ke mmuso boitshunyakong ba ona ba ho thibela tjotjo dinaheng tsa ka ntle ka ho e fokisa, ho e fuputsa le ho e tjhutjhisa.

src: The report outlines the progress made by government in its interventions to curb foreign bribery by detecting, investigating and prosecuting it.
tgt: Tlaleho hape e hlakisa boikitlaetso bo nkuweng ho hlahisa temoso ka botlokotsebe bona.7 Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana hore Lefapha la Merero ya Lehae (DHA) le kenyeletswe ka tlasa Lepheo la Toka, Thibelo ya Botlokotsebe le Polokeho.

src: The mandate of the DHA is to maintain a secure, accurate register of the identity and status of all within the borders of our country, which is a critical enabler of all other functions of the state.
tgt: Thomo ya Lefapha la Merero ya Lehae ke ho boloka rejisatara e tshireleditsweng, e nepahetseng ya boitsebiso le maemo a bohle ba ka hara meedi ya naha ya bo rona, e leng sethusi se hlokolosi sa mesebetsi e meng kaofela ya puso.

src: It is also mandated to manage the immigration system, which impacts directly on national security, social cohesion and achievement of development goals.
tgt: Hape le romilwe ho laola tsamaiso ya bofalli, bo nang le kgahlamelo e otlolohileng ho tshireletso ya naha, momahano ya kahisano le phihlello ya dipheo tsa ntshetsopele.

src: Previously DHA was classified as a general administration support services under the Governance and Administration Cluster.
tgt: Mehleng DHA e ne e nkuwa jwaloka tshehetso e akaretsang ya ditshebeletso tsa tsamaiso tlasa lepheo la Taolo le Tsamaiso.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Protection, Promotion, Development and Management of Indigenous Knowledge Bill to Parliament.
tgt: Dibili.1 Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa ha Bili ya Tshireletso, Kgothaletso, Ntshetsopele le Bolaodi ba Tsebo ya tsa Lapeng ho Palamente.

src: This Bill seeks to protect and promote the development and management of Indigenous Knowledge WEBTOKEN provides for the establishment and functions of the National Indigenous Knowledge systems office, management of the rights of indigenous knowledge holders, establishment and functions of the advisory panel on indigenous knowledge WEBTOKEN also allows access and conditions of access to the knowledge of indigenous and local communities, establishment of a national recordal system of indigenous knowledge systems, registration, accreditation and certification of indigenous practitioners, facilitation and co-ordination of indigenous knowledge based innovation.
tgt: Bili ena, e reretswe ho tshireletsa, ho kgothaletsa ntshetsopele le bolaodi ba ditsamaiso tsa Tsebo ya ka Lapeng.

src: The Bill will complement the Intellectual Property Laws Amendment Act, 2013 (Act 28 of 2013).Cabinet approved the publication of the Deeds Registries Amendment Bill of 2015 for public comments.
tgt: E fana ka ho thehwa le mesebetsi ya kantoro ya ditsamaiso tsa Naha tsa Tsebo ya ka Lapeng, bolaodi ba batshwari ba ditokelo tsa tsebo ya tsa lapeng, ho thehwa le mesebetsi ya moifo wa Boeletsi wa ditsamaiso tsa tsebo ya tsa lapeng.

src: The Bill aims to amend the Deeds Registries Act, 1937 (Act 47 of 1937) in order to migrate from paper to electronic methods deeds office.
tgt: Bili e tla tlatseletsa Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Thuo ya Thepa, 2013 (Molao 28 wa 2013).Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana phatlalatso ya Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Dingodiso tsa Mangolo a Matlo ya 2015 bakeng sa ho tshwaela ha setjhaba.

src: It address security issues by providing of registration of conveyances as authorised users of the electronic deeds registration system.
tgt: Bili e hlomathisa Molao wa Dingodiso tsa Mangolo a Matlo, 1937 (Molao 47 wa 1937).

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Plant Health (Phytosanitary) Bill of 2015 to Parliament.
tgt: Bili e rerile ho hlomathisa Molao wa Dingodiso tsa Mangolo a Matlo, 1937 (Molao 47 wa 1937) bakeng sa ho falla ho tloha ho mekgwa ya pampiri ho ya ho ya elektroniki kantorong ya mangolo a matlo.

src: The Bill aligns South Africa’s legislation with relevant obligations and standards to facilitate safe and fair international trade to secure the country’s domestic and international trade in plants and plant products.
tgt: E shebana le dintlha tsa polokeho ka ho fana ka boingodiso ba boramolao ba matlo jwaloka basebedisi ba tsamaiso ya elektroniki ya boingodiso ba mangolo a matlo.

src: Once the Bill is passed, South Africa will be able to prevent the introduction of foreign quarantine pests and diseases that may spread harmful pests and diseases of plants in the country.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa ha Bili ya Tshireletso ya Dimela (Bophelo bo botle ba dimela) ya 2015 ho Palamente.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Courts of Law Amendment Bill of 2015 to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa ha Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Molao wa Makgotla a Dinyewe wa 2015 ho Palamente.

src: The Bill amends the Magistrates’ Courts Act, 1944 (Act 32 of 1944) and the Superior Courts Amendment Act, 2013 (Act 10 of 2013).The amendments seek to alleviate the plight of debtors who find themselves on the receiving end of abuses in the debt-collecting system in the magistrates’ courts and to accommodate the dti’s project to remove adverse consumer credit information.
tgt: Bili e hlomathisa Molao wa Makgotla a Bomaseterata, 1944 (Molao 32 wa 1944) le Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Makgotla a Maholo, 2013 (Molao 10 wa 2013).Dihlomathiso di rerile ho fedisa bothata ba boradikoloto ba iphumanang ba le lehlakoreng la tshebediso e mpe tsamaisong ya ho bokella mekitlane makgotleng a bomaseterata le ho amohela porojeke ya Lefapha la Dikgwebo le Diindaseteri ho tlosa tlhahisoleseding e tlontlollang ya mekitlane ya bareki.

src: The Bill seeks to amend sections of the Magistrates’ Courts Act, 1994 (Act 32 of 1994), to address abuses in the Emoluments Amendments Order (EAO).
tgt: Bili e rerile ho hlomathisa dikarolo tsa Molao wa Makgotla a Bomaseterata, 1994 (Molao 32 wa 1994) (MCA), ho shebana le tshebediso e mpe ho Taelo ya Kgapo ya Thepa (EAO).

src: The Bill seeks to address and bring to an end judgments that are granted irregularly, mostly by clerks of courts without any judicial oversight, many times due to inexperience or collusion with the creditors, their attorneys or debt collectors.
tgt: Bili e rerile ho shebana le, le ho fedisa dikahlolo tse fanwang ka tsela e seng molaong, haholo ke ditlelereke tsa makgotla a dinyewe ntle le ho laelwa ke lekgotla, boholo ba nako ka lebaka la ho hloka boiphihlelo kapa ho sebetsa mmoho le ba kolotwang, babuelli ba bona kapa babokelli ba mekitlane.

src: The Bill would ensure debtors are granted judgement that comply with an instalment order or EAO that is within the legal set out instalment threshold.
tgt: Bili e tla netefatsa hore boradikoloto ba fuwa kahlolo e imatahanyang le taelo ya setolomente kapa Taelo ya Kgapo ya Thepa e ka hara sekepele se molaong sa setolomente.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: The first voter registration weekend for the 2016 Local Government Elections will take place from 5 to 6 March 2016.
tgt: Mafelo a beke a boingodiso ba pele ba bakgethi bakeng sa Dikgetho tsa Mebuso ya Lehae tsa 2016 bo tla etsahala ho tloha ka la 5 ho isa ka la 6 Tlhakubele 2016.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to take advantage of and honour this hard-won democracy by going out to exercise their democratic right to register and vote in the forthcoming elections.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa kaofela ho nka monyetla wa, le ho hlompha demokerasi ena e lwanetsweng ka thata ka ho tswa ho ya sebedisa tokelo ya bona ya demokerasi ya ho ingodisa le ho vouta dikgethong tse tlang.

src: President Zuma will undertake a State Visit to the Islamic Republic of Iran from 28 to 29 February 2016.The visit will strengthen our ongoing political and economic engagements with Iran and boost South-South WEBTOKEN the Commander-in-Chief of the South African National Defence Force (SANDF), President Zuma will officiate at the fifth segment of the Armed Forces Day celebrations in Port Elizabeth, Eastern Cape, on 21 February 2016.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla nka Leeto la Mmuso ho etela Rephaboliki ya MaIsilamo ya Iran ho tloha ka la 28 ho isa ka la 29 Hlakola 2016.Leeto le tla matlafatsa dipuisano tsa rona tse ntseng di tswela pele tsa sepolotiki le moruo le Iran le ho matlafatsa dikamano tsa rona tsa Dinaha tse Borwa ba Ekhweita.

src: This annual celebration demonstrates the support and gratitude to the men and women of the SANDPresident Zuma will address the opening of the National House of Traditional Leaders in Parliament, Cape Town on 26 February 2016.
tgt: Jwaloka Molaodi-ya- ka-Sehloohong wa Lebotho la Naha la Tshireletso la Aforika Borwa (SANDF), Moporesidente Zuma e tla ba motshwara-marapo wa mekete ya karolo ya bohlano ya Letsatsi la Sesole Port Elizabeth, ho la Kapa Botjhabela, ka la 21 Hlakola 2016.

src: On Saturday, 20 February 2016, Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa will lead a delegation of Ministers to the Presidential Youth Development Expo at the Grace Bible Church in Pimville, Soweto.
tgt: Mokete ona wa selemo ka seng o bontsha tshehetso le teboho ho banna le basadi ba SANDMoporesidente Zuma o tla tshetleha puo pulong ya Ntlo ya Naha ya Baetapele ba Setso Palamenteng, Motse Kapa ka la 26 Hlakola 2016.

src: The expo is supported by the departments of Home Affairs, Labour, Social Development and Defence.
tgt: Dikamano pakeng tsa mmuso le baetapele ba setso di hlokolosi kaha di sebetsa ho lebiseng ntlafatsong ya bophelo ba batho.

src: Cabinet calls on young people in the area to attend the expo, which will provide information on how they can further their studies, start their own business or benefit from government’s support initiatives.
tgt: Ka Moqebelo, 20 Hlakola 2016, Motlatsi wa Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa o tla etella pele kemedi ya Matona ho Dipontsho tsa Boporesidente tsa Ntshetsopele ya Batjha Kerekeng ya Grace Bible Pimville, ho la Soweto.

src: Cabinet approved the hosting of the Africa Regional Seminar on the Protection of Persons based on Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Expression, by the South African Human Rights Commission, from 3 to 5 March 2016.The seminar will facilitate a dialogue to establish greater understanding of the root causes and manifestation of these challenges so as to find practical solutions and options available to States to address these violations.
tgt: Dipontsho di tshehetswa ke mafapha a Merero ya Lehae, Mesebetsi, Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba le la Tshireletso.

src: Cabinet wishes all learners who are writing their Supplementary Senior Certificate examination the best.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho batho ba batjha sebakeng sena ho kenela dipontsho tsena, tse tla fana ka tlhahisoleseding ya kamoo ba ka tswellisang dithuto tsa bona, ba ka iqallang dikgwebo kapa kamoo ba ka kgolang molemo boikitlaetsong ba tshehetso ya mmuso.

src: Supplementary examinations form part of the department’s Second Chance Matric Support Programme and afford candidates that have not met the minimum promotion and certification requirements‚ but who require a maximum of two subjects to obtain a NSC an opportunity to do so.
tgt: Kabinete tjhaelletse monwana ho tshwarwa ha Seminara ya Lebatowa la Aforika ya Tshireletso ya Batho e itshetlehileng ho Tshekamelo ya tsa Motabo, Boitsebiso ba Bong le ho Ipolela, ke Khomishene ya Ditokelo tsa Botho ya Aforika Borwa, ho tloha ka la 3 ho isa la 5 March 2016.Seminara e kgothaletsa dipuisano ho theha kutlwisiso e batlang e ba matla ya motso wa disosa le ho itjala ha diphephetso tsa hore ho tle ho fumanwe ditharollo tse kgonehang le mekgwa e meng e teng ho Puso ya ho sebetsana le ditlolo tsena tsa molao.

src: Cabinet welcomes the announcement by the President of the names of the members of the Commission of Inquiry into Higher Education.
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa baithuti bohle ba ngolang dihlahlobo tsa Tlatsetso tsa Materiki tse molemo ka ho fetisisa.

src: It calls upon all the interested stakeholders in Higher education to contribute to the commission’s work in order to find a lasting solution to the challenges faced by the Higher Education.
tgt: Baithuti ba kgothaletswa ho iphumanela Lenaneo la monyetla wa bobedi le sa tswa thakgolwa la tshehetso le fumanehang diporofenseng kaofela le ho thusa baithuti ka dithuto tsa bona ka mehlodi e fapafapaneng.

src: Cabinet extends its appreciation to those who have heeded the call to report any leaks in support of the War on Leaks Campaign led by Minister of Water and Sanitation Nomvula Mokonyane.
tgt: E ipiletsa ho bankakarolo bohle ba nang le kgahleho ho Thuto e Phahameng ho nyehela mosebetsing wa khomishene bakeng sa ho fumana ditharollo tsa moshwelella ho diphephetso tse tobileng Thuto e Phahameng.

src: Cabinet appreciates the spirit of Ubuntu shown by the initiative led by Operation Hydrate that has made a difference to communities in distress.
tgt: Maemo a Kabinete Mabapi le Dintlha tsa Bohlokwa Maemong a Hajwale.

src: The Cabinet debated and considered the full implications of the commencement of the Taxation Laws Amendment Act, 2014.
tgt: Letona la Mehlodi ya Diminerale Mosebenzi Zwane, Letona Kantorong ya Moporesidente Susan Shabangu le Letona la Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba Bathabile Dlamini – ba thontsweng ke Moporesidente Zuma ho fana ka tshehetso ho mebuso ya diporofense, beng ba morafo le malapa a amehang ho latela koduwa ya Morafong wa Gauta wa Lily ho la Barberton – ba tsebisitse Kabinete ka diketsahalo tsa moraorao tjena.

src: For that reason, Cabinet has decided to table a legislative amendment to the Taxation Laws Amendment Act as a matter of urgency to postpone the commencement date from 1 March 2016 to 1 March 2018 to allow for further consultations with all key stakeholders.
tgt: Kabinete e kene dingangisanong le ho sekaseka kgahlamelo ka botlalo ya ho qala ha Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Melao ya Lekgetho, 2014.

src: Cabinet congratulates Mr Kevin Govender from the Cape Town-based Office of Astronomy for Development and the International Astronomical Union who will be jointly awarded the prestigious Edinburgh Medal for 2016 for establishing the Office of Astronomy for Development in Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisa matshediso a yona ka ho hlokahala haufinyana tjena ha Motlotsuwa Bishopo Glayton Modise wa Kereke ya International Pentecostal Holiness.

src: Govender is the first South African to receive this prestigious award for science and technology achievements which contribute to the understanding and well-being of humanity.
tgt: Bishopo Modise o eteletse pele phutheho ena e nang le ditho tse fetang dimilione tse tharo ho phatlalla le Aforika e borwa, ho latela lefu la ntatae le mothehi wa kereke, Motlotsuwa Moemedi Frederick Modise ka 1996.

src: Cabinet commends 16-year-old ballet dancer Leroy Mokgatle who won an Audience Favourite award and a scholarship at the Prix de Lausanne International Ballet Competition in Switzerland.
tgt: Kabinete hape e fetisa kutlwelo bohloko ya yona e tebileng ka ho hlokahala haufinyana tjena ha Mongodi-Kakaretso wa mehleng wa Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) Morena Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

src: He is the first South African to win this scholarship in 28 years and the second in the country’s history.
tgt: O ile a nka marapo ka 1992 nakong eo kgahlamelo ya UN e neng e le matla bakeng sa karolo ya yona ho Ntwa ya Koung ya Persia, o sebeditse nako ya dilemo tse hlano.

src: Cabinet congratulates flautist Wouter Kellerman, cappella group Ladysmith Black Mambazo and gospel singer Neville D for their 2016 Grammy nominations.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Monghadi Kevin Govender ho tswa Kantorong ya Thuto ya Dinaledi bakeng sa Ntshetsopele le Kopano ya Matjhaba ya Thuto ya Dinaledi e Motse Kapa ya tla abelwa ka kopanelo kgau ya maemo a hodimo ya Medale wa Edinburgh wa 2016 bakeng sa ho theha Kantoro ya Thuto ya Dinaledi bakeng sa Ntshetsopele ho la Motse Kapa.

src: These artists are an inspiration and hold the South African flag high.
tgt: Govender ke moAforika Borwa wa pele wa ho amohela kgau ena ya maemo a hodimo bakeng sa diphihlello tsa saense le thekenoloji tse nyehelang kutlwisisong le ho pheleng hantle ha batho.

src: Implementation of key government programmes.
tgt: Ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha mananeo a bohlokwa a mmuso.

src: Cabinet welcomed the 2016 Budget Speech delivered by Finance Minister Pravin Gordhan on 24 February 2016.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Puo ya Ditekanyetso ya 2016 e entsweng ke Letona la Ditjhelete Pravin Gordhan ka la 24 Hlakola 2016.
