src: The draft White Paper was first published for public comment in March 2015.
tgt: Pampiri e Tshweu ya moralo e qadile ho phatlalatswa bakeng sa tshwaelo ya setjhaba ka Tlhakubele 2015.

src: The paper provides for a police service that is biased towards active citizenry and responds to the existing policing environment.
tgt: Pampiri e teka ntlha ya sepolesa se sekametseng ka ho baahi ba itahlelang ka setotswana le ho arabela ho tikoloho e teng hajwale ya sepolesa.

src: It also provides for a South African Police Service and metro police that is accountable and professional.
tgt: Hape e teka ntlha ya Tshebeletso ya Sepolesa ya Aforika Borwa le Sepolesa sa Metse Meholo se nang le boikarabelo le ho ba sa seporofeshenale.

src: The White Paper also calls for the establishment of a National Police Board which, amongst other tasks, will be responsible for setting up the objective criteria for the recruitment, selection and appointment of new recruits in the police services.
tgt: Pampiri e Tshweu e etsa boipiletso ba ho thehwa ha Boto ya Naha ya Sepolesa eo, hara mesebetsi e meng, e tla ikarabella bakeng sa ho tla ka mokgwa o se nang leeme wa ho thaotha, ho kgetha le ho thonya makolwane a matjha ka hara ditshebeletso tsa sepolesa.

src: Cabinet adopted the White Paper on Safety and Security.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse Pampiri e Tshweu e mabapi le Polokeho le Tshireletso.

src: The White Paper, which has already been out for public consultation in February 2015, focuses on an integrated and developmental approach to safety beyond policing.
tgt: Pampiri ena e Tshweu, e seng e tswile bakeng sa tjhebisano le setjhaba ka Hlakola 2015, e tsepamisitse maikutlo hodima katamelo e kopanetsweng le ya ntshetsopele ya polokeho e shebileng ka nqane ho sepolesa.

src: It seeks to guide on preventative safety measures for communities.
tgt: E batla ho fana ka tataiso bakeng sa mekgwa ya polokeho ya ba badudi.

src: The White Paper identifies all the relevant departments and community-based organisations that contribute to the safety of communities.
tgt: Pampiri e Tshweu e hlwaya mafapha kaofela a amehang le mekgatlo ya badudi e nyeheleng bakeng sa polokeho ya badudi.

src: Cabinet approved the draft Policy on the Customary Practice of Initiation in South Africa and approved for the Department of Traditional Affairs to commence drafting national legislation on initiation.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaellese monwana moralo wa Leano o mabapi le Ketso ya Moetlo wa lebollo ka hara Aforika Borwa le ho tjhaella monwana hore Lefapha la Merero ya Setso le qale ho rala molao wa naha wa tsa lebollo.

src: The policy has already gone through an extensive public consultation process with relevant stakeholders.
tgt: Leano lena le se le sebeditswe haholo ka tsamaiso ya dipuisano le setjhaba le bankakarolo ba amehang.

src: The policy provides guidelines that ensure the protection of the traditional custom of the annual initiation of young boys without compromising their safety.
tgt: Leano le fana ka ditataiso tse netefatsang tshireletso ya meetlo ya setso ya lebollo la selemo ka seng la bashemane ntle le ho beha polokeho ya bona tsietsing.

src: This forms part of the steps that government is taking to reinforce appropriate and acceptable customs.
tgt: Sena se etsa karolo ya mehato eo mmuso e e nkang ho hatella meetlo e amohelehang e nepahetseng.

src: It restores an acceptable level of accountability to those that run initiation schools and parents that send their children to these schools.
tgt: Le ho busetsa boemo bo amohelehang ba maikarabelo ho ba tsamaisang mabollo le batswadi ba romelang bana ba bona mabollong ana.

src: Cabinet approved the recommendations made by the Committee of Inquiry on the feasibility of trading in rhino horns as one of the options to preserve the country’s rhino population.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana dikgothaletso tse entsweng ke Komiti ya Dipatlisiso e mabapi le kgwebisano ka manaka a ditshukudu e le e nngwe ya kgetho ya ho baballa mohlape wa naha wa ditshukudu.

src: The recommendations were endorsed by the Interdepartmental Technical Advisory Committee and the Inter-Ministerial Committee appointed to investigate the possibility of legalising commercial international trade in rhino horn.
tgt: Dikgothaletso di ile tsa tshehetswa ke Komiti ya Boeletsi ba Setekginiki e Kopanetsweng ke Mafapha le Komiti e Kopanetsweng ya Matona e thontsweng ho batlisisa kgonahalo ya ho kenya molaong kgwebisano ya matjhaba ya manaka a ditshukudu.

src: The recommendations endorse South Africa’s integrated strategic management approach to resolving the poaching of rhino and illegal trade in rhino.
tgt: Dikgothaletso di tshehetsa lewa le kopanetsweng la Aforka Borwa la katamelo ya bolaodi ba ho rarolla ho tsongwa ho seng molaong ha ditshukudu le kgwebisano e seng molaong ya manaka a ditshukudu.

src: The committee recommends that the current mode of keeping the country’s stock levels be kept as opposed to the trading in rhino horns.
tgt: Komiti e kgothaletsa hore mokgwa wa hajwale wa ho boloka mohlape o ntseng o le teng wa naha kgahlanong le kgwebisano ka manaka a ditshukudu.

src: The country’s strategic approach entails security community empowerment biological management responsive legislative provisions that are effectively implemented and enforced and demand management.
tgt: Lewa la katamelo la naha le kenyeletsa polokeho matlafatso ya badudi taolo ya tswadiso diphano tsa molao o tla kenngwang tshebetsong ka tsela e hlwahlwa le ho hatellwa le taolo ya ho batleha ha manaka a ditshukudu.

src: Cabinet approved the following 2016 commemorative coin designs:a) The National Geographic Coin Series – Big Cats Initiative: ‘The Cheetah’.b) The Sterling-silver crown and tickey coin series ‘South African inventions – ‘Dolosse’.The coin designs, together with their proclamations, will be printed in the Government Gazette, and will then be manufactured and sold through the normal channels.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana meralo ya dikhoine tsa 2016 tsa sehopotso tse latelang:a) Letoto la Naha la Khoine ya Tlhaho– Boikitlaetso ba BigCats : ‘The Cheetah’.b) Letoto la dikhoine tsa Sterling-silver crown le dikhoine tsa tickey ‘Ditshibollo tsa Aforika Borwa–‘Dolosse’.Meralo ya dikhoine,mmoho le diphatlalatso tsa tsona, di tla hatiswa Koranteng ya Mmuso, mme ebe di tla be se di hlahiswa ka metjha e tlwaelehileng.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: President Zuma will between the 18 and 22 April 2016 undertake working visits to member states of the Southern Africa Custom Union (SACU) which include Namibia, Botswana, Lesotho and Swaziland.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma dipakeng tsa la18 le 22 Mmesa 2016 o tla nka maeto a tshebetso ho ya mebusong ya ditho tsa Kopano ya Makgetho a Madiboho ya Aforika e Borwa (SACU) e kenyeletsang Namibia, Botswana, Lesotho le Swaziland.

src: The visits will enhance the important role that SACU plays in promoting regional integration and economic development of all its members.
tgt: Maeto a tla ntlafatsa karolo ya bohlokwae bapalwang ke SACU bakeng sa ho hodisa momahano ya lebatowa le ntshetsopele ya moruo wa ditho tsa yona kaofela.

src: The President will undertake a State Visit to the Islamic Republic of Iran on 23 and 24 April 2016 to strengthen political and economic engagements between the two countries.
tgt: Moporesidente o tla nka leeto la Puso ho etela Riphaboliki ya MaIsilamo ya Iran ka la 23 le 24 Mmesa 2016 ho matlafatsa maqhama a sepolotiki le a moruo pakeng tsa dinaha tsena tse pedi.

src: The President will lead the National Freedom Day celebrations on 27 April 2016 in Limpopo, Giyani Stadium under the theme: “Together building better communities – Local Government is everyone’s business”.Cabinet calls on all South Africans and sectors to demonstrate their patriotism by participating in the various events commemorating Freedom Month.
tgt: Moporesidente o tla etella pele mekete ya Naha ya Letsatsi la Tokoloho ka la 27 Mmesa 2016 Limpopo, Lebaleng la dipapadi la Giyani tlasa mookotaba: “Mmoho re aha metse e betere–Mebuso ya le hae ke taba ya mang le mang”.Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa kaofela le makala a mang ho bontsha lerato la naha ka ho nka karolo diketsahalong tse fapafapaneng tsa ho hopola Kgwedi ya Tokoloho.

src: During the upcoming weeks, Parliament will be holding departmental Budget Votes.
tgt: Dibekeng tse tlang,Palamente e tla be e tshwara Divoutu tsa Ditekanyetso tsa mafapa ka mafapha.

src: The respective departmental Executives will unpack their operational plans for the 2016/17 financial year.
tgt: Ba Phethahatso ba mafapha ka ho latelana ba tla be ba hlopholla meralo ya bona ya tshebetso bakeng sa selemo sa ditjhelete sa 2016/17.

src: Members of the public will be informed about service-delivery programmes of government.
tgt: Ditho tsa setjhaba di tla tsebiswa ka mananeo a mmuso a phano ya ditshebeletso.

src: Cabinet’s position on key issues in the environment.
tgt: Maemo a Kabinete Mabapi le Dintlha tsa Bohlokwa Maemong a Hajwale Kabinete e amohetse karabelo le kopo ya tshwarelo e ileng ya latela ka Moporesidente Zuma ho kahlolo ya Lekgotla la Dinyewe la Molaotheo mabapi le boimatahanyo le diketso tsa ditokiso tse tekilweng tlalehong ya Mosireletsi wa Setjhaba.

src: Cabinet welcomed the response and subsequent apology by President Zuma to the Constitutional Court judgment relating to compliance with remedial actions set out in a report of the Public Protector.
tgt: Kabinete e ntse e hlahloba kahlolo bakeng sa ho sheba haeba ho na le mehato e ka nkuwang ho matlafatsa mosebetsi wa Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba.

src: Cabinet is studying the judgment to establish if there are any other actions to be undertaken to strengthen the role of the Public Service.
tgt: Kahlolo ya Lekgotla la Dinyewe la Molaotheo e thathiselletsa le ho mafiella demokerasi ya molaotheo ya Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet noted the actions by the four banks that gave notice to close the bank account of a company.
tgt: Kabinete e lemohile ketso ya dibanka tse nne tse fanneng ka tsebiso ya ho kwala diakhaonte tsa banka tsa khamphani e nngwe.

src: Whilst Cabinet appreciate the terms and conditions of the banks, the acts may deter future potential investors who may want to do business in South Africa.
tgt: Leha Kabinete e ananela dipehelo le maemo a dibanka, diketso tsena di ka sitisa boramatsete ba ka nnang ba ba teng ba ka batlang ho tsamaisa dikgwebo ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet has endorsed that the Ministers of Finance, Labour and Mineral Resources should open a constructive engagement with the banks to find a lasting solution to this matter.
tgt: Kabinete e tsheheditse ntlha ya hore Matona a Ditjhelete, Mesebetsi le Mehlodi ya Diminerale a tshwanela ho bula dipuisano tse ahang le dibanka bakeng sa ho fihlella tharollo ya nako e telele tabeng ena.

src: Cabinet congratulated the Minister of Health, Dr Aaron Motsoaledi, who received the USAID-TB international award in recognition of his leadership in the global fight against tuberculosis (TB) as well as championing South Africa's and regional initiatives in the screening, treatment and prevention of TB TB/HIV co-infection and multi-drug resistant TCabinet welcomes the nomination of South Africa as the 2016 recipient of the Distinguished Diplomatic Service Award by the World Affairs Council in Washington, DAs the first African country to receive this award, it recognises the country’s outstanding commitment to global education, international affairs and global communications to advance our national interests.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Letona la Bophelo bo Botle, Ngaka Aaron Motsoaledi, ya fumaneng kgau ya matjhaba ya Lefuba ya USAID-TB jwaloka kananelo ya boetapele ba hae mabapi le ntwa ya lefatshe kgahlanong le lefuba (TB) mmoho le ho etella pele boikitlaetso ba Aforika Borwa le ba lebatowa mabapi le ho hlahloba, kalafo le thibelo ya TB tshwaetso e kopaneng ya TB/HIV le TB e itwanelang ho meriana e mengata.

src: Cabinet commends the Minister of International Relations and Cooperation, Ms Maite Nkoana-Mashabane, for her contribution to South Africa’s international engagements, which are driven by the vision of a “united African continent that is peaceful, democratic, non-racial, non-sexist and prosperous, and which contributes to a just and equitable world.”.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho kgethwa ha Aforika Borwa ho ba moamohedi wa 2016 wa Kgau ya Tshebeletso e Ipabotseng ya Sedipolomate ke Lekgotla la Merero ya Lefatshe ho la Washington,DJwaloka naha ya pele ya Aforika ya ho amohela kgau ena, e ananela boitlamo bo babatsehang ba naha mabapi le thuto ya lefatshe, merero ya matjhaba le dikgokahanyo tsa lefatshe bakeng sa ho hodisa ditabatabelo tsa rona tsa naha.

src: Cabinet welcomes the appointment by President Zuma of Advocate Jan Lekhoa Mothibi, as the Head of the Special Investigating Unit, and wishes him all the best in his new responsibilities of combating corruption and maladministration.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Letona la Dikamano tsa Matjhaba le Tshebedisano, Mofumahadi Maite Nkoana-Mashabane, bakeng sa nyehelo ya hae ho dipuisano tsa matjhaba tsa Aforika Borwa, tse kgannwang ke pono ya “kontinente ya Aforika e kopaneng e nang le kgotso, ya demokerasi, e hlokang semorabe, e hlokang kgethollo ya bong le e tswelang pele, le ho ba e nyehelang ho lefatshe le nang le toka le tekatekano.”.

src: Cabinet conveys its heartfelt condolences to the Makwetu family and the Pan Africanist Congress on the passing of Mr Clarence Makwetu.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela thonyo ke Moporesidente Zuma ya Moatefokate Jan Lekhoa Mothibi, jwaloka Hlooho ya Lekala la Diphuputso tsa Sepolesa le Ikgethang, le ho mo lakaletsa tse molemo boikarabelong ba hae bo botjha ba ho lwantsa bobodu le tsamaiso e mamphemphe.

src: Mr Makwetu will be remembered for his immense contribution and personal sacrifices to the liberation movement and the establishment of the new democratic South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisetsa matshediso a tswang botebong ba pelo ho lelapa la Makwetu le Pan Africanist Congress ka ho hlokahala ha Monghadi Clarence Makwetu.

src: The President declared a Special Provincial Official Funeral for the liberation struggle stalwart.
tgt: Monghadi Makwetu o tla hopolwa ka nyehelo ya hae e matla le ho intsha sehlabelo bakeng sa mokgatlo wa tokoloho le ho thehwa ha Aforika Borwa e ntjha ya demokerasi.

src: Cabinet conveys its heartfelt condolences to the Naidoo family on the passing of Mr Kumaran Naidoo.
tgt: Moporesidente o phatlaladitse Lepato le Ikgethang la Semmuso la Porofense bakeng sa mohale enwa wa ntwa ya tokoloho.

src: Mr Naidoo was the Acting Director-General of the Department of Economic Development.
tgt: Monghadi Naidoo e ne e le Motsamaisi-Kakaretso ya Tshwereng Mokobobo wa Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Moruo.

src: He previously served as the Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Trade and Industry.
tgt: Pele o ne a sebetsa jwaloka Mohlanka ya ka Sehloohong wa Ditjhelete wa Lefapha la Dikgwebo le Diindaseteri.

src: Mr Naidoo has contributed immensely in financial management within the Public Service.
tgt: Monghadi Naidoo o entse nyehelo e matla ho taolo ya ditjhelete ka hara Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba.

src: Cabinet expressed its appreciation on the contribution made by Mr William Smith, who served as Cabinet Secretariat.
tgt: Kabinete e hlahisa kananelo ya yona ka nyehelo e entsweng ke Monghadi William Smith, ya sebeditseng ho Bongodi ba Kabinete.

src: Mr Smith retired at the end of March after serving the Public Service for 27 years.
tgt: Monghadi Smith o behile meja fatshe mafelong a Tlhakubele kamora ho sebeletsa Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba dilemo tse 27.Kabinete e mo lakaletsa tse molemo phomolong ya hae.

src: The Cabinet was briefed about the Report of the Commission of Inquiry into Allegations of Fraud, Corruption, Impropriety or Irregularity in the Strategic Defence Procurement Package (Arms Procurement Commission) which was released by the President this morning.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka Tlaleho ya Khomishene ya Dipatlisiso e mabapi le Dipelaelo tsa Boqhekanyetsi, Bobodu, Boitshwaro bo Bobe kapa Tsamaiso e Mpe ho Pakana ya Lewa la Ditheko la Tshireletso (Khomishene ya Ditheko tsa Dibetsa) e lokolotsweng ke Moporesidente hoseng hona.

src: The Report has found no evidence of wrongdoing, bribery, fraud or corruption in the arms procurement process, As Government we welcome the findings of the Commission.
tgt: Tlaleho e fumane hore ha ho bopaki ba ketso e fosahetseng, tjotjo, boqhekanyetsi kapa bobodu tsamaisong ya theko ya dibetsa.

src: We join President Zuma in thanking Justice Willie Seriti and Judge Thekiso Musi, all the witnesses, including former President Thabo Mbeki, evidence leaders, legal teams, staff and those who contributed to making the work of the Commission a success.
tgt: Re hlakotswe bobe kaha esale re bolela ka dilemo tse ngata hore ha ho letho le lebe le etsahetseng le hore theko ena e ne e se na WEBTOKEN tshepa hore sephetho se tla kwala taba ena e nkileng nako e WEBTOKEN kgema mmoho le Moporesidente Zuma mabapi le ho leboha Moahlodi Willie Seriti le Moahlodi Thekiso Musi, dipaki kaofela, ho kenyeletswa le Moporesidente wa mehleng Thabo Mbeki, baetapele ba bopaki, dihlopha tsa semolao, basebeletsi le ba nyehetseng bakeng sa ho etsa hore mosebetsi wa Khomishene o atlehe.

src: AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: DithonyoDithonyo kaofela di lokelwa ke ho netefatswa ha mangolo a thuto le tumello e amehang.

src: Mr Siyabonga Gama as Group Executive and Mr Garry Pita as Group Chief Financial Officer of Transnet.
tgt: Monghadi Siyabonga Gama jwaloka Mohlanka wa Phethahatso wa Sehlopha le Monghadi Garry Pita jwaloka Mohlanka ya ka Sehloohong wa Ditjhelete wa Sehlopha waTransnet.

src: Mr Lufuno Leslie Nevhutalu as member and Chairperson of the Construction Industry Development Board.
tgt: Monghadi Lufuno Leslie Nevhutalu jwaloka setho le Modulasetulo wa Boto ya Ntshetsopele ya Indaseteri ya Kaho.

src: Mr Andile Nongogo as the Chief Executive Officer of the Services Sector Education Training Authority.
tgt: Monghadi Andile Nongogo jwaloka Mohlanka ya ka Sehloohong wa Phethahatso wa Bolaodi ba Lekala la Ditshebeletso tsa Thuto.

src: Implementation of Key Government Programmes.
tgt: Ho kenngwa Tshebetsong ha Mananeo a Bohlokwa a Mmuso.

src: Cabinet welcomes President Jacob Zuma’s State Visit of to the Islamic Republic of Iran, which escalates economic and trade relations between both countries, through the signing of several agreements and commitments.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela Leeto la Puso la Moporesidente Jacob Zuma la ho etela Rephaboliki ya maIsilamo ya Iran, le hodisang dikamano tsa moruo le kgwebisano dipakeng tsa dinaha ka bobedi, ka ho saenwa ha ditumellano le maitlamo a mmalwa.

src: President Jacob Zuma and President Hasan Rouhani strengthened cooperation in the fields of trade, education and skills development science and technology energy, including petrochemical gas exploration and refining capacity agriculture mining and mineral beneficiation infrastructure development and transport finance, banking and insurance and tourism.
tgt: Moporesidente Jacob Zuma le Moporesidente Hasan Rouhani ba tiisitse tshebedisano-mmoho mapatlelong a kgwebisano, thuto le ntshetsopele ya maitsebelo saense le thekenoloji eneji, ho kenyeletswa le bokgoni ba ho tsoma kgase le ho e lokisetsa tshebediso temo merafo le bokgolamolemo ba diminerale ntshetsopele ya meralo ya motheo le dipalangwang ditjhelete, merero ya dibanka le inshorense le bohahlaudi.

src: All of which contributes to the implementation of the National Development Plan.
tgt: E leng kaofela tse nyehelang ho Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP).Boemong ba tsa Matjhaba, baetapele ba babedi ba dumellane ka ho matlafatsa kgoeletso bakeng sa tlhabollo ya Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng ka ho qolleha Lekgotla la Tshireletso la UN, molemong wa lefatshe le ntseng le tswela pele.

src: On the international front, the two leaders agreed to intensify the call for the reform of the United Nations especially the UN Security Council, in the interests of the developing world.
tgt: Diphetho tsena di matlafaditse Leeto la Tshebetso la Moporesidente ho ya United Arab Emirates (UAE) moo dipuso ka bobedi di ntjhafaditseng boitlamo ba tsona ho lebiseng matlafatsong le kgodisong ya dikamano tsa bobedi, ka ho qolleha kgwebisanong, matseteng le mapatlelong a moruo hore e be bolekane ba lewa le pharalletseng.

src: These outcomes reinforced the President’s Working Visit to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) where both states renewed their commitment towards the consolidation and elevation of bilateral relations, particularly in the trade, investment and economic fields into a comprehensive strategic partnership.
tgt: Sena se ahella hodima Leeto la Puso la Moporesidente Jacob Zuma ka Pudungwana 2011 moo ho bonahetseng ho thehwa ha Khomishene e Kopanetsweng ya SA-UAE e akofisitseng lebelo la kgwebisano e phethahetseng dipakeng tsa dinaha tse pedi tsena ho tloha ho R13 bilione ka 2011 ho ya ho R27 bilione ka 2015.Aforika Borwa le UAE hape di dumellane ho eketsa tshebedisano-mmoho ho sebetsana le menyetla ho Moruo wa Lewatle, ho hodisa ho romellwa dinaheng tse ka ntle ha dihlahiswa tsa temo tsa Aforika Borwa, dihlahiswa tse entsweng difemeng mme ka ho qolleha theko ya tsa tshireletso le bomphato.

src: This built on President Jacob Zuma’s State Visit in November 2011 which saw the establishment of the SA-UAE Joint Commission that accelerated total trade momentum between the two countries from R13 billion in 2011 to R27 billion in 2015.South Africa and the UAE also agreed to expand cooperation to take advantage of opportunities in the Ocean Economy, to promote the export of South African agricultural products, manufactured products and particularly defence procurement and partnerships.
tgt: Leeto hape le hodisitse bokgoni ba Aforika Borwa ba ho aha meralo ya motheo ho shebanwe le menyetla bakeng sa dikhamphani tsa Aforika Borwa ho EXPO 2020 ho la Dubai, hammoho le tshebedisano-mmoho lepatlelong la kgotso le botsitso.

src: The visit also promoted South African infrastructure building capacity targeting opportunities for South African companies at EXPO 2020 in Dubai, as well as cooperation in the field of peace, security and stability.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse mehato e tiileng e kentsweng tshebetsong ke Letona la Dipapadi le Boikgathollo Fikile Mbalula ho aha botjha maemo a qhetsohileng le ho ba le kgethollo e tebileng ho tsa dipapadi le boikgathollo ka tshebediso ya Tjhata ya Diphethoho.

src: Cabinet welcomed the firm measures that have been put in place by the Minister of Sport and Recreation Fikile Mbalula to reconstruct the fragmented and deeply discriminatory sport and recreation landscape through its Transformation Charter.
tgt: Sena se tla akofisa diphethoho tse tla lebisang tsamaisong e kopaneng ya dipapadi e thehilweng hodima dipehelo tsa demokerasi, tekatekano, ponaletso le boemedi ho ya ka mekgahlelo e fapaneng ya setjhaba, phumantsho le bonkakarolo bo eketsehileng ho ipapisitswe le ditabatabelo tsa NDKabinete e amohela dipuo tsa ditekanyetso tse ntseng di tekwa ke mafapha a fapafapaneng le ditlaleho tse batsi tse supang kgatelopele e entsweng bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa bophelo ba maAforika Borwa.

src: This demonstrates implementation of the Medium Term Strategic Framework which takes us closer to the realisation of Vision 2030 of the National Development Plan.
tgt: Sena se bontsha ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Moralo wa Lewa la Nako e Bohareng (MTSF) o re atametsang haufi le ho fihlellwa ha Pono ya 2030 ya NDP.

src: Cabinet calls on South Africans to follow the budget votes on various media platforms to better understand Government’s Programme of Action.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ho latela dipuo tsa ditekanyetso mapatlelong a fapafapaneng a boraditaba bakeng sa ho utlwisisa betere ka Lenaneo la Mmuso la Tshebetso.

src: Cabinet calls for continued commitment to secure meaningful workplace transformation in view of the findings from the 16th Commission for Employment Equity Annual Report for all designated employers which was launched under the theme “Transformation does make business sense”.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso bakeng sa boitlamo bo tswellang mabapi le diphetho tse bonahalang dibakeng tsa mosebetsi ho itshetlehilwe hodima diphetho ho tswa ho Tlaleho ya Selemo ka seng ya Khomishene ya bo-16 ya Tekatekano Mosebetsing bakeng sa bahiri ba tobilweng e thakgotsweng tlasa mookotaba “Diphethoho di bohlokwa kgwebong”.

src: The Report helps government to understand the status of employment equity in the country and its progress in workplace transformation for the year 2015.
tgt: Tlaleho ena e thusa mmuso ho utlwisia maemo a tekatekano mosebetsing ka hara naha le kgatelopele ya yona ho diphethoho mosebetsing bakeng sa selemo sa 2015.

src: Cabinet congratulated the Department of Human Settlements on the delivery of 4, 3 million houses and housing opportunities since the dawn of democracy.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholeditse Lefapha la Bodulo ba Batho ka phano ya matlo a 4, 3 milione le menyetla ya matlo ho tloha mathwasong a demokerasi.

src: These opportunities include 2, 806 235 fully subsidized houses (BNG houses), 121 784 social/rental housing, 6329 Financial Linked Individual Subsidy Programme and 986 608 serviced sites.
tgt: Menyetla ena e kenyeletsa matlo a tsheheditsweng ka botlalo a 2, 806 235 (matlo a BNG), matlo a hiriswang/kahisano a 121 784, a 6329 a Lenaneo le Hoketsweng ho Ditshehetso tsa Ditjhelete tsa ka Bomong le ditentshe tse nang le ditshebeletso tse 986 608.Mokolokotwane ona o etsang nalane o fane ka bodulo ho batho ba fetang 20 milione mme ho keteka phihlello ena mmuso o thakgotse letsholo la naha la ho bontsha katleho ya naha.

src: This historic milestone has provided a roof for more than 20 million people and to celebrate this achievement the department has launched a national campaign to profile the country’s success.
tgt: Ho thakgolwa ha morero ona wa naha ho etsahetse COSMO City, e leng e nngwe ya diporojeke tse kopanetsweng tse ka sehloohong ho potoloha le naha eo hape e ketekang dilemo tse leshome e le teng.

src: The national launch took place in COSMO City, one of the integrated priority projects around the country which is also celebrating ten years of its existence.
tgt: Kabinete e lebohile maAforika Borwa kaofela bakeng sa dinyehelo tsa ona, boitelo le mosebetsi o matla wa ho netefatsa hore seriti sa maAforika Borwa a hlokang se babaletswe ka bodulo ba batho.

src: Cabinet thanked all South Africans for their contributions, dedication and hard work in ensuring that the dignity of South Africans in need is restored through human settlements.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Mongodikakaretso wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng ka ho hlophisa Mokete wa Maemo a Hodimo wa ho Saena Tumellano ya Paris, e amohetsweng ke Mekga e 176 ka Tshitwe 2015.

src: Cabinet commends the United Nations Secretary-General for convening the High-Level Signing Ceremony of the Paris Agreement, which was adopted by 176 Parties in December 2015.
tgt: Ho saenwa ha Tumellano ya Paris ho tshwaile mohato wa pele ho kenngweng tshebetsong ha yona o tla tataisa mekutu ya matjhaba ya ho fokotsa ho ntshwa ha dikgase tse kotsi le ho mekamekana le diphephetso kaofela tse amanang le ho fetofetoha ha tlelaemete.

src: Cabinet looks forward to the conclusion of the respective domestic ratification procedures, by all, to enable timely entry into force for full implementation of the Paris Agreement by 2020.
tgt: Kabinete e lebeletse ka tshepo sephetho sa ditsamaiso tsa tiisetso tsa lehae, ke bohle, ho thusa hore ho be le ho kenngwa ka nako ka botlalo ha Tumellano ya Paris ka 2020.

src: Cabinet also notes that the Department of Environmental Affairs has partnered with the Department of Tourism in convening delivery labs titled “Biodiversity Lab: Growing the economic contribution of South Africa’s biological resources” from 10 April to 13 May 2016.The aim is to realise the economic potential of South Africa’s rich biological diversity which is articulated in the draft National Biodiversity Economy Strategy that was approved by Cabinet in July 2015 for public participation.
tgt: Kabinete hape e ananetse hore Lefapha la Merero ya Tikoloho le entse semphato le Lefapha la Bohahlaudi bakeng sa ho fana ka dilaboratori tsa sehlooho se reng “Biodiversity Lab: Re hodisa nyehelo ya moruo ya mehlodi ya Aforika Borwa ya tlhaho” ho tloha ka la 10 Mmesa ho isa la 13 Motsheanong 2016.Sepheo ke ho elellwa bokgoni ba moruo ba diphapang tsa tlhaho tse ruileng tsa Aforika Borwa tse tekilweng ho moralo wa Lewa la Naha la Moruo wa Tlhaho o tjhaelletsweng monwana ke Kabinete ka Phupu 2015 hore setjhaba se nke karolo.

src: Key Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa bohlokwa tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved the Industrial Policy Action Plan (IPAP) 2016/17 – 2018/19, which is a key pillar of the President’s Nine-Point Plan and contributes towards implementation of the National Development Plan.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Moralo wa Tshebetso wa Leano la Diindaseteri (IPAP) 2016/17 – 2018/19, e leng tshiya ya bohlokwa ya Moralo wa Dintlha tse Robong wa Moporesidente o lebisang ho kenngweng tshebetsong ha NDP.

src: This is the eighth annual iteration of successive government industrialisation plans which builds on the achievements, policy platforms and programmes of previous iterations.
tgt: Sena ke ho phetwa ka tatelano ha borobedi ha selemo ka seng ha meralo ya mmuso ya akofiso ya diindaseteri ho ahellang hodima diphihlello, mapatlelo a leano le mananeo a ho phetwa ho fetileng.

src: IPAP 2016/17 seeks to achieve a higher impact industrial policy in difficult economic circumstances.
tgt: IPAP 2016/17 e rerile ho fihlella leano la diindaseteri le nang le kgahlamelo e batlang e phahame maemong a boima a moruo.

src: These include the on-going effects of the global economic recession including the steel crisis and commodity slump as well as the severe drought and other significant domestic constraints.
tgt: Tsena di kenyeletsa dikgahlamelo tse ntseng di tswela pele tsa ho thefuleha ha moruo wa lefatshe ho kenyeletswa le koduwa ya diindaseteri tsa tshepe le ho putlama ha thepa hammoho le komello e matla le mathata a mang a ka lapeng.

src: Achievements from the previous year include the saving of approximately 67 000 jobs and the creation of an estimated 7 000 new decent jobs in the Clothing and Textile Leather and Footwear sector.
tgt: Diphihlello tsa ho tswa selemong se fetileng di kenyeletsa ho baballwa ha mesebetsi e ka bang 67 000 le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi e hlamatsehang e metjha e ballwang ho 7 000 lekaleng la Diaparo le Masela le Dieta.

src: The Agro-processing sub-sector is one of the largest domestic manufacturing sectors by employment, providing an estimated 216 090 jobs in 2015 compared to 208 822 in 2014.
tgt: Lekala la tlatsetso la dihlahiswa tsa Temo ke le leng la makala a maholo a tlhahiso la phano ya mesebetsi, e ballwang ho mesebetsi e 216 090 ka 2015 ha ho bapiswa le e 208 822 ka 2014.Matsete a boleng ba R600 milione a ile a hohelwa ka 2015/16, mme a etsa motheo bakeng sa ho matlafatsa ntshetsopele ya kgwebo ho tsepamisitswe maikutlo hodima badudi ba mahaeng.

src: Over R600 million worth of investment was attracted in 2015/16, laying the basis for strengthening enterprise development with a focus on rural communities.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Moralo o Kopanetsweng wa Ntshetsopele ya Ditoropo wa ho Phethela le Moralo wa ho Kenya Tshebetsong wa 2016/19.

src: The overall outcome of the Integrated Urban Development Framework is spatial transformation.
tgt: Sephetho ka kakaretso sa Moralo o Kopanetsweng wa Ntshetsopele ya Ditoropo ke ho fetola qaqolohano ya dibaka tsa bodulo.

src: This marks a new deal for South African cities and towns, which will steer urban growth towards a sustainable growth model of compact, connected and coordinated cities and towns, which are safer, resource efficient and good places to work and live in.
tgt: Sena se tshwaya tsamaiso e ntjha ya metsemeholo le ditoropo tsa Aforika Borwa, sena se tla tataisetsa kgolo ya ditoropo ho lebiseng ho motlolo wa kgolo wa moshwelella o kopaneng, o hokahanyang le ho kopanya metsemeholo le ditoropo, tse bolokehileng, tse nang le mehlodi e hlwahlwa le ho ba dibaka tse ntle tsa ho sebetsa le ho dula ho tsona.

src: This responds to the National Development Plan directive to develop an urban development policy that will ensure proper planning, infrastructure investments and management to support growth and unlock the economic potential of our cities and towns.
tgt: Sena se arabela ho taelo ya NDP la ho hodisa leano la ntshetsopele ya ditoropo le tla netefatsa moralo o nepahetseng, matsete a meralo ya motheo le taolo ya ho tshehetsa bokgoni ba kgolo le ho bula bokgoni ba moruo ba metsemeholo le ditoropo tsa rona.

src: Cabinet approved publication of the Draft National Career Development Services Policy – Building an effective and Integrated Career Development Services System for South Africa, in the Government Gazette for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana phatlalatso ya Moralo wa Leano la Naha la Ntshetsopele ya Ditshebeletso tsa Makala a Thuto – Re aha Tsamaiso e hlwahlwa le e Kopanetsweng ya Ntshetsopele ya Ditshebeletso tsa Makala a Thuto bakeng sa Aforika Borwa, Koranteng ya Mmuso bakeng sa tshwaelo ya setjhaba.

src: The draft Policy once implemented will provide a coordinated approach to quality career development services for all citizens.
tgt: Moralo ona wa Leano hang feela ha o kentswe tshebetsong o tla fana ka katamelo e kopanetsweng bakeng sa ditshebeletso tsa ntshetsopele ya makala a thuto a boleng bakeng sa baahi kaofela.

src: This will enable them to make informed career choices to obtain employment, contribute to society and build the South African WEBTOKEN Development Services plays a key role in helping labour markets work and education systems meet their goals.
tgt: Sena se tla ba thusa ho etsa diqeto tse kgabane tsa makala a thuto hore ba thole mesebetsi, ba nyehele setjhabeng le ho aha moruo wa Aforika Borwa.

src: This contributes towards the achievement of the National Development Plan recommendations of promoting economic growth and employment, matching of employed workers to jobs and increasing skills development and the number of university graduates.
tgt: Ditshebeletso tsa Ntshetsopele ya Makala a Thuto di bapala karolo ya bohlokwa mabapi le ho thusa mebaraka ya rona ya mosebetsi hore e sebetse le hore mekgwa ya thuto e fihlelle merero ya yona.

src: Cabinet was briefed on implementation of the National Evaluation System and approved the Annual report 2014/15 and the fifth National Evaluation Plan for 2016/17 to 2018/19, as part of the drive to improve service delivery,The National Evaluation System emanates from the National Evaluation Policy Framework which ensures that credible and objective evidence from evaluations is incorporated in processes of planning, budgeting, organisational improvement, policy review, as well as on-going programme and project management so as to improve performance.
tgt: Sena se nyehela ho lebiseng ha phihlello ya dikgothaletso tsa NDP tsa ho hlasimolla kgolo ya moruo le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi, le ho matahanya basebeletsi le mesebetsi e loketseng eo ba e etsang le ho eketsa ntshetsopele ya maitsebelo le palo ya ba nang le mangolo a diyunivesithi.

src: Forty-seven (47) evaluations have been completed or are underway, covering R75 billion of government expenditure.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Tsamaiso ya Naha ya Tekolo le ho tjhaella monwana Tlaleho ya Selemo ka seng ya 2014/15 le Moralo wa Naha wa Tekolo bakeng sa 2016/17 ho ya ho 2018/19, jwaloka karolo ya boikitlaetso ba ho ntlafatsa phano ya ditshebeletso.

src: Cabinet was briefed on the evaluation findings and approved recommendations with a view to increase impact from the implementation of the Expanded Public Works Programme Social Sector (EPWP-SS).This Programme plays an important social protection role for unemployed able bodied adults, by drawing them into productive work and receiving a monthly stipend of an average amount of R1 517.
tgt: Tsamaiso ya Naha ya Tekolo e tswa ho Moralo wa Leano la Naha la Tekolo o netefatsang hore bopaki bo tshepahalang le bo hlokang tshekamelo ho tswa ho ditekolo bo kenyeletswa tsamaisong ya ho etsa meralo, ho etsa ditekanyetso tsa ditjhelete, ntlafatso ya mekgatlo, tjhebo-botjha ya maano, hammoho le lenaneo le tswellang le taolo ya diporojeke ka morero wa ho ntlafatsa tshebetso.

src: Most of the social sector programmes provide specialised services to vulnerable and poor communities.
tgt: Ditekolo tse 47 di se di phethetswe kapa di motjheng, tse akaretsang R75 bilione ya ditjeho tsa mmuso.

src: The EPWP-SS grew rapidly between phase one and phase two, from 5 to 22 programmes which resulted in the sector achieving 175 769 work opportunities in phase one and 866 246 work opportunities in phase two, well above the 750 000 target.
tgt: Ditlaleho tsa tekolo tse15 di ile tsa tjhaellwa monwana mme tse 12 tsa tekelwa Kabinete ho fihlela mona.

src: The recommendations focus on improving implementation to reduce inefficiencies in decision-making, implementation (payments of stipends) and provision of training, as well as coordination.
tgt: Meralo ya ntlafatso e 14 e ntse e kenngwa tshebetsong mme kgatelopele ho tsena e bontsha diphethoho tse hlamatsehang, bakeng sa ho pharalatsa sekgahla.

src: Cabinet was briefed on the findings and endorsed the recommendations of the design and implementation evaluation of the Urban Settlement Development Grant and its Improvement Plan.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka diphetho tsa tekolo le ho tjhaella monwana dikgothaletso ka morero wa ho eketsa sekgahla ho tswa ho ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Lekala la Kahisano la Lenaneo la Katoloso ya Mesebetsi ya Setjhaba (EPWP-SS).Lenaneo lena le bapala karolo ya bohlokwa bakeng sa tshireletso ya kahisano bakeng sa batho ba baholo ba ntseng ba itekanetse ba sa sebetseng, ka ho ba hulela mosebetsing o nang le tlhahiso le ho amohela ditlhapiso tsa kgwedi ka palohare ya tjhelete e etsang R1 517.

src: The findings support retaining the Urban Settlement Development Grant as a supplementary grant that funds a wider notion of sustainable and equitable human settlements for the benefit of poor and moderate income households.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka diphetho le ho tiisetsa dikgothaletso tsa moralo le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha tekolo ya Thuso ya Ditjhelete ya Ntshetsopele ya Bodulo ba Ditoropong le Moralo wa Ntlafatso ya tsona.

src: This is instrumental in achieving the targets from the Medium Term Strategic Framework provision of 1 495 million housing opportunities in quality living environments by 2019.
tgt: Diphetho di tshehetsa ho baballwa ha Thuso ya Ditjhelete ya Ntshetsopele ya Ditoropo jwaloka thuso ya tshehetso e thusang ka matlole mohopolo wa bodulo ba batho ba moshwelella le bo lekalekanang molemong wa bafumanehi le malapa a lekeno le mahareng.

src: Cabinet approved the report on the Implementation and Impact Evaluation of the Technology and Human Resources for Industry Programme, the management response to the report and the improvement plan submitted by the Department of Trade and Industry.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana tlaleho ya Ho kenngwa Tshebetsong le Tekolo ya Kgahlamelo ya Thekenoloji le Mehlodi ya Batho bakeng sa Lenaneo la Diindaseteri, karabelo ya botsamaisi ho tlaleho le moralo wa ntlafatso o kentsweng ke Lefapha la Dikgwebo le Diindaseteri.

src: This Programme was introduced by the Department of Trade and Industry in 1992 to strengthen skills development in science, engineering and technology.
tgt: Lenaneo lena le ile la hlahiswa ke Lefapha la Dikgwebo le Diindaseteri ka 1992 ho matlafatsa ntshetsopele ya maitsebelo ho tsa saense, boenjinere le thekenoloji.

src: It contributes to job creation by producing a flow of highly skilled researchers and technology managers for industry and by improving the competitiveness of the participating business organisations.
tgt: Le nyehela ho tlhahiso ya mesebetsi ka ho hlahisa phallo ya bafuputsi ba nang le maitsebelo a maholo le batsamaisi ba thekenoloji bakeng sa diindaseteri le ho ntlafatsa bophehisani ba mekgatlo ya kgwebo e nkang karolo.

src: The Programme is a valid, important and efficient element of innovation support that offers considerable value for money both in terms of technology development and developing human resources and industry-related skills.
tgt: Lenaneo lena ke la sebele, la bohlokwa le ho ba ntlha e hlwahlwa ya tshehetso ya ntjhafatso e fanang ka boleng ba tjhelete bo hlamatsehang ka bobedi mabapi le ntshetsopele ya thekenoloji le ho ntshetsapele mehlodi ya batho le maitsebelo a tsamaelanang le diindaseteri.

src: It also compares favourably to some international programmes.
tgt: Hape le bapiseha hantle le mananeo a mang a matjhaba.

src: Cabinet was briefed on the findings of the Report by the Ministerial Task Team probe into the allegations of the ‘educator posts for sale’ involving individuals, teacher unions and officials of certain Provincial Education Departments.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka diphetho tsa dipatlisiso tsa Tlaleho ya Moifo wa Tshebetso wa Matona mabapi le dipelaelo tsa ‘thekiso ya dikgeo tsa mosebetsi tsa matitjhere’ tse amang batho ka bo mong, mekgatlo ya matitjhere le bahlanka ba Mafapha a itseng a Thuto a Diporofense.

src: Cabinet endorsed recommendations to deal systematically and pointedly with the WEBTOKEN its final Report the Ministerial Task Team provides a critique of the role played by all stakeholders in the process of the selection and recruitment of WEBTOKEN also notes the significant problems in the current system of appointments to posts in the basic education sector and provides recommendations to assist the Department of Basic Education and the basic education sector in general to address the identified challenges.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya thathiselletsa dikgothaletso tsa ho sebetsa hantle le ho tobana le diphetho.

src: Cabinet approved submission of the National Forest Amendment Bill to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho kenngwa ha Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Naha ya Meru Palamenteng.

src: The Bill amends the National Forests Act, 1998 (Act No.
tgt: Bili e fetola Molao wa Naha wa Meru, 1998 (Molao No.

src: 84 of 1998).Implementation of the amendments will improve sustainable forest management and also encourage participation of vulnerable groups, who rely on forestry for their livelihoods, into the National Forests Advisory Council.
tgt: 84 wa 1998).Ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha dihlomathiso ho tla ntlafatsa taolo ya moshwelella ya meru le hape ho kgothaletsa bonkakarolo ba dihlopha tse kotsing, tse itshetlehileng hodima tjalo ya meru bakeng sa bophelo ba tsona, ka hara Lekgotla la Naha la Boeletsi la Meru.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: President Jacob Zuma will attend the inauguration and swearing-in ceremony of Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni in Kampala on 12 May 2016.
tgt: Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o tla kenela mokete wa ho behwa le ho nkiswa kano ha Moporesidente wa Uganda Yoweri Museveni Kampala ka la 12 Motsheanong 2016.

src: The outgoing visit will further strengthen bilateral relations between South Africa and Uganda.
tgt: Leeto la ho tswa ka hara naha le tla boela le matlafatsa dikamano tsa bobedi bona pakeng tsa Aforika Borwa le Uganda.

src: President Jacob Zuma will officiate a National Day of Prayer to be held at ABSA Stadium in Durban on 29 April 2016.
tgt: Moporesident Jacob Zuma o tla di hula pele ho ketsahalo ya Letsatsi la Naha la Thapelo e tla tshwarelwa Lebaleng la Dipapadi la ABSA Durban ka la 29 Mmesa 2016.

src: Religious leaders and leaders of civil society formations will join government in praying for the further consolidation of democracy, national unity, social cohesion as well as successful and peaceful 2016 Local Government Elections.
tgt: Baetapele ba Ditumelo le ba mekgatlo ya badudi ba tla imatahanya le mmuso bakeng sa ho rapella ho matlafala ho ya pele ha demokerasi, bonngwe ba setjhaba, momahano ya kahisano hammoho le Dikgetho tsa Mebuso ya Lehae tse atlehileng tsa 2016.

src: Cabinet was briefed on plans by the Department of Arts and Culture to host Africa Month in May 2016 under the theme: “Building a Better Africa and a Better World” as part of the continent’s celebration of the establishment of the Organisation of Africa Unity, now the African Union and the work it has done.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka meralo ya Lefapha la Bonono le Botjhaba ya ho tshwara mokete wa Kgwedi ya Aforika ka Motsheanong 2016 tlasa mookotaba: “Re aha Aforika e Betere le Lefatshe le Betere” jwaloka karolo ya kontinente ya ho keteka ho thehwa ha Kopano ya Mokgatlo wa Aforika, oo hajwale e leng Kopano ya Aforika le mosebetsi oo e o entseng.

src: President Jacob Zuma will launch Africa Month on the National Day of Prayer on 29 April WEBTOKEN 2016 Africa Month will focus on women and youth development initiatives, while we commemorate the 60th year of the Women’s March and the 40th year of the Youth Uprisings in Soweto.
tgt: Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o tla thakgola Kgwedi ya Aforika ka Letsatsi la Naha la Thapelo ka la 29 Mmesa 2016.Ka 2016 Kgwedi ya Aforika e tla tsepamisa maikutlo hodima boikitlaetso ba ntshetsopele ya basadi le batjha, ha re ntse re hopola selemo sa bo-60 sa Mohwanto wa Basadi le selemo sa bo-40 sa Merusu ya Batjha ya Soweto.

src: South Africans are urged to participate in the multi-disciplinary programme that involves a wide range of activities including visual arts, theatre, music, lectures and colloquia as well as the 10th anniversary of the African World Heritage Fund.
tgt: MaAforika Borwa a kgothaletswa ho nka karolo lenaneong lena la dintlha tse ngata le kenyeletsang diketsahalo tse pharaletseng tse akgang ka hare bonono ba pono, theatara, mmino, dithuto le dipuisano hammoho le sehopotso sa bo-10 sa Letlole la Lefatshe la Lefa.

src: Africa Month serves as a platform to reconnect and recommit ourselves to Pan Africanism and African Renaissance in bringing the people of the continent closer.
tgt: Kgwedi ya Aforika e sebetsa jwaloka lepatlelo la ho kopana botjha le ho itlama botjha ho boAforika le Tsoseletso ya Aforika ka ho etsa hore batho ba kontinente ba atamelane ho feta.

src: On 20 May 2016 government will lead the national celebration of the centenary of the University of Fort Hare at the Alice campus in the Eastern Cape.
tgt: Ka la 20 Motsheanong 2016 mmuso o tla etella pele mokete wa naha wa dilemo tse lekgolo wa Yunivesithi ya Fort Hare khemapaseng ya Alice ho la Kapa Botjhabela.

src: In preparation for the main celebration, President Jacob Zuma has established an Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) to plan and coordinate the historic centenary celebration.
tgt: Bakeng sa boitokisetso ba mokete o moholo, Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o thehile Komiti ya Matona (IMC) ho rera le ho hokahanya mokete ona o etsang nalane wa dilemo tse lekgolo.

src: This historic learning institution served as a beacon during our struggle for freedom and is also known as the “crucible of African leadership” with it being the alma mater of anti-apartheid struggle figures such as the great ZK Matthews, Nelson Mandela, Robert Sobukwe, Oliver Tambo and Govan Mbeki.
tgt: Setheo sena sa thuto se etsang nalane se sebeditse jwaloka mokolokotwane nakong ya ntwa ya tokoloho mme hape e tsebahala jwaloka “pitsa ya boetapele ba Aforika” hape e le setsi sa thuto sa mehleng sa batho bao e neng e le bahale ba ntwa kgahlanong le mmuso wa kgethollo ba kang ZK Matthews, Nelson Mandela, Robert Sobukwe, Oliver Tambo le Govan Mbeki.

src: It is the only Southern African university to have produced five heads of state: Nelson Mandela of South Africa, Yusuf Lule of Uganda, Robert Mugabe of Zimbabwe, Ntsu Mokhehle of Lesotho and Sir Seretse Khama of WEBTOKEN part of the University of Fort Hare’s centenary celebrations Cabinet calls on the Alumni and members of the public to share their Fort Hare memories for the Tell Your Story campaign using the hashtag #MyFortHare.
tgt: Ke yona feela yunivesithi ya Aforika e Borwa e hlahisitseng dihlooho tsa puso tse hlano: Nelson Mandela wa Aforika Borwa, Yusuf Lule wa Uganda, Robert Mugabe wa Zimbabwe, Ntsu Mokhehle wa Lesotho le Sir Seretse Khama wa Botswana.

src: Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa will lead the South Africa delegation to the 26th World Economic Forum (WEF) Africa in Rwanda between 11 and 13 May 2016.
tgt: Jwaloka karolo ya ho keteka dilemo tse lekgolo tsa Yunivesithi ya Fort Hare Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho Baithuti ba Mehleng le ditho tsa setjhaba ho arolelana mehopolo ya bona ya Fort Hare bakeng sa letsholo la Re arolele Pale ya Hao ka ho sebedisa hashtag #MyFortHare.

src: The forum is hosted under the theme: “Connecting Africa’s Resources through Digital Transformation”.Government through its Nine-Point Plan is advancing the country’s own digital transformation.
tgt: Motlatsi wa Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa o tla etella pele kemedi ya Aforika Borwa ho Foramo ya bo-26 ya Moruo wa Lefatshe (WEF) ya Aforika ho la Rwanda pakeng tsa la 11 le 13 Motsheanong 2016.

src: It is rolling out the first phase of its broadband initiative that will connect more than 5 000 government facilities in eight district municipalities over a three-year period.
tgt: Foramo e tla tshwarwa tlasa mookotaba: “Re hokahanya Mehlodi ya Aforika ka Diphethoho tsa Dijithale”.Mmuso ka Moralo wa ona wa Dintlha tse Robong o ntshetsapele diphethoho tsa ona tsa dijithale.

src: Funding to the tune of R740 million has been allocated in support of the rollout.
tgt: Thuso ya ditjhelete e ka fihlang ho R740 milione e se abilwe bakeng sa ho tshehetsa phano.

src: INDABA 2016 at the Inkosi Albert Luthuli Convention Centre in Durban from 7 to 9 May 2016, is a Pan-African platform that will promote our tourism products to international buyers.
tgt: INDABA 2016 e tla tshwarwa Setsheng sa Dikopano sa Inkosi Albert Luthuli ho la Durban ho tloha ka la 7 ho isa ho la 9 Motsheanong 2016, ke lepatlelo la Bo-Aforika le tla kgothaletsa dihlahiswa tsa bohahlaudi ho bareki ba matjhaba.

src: Tourism, as one of the six pillars of economic growth of the National Development Plan, contributed R357 billion to our GDP in 2014 and supported 9 per cent of total employment in South Africa.
tgt: Bohahlaudi, jwaloka e nngwe ya ditshiya tse tsheletseng tsa kgolo ya NDP, bo nyehetse R357 bilione ho GDP ya rona ka 2014 le ho tshehetsa diphesente tse 9 tsa mesebetsi ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: The World Travel and Tourism Council estimates that tourism will contribute R560 billion to our GDP by 2025 and will support over two million jobs.
tgt: Lekgotla la Lefatshe la Boeti le Bohahlaudi le akanya hore bohahlaudi bo tla nyehela R560 bilione ho GDP ya rona ka 2025 mme e tla tshehetsa mesebetsi e fetang dimilione tse pedi.

src: Growing the Tourisms impact in the Oceans Economy is a critical pillar of the Nine-Point Plan, informed by the untapped potential of our oceans, which can contribute to economic growth.
tgt: Kgodiso ya kgahlamelo ya Bohahlaudi ho Moruo wa Mawatle ke tshiya e hlokolosi ya Moralo wa Dintlha tse Robong, ha ho shejwa hore ho na le bokgoni bo so kang bo sibollwa hantle ba mawatle a rona, bo ka nyehelang kgolong ya moruo.

src: The oceans economy and tourism provide tremendous opportunities for economic growth and job creation.
tgt: Moruo wa mawatle le bohahlaudi di fana ka menyetla e matla bakeng sa kgolo ya moruo le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi.

src: In commemoration of Workers’ Day on 1 May 2016, Cabinet reiterates the country’s commitment to protect worker rights through our progressive labour legislation.
tgt: Bakeng sa ho hopola Letsatsi la Basebetsi ka la 1 Motsheanong 2016, Kabinete e boeletsa boitlamo ba naha ba ho tshireletsa ditokelo tsa basebetsi ka melao ya rona ya mesebetsi e tswetseng pele.

src: Since 1994 government has through legislation such as the Labour Relations Act, the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, Employment Equity Act and Occupational Health and Safety advanced workers’ rights.
tgt: Ho tloha ka 1994 mmuso ka melao e kang Molao wa Dikamano tsa Basebetsi, Molao wa Maemo a Motheo a Kgiro, Molao wa Tekatekano ya Kgiro le wa Bophelo bo Botle le Polokeho Mosebetsing e hodisitse ditokelo tsa basebetsi.

src: Cabinet urges Grade 12 learners to start downloading application forms or apply online to institutions of higher learning as part of the Apply Now/ Khetha Career Guidance Campaign.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa baithuti ba Kereiti 12 learners ho qala ho hula diforomo tsa kopo kapa ba etse dikopo ka inthanete ho ditsha tsa thuto e phahameng jwaloka karolo ya Letsholo la Apply Now/ Khetha Career Guidance.

src: The Campaign undertaken annually by the Department of Higher Education and Training, will run nationally until September 2016 and assists learners in making informed choices when applying to institutions of higher learning.
tgt: Letsholo lena le nkuwang selemo ka seng ke Lefapha la Thuto e Phahameng le Thupello, le tsamaya naha ka bophara ho fihlela ka Loetse 2016 le ho thusa baithuti ho etsa kgetho e hlokolosi ha ba etsa dikopo ho ditsha tsa thuto e phahameng.

src: Learners are encouraged to contact the Career Development Services Centre through SMS or a “please call me” on 072 204 5056 or 086 999 0123, email EMAILTOKEN, on Facebook at WEBTOKEN or on Twitter at WEBTOKEN Cabinet’s position on key issues in the environment.
tgt: Baithuti ba kgothaletswa ho ikopanya le Setsha sa Ditshebeletso tsa Ntshetsopele ya Makala a Thuto ka SMS kapa “please call me” ho 072 204 5056 kapa 086 999 0123, imeile EMAILTOKEN,Feisebukung ho WEBTOKEN kapa Twitter ho WEBTOKEN Maemo a Kabinete Mabapi le Dintlha tsa Bohlokwa Maemong a Hajwale.

src: Cabinet encourages relevant stakeholders to comment on the draft reviewed Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment Charter for the South African Mining and Minerals Industry, 2016 which was published in the Government Gazette.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa bankakarolo ba amehang ho tshwaela ka moralo wa Tjhata e Shebilweng botjha ya Matlafatso e Pharaletseng ya Matlafatso ya Batho ba Batsho Moruong mabapi le indaseteri ya Aforika Borwa ya Merafo le Diminerale ya 2016 e ileng ya phatlalatswa Koranteng ya Mmuso.

src: The draft reviewed Mining Charter further integrates government’s transformation policies and legislation to enhance the ease of doing business, create regulatory clarity, predictability and certainty.
tgt: Moralo o shebile botjha Tjhata ya Merafo le ho tswela pele ho kopanya maano a mmuso a diphethoho le melao bakeng sa ho matlafatsa bobebe ba ho kena kgwebong, ho hlahisa tlhakiso ya taolo, bokgoni ba tjhebelopele le bonnete.

src: It is also aligned to the provisions of the Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment Act, 2003 (Act No.
tgt: Hape e matahantswe le dipehelo tsa Molao wa Matlafatso ya Moruo o Pharaletseng wa Batho ba Batsho, 2003 (Molao No.

src: 53 of 2003) and the Codes of Good Practice (DTI Codes).
tgt: 53 wa 2003) le Dikhoutu tsa Tshebetso e Ntle (Dikhoutu tsa DTI).

src: Cabinet notes that approval of the proposed acquisition of SAB Miller by AB InBev is under consideration by the competition authorities.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela ho tjhaellwa monwana ha kgapo e lohothwang ya SAB Miller ke AB InBev e ntseng e shebisiswa ke ba ka taolong ba diphehisano.

src: Cabinet welcomes the agreed approach by the Minister of Economic Development and AB InBev to the competition authorities on a range of public interest issues.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela katamelo eo ho dumellanweng ka yona ke Letona la Ntshetsopele ya Moruo le AB InBev le ba ka taolong ba phehisano mabapi le letoto la dintlha tse amang kgahleho ya setjhaba.

src: The commitment by the company serves as a guide, on public interest issues, to other companies in merger and acquisitions in similar circumstances.
tgt: Boitlamo ba khamphani bo sebetsa jwaloka tataiso, hodima dintlha tsa kgahleho ya setjhaba, ho dikhamphani tse ding tse maemong a ho kopana le kgapo tse ikemiseditseng seo.

src: This includes an agreed commitment by the company to spend R1 billion over the next five years to promote small-scale farming and local supplier development, new enterprises, energy and water efficiency technologies and youth development.
tgt: Sena se kenyeletsa boitlamo boo ho dumellanweng ka bona ke khamphani ho sebedisa R1 bilione nakong ya dilemo tse hlano tse tlang bakeng sa ho hodisa dihwai tse nyenyane le ntshetsopele ya bafani ba lehae, dikgwebo tse ntjha, dithekenoloji tsa eneji le metsi tse hlwahlwa le ntshetsopele ya batjha.

src: The commitment on jobs including an undertaking to avoid involuntarily retrenchment of workers as a result of the merger and to maintain employment levels at the company for the next five years, are part of a ground-breaking agreement between the company and government to support industrialisation, small business development and job creation.
tgt: Boitlamo ho tsa mesebetsi ho kenyeletswa le maikemisetso a ho qoba phokotso mosebetsing eo e seng ya boithaopo ya basebetsi ka lebaka la ho kopanngwa le ho baballa maemo a kgiro khamphaning bakeng sa dilemo tse hlano tse tlang, ke karolo ya tumellano ya bohlokwa pakeng tsa khamphani le mmuso ho tshehetsa ntlafatso ya indaseteri, ntshetsopele ya dikgwebo tse nyane le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi.

src: In a separate development, Cabinet notes the coming into effect of provisions of the Competition Amendment Act that makes it a criminal offence for directors and management to collude in the fixing of prices, tenders or markets.
tgt: Ntlheng e nngwe e ka thoko, Kabinete e lemoha ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha dipehelo tsa Sehlomathiso sa Molao wa Phehisano se etsang hore e be tlolo ya molao ya batsamaisi le bolaodi ho etsa mmommori wa ho henahena ditheko, dithenda kapa mebaraka.

src: These provisions are part of the measures to step up the fight against cartels that damage the economy and impose high prices on consumers.
tgt: Dipehelo tsena ke karolo ya ho matlafatsa ntwa kgahlanong le maqulwana a senyang moruo le ho beha ditheko tse hodimo bakeng sa WEBTOKEN ipiletsa ho dikgwebo ka hara Aforika Borwa ho phehisana ho itshetlehilwe hodima ditheko tse tlase, ntlafatso e eketsehileng, boleng bo ntlafetseng ba thepa e fanwang kapa tshebeletso e phahameng ho bareki ho na le mmommori.

src: We call on businesses in South Africa to compete based on lower prices, more innovation, improved quality of goods offered or superior service to customers rather than on collusion.
tgt: Kabinete lemohile kamoo lekala la dibanka le laolwang haholo ka teng Aforika Borwa – le lefatsheng, le tlhokeho ya Aforika Borwa ya ho imatahanya le maemo a matjhaba a kang Basel III le melao e kgahlanong le tshebediso ya tjhelete ka bolotsana ya Lebotho la Tshebetso la Ditjhelete (FATF), tseo esale di tjhaellwa monwana ke Kabinete.

src: Cabinet noted how highly regulated the banking sector is in South Africa - and globally, and the need for South Africa to comply with international standards like Basel III and Anti-money laundering regulations of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), which have been previously approved by Cabinet, and supported by underlying legislation approved by Government.
tgt: Mokgwa wa Twin Peaks le ona o tla laola boitshwaro ba mmaraka ka hara lekala la dibanka le a mang a phatlaletseng a ditjhelete.".

src: The Twin Peaks system will also regulate market conduct in the banking and broader financial sector.".
tgt: Kabinete e amohela diphetho ho tswa ho Kopano ya Selemo ya Letlole la Ditjhelete la Matjhaba le Dihlopha tsa Banka ya Lefatshe ya 2016 e neng e tshwerwe tlasa mookotaba:“diphephetso tsa Lefatshe, Ditharollo tsa Lefatshe”.

src: A three-pronged approach to ignite growth at a global level was proposed, encouraging countries to use all policy levers to spur growth, i. e. monetary, fiscal and structural reforms.
tgt: Katamelo ya dintlha tse tharo ya ho rotetsa kgolo maemong a lefatshe e ile ya sisinngwa, e le ho kgothaletsa dinaha ho sebedisa dibetsa tsohle tsa ho akofisa kgolo, ke hore, ditlhabollo tsa tjhelete, matlotlo le tsa sebopeho.

src: Countries with monetary and fiscal space were encouraged to do more to boost demand however, implementation of structural reforms was critical for all.
tgt: Dinaha tse nang le sebaka sa ditjhelete le matlotlo di ile tsa kgothaletswa ho etsa haholwanyane bakeng sa ho matlafatsa tlhokeho leha ho le jwalo, ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha ditlharollo tsa sebopeho ho ne ho le hlokolosi bakeng sa bohle.

src: For many this includes investment in infrastructure, innovation and improving the regulatory environment, amongst others.
tgt: Ho ba bangata sena se kenyeletsa matsete ho meralo ya motheo, ntjhafatso le ntlafatso ya tikoloho ya bolaodi, hara tse ding.

src: Cabinet reminds all those eligible voters who have not yet registered and verified their details that they can still do so by visiting their local Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) Office.
tgt: Kabinete e hopotsa bakgethi bohle ba tshwanelehang ba so kang ba ingodisa le ho netefatsa dintlha tsa bona hore ba ka nna ba etsa jwalo ka ho etela Kantoro ya bona ya lehae ya Khomishene e Ikemetseng ya Dikgetho (IEC).

src: This is needed to secure your name on the voters’ roll which will enable eligible voters to exercise their democratic right on 3 August 2016.Cabinet urges eligible voters to ensure that they meet the requirement of providing their address to their local Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) office.
tgt: Sena se a hlokahala ho netefatsa lebitso la hao lenaneng la bakgethi e leng se tla thusa bakgethi ba tshwanelehang ho sebedisa tokelo ya bona ya demokerasi ka la 3 Phato 2016.Kabinete e kgothaletsa bakgethi ho netefatsa hore ba kgotsofatsa ditlhokeho tsa ho fana ka diaterese tsa bona kantorong ya Lehae ya Khomishene e Ikemetseng ya Dikgetho (IEC).Dipotso ka ditaba tsa dikgetho di ka lebiswa setsheng sa mehala sa IEC ho 0800 11 8000, se bulwang Mantaha ho isa Labohlano, ho tloha ka 7 hoseng ho isa ka to 9 bosiu.

src: Cabinet congratulates Transnet, National Prosecuting Authority, SABC and the Departments of Higher Education and Training, International Relations and Cooperation, and Justice and Constitutional Development for being ranked “Most Attractive Employers” in South Africa by employer branding company, UNIVERSUCabinet commends Minister of Science and Technology, Naledi Pandor, who received an Order of Merit from the Federal Republic of Germany for her contribution to the development of science globally.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Transnet, Bolaodi ba Naha ba Botjhutjhisi, SABC le Mafapha a Thuto e Phahameng le Thupello, Dikamano tsa Matjhaba le Tshebedisano, le la Toka le Ntshetsopele ya Molaotheo ka ho nkuwa e le “Bahiri ba nang le Kgohedi ka ho fetisisa” ka hara Aforika Borwa ke khamphani ya matshwao, UNIVERSUKabinete e thoholetsa Letona la Saense le Thekenoloji, Naledi Pandor, ya amohetseng Kgau ya Bokgabane ho tswa ho Riphaboliki ya Bofederale ya Jeremane bakeng sa nyehelo ya hae ho tsa saense lefatsheng.

src: The merit has been awarded to people from around the world for their achievements in political, social or intellectual spheres.
tgt: Kgau e fuwa batho ba ho tswa lefatsheng ka bophara bakeng sa diphihlello tsa bona mapatlelong a sepolotiki, a kahisano le a mautlwela.

src: Cabinet congratulates the Environmental Affairs Director-General Nosipho Ngcaba for receiving the 2015/16 Lifetime Achievement Eco-Logic Award from environment publication, The Enviropaedia.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Motsamaisi-Kakaretso wa Lefapha la Merero ya Tikoloho Nosipho Ngcaba bakeng sa ho amohela Kgau ya 2015/16 Lifetime Achievement Eco-Logic ho tswa ho phatlalatso ya Enviropaedia.

src: Cabinet applauds artist Kemang Wa Lehulere for becoming "Artist of the Year" for 2017 which is supported by Deutsche Bank.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa setaki Kemang Wa Lehulere bakeng sa ho ba "Setaki sa sa Selemo" bakeng sa 2017 e leng se tshehetswang ke Deutsche Bank.

src: Wa Lehulere, who explores the relevance of the artistic gesture in post-Apartheid South Africa, will present his first institutional solo exhibition in Germany at the Deutsche Bank KunstHalle in Berlin next year.
tgt: Wa Lehulere, ya sibollang kamano ya pontsho ya bonono ka hara Aforika Borwa ya kamora mmuso wa kgethollo, o tla pepesa dipontsho tsa hae a le mong Jeremane sebakeng sa Deutsche Bank KunstHalle ho la Berlin selemong se tlang.

src: Cabinet congratulates the Department of Tourism for winning the Best Public Policy/Support prize in the 2016 African Responsible Tourism Awards.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Lefapha la Bohahlaudi bakeng sa ho hapa moputso wa Leano/Tshehetso ya Setjhaba e Ipabotseng ka ho fetisisa ho Dikgau tsa 2016 tsa Bohahlaudi bo nang le Boikarabelo.

src: This accolade is awarded to a public sector department, authority or entity that has made a clear commitment and contribution to advancing responsible tourism.
tgt: Makgabane ana a abelwa lefapha la lekala la setjhaba, bolaodi kapa setheo se entseng boitelo bo hlakileng le nyehelo bakeng sa ho hodisa bohahlaudi bo nang le boikarabelo.

src: Cabinet congratulates golfer Branden Grace for winning his first PGA Tour at the RBC Heritage in Hilton Head, UCabinet is saddened by the death of Bertie Lubner who made significant contributions to the development of South Africa as a business leader, philanthropist and honorary life chairman of the SA Jewish Board of Deputies.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa sebapadi sa kolofo Branden Grace bakeng sa ho hapa papadi ya hae ya pele ya PGA Tour ho RBC Heritage ho la Hilton Head, Amerika.

src: Cabinet extends its deepest condolences to the friends and families of the ten victims (Tiisetso Tselo, Sesi Mtshali, Sana Sibeko, Mphikeleli Malindi, Gugulethu Sithole, Vusi Nkabinde, Daphney Linda, Sicelo Kheswa, Sphamandla Gedle and Simphiwe Nhlapo) of a tragic bus crash while they were returning from the ANC Manifesto Rally in Port Elizabeth.
tgt: Kabinete e utlwisitswe bohloko ke lefu la Bertie Lubner ya entseng nyehelo e kgolo bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya Aforika Borwa jwaloka moetapele wa kgwebo, mosebeletsi wa batho le modulasetulo wa tlotlo wa bophelo bohle wa Mokgatlho wa maJuta a Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet conveyed its condolences to the family and friends of Dr Herman Nditsheni Netshidzivhani, South Africa’s first black fertility specialist.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisetsa matshediso a yona a tswang boteng ba pelo ho metswalle le bamalapa a mahlatsipa (Tiisetso Tselo, Sesi Mtshali, Sana Sibeko, Mphikeleli Malindi, Gugulethu Sithole, Vusi Nkabinde, Daphney Linda, Sicelo Kheswa, Sphamandla Gedle le Simphiwe Nhlapo) a kotsi e sisimosang ya bese ha ba ne ba kgutla Raling ya Mohoo wa Dikgetho wa ANC Port Elizabeth.

src: As a founder of the fertility clinic in the Park Lane Hospital in Johannesburg, Netshidzivhani helped many South Africans start their own families.
tgt: Kabinete e fetiseditse matshidiso a yona ho lelapa le metswalle ya Ngaka Herman Nditsheni Netshidzivhani, setsebi sa pele sa Aforika Borwa sa motho e motsho sa bokgoni ba pelehi.

src: Cabinet conveyed condolences to the family and friends of Dene Smuts, former Democratic Alliance Member of Parliament.
tgt: Jwaloka mothei wa tliliniki ya bokgoni ba pelehi ka hara Sepetlele sa Park Lane ho la Johannesburg, Netshidzivhani o thusitse maAforika Borwa a mangata ho qala malapa.

src: Cabinet salutes her sterling contribution to the development of our constitutional democracy.
tgt: Kabinete e fetiseditse matshediso a yona ho lelapa le metswalle ya Dene Smuts, Setho sa Mehleng sa Palamente sa Democratic Alliance.

src: Cabinet joins President Jacob Zuma in wishing Mama Winnie Madikizela-Mandela a speedy recovery and urges that the privacy of the family be respected during this time.
tgt: Kabinete e imatahanya le Moporesidente President Jacob Zuma bakeng sa ho lakaletsa Mama Winnie Madikizela-Mandela pholo e potlakileng le ho kgothaletsa ho hlomphuwa ha boinotshi ba lelapa nakong ena.

src: Winnie Mandela is widely respected for her role in our struggle for freedom which contributed to ending oppressive policies and bringing democracy to South Africa.
tgt: Winnie Mandela o hlomphuwa hohle ka lebaka la karolo ya hae ntweng ya tokoloho e nyehetseng ho phediso ya maano a kgatello le ho tlisa demokerasi Aforika Borwa.

src: AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: DithonyoDithonyo kaofela di ho ya ka netefatso ya mangolo a thuto le tumello e amehang.

src: Paul Steenkamp to the National Advisory Council on Innovation.
tgt: Paul Steenkamp ho Lekgotla la Naha la Boeletsi ka Ntlafatso.

src: Clarinda Elizabeth Simpson as the Chief Financial Officer of SENTECLumko Caesario Mtimde as the Chief Executive Officer of the Universal Services and Access Agency of South Africa.
tgt: Clarinda Elizabeth Simpson jwaloka Mohlanka ya ka Sehloohong wa Ditjhelete wa SENTECLumko Caesario Mtimde jwaloka Mohlanka ya ka Sehloohong wa Phethahatso wa Ditshebeletso tsa Lefatshe le Lekala la Phihlello la Aforika Borwa.

src: Rory Wayne Voller as the Deputy Commissioner of the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission.
tgt: Ho thonngwa hape ha Moatefokate Rory Wayne Voller jwaloka Motlatsi wa Mokhomishenara wa Khomishene ya Dikhamphani le Thepa ya Mautlwela.

src: Extension of the contract for Lungisa Fuzile as the Director General of the National Treasury.
tgt: Katoloso ya konteraka bakeng sa Lungisa Fuzile jwaloka Motsamaisi Kakaretso wa Lefapha la Matlotlo.

src: Extension of the contract for Nosipho Ngcaba as the Director General of the Department of Environmental Affairs.
tgt: Katoloso ya konteraka bakeng sa Nosipho Ngcaba jwaloka Motsamaisi Kakaretso wa Lefapha la Merero ya Tikoloho.

src: N Mafu as the Deputy Director-General: Empowerment and Stakeholder Management in the Department of Military Veterans.
tgt: N Mafu jwaloka Motlatsi wa Motsamaisi-Kakaretso: Matlafatso le Botsamaisi ba Bankakarolo ka hara Lefapha la Mekaubere ya Sesole.

src: TLM Makotoko as the Chief Operations Officer for the Department of Environmental Affairs.
tgt: TLM Makotoko jwaloka Mohlanka ya ka Sehloohong wa Tshebetso bakeng sa Lefapha la Merero ya Tikoloho.

src: Implementation of Key Government Programmes.
tgt: Ho kenngwa Tshebetsong ha Mananeo a Bohlokwa a Mmuso.

src: Cabinet took note of the report-back by the Minister of Finance to the President, on the progress of Government’s consultations with the private sector and labour on the economy.
tgt: Kabinete e lemohile tlalehelo ya Letona la Ditjhelete ho Moporesidente, mabapi le kgatelopele ya dipuisano tsa Mmuso le lekala la poraefete le la mesebetsi ka moruo.

src: The President mandated the Minister to lead engagements with these social partners to map out a strategy and come up with measures for growing the economy and preserving the country’s credit rating.
tgt: Moporesidente o romme Letona hore le etelle pele ditherisano le balekane ba kahisano ho rala lewa le ho tla ka mekgwa ya ho hodisa moruo le ho baballa maemo a naha sekaleng sa mekitlane.

src: Cabinet is pleased that this work has culminated in concrete initiatives that will improve the country’s economic prospects.
tgt: Kabinete e thabile ka hobane mosebetsi ona o tswetse boikitlaetso bo bonahalang bo tla ntlafatsa menyetla ya naha ya moruo.

src: The President announced several priority initiatives on Monday, which include: (1) a joint private and public sector fund for Small Business Support, (2) addressing constraints to increasing investment in order to accelerate inclusive growth, (3) government and private sector co-investment in infrastructure drawing on experience of the successful Independent Power Producer Programme and (4) strengthening State Owned Enterprises to ensure their financial sustainability and reinforcing their role in driving development.
tgt: Moporesidente o tsebisitse dintlha tse seng kae tsa boikitlaetso bo ka sehloohong ka Mantaha, tse kenyeletsang: (1) letlole le kopanetsweng la lekala la poraefete le la setjhaba bakeng sa Tshehetso ya Dikgwebo tse Nyenyane, (2) ho sebetsana le ditshita bakeng sa ho eketsa matsete hore ho tle ho akofiswe kgolo e kenyeletsang, (3) matsete a kopanetsweng ke mmuso le lekala la poraefete ho meralo ya motheo ho itshetlehilwe hodima boiphihlelo ba katleho ya Lenaneo la Bahlahisi ba Matla ba Ikemetseng le (4) ho matlafatsa Dikgwebo tsa Mmuso ho netefatsa maemo a tsona a ditjhelete a moshwelella le ho matlafatsa botjha karolo ya tsona bakeng sa ho kganna ntshetsopele.

src: These announcements are testament to what this country can achieve when all social partners come together to work towards the same goal.
tgt: Ditsebiso tsena ke bopaki ba seo naha ena e ka se fihlellang ha balekane bohle ba kahisano ba ka ikopanya mmoho ho sebeletsa ho fihlella morero o tshwanang.2 Kabinete e dula e na le boitshepo ba hore matlafatso e matla ya matlotlo, pokeletso e etsang nalane ya R1 trilione ke Tshebeletso ya Lekgetho ya Aforika Borwa le boitshunyako ba dintlha tse hlano ba nako e kgutshwane bo tsebisitsweng haufinyana tjena, kaofela di tshehetsa moralo wa Dintlha tse Robong hore ho tle ho netefatswe dintlafalo katlehong ya rona ya moruo.

src: Cabinet remains confident that government’s aggressive fiscal consolidation, the historic R1 trillion collection by the South African Revenue Service and the recently announced five short-term interventions, all complement the Nine Point plan so as to ensure a turn-around in our economic fortunes.
tgt: Pokeletso e eketsehileng ya lekeno ke SARS e tla boela e thuse Mmuso ho fana ka ditshebeletso tse tla ntlafatsa boleng ba bophelo ba baahi ba ona.

src: The increased revenue collection by SARS will further enable Government to deliver services that will improve the quality of lives of all its citizens.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela tsebiso ya lekala le methang maemo a mekitlane, Moody’s Investor Services, leo beke e fetileng le tiiseditseng botjha hore ho methwa ha mekitlane ke dikoto tse pedi ho feta sekala se tlase-tlase sa matsete.

src: Cabinet welcomes the announcement by ratings agency, Moody’s Investor Services, which over the past week reaffirmed the country’s credit rating at two notches above sub-investment grade.
tgt: Bakeng sa ho tiisetsa ho methwa hona, ba ha Moody ba lemohile hore Aforika Borwa e atamela ntlha ya phethoho kamora dilemo tsa kgolo e fokolang le mekgwa e bohale ya matlafatso ditekanyetsong tsa 2016 di tla tsitsisa sekoloto sa mmuso ho GDP selemong sena se hodimo.

src: All parties are agreed that collaborative efforts need to be strengthened to give impetus to the economic recovery.
tgt: Mekga yohle e dumellana hore mekutu ya tshebedisano e lokela ho matlafatswa ho fana ka sekgahla tlhasimolohong ya moruo.

src: We also note that the Minister of Finance’ work with social partners includes a credit ratings workstream that will identify potential reforms and interventions to preserve South Africa’s strong capital markets and investment grade credit rating.4 The President appreciates the Budget Votes by respective Ministers which address the needs of all South Africans.
tgt: Re boela re lemoha hore mosebetsi wa Letona la Ditjhelete le balekane ba kahisano ho kenyeletsa motjha wa tshebetso wa ho methwa ha mekitlane ho tla hlwaya ditlhabollo tse ka bang teng le boitshunyako bakeng sa ho baballa mebaraka e matla ya ditjhelete ya Aforika Borwa le ho methwa ha maemo a sekala sa mekitlane.

src: The progress reports and plans emanating from the Departmental Budget Votes demonstrates that South Africa is a nation at work, with government leading the way, in building a better life for all.
tgt: Ditlaleho tsa kgatelopele le meralo e tswang ho Dipuo tsa Ditekanyetso tsa Mafapha di bontsha hore Aforika Borwa ke setjhaba se keneng mosebetsing, ka mmuso o supang tsela, bakeng sa ho aha bophelo bo botle bakeng sa bohle.

src: Concrete measures have been put in place to reduce the negative impact of the global economic downturn on our economy, and to prepare for robust growth when the economic cycle turns positive.
tgt: Mekgwa e bonahalang e se e kentswe tshebetsong ho fokotsa sekgahla se sebe sa ho wa ha moruo wa lefatshe hodima moruo wa rona, le ho itokisetsa kgolo e matla ha tsamao ya moruo e bontsha ho loka.

src: We are also working hard to remove domestic impediments to growth.
tgt: Hape re sebetsa ka matla ho tlosa ditshita tsa ka lapeng tsa kgolo ya moruo.

src: The budget votes also demonstrate that government, labour and business are working together, more than any other time, to find ways of re-igniting growth and building a better life for all.
tgt: Dipuo tsa ditekanyetso hape di bontsha hore mmuso, lekala la mesebetsi le dikgwebo di sebetsa mmoho, ho feta ka nako efe kapa efe, ho fumana ditsela tsa ho rotetsa botjha kgolo le kaho ya bophelo bo betere bakeng sa bohle.

src: This includes vigorous implementation of the Nine Point Plan, announced by President Jacob Zuma in his 2015 State of the Nation Address as well as Operation Phakisa, designed to fast track implementation of solutions to critical development areas.
tgt: Sena se kenyeletsa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ho matla ha Moralo wa Dintlha tse Robong, o tsebisitsweng ke Moporesidente Jacob Zuma ho Puo ka Maemo a Setjhaba ya 2015 hammoho le Operation Phakisa, e reretsweng ho potlakisa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha ditharollo tsa dibaka tsa ntshetsopele tse hlokolosi.

src: These programmes address critical issues from the National Development Plan, such as reducing poverty and unemployment.
tgt: Mananeo ana a sebetsana le dintlha tse hlokolosi ho tswa ho Lewa la Naha la Ntshetsopele, tse kang ho fokotsa bofuma le tlhokeho ya mesebetsi.

src: Cabinet reassures South Africans that the country’s unemployment situation is being addressed through the implementation of the country’s National Development Plan (NDP) through the Nine Point Plan economic intervention which seeks to ignite growth and boost jobs in key sectors of our economy.
tgt: Kabinete e netefaletsa maAforika Borwa hore boemo ba naha ba tlhokeho ya mesebetsi ho ntse ho sebetsanwa le bona ka ho kenngwa tshebetsong Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP) ka boitshunyako ba moruo ka Moralo wa Dintlha tse Robong oo sepheo sa ona e leng ho rotetsa kgolo le ho matlafatsa mesebetsi makaleng a bohlokwa a moruo wa rona.

src: The collaboration of the private sector is pivotal for a successful outcome.
tgt: Tshebedisano ya lekala la poraefete ke taba e ka sehloohong bakeng sa sephetho se atlehileng.

src: Government is using all available initiatives including its Industrial Policy Action Plan (IPAP) to create more labour absorbing production and services sectors to address unemployment which has been further impacted by the difficult global and local economic conditions.
tgt: Mmuso o sebedisa dintlha tsohle tsa boikitlaetso tse teng ho kenyeletswa le Moralo wa Tshebetso wa Leano la Diindaseteri (IPAP) ho bopa tlhahiso e hohelang basebetsi haholwanyane le makala a ditshebeletso ho sebetsana le tlhokeho ya mesebetsi ho mpefaditsweng ho feta ke maemo a boima a moruo wa lefatshe le wa lehae.

src: Minister of Trade and Industry, Rob Davies launched the eighth annual iteration of the IPAP 2016/17 to 2018-19 on 9 May 2016 at a 100% black-owned casting and machining foundry in Gauteng.
