tgt: Dithonyo tsa kantoro ya Moporesidente ho Lekgotla la Dinyewe tsa Naha tsa Bareki, le tla qala ho sebetsa ho tloha ka letsatsi la Taelo ya Boporesidente e amehang:Moporofesara Joseph Mandal Maseko (Modulasetulo wa Phethahatso)Mofumahadi Laura Best (Motlatsi wa Modulasetulo)Monghadi Lulama Andisa Potwana (setho sa nako tsohle)Mofumahadi Penelope Anne Beck (setho sa nakwana)Moatefokate Hope Fiona Neo Sephoti (setho sa nakwana)Mofumahadi Diane Reinette Terblanche (setho sa nakwana)Mofumahadi Nomfundo Maseti (setho sa nakwana)Mofumahadi Maleho Margaret Daisy Nkomo (setho sa nakwana)Moporofesara Bonke Clayton Dumisa (setho sa nakwana)Moporofesara Tanya Ann Woker (setho sa nakwana)Moporofesara Kasturi Moodaliyar (setho sa nakwana)Ngaka Maria Claudina du Toit (setho sa nakwana)Monghadi Xolela Christopher May (setho sa nakwana)Monghadi Fungai Khumbulani Sibanda (setho sa nakwana)Monghadi Lehlohonolo Lucky Rabotapi (setho sa nakwana)Monghadi Trevor Albert Bailey (setho sa nakwana) leMoatefokate Frans Kgolela Manamela (setho sa nakwana).Thonyo ya ditho tseo e seng tsa phethahatso ho Boto ya Khoporeishene ya Dibetsa ya Aforika Borwa (ARMSCOR):Motlatsi wa Moadimirale (ya behileng mejafatshe) RJ Mudimu (Modulasetulo ebile o thontswe hape)Mofumahadi Thuthukile Skweyiya (Motlatsi wa Modulasetulo ebile o thontswe hape)Ngaka Moses Khanyile (o thontswe hape)Monghadi Ndumiso M Tyibilika (o thontswe hape)Monghadi Raymond Mlungwana Vokwana (o thontswe hape)Moatefokate Virginia Lee Anne De La Hunt (o thontswe hape)Mofumahadi CE SimpsonMofumahadi T Mhlan leMoambasadara TJ Ndhlovu.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 10 May 2017, at Tuynhuys, Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e kopane ka Laboraro, la 10 Motsheanong 2017, Tuynhuys, Motse Kapa.

src: Cabinet welcomes the successful hosting of the 27th World Economic Forum on Africa, which saw President Jacob Zuma leading Team South Africa, Heads of State and Governments from the African continent, global captains of industry and commerce and civil society leadership.
tgt: Foramo ya Moruo wa Lefatshe (WEF) ya AforikaKabinete e amohela ho tshwarwa ka katleho ha WEF ya Aforika ya bo-27 mooMoporesidente Jacob Zuma a neng a eteletse pele Moifo wa Aforika Borwa, Dihlooho tsa Dipuso le Mebuso ho tswa kontinenteng ya Aforika, baetapele ba lefatshe ba diindaseteri le dikgwebo le ketapele ya setjhaba ka kakaretso.

src: The conference was held under the theme: “Achieving inclusive growth: responsive and responsible leadership”.
tgt: Pitso e ne e tshwerwe tlasa mookotaba:“Re fihlella kgolo e kenyeletsang: boetapele bo arabelang le ho ikarabella”.Ho dula habo-27 ha WEF ya Aforika ho tiiseditse lefatshe botjha hore Aforika Borwa e dula e le karolo ya sebaka se nang le bokgoni ba matsete ka hara kontinente ya Aforika.

src: This 27th session of the WEF on Africa reaffirmed to the world that South Africa remains part of the potential investment destination in the African continent.
tgt: Bahlophisi ba tiisitse hore baemedi ba fetang 1000 ba ne ba kenetse ketsahalo eo, e leng palo e neng e sa lebellwa ha ho bapiswa leWEF ya Aforika e fetileng.

src: The organisers confirmed that more than 1 000 delegates attended the event, a number that is unprecedented when compared with the previous WEF on Africa.
tgt: Moya o matla wa bolekane pakeng tsa mmuso le boradikgwebo nakong ya WEF ya Aforika o ne o le kgabane haholo.

src: The strong spirit of partnership between government and the business community during WEF on Africa was extremely positive.
tgt: Puisano e matla e nehile Aforika Borwa monyetla wa ho bontsha kgatelopele eo o e etsang e lebisang kgolong ya moruo e kenyeletsang le ho bontsha hore Aforika Borwa e bulehile bakeng sa kgwebo.

src: The rich discussion afforded South Africa an opportunity to showcase progress it was making towards an inclusive economic growth and to demonstrate that South Africa is open to business.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tla dula e itlametse ho dula motjheng wa ho kenya tshebetsong Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP) ho fokotsa maemo a bofuma, ho se lekalekane le tlhokeho ya mesebetsi.

src: South Africa remains committed to staying on course in implementing its National Development Plan (NDP) to reduce levels of poverty, inequality and unemployment.
tgt: Dipalangwang Hothakgolwa ha diterene tse ntjha le tshebeletso ya Lekala la Bapalami ba Diterene la Aforika Borwa(PRASA), ke Moporesidente Jacob Zuma ka la 9 Motsheanong 2017 Seteisheneng sa Pretoria ke karolo ya boitlamo ba mmuso bo tswelang pele ba ho netefatsa dipalangwang tsa setjhaba tse kgonehang le ho tshepahala, le ho matlafatsa meralo ya motheo ya moruo wa naha.

src: The launch of the new Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa (PRASA) trains and train service by President Zuma on 9 May 2017 at the Pretoria Station is part of government’s ongoing commitment to ensure affordable and reliable public transport, and boost the country’s economic infrastructure.
tgt: Diterene tse ntjha tsa Metrorail (tse palangwang ke Batho) ke karolo ya diterene tse ntjha tse tla fanwa ke mmuso nakong ya dilemo tse10 ho isa ho tse15 tse tlang e le karolo ya Lenaneo la Sejwalejwale la PRASBoikitlaetso bona bo tla bopa dikete tsa mesebetsi ya moshwelella le menyetla ya mosebetsi, ka polante e motjheng e tla hlahisa diterene tse ntjha e Nigel, WEBTOKEN qalo ya ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Tumellano ya Fora le Brazil e saennweng pakeng tsa PRASA le Alstom.

src: The new Metrorail (People's) trains are part of the new fleet that will be rolled out by government over the next 10 to 15 years as part of PRASA’s Modernization Programme.
tgt: Diterene tse ntjha tsa maemo tsa Metrorail (tse palangwang ke Batho) di fana ka maemo a se nang thaka a boiketlo le tshebeletso, mme di tla fetola boiphihlelo ba maeto a terene a bapalami.

src: This initiative will create thousands of sustainable jobs and job opportunities, with the manufacturing plant for the new trains underway in Nigel, Ekurhuleni.
tgt: Ke karolo ya mmuso ya ntshetsopele ya moruo ka ntshetsopele e matla ya meralo ya motheo mme diterene tsena di lokile bakeng sa batho ba qhwadileng.

src: It is the beginning of the operationalization of the French and Brazil Agreement signed between PRASA and Alstom.
tgt: Kabinete e ipileditse ho maAforika Borwa kaofela ho ba motlotlo le ho tshireletsa diterene tse ntjha kgahlanong le diketso tsa bosenyi.

src: The new state-of-the-art Metrorail (People's) trains offer unparalleled levels of comfort and service, and will transform commuters’ travelling experience.
tgt: Boipelaetso ba VuwaniKabinete e amohela boitshunyako bo atlehileng ba Moporesident Zuma, Vuwani, ho la Limpopo.

src: Cabinet made a call to all South Africans to be proud of and protect the new trains against acts of vandalism.
tgt: Kopano e amohetse tshisinyo ya Motlotlehi ya hore Masepala wa Setereke wa Vhembe o tshwanetse ho fana ka ditshebeletso ho batho ba Vuwani ha ho ntse ho batlanwa le tharollo ya moshwelella ya ntlha ya tsheho ya meedi.

src: The engagement of the President and all the stakeholders resulted in schooling and business operations returning to normal.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho batswadi le badudi ho tshehetsa maitshunyako a mafapha ho netefatsa hore bana ba kgutlela dikolong le ho tsepamisa maikutlo le ho kgahlametsa nako e senyehileng ka maitshunyako a sebediswang dikolong.

src: Cabinet appeals to parents and the community to support the departmental interventions to ensure that learners are back in class and focus on learning and catching up through interventions being rolled out at all schools.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsabadudi ho nyahlatsa merusu, ditshoso le ho utswa thepa ha ba hlahisa dingongoreho tsa bona.

src: Violent protests Cabinet urges communities to refrain from violence, intimidation and looting when they raise their concerns.
tgt: Merusu le diketso tsa ho utswa thepa le tshenyo ya thepa ya dikgwebotse etsahetseng haufinyana tjena Coligny,Eldorado Park le Ennerdale di tshwelwa ka mathe ka matla ke Kabinete.

src: The violence and acts of looting and the destruction of business properties that took place recently in Coligny, Eldorado Park, and Ennerdale is strongly condemned by Cabinet.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho badudi ho hlahisa matshwenyeho a bona ka mokgwa o batlang ditharollo ntle le ho senya thepa ya setjhaba kapa ho hatikela ditokelo tsa ditho tse ding tsa setjhaba.

src: Cabinet calls on communities to raise their concerns in a manner that seeks solutions without necessarily destroying public property or infringing on the rights of other members of society.
tgt: Moporesidente o entse kgoeletso ka selemo sa 2015 Nakong ya Puo ya Maemo a Naha, a ipiletsa ho Moifo wa Toka, Thibelo ya Botlokotsebe le Tshireletso (JCPS) ho sebetsana ka matla le boipelaetso bo tletseng merusu le tshenyo.

src: During his State of the Nation Address in 2015, President Zuma made a call on the Justice, Crime Prevention and Security Cluster to deal decisively with violent and destructive protests.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa kgoeletso ena ya hore ba tlolang molao ba tla tobana le letsoho le matla la molao.

src: Cabinet urges all stakeholders to engage with the view to speedily resolving the disputes in Ennerdale, Eldorado Park and Coligny.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa bankakarolo bohle ho buisana ka morero wa ho rarolla ka potlako dikgang Ennerdale, Eldorado Park le Coligny.

src: Financial Intelligence Centre Amendment Act.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Setsi sa Mautlwela a Ditjhelete.

src: Cabinet welcomes the signing of the Financial Intelligence Centre Amendment Bill into law by President Zuma.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho sennwa ha Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Setsi sa Mautlwela a Ditjhelete (FICA) hore e be molao keMoporesidenteZuma.

src: South Africa, as part of the global community that is aligned with fighting illegal financial activities, will be aligned to the international intervention that seeks to fight money laundering and financing of terrorism.
tgt: Aforika Bowa jwaloka karolo ya badudi ba lefatshe e imatahantseng le ho lwantsha diketso tse seng molaong tsa ditjhelete, e tla imatahanya le boitshunyako ba matjhaba bo batlang ho lwantsha ho pata mohlodi wa tjhelete le ho thusa boferakanyi ka ditjhelete.

src: This Bill will also contribute to strengthening the transparency and integrity of the South African financial system and make it harder for criminals involved in tax evasion, money laundering and illicit financial flows to hide using the South African financial systems.
tgt: Bili ena hape e tla nyehela mabapi le ho matlafatsa ponaletso le seriti tsa tsamaiso ya ditjhelete ya Aforika Borwa le ho etsa hore ho be thata bakeng sa ditlokotsebe ho baleha ho lefa lekgetho, ho pata mohlodi wa tjhelete le ho pata phallo e seng molaong ya ditjhelete ba sebedisa mekgwa ya tsamaiso ya ditjhelete ya Aforika Borwa.

src: It forms part of the number of instruments we have as a country to fight white-collar crime in both the private and public sectors.
tgt: E bopa se seng sa disebediswa tse ngata tseo re nang le tsona jwaloka naha bakeng sa ho lwantsha botlokotsebe ba maemo a hodimo makaleng ka bobedi a poraefete le a mmuso.

src: Cabinet was apprised by the Minister of Finance that consultations are ongoing and will be finalised soon so as to ensure the process of promulgating the regulations that will effect the Financial Intelligence Centre Act.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ke Letona la Ditjhelete hore ditherisano di ntse di tswela pele mme di tla phethelwa haufinyana ho netefatsamotjha wa phatlalatso ya melawana e tla kenya tshebetsong Molao wa FICDiqeto tsa KabineteLetona la Ditjhelete le tsebisitse Kabinete ka dikopano tsa haufinyana tjena tsa Selemo tsa Letlole laLefatshe la Ditjhelete (IMF)/ tsa Banka ya Lefatshe, dikopano tsa Leeto la Dipontsho le Batsetedi le tsa WEF ya Aforika.

src: The Minister of Finance briefed Cabinet on the recent International Monetary Fund/World Bank Spring meetings, Investor Roadshow and the WEF on Africa meetings.
tgt: Hape le tsebisitse ka ditshisinyo tsa Aforika ho G20 Compact le matshwenyeho a batsetedi le makala a Balekodi ba mekitlane.

src: He further briefed Cabinet on the G20 Compact with Africa proposals, and investors’ and rating agencies’ concerns.
tgt: Ho bile le dipuisano tse matla mabapi le tjhebahalo ya moruo wa lefatshe le wa lebatowa le seo re lokelang ho se etsa ho etsolla ho theolwa ha maemo a moruo.

src: There was an extensive discussion on the world and regional economic outlook, and what we need to do to reverse the downgrades.
tgt: Kabinete e boeleditse hore e dula e itlamme bakeng sa boemo ba leano la ditjhelete tsa mmuso le tekilweng Puong ya Ditekanyetso ya selemo sa 2017, ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha diphethoho bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa taolo ya dikhamphani tsa mmuso ho baballa sekepele se amohelehang sa ditshenyehelo le ho netefatsa botsitso ba mekitlane ya mmuso.

src: Cabinet reiterated that it remains committed to the fiscal policy trajectory outlined in the Budget Speech 2017 the implementation of reforms to improve governance in state-owned companies maintain the expenditure ceiling and ensuring stabilization of government debts.
tgt: Lenaneo la Mmuso la ho akofisa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha diphethoho tsa dibopeho tse reretsweng ho matlafatsa kgolo ya moruo jwaloka ha di tekilwe ho Moralo wa Dintlha tse Robong le dula le nepahetse bakeng sa ho tobana le dintlha tse ding tse hlahisitsweng ke batsetedi.

src: Government’s programme on fast-tracking the implementation of structural reforms aimed at boosting economic growth, as contained in the Nine-Point Plan, remains relevant to addressing some of the issues raised by investors.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela tlaleho e lokolotsweng haufinyana ke feme ya boeletsi ya EY Consultancy mabapi le Matsete a Otlolohileng ka hara Aforika.

src: The report names South Africa as one of the largest economic hub and that it is ranked second in the 2017 Africa Attractiveness Index.
tgt: Tlaleho e supa Aforika Borwa jwaloka setsi se seholo ka ho fetisisa sa moruo le ho behwa maemong a bobedi ho Lenane la Kgohedi la Aforika la selemo sa 2017.Kabinete hape e tsebisitswe ka leeto le tlang la Makala a Bolekodi ba mekitlane ho buisana le mekgatlo e mengata le bahlomphehi ba phethahatso ba mmuso.

src: Cabinet was also apprised on the upcoming visits by the rating agencies to interact with a number of organisations and government executives.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Moralo wa Lewa le Shebilweng Botjha la Dipalangwang tsa Metse ya Mahae.

src: Cabinet approved the Draft Reviewed Rural Transport Strategy.
tgt: Lewa lena le arabela ho dintlha tse ka sehlohlolong tsa bomasepala ba setereke le diporofense, ka ho tobana le phano e sa lokang ya Meralo ya Motheo ya Dipalangwang tsa Metse ya Mahae le ditshebeletso e fokotsang ntshetsopele ya moruo wa kahisano.

src: The strategy responds to the priorities of rural district municipalities and provinces, by addressing the inadequate provision of Rural Transport Infrastructure and services which limits socio-economic development.
tgt: Ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha lewa lena ho tla nyehela bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya moruo wa lehae le wa porofense ka ho ntlafatsa phumantsho ya dipalangwang tsa setjhaba.

src: Implementation of this strategy will contribute towards the development of the local and provincial economy by improving access to public transport.
tgt: Sena se tla eketsa kgokahanyo pakeng tsa dibaka tsa ditoropo le tsa mahae, ka morero wa ho kenyeletsa tikoloho tsa mahaeng ka hara moruo o bataletseng.

src: Cabinet approved the Comprehensive Maritime Transport Policy.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Leano le Pharaletseng la Dipalangwang tsa Mawatleng.

src: This articulates government’s commitment to the growth, development and transformation of South Africa’s maritime transport sector, in support of socio-economic development while contributing to international trade.
tgt: Sena se supa boitlamo ba mmuso bakeng sa kgolo, ntshetsopele le diphethoho tsa lekala la dipalangwang tsa mawatleng tsa Aforika Borwa, mabapi le ho tshehetsa ntshetsopele ya moruo wa kahisano ha ka nqa e nngwe le nyehela kgwebisanong ya matjhaba.

src: This is in line with the government priorities relating to Operation Phakisa on growing the Oceans Economy.
tgt: Sena se tsamaelana le dintlha tse ka sehlohlolong tsa mmuso tse amanang le Operation Phakisa mabapi leho hodisa Moruo wa Mawatle.

src: It is also aligned to broader goals of promoting economic growth and boosting job creation, as outlined in the NDP and National Infrastructure Plan.
tgt: Hape se tsamaelana le merero e bataletseng ya ho hodisa kgolo ya moruo le ho matlafatsa tlhahiso ya mesebetsi, jwaloka ha ho tekilwe ho NDP le Moralo wa Naha wa Meralo ya Motheo.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the Draft Green Transport Strategy for public comments.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana phatlalatso ya Moralo wa Lewa la Dipalangwang tse Hlwekileng bakeng sa tshwaelo ya setjhaba.

src: Transport plays a key role in enabling global trade in an economically, socially and environmentally sustainable manner.
tgt: Dipalangwang di bapala karolo ya bohlokwa mabapi le ho kgontsha kgwebisano ya matjhaba ka mokgwa o tla bang wa moshwelella ho tsa moruo, kahisano le tikoloho.

src: Transport systems form the backbone of South Africa’s socio-economic activities by enabling the movement of people and goods.
tgt: Mekgwa ya Dipalangwang e bopa mokokotlo wa mesebetsi ya moruo wa kahisano ka ho thusa ka ho tsamaiswa ha batho le dithoto.

src: However, emissions from the transport sector contribute to the country’s total greenhouse gas emissions (GHG), with road transport being the leading contributor.
tgt: Leha ho le jwalo, mesi e tswang lekaleng la dipalangwang e nyehela ho palo kaofela ya ho ntshuwa ha dikgase tse kotsi (GHG), moo makoloi e leng ona a nyehelang haholo.

src: The strategy seeks to propose interventions that will reduce GHG emissions within the sustainable development principles.
tgt: Lewa lena le rerile ho sisinya maitshunyako a tla fokotsa mesi ya GHG ka hara dipehelo tsa ntshetsopele ya moshwelella.

src: Cabinet approved that South Africa joins the Smart Africa Alliance.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana hore Aforika Borwa e kenele Smart Africa Alliance.

src: This is an African-led collaboration focusing on developing relevant solutions and sharing resources to address the development challenges facing the continent.
tgt: Sena ke tshebedisano e etelletsweng pele ke Aforika mabapi le ho hlahisa le ho abelana mehlodi ya ho tobana le diphephetso tsa ntshetsopele tse shebaneng le kontinente.

src: It places Information and Communications Technologies at the centre of the Development Agenda 2063 of African countries.
tgt: E beha Dithekenoloji tsa Tlhahisoleseding le Dikgokahanyo bohareng ba lenaneo la ntshetsopele la selemo sa 2063 la dinaha tsa Aforika.

src: South Africa will benefit both economically and politically through its participation in Smart WEBTOKEN positioning the South African industry and expertise at the heart of Smart Africa’s development agenda, South Africa will contribute to the growth of local business in the region.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tla kgola molemo ka bobedi ho tsa moruo le sepolotiki ka bonkakarolo ba yona ho Smart Africa.

src: Cabinet approved the promulgation of the Department of Basic Education National Policy on Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), Sexually Transmitted Infections and Tuberculosis (TB).
tgt: Ka ho beha diindaseteri tsa Aforika Borwa bohareng ba lenaneo la ntshetsopele la Smart Africa, Aforika Borwa e tla nyehela kgolong ya kgwebo ya lehae ka hara lebatowa.

src: The 1999 policy focused on universal precautions and biomedical aspects of prevention, and less on the structural, social and behavioral drivers of HIV.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwanaphatlalatso ya Leano la Naha la Lefapha la Thuto ya Motheo ya (HIV), Ditshwaetso tse Fetiswang ka Thobalano (di-STI) le Lefuba (TB).Leano lena la selemo sa1999 le tsepamisitse maikutlo hodima ditemoso tse tlwaelehileng le dintlha tsa bophelo tsa bongaka tsa thibelo, le hanyenyane hodima mekgwa ya boitshwaro ya dibopeho le ya kahisano e hlohleletsang HIV.

src: This policy proposes a paradigm shift towards approaching HIV as a core management issue using a public-health approach, as well as the inclusion of TB as a priority within schools, amongst others.
tgt: Leano lena le sisinya tsela ya ho swaela lehakoreng la ho bona HIV jwaloka taba e bohareng ya bolaodi ho sebediswa katamelo ya bophelo bo botle ba setjhaba, hammoho le ho kenyeletswa ha TB jwaloka ntlha e ka sehlohlolong ka hara dikolo, hara tse ding.

src: The scope of application is widened to learners, educators and officials, in public as well as independent schools.
tgt: Ho phatlalla ha tshebediso ho pharaleditswe ho ya baneng, matitjhereng le ho bahlanka, dikolong tsa mmuso le tsa poraefete.

src: Cabinet approved the introduction of the Airports Company Amendment Bill, 2017 and the Air Traffic and Navigation Services Amendment Bill to Parliament.
tgt: DibiliKabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho hlahiswa haSehlomathiso sa Bili ya Khamphani ya Maemafofane, ya selemo sa 2017 le Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Ditshebeletso tsa Sephethephethe sa Moyeng le Tsamaiso ya Difofane Palamenteng.

src: Amendments in these two Bills seek to provide for a permanent regulatory structure.
tgt: Diphetoho dibiling tsena tse pedi di reretswe bakeng sa ho fana ka Sebopeho sa Taolo sa moshwelella.

src: They also provide for the setting up of appeal mechanism committees, which will serve to resolve disputes.
tgt: Hape diphethoho di fana ka monyetla wa ho theha dikomiti tsa mekgwa ya maipiletso, tse tla sebetsa mabapi le ho rarolla dikgang dife kapa dife.

src: Upcoming events President Zuma will deliver the opening address at the 2017 Tourism Indaba, which will be hosted at the Inkosi Albert Luthuli International Convention Centre in Durban between 16 and 18 May 2017.This is the international Indaba that will again showcase South Africa’s products and services in the tourism and hospitality sector.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlangMoporesidente Jacob Zuma o tla fana ka puo ya pulo ya Indaba ya Bohahlaudi ya selemo sa2017 e tla tshwarelwa Setsing sa Matjhaba sa Dikopano sa Inkosi Albert Luthuli Durban pakeng tsa la 16 le la 18 Motsheanong 2017.Ena ke indaba ya matjhaba eo hape e tla pepesa dihlahiswa le ditshebeletso tsa Aforika Borwa ka hara lekala la bohahlaudi le bodulo ba baeti.

src: Tourism Indaba 2017 will also promote and support the ongoing transformation and development of the South African tourism industry, notably the role entrepreneurs and small-business owners WEBTOKEN South Africa, more than 10 million international tourists arrived in 2016, 13% more than 2015.
tgt: Indaba ya Bohahlaudi ya 2017 hape e tla hodisa le ho tshehetsa diphethoho tse ntseng di tswela pele le ntshetsopele ya indaseteri ya bohahlaudi ya Aforika Borwa ka ho qolleha karolo e bapalwang ke baetapele ba dikgwebo le beng ba dikgwebo tse nyenyane.

src: This is well over the global average growth rate of 3% for the period.
tgt: Sena se ka hodimo ho feta palohare ya sekgahla sa kgolo ya lefatshe sa 3 % bakeng sa nako eo.

src: During this period of the Tourism Indaba, South Africa will benefit from the number of delegates that will be visiting our country.
tgt: Nakong ya indaba ena ya Bohahlaudi, Aforika Borwa e tla kgola molemo ho tswa palong ya baemedi ba tla kena naheng ya bo rona.

src: The Minister of Energy, Ms Mmamoloko Kubayi, will this month lead the Energy Month campaign under the theme: “Promoting affordable and sustainable energy mix in support of radical socio-economic transformation”.
tgt: Letona la Eneji Mmamoloko Kubayi kgweding ena o tla etella peleletsholo la Kgwedi ya Eneji tlasa mookotaba,“Re kgothaletsa motswako wa eneji e kgonehang le ya moshwelella mabapi le ho tshehetsa diphethoho tse matla tsa moruo wa kahisano”.

src: The campaign will educate, create awareness and engage the public on energy efficiency, energy security, alternative energy matters and how they are all central to household, commercial and industrial consumption.
tgt: Letsholo le tla ruta, le bope temoso le ho buisana le setjhaba mabapi le bokgabane ba eneji, polokeho ya eneji, dintlha tsa eneji e nngwe e fapaneng le kamoo e leng tsa bohlokwa bakeng sa tshebediso ya malapa, dikgwebo le diindaseteri.

src: The 2017 Departmental Budget Votes in May 2017 present an opportunity for departments to present to Parliament and the general public how they will be use the 2017 budgets allocated to them.
tgt: Dingangisano tsa Ditekanyetso tsa Mafapha tsa selemo sa2017ka Motsheanong2017 di hlahisa monyetla wa mafapha a ho hlahisa Palamenteng le setjhabeng ka kakaretso kamoo a tla sebedisang Ditekanyetso tseo a di abetsweng tsa selemo sa 2017.

src: They will use these submissions to also share with the public what their programmes will entail for the current financial year.
tgt: A tla sebedisa dintlha tsena hape hore a abelane le setjhaba hore ke eng seo mananeo a ona a se fupereng bakeng sa selemo sa hajwale sa ditjhelete.

src: Cabinet calls on the public to engage with these presentations as they are presented through the parliamentary process.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho setjhaba ho itahlela ka setotswana ditlhakisetsong tsena kaha di hlahiswa ka motjha wa Palamente.

src: The Department of Water and Sanitation will host Sanitation Week between 16 and 22 May 2017 under the theme: “Sanitation for Health and Dignity”.
tgt: Lefapha la Metsi le Tsamaiso ya Dikgwerekgwere le tla tshwara Beke ya Dikgwerekgwere pakeng tsa la 16 le la 22 Motsheanong 2017 tlasa mookotaba: “Tsamaiso ya Dikgwerekgwere bakeng sa Bophelo bo botle le Seriti”.Mmuso o itlamme ho tlisa seriti ho maAforika Borwa ka phano ya ditshebeletso tsa tsamaiso ya dikgwerekgwere.

src: The main focus during the week will be the priority Bucket Eradication Programme.
tgt: Ntlha e ka sehloohong e tla tsepamisetswa maikutlo bekeng ena e tla ba taba e ka sehlohlolong ya Lenaneo la Phediso ya Mabakete.

src: This will see the handover of waterborne sanitation to communities in the Nketoana Local Municipality, Free State and Dawid Kruiper Local Municipality, Northern Cape, as part of accelerating services to replace bucket toilets.
tgt: Sena se tla bonahala ka phano ya dintlwana tse sebedisang metsi Masepala wa Lehae waNketoana, ho la Freistata le Masepaleng wa Lehae wa Dawid Kruiper, ho la Kapa Leboya jwaloka karolo ya ho akofisa ditshebeletso bakeng sa ho fedisa matlwana a mabakete.

src: South Africa is celebrating Africa Month under the theme: “Building a better Africa and a Better World”.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e keteka Kgwedi ya Aforika tlasa mookotaba: Aforika e Betere le Lefatshe le Betere.

src: The Department of Arts and Culture is leading a number of activities which are aimed at promoting African unity.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse ngata di ntse di tswela pele tse eteletsweng pele ke Lefapha la Bonono le Botjhabatse reretsweng ho kgothaletsa bonngwe ba Aforika.

src: The activities will culminate in a luncheon hosted by President Zuma at the Sefako Makgatho Presidential guesthouse on 25 May 2017.
tgt: Diketsahalo tsena di tla fihla sehlohlolong ka la 25 Motsheanong 2017 moo Moporesidente Zuma a tla hlophisang dijo tsa motsheare ntlong ya baeti ya Boporesidente ya Sefako Makgatho.

src: Invited to the luncheon will be the leaders of organisations of foreign nationals resident in South Africa, which the President met with during SANDF deployment Cabinet welcomes the decision by President Zuma to extend the deployment of members of the South African National Defence Force (SANDF) in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
tgt: Ba memetsweng dijong e tla ba baetapele ba mekgatlo ya melata ba dulang ka hara Aforika Borwa bao Moporesidente a kopaneng le bona ka selemo sa Tshebediso ya Lebotho la Naha la Tshireletso (SANDF).

src: This is in an effort to contribute to peace and stability on the African continent and in particular the region in line with our international obligations and our foreign policy of contributing to a better Africa and world.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela qeto ya Moporesidente Jacob Zuma ya hoatolosa ho sebediswa ha ditho tsa SANDF ho la Rephabliki ya Demokerasi ya Congo (DRC).Sena ke mohato wa ho nyehela bakeng sa kgotso le botsitso kontinenteng ya Aforika mme ka ho qolleha lebatoweng la rona ho imatahantswe le maitlamo a rona a matjhaba le leano la rona la matjhaba la ho nyehela bakeng sa Aforika e betere le lefatshe le betere.

src: A total 1 371 members of the SANDF are deployed in the DRC in support of the United Nations Organisation Stabilisation Mission.
tgt: Palo e etsang 1371 ya ditho tsa SANDF di sebediswa ka hara DRC ho tshehetsa Morero wa Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) wa Botsitso.

src: Their deployment has been extended from 1 April 2017 to 31 March 2018.
tgt: Ho sebediswa ha bona ho atolositswe ho tloha ka la 01 Mmesa 2017 ho isa ho la 31 Hlakubele 2018.

src: Our deployments on the continent are in continued support of regional and continental processes to respond to and resolve crises, promote peace and security, strengthen regional integration, significantly increase intra-African trade and champion sustainable development in Africa.
tgt: Tshebediso ya rona ya sesole kontinentengbakeng sa tshehetso e tswelang pele ya metjha ya lebatowa le kontinente bakeng sa ho arabela le ho rarolla dikoduwa, ho kgothaletsa kgotso le polokeho, ho matlafatsa momahano ya lebatowa, e eketsa ka bokgabane ba kgwebisano ya ka hara Aforika le ho sebeletsa ntshetsopele ya moshwelella ka hara Aforika.

src: National Orders Cabinet congratulates all the recipients of the 2017 National Orders.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa bohle baamohedi ba Ditlotlo tsa Naha tsa selemo sa 2017.

src: In the year of OR Tambo they have shown us the power of working towards a better South Africa and better nation.
tgt: Selemong sena sa OR Tambo ba re bontshitse matla a ho sebeletsa ho lebisang ho Aforika Borwa e betere le setjhaba se betere.

src: We draw inspiration from their achievements, their dedication, passion and willingness to advance humanity.
tgt: Re fumana kgothatso ho tswa ho diphihlello tsa bona, boitelo ba bona, lerato le maikemisetso a bona a ho ntshetsapele botho.

src: The Order of Ikhamanga in Gold (1) The Order of Ikhamanga in Silver (7) The Order of Ikhamanga in Bronze (1) The Order of the Baobab in Gold (1) The Order of the Baobab in Silver (2) The Order of the Baobab in Bronze (2) The Order of Luthuli in Silver (29) The Order of Luthuli in Bronze (1) The Order of Mapungubwe in Silver (2), and The Order of the Companions of OR Tambo in Gold (1).
tgt: Tlotlo ya Ikhamanga ya Gauta (1),Tlotlo ya Ikhamanga ya Silifera (7),Tloto ya Ikhamanga ya Boronse (1),Tlotlo ya Baobab ya Gauta(1),Tlotlo ya Baobab ya Silifera (2),Tlotlo ya Baobab ya Boronse(2),Tlotlo ya Luthuli ya Silifera (29),Tlotlo ya Luthuli ya Boronse (1),Tlotlo ya Mapungubwe ya Silifera (2),Tlotlo ya Metswalle ya OR Tambo ya Gauta (1).

src: The release of the 17th Commission for Employment Equity Report by the Minster of Labour, Ms Mildred Oliphant, shows the stubbornly slow pace of transformation at various workplaces in the South African labour market.
tgt: Ho lokollwa ha Tlaleho yabo-17th ya Khomishene ya Tekatekano Mesebetsing ke Letona la Mesebetsi, Mofumahadi Mildred Oliphant e bontsha monyebe o tletseng manganga wa diphethoho dibakeng tsa mosebetsi tse fapafapaneng ka hara mmaraka wa basebetsi wa Aforika Borwa.

src: The report demonstrates that we are still far from achieving a workforce that is truly representative of our nation.
tgt: Tlaleho e bontsha hore re sa le hole le ho fihlella lebotho la basebetsi le emelang ka nnete setjhaba sa bo rona.

src: African people, women and persons with disabilities remain severely under-represented in all aspects of the Employment Equity.
tgt: Batho ba batsho, Basadi le Batho ba Phelang ka Boqhwala ba dula ba ntse ba hlahella hanyenyane mekgahlelong kaofela ya Tekatekano Mesebetsing.

src: The report showed that white people occupied 68% of the country’s top-management positions in the public and private sectors, six times the group’s economically active population.
tgt: Tlaleho e bontshitse hore makgowa a tshwere 68% ya mesebetsi e ka hodimo ya botsamaisi ya nahamakaleng a mmuso le a poraefete, e leng makgetlo a tsheletseng ho feta sehlopha se ntseng se le dilemong tsa ho sebetsa.

src: Africans made up only 14.4% of top management.
tgt: Batho ba batsho ba etsa feela 14.4%ya mesebetsi e ka hodimo ya botsamaisi.

src: Given the urgent need to transform the economy and ensure inclusive growth, this is simply not good enough.
tgt: Ha re sheba hore ho na le tlhokeho e potlakileng ya ho fetola moruo le ho netefatsa kgolo e kenyeletsang batho kaofela, sena ha se a lekana hohang.

src: Cabinet welcomes the announcement by the Minister of Labour that her department is considering adopting harsher consequences for non-compliance.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela phatlalatso ya Letona la Mesebetsi ya hore lefapha le lohotha ho nka mehato e matla bakeng sa ho se imatahanye.

src: Cabinet joins President Zuma in congratulating Mr Emmanuel Macron, President-elect of the Republic of France, following his victory on 7 May 2017 of the French presidential elections.
tgt: Kabinete e ipapisa le Moporesidente Jacob Zuma mabapi le ho thoholetsa Monghadi Emmanuel Macron, Moporesidente ya tla nka marapo a Rephabliki ya Fora, ho latela tlholo ya hae ka la 7 Motsheanong 2017 ya dikgetho tsa boporesidente tsa Fora.

src: South Africa looks forward to working with the French government under the leadership of Mr Macron to consolidate the already strong political, economic and trade ties between South Africa and France.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e lebeletse ho sebetsa mmoho le mmuso wa Fora tlasa boetapele ba Monghadi Macron ho matlafatsa maqhama a ntseng a le matla a sepolotiki, a moruo le kgwebisano pakeng tsa Aforika Borwa le Fora.

src: Cabinet congratulates the former Mayor of Johannesburg and South African Local Government Association chairperson, Parks Tau, on his appointment as co-chair of the United Nations High Level Independent Panel to oversee the effectiveness of the Habitat IIThe programme was adopted by the UN to reinvigorate the global commitment to sustainable urbanisation.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa ramotse wa mehleng wa Johannesburg, le modulasetulo wa Mokgatlo wa Mebuso ya Lehae wa Aforika Borwa (SALGA), Parks Tau ka ho thonngwa jwaloka modulasetulo-mmoho wa Phanele ya Boemo bo Hodimo e Ikemetseng ya UN ho disa bohlwahlwa ba Habitat III.

src: The Department of Trade and Industry took home the Best Foreign Exhibitor Award at the 58th Zimbabwe International Trade Fair.
tgt: Lenaneo lena le ile la amohelwa ke UN ho tsoseletsa boitlamo ba lefatshe mabapi le kgodiso ya moshwelella ya dibaka tsa ditoropo.

src: This acknowledges that the outstanding efforts by Team South Africa towards ensuring the country’s commitment to building partnerships with Zimbabwe have yielded the desired economic gains.
tgt: Lefapha la Dikgwebo le Diindaseteri (dti) le hapilekgau ya mopepesi ya hlwahlwa ka ho fetisisa wa molata ho Dipontsho tsa Kgwebisano ya Matjhaba ya Zimbabwe (ZITF) yabo-58.Sena se ananela mekutu e babatsehang ya Sehlopha sa Aforika Borwa mabapi le ho netefatsa boitlamo ba naha ba ho aha bolekane le Zimbabwe mme sena se hlahisitse dikuno tsa moruo tse neng di labalabelwa.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 24 May 2017, at Tuynhuys, Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e kopane ka Laboraro, la 24 Motsheanong 2017, Tuynhuys, Motse Kapa.

src: Issues in the environment.1 Cabinet is concerned with the rising incidences of abuse and violence against women in our society.
tgt: Kabinete e tshwenyehile ka diketsahalo tse ntseng di phahama tsa tlhekefetso le merusu kgahlanong le basadi ka hara setjhaba sa bo rona.

src: Recent incidents involving intimate partner violence have seen many brave and courageous women speaking out against this violation of their rights.2 Cabinet acknowledges that as a country we continue to have a patriarchal society and as such calls for more to be done to fight the scourge of femicide and human trafficking.3 Cabinet calls on all sectors of society to join hands in defeating this scourge, oppose any form of violence committed against women and children, and work with the police and justice system in order to bring perpetrators to justice.
tgt: Diketsahalo tsa haufinyana tjena tsa merusu ya balekane ba ratanang di bonahetse ha basadi ba sebete ba ema ka maoto ho bua kgahlanong le kgatikelo ya ditokelo tsa bona.

src: President Jacob Zuma has called for a stop to the continued abuse of women and children.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela hore jwaloka naha re ntse re tswela pele ho ba le setjhaba se laolwang ke banna mme ke kahoo ho nang le boipiletso ba hore ho sebetswe ho feta bakeng sa ho lwantsha koduwa ya dipolao tsa basadi le kgwebisano ka batho.

src: Cabinet has instructed the Social Protection, Community and Human Development Cluster to put in place a programme of action that will drive the country in the fight to stop the abuse of women and children.5 Cabinet welcomes the results of the 2016 South African Demographic and Health Survey by Statistics South Africa, which measures the health status of South Africans, and the reach and quality of health programmes.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho makala kaofela a setjhaba ho ipopa bakeng sa ho lwantsha koduwa ena, ho hanyetsana le mokgwa ofe kapa ofe wa merusu e etswang kgahlanong le basadi le bana, le ho sebetsa le sepolesa le tsamaiso ya toka bakeng sa ho tshwara baetsi ba diketso tsena.

src: The survey amongst others reports a 20% drop in infant mortality and a 11% drop in the number of women and men who smoke tobacco.
tgt: Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o entse boipiletso ba hore ho emiswe ka tlhekefetso ya basadi le bana e ntseng e tswela pele.

src: Some 32% and 42% of women and men respectively indicated that they have never been tested for HIV despite government efforts to raise awareness on HIV testing.
tgt: Tekolo ena hara tse ding e tlaleha hore ho na le phokotseho ya 20% ya ho shwa ha masea le phokotseho ya 11% palong ya basadi le banna ba tsubang.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to take personal responsibility for their health and well-being, practice safe sex and get tested regularly for HIV and all communicable and non-communicable diseases.6 Cabinet calls on parents and guardians to ensure their children are vaccinated against childhood diseases.
tgt: Sephetho sena se bontsha hore maitshunyako a maano a behilweng ke tsamaiso ya Moporesidente Zuma a beha ditholwana tse ntle.

src: Cabinet remains committed to ensuring children are immunised to eliminate life threatening infectious diseases.
tgt: Kabinete, le ha ho le jwalo, e tshwenyehile ka palo ya maAforika Borwa e ntseng e tswela pele ho kena thobalanong e sa tshireletsehang le balekane ba bangata.

src: Cabinet reassures parents and guardians that the drugs administered by the Department Health are safe.7 Cabinet welcomed the first phase of the revitalised Vulindlela Heights Industrial in Mthatha in the Eastern Cape.
tgt: Se ka etsang 32% le 42% ya basadi le banna ka tatelano se bontshitse hore ha ba e so ka ba kenela diteko tsa HIV leha mmuso o entse mekutu ya ho hlahisa temoso ka ho kenela diteko tsa HIV.

src: Government is revitalising industrial parks to boost job creation and ensure inclusive growth.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse mokgahlelo wa pele o tsoseleditsweng wa Setsi sa Diindaseteri sa Vulindlela Heights Mthatha ho la Kapa Botjhabela.

src: The move of economic activities away from urban centres is also part of government’s economic transformation efforts.
tgt: Sena ke karolo ya Lenaneo la Tsoseletso ya Diphaka tsa Diindaseteri.

src: Information on how to take advantage of opportunities available at our industrial parks, access government support and incentives programmes, and investment opportunities in various sectors is available at WEBTOKEN or through the Department of Trade and Industry’s (the dti) Customer Contact Centre on 0861 843 3.8 Cabinet has noted with regret the decision by General Motors South Africa (GMSA) (Pty) Ltd to phase out the manufacturing and sale of Chevrolet vehicles in the country.
tgt: Ke ya bobedi ya mofuta wa yona ho la Kapa Botjhabela le ho ba ya botshelela ya diphaka tse ntseng di tsoseletswa ho phatlalla le naha.

src: Government remains committed to support the country’s automotive sector, which is critical for the economy and job creation.
tgt: Mmuso o tsoseletsa diphaka tsa diindaseteri ho matlafatsa tlhahiso ya mesebetsi le ho netefatsa kgolo e kenyeletsang.

src: Cabinet notes that Isuzu, which has been partnering with GMSA over the years in South Africa, will take over the operations from GMSA.9 Cabinet has noted the deterioration of the drought situation in the Western Cape and Eastern Cape.
tgt: Kabinete e lemohile ka maswabi qeto ya General Motors South Africa (GMSA) (Pty) Ltd ya ho fedisa tlhahiso le thekiso ya makoloi a Chevrolet ka hara naha.

src: A team comprising officials from the Department of Water and Sanitation, the National Disaster Management Committee working with the provinces and local government, had been actively engaged in ensuring that short to medium-term solutions are fast-tracked to guarantee the water security of the province in the long term.
tgt: Mmuso o dula o itlamme bakeng sa ho tshehetsa lekala la naha la tlhahiso ya makoloi, e leng le hlokolosi bakeng sa moruo le tlhahiso ya WEBTOKEN dti ba tswela pele ho sebetsa le bankakarolo kaofela ho bebofatsa sekgahla sa sena.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans including domestic users, businesses, mining sector, energy and agriculture to work together and use water more sparingly.10 Cabinet welcomed the released Anti-Corruption Strategy discussion document, which will inform the National Anti-Corruption Strategy.
tgt: Bakeng sa ho eketsa tlhahiso, tlhahiso ya mesebetsi le matlafatso ya dihlahiswa tse rekiswang ka ntle, haufinyana tjena re thakgotse mokgahlelo wa borobong wa Moralo wa Leano la Tshebetso la Diindaseteri (IPAP) bakeng sa ho tataisa mesebetsi ya rona.

src: Cabinet invites the public to make written inputs through the Department of Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation website: www.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela hore Isuzu, eo esale e le selekaneng le GMSA ka dilemo tse ngata ka hara Aforika Borwa, e tla nka ditshebetso tsa GMSKabinete e lemohile ho mpefala ha maemo a komello ka hara Kapa Bophirima le Kapa Botjhabela.

src: Cabinet urges all South Africans to take the necessary precautions when using electronic means of communicating or transacting.
tgt: Kabinete e mema setjhaba ho etsa diphehiso tse ngotsweng ka websaete ya Lefapha la Meralo, Bodisa le Tlhatlhobo ya Tshebetso: www.

src: The allocation of spectrum by the World Radiocommunication Conference has a significant impact on the economic growth of South Africa.
tgt: Bobodu le ho nyehla ha seriti ho ka bobedi makala a mmuso le a poraefete di na le kgahlamelo e kotsi hodima ntshetsopele ya naha ya bo rona.

src: The National Radio Frequency Plan 2017 is a comprehensive source of radio frequency spectrum allocation for different radiocommunication services.
tgt: Kabinete e hlahisitse ngongoreho ka tlhaselo ya lefatshe ka marangrang a dikgokahano ya haufinyana tjena, e tlalehilweng e le tlhaselo e kgolo ka ho fetisisa ho fihlela hajwale.

src: The revised National Radio Frequency Plan 2017 ensures South Africa is aligned with the approved International Radio Regulations that were adopted in the 2015 International Telecommunication Union conference.3 Cabinet approved the Inland Waterways Safety Strategy.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa maAforika Borwa kaofela ho nka mehato ya tlhokomelo ha ba sebedisa mekgwa ya dikgokahanyo ya elektroniki le ho etsa ditumellano.

src: The strategy, through the South African Maritime Safety Authority, sets standards and enhances procedures for permitting and licensing arrangements for boats operating on inland waterways.
tgt: Ho sebedisa disebediswa tsa antivaerase ya khomphyutha kgafetsa tse tla hlahloba tikoloho e sa lokang inthaneteng le tsona di a kgothaletswa.

src: Designs for the following 2017 and 2018 commemorative coin series have been developed:2017 coin series: Oliver Reginald Tambo Centenary Celebration2017 circulation coin: R5 coin depicting the Order of the Companies of OR Tambo2017 Protea coin series: Life of a Legend – Nelson Mandela2017 R1 coin series: Reptiles of South Africa – the Puff Adder2018 UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) Man and the Biosphere coin series: The Waterberg Biosphere Reserve2018 coin series: National Geographic Society ‘Big Cats Initiative’ – The Lion2018 coin: 2018 FIFA World Cup RussiaTUpcoming events.1 Cabinet calls on all South Africans to support the Child Protection Week from 28 May to 4 June under the theme: “Let us all protect children to move South Africa forward”.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana phatlalatso ya Tjhata e Shebilweng Botjha ya Matlafatso e Pharaletseng ya Batho ba Batsho Moruong bakeng sa Indaseteri ya Aforika Borwa ya Merafo le Diminerale ka selemo sa 2017.Letona la Mehlodi ya Diminerale Mosebenzi Zwane o tla fana ka tsebiso hang feela ha tjhata e se e kentswe koranteng ya mmuso.

src: The purpose is to expose girls from Grade 10 to 12 learners to different career options.4 President Zuma will on Thursday, 25 May 2017, host the national 2017 Africa Day celebration at the Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guesthouse in Pretoria.
tgt: Moralo o shebilweng botjha wa Naha wa Maqhubu a Radio wa selemo sa 2017 o netefatsa hore Aforika Borwa e matahantswe le Melawana ya Matjhaba ya Radio e tjhaelletsweng monwana e ileng ya amohelwa ka selemo sa 2015 ho Pitso ya Matjhaba ya Meralo ya Motheo ya Dikgokahanyo (ITU).

src: The annual commemoration of Africa Day marks the founding of the Organisation of African Unity in WEBTOKEN we end Africa Month, Cabinet calls on all South Africans to partner with our fellow Africans residing in South Africa and elsewhere on the continent to ensure the prosperity for our region and the rest of WEBTOKEN is also incumbent on all who reside within our borders, South Africans and foreign nationals alike to adhere to the laws of the country.
tgt: Lewa lena, ka Bolaudi ba Boipaballo ba Mawatleng ba Aforika Borwa, le beha maemo le ho ntlafatsa ditsamaiso mabapi le ho dumella le ho etsa ditlhophiso tsa dilaesense bakeng sa diketswana tse sebedisang ditsela tsa rona tsa metsi tsa ka hara naha.

src: The success of this procedure in the hands of our transplant team is testimony to the high level of skill and expertise that exists in the public health sector in South Africa.2 Cabinet congratulated iSimangaliso Wetland Park for receiving the Audit Excellence Award at the South African Institute of Chartered Accountants (SAICA) Public Sector Excellence Awards earlier this month.
tgt: Lewa lena le rerile ho hlahisa moralo o kopanetsweng wa taolo le tshebetso, o tla kgontsha Aforika Borwa ho fihlella maemo a hlwahlwa ka ho fetisisa a matjhaba a ditshebetso tsa mebila ya tsamaiso ya dithoto.

src: The award was in recognition of the Park receiving clean audits over five consecutive years.
tgt: Dikgothaletso leweng lena di tla matlafatsa bohlwahlwa ba qobello, ho hodisa boipaballo mebileng, ho matlafatsa tshireletso ya meralo ya motheo, ho fokotsa dikgahlamelo tsa tikoloho, le ho bopa moralo o kopanetsweng wa phehisano e laolwang ho ya ka boleng boo ka hara lekala la tsamaiso ya dithoto le ka tswelang pele ho sebeletsa ditlhoko tsa moruo wa Aforika Borwa.

src: iSimangaliso was declared South Africa’s first World Heritage Site in December 19.3 Cabinet congratulates the Working on Fire programme for receiving a plaque from the Alberta Government in Canada commemorating the assistance provided by the programme in managing wildfires in their Province in 2016.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana meralo ya Khamphani ya Mente ya Aforika Borwa bakeng sa dikhoine tsa sehopotso le tse tla sebediswa tsa dilemo tsa 2017 le 2018.Ka tshebedisano le Kabinete, ho hlahisitswe letoto le letjha le emelang botjhaba, tokoloho le demokerasi tlasa mookotaba: “Re keteka Aforika Borwa”.

src: Cabinet reiterates President Jacob Zuma’s call for South Africans to unite against violence and abuse of women and children, and calls on all South Africans to take urgent steps to eradicate this scourge in our communities.
tgt: DINTLHA TSA HAJWALE Kabinete e boeletsa kgoeletso ya Moporesidente Jacob Zuma bakeng sa hore maAforika Borwa a ipope kgahlanong le dikgoka le tlhekefetso ya basadi le bana, le ho ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa kaofela ho nka mehato e potlakileng ho fedisa koduwa ena ka hara metse ya bo rona.

src: This follows the President’s visit to Elsies River in Cape Town in support of the Fight against Crime Imbizo.
tgt: Sena se latela leeto la Moporesidente Elsies River ho la Motse Kapa mabapi le ho tshehetsa Imbizo ya Ntwa e kgahlanong le Botlokotsebe.

src: This visit once again highlighted the vulnerability of women and children in our society.
tgt: Leeto lena hape le hlakisitse ho ba kotsing ha basadi le bana ka hara setjhaba sa rona.

src: The President undertook to return to the area to look into the many challenges of crime and murder, especially of children and how law-enforcement authorities would improve their services to the community.
tgt: Moporesidente o ikemiseditse ho kgutlela sebakeng seo ho ya fatisisa diphephetso tse ngata tsa botlokotsebe le dipolao, ka ho qolleha tsa bana le kamoo balaodi ba qobello ya molao ba ka ntlafatsang ditshebeletso tsa bona ho badudi.2 Kabinete e amohela ho lokollwa ha Diphuputso tse Akaretsang tsa Malapa tsa selemo sa 2016, tse tswellang ho bontsha kgatelopele mabapi le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha mananeo a mmuso a ho ntlafatsa maphelo a maAforika Borwa, haholoholo badudi ba neng ba tingwe menyetla pele.

src: Cabinet welcomes the release of the General Household Survey 2016, which continues to show progress in the implementation of government programmes to improve the lives of South Africans, especially the previously disadvantaged communities.
tgt: Dipalopalo di bontsha hore mmuso e etsa menyabuketso mabapi le ho fana ka bodulo, moo malapa a maAforika Borwa a dulang ka hara matlo a ‘RDP’ kapa matlo a tsheheditsweng ke mmuso a phahameng ho tloha ho 5% ka selemo sa 2002 ho ya ho 13,5% ka selemo sa 2016.

src: The statistics show that government is making inroads in providing housing, with South African households living in ‘RDP’ or state-subsidised dwellings increasing from 5% in 2002 to 13, 5% in 2016.
tgt: Diphuphutso tsena hape di bontsha hore mananeo a mmuso a thuso ya kahisano a supa keketseho ho tloha ho 12,7% ka selemo sa 2003 ho ya ho 29,7% ka selemo sa 2016.Hape ho na le keketseho e bonahalang ho phumantsho ya metsi, motlakase le tsamaiso ya dikgwerekgwere, e leng letshwao la bohlokwa bakeng sa maikemisetso a Mmuso wa Aforika Borwa wa ho lokisa dimpe tsa mmuso wa kgethollo le ho fana ka ditshebeletso tsa mantlha ho batho kaofela.

src: The survey also shows that government’s social-assistance programmes indicates an increase from 12, 7% in 2003 to 29,7% in 2016.There is also a marked increase in access to water, electricity and sanitation, which is an important marker for the South African Government’s ambition to redress the wrongs of apartheid and provide basic services to all the people.
tgt: Kabinete, leha ho le jwalo, e lemohile hore ha boingodiso thutong e phahameng bo ntse bo eketseha, leha e le ka monyebe, ebile feela 3,3% ya maAforika Borwa a ba Batsho a dilemong tse 18 ho ya ho tse 29 a neng a ithuta papisong le 18,8% ya baithuti ba maIndia/maAsia le 17,5% ya makgowa sehlopheng sa ba dilemong tsena.

src: Cabinet has, however, noted that while higher education enrolments are on the increase, albeit at a slow pace, only 3, 3% of black Africans aged 18 to 29 years were studying as opposed to 18, 8% of Indian/Asian individuals and 17, 5% of the white population in this age group.
tgt: Ke feela 3,5% ya ba Mmala ba neng ba ithuta nakong ya selemo sa 2016.Diphuputso ho ya pele di supile phokotseho ho tloha ho 23,8% ho ya ho 11,8% ya malapa a neng a phela ka tlala, e leng se bontshang kgatelopele mabapi le ho shebana le malapa a phelang bofutsaneng bo feteletseng.3 Kabinete e lemohile Diphuputso tsa Kotara ka Nngwe tsa Lebotho la Basebetsi bakeng sa kotara ya pele ya selemo tse bontshitseng hore moruo o ekeditse mesebetsi ka mesebetsi e 144 000.

src: These numbers were offset by an increase in the number of job-seekers by 433 00 people.
tgt: Dipalo tsena di thuntheditswe ke keketseho ya batho ba neng ba batla mosebetsi ba 433 000.

src: Cabinet reaffirms its commitment to continue partnering with the private sector and labour in its attempts to address the country’s unemployment challenges.
tgt: Kabinete e thathiselleditse boitlamo ba yona ba ho tswela pele ho theha selekane le lefapha la poraefete le basebetsi maitekong a yona a ho sebetsana le diphephetso tsa naha tsa tlhokeho ya mesebetsi.4 Kabinete e amohela ho thakgolwa ha Phaka ya Diindaseteri ya Babelegi e ntjhafaditsweng ho la Hammanskraal jwaloka karolo ya meralo ya mmuso ya ho akofisa ntshetsopele ya moruo le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi sebakeng seo.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch of the refurbished Babelegi Industrial Park in Hammanskraal as part of government’s plans to accelerate economic development and job creation in the area.
tgt: Porojeke ena ya R42-milione ke karolo ya mmuso ya Lenaneo la Tsoseletso ya Diphaka Tsa Diindaseteri le e nngwe ya diphaka tse tsheletseng tse ntseng di tsoseletswa ho phatlalla le naha bakeng sa ntshetsopele e pharaletseng ya moruo le diindaseteri.

src: The R42-million project is part of government’s Revitalisation of Industrial Parks Programme and one of six parks that are being revitalised across the country for broader economic and industrial development.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa diindaseteri le dikgwebo tsa lehae ho sekaseka ho atolosetsa ditshebetso tsa bona ho ya sebakeng sena sa diindaseteri bakeng sa ho fumantshwa mekgwa e fapafapaneng ya tshehetso e teng bakeng sa ho hodisa dikgwebo tsa bona ho ya pele.5 Kabinete e tsebisitswe ke Letona la Ditjhelete, Monghadi Malusi Gigaba, mabapi le dipalo tsa moraorao tsa Palohohle ya Dihlahiswa tsa Aforika Borwa (GDP), e honyetseng ka 0,7% kotareng ya pele ya selemo sa 2017.

src: Cabinet was briefed by Minister of Finance, Mr Malusi Gigaba, on the latest South Africa’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) figures, which contracted by 0,7% in the first quarter of 2017.
tgt: Sephetho sena sa GDP se mpefetseng ho feta kamoo ho neng ho lebeletswe se tlase haholo ho feta Tjhebobotjha ya Ditekanyetso tsa selemo sa 2017, e neng e lepile kgolo ya GDP ya selemo sa 2017 ho ba 1,3%.

src: This has been attributed to, among other things, the contraction of the manufacturing, trade, catering and accommodation industries.
tgt: Sena se bakuwe ke, hara tse ding, ho honyela ha tlhahiso, kgwebisano, diindaseteri tsa phano ya dijo le bodulo.

src: The economy was nevertheless supported by growth in the mining and quarrying industry which increased 12.8%.
tgt: Leha ho le jwalo moruo o ile wa tshehetswa ke kgolo merafong le diindasetering tsa dikwari e eketsehileng ka 12.8%.

src: The agriculture, forestry and fishing industry rebounded in the first quarter of 2017 with an increase of 22, 2%.There are green shoots that the country can leverage to boost its own economic growth outlook.
tgt: Diindaseteri tsa temo, meru le ditlhapi di ile tsa hlasimoloha kotareng ya pele ya selemo sa 2017 ka keketseho ya 22,2%.Ho na le matshwao a tshepisang a hore naha e ka itseka bakeng sa ho matlafatsa tjhebahalo ya yona ya kgolo ya moruo.

src: These include improving global growth, stabilising commodity prices, more favourable climate conditions, reliable electricity supply and less volatile labour WEBTOKEN a matter of urgency, Cabinet calls on business, labour and the broader society to partner with government to intensify our growth programme and improve confidence so as to arrest the decline and set the economy on a higher trajectory, to achieve inclusive economic growth.
tgt: Tsena di kenyeletsa kgolo ya ho kenella lefatsheng, ho tsitsisa ditheko tsa phahlo, maemo a matle a tlelaemete, phepelo e tshepahalang ya motlakase le dikamano tse batlang di tsitsitse tsa basebetsi.

src: In this regard the Minister of Finance will meet with business leaders in a bid to formulate strategies to counter economic recession and achieve inclusive growth.
tgt: Jwaloka taba e potlakileng, Kabinete e ipiletsa ho dikgwebo, basebetsi le setjhaba ka kakaretso ho theha selekane le mmuso bakeng sa ho matlafatsa lenaneo la rona la kgolo le ho ntlafatsa tshepahalo bakeng sa ho kgina ho fokola le ho beha moruo maemong a batlang a phahame, ho fihlella kgolo ya moruo e kenyeletsang.

src: Cabinet endorsed a full media briefing by the Minister of Finance to share with South Africans the interventions government will embark upon within the current budget framework.
tgt: Ntlheng ena Letona la Ditjhelete le tla kopana le baetapele ba dikgwebo ka morero wa ho bopa mawa a ho lwantsha ho putlama ha moruo le ho fihlella kgolo e kenyeletsang.

src: Cabinet further reaffirms the adopted budget framework for the country.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana kopano ya boraditaba le Letona la Ditjhelete bakeng sa ho arolelana le maAforika Borwa maitshunyako ao mmuso o tla a etsang ka hara meralo ya ditekanyetso tsa hajwale.

src: The rating agencies Fitch and Standard & Poor’s affirmed South Africa’s long-term foreign currency debt ratings of ‘BB+’.This comes amid Minister Gigaba’s engagements with the private sector to ensure that the joint work of government, business, labour and civil society continues, and that the pledges made are fulfilled.
tgt: Kabinete hape e thathiselletsa moralo o amohetsweng wa ditekanyetso bakeng sa naha.6 Lekala la tekolo la Fitch le la Standard & Poor’s a thathiselleditse ditekolo tsa Aforika Borwa tsa mekitlane ya ditjhelete tsa maatjhabeng tsa nako e telele tsa ‘BB+’.Sena se tla hara nako eo dipuisano tsa Letona Gigaba le lekala la poraefete bakeng sa ho netefatsa hore mosebetsi o kopanetsweng wa mmuso, dikgwebo, basebetsi le setjhaba ka kakaretso di ntseng di tswela pele, le hore maitlamo a entsweng a ya phethahatswa.

src: Cabinet reiterates that South Africans must continue to act in unison, especially during difficult times and work even harder to ensure that the country reclaims its investment grade status.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa hore maAforika Borwa a lokela ho tswela pele ho sebetsa e le ntho e le nngwe, haholoholo dinakong tse thata le ho sebetsa ka thata ho feta ho netefatsa hore naha e tseke maemo a yona a tekolo ya matsete.7 Kabinete e ananela ditherisano tse thakgolwang kgetlo la pele tsa Komiti e Kopanetsweng ya Tsamaiso bakeng sa Mmaraka o Tshwanang wa Borwa (MERCOSUR) le Mokgatlo wa Lekgetho la Madiboho a Dinaha tsa Aforika e Borwa (SACU (SACU) tse neng di tshwerwe haufinyana tjena ka hara naha.

src: Cabinet welcomes deliberations at the inaugural Joint Administration Committee for the Common Market of the South (MERCOSUR) and the Southern Africa Customs Union (SACU) recently held in the country.
tgt: Mekga e dumellane hore ka kopanelo e tla sekaseka menyetla ya ho hodisa Tumellano e ka Sehloohong ya Kgwebisano (PTA) ya MERCOSUR-SACU ka ho kenyeletsa makala a yona a kgodiso ya kgwebisano, mekgatlo ya kgwebo, lekala la poraefete, le matlo a bona a bonqosa le dikantoro tsa matjhabeng ka ho latelana.

src: The MERCOSUR-SACU agreement provides local exporters with the opportunity to tap into a market of more than 280-million people.
tgt: PTA ya MERCOSUR-SACU e neha ba romellang thepa ya lehae ka ntle monyetla wa ho kenella mmarakeng wa batho ba fetang 280-milione.

src: Cabinet calls on all the country’s exporters to take advantage of the PTA as local products are now able to enter the MERCOSUR bloc at preferential duty rates.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho ba romellang thepa ka ntle ho nka monyetla ona wa PTA kaha jwale dihlahiswa tsa mona hae di kgona ho kena lepatlelong la MERCOSUR ka dikgahla tse kgothaletswang tsa lekgetho.8 Kabinete e hlahisitse tshwabo ya yona ka qeto ya Amerika (USA) ya ho ikgula Tumellanong ya Paris.

src: Cabinet expressed regret at the decision of the United States of America (USA) to withdraw from the Paris Agreement.
tgt: Tumellano ya Paris, e tla sebetsa ka botlalo ka selemo sa 2020, e thehilwe hodima dinyehelo tse tekilweng ke dinaha ka botsona mabapi le merero ya lefatshe eo ho dumellanweng ka kopanelo ka yona.

src: The Paris Agreement, which will be fully operational by 2020, is premised on contributions determined by countries themselves towards collectively agreed global goals.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e ipileditse ho USA ho sekaseka botjha boemo ba yona le ho itlama botjha tsamaisong e kopanetsweng ke dinaha ka bongata.9 Memorandamo wa Kutlwano (MoU) pakeng tsa Novartis, Lekgotla la Aforika Borwa la Diphuputso tsa Bongaka le Lefapha la Saense le Thekenoloji, o betla tsela ya ho matlafatsa mothamo le boleng ba diteko tsa bongaka le ho aha bokgoni ba diphuputso ka hara kontinente.

src: South Africa has called on the USA to reconsider its position and recommit to the multilateral process.
tgt: Tumellano e tla thusa bakeng sa mananeo a kopanetsweng a diphuputso mahlokong a kgethilweng a tshwaetsanang le a sa tshwaetsaneng, ho ntlafatsa phumantsho ya bakudi ba Aforika Borwa ya meriana e ntjhafatsang, le ho aha bokgoni ba naha le ba kontinente ba diphuputso le ntshetsopele.

src: The Memorandum of Understanding between Novartis, the South African Medical Research Council and the Department of Science and Technology, paves the way to boost the volume and quality of clinical trials and build research capability on the continent.
tgt: Kabinete e dumela hore ho na le sebaka bakeng sa bolekane bo eketsehileng ba mmuso le ba poraefete, le ho kgodiseha hore tsena di ka bula tsela ya ho sebetsana le diphephetso tse ngata tse matla tseo re tobaneng le tsona.10 Kabinete e amohela Tlaleho ya selemo sa 2017 ho tswa ho Mokgatlo wa Khonkerese ya Matjhaba le Khonvenshene, e tswellang ho beha Aforika Borwa jwaloka sebaka se ka hodimo sa ho tshwara diketsahalo tsa kgwebo ka hara Aforika le Botjhabela bo Hare.

src: The agreement will allow for joint research programmes in selected communicable and non-communicable diseases, improve South African patients' access to innovative medicines, and build the country and continent's research and development capabilities.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e dula e le se seng sa dibaka tse tummeng ka ho fetisisa sa bohahlaudi lefatsheng le ho tswela pele ho nka maemo a hodimo hape ho lenaneo la bophehisane la Foramo ya Moruo wa Lefatshe la ho eta le bohahlaudi lefatsheng jwaloka ha le lokolotswe ka Mmesa 2017.Kabinete e rata ho bona bongata ba ditoropo le metsemeholo e menyenyane ya Aforika Borwa e iketa bakeng sa dikopano tse nyenyane moo di ka kgonang ho imatahanya le ditlhokeho tsa ho tshwara dikopano.

src: Cabinet believes that there is room for more public-private partnerships, and is convinced that these can lead the way in addressing the many pressing challenges we face.
tgt: Sena se tla thusa ho ntlafatsa qaqolohano ho ya ka sebopeho sa naha bakeng sa bohahlaudi ka nqane ho ditsi tse kgolo le ho ala moruo o fehlilweng ke diketsahalo tsena ka tsela e batlang e lekalekana.11 Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa kaofela hore a fadimehele ditaba tsa leshano, ka ho qolleha keketseho ya ho maneha ditaba tse fosahetseng ho marangrang a ditaba a kahisano mabapi le banana le basadi ba lahlehileng, ba kwetetsweng le ba hapilweng ka mahahapa.

src: Cabinet welcomes the 2017 Report from the International Congress and Convention Association, which continues to rank South Africa as the top business events destination in Africa and the Middle East.
tgt: Ho ropoha ha haufinyana tjena ha merusu KwaMashu, pela Durban ka lebaka la ditlaleho tse fosahetseng tsa hore bana ba nkuwa ka mahahapa sebakeng seo le ho belaellwa ha ho hapuwa ka mahahapa ha ngwanana Naledi, ho la Soweto ke batho ba tsamayang ka Toyota Quantum ho kenyeleditswe le nomoro ya yona ya boingodiso e ileng ya phatlalla ho marangrang a ditaba a kahisano, moo ho tholahetseng hamorao hore ha se nnete.

src: South Africa remains one of the world’s most popular tourist destinations and continues to top the rankings also on the World Economic Forum Travel’s global travel and tourism competitiveness index as released in April 2017.Cabinet would like to see more of South Africa’s smaller towns and cities bidding for smaller meetings where they can meet the hosting requirements.
tgt: Re ipiletsa ho batho hore ba seke ba pheta ho maneha le ho tsamaisa ditaba tsa leshano ho marangrang a ditaba a kahisano, ho fihlela ba tiisitse bonnete ba tsona.12 Kabinete e lemohile ka ngongoreho e kgolo ditlaleho tsa ditaba ka ‘diimeile tse nyenyelepisitsweng tse hlokang nnete’ tseo ho hopolwang hore di beha Matona, bahlanka ba mmuso le batho ba poraefete ka mosing ba belaellwa hore ba entse tse sa lokang.

src: This will help to improve the geographic distribution of tourism beyond the major centres and spread the wealth generated by these events more equitably.
tgt: Kabinete e dula e itlamme bakeng sa puso e hlwahlwa le ka nako e le nngwe, hape e ananela hore batho kaofela ba nkuwa ba hloka molato ho fihlela ba bonwe molato ho ya ka dipehelo tsa Molaotheo wa rona.

src: Cabinet calls on South Africans to be vigilant of fake news, in particular the increase in false posts on social media over missing, kidnapped and abducted girls and women.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa bohle ba nang le tlhahisoleseding ka molato ofe kapa ofe o etswang ke bahlanka ba mmuso kapa Matona ho tsebisa makala a qobello ya molao hore ho tle ho etswe dipatlisiso.

src: The recent outbreak of violence in KwaMashu, near Durban over fake reports of children being abducted in the area and the alleged abduction of a girl in Naledi, Soweto by persons in a Toyota Quantum with registration number included went viral on social media, which was later found to be untrue.
tgt: Kabinete e hlokometse hore ho se ho na le dinyewe tse ritetsweng, mme sepolesa se ntse se etsa dipatlisiso tse lokelang.

src: These hoaxes, fake news and the dissemination of false information cause panic among our communities and waste time and resources of the police.
tgt: Bohle ba anngweng ke diimeile tseo ba kgothaletswa ho sebetsa mmoho le makala a qobello ya molao.

src: Cabinet was apprised of the 4th performance quarterly progress reports for 2016/17 (January-March 2017) on the implementation of priority outcomes.
tgt: Lenaneo le hlophisitsweng hantle le tla manehuwa ho WEBTOKEDIKETSAHALO TSE TLANG.1 Moporesidente Zuma o thakgotse Kgwedi ya Batjha tlasa mookotaba “Selemo sa OR Tambo: Re Ntshetsapele Matlafatso ya Batjha Moruong”, ka kopano ya Sehlopha sa Tshebetso sa Batjha sa Kantoro ya Moporesidente.

src: President Zuma launched Youth Month under the theme “The Year of OR Tambo: Advancing Youth Economic Empowerment”, with a meeting of the Presidential Youth Working Group.
tgt: Selemo sena se tshwaya selemo sa bo-41 sa Merusu ya Soweto mme sehopotso se sebetsa jwaloka kgopotso ya hore batjha ka hara naha ba ne ba le ka pele Ntweng.

src: This brought together government and leaders of youth organisations, who took stock of progress in the socio-economic advancement of young people.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa batjha kaofela ho nka karolo diketsahalong tsa Letsatsi la Batjha le ho sebedisa tshehetso kaofela le mehlodi eo mmuso e e hlahisitseng bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa menyetla ya bona le ho ntshetsapele bonkakarolo ba bona ka hara moruo.2 PITSO YA MEBUSO YA LEHAE E LENG KA BATJHALetona la Kopanelo ya Puso le Merero ya Botjhaba, Monghadi Des van Rooyen, o tla epa Pitso ya Mebuso ya Lehae ho tloha ka la 19 ho isa ka la 22 Phuptjane 2017, tlasa mookotaba “Batjha ba nka marapo ho tsa ntshetsopele”.

src: Ministers and Deputy Ministers will engage in various activities aimed at promoting youth development and empowerment.
tgt: Pitso e tla thakgola Foramo ya Mebuso ya Lehae ya Ntshetsopele ya Batjha.

src: The National Youth Day commemoration event will take place in Ventersdorp, North West on 16 June 2017.
tgt: Sena se tla kgontsha batjha ho sheba botjha kgatelopele ya mebuso ya lehae papisong le phihlello ya Leano la Naha la Batjha (NYP) la 2020.

src: This year marks the 41st anniversary of the Soweto Uprising and the commemoration serves as a reminder that young people in the country were at the forefront of our Struggle.
tgt: E tla boela e matlafatsa bolekane pakeng tsa mmuso, dikgwebo le setjhaba ka kakaretso mabapi le ho ntshetsapele baetapele ba batjha lepatlelong la lehae.3 Letona la Tshebeletso ya Mmuso le Tsamaiso, Mofumahadi Faith Muthambi, o tla etella pele kemedi ya Aforika Borwa e tla kenela Letsatsi la Tshebeletso ya Mmuso la Aforika Kigali, ho la Rwanda ho tloha ka la 21 ho isa ka la 23 Phuptjane 2017.

src: Local Government Youth ConferenceThe Minister of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs, Mr Des van Rooyen, will convene the Local Government Conference from 19 to 22 June 2017, under the theme “Young people taking charge in development”.
tgt: Mookotaba wa selemo sena ke: “Re Tebisa Tlwaelo e Tobaneng le Batho ya Phano ya Ditshebeletso: Re theha selekane le batjha bakeng sa Phethoho ya Aforika.” Mookotaba o fana ka menyetla ya ho lekola kamoo Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba e hlalosang le ho arabela ho tlwaelo e tobaneng le batho ya phano ya ditshebeletso e hlaloswang ke tsela eo dintho di etswang ka yona hajwale.

src: Minister of Public Service and Administration, Ms Faith Muthambi, will lead the South African delegation to attend the Africa Public Service Day in Kigali, Rwanda from 21 to 23 June 2017.
tgt: Kabinete e fetiseditse matshediso a yona ho mmuso le batho ba UK, ka ho qolleha malapa le baratuwa ba ba hlokahetseng, le ho lakaletsa ba lemetseng ho fola ka potlako.3 Kabinete e fetisetsa matshediso a yona ho lelapa le metswalle ya Moporofesara Babatunde Osotimehin, ya hlokahetseng bekeng ena.

src: Cabinet extends its condolences to the family and friends of the commuter who died when two Metrorail trains collided near the Elandsfontein station in Ekurhuleni and wishes a speedy recovery to those injured in the accident.
tgt: O lwanetse ka mafolofolo ditokelo tsa Basadi ba ratanang le basadi ba bang, Banna ba ratanang le banna ba bang, Ba bong bo habedi, Ba fetotseng bong, Ba ditlwaelo tse makatsang tsa bong le ba kopanelo ya bong.4 DIFEFO TSA KAPA LE MELLO YA KNYSNAKabinete e hlokometse ka difefo tse ammeng boholo ba dibaka tsa Kapa Bophirima le tshenyo e latetseng difefo tseo.

src: Cabinet calls for the investigation into the root cause of the accident to be fast-tracked to prevent a recurrence of such fatal accidents.
tgt: Kabinete e romela matshediso a yona ho malapa a ba lahlehetsweng ke maphelo le thepa nakong ya dikoduwa tsena palo ya moraorao e tlalehilweng ke ya mafu a batho ba robedi.

src: Cabinet joined the international community in strongly condemning the latest terrorist attack in the United Kingdom (UK).
tgt: Setsi sa Taolo ya Dikotsi tsa Dikoduwa sa Motse Kapa se kgothaletswa ho sebetsa ka matla mabapi le ho pholosa maphelo le thepa, ho kenyeletswa sebaka sa Knysna moo ho nang le mello e befileng.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 21 June 2017, at Tuynhuys, Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e kopane ka Laboraro,la 21 Phuptjane 2017, Tuynhuys, Motse Kapa.

src: Cabinet reflected on the recent announcements by the three major ratings agencies.
tgt: Kabinete e tshohlile ditsebiso tsa haufinyana tjena tsa makala a maholo a tekolo ya maemo a moruo.

src: All three ratings agencies raised similar issues such as the slow pace of growth-enhancing reforms, the performance of state-owned companies (SOCs) and political risks, among other issues.
tgt: Ka boraro ba ona a hlahisitse dintlha tse tshwanang tse kang diphethoho tse monyebe tsa matlafatso ya kgolo, tshebetso ya dikhamphani tsa mmuso(di-SOC) le dikotsi tsa sepolotiki, hara dintlha tse ding.

src: Cabinet expressed confidence in its systematic interventions to address the country’s economic challenges as well as work undertaken to strengthen the performance of the SOCs.
tgt: Kabinete e hlahisitse tshepo maitshunyakong a yona a hlohlomisitsweng hantle bakeng sa ho sebetsana le diphephetso tsa naha tsa moruo hammoho le mosebetsi oo ho kenweng ho ona wa ho matlafatsa tshebetso ya di-SOMmuso o ntse o le motjheng mabapi le ho baballa moralo wa ona wa maemo a ditjhelete tsa puso, ho netefatsa maano a tsitsitseng, le ho sebetsa bakeng sa ho netefatsa kgolo le diphethoho moruong.

src: Government remains on track in maintaining its fiscal framework, ensuring policy certainty, and working to ensure inclusive growth and economic transformation.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa hore motheo wa motjha o phahameng wa kgolo le ntshetsopele ya moruo wa kahisano o se o behilwe.

src: Cabinet reiterates that the foundation for a higher growth path and socio-economic development has already been WEBTOKEN focuses on improving investor and consumer confidence by fast-tracking the implementation of the structural reforms for economic growth.
tgt: O tsepamisitse maikutlo hodima tshepo ya batsetedi le basebedisi ka ho akofisa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha diphethoho tsa sebopeho bakeng sa kgolo ya moruo.

src: President Jacob Zuma convened the Black Economic Empowerment (BEE) Advisory Council workshop on Tuesday, 20 June 2017, which focused on radical socio-economic transformation.
tgt: Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o bitseditse ba Lekgotla la Boeletsi la Matlafatso ya Batho ba Batsho Moruong(BEE) boitjhorisong ka Labobedi, la 20 Phuptjane 2017, moo ho neng ho tsepamisitswe maikutlo hodima diphethoho tse matla tsa moruo.

src: The workshop, amongst others, addressed the systematic and structural implementation challenges of the Broad-Based BEE Act, 2003 (Act 53 of 2003) and the proposed recommendations to realise government’s objectives on radical socio-economic transformation.
tgt: Boitjhoriso bona, hara tse ding, bo ile ba shebana le diphephetso tse hlohlomisitsweng le tsa sebopeho tsa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Molao o Pharaletseng wa Matlafatso ya Batho ba Batsho Moruong (BBBEE), wa selemo sa 2003 (Molao bo-53 wa selemo sa 2003) le dikgothaletso tse sisintsweng tsa ho fihlella merero ya mmuso mabapi le diphethoho tse matla tsa moru wa kahisano.

src: The partnership between government, business, labour and civil society is critical to boost confidence levels, so that working together we can reclaim and maintain investment-grade ratings.
tgt: Bolekane pakeng tsa mmuso, dikgwebo, basebetsi le setjhaba ka kakaretso bo hlokolosi bakeng sa ho matlafatsa maemo a tshepo, hore ha re sebetsa mmoho re kgone ho tseka botjha le ho baballa ditekolo tsa maemo a botsetedi.

src: As Youth Month draws to a close, Cabinet thanks all sectors who participated in activities across the country.
tgt: Jwaloka ha Kgwedi ya Batjha e ya mafelong, Kabinete e leboha makala kaofela a nkileng karolo diketsahalong tsa ho phatlalla le naha.

src: The participation of thousands of young people in the various Youth Month empowerment activities that were hosted by departments, government entities and the private sector is encouraging.
tgt: Bonkakarolo ba dikete tsa batjha diketsehalong tse fapafapaneng tsa Kgwedi ya Batjha tsa matlafatso tse neng di tshwerwe ke mafapha, dikaho tsa mmuso le lekala la poraefete ke bo kgothatsang.

src: This year marks the 41st anniversary of the 1976 Soweto Student Uprising and the commemoration serves as a reminder that young people in the country were at the forefront of our Struggle.
tgt: Selemo sena se tshwaya selemosabo-41 sa Meruso ya Baithuti ya Soweto ya selemo sa1976 mme sehopotso se sebetsa jwalo ka kgopotso ya hore batjha ba ka hara naha ba ne ba le ka pele Ntweng ya rona.

src: Cabinet calls on youth to use all the support and resources that government has made available to improve their prospects and advance their participation in the economy.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho batjha ho sebedisa tshehetso yohle le mehlodi eo mmuso e di hlahisitseng bakeng sa ho ntlafatsa maemo a bona le ho ntshetsapele bonkakarolo ba bona moruong.

src: Cabinet condemns the recent violence and intimidation of commuters during the protests by taxi owners.
tgt: Kabinete e tshwela ka mathe merusu le ditshoso tsa bapalami tsa haufinyana tjena nakong ya boipelaetso ba beng ba ditekesi.

src: Such actions are out of place in a democratic society.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse jwalo ha di tsamaelane le bophelo ba rona ba demokerasi.

src: Peaceful interventions on any matter will always be beneficial to all parties involved.
tgt: Maitshunyako a tletseng kgotso tabeng efe kapa efe a tla dula a tswela bohle ba amehang molemo.

src: The subsequent agreement between the South African National Taxi Association and SA Taxi Finance Holdings is further confirmation that peaceful dialogue can resolve such issues without impacting on innocent people and disrupting the economy.
tgt: Ditumellano tse latetseng seo pakeng tsa Mokgatlo wa Ditekesi wa Aforika Borwa le Lekala la Dithuso tsa Ditjhelete tsa Ditekesi la Aforika Borwa ke tiisetso e nngwe ya hore dipuisano tsa kgotso di ka rarolla dintlha tse jwalo ntle le ho hahlamela batho ba hlokang molato le ho sitisa moruo.

src: Cabinet welcomes this decision, which is in the best interest of commuters and the taxi industry.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela qeto eo, e leng molemong wa bapalami le indaseteri ya ditekesi.

src: Cabinet welcomes the dialogue currently taking place between the Department of Transport and the leadership of the taxi industry in finding a lasting solution.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela dipuisano tse ntseng di tswela pele hajwale pakeng tsa Lefapha la Dipalangwang le baetapele ba indaseteri ya ditekesi mabapi le ho fumana tharollo ya moshwelella.

src: The department will be engaging development finance institutions to seek alternative taxi finance options.
tgt: Lefapha le tla buisana le dikaho tsa ntshetsopele ya ditjheletebakeng sa ho batlana le ditsela tse ding tsa ho thusa boraditekesi ka ditjhelete.

src: Cabinet conveys its deepest sympathy to all who lost loved ones during the recent disasters in the Western and Eastern Cape respectively.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisetsa matshediso a yona a tebileng ho bohle ba lahlehetsweng ke baratuwa ba bona dikoduweng tsa haufinyana tjenaho la Kapa Bophirima le Kapa Botjhabela ka tatelano.

src: A number of residents also suffered displacement and loss of property.
tgt: Bongata ba badudi hape ba feletswe ke bodulo le ho lahlehelwa ke thepa.

src: Cabinet commends the prompt integrated approach and response from government, business and ordinary South Africans in assisting the affected families.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa katamelo ya ka potlako e kopanetsweng le karabelo ho tswa mmusong, borakgwebo le maAforika Borwa ka kakaretso mabapi le ho thusa malapa a amehileng.

src: Cabinet pays tribute to the heroic volunteer firefighter, Bradley Richards and the truck driver John Blaaw who assisted firefighters in transporting water who paid with their lives saving their community.
tgt: Kabinete e lebisa hlompho ho mohale wa moithaopi wa ditimamollo, Bradley Richards le mokganni wa dilori John Blaaw ba thusitseng batimamollo ka ho tsamaisa metsi le ho lahlehelwa ke bophelo ba e mong wa bona ha ba ne ba thusa batho ba motse wa bo bona.

src: Cabinet further extends a special appreciation to the Working on Fire team that bravely fought the raging fires.
