tgt: Dilemong tse 23 tse fetileng, mmuso o ekeditse lenaneo la dithuso tsa ditjhelete ho badudi ba futsanehileng le ba kotsing ho tloha ho batho ba 2,7 milione ho ya ho ba 17 milione.

src: This programme covers over 91% of eligible children and 95,5% of the eligible old age people.
tgt: Lenaneo lena le akaretsa bana ba tshwanelehang ba fetang 91% le 95,5% ya maqheku a tshwanelehang.

src: Over 20 000 schools have been declared no-fee schools, with over nine million learners benefiting from the school nutrition programmes.
tgt: Dikolo tse fetang 20 000 di nkuwe e le tse sa lefiseng ditjhelete tsa sekolo, ka baithuti ba fetang dimilione tse robong ba kgolang molemo mananeong a phepo a dikolo.

src: The National Student Financial Aid Scheme has since 1999 disbursed more than R72 billion in loans and bursaries to students from poor households.
tgt: Sekema sa Naha sa Thuso ya Ditjhelete ho Baithuti(NSFAS) ho tloha ka selemo sa 1999 se se se fanne ka ho fetang R72 bilione ya dikadimo le dibasari ho baithuti ba tswang malapeng a futsanehileng.

src: This has resulted in more than two million students from poor communities accessing tertiary education.
tgt: Sena se bakile hore baithuti ba fetang dimilione tse pedi ba tswang metseng e futsanehileng ba fihlelle thuto e phahameng.

src: A total of 1,7 million children are accessing registered Early Childhood Development services, which is a critical foundation for education.
tgt: Palohohle ya bana ba 1,7 milioneba fihlella ditshebeletso tse ngodisitsweng tsa Dikolo tsa Thuto ya Dikonyana (ECD), e leng motheo o hlokolosi bakeng sa thuto.

src: In 2012 government also introduced a school health programme, which is an intervention to some of the barriers that hinder progress in some of the learners.
tgt: Ka selemo sa 2012 mmuso o boetse o tsebahaditse lenaneo la boitekanelo la dikolo, e leng boitshunyako ditshiteng tse ding tse sitisang kgatelopele ya ba bang ba baithuti.

src: Additionally, government has a number of anti-poverty measures which provide free access to basic services to millions of indigent families such as free piped water, sanitation, free electricity and refuse removal.
tgt: Hodima moo, mmuso o na le mekgwa e mengata ya ho ema kgahlanong le bofutsana e fanang ka phihlello ya mahala ya ditshebeletso tsa motheo ho dimilione tsa malapa a fumanehileng tse kang metsi a mahala a pompo, tsamaiso ya dikgwerekgwere, motlakase wa mahala le ho thotha matlakala.

src: Government has also implemented public employment programmes and housing schemes to enable poor families to have houses.
tgt: Mmuso hape o kentse tshebetsong mananeo a kgiro ya setjhaba le dikema tsa matlo ho thusa batho ba futsanehileng ho ba le matlo.

src: Government will continue to find ways to strengthen some of the social security programmes that are designed to cushion the poor and vulnerable communities.
tgt: Mmuso o tla tswela pele ho batlana le ditsela tse ding tsa ho matlafatsa mananeo a tsa polokeho ya kahisano a reretsweng ho tshehetsa badudi ba futsanehileng le ba kotsing.

src: Cabinet commends the launch of the Ghana Radio Astronomy Observatory, by the Ghanaian President Nana Akufo-Addo and South Africa’s Minister of Science and Technology, Ms Naledi Pandor.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsaho thakgolwa ha Sebaka sa Radio sa Tekolo ya Dinaledi sa Ghana, ke Moporesidente wa Ghana Nana Akufo-Addo le Letona la Saense le Thekenoloji la Aforika Borwa, MofumahadiNaledi Pandor.

src: This is significant for Africa’s participation in the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) project.
tgt: Sena ke sa bohlokwa bakeng sa bonkakarolo ba Aforika porojekeng ya Dipontsho tsa Sekwere sa Kilomithara (SKA).

src: The observatory in Ghana is the first other than South Africa, as one of the partner WEBTOKEN SKA Africa partners, the SKA South Africa/Hartebeesthoek Radio Astronomy Observatory group collaborated with Ghana to harness the radio astronomy potential of the redundant satellite communication antenna at Kuntunse.
tgt: Sebaka sa tekolo ya dinaledi ho la Ghana ke sa pele ntle le Aforika Borwa, jwaloka e nngwe ya dinaha tsa bomphato.

src: The Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) has funded a large part of the conversion project through the African Renaissance and International Cooperation Fund, which is aimed at strengthening cooperation between South Africa and other African countries.
tgt: Jwaloka bomphato ba SKA ya Aforika, sehlopha sa SKA South Africa/Hartebeesthoek Radio Astronomy Observatory se sebedisane mmoho le Ghana ho qhaneha bokgoni ba anthena ya astronomi ya radio ya dikgokahanyo tsa disatalaete e teng Kuntunse.

src: A vital part of the effort towards building the SKA on the African continent over the next decade is to develop the skills, regulations and institutional capacity needed in SKA partner countries to optimise African participation in the project.
tgt: Lefapha la Dikamano le Tshebedisano ya Matjhaba (DIRCO) le thusitse ka ditjhelete karolo e kgolo ya porojeke ena ya ho fetolaka Letlole la Tlhaboloho ya Aforika le Tshebedisano ya Matjhaba, le reretsweng ho matlafatsa tshebedisano-mmoho pakeng tsa Aforika Borwa le dinaha tse ding tsa Aforika.

src: Cabinet welcomes the announcement from the Minister of Environmental Affairs, Ms Edna Molewa that South Africa is finalizing in the outstanding three provinces, a verification and audits of all the existing privately owned rhino horn stockpiles.
tgt: Karolo ya bohlokwa ya mokutu o lebisitseng kahong ya SKA kontinenteng ya Aforika dilemong tse leshome tse tlang ke ho ntshetsa pele maitsebelo, melawana le bokgoni ba ditheo tsebatlehang dinaheng tsa bomphato ba SKA ho phahamisa bonkakarolo ba Aforika porojekeng ena.

src: The initial audit which was conducted by the provinces is being checked and verified by the national Department of Environmental Affairs.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela tsebiso ya Letona la Lefapha la Merero ya Tikoloho, Mofumahadi Edna Molewa ya hore Aforika Borwa e qetella diporofenseng tse saletseng morao, netefatso ya bohlakisiya pokello e teng ya beng ba poraefete ba manaka a ditshukudu.

src: This will assist in preventing the potential smuggling of illegally obtained rhino horns and will ensure that the country has full and accurate information on the number of horns in South Africa at any given time, as well as the registered owner of each one of such horns.
tgt: Sena se tla thusa bakeng sa ho thibela kgonahalo ya ho mokolwa ha manaka a ditshukudu a fumanweng ka tsela e seng molaong mme se tla netefatsa hore naha e na le tlhahisoleseding e nepahetseng mabapi le palo ya manaka a ditshukudu ka hara Aforika Borwa nakong leha e le efe, hammoho le monga manaka a jwalo ya ngodisitsweng.

src: On the ruling by the North Gauteng High Court on the issuing of the permit on the selling of Rhino horns to breeder Mr John Hume, which saw South Africa’s first online auction of Rhino horn, Cabinet reiterates amongst several other operational conditions, that the position permit holder, who must have acquired a sellers permit can only sell rhino horn to a person who has a buyers permit issued in terms of the National Environmental Management Biodiversity Act, 2004 (Act 10 of 2004), authorizing him/her to buy rhino horn from a sellers permit holder, in this case being Mr Hume.
tgt: Kahlolong ya Lekgotla la Dinyewe le Phahameng la Gauteng Leboya mabapi le ho ntsha tumello ya ho rekiswa ha manaka a Ditshukudu bakeng sa motswadisi wa ditshukudu Monghadi John Hume, moo ho bonahetseng ho ba le fantisi ya pele ya manaka a Ditshukudu ho marangrang a inthanete ka hara Aforika Borwa, Kabinete e boeletsa hara maemo a mang a tshebetso, hore maemo a monga tumello, ya lokelang hore a fumane tumello ya ho rekisa e ntshitsweng ho ya kaMolao wa Naha wa Bolaodi ba Tikoloho ya Diphapang tsa Tlhaho, 2004 (Molao wa bo-10 wa selemo sa 2004), o mo dumellang ho reka manaka a ditshukuduho monga tumello ya ho rekisa, tabeng ena e leng Monghadi Hume.

src: The permit does not authorize international trade in rhino horn.
tgt: Tumello ena hae e dumelle kgwebisano ya matjhaba ya manaka a ditshukudu.

src: International trade on horn remains banned, in terms of the provisions on the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).During the entire auction the department of environment must be granted access to the online auction to do the necessary compliance monitoring.
tgt: Kgwebisano ya matjhaba ya manaka a ditshukudu e ntse e thibetswe, ho ya ka dipehelo tsa Khonvenshene ya Kgwebisano ya Matjhaba ka Mefuta e Kotsing ya Diphoofolo le Dimela tse Hlaha (CITES).

src: South Africa remains committed to a regulated process that manages the trade in threatened or protected species in line with the domestic legislation, as well as the legally binding provisions of the CITECabinet welcomes the High Court guilty verdict against the perpetrators involved in a case involving racially motivated violation of an African man by being put in a coffin.
tgt: Nakong ya fantisi ena kaofela lefapha la tikoloho le lokela ho nehwa phumantsho ya fantisi ya marangrang a inthanete ho etsa bodisa ba boimatahanyo bo batlehang.

src: The guilty verdict will serve as a warning to those who still continue to harbor racial prejudices in the country.
tgt: Kahlolo ya ho bonwa molato e tla sebetsa jwaloka temoso ho ba ntseng ba tswela pele ho phehella kgethollo ya semorabe ka hara naha.

src: Cabinet reassures South Africans that any form of racism or act of hate will not be tolerated.
tgt: Kabinete e netefaletsa maAforika Borwa hore sebopeho leha e le sefe sa semorabe kapa ketso ya lehloyo di keke tsa mamellwa.

src: Social cohesion remains an imperative that all of us as a society needs to build and strengthen.
tgt: Momahano ya kahisano e dula e le tokelo eo rona kaofela jwaloka setjhaba eo re lokelang ho e aha le ho e matlafatsa.

src: Cabinet welcomed the Constitutional Court Judgement that ruled that municipalities can no longer hold new property owners liable for previous owners’ historical municipal debt.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse Kahlolo ya Lekgotla la Molaotheo le laetseng hore bomasepala ba keke ba hlola ba beha boikarabelo ho beng ba batjha ba matlo bakeng sa mekitlane ya masepala ya beng ba pele ba matlo.

src: The ruling is a relief to property owners, some of whom have been burdened with debt dating back 20 years.
tgt: Taelo ena ke kimoloho ho beng ba matlo, bao bang ba bona esale ba imetswa ka mokitlane wa dilemo tse 20 tse fetileng.

src: Such a ruling paves way for future new property owners.
tgt: Taelo e jwalo e betla tsela bakeng sa beng ba thepa ba kamoso.

src: Cabinet calls on municipalities to align their debt collections system to the ruling.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho bomasepala ho matahanya mekgwa ya bona ya pokello ya mekitlane le taelo ena.

src: Cabinet notes that National Treasury is overseeing a forensic investigation into alleged irregularities in the Integrated Financial Management System (IFMS) programme.
tgt: Kabinete e lemohile hore Lefapha la Naha la Matlotlo le okametse dipatlisiso tsa diforensiki mabapi le ho se sebetse hantle ha lenaneo la Tsamaiso e Kopanetsweng ya Bolaodi ba Ditjhelete (IFMS).Kabinete e thoholetsa Lefapha la Naha la Matlotlo bakeng sa ditaolo tsa yona tsa ka hare tsa tlhatlhobo tse matla, tse hlwaileng ditshenyehelo tse sa lokang.

src: Cabinet commends National Treasury for its robust internal audit controls, which identified irregular expenditure.
tgt: E tshepa hore ho tla ba le thuto e nepahetseng mabapi le diphephetso tse fihlelletsweng, le hore ketso efe ya phoso ya ka boomo kapa ho se tsotelle e tla hlwauwa mme ba amehang batla ikarabella.

src: Cabinet has full confidence in the institutional strength of National Treasury and its custodianship of public finances.
tgt: Kabinete e na le tshepo e feletseng ho matla a semolao a Lefapha la Naha la Matlotlole bohlokomedi ba lona ba ditjhelete tsa mmuso.

src: Cabinet further expresses its faith in the IFMS programme’s implementing agencies – National Treasury, the Department of Public Service and Administration, and the State Information Technology Agency – to implement the project successfully.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e hlahisa tshepo ya yona ho makala a kenyang tshebetsong mananeo a IFMS – Lefapha la Naha la Matlotlo, Lefapha la Tshebeletso ya Mmuso, le Lekala la Thekenoloji ya Tlhahisoleseding ya Puso– bakeng sa ho kenya tshebetsong porojeke ena ka katleho.

src: Cabinet condemns the leak of a Cabinet Memo proposing options for recapitalizing the South African Airways.
tgt: Kabinete e tshwela ka mathe ho nyenyelepa ha Memo wa Kabinete o sisinyang mekgwa e fapaneng ya ho thusa botjha Tshebeletso ya Difofane ya Aforika Borwa (SAA).

src: A Cabinet Memo is a classified document and leaking it contravenes the government’s information security framework, the Minimum Information Security Standards.
tgt: Memo wa Kabineteke tokomane ya lekunutu mme ho e nyenyelepisa ke tlolo ya moralo wa tshireletso ya tlhahisoleseding ya mmuso, o bitswang Maemo a Tlase a Tshireletso yaTlhahisoleseding.

src: Cabinet has tasked the Justice, Crime Prevention and Security Cluster to investigate the leak of classified information and calls for relevant punitive measures to be applied to those responsible.
tgt: Kabinete e fane ka mosebetsi ho Karolo ya Tshireletso, ya Toka, le Thibelo ya Botlokotsebe ho batlisisa ho nyenyelepa ha tlhahisoleseding ya lekunutu le ho ipiletsa bakeng sa mekgwa ya kotlo e tla sebediswa hodima ba ikarabellang.

src: Cabinet welcomes the increase in funding by the Industrial Development Corporation (IDC) for investment in productive capacity in South Africa, as reflected in its recently released financial results to March 2017.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho eketswa ha thuso ka ditjhelete ke Koporasi ya Ntshetsopele ya Diindaseteri (IDC) bakeng sa botsetedi hobokgoni ba tlhahiso ka hara Aforika Borwa, jwaloka ha ho bonahala sephethong sa yona se lokolotsweng haufinyana tjena sa ditjhelete ho fihlela ka Hlakubele 2017.

src: During the National Women’s Month, the IDC approved funding of R3,2 billion for women-empowered businesses, an increase of 178% compared to the previous year.
tgt: Kgweding ya Naha ya Basadi, IDC e tjhaelletse monwana dithuso tsa matlole tsa R3,2 bilione bakeng sa dikgwebo tse matleng a basadi, e leng keketseho ya 178% ha ho bapiswa le selemong se fetileng.

src: This included funding for a transaction that places control of a large manganese mine in the hands of a black South African woman.
tgt: Sena se kenyeleditse thuso ya matlole bakeng sa tumellano e behang taolo ya morafo o moholo wa mankanisi matsohong a mosadi wa motho e motsho wa Aforika Borwa.

src: Funding for black-empowered companies amounted to R10,1 billion, of which R4,7 billion was for investment projects led by black industrialists.
tgt: Dithuso tsa matlole bakeng sa dikhamphani tse matleng a ba batsho di ne di fihla ho R10,1 bilione, moo R4,7 bilione ya yona e ne e le ya diporojeke tsa matsete tse eteletsweng pele ke boradiindaseteri ba batho ba batsho.

src: These numbers underscore the progress made with transformation of economic ownership in the country.
tgt: Dipalo tsena di pakahatsa kgatelopele e entsweng ka diphethoho tsa ho ba le dikgwebo moruong ka hara naha.

src: A total of 20 881 jobs were created or saved in the full IDC funding for the year, which amounted to R15,3 billion, the highest level yet.
tgt: Ho hlahisitswe palohohle ya mesebetsi e 20 881 kapa ho e baballa ka selemo se tletseng sa thuso ya matlole ke IDC, e leng tjhelete e fihlileng ho R15,3 bilione, e leng boemo bo phahameng ka ho fetisisa ho fihlela jwale.

src: Over the past five years from 2013, the IDC committed R68 billions of funding to investment projects.
tgt: Dilemong tse hlano tse fetileng ho tloha ka selemo sa 2013, IDC e ne e nyehetse R68 bilione ya matlole bakeng sa diporojeke tsa matsete.

src: Together with private sector co-funding, this facilitated investments worth R200 billion and created or saved 99 000 jobs.
tgt: Mmoho le thuso ya matlole e kopanetsweng le lekala la poraefete, sena se bakile matsete a etsang R200 bilione le ho hlahisa kapa ho baballa mesebetsi e 99 000.

src: Cabinet congratulates the IDC and the Economic Development Department on this performance at a time when efforts to boost investment and job creation are critical.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa IDC le Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Moruo ka tshebetso ena nakong ena eo mekutu ya ho matlafatsa matsete le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi di leng hlokolosi.

src: Cabinet welcomes the setting up of a Market Inquiry into high data costs and notes the gazetting of the terms of reference by the Competition Commission.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho thehwa ha Diphuputso tsa Dimmaraka mabapi le ditjeho tse hodimo tsa datha le ho lemoha ho kenngwa koranteng ya mmuso ha dintlha tsa tshupiso ke Khomishene ya Tlhodisano.

src: The Market Inquiry arose out of a request by the Minister of Economic Development in terms of the Competition Act.
tgt: Diphuputso tsa Dimmaraka di hlahisitswe ke kopo ya Letona la Ntshetsopele ya Moruo ho ya ka dipehelo tsa Molao wa Tlhodisano.

src: High data costs have serious economic effects, increases the costs of doing business and can limit the ability of South Africa to successfully utilise new information technologies.
tgt: Ditjeho tse hodimo tsa datha di na le ditlamorao tse matla tsa moruo, di eketsa ditjeho tsa ho etsa kgwebo le ho ka fokotsa bokgoni ba Aforika Borwa ho sebedisa ka katleho dithekenoloji tse ntjha tsa tlhahisoleseding.

src: Cabinet supports the call on service providers in the sector to cut data costs.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho bafani ba ditshebeletso ka hara lekala lena ho fokotsa ditjeho.

src: Cabinet welcomes the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Government of Flanders on promotion of the Social Economy in South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e amohelaho saenwa ha Memorandamo wa Kutlwano (MoU) le Mmuso wa Flanders wa kgodiso ya Moruo wa Kahisano ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: The New Growth Path economic strategy adopted in 2010 identified the social economy as one of 10 job WEBTOKEN terms of the MoU, the Minister of Economic Development will work in partnership with the International Labour Organisation (ILO) and the Government of Flanders to document successful examples of social enterprises and will engage local stakeholders on the development of a policy framework to consolidate and strengthen work on the social economy.
tgt: Lewa la moruo la Tsela e Ntjha ya Kgolo le amohetsweng ka selemo sa 2010 le hlwaile moruo wa kahisano jwalo ka se seng sa dintlha tse 10 tsa ho hlahisa mesebetsi.

src: Flanders will also partner with the Department of Environmental Affairs in a project on climate change and the green economy, which will focus on adaptation strategies.
tgt: Ho ya ka MoU, Letona la Ntshetsopele ya Moruole tla sebetsa ka bomphato le Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba wa Basebetsi (ILO) le Mmuso wa Flanders ho hlahisa mehlala e atlehileng ya dikgwebo tsa kahisano mme le tla buisana le bankakarolo ba lehae mabapi le lewa la maano ho tiisa le ho matlafatsa mosebetsi wa moruo wa kahisano.

src: Cabinet is saddened by the loss of life on the country’s roads caused by persistent negligent, reckless and irresponsible drivers.
tgt: Flanders hape e tla etsa bomphato le Lefapha la Merero ya Tikoloho porojekeng ya diphethoho tsa tlelaemete le moruo o hlwekileng, botla tsepamisa maikutlo hodima ho amohela mawa.

src: Recently 13 children were injured after an alleged drunken driver crashed a taxi into a tree.
tgt: Kabinete e utlwisitswe bohloko ke mafu a batho mebileng ya naha a bakwang ke bakganni ba dulang ba sa tsotelle, ho kganna bohlwaswa le ho hloka boikarabelo.

src: Two weeks ago another incidence happened in KwaZulu-Natal, which resulted in 19 deaths and nine injured after a taxi crashed into a bridge.
tgt: Haufinyana tjena bana ba 13 ba lemetse kamora ho ba mokganni eo ho belaellwang ho re o ne a tahilwe a thule sefate ka tekesi.

src: Cabinet appeals to all those with children in their care to be extra vigilant about drivers transporting children and commuters.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho bohle ba nang le bana ba tlhokomelong ya bona ho fadimehela ka matla bakganni ba tsamaisang bana le bapalami.

src: Cabinet calls on the law enforcement agencies to be more vigilant on our roads to ensure the safety of the road users.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho makala a qobello ya molao ho fadimeha haholo mebileng ya rona ho netefatsa polokeho ya basebedisi ba mebila.

src: Cabinet condemns violence, vandalism, and burning of public infrastructure such as the recent Rea Vaya bus station in Gauteng.
tgt: Kabinete e tshwela ka mathe merusu, tshenyo ya thepa, le ho tjhesa meralo ya motheo ya setjhaba e kang ya haufinyana tjena ya seteishene sa dibese sa Rea Vaya Gauteng.

src: Public transport Infrastructure is a national resource that is meant to serve the public.
tgt: Meralo ya Motheo ya Setjhaba ya dipalangwang ke mohlodi wa naha o reretsweng ho sebeletsa setjhaba.

src: No amount of dissatisfaction by communities can justify the destruction of property.
tgt: Ha ho na ho se kgotsofale ho hokalo ho ka bakang tshenyo ya thepa.

src: Cabinet calls on the law enforcement agencies to deal with such criminality.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho makala a qobello ya molao ho sebetsana le botlokotsebe bo kang bona.

src: Cabinet applauded the financial contribution by the National Disaster Management Centre to the Western Cape Provincial Government.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholeditse nyehelo ya ditjhelete ya Setsi sa Naha sa Bolaodi ba Dikoduwa ho Mmuso wa Porofense ya Kapa Bophirima.

src: More than R74 million was made available to address drought-related challenges, including recent ravaging fires and shortage of livestock feed.
tgt: Tjhelete e fetang R74 milione e ile ya ba teng ho shebana le diphephetso tse amanang le komello, ho kenyeletsa le mello ya haufinyana tjena e matla le kgaello ya furu.

src: Cabinet continues to call on South Africans to utilize water sparingly.
tgt: Kabinete e tswela pele ho ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ho sebedisa metsi ka paballo.

src: Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet welcomed an increase in the uptake of locally developed technologies and innovations in South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse keketseho ya tshebediso ya dithekenoloji le dintlafatso tse entsweng lapeng ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: Science and technology is a key enabler in the multipronged national effort to secure higher economic growth rates in the National Development Plan.
tgt: Saense le thekenoloji ke dithusi tse kgolo mokutung wa mekgahlelo e mengata ya naha bakeng sa ho tiisetsa sekgahla se phahamang sa kgolo ya moruo ho Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP).Ho ya ka Tlaleho ya Tshebetso ya Saense, Thekenoloji le Ntlafatso ya 2015 ya Lekgotla la Naha la Boeletsi Ntlafatsong (NACI) ditjeho tsa thekenoloji di batlile di menahana habedi jwaloka phesente ya Palohohle ya Dihlahiswa tsa Naha (GDP) ho tloha ho 0.018% ka selemo sa 2005 ho isa ho 0.033% ka sa 2015.Mafapha a mangata, lekala la poraefete le ditheo tsa diphuputso di tsetetse thekenoloji le ntlafatso tse ngata haholo mananeong a tsona a ntshetsopele ka ho latelana.

src: According to the 2015 Science, Technology and Innovation Performance Report of the National Advisory Council on Innovation (NACI) a technology expenditure nearly doubled as a percentage of GDP from 0.018% in 2005 to 0.033% in 2015.
tgt: Jwaloka tsela ya ho matlafatsa diphihlello tsena ho ya pele, Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana dibaka tse tharo tsa menyetla tse hlwailweng ke Lefapha la Saense le Thekenoloji ho tshehetsa dithekenoloji tsa kalafo, tshireletso le dithekenoloji tse amanang le polokeho le meralo ya motheo e mabapi le thekenoloji.

src: More departments, private sector and research institutions have invested a great deal of technology and innovation in their respective developmental WEBTOKEN a way of further strengthening these achievements, Cabinet approved three opportunity areas identified by Department of Science and Technology to support in the health technologies, defense and security related technologies and social infrastructure in respect of technology.
tgt: Kabinete hape e tjhaelletse monwana mosebetsi wa tlatsetso wa ho ba mohlaleng le ho metha ntshetsopeleya thekenoloji le ntlafatso ntshetsopeleng ya kahisano le moruo.

src: Cabinet approved for the introduction of the Overvaal Resorts Limited Bill of 2017 into Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho tsebahatswa ha Bili ya Overvaal Resorts Limited ya selemo sa 2017 Palamenteng.

src: The focus of the Bill is to repeal Aventura’s founding legislation, the Overvaal Resorts Limited Act, 1993 (Act 127 of 1993).
tgt: Morero wa Bili ke ho hlakola molao wa ho thehwa ha Aventura, Molao wa Overvaal Resorts Limited, 1993 (Molao wa bo-127 wa selemo sa 1993).

src: This will enable the completion of the disposal of Aventura.
tgt: Sena se tla thusa ho phethelwa ha ho fediswa ha Aventura.

src: Cabinet took the decision to dispose of Aventura after it considered it as a non-core asset in government.
tgt: Kabinete e nkile qeto ya ho fedisa Aventura kamora ho ba e nkuwe e le thepa eo e seng ka sehloohong ya mmuso.

src: The Bill went out for public consultation in March 2017.
tgt: Bili ena e tswile bakeng sa hore e tshohlwe le setjhaba ka Hlakubele 2017.

src: In aligning legislation with developments in the education landscape, Cabinet approved for the publication of the Basic Education Laws Amendment Bill of 2017 in the Government Gazette for public comment.
tgt: Bakeng sa ho matahanya molao le dintshetsopele lepatlelong la thuto, Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana phatlalatso ya Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya Melao ya Thuto ya Motheo sa 2017 Koranteng ya Mmuso bakeng sa tshwaelo ya setjhaba.

src: The Bill is the outcome of the review of all basic education legislation with a view to enhancing organisational efficiency so as to improve school governance, leadership and accountability, transforming education services, and protecting vulnerable groups to ensure the well-being of learners.
tgt: Bili ke sephetho sa ho shejwa botjha ha melao kaofela ya thuto ya motheo ka morero wa ho matlafatsa bohlwahlwa ba tsamaisohore ho tle ho ntlafatswe taolo, boetapele le boikarabelo, ho fetola ditshebeletso tsa thuto, le ho sireletsa dihlopha tse kotsing ho netefatsa boitekanelo ba baithuti.

src: Amendments were proposed to the South African Schools Act, 1996 (Act 84 of 1996), and the Employment of Educators Act, 1998 (Act 76 of 1998).
tgt: Dihlomathiso di sisintswe ho Molao wa Dikolo wa Aforika Borwa, 1996 (Molao wa bo-84 wa selemo sa 1996), le Molao wa Kgiro ya Matitjhere, 1998 (Molao wa bo-76 wa 1998).

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: In September we will mark Heritage Month, Tourism Month, Arbor Week, Public Service Month, National Development Plan (NDP) Month and Thusong Service Centre Week.
tgt: Ka Loetse re tla tshwaya Kgwedi ya Botjhaba, Kgwedi ya Bohahlaudi, Beke ya Tjalo ya Difate, Kgwedi ya Tshebeletso ya Mmuso, Kgwedi ya NDP le Beke yaThusong Service Centre.

src: Further details on these events will be communicated by the relevant departments.
tgt: Dintlha tse batsi ka diketsahalo tsena di tla tsebiswa ke mafapha a amehang.

src: As the chair of the SADC, South Africa has offered to host the SADC ICT Ministers Meeting from 4 to 7 September 2017 to discuss progress made on the implementation of the SADC Communications and ICT Programme.
tgt: Jwaloka modulasetulo wa SADC, Aforika Borwa e dumetse ho tshwara Kopano ya Matona a Dikgokahanyo tsa Tlhahisoleseding ya Thekenoloji (ICT) a SADC ho tloha ka la 4 ho isa ka la 7 Loetse 2017 ho tshohla kgatelopele e entsweng mabapi le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Lenaneo la Dikgokahanyo le ICT la SADC.

src: Minister Ayanda Dlodlo and Minister Siyabonga Cwele will lead the South African delegation in this meeting.
tgt: Letona Ayanda Dlodlo le Letona Siyabonga Cwele ba tla etella pele kemedi ya Aforika Borwa kopanong ena.

src: The meeting is to provide guidance on strategic communications and ICT issues and also track implementation of decisions made at previous meetings.
tgt: Morero wa kopano ke ho fana ka tataiso mabapi le dintlha tsa mawa a dikgokahanyo le ICT le ho ba mohlaleng wa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha diqeto tse entsweng dikopanong tse fetileng.

src: South Africa will use the meeting to promote access to affordable ICT infrastructure services, thereby positioning the country as a regional infrastructure hub and promoting small, medium and micro enterprises under the overall SADC industrialisation and regional integration agendas.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tla sebedisa kopano ena ho hodisa ho fihlellwa ha ditshebeletso tsa meralo ya motheo tsa ICT, ka seo naha e tla ba boemong ba ho ba sebaka sa meralo ya motheo ya lebatowa le ho hodisa dikgwebo tse nyenyane, tse mahareng le tse kgolo (di-SMME) tlasa mananeo a akaretsang a ho thehwa ha diindaseteri le kopano ya lebatowa a SADSeboka sa bo-9 sa Brazil, Russia, India, China le Aforika Borwa (BRICS) se tla tshwarwa Xiamen, China ho tloha ka la 4 ho isa la 5 Loetse 2017.

src: The 9th Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa (BRICS) Summit will take place in Xiamen, China from 4 to 5 September 2017.
tgt: Mookotaba wa bodulasetulo ba China ho BRICS ke:“BRICS: Dilekane tse Matla bakeng sa Bokamoso bo Kganyang”.Kgwebisano ka botlalo pakeng tsa Aforika Borwa le dinaha tsa BRICS e fihlile ho US$29 bilione ka selemo sa 2016.

src: The theme of China’s BRICS Chairpersonship is: “BRICS: Stronger Partnerships for a Brighter Future”.Total bilateral trade between South Africa and other BRICS countries amounted to US$29 billion in 2016.
tgt: Sebaka se seholo ka ho fetisisa sa thekiso ya ka ntle sa Aforika Borwa ka hara BRICS e dutse e le China, e latelwe ke India, Brazil mme e be Russia.

src: South Africa’s biggest export destination within BRICS remains China, followed by India, Brazil and then Russia.
tgt: Paterone e tshwanang e ya bonahala mabapi le dihlahiswa tse kenang ka hara naha, moo China e dutseng e le mohlodi o moholo ka ho fetisisa wa dihlahiswa tsa ka ntle.

src: The 2017 BRICS Summit will feature five key priorities namely, deepening cooperation, strengthening global governance, undertaking people-to-people exchanges, advancing institutional improvements and building broader partnerships.
tgt: Seboka sa selemo sa 2017 sa BRICS se tla tobana le dintlha tse hlano tse ka sehlohlolong e leng, ho tebisa tshebedisano-mmoho, ho matlafatsa taolo ya lefatshe, ho etsa diphapanyetsano tsa batho-ho-batho, ho ntshetsapele dintlafatso tsa ditheo le ho aha dilekane tse batsi.

src: The strategic focus for South Africa in BRICS is to promote value-added trade, attract investment into the country’s productive sectors and enhance cooperation to advance our development objectives.
tgt: Lewa la tsepamiso ya maikutlo bakeng sa Aforika Borwa ka hara BRICS ke ho hodisa kgwebisano ya boleng bo eketsehileng, ho hohella matsete ka hara makala a naha a tshepisang a tlhahiso le ho matlafatsa tshebedisano-mmoho ho hodisa merero ya rona ya ntshetsopele.

src: Cabinet noted the participation of South African companies in the 53rd edition of the Maputo International Trade Fair, commonly known as FACIM, which is taking place in Mozambique from 28 August to 3 September 2017.
tgt: Kabinete e lemohile bonkakarolo ba dikhamphani tsa Aforika Borwa Mokgahlelong wa bo-53 wa Dipontsho tsa Kgwebo tsa Matjhaba tsa Maputo, tse tlwaelehileng jwaloka FACIM, tse tla tshwarwa Mozambique ho tloha ka la 28 Phato ho isa ka la 3 Loetse 2017.

src: FACIM is an international multi-sectoral trade fair held annually to showcase Mozambique as an attractive destination for trade and investment.
tgt: FACIM ke dipontsho tsa matjhaba tsa kgwebo ya makala a fapaneng tse tshwarwang selemo ka seng ho pepesa Mozambique jwaloka sebaka se hohelang bakeng sa kgwebo le matsete.

src: Twenty companies were funded by the Department of Trade and Industry (the dti) while 10 were supported by the Mpumalanga Economic Growth Agency.
tgt: Dikhamphani tse 20 di ile tsa thuswa ka matlole ke Lefapha la Dikgwebo le Diindaseteri (dti) ha tse 10 di ile tsa tshehetswa ke Lekala la Mpumalanga la Kgolo ya Moruo.

src: The companies represented various sectors including chemicals, agro-processing, clothing and textile, engineering, mining and capital equipment, and electro-technical and built environment sectors.
tgt: Dikhamphani tsena di ne di emetse makala a fapafapaneng ho kenyeletsa makala a dikhemikhale, a tswelliso ya dihlahiswa tsa temo, a diaparo le masela, a boenjineri, a merafo le thepa ya dikaho tse kgolo, lea tekginiki ya motlakase le a tikoloho ya kaho.

src: Mozambique is South Africa’s third largest trade partner in the SADC region, after Botswana and Namibia.
tgt: Mozambique ke molekane wa boraro ya moholo ka ho fetisisa wa Aforika Borwa ka hara lebatowa la SADC, kamora Botswana le Namibia.

src: Trade between the two countries increased from R29 billion in 2012 to R43 billion in 2016.
tgt: Kgwebisano pakeng tsa dinaha tsena tse pedi e eketsehile ho tloha ho R29 bilione ka 2012 ho isa ho R43 bilione ka sa 2016.

src: There are currently 300 South African companies operating in Mozambique.
tgt: Hajwale ho na le dikhamphani tse 300 tsa Aforika Borwa tse sebetsang ka hara Mozambique.

src: The participation of the South African companies in FACIM received a particular recognition during last week’s Binational Commission as one of the platforms that business communities in the two countries can use for engaging on possible cooperation and partnerships for increasing trade and investment between our countries.
tgt: Bonkakarolo ba dikhamphani tsa Aforika Borwa ho FACIM bo fumane kananelo e itseng bekeng e fetileng ya Khomishene ya Dinaha tse Pedi jwaloka e nngwe ya mapatlelo ao badudi ka hara dinaha ka bobedi ba ka a sebedisang bakeng sa ho buisana mabapi le kgonahalo ya tshebedisano-mmoho le dilekane bakeng sa ho eketsa kgwebisano le matsete pakeng tsa dinaha tsa bo rona.

src: The Minister of Home Affairs, Profssor Hlengiwe Mkhize, will participate in the Ministerial Migration Dialogue for Southern Africa to be held in the Kingdom of Swaziland from 2 to 4 September 2017.
tgt: Letona la Lefapha la Merero ya Lehae, Moporofesara Hlengiwe Mkhize, o tla nka karolo ho Dipuisano tsa Matona tsa Bofalli bakeng sa Dinaha tsa Borwa ba Aforika tse tla tshwarelwa naheng ya Borena ba Swaziland ho tloha ka la 2 ho isa ka la 4 Loetse 2017.

src: The overall objective of the event is to foster dialogue among SADC member states to improve migration governance in the region.
tgt: Morero ka kakaretso wa ketsahalo ena ke ho kgothaletsa puisano hara ditho tsa dipuso tsa SADC ho ntlafatsa taolo ya bofalli ka hara lebatowa.

src: Issues to be explored include statelessness, migration, border management and labour migration.
tgt: Dintlha tse tla sekasekwa di kenyeletsa tlhokahalo ya puso e tsitsitseng, bofalli, bolaodi ba meedi le bofalli ba basebetsi.

src: Messages.
tgt: Melaetsa.

src: Cabinet expressed its deepest and heartfelt condolences to:Police Minister Fikile Mbalula and his family following the passing of his mother, Mama Emma Mbalula.
tgt: Kabinete e hlahisitse matshediso a yona a tebileng le kutlwelo-bohloko ho:Letona la Sepolesa Fikile Mbalula le lelapa la hae ho latela ho hlokahala ha mme wa hae, Mama Emma Mbalula.

src: May they find strength to cope with the difficulty and deep-seated pain that the passing of a mother brings to any home.
tgt: E se e ka ba ka thola matla a ho tobana le bothata le lehlaba le tebileng le tliswang ke ho lahlehelwa ke mme lelapeng leha e ka ba lefe.

src: the loved ones of three mineworkers who have been confirmed dead following an underground collapse of the Kusasalethu Mine near Cartonville in Gauteng, due to seismic activity registering on the Richter Scale.
tgt: baratuwa ba basebeletsi ba bararo ba morafo bao ho tiisitsweng ba hlokahetse ho latela ho putlama mpeng ya lefatshe ha Morafo wa Kusasalethu haufi le Cartonville Gauteng, ka lebakala ho reketla ha lefatshe ho ngodisitseng Sekaleng sa Richter.

src: Cabinet is hopeful that the two other missing miners will be rescued by search teams currently on the ground and is relieved that dozens of miners were brought safely to the surface amid the incident.
tgt: Kabinete e tshepa hore barafi ba bang ba babedi ba so tholahale ba tla pholoswa ke moifo wa patlo o ntseng o sebetsa hajwale le ho imoloha hore bongata ba barafi ba ile ba tliswa ka hodima lefatshe ka polokeho le hara kotsi ena.

src: the Government and people of the Republic of Sierra Leone following one of the worst floods in our continent.
tgt: Mmuso le batho ba Rephabliki ya Sierra Leone ho latela tse ding tsa dikgohola tse mpe ka ho fetisisa ka hara kontinente ya bo rona.

src: This natural disaster devastated significant parts of the country, resulting in massive loss of life, destruction of property and leaving behind a catastrophic humanitarian crisis.
tgt: Koduwa ena ya tlholeho e ripitlile dikarolo tsa bohlokwa tsa naha eo, e leng se bakileng tahlehelo e kgolo ya maphelo, tshenyo ya thepa le ho siya koduwa e matla ya botho.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 13 September 2017, at Tuynhuys, Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e kopane ka Laboraro, la 13 Loetse 2017, Tuynhuys, Motse Kapa.

src: Economy.
tgt: Moruo.

src: Cabinet welcomes the positive growth in the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of 2.5% in the second quarter of 2017, which has moved the country out of a technical recession.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela kgolo e ntle ya Palohohle ya Dihlahiswa tsa Naha (GDP) ya 2.5% kotareng ya bobedi ya selemo sa 2017, e leng e ntshitseng naha ka hara ho putlama ha moruo wa setekginiki.

src: Last week, Statistics South Africa released the figures, which represent a year-on-year growth of 1.1%.
tgt: Bekeng e fetileng, Lefapha la Dipalopalo la Aforika Borwa (Stats SA) le lokolotse dipalo, tse bontshang kgolo ya selemo-ka-selemo ya 1.1%.

src: Although cautiously optimistic, Cabinet is convinced the country is seeing the first positive signs of what is hopefully the start of the country’s economic recovery firmly built on the implementation of the Nine-Point Plan, which aims to grow the South African economy and create much-needed jobs.
tgt: Leha re shebile ka leihlo le tjhatsi le tshepisang, Kabinete e kgodisehile hore naha e bona matshwao a pele a matle ao e tshepang hore sena ke qalo ya ho iphumana ha moruo wa naha a ahilweng hodima ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Moralo wa Dintlha tse Robong, oo morero wa ona e leng ho hodisa moruo wa Aforika Borwa le ho hlahisa mesebetsi e batlehang haholo.

src: This has resulted in the launch of four industrial parks and the rise in net exports of agricultural raw products on average by 14.6% a year since The Black Industrialist Programme has supported 62 projects that have attracted R26 billion in private-sector investment and created 19 859 jobs to date.
tgt: Sena se bakile hore ho thakgolwe diphaka tse nne tsa diindaseteri le ho phahama ha dihlahiswa tsa temo tse tala tse rekisetswang dinaha tsa ka ntle kgahlanong le tse kenang ka hara naha ka palohare ya 14.6% ka selemo ho tloha ka selemo sa Lenaneo la Boradiindaseteri ba Batho ba Batsho Ie se le tsheheditse diporojeke tse 62 tse hohetseng R26 bilione matseteng a lekala la poraefete le ho bopa mesebetsi e 19 859 ho fihlela kajeno.

src: To support localisation, 21 products and sectors have been designated for local production.
tgt: Ho tshehetsa tlhahiso ya lehae, dihlahiswa le makala a 21 di rerilwe bakeng sa tlhahiso ya lehae.

src: Operation Phakisa has so far unlocked an estimated R.6 billion in investment in the oceans economy, with Government contributing R15 billion of this amount.
tgt: Operation Phakisa ho fihlela mona e se e butse matsete a akanngwang ho R.6 bilione moruong wa mawatle, moo mmuso o nyehetseng R15 bilione ya tjhelete ena.

src: Although the investments are mainly in infrastructure development in ports, marine manufacturing in particular boatbuilding, aquaculture and scientific surveys in the oil and gas sector, several Government departments have made substantial contributions to ensure the growth of this sector.
tgt: Leha matsete haholo e le a ntshetsopele ya meralo ya motheo ya maemakepe, tlhahiso ya dihlahiswa tsa thepa ya lewatleng ka ho qolleha kaho ya dikepe, diphedi tsa lewatle le diphuputso tsa saense lekaleng la oli le kgase, mafapha a mmalwa a Mmuso a entse dinyehelo tse bonahalang ho netefatsa kgolo ya lekala lena.

src: A total of 6517 jobs had been created in the various sectors.
tgt: Palo ka kakaretso ya mesebetsi e 6 517 e hlahisitswe makaleng a fapafapaneng.

src: Cabinet reiterates calls to all sectors of society, particularly government, business and civil society, to build on the positive momentum gained during the second quarter to sustain higher rates of economic growth and development, and to help save jobs.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa kgoeletso ya yona ho mafapha kaofela a setjhaba, ka ho qolleha mmuso, dikgwebo le setjhaba ka kakaretso, ho ahella hodima lebelo le letle le unnweng nakong ya kotara ya bobedi ho tsitlallela sekgahla se phahameng sa kgolo ya moruo le ntshetsopele, le ho thusa ka ho baballa mesebetsi.

src: The Minister of Finance, Mr Malusi Gigaba, continues to engage with various sectors on the inclusive economic growth action plan, which is set to inspire confidence in the country.
tgt: Letona la Ditjhelete, Monghadi Malusi Gigaba, o tswela pele ho buisana le makala a fapafapaneng mabapi le moralo wa tshebetso wa kgolo ya moruo e kenyeletsang, e rerilweng ho hlohleletsa tshepo ka hara naha.

src: The Minister will further unpack this when he delivers the Medium Term Budget Policy Statement in Parliament, Cape Town, on 25 October 2017.
tgt: Letona le tla boela le hlopholla sena ha le fana ka Pehelo ya Leano la Ditekanyetso la Nako e Bohareng Palamenteng, Motse Kapa, ka la 18 Mphalane 2017.

src: InvestSA One Stop Shop – Western Cape.
tgt: Lebenkele le Abelanang ka Ditshebeletso Tsohle la InvestSA – Kapa Bophirima.

src: Cabinet commended the launch of the first provincial InvestSA One Stop Shop.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholeditse ho thakgolwa ha Lebenkele le Abelanang ka Ditshebeletso Tsohle la InvestSA la pele ka hara porofense.

src: President Jacob Zuma officially launched the InvestSA One Stop Shop in the Western Cape and affirmed government’s commitment to improving the investment climate in South Africa, which is an attractive destination for potential investors.
tgt: Moporesidente Jacob Zuma o thakgotse semmuso Lebenkele le Abelanang ka Ditshebeletso Tsohle la InvestSA ho la Kapa Bophirima le ho tiisa boitlamo ba mmuso ba ho ntlafatsa maemo a botsetedi ka hara Aforika Borwa, e leng sebaka se hohelang sa batsetedi ba ka bang teng.

src: The InvestSA One Stop Shop lowers the cost of doing business and eases doing business in the country by providing strategic guidance, reducing regulatory inefficiencies and cutting red tape for investors.
tgt: Lebenkele le Abelanang ka Ditshebeletso Tsohle la InvestSA Ie fokotsa ditjeho tsa ho etsa kgwebo le ho bebofatsa ho etsa kgwebo ka hara naha ka ho fana ka mawa a tataiso, ho fokotsa dikgaello tsa melawana le ho fokotsa mehato e mengata ya semolao bakeng sa batsetedi.

src: Government’s National InvestSA One Stop Shop was launched in March this year and through the dti, InvestSA One Stop shops will be established in all nine provinces – first in the Western Cape and followed by KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng respectively.
tgt: Lebenkele la Mmuso le Abelanang ka Ditshebeletso Tsohle la InvestSA le Thakgotswe ka Hlakubele selemong sena mme ka Lefapha la Dikgwebo le Diindaseteri (dti), Lebenkele le Abelanang ka Ditshebeletso Tsohle la InvestSA le tla thehwa diporofenseng kaofela tse robong – pele le tla thakgolwa ho la Kapa Bophirima mme e latelwe ke KwaZulu-Natal le Gauteng ka tatelano.

src: 5th Anniversary of the National Development Plan (NDP)1.
tgt: Sehopotso sa bo-5 sa Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP)1.

src: Cabinet joins South Africans in celebrating the 5th Anniversary of the NDP, which was adopted by Parliament on 12 September 2012 as the country’s socio-economic development blueprint to tackle the triple challenge of poverty, unemployment and inequality by As the country’s roadmap towards prosperity, the NDP belongs to all South Africans and represents the hopes and aspirations from all sectors of society, for a better South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e imatahanya le maAforika Borwa mabapi le ho keteka Sehopotso sa bo-5 sa NDP, eo e ileng ya amohelwa ke Palamente ka la 12 Loetse 2012 jwaloka moralo wa naha wa ntshetsopele ya moruo wa kahisano bakeng sa ho tobana le diphephetso tse tharo tsa bofuma, tlhokeho ya mesebetsi le ho se lekalekane ka selemo sa Jwaloka mmapa wa naha o lebisang mononong, NDP ke ya maAforika Borwa kaofela mme e emela ditakatso le ditabatabelo ho tswa Makaleng kaofela a setjhaba, bakeng sa Aforika Borwa e betere.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to rally behind the NDP Vision 2030.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa kaofela ho tshehetsa Tjhebelopele ya 2030 ya NDSeboka sa BRICKabinete e lemohile Seboka sa bo-9 se atlehileng sa Brazil, Russia, India, China le Aforika Borwa (BRICS), se neng se tshwaretswe Xiamen ka hara Riphabliki ya Batho ba China (PRC) ho tloha ka la 3 ho isa ka la 5 Loetse 2017 tlasa mookotaba: “BRICS: Bolekane bo Matla, bolekane bakeng sa Bokamoso bo Kganyang”.

src: The summit sets an important milestone towards building stronger solidarity and cooperation among emerging markets and developing countries to implement the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
tgt: Seboka se theha mokolokotwane wa bohlokwa o lebisitseng kahong ya kopano e matla le tshebedisano-mmoho hara mebaraka e ntseng e runya le dinaha tse ntseng di tswela pele ho kenya tshebetsong Lenaneo la 2030 bakeng sa Ntshetsopele ya Moshwelella.

src: South Africa’s partnership in BRICS is premised on advancing the country’s national interests, promoting regional integration and advocating a more inclusive global governance system.
tgt: Bolekane ba Aforika Borwa le BRICS bo thehilwe hodima ntshetsopele ya ditabatabelo tsa naha, ho hodisa kopano ya lebatowa le ho kgothaletsa tsamaiso e kenyeletsang ya taolo lefatsheng.

src: Total bilateral trade between South Africa and other BRICS countries amounted to US$29 billion last year.
tgt: Kgwebisano ka botlalo ya dinaha tse pedi pakeng tsa Aforika Borwa le dinaha tse ding tsa BRICS e fihlile ho US$29 bilione selemong se fetileng.

src: South Africa’s biggest export destination within BRICS remains China, followed by India, Brazil and Russia.
tgt: Sebaka sa thomello ya kantle ya thepa se seholo ka ho fetisisa sa Aforika Borwa ka hara BRICS e dutse e le China, e latelwa ke India, Brazil le Russia.

src: The same pattern is also evident in imports, with China remaining the biggest source of South African imports.
tgt: Paterone e tshwanang le ena hape e bonahala tabeng ya thepa e kenang ka hara naha, moo China e dutseng e le mohlodi o moholo wa thepa e rekisetswang ka Aforika Borwa.

src: Even though South Africa has abundant natural resources, it is critical to implement beneficiation programmes to support our industrialisation policy.
tgt: Leha Aforika Borwa e na le mehlodi ya tlhaho e mengata, ho hlokolosi ho kenya tshebetsong mananeo a bokgolamolemo ho tshehetsa leano la rona la kaho ya diindaseteri.

src: The adoption of the BRICS Xiamen Declaration and Action Plan highlighted the strong foundation that BRICS has made in terms of establishing institutional mechanisms for tangible cooperation.
tgt: Ho amohelwa ha Tumellano ya BRICS ya Xiamen le Moralo wa Tshebetso ho hlakisitse motheo o matla oo BRICS e o entseng mabapi le ho thehwa ha mekgwa ya dikaho bakeng sa tshebedisano-mmoho e tiileng.

src: Cabinet is honoured that South Africa is the incoming Chair of BRICS and entrenches its aim at the forefront to build on the BRICS programme of development and prosperity for partner countries, as it prepares to host the 10th BRICS Summit in 2018.
tgt: Kabinete e hlomphehile ka hore Aforika Borwa ke Modulasetulo ya tla tshwara marapo wa BRICS le ho tiiselletsa sepheo sa yona sa ho ba ka pele bakeng sa ho ahella hodima lenaneo la BRICS la ntshetsopele le monono bakeng sa dinaha tsa selekane, jwaloka ha e itokisetsa ho tshwara Seboka sa bo-10 sa BRICS ka selemo sa 2018. forika Borwa le Russia di saena tumellano.

src: South Africa and Russia sign agreement.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e amohela tumellano e saennweng pakeng tsa Aforika Borwa le Russia Sebokeng sa bo-9 sa BRICS, e tla hlahisa tjhelete e lakanang le US$400 milione e tla tsetelwa bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya lekala la oli le kgase la Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet further welcomes the agreement signed between South Africa and Russia at the 9th BRICS Summit, which will yield an amount of US$400 million being invested in the development of South Africa’s oil and gas sector.
tgt: Khamphani ya oli ya naha ya Aforika Borwa, PetroSA, le khamphani ya Federeishene ya Russia ya diphuputso tsa sebopeho sa mobu, Rosgeo, di dumellane ho ntshetsapele dibaka tsa ho fuputsa tsa diboloko tsa 9 le 11a Lebopong le ka Borwa la Aforika Borwa.

src: South Africa’s national oil company, PetroSA, and the Russian Federation geological exploration company, Rosgeo, have agreed to develop the exploration areas of blocks 9 and 11a off the South Coast of South Africa.
tgt: Ho batlana le mehlodi ya oli le kgase ka hara Aforika Borwa ke ntlha e kgolo ya lewa la polokeho ya eneji ya naha.

src: The search for oil and gas resources in South Africa is highly strategic for the country’s energy security.
tgt: Rosgeo ya Russia e tla etsa mosebetsi wa diphuputso tsa mobu hammoho le ho tjheka didiba tsa diphuputso.

src: Russia’s Rosgeo will conduct geological exploration work as well as drilling exploratory wells.
tgt: Porojeke ena e ka baka hore ho be le ho epollwa ha dikhubiki mithara tse dimilione tse nne tsa kgase ka letsatsi mme qetellong e tla romellwa tlhwekisong ya PetroSA Gas-To-Liquids maane Mossel Bay, Lebopong le ka Borwa.

src: South African export markets.
tgt: Mebaraka ya Aforika Borwa ya thepa e romellwang ka ntle.

src: Cabinet congratulates the dti in leading a group of 20 South African companies to the World Food Moscow 2017 exhibition, which is underway until 15 September While promoting South Africa’s agro-processing industry, the participation of these local companies from the agro-processing sector, consolidates and establishes market presence of South Africa in Russia.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa dti mabapi le ho etella pele moifo wa dikhamphani tse 20 tsa Aforika Borwa dipontshong tsa selemo sa 2017 tsa Moscow tsa Dijo tsa Lefatshe, tse ntseng di tswela pele ho fihlela ka la 15 Loetse Ha re ntse re hodisa indaseteri ya tswelliso ya dihlahiswa tsa temo tsa Aforika Borwa, bonkakarolo ba dikhamphani tsena tsa lehae ho tswa lekaleng la tswelliso ya dihlahiswa tsa temo, bo matlafatsa le ho theha boteng ba Aforika Borwa ka hara mmaraka ona ho la Russia.

src: Their participation is made possible through the Export Marketing and Investment Assistance Scheme of the dti, which is instrumental in developing export markets for South African products and services, as well as recruiting new foreign direct investment into the country.
tgt: Bonkakarolo ba bona bo kgonne ho ba teng ka lebaka la Sekema sa Mebaraka ya ka ntle le Thuso ya Matsete sa dti, e leng se thusang haholo mabapi le ho ntshetsapele mebaraka ya thomello ya thepa dinaheng tsa ka ntle bakeng sa dihlahiswa tsa Aforika Borwa le ditshebeletso, hammoho le ho thaotha matsete a otlolohileng ho tla ka hara naha.

src: Trade between South Africa and Russia increased significantly from R5 billion in 2012 to almost R8 billion in 2016.
tgt: Kgwebisano pakeng tsa Aforika Borwa le Russia e eketsehile ka bokgabane ho tloha ho R5 bilione ka selemo sa 2012 ho ya ho se batlang se etsa R8 bilione ka selemo sa 2016.

src: Major South African exports include fruits and nuts, manganese ores, beverages, spirits and vinegar, wine, electrical machinery and equipment.
tgt: Thepa e kgolo e romellwang ka ntle ya Aforika Borwa e kenyeletsa ditholwana le matokomane, manya a mankanisi, dino, dispiriti le asene, veine, metjhini ya motlakase le thepa.

src: Cabinet is concerned about recent incidents of child labour in which children were found working on farms in the North West and Free State.
tgt: Kabinete e tshwenyehile ka diketsahalo tsa haufinyana tjena tsa tshebediso ya bana moo ho fumanweng bana ba sebetsa mapolasing ka hara Leboya Bophirima le Foreistata.

src: Cabinet condemns this unacceptable abuse and exploitation of vulnerable children.
tgt: Kabinete e tshwela ka mathe tshebediso e mpe le tshotlo ena e sa amoheleheng ya bana ba kotsing.

src: Cabinet commends members of the public who alerted the Department of Labour which, together with the Department of Social Development, acted swiftly to deal accordingly with this heinous form of child abuse.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa ditho tsa setjhaba tse lemositseng Lefapha la Mesebetsi leo, hammoho le Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba, ba sebeditseng ka potlako ho sebetsana ka toka le mokgwa ona o sisimosang wa tshebediso e mpe ya bana.

src: Cabinet is pleased that the affected children have been relocated to places of safety and that the Department of Labour will intensify inspections and work together with law-enforcement agencies to bring perpetrators to book.
tgt: Kabinete e thabisitswe ke hore bana ba amehang ba falliseditswe dibakeng tsa polokeho le hore Lefapha la mesebetsi le tla matlafatsa ditlhatlhobo le ho sebetsa mmoho le makala a qobello ya molao ho tshwara baetsi ba sena ba molato.4 .

src: Our children are the future of the country.
tgt: Bana ba rona ke bokamoso ba naha.

src: Cabinet condemns all forms of child labour and calls on all South Africans to remain vigilant at all times and report those violating the principles of our Constitution.
tgt: Kabinete e tshwela ka mathe dibopeho kaofela tsa tshebediso ya bana le ho ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa kaofela ho dula ba fadimehile ka dinako tsohle le ho tlaleha ba tlolang dipehelo tsa Molaotheo wa rona.5 .

src: The South African Schools Act, 1996 (Act 84 of 1996), together with the Children’s Act, 2005 (Act 38 of 2005), clearly directs that all children between the ages of seven and 15 are compelled to attend school.
tgt: Molao wa Dikolo wa Aforika Borwa, 1996 (Molao wa bo-84 wa 1996), hammoho le Molao wa Bana, 2005 (Molao wa bo-38 wa 2005), o laela ka ho hlaka hore bana bohle ba dipakeng tsa dilemo tse supileng le tse 15 ba qobelletswe ho kena sekolo.

src: According to the law, parents and guardians should ensure that learners of this age group are registered and attend school regularly or face implications of not abiding.
tgt: Ho ya ka molao, batswadi le bahlokomedi ba lokela ho netefatsa hore baithuti ba dilemong tsena ba ngodisitswe le ho ba sekolong kamehla kapa ba tobane le ditlamorao tsa ho se ikobele molao.

src: Drought.
tgt: Komello.

src: Cabinet is grateful to those in South Africa who have heeded the call to save water.
tgt: Kabinete e lebohela bohle ka hara Aforoka Borwa ba mametseng kgoeletso ya ho baballa metsi.

src: South Africa is a water-stressed country and the persistent drought conditions in parts of the country are a reminder to all people to save every drop by using water wisely and sparingly.
tgt: Aforika Borwa ke naha e nang le kgaello ya metsi mme maemo a komello a ntseng a tswela pele dikarolong tse ding tsa naha ke kgopotso ho batho bohle ya ho baballa lerothodi ka leng ka ho sebedisa metsi ka bohlale le ka paballo.

src: Although efforts to save water help ease the pressure on water source the lower than normal seasonal rain reported in the Western Cape and KwaZulu-Natal is evidence that more needs to be done to conserve water.
tgt: Leha mekutu ya ho baballa metsi e thusa ho fokotsa kgatello hodima mohlodi wa metsi a pula ya sehla e tlase ho feta tlwaelo ka hara Kapa Bophirima le KwaZulu-Natal ke bopaki ba hore ho lokelwa ho etswa ho hongata bakeng sa ho baballa metsi.

src: The Inter-Ministerial Task Team on Drought, led by the Department of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs, continues to monitor the drought conditions and offer the required support through relevant sector departments to mitigate the situation.
tgt: Moifo wa Tshebetso wa Kopanelo wa Matona mabapi le komello, o eteletsweng pele ke Lefapha la Kopanelo ya Puso le Merero ya Setso, o tswela pele ho beha leihlo maemong a komello le ho fana ka tshehetso e hlokahalang ka makala a mafapha ho bebofatsa boemo bona.

src: Government has allocated R74 million in relief funding to respond to the persistent drought in the Western Cape.
tgt: Mmuso o beheletse ka thoko R74 milione e le letlole la pebofatso bakeng sa ho arabela mabapi le komello e ntseng e tswela pele ka hara Kapa Bophirima.

src: The Department of Water and Sanitation is also making progress with preparations for the implementation of the Berg River to Voelvlei Augmentation Scheme.
tgt: Lefapha la Metsi le Tsamaiso ya Dikgwerekgwere le lona le hatetse pele ka boitokisetso ba ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Sekema sa Thusetso sa ho tloha Berg River ho ya Voelvlei.

src: The Minister of Water and Sanitation, Ms Nomvula Mokonyane, has since directed the Trans-Caledon Tunnel Authority to raise the finance and implement the project.
tgt: Letona la Metsi le Tsamaiso ya Dikgwerekgwere, Mofumahadi Nomvula Mokonyane, o se a laetse Bolaodi ba Tonele ya Trans-Caledon ho tla ka ditjhelete le ho kenya tshebetsong porojeke ena.

src: They have already started engaging with major users and will shortly be approaching the Minister for concurrence with the Minister of Finance for borrowing limits for the project.
tgt: Ba se ba qadile ho buisana le basebedisi ba baholo mme haufinyana ba tla buisana le Letona bakeng sa tumellano le Letona la Ditjhelete mabapi le ditekanyo tsa dikadimo bakeng sa porojeke ena.

src: Cabinet reiterates calls to all in South Africa to ensure water conservation is exercised as part of their daily lives.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa dikgoeletso ho bohle ba ka hara Aforika Borwa ho netefatsa hore paballo ya metsi e ba teng jwaloka karolo ya bophelo ba bona ba letsatsi ka leng.

src: Lesotho.
tgt: Lesotho.

src: Cabinet joins President Zuma in condemning the senseless killing of Lesotho Defence Force Commander, General Khoantle Motšomotšo.
tgt: Kabinete e imatahanya le Mopresidente Zuma mabapi le ho tshwela ka mathe dipolao tse hlokang kelello tsa Molaodi wa Lebotho la Tshireletso la Lesotho, Mokgenerale Khoantle Motšomotšo.

src: This latest incident of violence is unacceptable.
tgt: Ketsahalo ena ya morao-rao ya dikgoka ha e amohelehe.

src: It is now incumbent on the people and leadership of Lesotho to ensure that calm and normality returns to the Kingdom as a matter of urgency.
tgt: Jwale ho matsohong a batho le boetapele ba Lesotho ho netefatsa hore kgutso le maemo a tlwaelehileng a kgutlisetswa ka hara Borena e le taba e potlakileng.

src: We remain hopeful that the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Ministerial Fact-Finding Mission will be able to assist Lesotho in determining appropriate interventions.
tgt: Re dula re na le tshepo ya hore Ketapele ya Matona e Batlisisang Dinnete ya Ntshetsopele ya Dinaha tse ka Borwa ba Aforika (SADC) e tla kgona ho thusa Lesotho ho teka maitshunyako a nepahetseng.

src: The SADC remains resolute in its objective to consolidate, defend and maintain democracy, peace, security and stability in the region working with the leadership of Lesotho.
tgt: SADC e dula e tiile mererong ya yona ya ho matlafatsa, ho tshireletsa le ho baballa demokerasi, kgotso, polokeho le botsitso ka hara lebatowa mme e sebedisana le boetapele ba Lesotho.

src: Libya.
tgt: Libya.

src: Cabinet welcomes the outcomes from the African Union (AU) High Level Committee on Libya at the Level of Heads of State and Government, which was held in Brazzaville, in the Republic of Congo.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela diphetho tsa Komiti ya Boemo bo Phahameng ya Kopano ya Aforika (AU) e mabapi le Libya Boemong ba Dihlooho tsa Dipuso le Mebuso e neng e tshwaretswe Brazzaville, ho la Riphabliki ya Congo.

src: President Zuma participated in the High Level Committee, which discussed and reviewed efforts towards finding a lasting solution to the prevailing conflict in Libya.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o ne a nkile karolo Komiting ya Boemo bo Phahameng, e tshohlileng le ho sheba botjha mekutu e lebisitseng ho tholeng tharollo ya moshwelella mabapi le diqabano tse tswellang ho ba teng ka hara Libya.

src: As a member of the High Level Committee on Libya, South Africa supports all efforts of the AU aimed at bringing about a peaceful resolution to the Libyan crisis.
tgt: Jwaloka setho sa Komiti ya Boemo bo Phahameng e mabapi le Libya, Aforika Borwa e tshehetsa mekutu kaofela ya AU e reretsweng ho tlisa tharollo ya kgotso bakeng sa koduwa ya Libya.

src: Cabinet reiterates President Zuma’s assertion that South Africa is ready to assist Libya in Post-Reconstruction and Development efforts and to share our country’s experiences in reconciliation, constitution-building and the democratic transformation of the State.
tgt: Kabinete e boeletsa maikutlo a Moporesidente Zuma a hore Aforika Borwa e malala-a-laotswe ho thusa Libya mekutung ya Kamora Kaho Botjha le Ntshetsopele le ho arolelana le yona boiphihlelo ba naha ya bo rona ho tsa poelano, kaho ya molaotheo le phethoho ya demokerasi ya puso.

src: Cabinet also reiterates the importance of coordinated and harmonised international engagement in Libya.
tgt: Kabinete hape e boeletsa bohlokwa ba dipuisano tsa matjhaba tse hokahaneng tse nang le kutlwano ka hara Libya.

src: Conference of the Parties (CoP13)1.
tgt: Pitso ya Mekga (CoP13)1.

src: Cabinet acknowledges that South Africa, as a signatory to the United Nations (UN) Convention to Combat Desertification, is participating in the 13th Session of the COP13 currently taking place in Ordos, PRC from 6 to 16 September It is envisaged that the conference will finalise and adopt a new strategic framework for 2018-2030 organised under the theme “Towards a Healthy Land for Present and Future Generations”.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela hore Aforika Borwa, jwalo ka mosaenedi ho Khonvenshene ya Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) ya Twantsho ya Mahwatata, e nka karolo Tulong ya bo-13 ya COP13 e ntseng e tswela pele hajwale Ordos, PRC ho tloha ka la 6 ho isa ka la 16 Loetse Ho lebeletswe hore pitso ena e tla phethela le ho amohela moralo o motjha wa lewa bakeng sa 2018-2030 e hlophisitsweng tlasa mookotaba “Re Lebisa Lefatsheng le Itekanetseng bakeng sa Meloko ya Hajwale le ya Kamoso”.

src: South Africa will work to ensure that policies are turned into concrete actions.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tla sebetsa ka matla ho netefatsa hore maano a fetolwa ho ba diketso tse phethahalang.

src: South Africa will work with all countries in Africa in advancing the country’s positions and that of the continent.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tla sebetsa le dinaha kaofela ka hara Aforika mabapi le ho ntshetsapele maemo a naha le a kontinente.

src: The High Level Segment of this conference will consider and provide political guidance on challenges to emerging issues in desertification, land degradation and drought.
tgt: Karolo ya Boemo bo Phahameng ba pitso ena bo tla sekaseka le ho fana ka tataiso ya sepolotiki mabapi le diphephetso tsa dintlha tse ntseng di runya mabapi le mahwatata, ho theoha ha maemo a mobu le komello.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to protect and take care of the environment in order to conserve it for future generations.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa kaofela ho tshireletsa le ho hlokomela tikoloho bakeng sa ho e baballa bakeng sa meloko ya kamoso.

src: Public transport operators.
tgt: Beng ba dipalangwang tsa setjhaba.

src: Cabinet condemns the acts of violence, torching of operators’ vehicles and acts of intimidation between the Meter Taxi Operators and the E-Hailing Partners that took place at Sandton, in Johannesburg.
tgt: Kabinete e tshwela ka mathe diketsahalo tsa dikgoka, ho tjheswa ha makoloi a beng ba thepa le diketso tsa ditshoso pakeng tsa Beng ba Ditekesi tsa Dimithara le Balekane ba E-Hailing tse etsahetseng Sandton, Johannesburg.

src: Cabinet calls on law-enforcement agencies to deal with perpetrators of violence and intimidation within the confines of our Constitution.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho makala a qobello ya molao ho sebetsana le baetsi ba dikgoka le ditshoso ka hara dipehelo tsa Molaotheo.

src: These developments detract from the country’s concerted efforts in creating a climate of free trade and fair competition.
tgt: Diketsahalo tsena di sutha mekutung ya naha ya ho bopa maemo a kgwebo e lokolohileng le tlhodisano e hlokang leeme.

src: Councillors.
tgt: Balekgotla.

src: Cabinet condemns the attacks and killings of councillors in some provinces and extends its deepest condolences to the families and friends of those murdered.
tgt: Kabinete e tshwela ka mathe ditlhaselo le dipolao tsa balekgotla ka hara diporofense tse ding le ho fetisetsa matshediso a yona ho malapa le metswalle ya ba bolauweng.

src: This goes against the ethos of the Constitution, and detracts from our developmental democracy and the right of people to elect their public representatives.
tgt: Sena se kgahlanong le dipehelo tsa boitshwaro tsa Molaotheo, le ho sutha demokerasing ya rona ya tswelopele le tokelo ya batho ya ho kgetha baemedi ba bona ba setjhaba.

src: Since the beginning of the year, there have been several deaths in KwaZulu-Natal and recently, deaths have also been reported in the Eastern Cape.
tgt: Esale ho tloha qalong ya selemo, ho bile le mafu a mmalwa ka hara KwaZulu-Natal, mme haufinyana tjena, ho tlalehilwe mafu ka hara Kapa Botjhabela.

src: This violence has taken the lives young activists, including the fearless former African National Congress Youth League Secretary-General Sindiso Magaqa, who still had much to contribute in building a prosperous South Africa.
tgt: Dikgoka tsena di nkile maphelo a balwanedi ba tokoloho ba batjha, ho kenyeletswa le Mongodi Kakaretso wa mehleng wa Liki ya Batjha ya ANC (ANCYL) Sindiso Magaqa, ya neng a sa ntsane a na le se sengata seo a ka se nyehelang mabapi le ho aha Aforika Borwa e tswetseng pele.

src: We call on political parties to promote tolerance amongst their members and call on communities to support the South African Police Service in their investigations.
tgt: Re ipiletsa ho mekga ya dipolotiki ho kgothaletsa mamellano hara ditho tsa yona le ho ipiletsa ho badudi ho tshehetsa ba Tshebeletso ya Sepolesa ya Aforika Borwa (SAPS) diphuputsong tsa bona.

src: Heritage Month.
tgt: Kgwedi ya Botjhaba.

src: Cabinet encourages all South Africans to continue to observe this year’s Heritage Month under the theme: “The Year of Oliver Reginald Tambo: Celebrating our Liberation Heritage”.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa maAforika Borwa kaofela ho tswela pele ho ananela Kgwedi ya Botjhaba ya selemong sena tlasa mookotaba: “Selemo sa Oliver Reginald Tambo: Re keteka Lefa la Tokoloho ya rona”.

src: This month coincides with the centenary birth of OR Tambo, an African Patriot, who showed an unwavering commitment to serve the people of South Africa, the continent and the world.
tgt: Kgwedi ena e tsamaelana le dilemo tse lekgolo tsa letsatsi la tswalo la OR Tambo, Morati wa naha ya habo ya Aforika, ya bontshitseng boitelo bo sa thekeseleng ba ho sebeletsa batho ba Aforika Borwa, kontinente le lefatshe.

src: We have also marked the 40th anniversary of the death of Steve Bantu Biko, who was brutally murdered by the apartheid regime.
tgt: Hape re tshwaile sehopotso sa bo-40 sa lefu la Steve Bantu Biko, ya ileng a bolawa ka sehloho ke mmuso wa kgethollo.

src: The Minister of Arts and Culture, Mr Nathi Mthethwa, has released a programme of celebration for this month.
tgt: Letona la Bonono le Botjhaba, Monghadi Nathi Mthethwa, o lokolotse lenaneo la mekete ya kgweding ena.

src: Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet was apprised on the 1st performance quarterly progress reports for 2017/18 on the implementation of priority outcomes for the period between April and June 2017.Government continues to make considerable progress in implementing the 14 priority outcomes, derived from the Medium Term Strategic Framework 2014-2019, which brings us closer to realising the NDP Vision 2030.
tgt: Kabinete e tsebisitswe ka ditlaleho tsa pele tsa tshebetso tsa kgatelopele ya kotara ka nngwe bakeng sa 2017/18 mabapi le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha diphetho tsa dintlha tse ka sehlohlolong bakeng sa nako e dipakeng tsa Mmesa le Phuptjane 2017.

src: Cabinet was also briefed on areas that experienced delays in the implementation and appraised on actions required to fast-track delivery.
tgt: Mmuso o tswela pele ho etsa kgatelopele e bonahalang mabapi le ho kenya tshebetsong diphetho tsa dintlha tse 14 tse ka sehlohlolong, tse itshetlehileng hodima Moralo wa Lewa wa Nako e Bohareng (MTSF) 2014-2019, o re atametsang tabeng ya ho fihlella Tjhebelopele ya 2030 ya NDKabinete hape e ile ya tsebiswa ka dibaka tse ileng tsa ba le ditiehiso mabapi le ho kenngwa tshebetsong le ho tsebiswa ka mehato e batlehang ho akofisa phano.

src: Cluster Ministerial media briefings will be held to brief on the outcomes of these reports during the week of 6 October until 15 October 2017.
tgt: Dikopano tsa boraditaba tsa Matona a Dikarolo ka ho fapana di tla tshwarwa ho tsebisa ka diphetho tsa ditlaleho tsena bekeng ya la 6 ho fihlela ka la 15 Mphalane 2017.

src: The schedule will be updated regularly and posted on WEBTOKECabinet has approved the proposal for South Africa to host the International Telecommunication Union Telecom World Exhibition in September 2018.
tgt: Sekejule se tla lokiswa kgafetsa le ho manehwa ho WEBTOKEKabinete e tjhaelletse monwana tshisinyo ya hore Aforika Borwa e tshware Dipontsho tsa Lefatshe tsa Kopano ya Telecom tsa Matjhaba tsa Meralo ya Motheo ya Dikgokahanyo tsa Mehala ka Loetse 2018.

src: This is an annual exhibition and forum for government and industry leaders to explore challenges, partnerships and solutions, and identify investment opportunities and best practices for socio-economic development through Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs).This will be the first time this event is held in Africa.
tgt: Tsena ke dipontsho tsa selemo ka seng le foramo bakeng sa mmuso le baetapele ba diindaseteri ho fuputsa diphephetso, dilekane le ditharollo, le ho hlwaya menyetla ya matsete le ditlwaelo tse ntle ka ho fetisisa bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya moruo wa kahisano ka Dithekenoloji tsa Tlhahisoleseding le Dikgokahanyo (di-ICT).Sena e tla be e le lekgetlo la pele ketsahalo ena e tshwarelwa Aforika.

src: During this event, the South African ICT industry will be afforded an opportunity to showcase their respective products.
tgt: Nakong ya ketsahalo ena, indaseteri ya ICT ya Aforika Borwa e tla thola monyetla wa ho pepesa dihlahiswa tsa yona ka ho latelana.

src: The country’s tourism sector will also benefit during this period.
tgt: Lekala la naha la bohahlaudi le lona le tla kgola molemo nakong ena.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: President Zuma will lead a South African delegation to the 72nd Regular Session of the UN General Assembly under the theme “Focusing on People: Striving for Peace and a Decent Life for All on a Sustainable Planet” in New York, United States of America.
tgt: Moporesidente Zuma o tla etella pele kemedi ya Aforika Borwa ho Tulo ya bo-72 e Tlwaelehileng ya Kopano Kakaretso ya UN tlasa mookotaba “Re Tsepamisa Maikutlo Bathong: Re Tsitlallela Kgotso le Bophelo bo Khabane bakeng sa Bohle Polaneteng ya Moshwelella” ho la New York, Amerika.

src: South Africa will continue to work on achieving reform at the UN as it participates in the 72th Session.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tla tswela pele ho sebeletsa ho fihlella diphetho ho UN ha e tla be e nka karolo Tulong ya bo-72.

src: President Zuma, as the Chairperson of the SADC, will convene an Extraordinary Double Troika Summit of Heads of State and Government on 15 September 2017 in Pretoria.
tgt: Moporesident Jacob Zuma jwaloka Modulasetulo wa SADC, o tla bitsa Seboka sa Double Troika sa Dihlooho tsa Dipuso le Mebuso ka la 15 Loetse 2017 Pretoria.

src: The Double Troika Summit is held as a result of the recent political and security developments in the Kingdom of Lesotho.
tgt: Seboka sa Double Troika se tla tshwarwa ka lebaka la diketsahalo tsa haufinyana tjena tsa dipolotiki le polokeho ka hara Borena ba Lesotho.3 Kemedi ya boemo bo phahameng ya Aforika Borwa e tla teka boiketo ba yona ba pele ba ho tshwara Mohope wa Lefatshe wa Rakbi wa 2023 London ka la 25 Loetse 2017.

src: South Africa has a strong proven record of hosting such events.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e na le rekoto e matla e nang le bopaki ya ho tshwara diketsahalo tse kang eno.

src: Cabinet wishes to reiterate its strong support of this Bid and calls upon South Africans to support this Bid that will contribute immensely to social cohesion and nation-building, and also serve as a catalyst for sport development.
tgt: Kabinete e lakatsa ho boeletsa tshehetso ya yona e matla ya Boiketo bona le ho ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ho tshehetsa Boiketo bona bo tla nyehela haholo mabapi le momahano ya setjhaba le kaho ya setjhaba le ho sebetsa hape jwaloka sethusi bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya dipapadi.

src: Messages.
tgt: Melaetsa.

src: Cabinet wishes the citizens of Germany every success in preparation for Federal elections on 24 September 2017 to elect members of the 19th Bundestag, which in turn will elect a Chancellor and form a new government.
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa baahi ba Jeremane katleho yohle ha ba itokisetsa dikgetho tsa Bofederale ka la 24 Loetse 2017 ho kgetha ditho tsa Bundestag ya bo-19, eo ka nqa e nngwe e tla kgetha Motjhanselara le ho bopa mmuso o motjha.

src: Germany is a prominent investor in South Africa, which looks forward to continued relations, cooperation and partnership.
tgt: Jeremane ke motsetedi e moholo ka hara Aforika Borwa, ya ikemiseditseng dikamano tse tswelang pele, tshebedisano le bolekane.

src: Cabinet extends its sympathies to the Caribean as wells as parts of Cuba and the Unites Sates following the devastation caused by Hurricane Irma.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisetsa matshediso a yona ho Caribean hammoho le dikarolo tsa Cuba le Amerika ho latela tshenyo e bakuweng ke Sefefo sa Irma.

src: Heartfelt condolences are extended to the loved ones of those who lost their lives and their belongings in this disaster.
tgt: Re fetisetsa matshediso a tswang botebong ba dipelo ho baratuwa ba ba lahlehetsweng ke maphelo le thepa ya bona koduweng ena.

src: Cabinet joins the nation in congratulating Kevin Anderson on making the finals of the US Open.
tgt: Kabinete e imatahanya le setjhaba mabapi le ho thoholetsa Kevin Anderson mabapi le ho fihlella makgaolakgang a US Open.

src: He is the first South African player to make the final of a major tennis championship since 1994.
tgt: Ke sebapadi sa pele sa moAforika Borwa ho fihlella makgaolakgang a bompodi bo boholo ba thenese esale ho tloha ka selemo sa 1994.

src: We are confident that he will continue building on his glittering achievement and inspiring other young and talented South Africans.
tgt: Re na le tshepo ya hore o tla tswela pele ho ahella hodima phihlello ya hae e kganyang le ho kgothatsa batjha ba bang ba nang le talente ba MaAforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 27 September 2017, at the Union Buildings, Pretoria.
tgt: Kabinete e kopane ka Laboraro, 27 Loetse 2017, Union Buildings, Pretoria.

src: Issues in the environmentUnited Nations General Assembly (UNGA)Cabinet welcomed President Jacob Zuma’s address to the 72nd Regular Session of the UNGA in New York, USA on 12 September 2017, under the theme “Focusing on People: Striving for Peace and a Decent Life for All on a Sustainable Planet”.Deliberations focused, amongst others, on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) climate change peace and security issues and UN reforms, especially UN Security Council reform.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse puo ya Moporesidente Jacob Zuma ho Tulo e Tlwaelehileng ya bo-72 ya UNGA New York, Amerika ka la 12 Loetse 2017, tlasa mookotaba “Re Tsepamisa Maikutlo Bathong: Re tsitlallela Kgotso le Bophelo bo Kgabane bakeng sa Bohle Polaneteng ya Moshwelella”.

src: President Zuma also signed the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, which reflects South Africa’s continued commitment towards the achievement of a world free from the threat posed by nuclear weapons and ensuring that nuclear technology is used for peaceful purposes only.
tgt: Dipuisano di ne di tsepamisitse maikutlo hodima, hara tse ding, Merero ya Ntshetsopele ya Moshwelella (di-SDG) ho fetofetoha ha tlelaemete le ditaba tsa kgotso le tshireletso le diphethoho tsa UN, ka ho qolleha diphethoho tsa Lekgotla la Tshireletso la UMoporesidente Zuma hape o saenne Tumellano e mabapi le Thibelo ya Dibetsa tsa Nutleleya, e bontshang boitlamo bo tswellang ba Aforika Borwa mabapi le ho fihlella lefatshe le hlokang tshoso e bakwang ke dibetsa tsa nyutleleya le ho netefatsa hore thekenoloji ya nutleleya e sebedisetswa merero ya kgotso feela.

src: President Zuma hosted a centenary celebratory dinner in honour of the late former President of the African National Congress, Mr Oliver Reginald Tambo.
tgt: Mopresidente Zuma o ne a hlophisitse dijo tsa mantsiboya tsa ho keteka dilemo tse lekgolo ho hlompha mofu Moporesidente wa mehleng wa African National Congress (ANC), Monghadi Oliver Reginald Tambo.

src: Heritage MonthCabinet thanks all South Africans for celebrating Heritage Month in September and reiterates President Zuma’s Heritage Day message for all in the country to aspire for greater unity in WEBTOKEN the country concludes Heritage Month under the theme “The Year of Oliver Reginald Tambo: Celebrating our Liberation Heritage”, South Africans are encouraged to build on the values espoused in the Constitution and strengthen efforts to build a nation free from poverty, hunger, homelessness and WEBTOKEN fostering a spirit of heritage, Cabinet welcomes the agreement signed between South Africa and Tanzania, which is aimed at preserving the history of the liberation struggle.
tgt: Kabinete e leboha maAforika Borwa kaofela bakeng sa ho keteka Kgwedi ya Bojalefa ka Loetse le ho boeletsa molaetsa wa Moporesidente Zuma wa Letsatsi la Bojalefa hore bohle ba ka hara naha ba hahamalle kopano e matla le ka hara diphapang.

src: It is a celebration of the spirit of solidarity and cooperation amongst Africa’s liberation movements and will see the construction of a museum, library and WEBTOKEN Tourism DaySouth Africa, under the leadership of the Minister of Tourism, Ms Tokozile Xasa, participated in World Tourism Day (27 September 2017) and the Tourism Month, under the theme “Sustainable Tourism – A Tool for Development”.
tgt: Jwaloka ha naha e phethela Kgwedi ya Bojalefa tlasa mookotaba “Selemo sa Oliver Reginald Tambo: ho keteka tokoloho ya letlotlo la bojalefa ba rona”, maAforika Borwa a kgothaletswa ho ahella hodima dipehelo tsa bophelo tse ka hara Molaotheo le ho matlafatsa mekutu ya ho aha setjhaba se hlokang bofuma, tlala, ho hloka bodulo le ho se lekalekane.

src: This provides a platform to support changes in policy, business practices and tourism consumer behaviour, towards a more sustainable tourism sector, which can contribute aggressively towards the attainment of the SDGs.
