src: Cabinet joins President Cyril Ramaphosa in his call on South Africans to reaffirm a shared commitment to serve people as we continue to celebrate the centenary of the birth of former President Nelson Mandela.
tgt: Kabinete e kgema mmoho le Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa kgoeletsong ya hae ho maAforika Borwa, ya ho tiisa botjha boikitlaetso bo abelanwang ba ho sebeletsa setjhaba, jwalokaha re tswelapele ho keteka dilemo tse lekgolo tsa tswalo ya Moporesidente wa mehleng Nelson Mandela.

src: Madiba is the first President of a Democratic South Africa and would have turned 100 years of age on 18 July 2018.
tgt: Madiba ke Moporesidente wa pele wa Aforika Borwa ya Demokrasi mme o ne a tla qeta le dilemo tse 100 ka la 18 Phupu 2018.

src: Madiba is a global icon who is revered worldwide as a Champion of Human Rights, non-racism and non-sexism.
tgt: Madiba ke thatohatsi ya lefatshe lohle e tlotlehang lefatshe ka bophara e le Mampodi wa Ditokelo tsa Botho, ho se kgetholle ka morabe le ka bong.

src: He played a critical role in unifying South Africans, and inspiring democratic unity across Africa and the globe.
tgt: O bile le seabo sa bohlokwa ho kopanyeng maAforika Borwa, esita le ho kgothaletsa kopano ya demokrasi Aforika ka bophara le lefatshe ka bophara.

src: The first celebration of Nelson Mandela’s centenary took place during the African Union Summit in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia in January 2018.
tgt: Moketjana wa pele wa dilemo tse lekgolo tsa Nelson Mandela o bile nakong ya Seboka sa Kopano ya Aforika Addis Ababa, Ethiopia ka Pherekgong ya 2018.

src: A number of events will be held throughout the country this year to reflect on the life of Tata Madiba.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse ngatanyana di tla tshwarwa naha ka bophara monongwaha, ho hetla morao bophelong ba Tata Madiba.

src: Cabinet calls upon all South Africans to join in the centenary celebrations in their workplaces, schools, churches and civic organisations.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa ohle hore a ikamahanye le meketjana ya dilemo tse lekgolo a le mesebetsing, dikolong, dikerekeng le mekgatlong ya setjhaba.

src: It calls on each one of us this year to emulate the values of Nelson Mandela by working in our respective ways to build a united, non-racist, non-sexist and prosperous country.
tgt: E etsa kgoeletso ho e mong le e mong wa rona hore re hate menyabuketsong ya Nelson Mandela ka ho sebetsa ka mekgwa ya rona e fapaneng ho aha naha e kopaneng, e se nang kgethollo ya morabe, le ya bong e bile e le e atlehileng.

src: The country also celebrates the centenary of one of the great daughters of the African soil Mama Albertina Sisulu, who dedicated her life to fight for the emancipation of women and the liberation of South Africa.
tgt: Naha ena e boela e keteka dilemo tse lekgolo tsa e mong wa baradi ba kgabane ba Aforika, Mama Albertina Sisulu, ya ileng a nyehela bophelo ba hae a lwanela tokoloho ya basadi le ya Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet will in the next meeting also outline a programme for the celebration of the Centenary of Mama Albertina Sisulu.
tgt: Kopanong ya yona e latelang, Kabinete e tla rala lenaneo la ho keteka Dilemo tse Lekgolo tsa Mama Albertina Sisulu.

src: Drought.
tgt: Komello.

src: Cabinet appreciates the relentless efforts made by the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Drought together with stakeholders in all spheres of government and society in dealing with the persistent drought conditions that have hit several parts of the country.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela matsapa a matla a entsweng ke Komiti ya Matona a Kopaneng ka komello, hammoho le ba amehang makaleng ohle a mmuso le kahisanong ho sebetsaneng le maemo a ntseng a ja setsi a komello a thefutseng dikarolo tse ngatanyana tsa naha.

src: Apart from the fact that South Africa is a water-scarce country, the effects of global warming continue to affect the rain patterns, thus causing our dam levels to remain low.
tgt: Ntle le taba ya hore Aforika Borwa ke naha e nang le leqeme la metsi, ditlamorao tsa phuthumalo ya lefatshe lohle di tswelapele ho ama mokgwa oo pula e nang ka wona, mme seo se etsa hore mothamo wa matamo a rona o dule o le tlase.

src: The Inter-Ministerial Task Team on Drought continues to facilitate work between national government, provinces and municipalities in all drought-affected areas.
tgt: Sehlopha sa Tshebetso sa Matona a Kopaneng se sebetsanang le Komello se tswelapele ho hlophisa mosebetsi dipakeng tsa mmuso wa naha, wa diprofense le wa bomasepala dibakeng tsohle tse thefutsweng ke komello.

src: This includes implementing short, medium and long-term measures to address and mitigate the potential impact of this drought.
tgt: Sena se akga ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha dikgato tsa nako e kgutshwane, e mahareng esita le e telele ho rarolla le ho nolofatsa ditlamorao tse ka etsahalang tsa komello ena.

src: Government has made funds available to provide short-term assistance to affected provinces.
tgt: Mmuso o bokelletse tjhelete ya ho fana ka thuso ya nako e kgutshwane diprofenseng tse amehileng.

src: It has provided a relief grant worth R473 million and an additional R6 billion in the 2018/19 financial year to augment water infrastructure in the Western Cape‚ Eastern Cape and Northern Cape.
tgt: O fane ka dithuso tsa ditjhelete tsa kinolo maqakabetsing tse kaalo ka R473 milione esita le R6 bilione e tla eketswa selemong sa ditjhelete sa 2018/19 ho tlatseletsa meralong ya motheo ya metsi Kapa Bophirimela, Kapa Botjhabela le Kapa Leboya.

src: Cabinet calls on all to continue to work with government in conserving water by using it responsibly and sparingly.
tgt: Mmuso o etsa kgoeletso ho bohle ho tswelapele ho sebetsa le mmuso ho bolokeng metsi, ka ho a sebedisa ka boikarabelo le ka paballo.

src: Cabinet remains committed to making South Africa a country of choice for visitors and potential investors alike.
tgt: Kabinete e dula e ntse e ikitlaelleditse ho etsa Aforika Borwa hore e be naha e tla kgethwa ke baeti le ke botsetedi ka ho tshwanang.

src: Police killings.
tgt: Dipolao tsa Mapolesa.

src: Cabinet expresses condolences to the families and friends of the five police officers and a former soldier who were recently brutally murdered in an attack on the Ngcobo Police Station in the Eastern Cape.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisa matshediso a yona ho ba malapa le metswalle ya bahlanka ba bahlano ba sepolesa mmoho le lesole la mehleng, ba sa tswa fenethwa ka sehloho tlhaselong ya Motebo wa Sepolesa wa Ngcobo Kapa Botjhabela.

src: Cabinet strongly condemns any senseless killing of our servicemen and women.
tgt: Kabinete e tshwela ka mathe polao efe kapa efe ya banna le basadi ba habo rona ba mapolesa.

src: The loss of one police officer, soldier or any other person who serves to protect society and our people is unacceptable.
tgt: Ho shwa ha mohlanka a le mong wa sepolesa, lesole kapa motho e mong ofe kapa ofe ya sebetsang mosebetsi wa ho tshireletsa kahisano le batho ba habo rona, ha e a amoheleha.

src: Cabinet has committed, through the Minister of Police, to do whatever possible to capacitate our police stations to prevent such attacks in the future.
tgt: Kabinete e ikitlaeditse, ka Letona la Sepolesa, ho etsa kahohlehohle kamoo e ka kgonang kateng ho matlafatsa metebo ya habo rona ya sepolesa, e le ho thibela ditlhaselo tse jwalo kamoso.

src: Cabinet further appeals to parents and society at large to ensure children are kept safe at all times and to partner with law-enforcement agencies to protect the rights of our children.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e ipiletsa ho batswadi le setjhaba ka kakaretso ho netefatsa hore bana ba bolokehile ka nako tsohle, esita le ho sebedisana le makala a kenyang molao tshebetsong, ho tshireletsa ditokelo tsa bana ba rona.

src: Any form of abuse against a child must be exposed and reported immediately.
tgt: Mokgwa ofe kapa ofe wa tlhekefetso kgahlanong le ngwana, o tlameha ho pepeswa o be o tlalehwe hanghang.

src: By working together, we can keep our communities safe and ensure that criminal elements have no place to hide.
tgt: Ha re sebetsa mmoho, re ka boloka dibaka tsa rona di bolokehile ra ba ra netefatsa hore baetsi ba ditlolo tsa molao ha ba fumane sekoti sa ho ipata.

src: Cabinet decisions Cabinet approved the Draft Revised White Paper on National Transport Policy to be published for public comments.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Moralo wa Leano le Lekotsweng Botjha la Pampiri e Tshweu ho tsa Dipalangwang tsa Naha le tla phatlalatswa bakeng sa ditshwaelo tsa setjhaba.

src: The policy aims to provide a transport system that is integrated with other related sector plans so as to reduce both the cost of commuting and doing business.
tgt: Leano le habile ho fana ka mokgwatsamaiso wa dipalangwang o tlamahanngwang le merero e meng e amanang le lekala ho etsetsa hore ho fokotswe ditjeo tsa ho eta le tsa ho etsa kgwebo.

src: It also aligns the country’s transportation plans to the global transportation trends.
tgt: Le boela le nyalanya merero ya dipalangwang ya naha ena le ditlwaelo tsa dipalangwang tsa lefatshe lohle.

src: Cabinet approved the Green Paper on Roads Policy for South Africa to be published for public comments.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Pampiri e Tala Leanong la tsa Mebila la Aforika Borwa, e tla phatlalatswa bakeng sa ditshwaelo tsa setjhaba.

src: The policy provides the overarching framework that ensures South Africa’s roads are better managed, safer and include all modes of transport to deliver a sustainable approach to roads management.
tgt: Leano le fana ka moralo o ka sehloohong o netefatsang hore mebila ya Aforika Borwa e laoleha betetshana, e batla e bolokehile mme e kenyeletsa mefuta yohle ya dipalangwang hore e fane ka mokgwa o tsitsitseng wa bolaodi ba mebila.

src: It guides the road regulations, infrastructure, safety, road funding and non- motorised transport.
tgt: Le tataisa melawana ya tsela, meralo ya motheo, polokeho, ditjhelete tsa mebila le dipalangwang tseo e seng makoloi.

src: Cabinet was briefed on the findings of the 2015/16 National Survey of Research and Experimental Development (R&D Survey).R&D is an integral part of the country’s socio-economic development.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka diphumano tsa Tshekatsheko ya Naha ya Tswelopele ya Diphuputso le Boithutwane (R&D Survey).R&D ke karolo ya bohlokwa ya tswelopele ya moruo wa kahisano naheng ena.

src: This has been collective efforts of government, industry and research institutions.
tgt: Ana e bile matsapa a kopanetsweng a mmuso, diindasteri le ditheo tsa diphuputso.

src: The report is available on the Department of Science and Technology (DST) website: WEBTOKECabinet approved the designs of the 2018 commemorative collector’s coin series, which will be produced by the South African Mint Company.
tgt: Tlaleho e a fumaneha websaeteng ya Lefapha la Saense le Theknolji (DST) ya: WEBTOKEKabinete e ananetse metako e fapaneng ya lethathama la 2018 la tjhelete ya sehopotso e lewana, le tla hlahiswa ke khamphane ya Minte ya Aforika Borwa.

src: The 2018 designs collection will be celebrating the Nelson Mandela Centenary.
tgt: Pokello ya 2018 ya metako e fapaneng e tla keteka Dilemo tse Lekgolo tsa Nelson Mandela.

src: These collections were preceded by the 2017 commemorative coins that celebrated South Africa under the theme of Freedom, Democracy and Cultures.
tgt: Dipokello tsena di ne di leleketswe ke tjhelete e lewana ya sehopotso ya 2017 e neng e keteka Aforika Borwa tlasa mokotaba wa Tokoloho, Demokrasi le Botjhaba.

src: Bills.
tgt: Dibili.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Customary Initiation Bill of 2018 to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha Bili ya Lebollo la Setho ya 2018 Palamenteng.

src: The Bill seeks to protect, promote and regulate the governance aspect of the practice of customary WEBTOKEN provides national norms and standards aimed at the protection of life and the prevention of injuries and all forms of abuse experienced by initiates.
tgt: Bili e habile ho tshireletsa, ho kgothaletsa le ho laola karolo ya tsamaiso ya lebollo la setho.

src: Cabinet approved for the submission of the National Qualifications Framework Amendment Bill of 2016 to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho tekwa ha Bili ya 2016 ya Sehlomathiso sa Moralo wa Naha wa Mangolo a Thuto Palamenteng.

src: The Bill, which amends the National Qualifications Framework Act, 2008 (Act 67 of 2008), strengthens the Act by improving measures to deal with issues of misrepresentation, imposes consequences on persons who misrepresent their qualifications or organisations that issue invalid WEBTOKEN also proposes regulations to ensure that fraudulent qualifications are referred to the relevant professional bodies (database of individuals who misrepresented their qualifications).
tgt: Bili ena, e hlomathisang Molao wa Moralo wa Naha wa Mangolo a Thuto, 2008 (Molao wa 67 wa 2008), e matlafatsa Molao ka ho ntlafatsa dikgato tsa ho sebetsana le maemo a ho se bue nnete, e qobella hore ho be teng ditlamorao bathong ba sa bueng nnete ka mangolo a bona a thuto kapa mekgatlo e ntshang mangolo a thuto a seng molaong.

src: It also addresses the accreditation of foreign qualifications.
tgt: E boela e sisinya hore ho be teng melawana ya ho netefatsa hore mangolo a thuto a boqhekanyetsi a fetisetswa mekgatlong ya seporofeshenale e tshwanelehileng (pokello ya lenane la batho ba sa bueng nnete ka mangolo a bona a thuto).

src: Cabinet approved the Railway Safety Bill of 2017 to be published for public comments.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Bili ya 2017 ya Polokeho Ditereneng, e tla phatlalatswa bakeng sa ditshwaelo tsa setjhaba.

src: The Bill seeks to improve railway safety and create a governance structure to oversee the work of the Rail Safety Regulator of South Africa.
tgt: Bili e habile ho ntlafatsa polokeho ya ditereneng esita le ho thea lekgotla la tsamaiso le lekolang mosebetsi wa Bolaodi ba Polokeho Ditereneng ba Aforika Borwa.

src: It is also aligned to the National Rail Policy regarding the strengthening of safety monitoring, and the promotion and enforcement of safety in our railways.
tgt: E boetse e amahanngwa le Leano la Naha la Diterene mabapi le ho matlafatsa bodisa ba polokeho, esita le ho kgothaletsa le ho qobella boteng ba polokeho ditereneng tsa rona.

src: Cabinet approved for the Draft Economic Regulation of Transport Bill of 2017 to be published for public comments and consultation.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Moralo wa Bili ya 2017 ya Taolo ya Ditshenyehelo Ditereneng, e tla phatlalatswa bakeng sa ditshwaelo tsa setjhaba le dipuisano.

src: The Bill addresses the regulatory and capacity gaps in respect of provision of a cost-effective and efficient transport system.
tgt: Bili e rarolla taba ya dikgaello tsa taolo le bokgoni mabapi le phano ya mekgwatsamaiso ya dipalangwang e sa senyeng tjhelete ebile e le e sebetsang ka bokgabane.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: South Africa will be hosting the Southern African Development Community Ministers of Labour, Employment and Social Security, as Chair, from 1 to 2 March 2018 at the Cape Town International Convention Centre.
tgt: Aforika Borwa, e le Modulasetulo, e tla tshwara Seboka sa Ntshetsopele ya Dinaha tse ka Borwa ba Aforika (SADC) sa Matona a tsa Bosebetsi, Kgiro le Tshireletso ya Setjhaba, ho tloha ka la 1 ho isa ho la 2 Hlakubele 2018 Setsing sa Diboka tsa Matjhaba sa Motse Kapa (CTICC).

src: The theme of the conference is: “Horizon decent work: Advancing connectivity, coherence and inclusivity”.
tgt: Mookotaba wa seboka o re: “Kgonahalo ya mosebetsi o motle: Ho ntshetsapele bohokahanyi, momahano le ho kenyeletsa ba bangata”.

src: Participants will include social partners – organised business, labour and community.
tgt: Ba tla nka seabo ba tla akga balekane ba kahisanong – dikgwebo tse kgolo, tsa bosebetsi hammoho le setjhaba.

src: President Ramaphosa in his capacity as the Chair of SADC will undertake consultative visits to Angola, Botswana and Namibia from 2 to 3 March 2018.
tgt: Boemong ba hae e le Modulasetulo wa SADC, Moporesidente Ramaphosa o tla kena maetong a dipontshano ho ya Angola, Botswana le Namibia ho tloha ka la 2 ho isa ho la 3 Hlakubele 2018.

src: He will be accompanied by the Minister of International Relations and Cooperation Lindiwe Sisulu and Minister of Defence and Military Veterans Nosiviwe Maphisa Nqakula.
tgt: O tla felehetswa ke Letona la Dikamano le Tshebedisano ya Matjhaba, Lindiwe Sisulu le Letona la Lebotho la Tshireletso le Mekaubere ya Sesole, Nosiviwe Maphisa Nqakula.

src: South Africa will co-host the 17th World Conference on Tobacco or Health (WCTOH) from 7 to 9 March 2018 in Cape Town under the theme: “Uniting the World for a Tobacco-free Generation”.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e tla tshwara Seboka sa Lefatshe sa bo-17 se mabapi le Kwae kapa Bophelo bo Botle (WCTOH) ho tloha ka la 7 ho isa ho la 9 Hlakubele 2018 Motse Kapa, katlasa mookotaba o reng: “Ho kopanya lefatshe bakeng sa Moloko o Lokolohileng ditlamong tsa Kwae”.

src: This is the first hosting in Africa.
tgt: Sena ke seboka sa pele sa ho tshwarelwa Aforika.

src: The WTCOH calls for committed action and provides a platform for governments, civil-society organisations, United Nations agencies, international organisations, health workers and other stakeholders to discuss shared knowledge and experiences, particularly regarding to youth and women who are exposed to tobacco WEBTOKEN the conference contributes towards addressing the National Development Plan’s goals by creating awareness and education on the harmful effects of tobacco use, and the need to intensify tobacco control measures.
tgt: WCTOH e etsa kgoeletso ya hore ho be teng kgato ya boitlamo ebile e fana ka lepatlelo la mebuso, mekgatlo ya setjhaba, makgotla a Matjhaba a Kopaneng, mekgatlo ya matjhaba, basebeletsi ba bophelo bo botle le ba bang ba amehang ho okgelana tsebo le ho thakelana malebela, haholoholo mabapi le batjha le basadi ba pepesehileng tshebedisong ya kwae.

src: On the 10 and 11 March the IEC will open the Voting Registration Centres for people to come and register and check their registration details.
tgt: Ho tshwara seboka ho a thusa mabapi le ho tla le ditharollo tsa sepheo sa Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha ka ho etsa tlhokomediso le thuto ka ditlamorao tse kotsi tsa tshebediso ya kwae, le tlhokeho ya ho matlafatsa dikgato tsa taolo ya kwae.

src: Cabinet urges all eligible voters to visit their voting stations to update the voters’ roll in preparation for the 2019 general elections.
tgt: Kabinete e kopa bakgethi bohle ba tshwanelehileng ho ya diteisheneng tsa bona tsa ho voutela, ho tsoseletsa lenane la bakgethi e le ho hlophisetsa dikgetho tse akaretsang tsa 2019.

src: Cabinet particularly calls on first-time voters to ensure they participate in their constitutional democratic right to vote by going to register to vote.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso, haholoholo ho ba tla be ba vouta lekgetlo la pele, ho netefatsa hore ba ba le seabo tokelong ya bona ya demokrasi ya molaotheo ya ho vouta, ka ho ya ba ilo ingodisetsa ho vouta.

src: This registration weekend is a milestone towards the culmination of a two-year project to obtain the residential addresses of all registered voters.
tgt: Mafelo ana a beke a boingodiso, ke katleho e kgolo mabapi le pheletso ya projeke ya dilemo tse pedi ya ho fumana diaterese tsa bodulo tsa bakgethi bohle ba ingodisitseng.

src: The voting stations will be open between 08:00 and 17:00 to assist new voters to register to vote, and allow registered voters who have relocated to reregister in their correct voting district and update their address details on the voters’ roll.
tgt: Diteishene tsa ho voutela di tla bulwa dipakeng tsa 08:00 hoseng le 17:00 mantsiboya ho thusa bakgethi ba qalang hore ba ingodisetse ho vouta, le ho dumella bakgethi ba seng ba ingodisitse ba falletseng dibakeng tse ding hore ba ingodise botjha diterekeng tsa bona tse nepahetseng tsa ho voutela, ba be ba lokise dintlha tsa diaterese tsa bona lenaneng la bakgethi.

src: Messages.
tgt: Melaetsa.

src: Cabinet commends all teachers who were honoured at the 18th National Teaching Awards which took place in Johannesburg on Saturday, 17 February 2018.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa matitjhere ohle a ileng a tlotlwa moketjaneng wa Dikgau tsa bo18 tsa Naha tsa Botitjhere, o neng o le Johannesburg ka Moqebelo wa la 17 Hlakola 2018.

src: The awards recognised outstanding teaching and leadership in several categories, including the Nelson Mandela Lifetime Achievement Award and Profssor Kader Asmal Award.
tgt: Dikgau di ne di ananela botitjhere le boetapele bo tswileng matsoho mekgahlelong e fapaneng, ho akga le Kgau ya Katleho ya Bophelo Bohle ya Nelson Mandela, le Kgau ya Moprofesara Kader Asmal.

src: Cabinet conveys its condolences to Deputy Minister Obed Bapela on the loss of his wife Constance Bapela, who served the country as a councillor at the time of her passing.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisa matshediso a yona ho Motlatsi wa Letona Obed Bapela ka ho hlokahallwa ke mofumahadi wa hae Constance Bapela, ya neng a sebeletsa naha e le molekgotla nakong ya ho hlokahala ha hae.

src: Cabinet joins President Ramaphosa in conveying condolences to the family, friends and associates of the political economist and author, ProfJohannes “Sampie” Terreblanche, who passed on at the age of Cabinet congratulates Minister Naledi Pandor on her recognition by Leiden University in the Netherlands as an Oort Honorary Visiting Profssor of Astronomy and Development.
tgt: Kabinete e ikamahanya le Moporesidente Ramaphosa ho fetisetseng matshediso ho ba lelapa, metswalle le bomphato ba moikonomi wa sepolotiki ebile e le mongodi, Moprofesara Johannes “Sampie” Terreblanche, ya hlokahetseng a na le dilemo tse Kabinete e thoholetsa Letona Naledi Pandor ho ananelweng ha hae ke Yunivesithi ya Leiden e Netherlands e le Moeti ya Tlotlwang wa Oort wa Moporofesara wa Astronomi le Ntshetsopele.

src: This is in recognition of the Minister’s extraordinary accomplishment in harnessing science, particularly astronomy, as a tool for global development and societal benefit.
tgt: Sena se etswa e le kananelo ya katleho e tswileng matsoho eo Letona le e entseng ka ho tlamahanya saense, haholoholo astronomi, e le sesebediswa bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya lefatshe lohle ebile e le molemong wa setjhaba.

src: AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: DithonyoDithonyo tsohle di emetse netefaletso ya mangolo a thuto esita le topollo e tshwanelehileng.

src: Ms Lerato Matabogeas Deputy Director-General (DDG): Tradeand Investment South Africa, Department of Trade and Industry (the dti).
tgt: Lerato Mataboge e le Motlatsi wa Molaodi e Moholo (DDG): Kgwebisano le Botsetedi Aforika Borwa, Lefapha la Kgwebisano le Diindasteri (dti).

src: Ms Shandokane Evelyn Masotjaas DDG: Consumer and Corporate Regulation, the dti.
tgt: Shandokane Evelyn Masotja e le DDG: Taolo ya tsa Boreki le Dikgwebo tse Kgolo, dti.

src: Ms Vuyelwa Vumendlini as DDG: International and Regional Economic Policy, National Treasury.
tgt: Vuyelwa Vumendlini e le DDG: Leano la Moruo la Matjhaba le Lebatowa, Lefapha la Matlotlo a Setjhaba.

src: Mr Joseph Tebogo Leshope as Chief Operations Officer of SENTECMs Vuyo Zitumane as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Amatola Water.
tgt: Joseph Tebogo Leshope e le Mohlanka e Moholo wa tsa Tshebetso wa SENTECMof.

src: Adv Seeng Catherine Ntsaba-Letele as Chief Ombud of the Community Schemes Ombud Service.
tgt: Vuyo Zitumane e le Mohlanka e Moholo wa Phethahatso (CEO) wa Amatola Water.

src: Mr Edward Mamadise as CEO of the National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications.
tgt: Moadvokheiti Seeng Catherine Ntsaba-Letele e le Molekodi e Moholo wa Tshebeletso ya Molekodi ya Dikema tsa Setjhaba.

src: Dr Sagren Moodley as the representative from the DST on the South African Council for Natural Scientific Profssions.
tgt: Edward Mamadise e le CEO ya Bolaodi ba Naha ba Ditotobatsuwa tse Tlamang.

src: Reappointments to the Patent Examination Board:a. Ms Shanaaz Tiry Mahomedb.
tgt: Ngaka Sagren Moodley e le moemedi wa DST Lekgotleng la Diporofeshene tsa Saense ya Tlhaho la Aforika Borwa.

src: Ms Sandra Cleilandc.
tgt: Dithonyo botjha ho Boto e Pepeneneng ya Ditlhahlobo:a. Mof.

src: ProfChristiena Maria van der Bank andd.
tgt: Shanaaz Tiry Mahomedb.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 14 March 2018, at Tuynhuys, Cape TownIssues in the environment.
tgt: Pehelo ka Kopano ya Kabinete ya la 14 Hlakubele 2018Kabinete e kopane ka Laboraro, 14 Hlakubele 2018, Tuynhuys, Motse KapaDintlha tsa Maemo a jwale.

src: Economic growth.
tgt: Kgolo ya moruo.

src: Cabinet welcomes the 1.3% growth in the economy in 2017.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela kgolo ya moruo ya 1.3% ka 2017.

src: This is an increase from 0.3% in 2016.
tgt: Sena ke keketseho ya ho tloha ho 0.3% ka 2016.

src: The performance of the economy under difficult conditions bodes well for the country’s future economic prospects.
tgt: Tshebetso ya moruo tlasa maemo a thata e lepa tse ntle bakeng sa menyetla ya kamoso ya moruo wa naha.

src: The growth figures signal that the economy is on an upward trajectory, with National Treasury expecting the economy to expand by 1.5% this year and accelerate to 2.1% in 2020.
tgt: Manane a kgolo ke letshwao la hore moruo o mathuleng a ho phahama, moo Lefapha la Matlotlo a Naha le lebeletseng hore moruo o hole ka 1.5% selemong sena o be o akofele ho 2.1% ka 2020.

src: Cabinet calls on all sectors of society to build on the positive momentum of 2017, and work with government to translate its plans into concrete action to sustain economic growth and create jobs.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho makala ohle a setjhaba ho ahella hodima mokoka o motle wa 2017, a be a sebetse le mmuso ho lokisa meralo ya ona hore e be kgato e tiileng ya ho tsitlallela kgolo ya moruo le ho thea mesebetsi.

src: Land reform Cabinet welcomes the adopted motion to amend the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996 so as to allow for the expropriation of land without compensation.
tgt: Tlhabollo ya Mobu Kabinete e amohela tshisinyo e ananetsweng ya ho hlomathisa Molaotheo wa Riphaboliki ya Aforika Borwa wa 1996 bakeng sa ho dumella kamoho ya mobu ntle le ditlhapiso.

src: Government has since 1994 worked hard to reverse the legacy of land dispossession under colonialism and apartheid.
tgt: Haesale ho tloha ka 1994 mmuso o sebetsa ka matla ho sotholla masalla a ho nkelwa naha tlasa bokoloniale le mmuso wa kgethollo.

src: Working within the law, government has done much to ensure the continued productivity of the land, while speeding up the process of redress for those affected by land dispossessions.
tgt: Mmuso, o sebetsa o itshetlehile ka molao, o se o entse boholo ho netefatsa tlhahiso e tswelang pele ya ditswamobung, ha ka nqa e nngwe o akofisa motjha wa ho lokisa botjha bakeng sa ba anngweng ke ho nkelwa mobu.

src: The matter has been referred to the Constitutional Review Committee, which must report back to Parliament by 30 August 2018.
tgt: Taba ena e fetiseditswe ho Komiti ya Tjhebobotjha ya Molaotheo, e tlamehang ho tlalehela Palamente ka la 30 Phato 2018.

src: The recommendations to the National Assembly will be informed by a series of public hearings followed by committee meetings.
tgt: Dikgothaletso tse iswang ho Seboka sa Naha di tlasusumetswa ke letoto la dipitso tsa nonyo ya maikutlo a setjhaba tse tla latelwa ke dikopano tsa komiti.

src: Cabinet calls on all stakeholders to make their input during this process of engagement, which will guide the solutions to take our country forward.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho bohle ba amehang hore ba tshwaele nakong ya mothati ona wa dipuisano, o tla tataisa ho utollweng ha ditharollo tse tla ntshetsa naha ya habo rona pele.

src: As a caring and people-centred government, all stakeholders will be engaged during this process.
tgt: Re lemmuso o tsotellang o bile o sebetsa le batho, bohle ba amehang ba tla kenyeletswa nakong ya mothati ona.

src: Cabinet further urges communities to desist from illegal land invasions.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e kopa setjhaba ho lesa ho inkela mobu ho seng molaong.

src: We are a law-abiding and peace-loving country with adequate mechanisms of dealing with issues, including the land issue.
tgt: Re naha e ikokobeletsang molao ebile e rata kgotso, ka mekgwa e amohelehileng ya ho rarolla diqaka, ho akga le qaka ya mobu.

src: South Africa remains open for business, and investments in agriculture and farming are welcomed.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e dula e butse menyetla bakeng sa kgwebo, mme botsetedi ho tsa temo le bohwai bo amohetswe.

src: It is in South Africa's interests to have commercial farmers and this process can ensure we have even greater numbers of successful commercial farmers.
tgt: Ho molemong wa Aforika Borwa hore e be le dihwai tsa kgwebo mme mothati ona o ka netefatsa hore re bile re na le manane a hodimo a dihwai tsa kgwebo tse atlehileng.

src: Nofingxana community’s Double Drift Wildlife Economy Project.
tgt: Porojeke ya setjhaba sa Nofingxana ya Double Drift Wildlife Economy.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch of the Nofingxana community’s Double Drift Wildlife Economy Project, at Double Drift Nature Reserve in the Eastern Cape by the Minister of Environmental Affairs, Dr Edna Molewa.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho thakgolwa ha Porojeke ya setjhaba sa Nofingxana ya Double Drift Wildlife Economy, Serapeng sa Diphoofolo tse Hlaha sa Double Drift Kapa Botjhabela ke Letona la Merero ya Tikoloho, Ngaka Edna Molewa.

src: This included the handing over of the title deed to the Likhaya Lethu Communal Property Association (CPA) on behalf of the Minister of Rural Development and Land Reform, Ms Maite Nkoana-Mashabane.
tgt: Sena se ne se kenyeleditse ho fana ka lengolo la bonga thepa ho Mokgatlo wa Likhaya Lethu Communal Property (CPA) lebitsong la Letona la Ntshetsopele ya Dibaka tsa Mahae le Tlhabollo ya Mobu, Mofumahadi Maite Nkoana-Mashabane.

src: The Double Drift community was dispossessed of the residential and grazing rights by the 1913 Land Act.
tgt: Setjhaba sa Double Drift se ne se nkelwe ditokelo tsa bodudi le tsa makgulo ke Molao wa Mobu wa 1913.

src: In 1994, this community lodged a land claim that was settled in 2012, resulting in Likhaya Lethu CPA being established.
tgt: Ka 1994, setjhaba sena se ile sa kenya tseko ya mobu e ileng ya rarollwa ka 2012, moo ho ileng ha thehwa Likhaya Lethu CPLikhaya Lethu CPA e na le ditho tsa Setjhaba sa Double Drift tse 1 500 mme e amohetse R6 milione e tswang Lefapheng la Merero ya Tikoloho, ho ntshetsapele boiteko ba kgwebo ya diphoofolo tse hlaha polasing ya Naudeshoek (1 400 ya dihektara).

src: The Likhaya Lethu CPA consists of 1 500 Double Drift Community members and received R6 million from the Department of Environmental Affairs to develop a wildlife economic business venture in the farm Naudeshoek (1 400 hectares).
tgt: Selekane se ile sa sebetswa ka Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Dibaka tsa Mahae le Tlhabollo ya Mobu.

src: VBS Mutual Bank.
tgt: Banka ya VBS Mutual.

src: Cabinet has noted the South African Reserve Bank announcement with regard to the VBS Mutual Bank.
tgt: Kabinete e nketse hloohong tsebiso ya Banka ya Resefe ya Aforika Borwa mabapi le Banka ya VBS Mutual.

src: The appointed curatorship will support the VBS Mutual Bank to restore its liquidity challenges and serve the interests of the public and VBS depositors.
tgt: Bohlokomedi bo thontsweng bo tla tshehetsa Banka ya VBS Mutual ho busetsa bokgoni ba yona ba maemo a ditjhelete bo be bo sebetsane le ditabatabelo tsa setjhaba esita le ba kwalletseng tjhelete VBKabinete e dula e ikitlaelleditse ho se tshwaneng le ho fetoleng lekala la tsa dtjhelete ntle le ho beha ditabatabelo tsa ba kwallang tjhelete tlokotsing.

src: Investment campaign.
tgt: Letsholo la botsetedi.

src: Cabinet welcomes the ‘CEOs Know’ campaign by Brand South Africa, in collaboration with Business Leadership South Africa, to promote South Africa as an investment destination.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela letsholo la ‘CEOs Know’ la Brand South Africa, ka tshebedisano le Boetapele ba Kgwebo ba Aforika Borwa, ho phahamisa Aforika Borwa jwaloka sebaka seo ho ka tsetelwang ho sona.

src: This builds on our world-class infrastructure through InvestSA One-Stop Shop, research and development capabilities, innovation and an established manufacturing base to support investors.
tgt: Sena se ahella hodima meralo ya rona ya motheo e maemong a hodimo, ka Lebenkele le Rekisang Tsohle la InvestSA, bokgoni ba diphuputso le ntshetsopele, ntlafatso le motheo o tsitsitseng wa tlhahiso ho tshehetsa batsetedi.

src: New growth areas have also been opened in the oceans economy, renewable energy, the green economy and shale-gas exploration.
tgt: Dibaka tse ntjha tsa kgolo le tsona di butswe moruong wa mawatle, ho eneji e hlwekileng, moruo o sa senyeng tikoloho le ho phopholetsa kgase ya shale.

src: The campaign features CEOs from multinational corporations based in South Africa sharing their insights on continued investment in South Africa.
tgt: Letsholo lena le kenyeletsa Bahlanka ba Baholo ba Phethahatso (di-CEO) ba tswang dikgwebong tsa dinaha tse ngata empa di tsepame kahara Aforika Borwa, tse thakelanang tsebo ya tsona mabapi le botsetedi bo tswelang pele Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet encourages all South Africans in the spirit of “Thuma Mina” (Send Me) sweeping across our nation to play their part by sharing their positive stories to build our country’s reputation and grow its investment appeal.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa maAforika Borwa kaofela ka moya wa “Thuma Mina” (Roma Nna) o fokang naha ka bophara hore ba be le seabo sa bona ka ho arolelana dipale tse monate mabapi le ho aha lebitso le letle la naha ya habo rona esita le ho hodisa boipiletso ba yona ba botsetedi.

src: Independent Power Producers (IPPs) Procurement Programme.
tgt: Lenaneo la Phumantsho la Bahlahisi ba Motlakase ba Ikemetseng (di-IPP).

src: Cabinet has noted the High Court case filed by two non-governmental organisations regarding government’s decision to sign the power purchase agreements with 27 IPPs.
tgt: Kabinete e e etse hloko taba ya nyewe ya Lekgotla le Phahameng e hlahletsweng ke mekgatlo e mmedi eo e seng ya mmuso mabapi le qeto ya mmuso ya ho tekena ditumellano tsa theko ya motlakase le di-IPP tse Taba ena e tla phethelwa ke Lekgotla le Phahameng ka la 27 Hlakubele 2018.

src: In the spirit of constitutionalism and the rule of law, the signing has been postponed.
tgt: Ka moya wa matla a molaotheo le taelo ya molao, ho tekena ho tjhetjhisitswe.

src: Cabinet affirms the commitment to resolve the matters around these programmes.
tgt: Kabinete e tiisa boikitlaetso ba ho rarolla diqaka tse amanang le mananeo ana.

src: The Renewable Energy Independent Power Producer Procurement Programme will ensure that consumers in our country have access to cost-efficient and clean energy, and will bring much-needed investment in South Africa.
tgt: Lenaneo la Phumantsho la Bahlahisi ba Ikemetseng ba Eneji e Hlwekileng ba Matla a Motlakase, le tla netefatsa hore basebedisi naheng ya rona ba fumantshwa eneji e theko e tlase ebile e le e hlwekileng, mme le tla tlisa matsete a hlokehang haholo kwano Aforika Borwa.

src: These projects will provide 61 600 full-time jobs, 95% of which are for South African citizens, specifically targeting the youth.
tgt: Diporojeke tsena di tla fana ka mesebetsi ya moshwelella e 61 600, moo 95% ya yona e tla ba ya baahi ba Aforika Borwa, ho tsepamisitswe maikutlo haholo ho batjha.

src: Cabinet reaffirms its commitment to a solid public-private partnership as we pursue our energy transition objectives of the future and a better life for all.
tgt: Kabinete e tiisa botjha boikitlaetso ba yona ba selekane se tiileng sa lekala la mmuso le la poraefete ha re ntse re hahamallela mererong ya rona ya kamoso ya diphetoho ho tsa eneji esita le bophelo bo betere bakeng sa bohle.

src: This is needed to bring much-needed policy and regulatory certainty, and maintain South Africa’s position as an energy investment destination of choice.
tgt: Sena se a hlokahala ho tlisa botsitso bo batlehang haholo ba maano le bolaodi, le ho baballa boemo ba Aforika Borwa jwaloka sebaka se setle se ka kgethelwang botsetedi ho tsa eneji.

src: Listeriosis.
tgt: Listeriosisi.

src: Cabinet extends its heartfelt condolences to the friends and family of those who lost their lives after contracting Listeriosis, and wishes those who are recuperating a speedy recovery.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisetsa matshediso a yona a tswang botebong ba pelo ho metswalle le ba malapa a ba ileng ba hlokahala kamora ho tshwarwa ke Listeriosisi, mme e lakaletsa ba ntseng ba hlaphohelwa hore ba fole ka potlako.

src: More than 180 people died and 940 cases were reported in South Africa.
tgt: Batho ba fetang 180 ba hlokahetse mme ho tlalehilwe diketsahalo tse 940 Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet is encouraged by the intensive efforts by the Department of Health, the National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD) and the World Health Organisation to stop the listeria bacteria from spreading.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothatswa ke matsapa a matla a Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle, Setheo sa Naha sa Mafu a Tshwaetsang (NICD) le Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Bophelo bo Botle (WHO) ho kgina kokwanahloko ya listeria hore e se ke ya jaleha.

src: To further strengthen these efforts, the Minister of Health, Dr Aaron Motsoaledi, will meet with the South African Nursing Council on Thursday, 15 March 2018.
tgt: Ho tswela pele ho matlafatsa matsapa ana, Letona la Bophelo bo Botle, Ngaka Aaron Motsoaledi, le tla kopana le Lekgotla la Baoki la Aforika Borwa (SANC) ka Labone, mohla la 15 Hlakubele 2018.

src: Cabinet acknowledges that the positive progress made in identifying and isolating the source of the deadly Listeriosis outbreak.
tgt: Kabinete e ananela kgatelopele e ntle e entsweng mabapi le ho hlwaya le ho kotela sesosa sa ho ropoha ha Listeriosisi ena e bolayang.

src: The subsequent recall of food products from three Enterprise and Rainbow meat processing plants – where the bacteria was found – was a defining moment to stop the outbreak.
tgt: Kgato e latetsweng ya ho tloswa ha dihlahiswa tsa dijo tse tswang ditsing tse tharo tsa tshebetso ya nama tsa Enterprise le Rainbow – moo ho kokwanahloko e fumanweng teng – e ne e le nako ya bohlokwa ya ho kgina ho ropoha hona.

src: The food-borne disease was first identified in June 2017.
tgt: Lefu lena le fumanehang dijong le hlwailwe kgetlo la pele ka Phupjane 2017.

src: Listeriosis is a serious and preventable illness that can be treated successfully with antibiotics.
tgt: Listeriosisi ke lefu le kotsi empa le ka thibelwang la ba la alafuwa ka katleho ka tshebediso ya diantibayothiki.

src: Those most at risk are pregnant women, very young infants, elderly persons and people with a weakened immune system.
tgt: Ba kotsing ka ho fetisisa ke basadi ba immeng, masea a manyane haholo, metsofe le batho bao masole a bona a mmele a fokolang haholo.

src: People who show symptoms of fever, muscle aches, nausea or diarrhoea should visit their medical practitioner or local clinic immediately.
tgt: Batho ba bontshang matshwao a feberu, mesifa e opang, ho nyekelwa ke pelo kapa letshollo ba lokela ho ya ngakeng kapa ditliliniking tse haufi hanghang.

src: Cabinet is optimistic that South Africa will defeat the current outbreak and urges all people to observe the five food safety rules during this time:Wash hands with soap and water before handling food, and after using a bathroomCook food thoroughly and do not eat half-cooked food as the Listeria bacteria will die when food is well cookedDo not handle raw and cooked food togetherKeep food at appropriate temperatures andMake sure that all milk products are pasteurised or at least parboiled and wash non-cooked food with clean running water before ingestion or at least with pre-boiled water.
tgt: Kabinete e na le tshepo ya hore Aforika Borwa e tla hlola ho ropoha ha lefu lena mme e kopa batho bohle ho lemoha melawana e mehlano ya boipaballo dijong nakong ena:Hatlela ka sesepa le metsi pele o tshwara dijo, le kamora ho sebedisa ntlwanaPhehisisa dijo mme o se ke wa ja dijo tse sa butswang kaha kokwanahloko e shwa ha dijo di butswitseO seke wa tshwara dijo tse tala le tse phehilweng mmohoBoloka dijo motjhesong o nepahetseng mmeEtsa bonnete ba hore dihlahiswa tsohle tsa lebese di hlwekile kapa bonnyane di hakonositswe o be o hlatswe dijo tse sa phehwang ka metsi a hlwekileng a phallang pele o di ja, kapa ka metsi a neng a bedisitswe.

src: Those with any uncertainty related to Listeriosis may contact the NICD on 011 386 Social grants.
tgt: Ba nang le qeaqeo efe kapa efe e amanang le Listeriosisi, ba ka ikopanya le NICD ho 011 386 Ditjhelete tsa dithuso tsa setjhaba.

src: Cabinet was briefed on the state of readiness by the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) to provide the hybrid model in the distribution of social grants to beneficiaries on 1 April 2018.
tgt: Kabinete e tsebisitswe ka boemo ba ho ba malalaalaotswe ha Lekala la Aforika Borwa la Polokeho ya Setjhaba (SASSA) ba ho fana ka mmotlolo o kopantsweng habedi wa kabo ya ditjhelete tsa dithuso tsa setjhaba ho bakgolamolemo ka la 1 Mmesa 2018.

src: This is in line with the Constitutional Court (ConCourt) judgement that ordered the extension of the current contract with the Cash Paymaster Services (CPS) up until 31 March 2018.
tgt: Sena se tsamaelana le kahlolo ya Lekgotla la Molaotheo (ConCourt) e laetseng katoloso ya konteraka ya hajwale le Cash Paymaster Services (CPS) ho fihlela ka la 31 Hlakubele 2018.

src: The current SASSA cards remain valid until December 2018.
tgt: Kabinete e kgotsofetse ka hore bakgolamolemo ba dithuso tsa ditjhelete tsa setjhaba ba tla lefuwa ka la 1 Mmesa 2018.Dikarete tsa hajwale tsa SASSA di tla dula di sebetsa ho fihlela ka Tshitwe 2018.

src: The process of changing the beneficiary cards will be done in a seamless manner that will not disrupt the payment of grants.
tgt: Mothati wa ho fetola dikarete tsa bakgolamolemo o tla etswa ka mokgwa o sa belaetseng ebile e le o sa tlo sitisa ho lefuwa ha ditjhelete tsa dithuso.

src: All beneficiaries who receive their grants through their respective paypoints which includes commercial banks, South African Post Office (SAPO) and other retailers.
tgt: Bakgolamolemo bohle ba tla fumana ditjhelete tsa bona tsa dithuso tsa mmuso ka makala a bona a ditefo a akgang dibanka, Posong ya Aforika Borwa (SAPO) le mabenkeleng a mang.

src: Cabinet has instructed the SASSA, together with the Government Communication and Information System (GCIS), to do everything possible to inform all the beneficiaries of any possible changes that may take place in the process of transition from CPS to the new hybrid model.
tgt: Kabinete e kopa setjhaba sohle, haholoholo bakgolamolemo le ba malapa a bona, ho ikopanya le SASSA ho 0800 60 10 11 kapa ho etela kantoro e haufi ya SASSA, ha o batla ho tseba haholwanyane.

src: Cabinet urges all members of the public, especially beneficiaries and their families, to contact SASSA on 0800 60 10 11 or visit their nearest SASSA office for more information.
tgt: Kabinete e ikamahanya le Khomishene e Ikemetseng ya Dikgetho (IEC) le Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa ho leboheng maAforika Borwa ohle a arabetseng kgoeletso ya ho ingodisetsa dikgetho kapa ho lokisa dintlha tsa diaterese tsa bona letsholong la bekeng e fetileng la boingodiso ba bakgethi.

src: This is a milestone in preparation for the sixth national and provincial elections expected to take place in 2019.
tgt: Sena ke mokolokotwane mabapi le boitokisetso ba dikgetho tsa botshelela tsa naha le tsa diporofense tse lebeletsweng ho tshwarwa ka 2019.

src: A total of 2 767 139 citizens visited voting stations over the past weekend.
tgt: Palo yohle ya baahi ba 2 767 139 e etetse diteishene tsa ho voutela mafelong a fetileng a beke.

src: Of the 2.76 million plus voters who visited their voting stations:Just over million re-registered in their current voting districtMore than 800 000 changed their registration to a new voting districtAlmost 500 000 were voters registering for the first timeOf the new votes registrations, 82% were under the age of 30 and approximately 54% were womenGauteng saw the most new registrations at 23.69%, followed by KwaZulu-Natal with 18.78% and Limpopo with 17.03%.
tgt: Ho bakgethi ba fetang 2.76 milione ba etetseng diteishene tsa bona tsa ho voutela:Ba kahodimonyana ho milione ba ingodisitse botjha diterekeng tsa bona tse ntjha tsa ho voutelaBa kahodimo ho 800 000 ba fetoletse boingodiso ba bona diterekeng tse ntjha tsa ho voutelaBa ka bang 500 000 e ne e le bakgethi ba ingodisang lekgetlo la peleBoingodisong bo botjha ba bakgethi, 82% ya bona e ne e le ka tlasa dilemo tse 30 mme ba ka etsang 54% e ne e le basadiGauteng ke yona e neng e na le boingodiso bo botjha bo bongata ka ho fetisisa ka 23.69%, ha latela KwaZulu-Natal ka 18.78% le Limpopo ka 17.03%.

src: The Eastern Cape had the highest level of registration at 87%, followed by the Free State at just over 82%, and KwaZulu-Natal, Limpopo and Northern Cape at 79% respectively.
tgt: Kapa Botjhabela e bile le boemo bo phahameng ba boingodiso ka 87%, ha latela Freistata hanyane ka hodima 82%, le KwaZulu-Natal, Limpopo le Kapa Leboya ka 79% ka tatelano.

src: Gauteng’s overall registration was at 67.3%.
tgt: Bongodiso ka kakaretso ba Gauteng e ne e le 67.3%.

src: The IEC reported that the voters’ roll now stands at 26 250 939 voters, which roughly equates to 75% of the eligible voting population, based on Statistics South Africa’s voting age population estimates.
tgt: IEC e tlalehile hore jwale lenane la bakgethi le na le bakgethi ba 26 250 939, e leng se ka lekanang le 75% ya batho ba nang le tokelo ya ho kgetha, ho itshetlehilwe hodima dikgakanyong tsa Lefapha la Dipalopalo la Aforika Borwa (StatsSA) tsa dilemo tsa baahi.

src: About 300 000 citizens who visited voting stations are among the almost million voters for whom the IEC did not have an address going into the weekend.
tgt: Baahi ba ka bang 300 000 ba etetseng diteishene tsa ho voutela, ba hara bakgethi ba ka fihlang ho milione bao IEC e neng e se na diaterese tsa bona pele ho mafelo ao a beke ya boingodiso.

src: An up-to-date and accurate voters’ roll affirms the credibility of the voters’ roll and strengthens our democracy by ensuring free, fair and credible elections.
tgt: Lenane la bakgethi le lokisitsweng ebile e le le nepahetseng le tiisa tshepahalo ya lenane la bakgethi mme le matlafatsa demokerasi ya rona ka ho netefatsa dikgetho tse lokolohileng, tse hlokang leeme ebile e le tse tshepahalang.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans who were not able to visit their local voting station over the past weekend to visit their local IEC office to verify and update their addresses.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAforika Borwa ohle a sa kgonang ho etela diteishene tsa ona tsa ho voutela mafelong a fetileng a beke, ho etela kantoro e haufi ya IEC ho ya netefatsa esita le ho lokisa diaterese tsa ona.

src: Alternatively, the IEC’s online facility at WEBTOKEN and the app remains available 24 hours a day for registered votes to check and update their address details.
tgt: Ka nqa e nngwe, sesebedisuwa sa IEC sa inthanete ho WEBTOKEN le app ya yona, di dula di fumaneha ka dihora tse 24 ka letsatsi bakeng sa bakgethi ba ingodisitseng ho lekola le ho lokisa dintlha tsa diaterese tsa bona.

src: Cabinet joins the Minister of Sport and Recreation, Ms Thokozile Xasa, in denouncing the barbaric act of violence against a young triathlete, Mhlengi Gwala, who was attacked with a chainsaw while cycling in KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Kabinete e ikamahanya le Letona la Dipapadi le Boithapollo, Mofumahadi Thokozile Xasa, mabapi le ho tshwela ka mathe ketso ya bosoto ya tlhaselo kgahlanong le moatlelete ya motjha dilemong, Mhlengi Gwala, ya hlasetsweng ka sakga ya difate ha a ntse a palame baesekele KwaZulu-Natal.

src: Cabinet wishes the athlete a speedy recovery and extends a warm thank you to the medical team of St Augustine Hospital who are caring for him.
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa moatlelete enwa hore a fole ka potlako mme e fetisetsa diteboho tse mofuthu ho moifo wa bongaka wa Sepetlele sa St Augustine o ntseng o mo hlokometse.

src: Crime has no place in our society and Cabinet calls on communities to work together with law-enforcement agencies to bring the criminals to book.
tgt: Ditlolo tsa molao ha di na sebaka setjhabeng sa habo rona mme Kabinete e ipiletsa ho badudi ho sebetsa mmoho le makala a qobello ya molao hore ho tshwarwe batlodi ba molao.

src: Drought declared a national disaster.
tgt: Komello e tsebahatswa e le koduwa ya naha.

src: Under the leadership of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs Minister Zweli Mkhize, government has declared a national state of disaster to deal with the country’s drought and water crisis.
tgt: Tlasa boetapele ba Letona la Kopanelo ya Mmuso le Merero ya Botjhaba Zweli Mkhize, mmuso o tsebahaditse boemo ba naha ba koduwa ho sebetsana le bothata ba naha ba komello le metsi.

src: Cabinet extends its appreciation to those in South Africa who continue to save water and the relentless efforts made by the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Drought, together with stakeholders in all spheres of government and society, in dealing with the persistent drought conditions that have hit several parts of the country.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisetsa kananelo ya yona ho bao ba tswelang pele ho boloka metsi ka hara Aforika Borwa, esita le matsapa a sa sisinyeheng a entsweng ke Komiti ya Matona a Kopaneng e mabapi le Komello, hammoho le ba amehang makaleng ohle a mmuso le a setjhaba, mabapi le ho sebetsana le maemo a sa sutheng a komello a thefutseng dikarolo tse ngatanyana tsa naha.

src: Apart from the fact that South Africa is a water-scarce country, Cabinet is assured that we remain a preferred choice of destination for tourists.
tgt: Ntle le taba ya hore Aforika Borwa ke naha e haellwang ke metsi, Kabinete e kgodisehile hore re dula re ntse re le sebaka se ratwang ke bahahlaudi.

src: Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved that the Agreement Amending Annex 1 (Cooperation on Investment) of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Protocol on Finance and Investment (FIP) be tabled in Parliament for ratification.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana hore Sehlomathisetso sa 1 se Hlomathisang Tumellano (Tshebedisano Botseteding) ya Porothokhole ya tsa Ditjhelete le Botsetedi (FIP) ya Ntshetsopele ya Dinaha tsa Aforika e ka Borwa (SADC) e tekwe Palamenteng bakeng sa kananelo.

src: The purpose of the FIP is to harmonise financial and investment policies of Member States, so that they are consistent with the objectives of the SADThis will ensure that any changes to financial and investment policies in one Member State does not necessitate undesirable adjustments in other Member States.
tgt: Sepheo sa FIP ke ho ntlafatsa maano a tsa ditjhelete le botsetedi a Dinaha tseo e leng Ditho, hore di tsamaisane le merero ya SADSena se tla netefatsa hore diphetoho dife kapa dife maanong a tsa ditjhelete le botsetedi Naheng e le nngwe eo e leng Setho ha di tlise diphetoho tse sa batleheng ho Dinaha tse ding tseo e leng Ditho.

src: The amendments aim to preserve the right of governments to regulate in the public interest, and to balance the rights and obligations of investors and governments.
tgt: Dihlomathiso tsena di habile ho baballa tokelo ya mebuso ya ho laola dintho molemong wa setjhaba, esita le ho tsitsisa ditokelo le ditshwanelo tsa batsetedi le mebuso.

src: Cabinet approved the tabling of the Revised and Renamed United Nations (UN) Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners (“Nelson Mandela Rules”), in Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana ho tekwa ha Melawana e Boemong bo Tlase e Shebilweng Botjha ya ba ya Rehwa Botjha ya Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) bakeng sa Tshwaro e Ntle ya Batshwaruwa (“Melawana ya Nelson Mandela”), Palamenteng.

src: The renaming of the Standard Minimum Rules to “Nelson Mandela Rules” honours the legacy of our former President, who spent 27 years in prison.
tgt: Ho rehwa botjha ha Melawana ya Boemo bo Tlase ya “Melawana ya Nelson Mandela” ho tlotla lefa la Moporesidente wa rona wa mehleng, ya qetileng dilemo tse 27 tjhankaneng.

src: There has also been a worldwide extension of the Nelson Mandela International Day scope, observed by UN Member States on 18 July, to promote humane conditions of imprisonment, raise awareness about prisoners being a part of society and value the work of prison staff as a social service.
tgt: Ho boetse ho bile le katoloso ya lefatshe ka bophara ya lepatlelo la Letsatsi la Matjhaba la Nelson Mandela, le hlomphuwang ke Dinaha tseo e leng Ditho tsa UN, ka la 18 Phupu, ho phahamisa maemo a botho a botshwaruwa, ho matlafatsa tlhokomediso mabapi le batshwaruwa hore ke karolo ya setjhaba esita le ho tlotla mosebetsi wa basebeletsi ba ditjhankana e le tshebeletso ya kahisano.

src: The rules will assist South Africa to speed up the transformation towards a people’s developmental correctional system that is consistent with various international principles and guidelines.
tgt: Melawana ena e tla thusa Aforika Borwa ho akofisa diphetoho tse mabapi le tsamaiso ya batho ya ntshetsopele ya tshokollo ya batshwaruwa e tsamaisanang le dipehelo le ditataiso tse fapafapaneng tsa matjhaba.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Prevention and Combating of Hate Crimes and Hate Speech Bill of 2018 into Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Bili ya Thibelo le Twantsho ya Ditlolo tsa Molao tsa Lehloyo le Puo ya Lehloyo ya 2018 hore e tekwe Palamenteng.

src: The Bill aims to create the offences of hate crimes and hate speech, and to put in place measures to prevent and combat these offences.
tgt: Bili e habile ho bopa ditlolo tsa molao tsa lehloyo le puo ya lehloyo, esita le ho kenya tshebetsong mekgwa ya ho thibela le ho lwantsha ditlolo tsena tsa molao.

src: It intends to address violence against persons on the basis of prejudice.
tgt: E rerile ho sebetsana le dikgoka kgahlanong le batho ka lebaka la kgethollo.

src: It will also give effect to South Africa’s obligations in terms of international human rights instruments.
tgt: E tla boela e fana ka tshusumetso ditshwanelong tsa Aforika Borwa ho ya ka disebedisuwa tsa matjhaba tsa ditokelo tsa botho.

src: Cabinet approved for the iKamva National e-Skills Institute (iNeSI) Bill of 2018 to be submitted to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Bili ya Setheo sa Naha sa Boitsebelo ba Inthanete sa iKamva (iNeSI) ya 2018 hore e kenngwe Palamenteng.

src: The Bill provides for the establishment of iNeSI as a legal entity with its own legislation to address e-skills (digital skills) capacity challenges in the country.
tgt: Bili e fana ka ho thehwa ha iNeSI jwaloka setheo se molaong se nang le boetsamolao boo e leng ba sona ho sebetsana le diphephetso tsa bokgoni ba boitsebelo ba inthanete (boitsebelo ba dijithale) ka hara naha.

src: Capacity development of e-skills is seen as one of the priority areas of government in building an inclusive economy, and to establish a capable and developmental state.
tgt: Ntshetsopele ya bokgoni ba boitsebelo ba inthanete e nkuwa e le e nngwe ya dintlha tse ka sehloohong tsa mmuso mabapi le ho aha moruo o kenyeletsang bohle, esita le ho thea naha e nang le bokgoni ebile e le e tswelang pele.

src: The iNeSI will act as a national catalytic collaborator and change agent, for the development of digital skills and organisational capacity in the country.
tgt: INeSI e tla sebetsa jwaloka sethusi sa tshebedisano le diphetoho, bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya boitsebelo ba dijithale le bokgoni ba ditlhophiso ka hara naha.

src: Cabinet approved for the introduction of the Hydrographic Bill of 2018 into Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaelletse monwana Bili ya Dibopeho tsa Metsing ya 2018 hore e lelekelwe Palamenteng.

src: The Bill seeks to recognise and grant legislative status to the Office of the Hydrographer, which has been in existence in the Department of Defence (South African Navy) since the inception of hydrographic services in South WEBTOKEN will enable the Hydrographer of the South African Navy to be recognised as the National Hydrographer.
tgt: Bili e habile ho ananela le ho fana ka maemo a ketsamolao Kantorong ya Setsebi sa Dibopeho tsa Metsing, eo esale e le teng ka hara Lefapha la Lebotho la Tshireletso (Lebotho la Lewatleng la Aforika Borwa) haesale ho tloha tshimolohong ya ditshebeletso tsa dibopeho tsa metsing ka hara Aforika Borwa.

src: It will ensure that the provision of hydrographic services is formalised and enacted into law.
tgt: E tla netefatsa hore phano ya ditshebeletso tsa dibopeho tsa metsing e ba ya semmuso mme e bopellwa ka hara molao.

src: This is in line with the International Maritime Organisation and the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea, which is an international maritime treaty that sets minimum safety standards in the construction, equipment and operation of merchant ships.
tgt: Sena se tsamaelana le Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba wa Mawatle le Mmoka wa Matjhaba ya Polokeho ya Bophelo Mawatleng, e leng tumellano ya matjhaba ya tsa mawatleng e beang maemo a tlase a polokeho mabapi le kaho, thepa le tshebetso ya dikepe tsa kgwebo.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: Human Rights Month/DayThe 2018 National Human Rights Month/Day commemorations will be held under the theme: “The year of Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela: promoting and deepening a human rights culture across society”.The national event will take place on 21 March 2018 at George Thabe Cricket Pitch, Sharpeville in Vereeniging.
tgt: Kgwedi/Letsatsi la Ditokelo tsa BothoMekete ya sehopotso sa Kgwedi/Letsatsi la Naha la 2018 la Ditokelo tsa Botho e tla tshwarwa tlasa mokotaba o reng: “Selemo sa Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela: ho phahamisa le ho tebisa tlwaelo ya ditokelo tsa botho setjhabeng ka bophara”.Ketsahalo ena ya naha e tla tshwarwa ka la 21 Hlakubele 2018 Lebaleng la Kirikete la George Thabe, Sharpeville ho la Vereeniging.

src: Cabinet urges all sectors to pay homage to this national day, which celebrates South Africa’s human rights tradition and honours people such as Madiba who paid the ultimate price and sacrificed for the achievement of liberation and freedom that we enjoy today.
tgt: Kabinete e kopa makala ohle ho hlompha letsatsi lena la Naha, le ketekang setso sa ditokelo tsa botho sa Aforika Borwa esita le ho tlotla batho ba kang Madiba ya ileng a intsha sehlabelo molemong wa phihlello ya topollo le tokoloho tseo re nang le tsona kajeno.

src: National Imbizo Focus WeekThe National Imbizo Focus Week will take place from 9 to 15 April 2018 under the theme: “Together we move South Africa forward”.
tgt: Beke ya Naha ya Tsepamiso ya Maikutlo ya ImbizoBeke ya Naha ya Tsepamiso ya Maikutlo ya Imbizo e tla ba ho tloha ka la 9 ho isa ho la 15 Mmesa 2018 tlasa mokotaba o reng: “Re le mmoho re Ntshetsa Aforika Borwa Pele”.

src: This year, the Mandela Centenary celebration forms a big part of the focus week, under the sub-theme: “Be the legacy”.
tgt: Monongwaha, Mokete wa Dilemo tse Lekgolo tsa Mandela o bopa karolo e kgolo ya beke ya tsepamiso ya maikutlo, tlasa mookotaba o monyane o reng: “E ba karolo ya lefa”.

src: The Executive will be engaging with communities in various parts of the country.
tgt: Ba Phethahatso ba tla buisana le setjhaba dikarolong tse fapaneng tsa naha.

src: The respective programmes of Ministers will be communicated in due course.
tgt: Mananeo a latelanang a Matona a tla tsebahatswa ha mmila o ntse o puta.

src: Youth employment President Ramaphosa is expected to launch the pilot of the Youth Employment Services initiative at the Riversands Incubation Hub in Diepsloot on 27 March 2018.
tgt: Kgiro ya Batjha Moporesidente Ramaphosa o lebeletswe ho thakgola bopulamadiboho ba kgato ya Ditshebeletso tsa Kgiro ya Batjha Setsing sa Thuthuhiso ya Dikgwebo sa Riversands ho la Diepsloot ka la 27 Hlakubele 2018.

src: The initiative, in collaboration with the private sector, aims to empower one million young people over the next five years to become economically active, either as a member of the workforce or running their own businesses or finding their passion for further study.
tgt: Kgato ena, ka tshebedisano le lekala la poraefete, e habile ho matlafatsa batjha ba milione dilemong tse hlano tse tlang hore ba kene kgabong ya moruo, mohlomong e le ditho tsa setlamo sa basebetsi kapa ba itsamaisetsa dikgwebo tseo e leng tsa bona kapa ba iphumanele tjantjello ya seo ba ratang ho ntshetsa dithuto tsa bona pele ka sona.

src: Working visits to Mozambique and ZimbabwePresident Ramaphosa will undertake working visits to the Republic of Mozambique and Republic of Zimbabwe respectively on Saturday, 17 March 2018.
tgt: Maeto a tshebetso ho ya Mozambique le ZimbabweMoporesidente Ramaphosa o tla nka maeto a tshebetso ho ya Riphaboliking ya Mozambique le Riphaboliking ya Zimbabwe ka tatelano, ka Moqebelo wa la 17 Hlakubele 2018.

src: The visits will mainly focus on strengthening bilateral relations with the abovementioned countries.
tgt: Maeto ana a tla tsepamisa maikutlo matlafatsang ya dikamano tsa dinahapedi le dinaha tse qollotsweng ka hodimo mona.

src: The President will also exchange views on peace and security matters in the region and the continent, and further deliberate on global issues of mutual interest.
tgt: Moporesidente o tla boela a thaka maikutlo ka dintho tse amanang kgotso le polokeho ka hara lebatowa esita le kontinenteng, a boele a tshohle ka dintlha tsa lefatshe tse molemong wa dinaha tsena.

src: Messages.
tgt: Melaetsa.

src: Cabinet congratulates Ntsiki Biyela, South Africa’s first black woman winemaker who launched her own brand.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Ntsiki Biyela, Mosadi wa pele wa motho e motsho wa Aforika Borwa wa serathodi sa veine ya thakgotseng veine ya letshwao la hae la boitsebahatso.

src: With a degree in viticulture from Stellenbosch University plus 13 years’ working experience, her Aslina Wines will in 2018 sell 12 000 bottles in the United States of America, Germany, Taiwan and Ghana.
tgt: Jwalokaha a na le lengolo la kgerata ya tsebo ya thitelo ya veine la Yunivesithing ya Stellenbosch hammoho le malebela a dilemo tse 13 a sebetsa, ka 2018 Diveini tsa hae tsa Aslina di tla rekisa dibotlolo tse 12 000 Dinaheng tse Kopaneng tsa Amerika, Jeremane, Taiwan le Ghana.

src: Cabinet congratulates Caster Semenya on breaking the South African 1 000m record that stood for 35 years at the Athletix Grand Prix meeting held at Tuks in Pretoria.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Caster Semenya ka ho roba rekoto ya Aforika Borwa ya 1 000m ya dilemo tse 35 mabelong a Athletix Grand Prix a neng a tshwaretswe Tuks ho la Pretoria.

src: Our golden girl won the race in a time of 2:35:44, beating the old record set in 1983 by Ilze Wicksell by almost two seconds.
tgt: Thope ya rona ya pabala e hapile lebelo leo ka nako ya 2:35:44, a hlola rekoto ya kgale ya 1983 ya Ilze Wicksell ka metsotswana e ka bang e mmedi.

src: Cabinet also commends Semenya for fulfilling her long-held goal to get a university qualification when she completed her Diploma in Sports Science at the North-West University in Potchefstroom.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e thoholetsa Semenya ka ho fihlella peelo ya hae ya nako e telele ya ho fumana mangolo a thuto a yunivesithi, ha a ne a phethela lengolo la hae la Diploma ho tsa Saense ya Dipapadi Yunivesithing ya Leboya Bophirima ho la Potchefstroom.

src: Cabinet expresses condolences to the friends and family of Honourable Member of Parliament, Ms Loliwe Fazeka, who was killed in a car crash in the Eastern Cape, last week.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisa matshediso a yona ho metswalle le ba lelapa ba Setho se Hlomphehang sa Palamente, Mofumahadi Loliwe Fazeka, ya hlokahaletseng kotsing ya koloi Kapa Botjhabela, bekeng e fetileng.

src: Cabinet also sends condolences to the loved ones of South Africa’s Ambassador to Sweden, Ms Faith Radebe, who passed on Tuesday, 13 March 2018.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e fetisa matshediso a yona ho baratuwa ba Lenqosa la Aforika Borwa naheng ya Sweden, Mofumahadi Faith Radebe, ya hlokahetseng ka Labobedi, mohla la 13 Hlakubele 2018.

src: She was previously the Inspector-General of Intelligence in South Africa.
tgt: Pele ho moo e ne e le Mohlahlobi-Kakaretso wa Mautlwela Aforika Borwa.

src: AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: DithonyoDithonyo tsohle di emetse ho netefatswa ka mangolo a thuto le tumello e amehang ya tlhathlobisiso.

src: Dr Philemon Mjwara as Director-General of the Department of Science and Technology for an extended contract period of three years, commencing on 1 April Ms Memme Sejosengwe as Secretary-General at the Office of the Chief Justice for an extended contract period of three years, effective from 1 April Ms Thuli E Radebe, as Executive Director at the Centre of Public Service Innovation for an extended contract period of six months.
tgt: Ngaka Philemon Mjwara e le Motsamaisi-Kakaretso wa Lefapha la Saense le Thekenoloji bakeng sa konteraka e ekeditsweng ya dilemo tse tharo, ho tloha ka la 1 Mmesa Mofumahadi Memme Sejosengwe e le Mongodi-Kakaretso Kantorong ya Moahlodi e Moholo bakeng sa konteraka e ekeditsweng ya dilemo tse tharo, ho tloha ka la 1 Mmesa Mofumahadi Thuli E Radebe, e le Motsamaisi wa Phethahatso Setsing sa Ntlafatso ya Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba bakeng sa konteraka e ekeditsweng ya dikgwedi tse tsheletseng.

src: Mr Thilivhali Archibald Ramawa as the Chief Financial Officer of the National Electronic Media Institute of South Africa.
tgt: Monghadi Thilivhali Archibald Ramawa jwaloka Mohlanka e Moholo wa tsa Ditjhelete wa Setheo sa Naha sa Mehlodi ya Ditaba tsa Elektroniki sa Aforika Borwa.

src: Board of Sentech SOC Limited:a. Mr Magatho Mello (reappointment as non-executive director and Chairperson)b. Mr Lumko Mtimde (reappointment as non-executive director)c. Dr Sandile Malinga (non-executive director) andd.
tgt: Boto ya Sentech SOC Limited:a. Monghadi Magatho Mello (o thontswe hape e le Motsamaisi le Modulasetulo eo e seng wa Phethahatso)b. Monghadi Lumko Mthimde (o thontswe hape e le Motsamaisi eo e seng wa Phethahatso)c. Ngaka Sandile Malinga (Motsamaisi eo e seng wa Phethahatso) led.

src: Ms Elizabeth Malaka (non-executive director).
tgt: Mofumahadi Elizabeth Malaka (Motsamaisi eo e seng wa Phethahatso).

src: Board of Broadband Infraco:a. Mr Mandla Ngcobo (reappointment as non-executive director and Chairperson)b. Ms Nokuthula Selamolela (reappointment as non-executive director)c. Mr Gift Mphefu (non-executive director)d. Ms Zandile Matilda Kabini (non-executive director) ande.
tgt: Boto ya Broadband Infraco:a. Monghadi Mandla Ngcobo (o thontswe hape e le Motsamaisi le Modulasetulo eo e seng wa Phethahatso)b. Mofumahadi Nokuthula Selamolela (o thontswe hape e le motsamaisi eo e seng wa Phthahatso)c. Monghadi Gift Mphefu (Motsamaisi eo e seng wa Phethahatso)d. Mofumahadi Zandile Matilda Kabini (motsamaisi eo e seng wa Phethahatso) lee.

src: Ms Jennifer Schreiner (non-executive director).
tgt: Mofumahadi Jennifer Schreiner (Motsamaisi eo e seng wa Phethahatso).

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 25 April 2018, at Tuynhuys, Cape TownIssues in the environment.
tgt: Kabinete e kopane ka Laboraro mohla la 25 Mmesa 2018, Tuynhuys, Motse KapaDitaba tsa Tikoloho.

src: Funerals of stalwarts and veterans.
tgt: Mapato a baitseki le mekaubere.

src: Cabinet thanks all people around the world, especially South Africans, for their warm and generous response in the wake of the passing of ‘imbokodo’ Mama Winnie Madikizela-Mandela, Struggle stalwart Dr Zola Skweyiya and trade unionist Archie Sibeko.
tgt: Kabinete e leboha batho bohle lefatsheng ka bophara, haholoholo maAforika Borwa, ka karabelo ya bona e mofuthu ebile e le mosa nakong ya ho hlokahala ha ‘imbokodo’ Mama Winnie Madikizela-Mandela, Moitseki wa ntwa ya tokoloho Ngaka Zola Skweyiya le moetapele wa mokgatlo wa basebetsi Archie Sibeko.

src: Our stalwarts dedicated their lives to the dream of a better South Africa and our countrymen and women are drawing inspiration from their struggles.
tgt: Baitseki ba rona ba nyehetse maphelo a bona boikitlaetsong ba Aforika Borwa e ntlafetseng, mme banna le basadi ba naha ya rona ba kgothatswa ba bile ba susumetswa ke ditshotleho tsa bona.

src: Cabinet also joins President Cyril Ramaphosa in paying tribute to the late Veteran diplomat, Ambassador George Nene, who served South Africa with distinction and dedication during his period in exile in mobilising our region and continent to secure the liberation of South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e boetse e ikamahanya le Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa ho iseng hlompho ho mofu Mokaubere wa modiplomate, Moambasadara George Nene, ya sebeleditseng Aforika Borwa ka bokgabane le boitelo nakong ya hae ya ha a ne a le palehong, ho ngoka lebatowa le kontinente ya rona ho netefatsa tokoloho ya Aforika Borwa.

src: North West protests.
tgt: Biopelaetso ba Leboya Bophirima.

src: Cabinet deliberated on the unstable situation that has unfolded in North West, which has affected a number of services, particularly health services.
tgt: Kabinete e sekasekile boemo bo hlokang botsitso bo ropohileng Leboya Bophirima, bo ammeng ditshebeletso tse ngatanyana, haholoholo ditshebeletso tsa bophelo bo botle.

src: As a caring government, Cabinet has approved two immediate interventions to restore order and stability in the area.
tgt: Jwaloka mmuso o tsotellang, Kabinete e ananetse mehato e mmedi ya hanghang ya bokenadipakeng ho busetsa kgutso le botsitso sebakeng seo.

src: Cabinet approved the invoking of Section 100(1) of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996 to address the apparent crisis, particularly in the health sector.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho sebediswa ha Karolo ya 100(1) ya Molaotheo wa Riphaboliki ya Aforika Borwa wa 1996, ho rarolla koduwa ena, haholoholo lekaleng la bophelo bo botle.

src: The main objective of this intervention will be to:restore trust and confidence between labour and governmentassist the province to upgrade its systems and capabilities to a new normalityensure compliance with the legislative and regulatory framework of governmentstabilise the labour environment, restore sustainable service delivery, ensure security of staff and improve financial management.
tgt: Sepheo se ka sehloohong sa bokenadipakeng bona e tla ba ho:busetsa tshepo le boitshepo dipakeng tsa basebetsi le mmusothusa porofense ho ntlafatsa mekgwatsamaiso le bokgoni ba yona tlwaelong e ntjhanetefatsa boikamahanyo le moralo wa mmuso wa ketsamolao le taolotsitsisa tikoloho ya basebetsi, ho kgutlisa phano ya ditshebeletso ya nako e telele, ho netefatsa tshireletseho ya basebetsi le ho ntlafatsa tsamaiso ya ditjhelete.

src: Cabinet also mandated a task team of Ministers to visit North West to establish the facts on the ground.
tgt: Kabinete e boetse e laetse sehlopha sa tshebetso sa Matona ho etela Leboya Bophirima ho fumana dintlha tsa sebele.

src: They are expected to submit a report in the next two weeks.
tgt: Matona a lebelletswe hore a fane ka tlaleho dibekeng tse pedi tse tlang.

src: The report back will assist in determining any further interventions that may still be required.
tgt: Tlaleho ena e tla thusa ho fumana haeba ho na le bokenadipakeng bo bong bo ka nnang ba hlokeha.

src: The Task Team comprises the Ministers of Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation (Convener) Health Finance Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs, as well as the Justice, Crime Prevention and Security Cluster of Ministers.
tgt: Sehlopha seo sa Tshebetso se akga Matona a Thero, Bodisa le Tlhahlobo (Mohlophisi) Bophelo bo Botle tsa Ditjhelete Kopanelo ya Puso le Merero ya Setso hammoho le Setlamo sa Matona a Toka, Thibelo ya Ditlolo tsa Molao le Tshireletso.

src: Whilst noting the concerns that were raised by communities, Cabinet strongly condemns the acts of violence, looting and destruction of property that accompanied protests in some areas of the province.
tgt: Leha e lemoha ditletlebo tse hlahisitsweng ke setjhaba, Kabinete e seolla ka matla diketso tsa dikgoka, boinyafelo le bosenyi ba thepa tse neng di tsamaisana le mehwanto ya boipelaetso dibakeng tse ding tsa porofense.

src: Public sector wage negotiations.1 Cabinet was briefed on the current Public Service wage negotiations.
tgt: Ditherisano tsa meputso lekaleng la setjhaba.1 Kabinete e ile ya tlalehelwa ka ditherisano tsa hajwale tsa meputso ya Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba.

src: Cabinet urged the Department of Public Service and Administration together with the mandating committee to work expeditiously to resolve the impasse on the wage negotiations.
tgt: Kabinete e kopile Lefapha la Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba le Tsamaiso hammoho le komiti e fanang ka matla hore di sebetse ka boikitlaetso ho rarolla ho se utlwisisane ho teng mabapi le ditherisano tsa meputso.

src: Bus strike.
tgt: Seteraeke sa dibese.

src: Cabinet calls on all stakeholders in the public transport sector to bring a speedy end to the national bus strike.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho baamehi bohle lekaleng la dipalangwang tsa setjhaba ho fedisa seteraeke sa naha sa dibese ka potlako.

src: We urge all parties to return to the negotiation table so as to reach an agreement that is in the best interest of all parties and the country.
tgt: Re kopa baamehi bohle hore ba kgutlele ditherisanong ho etsetsa hore ho tle ho fihlellwe tumellano e molemong wa bohle ba amehang esita le naha.

src: Violence at Moses Mabhida Stadium.
tgt: Merusu Lebaleng la Moses Mabhida.

src: Cabinet condemns the senseless violence and malicious damage to property by soccer fans following a pitch invasion at Durban’s Moses Mabhida Stadium during a Premier Soccer League game at the weekend.
tgt: Kabinete e tshwela ka mathe diketso tsa merusu le bosenyi bo soto ba thepa tse entsweng ke balatedi ba bolo ya maoto kamora hore ba itahlele ka Lebaleng la Moses Mabhida, Durban, nakong ya papadi ya Liki e Kgolo ya Bolo ya Maoto (PSL) mafelong a beke.

src: Law-enforcement agencies are urged to ensure that all those involved in hooliganism and acts of violence at the match are held responsible for their actions.
tgt: Ditheo tsa qobello ya molao di koptjwa ho netefatsa hore bohle ba bileng le letsoho bosenying le diketsong tsa merusu papading eo, ba nka boikarabello bakeng sa diketso tsa bona.

src: Cabinet calls for a swift investigation and the implementation of stricter security measures to ensure the safety of spectators and officials.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ya hore ho etswe dipatlisiso tse potlakileng le hore ho kenngwe tshebetsong mehato e tiileng ya tshireletso ho netefatsa polokeho ya babohi le bahlanka.

src: It urges all role players to cooperate with investigations to prevent future occurrences.
tgt: E kopa bohle ba amehang hore ba be le tshebedisano mmoho dipatlisisong, ho thibela hore kamoso diketso tse tjena di se ke tsa etsahala hape.

src: Cabinet welcomes the agreement reached to reconnect 15 community radio stations that were suspended by Sentech for non-payment of signal distribution fees, while more sustainable solutions are being sought.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela tumellano e fihletsweng ya ho hokela botjha diteishene tse 15 tsa seyalemoya tse neng di kwetswe ke Sentech hobane di sa lefa ditefello tsa kabo ya leqhubu la kgaso, ha ho ntse ho batlwa ditharollo tsa nako e telelele.

src: The agreement was reached after government met with Sentech, the National Community Radio Forum, the Media Development and Diversity Agency and the Independent Communications Authority of South Africa.
tgt: Tumellano e fihletswe kamora hore mmuso o be le kopano le Sentech, Foramo ya Naha ya Seyalemoya sa Setjhaba, Lekgotla la Ntshetsopele ya Mehlodi ya Ditaba le ho se Tshwane (MDDA) esita le Lekgotla le Ikemetseng la Dikgokahanyo la Aforika Borwa (ICASA).

src: The community radio sector is a critical communication platform that gives our people access to information and which serves as a means to creating an informed citizenry.
tgt: Lekala la seyalemoya sa setjhaba ke lepatlelo la bohlokwa la kgokahanyo le fang batho ba habo rona phihlello ho tlhahisoleseding, ebile e le tsela ya ho bopa setjhaba se nang le tsebo.

src: All parties have agreed to convene soon to come up with a long-lasting solution that will result in the sustainability of these stations.
tgt: Bohle ba amehang ba dumellane ka ho kopana haufinyane ho tla le tharollo ya nako e telele e tla tlisa boitjaro diteisheneng tsena.

src: Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.
tgt: Kopano ya Dihlooho tsa Mebuso ya Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tsa Selekane.

src: Cabinet welcomes the adoption of the Programme of Action for the Commonwealth for the next two years.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela kananelo ya Lenaneo la Tshebetso la Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tsa Selekane bakeng sa dilemo tse pedi tse tlang.

src: President Ramaphosa led a South African Delegation to the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM 2018) under the theme: “Towards a Common Future” from 19 to 20 April 2018.
tgt: Moporesidente Ramaphosa o etelletse pele Moifo wa Aforika Borwa Kopanong ya Dihlooho tsa Mebuso ya Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tsa Selekane (CHOGM 2018) tlasa mookotaba o reng: “Ho hahamalla Bokamosong bo Tshwanang” ho tloha ka la 19 ho isa ho la 20 Mmesa 2018.

src: In positioning South Africa as one of the world’s leading emerging market investment destination, President Ramaphosa also addressed the African Leaders’ Roundtable of the Commonwealth Business Forum, and engaged with senior international investors and business leaders.
tgt: Ha a teka Aforika Borwa e le se seng sebaka sa botsetedi se hlahelletseng ka mahetla mebarakeng e thuthuang, Moporesidente Ramaphosa o boetse a teka puo Kopanong ya Baetapele ba Aforika ba Foramo ya Kgwebo ya Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tsa Selekane, a ba a dula majwana le batsetedi ba baholo ba matjhaba hammoho le baetapele ba kgwebo.

src: He also extended an invitation to leading investors and leaders of business to attend South Africa’s much anticipated Investment Summit scheduled for later this year.
tgt: O boetse a fetisa memo ho batsetedi ba itlhommeng pele esita le baetapele ba kgwebo hore ba be teng Kopanong ya Botsetedi e hlophiseditsweng hore e tshwarwe hamorao selemong sena.

src: Under the leadership of President Ramaphosa, the South African delegation also used the opportunity presented by the CHOGM to continue lobbying for South Africa’s candidature to the United Nations (UN) Security Council for the term 2019 – 2020.
tgt: Tlasa boetapele ba Moporesidente Ramaphosa, moifo wa Aforika Borwa o boetse wa sebedisa monyetla ona o tlisitsweng ke CHOGM hore ba tswele pele ho thaothela bonkgetheng ba Aforika Borwa ho Lekgotla la Tshireletso la Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) bakeng sa sehla sa 2019 – 2020.

src: These elections are scheduled for 8 June 2018 in New York, USInvestment.
tgt: Dikgetho tsena di hlophiseditswe ho tshwarwa ka la 8 Phuptjane 2018 ho la New York, Amerika (USA).

src: Cabinet welcomes President Ramaphosa’s appointment of four special envoys on investment to engage both domestic and foreign investors around economic opportunities in South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela thonyo ya Mopresidente Ramaphosa ya maqosa a kgethehileng mabapi le botsetedi hore a dule majwana le batsetedi ba lapeng esita le ba dinaheng tsa bolata ka menyetla ya moruo e Aforika Borwa.

src: These envoys are mandated to attract investment in a focused and cost-effective manner.
