src: Cabinet also expresses its condolences to the family and friends of the miner who died at the Sibanye-Stilwater’s Khomanani Mine in Driefontein in Mpumalanga and remains concerned over the safety of miners at the mine.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e fetisetsa matshediso a yona ho lelapa le metswalle ya mosebetsi wa morafong ya hlokahaletseng Morafong wa Sibanye-Stilwater Khomanani Driefontein, Mpumalanga mme e tswella ho ngongoreha ka tshireletso ya basebetsi ba merafong.

src: Congratulations.
tgt: Ditebohiso.

src: Cabinet congratulates the National Library of South Africa (NLSA), which celebrated 200 years of its existence.
tgt: Kabinete e lebohisa Laebrorari ya Afrika Borwa ya Naha (NLSA), e ketekileng dilemo tse 200 e thehilwe.

src: Earlier this year, the NLSA marked this milestone by hosting an open exhibition titled “Treasure House of Knowledge”.
tgt: Maqalong a selemo sena, NLSA e ile ya fihlela katleho e bohlokwa haholo ka ho tshwara pontshahatso e bitswang “Ntlo ya Letlotlo la Tsebo”.

src: Cabinet welcomes the decision by the UN Education, Scientific and Cultural Organisation to declare the Makhonjwa Mountains in Mpumalanga, also known as the Barberton Greenstone Belt, as a World Heritage Site.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela qeto ya Mokgatlo wa Thuto, Saense le Botjha wa UN ya ho phatlalatsa Dithaba tsa Makhonjwa, Mpumalanga, tse boelang di tsejwa e le Barberton Greenstone Belt, ho ba Sebaka sa Bojalefa sa Lefatshe.

src: This is South Africa’s 10th World Heritage Site.
tgt: Sena ke Sebaka sa Bojalefa sa Lefatshe sa Afrika Borwa sa bo.

src: Cabinet calls on all stakeholders in the tourism sector to market all the heritage sites in South Africa as tourism is one of the accelerators towards developing our economy and creating jobs for local people.
tgt: Kabinete e mema bohle ba nang le seabo ho tsa lekala la bohahlaudi ho bapatsa dibaka tsohle tsa bojalefa tse Afrika Borwa jwalo ka ha bohahlaudi e le e nngwe ya dintho tse potlakisang ntshetsopele ya moruo wa rona le ho theha mesebetsi ya batho ba ka naheng.

src: Cabinet commemorates with pride the 63rd anniversary of the historic adoption of the Freedom Charter which formed the basis of the Constitution of the Republic of South WEBTOKEN its core principles are reflected in the principles of the then Organisation of African Unity (now AU) and the United Nation has aligned its Universal Declaration of Human Rights to these principles.
tgt: Kabinete e hopola ka motlotlo sehopotso sa bo63 sa kananelo ya nalane ya Tjhata ya Tokoloho e ileng ya theha motheo wa Molaotheo wa Rephaboliki ya Afrika Borwa.

src: AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: Kajeno ditheo tse bohlokwa tsa yona di bonahala ditheong tsa Mokgatlo wa Kopano ya Afrika (oo o seng o bitswa AU) mme UN e amahantse Phatlalatso ya Lefatshe Lohle ya Ditokelo tsa Botho le ditheo tsena.

src: Mr Sibusiso E Bukhosini as the Chief Executive Officer for iSimangaliso Wetland Park Authority.
tgt: Monghadi Sibusiso E Bukhosini jwalo ka Mohlanka e Moholo wa Phethahatso (CEO) wa Bolaodi ba Serapa sa Sebaka sa Metsi sa iSimangaliso.

tgt: Moadvokheiti Mmadikeledi Suzan Malebe jwalo ka Motlatsi wa Molaodikakaretso (DDG): Molao wa Menerale, ho Lefapha la Dirashwa (DMR).

tgt: Mme Buyisiwe Faith Ntokozo Ngcwabe jwalo ka DDG: Leano la Menerale le Phahamiso, ho DMR.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 22 August 2018 at Tuynhuys in Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya kopanela Tuynhuys Motse Kapa, ka Laboraro, mohla la 22 Phato 2018.Dintlha tsa Ha jwale.

src: Economy.
tgt: Moruo.

src: The recent economic developments in Turkey have led to a large depreciation of emerging market currencies, including the South African Rand.
tgt: Diketsahalo tsa moraorao tsa moruo Turkey, di lebisitse ho nyotobeleng ho hobe ha boleng ba ditjhelete tsa mebaraka e ntseng e thuthua, ho akga le Ranta ya Aforika Borwa.

src: Capital outflows from these markets have accelerated and bond yields have risen, slowing down economic growth and job creation.
tgt: Lephallo la ditjhelete tse tswang mebarakeng ena le nyollotse sekgahla mme ditswala tsa kadimo di eketsehile, e leng ntho e sisithehisang kgolo ya moruo le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi.

src: Turkey’s large foreign currency denominated liabilities and relatively low levels of foreign currency reserves predisposed the country to large and damaging capital outflows, as monetary policy started to normalise in advanced economies.
tgt: Mekitlane e meholo e qollotsweng ya tjhelete ya phapanyetsano le dinaha tse ding ya Turkey, le sekgahla se tlase sa dipolokelo tsa tjhelete ya phapanyetsano le dinaha tse ding, e beile naha tlokotsing ya lephallo la ditjhelete le leholo ebile e le le ruthuthang.

src: Cabinet notes that South Africa has a number of strengths, including an independent central bank, an inflation-targeting regime with inflation consistently within the target range, low levels of foreign-currency debt and a clear fiscal consolidation plan.
tgt: Kabinete e a elellwa hore Aforika Borwa e na le dintlha tse ngatanyana tseo e leng matla ho tsona, ho akga le banka e bohareng e ikemetseng, mmuso o tsepamisitseng maikutlo ho sekgahla sa tswala moo sekgahla sa tswala se dulang se le boemong bo lebeletsweng, mokitlane wa ditjhelete tsa phapanyetsano le dinaha tse ding o boemong bo tlase hammoho le morero o totobetseng wa momahanyo ya ditjhelete.

src: Cabinet is committed to maintaining these strengths.
tgt: Kabinete e ikemiseditse ho boloka dintlha tsena tseo e leng matla ho tsona di ntse di le jwalo.

src: At the same time, government will continue to implement reforms to increase the growth potential of the economy and improve the credibility of our policy decisions.
tgt: Ka ho tshwanang, mmuso o tla tswelapele ho kenya tshebetsong diphetoho tsa ho eketsa kgonahalo ya kgolo ya moruo, o be o ntlafatse ho tshepahala ha diqeto tsa maano a rona.

src: Government will continue to collaborate with business, labour and civil society to restore confidence in the economy and address the structural constraints to economic growth.
tgt: Mmuso o tla tswelapele ho sebedisana le ba kgwebo, bosebetsi le setjhaba ho kgutlisa boitshepo moruong esita le ho hleka ditshita tsa kgolo ya moruo.

src: Working together we can translate our plans into concrete actions to move the South African economy forward.
tgt: Ha re sebetsa mmoho, re ka fetola merero ya rona hore e be diketso tsa sebele tsa ho ntshetsapele moruo wa Aforika Borwa.

src: Value-Added Tax (VAT).
tgt: Lekgetho la Theko (VAT).

src: Cabinet welcomes the report by the Ministerial Panel of Experts which reviewed the list of zero-rated VAT items and recommended the inclusion of white bread, bread flour, cake flour, sanitary products and school uniforms.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela tlaleho ya Setlamo sa Ditsebi sa Matona, se hlophileng botjha lenane la dihlahiswa tse sa angweng ke lekgetho la theko yaba se kgothaletsa ho kenyeletswa ha bohobe bo bosweu, folouru ya bohobe, folouru ya dikukusi, disebediswa tsa bohlweki le diyunifomo tsa sekolo.

src: Cabinet encourages South Africans to voice their opinions on the report, which is open for public comment until 31 August 2018.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa maAforika Borwa ho hlahisa maikutlo ka tlaleho ena e buletsweng ditshwaelo tsa setjhaba, ho fihlela ka la 31 Phato 2018.

src: The Minister of Finance, Mr Nhlanhla Nene, will then make an informed choice on which proposals to implement.
tgt: Letona la tsa Ditjhelete, Monghadi Nhlanhla Nene, o tla etsa kgetho e tsepameng ka hore na ke dife ditshisinyo tseo a di kenyang tshebetsong.

src: Submissions can be made in writing to EMAILTOKEN Women’s Month.
tgt: Ditshwaelo di ka etswa ka ho ngolla ho EMAILTOKEN Kgwedi ya Basadi.

src: Cabinet calls on all citizens to continue with the drive to ensure the safety and empowerment of women in our society.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho baahi bohle hore ba tswele pele ka tjantjello ya ho netefatsa boteng ba polokeho le matlafatso ya basadi setjhabeng sa habo rona.

src: We commend all sectors of society for heading up initiatives aimed at fighting gender-based violence (GBV).
tgt: Re thoholetsa makala ohle a setjhaba ka ho etella pele dikgato tse reretsweng ho lwantsha ditlhekefetso tse amanang le bong (GBV).

src: As Women's Month draws to a close, Cabinet continues to honour women in the same spirit that we honour the women of 1956 who marched to the Union Buildings in Pretoria in defiance of a brutal regime that sought to use discriminatory pass laws to undermine their dignity.
tgt: Jwalokaha Kgwedi ya Basadi e ya mafelong, Kabinete e tswela pele ho tlotla basadi ka moya o tshwanang le oo re tlotlang basadi ba 1956 ka wona, ba ileng ba hwantela Union Buildings Pretoria, ba hanana le puso e soto e neng e batla ho sebedisa melao ya kgethollo ya dipasa ho hobosa seriti sa bona.

src: Since the start of our democracy in 1994, great strides have been made to ensure that women enjoy the same rights as their male counterparts in education, employment, property, inheritance and justice.
tgt: Haesale ho tloha tshimolohong ya demokerasi ya rona ka 1994, dikgato tse kgolo di se di nkilwe ho netefatsa hore basadi ba fumana ditokelo tse tshwanang le tsa bomphato ba bona ba banna thutong, mesebetsing, thepeng, mafeng le tokeng.

src: In driving an inclusive economy, we are working hard to ensure the full participation of women in the economy and driving an inclusive economy.
tgt: Tsamaisong ya moruo o kenyeletsang bohle, re tiisitse meqheleba ho netefatsa seabo se phethahetseng sa basadi moruong, le ho tsamaiseng moruo o kenyeletsang bohle.

src: As part of celebrating Women’s Month, the Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries – in partnership with the Department of Rural Development and Land Reform, and Total South Africa – will on Thursday, 23 August 2018 hold its 19th Annual Female Entrepreneur Awards in East London in the Eastern Cape.
tgt: E le karolo ya ho keteka Kgwedi ya Basadi, Lefapha la Temo, Meru le Botshwasi ba Ditlhapi –ka selekane le Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Mahae le Tlhabollo ya Mobu, le khamphane ya Total South Africa – ka Labone mohla la 23 Phato 2018, ba tla ba le moketjana wa bo19 wa Selemo le selemo wa Dikgau tsa Bahwebi ba Basadi East London Kapa Botjhabela.

src: Government, together with its partners, will hold a National Gender Summit to forge consensus on how best to deal with GBThe Minister of Police, Mr Bheki Cele, has recommitted members of the South African Police Service (SAPS) to prioritise cases that involve the abuse of women and children.
tgt: Mmuso, hammoho le balekane ba wona, ba tla tshwara Mmoka wa Naha wa Bong, ho hahamalla tumellanong ya kamoo ho ka sebetsanwang hantle ka teng le GBLetona la Sepolesa, Monghadi Bheki Cele, o laetse botjha ditho tsa Tshebeletso ya Sepolesa sa Aforika Borwa (SAPS) ho bea dinyewe tse amanang le tlhekefetso ya basadi le bana ka sehloohong.

src: When a woman or a child reports a crime or abuse, it must be followed up with the urgency it deserves and taken to its full conclusion.
tgt: Ha mosadi kapa ngwana a tlaleha tlolo ya molao kapa tlhekefetso, e tlameha ho salwa morao ka potlako yohle e e lokelang e be e ilo phethelwa ka botlalo.

src: Land expropriation Cabinet thanks South Africans who participated in the parliamentary public hearings into the possible review of Section 25 of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996 to allow for the expropriation of land without compensation.
tgt: Ho nkuwa ha mobuKabinete e leboha maAforika Borwa a bileng le seabo dipitsong tsa palamente tsa nonyo ya maikutlo a setjhaba ka kgonahalo ya tlhophobotjha ya Karolo ya 25 ya Molaotheo wa Rephaboliki ya Aforika Borwa wa 1996, ho dumella ho nkuwa ha mobu ntle le ditlhapiso.

src: Parliament’s Constitutional Review Committee has concluded hearings in all Provinces.
tgt: Komiti ya Palamente ya Tlhophobotjha ya Molaotheo e phethetse dipitso tsa yona diprofenseng tsohle.

src: The deliberations on these hearings as well as written inputs will now be considered by Parliament.
tgt: Dipuisano tse neng di le dipitsong tsena esita le diphehiso tse ngotsweng, jwale di tla sekasekwa ke Palamente.

src: Discussions on the issue of land ownership in South Africa is vital and working together we can ensure that land reforms can further assist in growing our economy particularly in the agricultural sector and address the land ownership inequalities in our country.
tgt: Dipuisano tabeng ya boithuelo ba mobu Aforika Borwa e bohlokwa, mme ha re sebetsa mmoho re ka netefatsa hore ditlhabollo tsa mobu di ka boela tsa thusa ho hodiseng moruo wa rona, haholoholo lekaleng la temo di be di rarolle qaka ya ho se lekane ha boithuelo ba mobu naheng ya rona.

src: President Cyril Ramaphosa has appointed an Inter-Ministerial Committee chaired by Deputy President David Mabuza to coordinate and implement measures to accelerate the redistribution of land, the extension of security of tenure, the provision of agricultural support and the redress of spatial inequality, within a broad and comprehensive land redistribution and agricultural development programme.
tgt: Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa o thontse Komiti ya Matona a Kopaneng, eo modulasetulo wa yona e leng Motlatsi wa Moporesidente David Mabuza, ho hlophisa le ho kenya tshebetsong dikgato tsa ho akofisa kabobotjha ya mobu, katoloso ya tshireletso ya ho dula sebakeng se itseng, phano ya tshehetso ya tsa temo le ho lokisa ho se lekane ho renang jwale, kahare ho kabobotjha e batsi e phethahetseng ya mobu esita le lenaneo la ntshetsopele ya temo.

src: Sanitation Appropriate for Education (SAFE) Initiative.
tgt: Letsholo la Matlwana a Loketseng Dikolo (SAFE).

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch by President Ramaphosa of the SAFE Initiative, as part of government’s response to the sanitation challenges facing some of the country’s poorest schools.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela kgakolo ya letsholo la SAFE ka Moporesidente Ramaphosa, e le karolo ya karabelo ya mmuso diphephetsong tsa matlwana tseo tse ding tsa dikolo tse futsanehileng ka ho fetisisa naheng ena di tobaneng le tsona.

src: The SAFE Initiative is led by the Department of Basic Education, in partnership with the National Education Collaboration Trust and the Nelson Mandela Foundation.
tgt: Kgato ya SAFE e etelletswe pele ke Lefapha la Thuto ya Motheo, ka selekane le Letsete la Tshebedisanommoho la Thuto ya Naha.

src: Cabinet calls on all sectors of society, including big business and non-governmental organisations, to support the initiative that is aimed at alleviating infrastructure backlogs for schools in poor communities.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso makaleng ohle a setjhaba, ho akga le dikgwebo tse kgolo le mekgatlo eo e seng ya mmuso, ho tshehetsa kgato ena e reretsweng ho fedisa tshallomorao ya meralo ya motheo bakeng sa dikolo tse dibakeng tse futsanehileng.

src: National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS)Cabinet was briefed by the Minister of Higher Education and Training, Ms Naledi Pandor, on the challenges facing the NSFAIn order to stabilise and decisively address the challenges faced by the NSFAS in the disbursement of funds to deserving students, Cabinet supported the appointment of the Administrator, Dr Randall Carolissen.
tgt: Sekema sa Naha sa Thuso ya Ditjhelete tsa Baithuti (NSFAS)Kabinete e ile ya hlajwa malotsana ke Letona la Thuto e Phahameng le Thupelo, Mofumahadi Naledi Pandor, ka diphephetso tseo NSFAS e tobaneng le tsona.

src: The appointment of the Dr Carolissen effectively dissolves the current NSFAS Board.
tgt: E le ho tsitsisa le ho rarolla ka nepo diphephetso tseo NSFAS e tobaneng le tsona kanetsong ya ditjhelete baithuting ba tshwanelehileng, Kabinete e tsheheditse ho thonngwa ha Motsamaisi, Ngaka Randall Carolissen.

src: The Administrator together with the management will work towards dealing decisively with backlogs and other challenges facing the entity so as to ensure student funding is administered optimally for 2019, and that all outstanding issues for 2017 and 2018 are resolved.
tgt: Thonyo ya Ngaka Carolissen e qhala Boto ya jwale ya NSFAS hanghang.

src: RetrenchmentsCabinet is concerned by recent announcements over possible retrenchments and job losses in some industries, including mining and media.
tgt: Motsamaisi hammoho le setlamo sa botsamaisi ba hae ba tla sebeletsa ho nka qeto e ntle ka tshallomorao le diphephetso tse ding tseo setheo se tobaneng le tsona, ho netefatsa hore letlole la baithuti le tsamaiswa ka bokgabane ka 2019, le hore diqaka tsohle tse salletseng morao tsa 2017 le 2018 di a rarollwa.

src: We reiterate our appeal to business to consider retrenchment only as a last resort, and to explore other available and innovative ways to sustain jobs.
tgt: Ho heletswa mosebetsingKabinete e tshwenyehile ka ditsebiso tse sa tswa etswa ka ho heletswa mosebetsing le ho fela ha mesebetsi ho ka nnang ha etsahala diindastering tse ding, ho akga le merafo le mehlodi ya ditaba.

src: Government continues to partner with business and labour, and remains convinced that working together, we can grow our economy and create new jobs.
tgt: Re thasisetsa boipiletso ba rona ho ba kgwebo hore ba lekodisise mekgwa e mengata e fapaneng pele ba ka nahana ka taba ya ho heletsa mosebetsing, ba boele ba lekole mekgwa e meng e teng ya ntlafatso ya ho boloka mesebetsi.

src: BroadcastingCabinet welcomes the news that the SABC will screen English Premiership League games.
tgt: Mmuso o tswelapele ho sebedisana le ba kgwebo le ba bosebetsi, mme o ntse o na le tshepo ya hore ha re sebetsa mmoho, re ka hodisa moruo wa rona re be re thee mesebetsi e metjha.

src: While this may be a revenue opportunity for the SABC, government hopes that the screening of these games will not sacrifice local sports and also worsen the financial position of the public broadcaster, given its current liquidity challenges.
tgt: KgasoKabinete e amohela ditaba tsa hore Lekgotla la Kgaso la Aforika Borwa (SABC) le tla hasa dipapadi tsa English Premiership League.

src: Cabinet notes the Invitation to Apply for the licensing of spectrum for the provision of subscription broadcasting services by the Independent Communications Authority of South Africa.
tgt: Leha kgaso ena e ka nna ya eba monyetla wa pokello ya tjhelete ho SABC, mmuso o tshepa hore ho haswa ha dipapadi tsena ha ho ka ke ha sekisetsa dipapadi tsa lapeng kapa wa mpefatsa boemo ba ditjhelete ba mohasi wa setjhaba, ha ho shejwa diphephetso tsa jwale tsa ho fellwa ke tjhelete.

src: While matters pertaining to licensing are the exclusive domain of the regulator, consistent with Section 192 of the Constitution, the licensing process should be done in a manner that does not destabilize the free-to-air platform during the transition from analogue to digital or encourages uncompetitive behaviour.
tgt: Leha merero ya ho ntshuwa ha dilaesense e le boikarabelo bo qollehileng ba ICASA, ho ya ka Karolo ya 192 ya Molaotheo, mosebetsi wa ho ntshuwa ha dilaesense o tshwanela ho etswa ka mokgwa o sa thunthetseng lepatlelo la maqhubu a kgaso nakong ya phetoho ya ho tloha mokgweng wa kgale wa kgaso wa analoko ho ya ho o motjha wa dijithale, kapa o kgothaletsang ho se qothisane lehlokwa.

src: It should ensure that new licensees are able to compete fairly and openly.
tgt: E tshwanela ho netefatsa hore beng ba dilaesense ba batjha ba kgona ho qothisana lehlokwa ka mokgwa o lokolohileng ebile e le o se nang leeme.

src: Cabinet Decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Agreement establishing the African Continental Free Trade Area to Parliament for ratification.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho kenngwa Palamenteng ha Tumellano ya ho thewa ha Sebaka sa Kgwebisano ya Mahala sa Kontinente ya Aforika, bakeng sa ho tjhaellwa monwana.

src: This agreement will result in access to new and dynamic markets in the rest of Africa, in particular new markets in West Africa and North Africa.
tgt: Tumellano ena e tla thusa ka phihlello mebarakeng e metjha e hatetseng pele Aforika yohle, haholoholo mebaraka e metjha ya Aforika Bophirimela le Aforika Leboya.

src: It will also provide export opportunities for South African products.
tgt: E tla boela e fana ka menyetla ya diyantle bakeng sa dihlahiswa tsa Aforika Borwa.

src: This will also be in line with the integrated development approach in the continent.
tgt: Sena se tla boela se tsamaisana le mokgwa wa ntshetsopele e momahantsweng kontinenteng.

src: It will stimulate industrial development, investment and the creation of jobs in the continent.
tgt: E tla qholotsa ntshetsopele ya diindasteri, botsetedi le ho thewa ha mesebetsi kontinenteng.

src: Study on spectrum licensingCabinet approved the outcome of the commissioned study by the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research, which sought to determine the amount of spectrum for open access and licensing to the industry.
tgt: Diphuputso tsa bobatsi ba tikoloho ya kgaso ha ho ntshuwa ha dilaesenseKabinete e ananetse sephetho sa diphuputso tse entsweng ke Lekgotla la Diphuputso tsa Saense le Diindasteri (CSIR), tse neng di habile ho fumana hore na bobatsi ba kgaso bo teng bo boholo hakae bakeng sa phihlello le ho ntshuwa ha dilaesense ka bolokolohi indastering.

src: The study confirms that spectrum can be licensed to both the Wireless Open Access Network (WOAN) and the industry.
tgt: Diphuputso di netefatsa hore bobatsi ba tikoloho ya kgaso bo ka ntshetsa dikhamphane tse qalang tse nang le boitsebelo tsa Marangrang a Phihlello e Bulehileng ya Waelese (WOAN) le diindasteri tseo e leng kgale di le teng sebakeng sena dilaesense tsa kgaso.

src: This will, amongst others, achieve the national policy obligations, cost of communication remove the entry barriers for small and medium companies, and sustain the current investments.
tgt: Ho tse ding, ho tla fihlellwa ditlhoko tsa leano la naha, ditjeo tsa dikgokahano ho tlosa ditshita tsa ho kena bakeng sa dikhamphane tse nyenyane le tse mahareng, esita le ho boloka matsete a seng a le teng.

src: The Minister of Telecommunications and Postal Services, Dr Siyabonga Cwele, will hold a full media briefing to unpack this report.
tgt: Letona la Meralo ya Dikgokahanyo le Ditshebeletso tsa Poso, Ngaka Siyabonga Cwele, o tla tshwara seboka se phethahetseng sa ditaba ho manolla tlaleho ena.

src: Progress on North WestCabinet received the fourth progress report on the Section 100(1) intervention in North West.
tgt: Kgatelopele profenseng ya Leboya Bophirimela Kabinete e amohetse tlaleho ya bone ya kgatelopele ka Karolo ya 100(1) ya bokenadipakeng Leboya Bophirimela.

src: Cabinet is satisfied with the implementation stage, with several milestones reached in terms of the institutionalization of the project in the province.
tgt: Kabinete e kgotsofetse ka kgato ya ho kenngwa tshebetsong, moo dikatleho tse ngatanyana di fihlelletsweng, ho ya ka mokgwa oo projeke e hlophisitsweng ka teng profenseng.

src: The Memorandum of Understanding between the national and provincial government has been signed from the Inter-Ministerial Task Team (IMTT) on North West Five administrators for the departments placed under Section 100(1)b have been appointed and formally installed as accounting officersThe protocols and directives between the respective National Ministers and provincial MECs have been signed in line with Section 100(1) andAn overall coordinator for the management of the North West intervention has been appointed.
tgt: Tokomane ya Kutlwisisano dipakeng tsa mmuso wa naha le wa profense e tekennwe ke Sehlopha sa Tshebetso ya Matona a Kopaneng (IMTT) mabapi le Leboya BophirimelaBatsamaisi ba bahlano ba mafapha a kentsweng katlasa Karolo 100(1) ba se ba thontswe mme ba kentswe semmuso e le bahlanka ba ikarabellangMetjha le methati e latelwang dipakeng tsa Matona a Naha le Ditho tsa Lekgotla la Ketsamelao (bo-MEC) e se e tekennwe, ho ipapisitswe le Karolo ya 100(1) ebileMohlophisi ya akaretsang wa bolaodi ba bokenadipakeng ba Leboya Bophirimela o se a thontswe.

src: Cabinet further expressed appreciation to the immediate intervention by the South African National Defense Force (SANDF) and the Municipal Infrastructure Support Agent to the sewage crisis in the Ditsobotla Local Municipality in North West.
tgt: Kabinete e boetse ya bontsha kgotsofalo ka bokenadipakeng ba hanghang ba Lebotho la Sesole sa Naha la Aforika Borwa (SANDF), esita le Akgente ya Tshehetso ya Meralo ya Motheo ya Bomasepala qakeng ya dikgwerekgwere Masepaleng wa Dibaka wa Ditsobotla Leboya Bophirimela.

src: The spillage of the sewerage, which had become a health hazard to the community, has been cleared.
tgt: Ho qhalana ha dikgwerekgwere, e leng ntho e fetohileng tlokotsi bophelong bo botle ba setjhaba, ho se ho lokisitswe.

src: Cabinet commended the work that has been done to date by the Administrators under the leadership of the IMTT, chaired by Minister Nkosazana Dlamini Zuma.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholeditse mosebetsi o seng o entswe ke Batsamaisi ho fihlela jwale katlasa boetapele ba IMTT, moo modulasetulo e leng Letona Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma.

src: Integrated Resource Plan (IRP)Cabinet approved the publication of the updated Integrated Resource Plan for public input.
tgt: Morero wa Mehlodi e Kopantsweng (IRP)Kabinete e ananetse ho phatlalatswa ha Morero o ntlafaditsweng wa Mehlodi e Kopantsweng bakeng sa ditshwaelo tsa setjhaba.

src: The National Development Plan identifies the need for South Africa to invest in a strong network of economic infrastructure designed to support the country’s medium- and long-term economic and social objectives.
tgt: Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP) o hlwaya tlhokeho ya Aforika Borwa ya ho tsetela marangrang a matla a meralo ya motheo ya moruo, a raletsweng ho tshehetsa dipheo tsa naha tsa nako e bohareng le tsa e telele ya moruo le setjhaba.

src: Energy infrastructure is a critical component that underpins economic activity and growth across the country it needs to be robust and extensive enough to meet industrial, commercial and household needs.
tgt: Meralo ya motheo wa eneji ke sesebediswa sa bohlokwa se matlafatsang diketsahalo tsa moruo le kgolo ho pharalla le naha e tshwanela ho ba matla le ho ba batsi ka ho lekaneng ho fihlela ditlhoko tsa diindasteri, dikgwebo le tsa malapeng.

src: The finalisation of the IRP will provide the necessary certainty to industry players as well as consumers in so far as security of electricity supply in the medium to long term is concerned.
tgt: Ho phethelwa ha IRP ho tla fana ka botsitso bo hlokehang ho ba nkang seabo indastering esita le ho bareki, ho ya kamoo tshireletso ya phepelo ya motlakase ya nako e bohareng le e telele e leng ka teng.

src: The Minister of Energy, Mr Jeff Radebe, and the department will engage the National Economic Development and Labour Council EXCO on Friday, 24 August on the draft report, which will also be published in the Government Gazette and the Department of Energy’s website (WEBTOKEN) by not later than Monday, 27 August Cabinet approved the Government Communication Policy, which will be applicable across government.
tgt: Letona la Eneji, Monghadi Jeff Radebe, le lefapha ba tla dula majwana le Ntshetsopele ya Moruo wa Naha le Lekgotla la Bosebetsi EXCO ka Labohlano, mohla la 24 Phato 2018 mabapi le tlaleho ya nakwana, e tla boela e phatlalatswa Koranteng ya Mmuso le websaeteng ya Lefapha la Eneji (WEBTOKEN) ho fihlela ka Mantaha, mohla la 27 Phato Kabinete e ananetse Leano la Mmuso la Dikgokahano, le tla sebediswa mmusong ka kakaretso.

src: The policy sets norms and standards for government communication practitioners.
tgt: Leano lena le rala mekgwa le maemo bakeng sa basebetsi ba mmuso ba dikgokahano.

src: It also compels all government departments to provide a communication budget and a fully funded personnel capacity.
tgt: Le boela le qobella mafapha ohle a mmuso ho fana ka bajete ya dikgokahano le thupello ya basebetsi e lefelletsweng ka botlalo.

src: The policy will complement the current Code of Conduct for the Public Service.
tgt: Leano lena le tla thusana le Khoutu ya jwale ya Boitshwaro bakeng sa Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba.

src: Cabinet approved the Final Strategy to Addressing Air Pollution in Dense Low-Income Communities of South Africa for implementation.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse hore Lewa la ho Qetela la ho Rarolla Tshilafalo ya Moya Bathong ba fumanang Lekeno le Tlase Aforika Borwa le kenngwe tshebetsong.

src: The strategy provides a coordinated approach in reducing air pollution associated with fossil fuel in dense low-income communities.
tgt: Leano lena le fana ka mokgwa o hlophisitsweng wa ho fokotsa tshilafalo ya moya e amanang le mesi e kunkelang dibakeng tsa batho ba fumanang lekeno le tlase.

src: The current air circulation in these communities exceed the National Ambient Air Quality Standards set out in the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act, 2004 (Act 39 of 2004).
tgt: Moya o fokaelang ha jwale dibakeng tsena, o feta tekanyo ya Maemo a Naha a Boleng ba Moya wa Tikoloho jwalokaha a lekantswe Bolaoding ba Naha ba Tikoloho: Molao wa Boleng ba Moya, 2004 (Molao wa 39 wa 2004).

src: The strategy provides for interventions to reduce pollution and recommends an awareness programmes that will highlight the health impact of continued pollution.
tgt: Lewa lena le fana ka bokenadipakeng ba ho fokotsa tshilafalo le bile le kgothaletsa mananeo a tlhokomediso a tla totobatsa thefuleho ya bophelo bo botle ha tshilafalo e tswelapele.

src: It also provides for alternative energy options.
tgt: Le boela le fana ka mekgwa e meng ya eneji.

src: Cabinet approved the Green Transport Strategy, which will contribute towards reducing the emission of greenhouse gas (GHG) in the environment.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Lewa la Dipalangwang tse sa Senyeng Tikoloho, le tla thusa ho fokotsa ho kunkela ha dikgase tse senyang tikoloho (GHG) hore di se ke tsa ya tikolohong.

src: Currently, the transport sector accounts for 10, 8% of the total GHG emissions, with road transport being responsible for 91.2% of these GHG emissions.
tgt: Ha jwale, lekala la dipalangwang le na le karolo ya 10,8% palong yohle ya di-GHG tse kunkelang, moo dipalangwang tsa mebileng le ikarabelang ka 91,2% ya di-GHG tsena tse kunkelang.

src: The strategy introduces a number of interventions that will provide less emissions.
tgt: Lewa lena le hlahisa mekgwa e mengatanyana ya bokenadipakeng e tla fana ka phokotseho ya ho kunkela.

src: It recommends alternative modes of transportations that emit less GHG in the environment.
tgt: Le kgothaletsa mekgwa e meng esele ya dipalangwang e tla ntsha di-GHG tse fokolang hore di ye tikolohong.

src: The strategy has already gone through public consultations in Cabinet approved submission of the charter establishing the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Aviation Safety Organisation (SASO) to Parliament for approval.
tgt: Lewa lena le se le fetile dipuisanong mmoho le setjhaba ka Kabinete e ananetse ho kenngwa Palamenteng ha tokomane e theang Mokgatlo wa Polokeho ya Bofofisi ba Difofane (SASO) wa Ntshetsopele ya Dinaha tsa Borwa ba Aforika (SADC), bakeng sa ho tjhaellwa monwana.

src: The charter provides a legal and institutional framework to establish SASO, to assist SADC Member States with their civil aviation safety oversight.
tgt: Tokomane ena e fana ka moralo wa molao wa ho thea SASO, ho thusa Dinaha tseo e leng Ditho tsa SADC ka tekolo ya polokeho ya bofofisi ba tsona ba difofane.

src: It will also facilitate the development of efficient and effective civil-aviation infrastructure in SADC Member States.
tgt: E tla boela e nolofatsa kaho e kgabane ya meralo ya motheo ya bofofisi ba difofane Dinaheng tseo e leng Ditho tsa SADKabinete e ananetse Tokomane ya Tataiso ho tsa Bonono, Botjhaba le Letlotlo la botjhaba ya 2018.

src: Cabinet approved the White Paper on Arts, Culture and Heritage of 2018.
tgt: Tokomane ena ya Tataiso e hlakola dikateng tsa Tokomane ya Tataiso ho tsa Bonono, Botjhaba le Letlotlo la botjhaba ya 1996.

src: The White Paper revokes elements of the White Paper on Arts, Culture and Heritage of 1996.
tgt: Tokomane ya Tataiso ena ke sephetho sa tlhophobotjha ya Tokomane ya Tataiso ya 1996, e neng e ananela dikatleho mapatlelong ohle a bonono, botjhaba le letlotlo la botjhaba ebile e lekola dikarolong tse neng di dula e le phephetso ntshetsopeleng ya kaho ya setjhaba le momahanyo ya setjhaba demokerasing ya rona.

src: The White Paper is a culmination of the review of the 1996 White Paper, which appreciated the achievements in all the facets of arts, culture and heritage and reflected on areas that remained a challenge in advancing nation-building and social cohesion in our democracy.
tgt: Tokomane ya Tataiso e hahamalletse ho etsa lekala le tswelang pele, le mahlahahlaha ebile e le le hlabollotsweng la bonono, botjhaba le letlotlo la botjhaba la Aforika Borwa le tla kenya letsoho kahong ya setjhaba, momahanong ya setjhaba esita le ho kenyeletswa ha moruo wa setjhaba.

src: The White Paper aims for a dynamic, vibrant and a transformed South African arts, culture and heritage sector that will contribute towards nation-building, social cohesion and socio-economic inclusion.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Moralo wa Leano la Naha wa Letlotlo la botjhaba ho tsa Botjhaba ba Metsing, o momahanyang Selekane sa Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tse Kopaneng Thutong, Saense le Botjhaba, Molao wa Naha wa Mehlodi ya Letlotlo la botjhaba, 1999 (Molao wa 25 wa 1999) le melao e meng e tshwanelehileng ya naha.

src: Cabinet approved the National Policy Framework on Underwater Cultural Heritage, which synergizes the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation Convention, the National Heritage Resources Act, 1999 (Act 25 of 1999) and other relevant national legislation.
tgt: Leano lena le tsheheditswe ke tumelo ya hore letlotlo la botjhaba ho tsa botjhaba ke la batho bohle ba Aforika Borwa.

src: The policy is underpinned by the principle that cultural heritage belongs to all people of South Africa.
tgt: Le hlwaya lethathama la ba amehang le bobapatsi ba letlotlo la botjhaba ho tsa botjhaba ba metsing, esita le ho etsa tlhokomediso ka bohlokwa ba lona le popo ya bokgoni.

src: Cabinet approved the 2018 and 2019 Annual Stamp Programme from the South African Post Office.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Lenaneo la Selemo le Selemo la Ditempe la 2018 le 2019 la Posong ya Aforika Borwa.

src: The stamps reflect South Africa’s diverse culture, national identity, history, rich heritage, heroes and heroines, the environment as well as socio-economic development.
tgt: Ditempe tsena di bontsha botjhaba bo kopakopaneng ba Aforika Borwa, boitsebahatso ba naha, nalane, letlotlo la botjhaba le manoni, bahale ba batona le ba batshehadi, tikoloho esita le ntshetsopele ya moruo wa setjhaba.

src: The stamps further serve as small ambassadors for South Africa as they travel across the world through the postal network.
tgt: Ditempe tsena di boela di sebetsa e le maqosa a manyenyane a Aforika Borwa kaha di hlwahlwaela lefatshe ka bophara ka marangrang a poso.

src: Cabinet approved the designs of the commemorative collectors’ coin series to be issued in 2019 by the Mint Company.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse meetso ya lethathama la tjhelete ya tshepe ya babokelli ba letlotlo la sehopotso, e tla ntshuwa ka 2019 ke Khamphane e hatisang Tjhelete ya SA Mint.

src: Bills.
tgt: Dibili.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Electoral Laws Amendment Bill of 2018 to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho kenngwa Palamenteng ha Bili ya Sehlomathiso sa Melao ya Dikgetho ya 2018.

src: The Bill amends three pieces of legislation, namely the Electoral Commission Act, 1996 (Act 51 of 1996) Electoral Act, 1998 (Act 73 of 1998) and the Local Government: Municipal Electoral Act, 2000 (Act 27 of 2000).The Bill makes a number of amendments to adjust the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) election processes.
tgt: Bili ena e hlomathisa dikoto tse tharo tsa melao, e leng Molao wa Khomishene ya Dikgetho, 1996 (Molao wa 51 wa 1996) Molao wa Dikgetho, 1998 (Molao wa 73 wa 1998) le Mmuso wa Dibaka: Molao wa Dikgetho tsa Bomasepala, 2000 (Molao wa 27 wa 2000).Bili e etsa dihlomathiso tse ngatanyana ho fetola mesebetsi ya dikgetho ya Khomishene e Ikemetseng ya Dikgetho (IEC).

src: Some of the proposed changes provides that the IEC can use all available sources of data to obtain information necessary to compile and maintain the national common voters’ roll.
tgt: Tse ding tsa diphetoho tse sisintsweng di fana ka hore IEC e ka sebedisa mehlodi yohle e teng ya deitha, ho fumana lesedi le hlokehang la ho hlophisa le ho boloka lenane la naha la bakgethi.

src: It also provides for the prohibition of the use of the name and its acronym, logo designs or material use or owned by the IECabinet approved submission of the Electronic Communications Amendment Bill to Parliament.
tgt: E boela e thibela tshebediso ya lebitso le kgutsufatso ya lona, meetso ya matshwao kapa tshebediso ya dintho tseo e leng tsa IEKabinete e ananetse ho kenngwa Palamenteng ha Bili ya Sehlomathiso sa Dikgokahano tsa Diilektroniki.

src: The Bill amends the Electronic Communication Act, 2005 (Act 36 of 2005) to give effect to the National Integrated ICT Policy White Paper, for the transformation of South Africa into an inclusive, and innovative knowledge and digital society.
tgt: Bili ena e hlomathisa Molao wa Dikgokahano tsa Diilektroniki, 2005 (Molao wa 36 wa 2005) ho fa Tokomane ya Tataiso ya Leano la Naha la ICT e Kopantsweng matla, bakeng sa ho hlabolla Aforika Borwa ho ba setjhaba se kenyeletsang bohle, se nang le tsebo le dijithale tsa maemo a hodimo.

src: It also provides for the transformation of the sector through enforcement of broad-based black economic empowerment.
tgt: E boela e fana ka tlhabollo ya lekala ka ho qobella matlafatso e batsi ya ba batsho moruong.

src: Amongst others, it provides for the lowering of the cost of communications.
tgt: Ho tse ding, e fana ka phokotso ya ditjeo tsa dikgokahano.

src: It also reduces infrastructure duplications and encourages service-based competition through a WOAN service.
tgt: E boela e fokotsa phetapheto ya meralo ya motheo ebile e kgothaletsa qothisano ya lehlokwa ya ditshebeletso, ka tshebeletso ya WOAKabinete e ananetse phatlalatso ya Bili ya Sehlomathiso sa Merero ya tsa Ditjhelete bakeng sa hore setjhaba se tshwaele.

src: Cabinet approved for the publication of the Financial Matters Amendment Bill of 2018 for public comment.
tgt: Dihlomathiso di dikotong tse hlano tsa melao:Molao wa Putlamo ya Kgwebo wa 1963, ho matlafatsa taolo ya dikonteraka tseo ho utlwanweng ka tsona, ho ya ka boitlamo ba G20 Molao wa Dipenshene tsa Masole wa 1976, ho rarolla karolo ya kgethollo le ho netefatsa bosiyo ba tshekamelo ya bong, e le ho amohela mefuta e fapaneng ya dikamanoMolao wa Dibanka wa 1990, ho dumella dikhamphane tseo e leng tsa mmuso tse tshwanelehileng ho etsa kopo ya dilaesense tsa dibanka, haeba ba Phethahatso ba ananelaMolao wa Dipenshene tsa Basebetsi ba Mmuso wa 1996, ho fetola mokgwa wa ditefo tlhalanong, ho netefatswe hore ditefo tsa penshene ya ditho ho balekane ba mehleng ha di fetolwe ho ba sekoloto leMolao wa Porofeshene ya Bohlahlobi ba Dibuka wa 2005, ho rarolla diphephetso le dithibelo tseo Boto e Ikemetseng ya Taolo ya Bahlahlobi ba Dibuka e tobaneng le tsona ha e etsa mesebetsi ya yona ya taolo le tekolo.

src: The amendments are in five pieces of legislations:The Insolvency Act of 1963, to strengthen the regulation of over-the-counter derivative market, in line with G20 commitmentsThe Military Pensions Act of 1976, to address discriminatory provision and ensure gender neutrality to recognise different types of relationshipsThe Banks Act of 1990, to allow for qualifying state-owned companies to apply for banking licences, subject to Executive approvalThe Government Employment Pension Law of 1996, to change the clean break principle in the case of divorce, ensuring that members’ pension pay outs to former spouses on divorce are not converted to a debt obligation andThe Auditing Profssion Act of 2005, to address challenges and limitations that the Independent Regulatory Board for Auditors faces in discharging its regulatory and oversight responsibilities.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho kenngwa ha Bili ya Kgalemo Sesoleng ya 2018 Palamenteng.

src: It addresses the administration of military judicial system, creation and appointment of military police services, and disciplinary hearings.
tgt: E lokisa tsamaiso ya mokgwatsamaiso wa boahlodi ba sesoleng, ho thea le ho thonngwa ha ditshebeletso tsa sepolesa sa sesole, le ho mamelwa ha dikgalemo.

src: The Bill will repeal the current Military Discipline Supplementary Measures Act, 1999 (Act 16 of 1999).
tgt: Bili ena e tla hlakola Molao wa jwale wa Dikgato tsa Tlatsetso tsa Kgalemo ya Sesoleng, 1999 (Molao wa 16 wa 1999).

src: This Bill will align SANDF Military Discipline to the UN, especially on soldiers in peacekeeping missions.
tgt: Bili e tla amanya Kgalemo ya Sesoleng ya SANDF ho ya UN, haholoholo masoleng a dithomong tsa ho boloka kgotso.

src: Cabinet approved publication of the Companies Amendment Bill of 2018 in the Government Gazette for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho phatlalatswa ha Bili ya Sehlomathiso sa Dikhamphane ya 2018 Koranteng ya Mmuso, hore setjhaba se tshwaele.

src: The Bill amends the Companies Act, 2008 (Act 71 of 2008).
tgt: Bili e hlomathisa Molao wa Dikhamphane, 2008 (Molao wa 71 wa 2008).

src: It reduces the regulatory and administrative burdens to business owners and enhances South Africa’s attractiveness to potential investors.
tgt: E fokotsa merwalo ya taolo le tsamaiso ho beng ba dikgwebo ebile e ntlafatsa kgohedi ya Aforika Borwa ho batsetedi ba nang le tjheseho ya ho tsetela naheng ena.

src: Upcoming Events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: Tourism Month in September was launched on 16 August 2018 in Tsitsikamma in the Eastern Cape, under the theme: “Tourism and the digital transformation”, which mirrors the theme of the UN World Tourism Organisation World Tourism Day taking place on 27 September 2018.According to the World Travel and Tourism Council report released in November 2016, tourism employs 1.55 million people directly and indirectly in South Africa, and its direct contribution to the gross domestic product is R118 billion.
tgt: Kgwedi ya Bohahlaudi ya Lwetse e kgakotswe ka la 16 Phato 2018 Tsitsikama Kapa Botjhabela, katlasa mokotaba o reng: “Bohahlaudi le tlhabollo ya dijithale”, o bontshang mokotaba wa Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Bohahlaudi wa UN le Letsatsi la Lefatshe la Bohahlaudi le tla ba ka la 27 Lwetse 2018.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to support this vital sector of the economy.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa ohle ho tshehetsa lekala lena la bohlokwa la moruo.

src: It is also important that we work towards a more inclusive tourism sector that unlocks entrepreneurship, economic opportunities and jobs in our communities.
tgt: Ho boetse ho bohlokwa hore re sebeletse ho ba le lekala la bohahlaudi le kenyeletsang bohle le bile le utolla bohwebi, menyetla ya moruo le mesebetsi setjhabeng sa habo rona.

src: Cabinet approved the 2018 Public Service Month Programme under the theme: “Thuma Mina: Taking Public Service to the People: Batho Pele: “We Belong, We Care and We Serve”.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Lenaneo la 2018 la Kgwedi ya Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba katlasa mokotaba o reng: “Thuma Mina: Re isa Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba Bathong: Batho Pele: “Re ba lona, Re a Tsotella ebile Re a le Sebeletsa”.

src: The full-month programme of activities will be made available through the government website (WEBTOKEN).
tgt: Lenaneo la diketsahalo tsa kgwedi kaofela le tla fumantshwa ka websaete ya mmuso (WEBTOKEN).

src: SAPS National Commemoration Day on 2 September 2018, with commemoration activities commencing from 31 August.
tgt: Letsatsi la naha la Sehopotso la SAPS ka la 2 Lwetse 2018, ka diketsahalo tsa sehopotso tse qalang ho tloha ka la 31 Phato 2018.

src: This is in memory of police officials and reservists who were killed in the line of duty, having paid the highest price in service of the nation.
tgt: Sena se etsetswa ho hopola bahlanka ba sepolesa le marisefe ba ileng ba bolawa ba le mosebetsing, kaha ba intshitse sehlabelo ho sebeletseng setjhaba.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to recognise and celebrate the lives of these heroes and heroines who died in the line of duty.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa ohle ho ananela le ho keteka maphelo a bahale bana ba shweleng ba le mosebetsing.

src: It calls on all communities across the country to fly the flag at half-mast, and to observe a moment of silence in all religious ceremonies during the period 31 August to 2 September 2018, as a symbol of support to the SAPSouth Africa will host the International Conference on Science, Technology, Engineering and Management, organised by the Research World, from 24 to 25 August 2018 in Cape Town.
tgt: E etsa kgoeletso mafapheng a mmuso ho pharalla le naha ho theolela difolakga halofong, esita le ho ba le motsotso wa kgutso meketjaneng yohle ya bodumedi nakong ya la 31 Phato ho ya ho la 2 Lwetse 2018, e le letshwao la tshehetso ho SAPAforika Borwa e tla tshwara Seboka sa Matjhaba ho Saense, Thekenoloji, Injiniereng le Bolaodi, e hlophisitsweng ke Bofuputsi ba Lefatshe, ho tloha ka la 24 ho ya ho la 25 Phato 2018 Motse Kapa.

src: The conference, which will provide opportunities for participants to share their ideas and experiences with a global audience, reaffirms that South Africa is a premier destination for global events.
tgt: Seboka sena, se tla fana ka menyetla ho ba nkang seabo hore ba thakelane tsebo le malebela le batho ba lefatshe lohle, se boela se netefatsa hore Aforika Borwa ke sebaka se seholo seo ho tshwarelwang diketsahalo tsa matjhaba ho sona.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to participate in activities to celebrate Heritage Month in September.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa ohle ho ba le seabo diketsahalong tsa ho keteka Kgwedi ya Letlotlo la Botjhaba ka Lwetse.

src: Heritage Month is observed annually to encourage the public to celebrate their unity in diversity and to continue to build a country where its people care for each other and respect one another.
tgt: Kgwedi ya Letlotlo la Botjhaba e nkelwa hloohong selemo le selemo, ho kgothaletsa setjhaba ho keteka kopano ya sona ka ho se tshwane ha sona esita le ho tswela pele ho aha naha eo batho ba yona ba tsotellanang ba bile ba hlomphana.

src: Messages.
tgt: Melaetsa.

src: Nominations for National OrdersCabinet reiterates President Ramaphosa’s invitation to members of the public to nominate citizens and eminent foreign nationals that they believe deserve to receive the country’s highest honours, the National Orders.
tgt: Dithonyo bakeng sa Ditlokola tsa NahaKabinete e thasisetsa memo ya Moporesidente Ramaphosa ho ditho tsa setjhaba hore di thonye baahi le melata e ipabotseng, bao ba nahanang hore ba lokela ho amohela ditlotla tse hodimodimo tsa naha, Ditlokola tsa Naha.

src: The deadline for nominations is 7 September EidCabinet conveyed best wishes to the Muslim community in South Africa and around the world on the celebration of Eid-ul-Adha yesterday, Wednesday 22 August 2018.
tgt: Letsatsi la ho qetela la dithonyo ke mohla la 7 Lwetse EidKabinete e fetisitse molaetsa wa mahlohonolo ho setjhaba sa Mamoseleme Aforika Borwa le lefatshe ka bophara ha se ne se keteka Eid-ul-Adha maobane, ka Laboraro mohla la 22 Phato 2018.

src: More than 2 500 Muslims from South Africa have travelled to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to join an estimated two million Muslims from around the world for the Hajj pilgrimage.
tgt: Mamoseleme a kahodimo ho 2 500 a tswang Aforika Borwa a etetse Saudi Arabia ho ya ikamahanya le Masolomane a lekanyetswang ho dimilione tse pedi a tswang lefatsheng lohle bakeng sa leeto le halalelang la Hajj.

src: Cabinet joins President Ramaphosa in expressing condolences to the family and friends of Mama Zondeni Sobukwe, who was affectionately known as “Mother of Azania”.
tgt: Kabinete e ikamahanya le Moporesidente Ramaphosa ho fetiseng matshediso ho lelapa le metswalle ya Mme Zondeni Sobukwe, ya neng a tsejwa ka hore ke “Mme wa Azania”.

src: President Ramaphosa has declared a Special Official Funeral Category 2 for her.
tgt: Moporesidente Ramaphosa o tsebahaditse hore o tla tlotlwa ka Lepato le Kgethehileng la Semmuso la Mokgahlelo wa E ne e le mohale wa ntwa ya kgano ebile e le molwanedi wa tokoloho ya maAforika Borwa ohle, ya ileng a tswela pele ka bolwanedi ba hae ho fihlela nakong ya demokerasi.

src: She was a heroine of resistance and a fighter for the freedom of all South Africans, who continued her activism into our democratic dispensation.
tgt: Mohla la 28 Mmesa 2018 – ebile e le katoloso ya meketjana ya Letsatsi la Tokoloho – Moporesidente Ramaphosa o ile a rwesa Mme Sobukwe Tlokola ya Naha ya Luthuli ya Silifera.

src: On 28 April 2018 – and as an extension of Freedom Day celebrations – President Ramaphosa bestowed the National Order of Luthuli in Silver on Mama Sobukwe.
tgt: E ne e boetse e le mofumahadi wa Moporesidente wa Pan Africanist Congress (PAC) Robert Mangaliso Sobukwe.

src: She was also the wife of Pan Africanist Congress founding President Robert Mangaliso Sobukwe.
tgt: Selemo sa 2018 se boela se tshwaya sehopotso sa bo40 sa lefu la Monghadi Sobukwe.

src: Mama Sobukwe will be laid to rest on Saturday, 25 August 2018, at the Kroonvale Cemetery in Graaff-Reinet in the Eastern Cape.
tgt: Mme Sobukwe o tla bolokwa ka Moqebelo, mohla la 25 Phato 2018, Setsheng sa Bafu sa Kroonvale Graaff-Reinet Kapa Botjhabela.

src: Cabinet also joins President Ramaphosa in expressing condolences on the passing of His Excellency Kofi Atta Annan, former UN Secretary-General (UNSG).
tgt: Kabinete e boela e ikamahanya le Moporesidente Ramaphosa ho fetiseng matshediso ka ho hlokahala ha Mobabatsehi Kofi Atta Annan, Mongodi Kakaretso wa mehleng wa UN (UNSG).

src: Mr Annan was the first black African to become UNSG and he used his position to advance the African agenda.
tgt: Monghadi Annan e bile motho e motsho wa pele ho ba UNSG mme a sebedisa setulo sa hae ho ntshetsapele mananeo a Aforika.

src: His death is a great loss to the global community.
tgt: Lefu la hae ke tahlehelo e kgolo lefatsheng lohle.

src: Cabinet also expresses its condolences on the passing of world-renowned singer and United States civil-rights activist, Aretha Franklin.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e fetisa matshediso ka ho hlokahala ha sebini se tswileng matsoho lefatsheng ebile e le molwanedi wa ditokelo tsa setjhaba Amerika, Aretha Franklin.

src: Cabinet joins the international community in sending condolences to the Italian Government and people, and the families of the victims, following the collapse of the Morandi motorway bridge in the north-western Italian city of Genoa.
tgt: Kabinete e ikamahanya le batho ba matjhaba ho romeleng matshediso Mmusong le bathong ba Italy, le malapa a mahlatsipa, kamora ho wa ha borokgo ba makoloi ba Morandi ka leboya bophirimela ho motse wa Italy wa Genoa.

src: Cabinet also wishes the injured a speedy recovery.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e lakaletsa ba lemetseng hore ba fole ka potlako.

src: Cabinet expresses its condolences to the family and friends of world-renowned political economist and African academic Samir Amin, who passed away on 12 August at the age of Throughout his life he was a tireless advocate for Third World liberation, and his thinking transformed the way we understand capitalism and imperialism.6 Cabinet also conveys its condolences to the government and the people of India on the loss of lives during the recent floods and landslides in the state of Kerala.7 Condolences were also sent to the government and people of Sudan following the drowning of 24 school children in the Nile River.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisa matshediso ho lelapa le metswalle ya radipolotiki ya tummeng lefatsheng ho tsa moruo ebile e le morutehi wa Aforika, Samir Amin, ya hlokahetseng mohla la 12 Phato 2018 a na le dilemo tse Nakong ya bophelo bohle ba hae e ne e le molwanedi ya matla wa tokoloho ya Dinaha tse Thuthuang, mme maikutlo a hae a fetotse mokgwa oo re utlwisisang bokapitale le boimpheriale ka teng.6 Kabinete e boela e fetisetsa matshediso a yona ho mmuso le batho ba India ka tahlehelo ya maphelo nakong ya dikgohola tsa moraorao le ho ritsa ha seretse tikolohong ya Kerala.

src: AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: DithonyoDithonyo kaofela di lokela ho netefatswa ka mangolo a thuto le tumello e amehang.

src: Ms Deshni Subbiah as Director to the Board of the Export Credit Insurance Corporation of South Africa SOC Limited.
tgt: Mofumahadi Deshni Subbiah e le Molaodi Botong ya Koporasi ya Inshorense ya Sekoloto sa Diyantle ya Aforika Borwa SOC Limited.

src: Ms Thezi Rosemary Mabuza, reappointed as Deputy Commissioner of the National Consumer Commission.
tgt: Mofumahadi Thezi Rosemary Mabuza, o thontswe botjha e le Motlatsi wa Mokhomishinara wa Khomishene ya Naha tsa Bareki.

src: Non-executive directors on the Land and Agricultural Development Bank Board of Directors:Adv Sandra Coetzee (reappointment) andMs Mathane Eveline Makgatho (reappointment).
tgt: Balaodi bao e seng ba phethahatso ba Boto ya Balaodi ba Banka ya Ntshetsopele ya Mobu le Temo:Moadvokheiti Sanngakaa Coetzee (thonyobotjha) leMofumahadi Mathane Eveline Makgatho (thonyobotjha).

src: Non-executive directors to the Board of the Airports Company South Africa:Dr Nolulamo Nobambiswano Gwangwa (Chairperson)Ms Phydelis Ntombifuthi MvelaseMr Yershen PillayMr Bonang Francis MohaleMr Pascalis Mathealira MokupoMs Nosizwe Nokwe-Macamo andMr Nqobizitha Irvin Phenyane.
tgt: Balaodi bao e seng ba phethahatso ba Boto ya Khamphane ya Baemafofane ba Aforika Borwa:Ngaka Nolulamo Nobambiswano Gwangwa (Modulasetulo)Mofumahadi Phydelis Ntombifuthi MvelaseMonghadi Yershen PillayMonghadi Bonang Francis MohaleMonghadi Pascalis Mathealira MokupoMofumahadi Nosizwe Nokwe-Macamo leMonghadi Nqobizitha Irvin Phenyane.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 5 September 2018 at Tuynhuys, Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya kopanela Tuynhuys Motse Kapa, ka Laboraro, mohla la 5 Loetse 2018.Dintlha tsa Ha jwale.

src: Economy.
tgt: Moruo.

src: Cabinet calls on all sectors of South Africa to rally behind government-led initiatives to boost economic growth following the release of growth figures showing our economy contracted by zero point 7 per cent in the second quarter from a revised -2.6 percent in the first quarter.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa makaleng ohle a Aforika Borwa hore a tshehetse dikgato tse etelletsweng pele ke mmuso ho matlafatsa kgolo ya moruo, kamora ho ntshuwa ha dipalopalo tsa kgolo tse bontshang hore moruo wa rona o nyotobetse ka 0.7% sehleng sa bobedi, ho tloha ho -2.6% e neng e hlophisitswe botjha sehleng sa pele.

src: Although some sectors of the economy, such as mining, construction and finance, recorded an improvement in growth, this was insufficient to offset fully the contraction in other sectors, in particular the agricultural sector.
tgt: Leha makala a mang a moruo a kang merafo, dikonteraka le tsa ditjhelete a bile le dintlafalo kgolong, empa e ne e sa lekana ho akaretsa ka phethahalo nyotobelo e makaleng a mang, haholoholo lekaleng la temothuo.

src: From the expenditure side, net exports recorded a strong recovery, however this was offset by a contraction in household expenditure and very large draw down in inventories.
tgt: Ka lehlakoreng la ditjeo, diyantle tsohle di bile le tsosoloso e matla, leha ho le jwalo sena se ile sa sithabetswa ke ho nyotobela ha ditjeo tsa malapeng esita le ho hula ka falese ha ditlhahiso.

src: Investment growth by private companies increased, while investment by the public sector contracted.
tgt: Kgolo ya botsetedi e eketsehile dikhamphaneng tsa poraefete, ha botsetedi ba lekala la setjhaba bona bo nyotobetse.

src: The rising volatility in global markets and the GDP outcome require that government accelerates efforts to unblock constraints to economic growth while providing support to vulnerable groups.
tgt: Tlhokeho ya botsitso e ntseng e hola mebarakeng ya lefatshe le sephetho sa GDP, di hloka hore mmuso o akofise matsapa a ho ribolla ditshita tsa kgolo ya moruo ha o ntse o fana ka tshehetso dihlopheng tse tlokotsing.

src: Economic growth has slowed down significantly over the last four years.
tgt: Kgolo ya moruo e ile ya sisitheha ka matla nakong ya dilemo tse nne tse fetileng.

src: This reflects factors such as drought conditions in the agricultural sector and low commodity prices but also domestic structural constraints, which have discouraged investment and employment creation.
tgt: Sena se bontsha dintlha tse kang maemo a komello lekaleng la temothuo esita le ditheko tse tlase tsa dihlahiswa empa e boela e ba ditshita tsa sebopeho sa kwano lapeng, tse nyahamisitseng botsetedi le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi.

src: Government has committed, to amongst others, a complete overhaul of the visa system to support the tourism sector, the finalisation of key mining legislation to support the mining sector and further stabilise the finances of State-owned enterprises.
tgt: Mmuso o se o ikitlaeditse, ho tse ding, ka tlhophobotjha e phethahetseng ya tsamaiso ya visa e le ho tshehetsa lekala la bohahlaudi, ho phethelwa ha melao ya bohlokwa ya merafo ho tshehetsa lekala la merafo esita le ho tswelapele ka ho tsitsisa tsa ditjhelete tsa dikgwebo tsa mmuso.

src: The upcoming job and investment summits, as well as the proposed government stimulus package, will provide details on reforms needed to drive growth.
tgt: Diboka tse tlang tsa tlhahiso ya mesebetsi le botsetedi, esita le pakana ya ditsiane tsa mmuso tse sisintsweng, di tla fana ka dintlha tse tebileng ka ditlhabollo tse hlokehang tsa ho ntshetsa kgolo pele.

src: Cabinet affirms government’s commitment to fiscal sustainability and a revised fiscal framework will be presented in the Medium Term Budget Policy Statement.
tgt: Kabinete e tiisa boikitlaetso ba mmuso boitjarong ba nako e telele ba tsa ditjhelete mme moralo wa tsa ditjhelete o hlophilweng botjha o tla tekwa Polelong ya Leano la Ditekanyetso tsa Ditjhelete tsa Nako e Bohareng (MTBPS).

src: United Kingdom (UK) and Northern Ireland visit.
tgt: Ketelo ya United Kingdom (UK) le Northern Ireland.

src: Cabinet joins President Cyril Ramaphosa in welcoming the successful working visit by Prime Minister Theresa May of the UK of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
tgt: Kabinete e ikamahanya le Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa ho amoheleng ketelo e atlehileng ya tshebetso ka Tonakgolo Theresa May wa UK ya Great Brithane le Northern Ireland.

src: It will yield improved benefits for South Africa through strengthened bilateral trade and investment.
tgt: E tla tlisetsa Aforika Borwa melemo e ntlafetseng ya ho matlafatsa kgwebisano le botsetedi ba dinaha tse pedi.

src: The UK is one of the largest foreign investors in South Africa, with over 650 British firms present in our market.
tgt: UK ke enngwe ya batsetedi ba baholo ba Aforika Borwa, ka difeme tsa Brithane tse kahodimo ho 650 tse teng mebarakeng ya rona.

src: During the bilateral engagements, potential partnerships and efforts were discussed.
tgt: Nakong ya ho dula majwana ha dinaha tse pedi tsena, ho ile ha tshohlwa tsa kgonahalo ya bolekane le makgobonthithi a ka etswang.

src: Prime Minister May also handed over the SS Mendi Bell to South Africa’s Commander-in-Chief, President Ramaphosa, and the people of South Africa, to commemorate the sacrifice of over 600 South Africans who perished when the SS Mendi sank in the English Channel over 100 years ago.
tgt: Tonakgolo May o ile a boela a neelana ka SS Mendi Bell ho Molaodi e Moholo wa Lebotho, Moporesidente Ramaphosa, le batho ba Aforika Borwa, ho hopola bointshasehlabelo hwa maAforika Borwa a kahodimo ho 600 a ileng a timela ha SS Mendi e ne e teba Kanaleng ya Manyesemane, dilemong tse kahodimo ho 100 tse fetileng.

src: Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) Summit.
tgt: Seboka sa Foramo ya Tshebedisanommoho ya China le Aforika (FOCAC).

src: Cabinet considered the Beijing Action Plan (2019-2021), which details the outcomes of the FOCAC Summit co-chaired by President Ramaphosa and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
tgt: Kabinete e o nketse hloohong Morero wa Tshebetso wa Beijing (2019-2021), o thathamisang diphetoho tsa Seboka sa FOCAC moo Moporesidente Ramaphosa e leng e mong wa badulasetulo hammoho le Moporesidente wa China Xi Jinping.

src: To build the China-Africa comprehensive strategic and cooperative partnership, China committed to implementing 10 cooperation plans with Africa.
tgt: E le ho aha lewa le phethahetseng le selekane sa tshebedisanommoho tsa China-Aforika, China e ikitlaeditse ho kenya tshebetsong merero e 10 ya tshebedisanommoho le Aforika.

src: These are in the areas of industrialisation agricultural modernisation infrastructure financial services green development trade and investment facilitation poverty reduction and public welfare public health people-to-people exchanges, and peace and security.
tgt: Tsena ke dibaka tseo ho tsona ho etswang diindasteri temothuo ya sejwalejwale meralo ya motheo ditshebeletso tsa ditjhelete ntshetsopele e sa senyeng tikoloho tlhophiso ya kgwebisano le matsete phokotso ya bofuma le thekolohelo ya setjhaba bophelo bo botle ba setjhaba diphapanyetsano tsa batho le batho ba bang esita le kgotso le tshireletso.

src: Over the period, cooperation between the two sides will be underpinned by the theme: “China and Africa: Towards an even stronger community with a shared future through win-win cooperation.”4.
tgt: Kgabareng, tshebedisanommoho dipakeng tsa mahlakore a mabedi ana di tla tiiswa ke mokotaba o reng: “China le Aforika: Ho hahamalla popong ya setjhaba se matla le ho feta se nang le bokamoso boo ho tla abelanwa ka bona, ka tshebedisanommoho eo ho yona e mong le e mong e bang mohlodi.”4.

src: Fuel price.
tgt: Theko ya mafura.

src: Cabinet welcomes the unchanged fuel price for this month as a once-off temporary relief for users of public transport, motorists and consumers, while other measures are being sought by the Department of Energy (DoE).
tgt: Kabinete e amohela taba ya theko ya mafura e sa fetolwang kgweding ena e le kimollo ya nakwana ya hang feela bakeng sa basebedisi ba dipalangwang tsa setjhaba, boramakoloi le bareki, ha ho ntse ho tsongwa mekgwa e meng ke Lefapha la Eneji (DoE).

src: Global factors including the increase of the price of crude oil and the negative sentiment around emerging markets have led to the cost of fuel rising rapidly in South Africa since April this year.
tgt: Mabaka a mang a amang lefatshe lohle a akgang nyollo ya theko ya oli e tala le maikutlo a mabe a mabapi le mebaraka e thuthuang, di bakile hore ditjeo tsa mafura di nyolohe ka potlako Aforika Borwa haesale ho tloha ka Mmesa monongwaha.

src: Cabinet has expressed concern about increases and the detrimental effects on the general consumer, including amongst others, effects relating to the inflationary impact as producers pass on the increases to the retail sector.
tgt: Kabinete e hlahisitse ngongoreho ka dinyollo le ditlamorao tse babang ho bareki ka kakaretso, ho akga le ditlamorao tse amanang le sekgahla sa nyollo ya ditheko ka ha bahlahisi ba fetisetsa dinyollo lekaleng la barekisetsi.

src: Taking this into account, the Minister of Energy, Mr Jeff Radebe, made a special intervention on behalf of government to cushion the public against yet another steep increase in the fuel price, with the exception of the cents per litre increase in the retail margin of petrol to cater for the annual salary increases of employees, such as petrol attendants, at fuel stations.
tgt: Ha a ne a nkela sena hloohong, Letona la Eneji, Monghadi Jeff Radebe, o entse bokenadipakeng bo kgethehileng lebitsong la mmuso ka ho inola setjhaba kgahlanong le ho hlwa mekwalaba ho hong hape thekong ya mafura, ntle le nyollo ya disente tse lithara kanngwe sekepeleng sa Thekiso ya peterole ho lokisetsa nyollo ya meputso ya selemo le selemo ya basebetsi, ba kang ba tshelang peterole diteisheneng tsa mafura.

src: At a time when the economy is being impacted by global headwinds, Cabinet is pleased that this intervention has no impact on the fiscus as it uses funds that are already in the fuel-pricing structure.
tgt: Nakong ena eo moruo o thefulwang ke difefo tsa lefatshe lohle, Kabinete e motlotlo ka hore bokenadipakeng bona ha bo ame pokello ya ditjhelete tsa setjhaba ka ha bo sebedisa ditjhelete tse seng di le morerong wa theko ya mafura.

src: Land reform Cabinet calls on all South Africans to use the debate around the issue of land reform to strengthen nation-building and social cohesion.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho maAforika Borwa ohle hore a sebedise ngangisano e amanang le tlhabollo ya mobu, ho matlafatsa kaho ya setjhaba esita le momahanyo ya setjhaba.

src: The unfolding parliamentary process will bring clarity and allow us to move forward as a nation.
tgt: Mesebetsi e ntseng e tswelapele ya palamente e tla tlisa tlhakisetso ebe e re dumelle ho hatela pele re le setjhaba.

src: The transparent, rules-based and constitutional process is in keeping with our commitment to jointly arrive at solutions for the betterment of society.
tgt: Mosebetsi o nang le ponaletso, o theilweng ka melawana le molaotheo o tsamaisana le boikitlaetso ba rona ba hore re le mmoho re fihlelle ditharollo molemong wa ntlafatso ya setjhaba.

src: Cabinet is convinced this process will allow us to determine a land reform model that works for everyone.
tgt: Kabinete e kgodisehile hore mosebetsi ona o tla re dumella ho utolla mokgwa wa tlhabollo ya mobu o sebeletseng bohle.

src: By working together, we can build a better nation where the dreams and aspirations of all our people are realised.
tgt: Ka ho sebetsa mmoho, re ka aha setjhaba se betere moo ditoro le ditabatabelo tsa batho bohle ba habo rona di tla fihlellwa.

src: Water.
tgt: Metsi.

src: Cabinet is pleased that the Department of Water and Sanitation has completed the construction of the Cornelis River Dam in the Free State.
tgt: Kabinete e kgotsofetse ka hore Lefapha la Metsi le Bohlweki le phethetse kaho ya Letamo la Nokeng ya Cornelis Freistata.

src: The dam, which is set to benefit 2 690 households and an estimated 10 674 people, will ease water challenges faced by the community of Warden and Ezenzeleni under the Phumelela Local Municipality.
tgt: Letamo lena, le reretsweng ho thusa malapa a 2 690 le batho ba hakanyetswang ho 10 674, le tla bebofatsa diphephetso tsa metsi tseo setjhaba sa Warden le Ezenzeleni se tobaneng le tsona katlasa Masepala wa Sebaka wa Phumelela.

src: South Africa is still experiencing water shortages as a result of drought conditions and Cabinet appeals to all people to use this resource sparingly and to remain water wise.
tgt: Aforika Borwa e ntse e na le dikgaello tsa metsi ka lebaka la maemo a komello, mme Kabinete e ipiletsa bathong bohle hore ba sebedise sesebediswa sena ka paballo ba be ba dule ba le sedi ka metsi.

src: Education.
tgt: Thuto.

src: Cabinet congratulated the Department of Basic Education for successfully handing over the Delft South Primary School, outside Cape Town in the Western Cape.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholeditse Lefapha la Thuto ya Motheo (DBE) ka ho neelana ka katleho ka Sekolo sa Poraemare sa Delft South, ka thoko ho Motse Kapa profenseng ya Kapa Bophirimela.

src: The school was built through the department’s Accelerated Schools Infrastructure Delivery Initiative (ASIDI) at a cost of R75 million.
tgt: Sekolo sena se ahilwe ka thuso ya Kgato e Potlakisitsweng ya Phano ya Meralo ya Motheo ya Dikolo (ASIDI) ka ditjeo tsa R75 milione.

src: It consists of 45 classrooms, a computer and science laboratory, library as well as a nutrition centre.
tgt: Se na le diphaposi tsa ho rutela tse 45, laboratori ya dikhomphyutha le saense, polokelo ya dibuka esita le setsi seo ho jellwang ho sona.

src: The new state-of-the-art facilities will provide a conducive learning and teaching environment to about 1 578 learners from the Delft community.
tgt: Sekolo sena se setjha sa maemo a hodimo se tla fana ka tikoloho e ntle ya ho ruta le ho ithuta baithuting ba ka bang 1 578 ba sebakeng sa Delft.

src: This is the final school out of 25 schools handed over to the Western Cape through the National Department of Education’s initiative.
tgt: Sena ke sekolo sa ho qetela dikolong tse 25 tse neelanweng Kapa Bophirimela ka kgato ya DBHo fihlela kajeno, lenaneo la ASIDI le ahile dikolo tsa maemo a hodimo tse 205 naha ka bophara.

src: A total of 685 schools have been provided with reliable water supply, some 486 schools have been provided with decent sanitation facilities and 372 schools have been connected to the electricity grid for the first time.
tgt: Palo yohle ya dikolo tse 685 di se di filwe phepelo e tshepahetseng ya metsi, dikolo tse ding tse 486 di filwe disebediswa tse ntle tsa bohlweki athe dikolo tse 372 di hoketswe marangranng a motlakase lekgetlo la pele.

src: 2019 National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS) applications.
tgt: Dikopo tsa 2019 tsa Sekema sa Naha sa Thuso ya Ditjhelete ho Baithuti (NSFAS).

src: Cabinet welcomed the overwhelming response from prospective students following the official opening of the 2019 NSFAS application process on 03 September.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho tla ka bongata ha baithuti ba tshwanelehileng kamora ho bulwa semmuso ha mosebetsi wa dikopo tsa 2019 tsa NSFAS ka la 3 Loetse.

src: Over 45 000 potential and current students logged onto the NSFAS website on the first day.
tgt: Ke baithuti ba tshwanelehileng le ba ha jwale ba kahodimo ho 45 000 ba keneng websaeteng ya NSFAS ka letsatsi la pele.

src: Progress has also been made to clear the backlog of outstanding payments to students.
tgt: Kgatelopele ya ho fedisa tshallomorao ya ditefo tsa ditjhelete tsa baithuti e se e entswe.

src: The application process is based on a new system which makes funding decisions quicker while applications are now easily filled in by students regardless of their location.
tgt: Mosebetsi wa dikopo o tsepamisitswe mokgwatsamaisong o motjha o potlakisang diqeto tsa ho fana ka tjhelete ka ha diforomo tsa dikopo jwale di tlatswa habobebe ke baithuti, ho sa natsehe hore na ba dula hokae.

src: Listeriosis.
tgt: Listeriosis.

src: Cabinet welcomes the declaration that the Listeriosis outbreak is over and it strongly demonstrates the impact of the emergency collaborative response plan by the Department of Health (DoH) and the National Institute for Communicable Diseases, supported by the World Health Organisation, to control and end the outbreak.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela tsebiso ya hore sewa sa Listeriosis se fedile ebile e bontsha ka matla sekgahla sa morero wa karabelo o kopanetsweng wa tshohanyetso wa Lefapha la Bophelo bo Botle (DoH) le Setheo sa Naha sa Mafu a Tshwaetsang, ba tsheheditswe ke Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Bophelo bo Botle, ho laola le ho fedisa sewa sena.

src: The DoH has put in place a surveillance system to prevent a recurrence.
tgt: DoH e beile mokgwa wa bodisa ba ho thibela hore e se ke ya ropoha hape.

src: All factories that make ready-to-eat processed meat and chicken need to have food safety management systems in place, according to Regulation R607 published on 14 June 2018.
tgt: Difeme tsohle tse hlahisang dinama tse seng di loketse ho jewa, di tshwanela ho ba le mekgwatsamaiso ya taolo ya polokeho ya dijo, ho ya ka Molawana wa R607 o phatlaladitsweng ka la 14 Phupjane 2018.

src: Inspections of factories remain ongoing, according to the updated hygiene regulations.
tgt: Ditlhahlobo tsa difeme di dula di ntse di tswelapele, ho ya ka melawana e ntjhafaditsweng ya tlhweko.

src: Allegations of fake and expired foods.
tgt: Diqoso tsa dijo mmotwana le tse felletsweng ke nako.

src: Cabinet commends the swift action taken by the Minister of Health, Dr Aaron Motsoaledi, to look into the allegations of fake and expired foods in South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa kgato e potlakileng e nkilweng ke Letona la Bophelo bo Botle, Ngaka Aaron Motsoaledi, ho shebisisa diqoso tsa dijo mmotwana le dijo tse felletsweng ke nako Aforika Borwa.

src: The DoH has received a high volume of complaints and noted concerns about unauthenticated food-related videos that are circulating on social media.
tgt: DoH e fumane lenane le hodimo haholo la ditletlebo yaba ya lemoha le dingongoreho ka dividiyo tse sa netefatswang tse amanang le dijo, tse ntseng di potoloha marangrang a dikgokahano tsa setjhaba.

src: Since August, inspection blitzes have taken place at various food premises and they continue in different parts of the country.
tgt: Haesale ho tloha ka Phato, ditlhaselo tsa bohlahlobi di entswe ditsheng tse fapaneng tsa tlhahiso ya dijo, ebile di ntse di tswelapele dibakeng tse fapaneng tsa naha.

src: In addition, the food industry has been requested to confirm the authenticity of potential counterfeit foodstuffs while other government regulatory authorities from the departments of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, and Trade and Industry, including the National Consumer Commission, are involved in confirming public claims of compromised quality standards.
tgt: Ho feta moo, indasteri ya dijo e kopilwe ho netefatsa bonnete ba kgonahalo ya dihlahiswa tsa bolotsana tsa dijo, ha makgotla a mang a taolo a mmuso ho tloha ho Mafapha a Temothuo, Meru le Botshwasi ba Ditlhapi, le Kgwebisano le Indasteri, ho akga le Khomishene ya Naha ya tsa Boreki (NCC), a se a le kgabong ya ho netefatsa dipelaelo tsa setjhaba tsa maemo a sa natsweng a boleng.

src: Cabinet appeals to the public to be vigilant in differentiating terms related to food:The best-before date refers to the long shelf life of dry and canned products, and is not an indicator of safety.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa setjhabeng hore se be sedi haholo mantsweng a fapaneng e amanang le dijo:Lentswe la best-before Date le bolela bolelele ba bophelo ba tshebediseho ya dihlahiswa tse ommeng le tse ka dikotikoting, mme seo ha se sesupo sa polokeho ya tsona.

src: The sell-by date is used for perishable food usually stored in a refrigerator and from July this year became no longer relevant, according to global authorities.
tgt: Lentswe la sell-by Date le sebedisetswa dijo tse bolang tse atisang ho bolokwa dihatsetsing mme ho tloha ka Phupu ya monongwaha ha le sa sebetsa, ho ya ka makgotla a nang le matla a lefatshe lohle.

src: The use-by or expiry date is the expiry date and means that food bearing this mark is no longer palatable after this date.
tgt: Lentswe la use-by Date kapa la expiry Date, ke letsatsi la ho fellwa ke nako ha sehlahiswa mme seo se bolela hore dijo tse nang le letshwao lena ha di ka ke tsa boela tsa hlabosa kamora letsatsi lena.

src: For perishable food, this means it can no longer be consumed.“Counterfeit goods” are typically goods sold under another company’s brand name while the term “fake food” has been used by social media to refer to food that does not contain food substances.
tgt: Dijong tse bolang teng, letshwao lena le bolela hore ha di ka ke tsa boela tsa jewa.“Thepa ya bolotsana” ke thepa e rekiswang tlasa lebitso la boitsebahatso la khamphane enngwe, ha lereo la “dijo mmotwana” lona le sebedisitswe marangrang a dikgokahano tsa setjhaba ho bolela dijo tseo dikateng tsa tsona di se nang metswako ya sebele ya dijo.

src: Cabinet reiterates calls on members of society to produce tangible evidence of foodstuff made from potentially harmful substances and chemicals.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e etsa kgoeletso setjhabeng hore se hlahise bopaki bo tshwarehang ka dihlahiswa tsa dijo tse entsweng ka metswako le dikhemikhale tse kotsi.

src: Furthermore, Cabinet condemns attacks on and looting of shops as a response to the sale of suspicious foods.
tgt: Ho feta moo, Kabinete e seolla ditlhaselo le boinkelo ba thepa mabenkeleng e le karabelo ya Thekiso ya dijo tse belaetsang.

src: Such criminal acts will not be tolerated and Law-enforcement agencies will not hesitate to arrest and prosecute persons found inciting or carrying out these criminal acts.
tgt: Diketso tse jwalo tsa ditlolo tsa molao ha di ka ke tsa mamellwa, mme ditheo tse sebetsanang le qobello ya molao ha di ka ke tsa qeaqea ho tshwara le ho tjhutjhisa batho ba hlohleletsang kapa ba etsang diketso tsena tsa ditlolo tsa molao.

src: Cabinet urges members of the public who are aware of suspicious foods to call the DoH hotline on 011 386 2003/6 and the National Consumer Commission hotline on 012 428 Payment of social grants.
tgt: Kabinete e kopa ditho tsohle tsa setjhaba tse nang le tsebo ka dijo tse belaetsang ho letsetsa mohala o qollehileng wa DoH ho 011 386 2003/6 le NCC ho 012 428 Ho lefshwa ha ditjhelete tsa dithuso tsa setjhaba.

src: Cabinet welcomes the progress report by Social Development Minister, Susan Shabangu, on the partnership between South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) and the South African Post Office (SAPO) to take over the payments of social grants from Cash Paymaster Services with effect from 1 October 2018.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela tlaleho ya kgatelopele ya Letona la Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba Susan Shabangu, ka selekane se dipakeng tsa Lekgotla la Tshireletso ya Setjhaba la Aforika Borwa (SASSA) le Poso ya Aforika Borwa (SAPO) ka ho nka mosebetsi wa ditefo tsa dithuso tsa setjhaba ho Cash Paymaster Services ho tloha ka la 1 Mphalane 2018.

src: SASSA has so far replaced about five and a half million old cards with the new SASSA gold card but thousands still need to be exchanged.
tgt: Ho fihlela ha jwale, SASSA e se e fane ka dikarete tse ntjha tsa kgauta tsa SASSA tse ka bang dimilione tse hlano le halofo, tse nkang sebaka sa dikarete tsa kgale, empa diketekete tsa tsona di ntse di hloka ho tjhentjhwa.

src: Cabinet strongly appeals to holders of old cards to make the switch.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa boipiletso bo matla ho beng ba dikarete tsa kgale hore ba ilo di tjhentjha.

src: SAPO will also take over the payment of cash to those recipients who were unable to withdraw cash from ATMs or merchants.
tgt: SAPO e tla boela e nka mosebetsi wa tefo ya tjhelete ho baamohedi bao ba sa kgonang ho hula tjhelete metjhineng ya di-ATM kapa mabenkeleng.

src: For further information, social-grant beneficiaries can call the SASSA toll-free number on 0800 60 10 11 during office hours.
tgt: Bakeng sa ho tseba haholwanyane, baamohedi ba dithuso tsa ditjhelete tsa mmuso ba ka letsetsa mohala wa mahala wa SASSA ho 0800 60 10 11 dihoreng tsa mosebetsi.

src: Train accident.
tgt: Kotsi ya terene.

src: Cabinet wishes the commuters who were injured when two Metrorail trains collided at the Eloff Extension in Selby, south of Johannesburg, a speedy recovery and calls for the investigation into the cause of the accident to be fast-tracked to prevent a recurrence.
tgt: Kabinete e lakaletsa bapalami ba ileng ba lemala ha diterene tse pedi tsa Metrorail di ne di tjhaisana Eloff Extension Selby, ka borwa ba Johannesburg, hore ba fole kapele ebile e etsa kgoeletso ya hore phuphutso ya sesosa sa kotsi e potlakiswe e le ho thibela phetapheto ya ketsahalo ya mofuta oo.

src: Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Kabinete.

src: Cabinet approved for the release of the 2017/18 National Crime Statistics by the South African Police Service.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho ntshuwa ha Dipalopalo tsa Naha tsa Ditlolo tsa Molao tsa 2017/18 ke Tshebeletso ya Sepolesa sa Aforika Borwa (SAPS).
