src: The annual crime statistics enable government to monitor key targets, in particular the reduction of reported serious crimes, as set out in the Medium Term Strategic Framework 2014-2019.
tgt: Dipalopalo tsa ditlolo tsa molao tsa selemo le selemo di thusa mmuso ho disa dibaka tsa bohlokwa, haholoholo phokotso ya ditlolo tsa molao tse mpempe tse tlalehilweng, jwalo ka ha ho tekilwe Moralong wa Lewa la Nako e Bohareng wa 2014-2019.

src: The crime statistics could also be used as early-warning indicators to strengthen crime-prevention operations and strategies of various government departments.
tgt: Dipalopalo tsa ditlolo tsa molao di ka boela tsa sebediswa e le matshwao a kgalemo ho sa kganya, hore ho matlafatswe ditshebetso tsa thibelo ya ditlolo tsa molao le mawa a mafapha a fapaneng a mmuso.

src: Cabinet was briefed on progress made in the management of discipline of public-service employees conducting business with an organ of state.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya hlajwa malotsana ka kgatelopele e entsweng bolaoding ba kgalemo ya basebetsi ba tshebeletso ya setjhaba, ba etsang kgwebo le ditheo tsa mmuso.

src: Promoting just and fair administration actions by senior government officials is a critical part of building an open and accountable government, as envisaged in the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996 and the building of a capable state as envisioned in the National Development Plan (NDP): Vision 2030.
tgt: Ho kgothaletsa diketso tsa toka le bosiyo ba leeme ho bahlanka ba baholo ba mmuso, ke karolo ya bohlokwa ya ho aha mmuso o bonaletsang o bile o na le boikarabello, jwalo ka ha ho lohothilwe ho Molaotheo wa Riphaboliki ya Aforika Borwa wa 1996 esita le kaho ya mmuso o nang le bokgoni jwalo ka ha ho radilwe ho Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP): Tjhebelopeleng ya 2030.

src: Progress has been made in terms of implementing Regulation 13 of the Public Service Regulations (PSR) of 2016, which prohibits public-service employees from conducting business with an organ of state, as well as Regulation 18 of the PSR of 2016, which requires members of the Senior Management Service (SMS) to disclose their financial and other private interests.
tgt: Kgatelopele e se e entswe mabapi le ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Molawana wa 13 wa Melawana ya Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba (PSR) wa 2016, o hanelang basebetsi ba tshebeletso ya setjhaba ho etsa kgwebo le ditheo tsa mmuso, esita le Molawana wa 18 wa PSR wa 2018, o hlokang hore ditho tsa Tshebeletso ya Bolaodi bo Boholo (SMS) di pepese ditabatabelo tsa tsona tsa boikunuto ba tsa ditjhelete le tse ding.

src: Cabinet also approved that relevant Executive Authority of government departments should monitor implementation of Regulation 13 of the PSR of 2016, take appropriate disciplinary steps and submit a report thereof to the Minister of Public Service and Administration (MPSA) by the end of each financial year.
tgt: Kabinete e boetse ya ananela hore Lekgotla la Phethahatso le nang le matla le tshwanelehileng la mafapha a mmuso, le lokela ho disa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Molawana wa 13 wa PSR wa 2016, le nke dikgato tsa kgalemo tse tshwanelehileng le be le kenye tlaleho ya tsona ho Letona la Lefapha la Tshebeletso le Tsamaiso ya Setjhaba (DPSA) mafelong a selemo se seng le se seng sa ditjhelete.

src: The first report is due for submission to the MPSA by the 31 March 2019.
tgt: Tlaleho ya pele e tshwanela ho kenngwa ho DPSA ka la 31 Hlakubele 2019.

src: In 2016 and 2017, the Department of Public Service and Administration identified public-service employees registered as suppliers on the Central Supplier Database, as supplied by National Treasury.
tgt: Ka 2016 le 2017, DPSA e hlwaile basebetsi ba tshebeletso ya setjhaba ba ngodisitsweng e le bafani ba ditshebeletso ho Dathabeisi e Bohareng ya Bafani ba Ditshebeletso (CSD), jwalo ka ha e neelanwe ke Lefapha la Matlotlo a Setjhaba.

src: Departments were requested to create awareness, to verify information and to report progress with implementation on the steps taken against transgressors.
tgt: Mafapha a ile a koptjwa ho etsa tlhokomediso, ho netefatsa lesedi le ho tlaleha kgatelopele ka ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha dikgato tse nkilweng kgahlanong le bao ba molato.

src: By the end of April 2018, 96% of all SMS members submitted their disclosures using the eDisclosure System.
tgt: Mafelong a Mmesa 2018, 96% ya ditho tsohle tsa SMS di kentse dipepeso tsa tsona, di sebedisa Mokgwatsamaiso wa eDisclosure.

src: Cabinet was briefed on progress made on the National School of Government (NSG) Funding Model.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya hlajwa malotsana ka kgatelopele e seng e entswe Mmotlolong wa Phano ya Ditjhelete Sekolong sa Naha sa Thupello ya Bahlanka ba Mmuso (NSG).

src: Cabinet approved a suit of mandatory and compulsory training programmes to be piloted by the NSG to undertake rapid capacity development interventions and to professionalize the public service.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse sebopeho sa mananeo a tlamang a thupello, a tla kgakolwa ke NSG hore a thakgole bokenadipakeng bo potlakileng ba ntshetsopele ya bokgoni esita le ho etsa tshebeletso ya setjhaba hore e be le boporofeshenale.

src: The direct payment for compulsory programmes to the NSG by relevant employing departments from their training budgets was also approved.
tgt: Tefo e otlolohileng bakeng sa mananeo a tlamang ho NSG e etswang ke mafapha a tshwanelehileng ho tswa ditjheleteng tsa ona tsa thupello, le yona e ile ya ananelwa.

src: This will lead to a developmental public administration that goes further in attaining Vision 2030 of the NDP by “building a capable and developmental state, which working together with an active citizenry, leads a relentless drive against poverty, unemployment and social inequality.”4.
tgt: Sena se tla lebisa tsamaisong ya setjhaba e hatelang pele, e hahamallelang pele ho fihlelleng Tjhebelopele ya 2030 ya NDP ka “ho aha naha e nang le bokgoni e hatelang pele, eo haeba e sebetsa mmoho le boahi bo mahlahahlaha, e tla etella pele tjantjello e matla kgahlanong le bofuma, leqeme la mesebetsi le ho se lekane setjhabeng.”4.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the White Paper on Science, Technology and Innovation of 2018, for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse phatlalatso ya Tokomane ya Tataiso ho Saense, Theknoloji le Tshibollo ya 2018, bakeng sa hore setjhaba se tshwaele.

src: The Minister of Science and Technology, Ms Mmamoloko Kubayi-Ngubane, will provide a full briefing in due course.
tgt: Letona la Saense le Theknoloji, Mofumahadi Mmamoloko Kubayi-Ngubane, o tla fana ka tlaleho e phethahetseng ha mmela o ntse o puta.

src: Cabinet also approved the publication of the National Protected Areas Expansion Strategy (NPAES) for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e boetse ya ananela phatlalatso ya Lewa la Katoloso la Dibaka tsa Naha tse Tshireleditsweng (NPAES) bakeng sa hore setjhaba se tshwaele.

src: The NPAES is a 20-year strategic plan aligned to the NDP, focusing on expanding the protected areas estate, with specific focus on economic growth, transformation and sustainability.
tgt: NPAES ke morero wa lewa la dilemo tse 20 o itshetlehileng ka NDP, o tsepamisitseng maikutlo katolosong ya setsha sa dibaka tse tshireleditsweng, ka tjhadimo e tsepameng kgolong ya moruo, phetoho le botsitso ba nako e telele.

src: The NPAES highlights how scarce human and financial resources can be efficiently and effectively allocated to achieve cost-effective protected area expansion, ecological sustainability and resilience to climate change.
tgt: NPAES e talola kamoo ho ka bang le kgaello ka teng ya hore ho ajwe ka bokgabane basebetsi le mehlodi ya ditjhelete, ho fihlella katoloso ya dibaka tse tshireleditsweng ka ditjeo tse fihlellehang, boitjaro ba nako e telele ba ikholoji le ho ikamahanya le phetoho ya tlelaemete.

src: South Africa’s protected area network includes world heritage sites, national parks, nature reserves, special nature reserves, protected environments, marine protected areas, mountain catchment areas, specially protected forest areas, and forest nature reserves.
tgt: Marangrang a Aforika Borwa a dibaka tse tshireleditsweng a akga ditsha tsa lefa la lefatshe, dirapa tsa naha, dirapa tsa paballo, dirapa tsa paballo tse kgethehileng, ditikoloho tse tshireleditsweng, dibaka tsa mawatleng tse tshireleditsweng, dikgakeletsi tsa metsi dithabeng, dibaka tse kgethehileng tsa meru e tshireleditsweng, le dirapa tsa paballo ya meru.

src: Cabinet approved South Africa’s Negotiating Positions for the 13th Meeting of the Conference of Contracting Parties to the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands (Ramsar COP 13) to be held in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, from 21 to 29 October 2018.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Maemo a Ditherisano a Aforika Borwa bakeng sa Kopano ya bo13 ya Seboka sa ho Notla Mekga e yang Mmokeng wa Ramsar o mabapi le Diqanthana tse Diphuleng (Ramsar COP 12) e tla tshwarelwa Dubai, United Arab Emirates, ho tloha ka la 21 ho isa ho la 29 Mphalane 2018.

src: The broad objectives of the Ramsar Convention are to ensure the conservation and wise use of all wetlands.
tgt: Dipheo tse batsi tsa Mmoka wa Ramsar ke ho netefatsa boteng ba paballo le tshebediso e tjhatsi ya diqanthana tsohle tse diphuleng.

src: In South Africa, wetlands are the most threatened of all ecosystems, with 48% of them critically endangered.
tgt: Aforika Borwa teng, diqanthana tse diphuleng ke tsona tse tlokotsing ka ho fetisisa ditikolohong tsohle, ka 48% ya tsona tse leng kotsing e mpe.

src: This contributes to water resources management as part of a proactive approach to drought management.
tgt: Di thusa taolong ya mehlodi ya metsi e le karolo ya mokgwa wa boitlhahanelo taolong ya komello.

src: Bills.
tgt: Dibili.

src: Cabinet approved publication of the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Disease Amendment Bill of 2018 for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse phatlalatso ya Bili ya Sehlomathiso sa Ditlhapiso tsa Dikotsi le Mafu tse Bakwang ke Maemo a Mosebetsing.

src: The Bill, which amends the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act, 1993 (Act 130 of 1993) recognises domestic workers, who were excluded from the Act, as employees for the purpose of benefits, as well as improving existing benefits.
tgt: Bili ena, e hlomathisang Molao wa Ditlhapiso tsa Dikotsi le Mafu tse Bakwang ke Maemo a Mosebetsing, 1993 (Molao wa 130 wa 1993) e ananela basebetsi ba malapeng, ba neng ba ntse ba teetswe kathoko Molaong, e le basebetsi ka sepheo sa hore ba fole melemo, esita le ho ntlafatsa melemo e seng e le teng.

src: The amendments improve the benefits payable to employees and their dependents, and aim to assist injured and diseased employees to be rehabilitated and reintegrated into the workplace and society.
tgt: Dihlomathiso tsena di ntlafatsa melemo e lefshwang ho basebetsi le beng ka bona, di bile di habile ho thusa basebetsi ba lemetseng le ba kulang hore ba hlabollwe ba be ba busetswe mesebetsing le setjhabeng.

src: Cabinet approved the introduction of the Child Justice Amendment Bill of 2018 into Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho lelekelwa ha Bili ya 2018 ya Sehlomathiso sa Toka ya Bana Palamenteng.

src: The Bill amends the Child Justice Act, 2008 (Act 75 of 2008) in order to review the minimum age of criminal capacity of a child by increasing it from the age of 10 to 12 years.
tgt: Bili ena e hlomathisa Molao wa Toka ya Bana, 2008 (Molao wa 75 wa 2008) e le ho hlopha botjha dilemo tsa mathomo tsa bokgoni ba botlodi ba WEBTOKEN bana, ka ho di eketsa ho tloha dilemong tse 10 ho ya ho tse Bili ena e boela e tswelapele ho sikara ditokelo tsa bana moo di hohlanang le molao teng.

src: The Bill goes further in upholding the rights of children in conflict with the law.
tgt: Bili ena e boela e hakolla taba ya bokgoni ba botlodi ba molao ho ya tshwepholo, ka ho tlosa tlhoko ena ya ho bontsha bokgoni ba botlodi ba molao molemong wa tshwepholo le dipatlisiso tse etswang pele.

src: Cabinet approved submission of the Civil Aviation Amendment Bill of 2018 to Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho kenngwa ha Bili ya 2018 ya Sehlomathiso sa Bofofisi ba Difofane Palamenteng.

src: The Bill, which amends the Civil Aviation Act, 2009 (Act 13 of 2009), will strengthen the aviation safety, security and environmental protection regulatory frameworks to ensure sustainability and stability of the civil-aviation industry.
tgt: Bili ena, e hlomathisang Molao wa Bofofisi ba Difofane, 2009 (Molao wa 13 wa 2009), e tla matlafatsa meralo ya tshireletso le taolo ya polokeho difofaneng, ho netefatsa boitjaro ba nako e telele esita le botsitso ba indasteri ya bofofisi ba difofane.

src: This will ensure that South Africa continues to meet her international obligations in the civil-aviation arena, which strengthens support to our economic development as a catalyst for increased trade, tourism and job creation.
tgt: Sena se tla netefatsa hore Aforika Borwa e tswelapele ho fihlella boitlamo ba yona ba matjhaba lepatlelong la bofofisi ba difofane, e leng ntho e matlafatsang tshehetso ntshetsopeleng ya moruo wa rona e le sehotetso sa keketseho ya kgwebisano, bohahlaudi le tlhahiso ya mesebetsi.

src: The Bill also provides for, amongst others, the operational independence of the aircraft accident and incident investigation, and to rectify inconsistencies and shortcomings.
tgt: Bili ena e boela e fana, ho tse ding, ka boikemelo ba tshebetso ba kotsi ya sefofane le patlisiso ya ketsahalo eo, esita le ho lokisa diphapano le mafokodi.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse tlang.

src: Thusong Service Centre Week.
tgt: Beke ya Thusong Service Centre.

src: Within the context of Public Service Month, the annual Thusong Service Centre Week from 17 to 21 September 2018 under the theme: “Thuma Mina: Taking Public Services to the People”, provides another platform for government to take public services to the people.
tgt: Kahare ho moeleo wa Kgwedi ya Tshebeletso ya Setjhaba, Beke ya Thusong Service Centre ya selemo le selemo ho tloha ka la 17 ho isa ho la 21 Loetse 2018 katlasa mokotaba o reng: “Thuma Mina: Ho isa Ditshebeletso tsa Setjhaba Bathong”, e fana ka lepatlelo le leng la hore mmuso o ise ditshebeletso tsa setjhaba bathong.

src: Thusong Service Centres are one-stop centres for access to government services and information, and the 133 Thusong Service Centres countrywide are centres of hope, access, redress, equality and empowerment for those previously marginalised from the mainstream of socio-economic development.
tgt: Di-Thusong Service Centre ke ditsi tseo ho tsona ho fumanehang dintho tsohle bakeng sa phihlello ya ditshebeletso tsa mmuso le lesedi, mme di-Thusong Service Centre kaofela tse 133 naha ka bophara ke ditsi tsa tshepo, phihlello, tokiso ya menyetla, tekano le matlafatso ho bao ba neng ba kotetswe kgubung ya ntshetsopele ya moruo wa setjhaba.

src: Government is working on installing a Queue Management System that will reduce the process flow to enable reduction in waiting time.
tgt: Mmuso o sebeletsa ho hokela Mokgwatsamaiso wa Taolo ya Mekoloko, o tla fokotsa mosebetsi wa lephallo e le ho thusetsa phokotsong ya nako ya ho leta.

src: The system will be installed in all centres countrywide with focus also on information and communications technology (ICT) connectivity, which is an enabler for service delivery.
tgt: Mokgwatsamaiso ona o tla hokelwa ditsing tsohle naha ka bophara, ka tsepamiso ya maikutlo e boelang e le kgokelong ya theknoloji ya lesedi la dikgokahano (ICT), e leng yona e thusang phanong ya ditshebeletso.

src: 2018 ITU Telecom World Conference.
tgt: Seboka sa Lefatshe sa Telecom sa Mokgatlo wa Basebetsi wa Dikgokahanyo tsa Mehala tsa Matjhaba (ITU) sa 2018.

src: Cabinet welcomes the 2018 International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Telecom World Conference in Durban from 10 to 13 September 2018, under the theme “Innovation for Smarter Digital Development”.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela Seboka sa Lefatshe sa Telecom sa ITU sa 2018 Durban ho tloha ka la 9 ho isa ho la 13 Loetse 2018, katlasa mokotaba o reng “Tshibollo bakeng sa Ntshetsopele ya Theknoloji ya Dijithale”.

src: The event, which is coming to Africa for the first time, provides an opportunity for increased participation of African countries towards bolstering ICT in Africa as a driver of development and innovation.
tgt: Ketsahalo ena, e tlang Aforika lekgetlo la pele, e fana ka monyetla wa seabo se eketsehileng sa dinaha tsa Aforika, ho habilwe ho matlafatsa ICT Aforika jwalo ka ha e le moetapele wa ntshetsopele le tshibollo.

src: The annual conference attracts more than 9 000 delegates from around the world, with government and industry leaders exploring and identifying investment opportunities and best practices for socio-economic development through ICKey issues for discussion include: 5G for smarter digital development, collaborating on cybersecurity, digital financial services and satellites for a smarter digital development.
tgt: Seboka sa selemo le selemo se hohela baromuwa ba kahodimo ho 9 000 ho tswa lefatsheng lohle, ka baetapele ba mmuso le ba diindasteri ba phopholetsang ba bile ba hlwaya menyetla le ditlwaelo tse ntle, haholo tsa ntshetsopele ya moruo wa setjhaba ka ICDintho tsa bohlokwa tse tla tshohlwa di akga: 5G bakeng sa ntshetsopele ya theknoloji ya dijithale, tshebedisanommoho tshireletsong ya inthanete, ditshebeletso tsa ditjhelete tsa dijithale esita le disatalaete bakeng sa ntshetsopele e theknoloji ya dijithale.

src: The ITU Telecom World Conference 2018 is hosted at a time when South Africa is implementing key national projects which include the National e-Government Strategy focusing on digital transformation of government services and the National ICT Small, Medium and Micro Enterprises (SMME) Support Strategy, which seeks to unlock the potential of the South African ICT SMMEs sector.
tgt: ITU ya 2018 ya Seboka sa Lefatshe sa Telecom e tshwarwa ka nako eo Aforika Borwa e kenyang tshebetsong diprojeke tsa bohlokwa tsa naha tse akgang Lewa la Naha la e-Government le tsepamisitseng maikutlo phetohong ya dijithale ya ditshebeletso tsa mmuso le ICT ya naha, Lewa la Tshebetso la Dikgwebo tse Nyane, tse Mahareng le tse Nyenyane (SMME), le tsetselelang ho utolla bokgoni ba lekala la Aforika Borwa la di-SMME tsa ICDisebediswa tsena di thea tikoloho e thusetsang kgolo ya lekala ebile e netefatsa boitjaro ba yona ba nako e telele.

src: Messages.
tgt: Melaetsa.

src: Cabinet conveys its deepest condolences to the:grieving family and entire Tshwane University of Technology community following the death of Katlego Monareng.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisa matshediso a yona ho:lelapa le mahlonokong esita le setjhaba sohle sa Yunivesithi ya Theknoloji ya Tshwane (TUT) kamora ho hlokahala ha Katlego Monareng.

src: Cabinet calls for calm while the police investigation is underway to ensure that whoever is responsible for the untimely death faces the full might of the WEBTOKEN and friends of the eight people who died in an explosion at the Denel munitions factory in Somerset West in the Western Cape.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ya hore ho theolwe moya ha sepolesa se ntse se batlisisa, ho netefatsa hore mang kapa mang ya molato ka ho shwa hoo, o tobana le letsoho la WEBTOKEN lelapa le metswalle ya batho ba robedi ba shwetseng ho phatloheng ho bileng femeng ya dibetsa ya Denel Somerset West Kapa Bophirimela.

src: loved ones of those who died in a fatal fire that broke out at a building shared by the Gauteng Provincial Government’s departments of Health, Human Settlements and Cooperative Governance.
tgt: baratuwa ba bao ba ileng ba shwela mollong o kotsi o ropohileng moahong o abelanwang ke Mafapha a Mmuso wa Profense ya Gauteng a Bophelo bo Botle, Bodulo ba Batho le Puso ya Tshebedisanommoho.

src: Congratulations.
tgt: Dithoholetso.

src: Cabinet congratulated the people of Zimbabwe for successfully transitioning into a new government led by President Emmerson Mnangagwa, who was inaugurated on 26 August 2018.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa batho ba Zimbabwe ka ho hahamalla katlehong ya mmuso o motjha o etelletsweng pele ke Moporesidente Emmerson Mnangagwa, ya ileng a hlomamiswa ka la 26 Phato 2018.

src: President Ramaphosa joined other African leaders in Harare to witness the occasion.
tgt: Moporesidente Ramaphosa o ikamahantse le baetapele ba bang ba Aforika Harare ho ya inwesa ka nkgo.

src: Cabinet supports President Ramaphosa’s commitment to work closely with Zimbabwe to enhance the historical, political and fraternal relations, with particular emphasis on strengthening economic cooperation.
tgt: Kabinete e tshehetsa boikitlaetso ba Moporesidente Ramaphosa ba ho sebedisana le Zimbabwe ho ntlafatsa dikamano tsa nalane, sepolotiki le tsa boena, ka thasisetso e tsepameng matlafatsong ya tshebedisanommoho ya moruo.

src: Cabinet commends the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research, and specifically its female researchers, on health research being undertaken to improve the country’s healthcare system.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Lekgotla la Saense le Diphuputso tsa Diindasteri (CSIR), haholoholo bafuputsi ba batshehadi, diphuputsong tsa bophelo bo botle tse etsetswang ho ntlafatsa mokgwatsamaiso wa bophelo bo botle wa naha ena.

src: These include:
tgt: Tsena di akga:

src: a diabetes-detecting chip to monitor blood sugar levels by analysing breath (ii) development of probiotics for use in the production of broiler chickens, dusky-cob and abalone, which will assist in the production of natural animal products, free of antibiotics, chemicals and growth stimulants (iii) and further stem cell research.
tgt: tjhipi e fofonelang lefu la tswekere e le ho disa bophahamo ba tswekere mading, ka ho sekaseka moya o tswang ka hanong (ii) ho etsuwa ha dibaktheriya tsa mmele hore di sebediswe tlhahisong ya ditsuonyana, tlhapi ya dusky-cob le ya abalone, di tla thusa tlhahisong ya dihlahiswa tsa tlholeho tsa diphoofolo, tse se nang antibayothiki, dikhemikhale le dithethefatsi tse hodisang ka potlako (iii) esita le ho tswelapele ho utolla diphuputso tsa disele.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 19 September 2018 at the Union Buildings, Pretoria.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya kopanela Union Buildings Pretoria, ka Laboraro, mohla la 19 Loetse 2018.Dintlha tsa Ha jwale.

src: Economy.
tgt: Moruo.

src: Cabinet welcomes the offer extended by business for the secondment of private-sector professionals to government.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela thuso e nanabetswang ke ba kgwebo bakeng sa ho romelwa ha baporofeshenale ba lekala la poraefete mmusong.

src: This emerged from a preparatory meeting held by President Cyril Ramaphosa with business leaders, special investment envoys and the CEO Initiative, ahead of the upcoming Job Summit and Investment Conference.
tgt: Sena se ropohile kopanong ya boitlhophisetso e neng e tshwerwe ke Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa le baetapele ba kgwebo, maqosa a kgethehileng a botsetedi le Mokgakolo wa Bahlanka ba Baholo ba Phethahatso (CEO), pele ho Seboka se tlang sa Mesebetsi le Botsetedi.

src: The meeting agreed that South Africa’s economic recovery demands urgent implementation of the stimulus package and promised growth-enhancing reforms.
tgt: Kopano e dumellane ka hore tsosoloso ya moruo wa Aforika Borwa e batla ho kenngwa tshebetsong ho potlakileng ha mokgekgetho wa diqholotsi le ditlhabollo tse tshepisitsweng tse ntlafatsang kgolo.

src: Proposals were also discussed to establish an infrastructure-development initiative that draws in private-sector funding and delivery expertise.
tgt: Ditshisinyo di ile tsa boela tsa tshohlwa mabapi le ho thea mokgakolo wa ntshetsopele ya meralo ya motheo e kenyang ditjhelete tse tswang lekaleng la poraefete esita le botsebi bo hodimo ba phano ya ditshebeletso.

src: Cabinet also welcomes the investment drive to Japan led by the Department of Trade and Industry.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e amohela thahasello ya botsetedi kwana Japan, e etelletsweng pele ke Lefapha la Kgwebisano le Indasteri (dti).

src: This is part of the broader drive that seeks to attract US$100 billion worth of investments into the South African economy over the next five years.
tgt: Thahasello ena e habile ho hohela matsete a boleng ba US$ 100 bilione moruong wa Aforika Borwa nakong ya dilemo tse hlano tse tlang.

src: Japan has been a long-term Top 10 investment partner of South Africa, with more than 140 of its companies operating in our country, which is seen as a regional manufacturing hub into Africa.
tgt: Haesale Japan e le molekane wa ba leshome ba kahodimodimo wa batsetedi ba nako e telele Aforika Borwa, ka dikhamphane tsa yona tse kahodimo ho 140 tse sebetsang naheng ena ya rona, e bonwang e le kgubu ya lebatowa la tlhahiso ya ho kena Aforika.

src: Cabinet encourages companies to both invest and expand in South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa dikhamphane ho tsetela le ho nama Aforika Borwa.

src: Training programmes.
tgt: Mananeo a thupello.

src: Cabinet welcomes the launch of the R22-million training project by the Minister of Labour, Ms Mildred Oliphant, which will create employment in the aviation, maritime commercial diving and agricultural sectors.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela kgakolo ya projeke ya thupello ya R22-milione ke Letona la tsa Mesebetsi, Mofumahadi Mildred Oliphant, e tla thea mesebetsi makaleng a bofofisi, a kgwebo ya ho qwela metsing a lewatle esita le a temothuo.

src: The project is being undertaken in partnership with the Dr John Langalibalele Dube Institute and the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF), an entity of the Department of Labour.
tgt: Projeke ena e sebetswa ka selekane le Setheo sa Ngaka John Langalibalele Dube esita le Letlole la Inshorense ya ba Feletsweng ke Mesebetsi (UIF), eo e leng setheo sa Lefapha la tsa Bosebetsi.

src: The project will focus on the former contributors to the UIF who lost their jobs.
tgt: Projeke ena e tla shadimana le ba kentseng letsoho ho UIF ba feletsweng ke mesebetsi.

src: The first group of beneficiaries includes 50 UIF contributors from the Durban Virginia Airport 50 from the maritime commercial diving project in Scottsburg, KwaZulu-Natal, and 100 rural women from Emadungeni will be trained towards forming a cooperative to plant and grow organic fruit, vegetables and cotton, including value-chain processing.
tgt: Sehlopha sa pele sa ba tla fola molemo se akga ba 50 ba kentseng letsoho ba tswang Boemafofaneng ba Virginia bo Durban ba 50 ba tswang projekeng ya kgwebo ya ho qwela metsing a lewatle e Scottsburg, KwaZulu-Natal, athe basadi ba mahaeng ba 100 ba tswang Emadungeni ba tla rupellwa hore ba thee koporasi ya ho lema le ho jala ditholwana, meroho le khothene tse holang ka mokgwa wa tlholeho, ho akga le ho lokisetswa ha thekiso ya tsona.

src: These cooperatives have signed an agreement with Pick n Pay for vegetable supply and with the Department of Social Development to source material for the manufacture of school uniforms.
tgt: Dikoporasi tsena di tekenne tumellano le Pick ‘n Pay bakeng sa ho e fepela ka meroho, hammoho le Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Setjhaba bakeng sa ho fumana disebedisuwa tsa ho roka diyunifomo tsa dikolo.

src: Cabinet welcomes the official opening by President Ramaphosa of new offices for the Department of Home Affairs at Hluhluwe in KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela pulo ya semmuso ya dikantoro tse ntjha tsa Lefapha la Merero ya Lehae tse Hluhluwe KwaZulu-Natal ke Moporesidente Ramaphosa.

src: The expanded roll-out of civic services to marginalised communities plays a key role in enabling and deepening democracy and social justice.
tgt: Nanabetso ena e atollotsweng ya ditshebeletso tsa setjhaba dibakeng tse neng di kotetswe, e na le seabo sa bohlokwa ho dumelleng le ho tebiseng demokrasi le toka setjhabeng.

src: This forms part of government’s commitment to bringing services closer to the people.
tgt: Sena se etsa karolo ya boikitlaetso ba mmuso ho atametseng ditshebeletso bathong.

src: Broadcasting Digital Migration Programme.
tgt: Lenaneo la ho Fallela Kgasong e Ntjha ya Dijithale.

src: Cabinet is satisfied with the progress being made in migrating the country from analogue to digital.
tgt: Kabinete e kgotsofetse ka kgatelopele e entsweng ya ho falla ha naha ho tloha kgasong ya kgale ya analoko ho ya ho e ntjha ya dijithale.

src: As part of the countdown to December 2018 for the Free State Analogue Switch-Off, the first transmitter in Senekal in the Free State will be switched off on 20 September 2018.
tgt: E le karolo ya ho bala nako e setseng ya ho ya ho Tshitwe ya 2018 bakeng sa ho Tingwa ha Kgaso ya Kgale ya Analoko Freistata, transmithara ya pele e Senekal Freistata e tla tingwa ka la 20 Loetse 2018.

src: This is in line with the commitment agreed to with the International Telecommunication Union.
tgt: Sena se tsamaisana le boikitlaetso boo ho dumellanweng ka bona le Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba wa Meralo ya Dikgokahano.

src: A communication campaign is underway to ensure that all households are ready for the switch-off.
tgt: Letsholo la dikgokahanyo le se le thakgotswe ho netefatsa hore malapa ohle a ba malalaalaotswe bakeng sa ho tingwa hona.

src: Households with analogue television (TV) sets looking to buy new ones are advised to choose those with an integrated digital tuner.
tgt: Malapa a nang le dithelevishene (TV) tse sebetsang ka analoko a batlang ho reka tse ntjha, a eletswa ka hore a reke tse nang le konopo ya dijithale e seng e hoketswe.

src: Households with an income above the threshold of R3 200 per month have an option of buying a new integrated digital TV set with the built-in Digital Terrestrial TV decoder, which is available through major retail outlets.
tgt: Malapa a nang le lekeno le kahodimo ho sekepele sa R3 200 ka kgwedi a na le kgetho ya ho reka TV e ntjha e seng e hoketswe dijithale ebile e le e nang le dikhoudara ya TV ya Dijithale e bopelletsweng kahare, e fumanehang mabenkeleng a maholo a rekisang thepa.

src: In line with President Ramaphosa’s call for a moratorium on job cuts resulting from the economic conditions in the country, Cabinet reiterates its appeal to employers that retrenchments must be a last resort, and that other available and innovative ways to contain costs be thoroughly explored to sustain jobs.
tgt: Ho ya ka kgoeletso ya Moporesidente Ramaphosa ya ho kginwa nakwana ha dipukutlo tsa mesebetsi ka lebaka la maemo a moruo naheng ena, Kabinete e thasisetsa boipiletso ba yona ho bahiri hore taba ya ho heletswa mesebetsing e mpe e be ntho ya ho qetela eo ba ka e nahanang, le hore mekgwa e meng e teng ya sejwalejwale ya ho notla ditjeo e shebisiswe ka hloko molemong wa ho boloka mesebetsi ka nako e telele.

src: Crime statistics.
tgt: Dipalopalo tsa ditlolo tsa molao.

src: Cabinet endorses the intervention by the Justice, Crime Prevention and Security Cluster to urgently engage on a comprehensive strategy to deal with various issues emanating from the recently released crime statistics.
tgt: Kabinete e bo tjhaella monwana bokenadipakeng ba Setlamo sa tsa Toka, Thibelo ya Ditlolo tsa Molao le Tshireletso, ba ho tshetshetha ka potlako ka lewa le phethahetseng la ho lwantshana le dintho tse fapaneng tse ropohang dipalopalong tsa ditlolo tsa molao tse sa tswa ntshuwa.

src: This includes the recently held National Summit on Crime and Violence Prevention held under the theme “Building safer communities through an integrated, developmental approach to crime and violence prevention”, which developed a joint vision on safety as a collective responsibility, and provided a platform for key stakeholders and experts to engage on the effective implementation of the 2016 White Paper on Safety and Security across all sectors.
tgt: Sena se akga Seboka sa Naha ho Thibelo ya Ditlolo tsa Molao le Merusu se neng se tshwerwe haufinyane katlasa mookotaba wa, “Ho aba dibaka tse bolokehileng ka mokgwa o kopantsweng ebile e le o tswelang pele wa thibelo ya ditlolo tsa molao le merusu”, e leng se ileng sa rala tjhebelopele ya kopanelo ho tsa polokeho e le boikarabello bo kopanetsweng, sa ba sa fana ka lepatlelo bakeng sa ba amehang ba ka sehloohong esita le ditsebi ho tshetshetha ka ho kenngwa tshebetsong ho kgabane ha Tokomane ya Tataiso ya 2016 ho tsa Polokeho le Tshireletso makaleng ohle.

src: Incidents of violence.
tgt: Diketsahalo tsa merusu.

src: Cabinet is deeply concerned by the level of violence in our society and calls on all sectors, communities and law-enforcement agencies to work together to ensure that schools and public spaces are safe and secure.
tgt: Kabinete e ngongorehile haholo ka sekgahla sa merusu setjhabeng sa habo rona mme e etsa kgoeletso makaleng ohle, dibakeng tsohle esita le ditheong tsa qobello ya molao hore ho sebetswe mmoho ho netefatsa hore dikolo le dibaka tsa setjhaba di bolokehile ebile di tshireletsehile.

src: The acts of violence that broke out in several parts of the country are unacceptable and go against our Constitution.
tgt: Diketsahalo tsa merusu tse ropohileng dikgutlwaneng tse ngata tsa naha ena ha di a amoheleha ebile di kgahlanong le Molaotheo wa rona.

src: Cabinet commends the South African Police Service for the swift responses in arresting those suspected of being involved in public violence and possession of suspected stolen goods.
tgt: Kabinete e thoholetsa Tshebeletso ya Sepolesa sa Aforika Borwa (SAPS) ka ho arabela ka potlako hore ho tshwarwe bao ba belaellwang ka ho ba le seabo merusung hara setjhaba, esita le ho fumanwa ba na le thepa e belaellwang ka hore e utswitswe.

src: Klebsiella outbreak.
tgt: Ho ropoha ha bohloko ba Klebsiella.

src: Cabinet extends condolences to the families of the six babies who died following an outbreak of Klebsiella pneumoniae at the Thelle Mogoerane Hospital in Vosloorus.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisa matshediso malapeng a masea a tsheletseng a hlokahetseng kamora ho ropoha ha bohloko ba Klebsiella pneumoniae Sepetleleng sa Thelle Mogoerane se Vosloorus.

src: The Minister of Health, Dr Aaron Motsoaledi, has since announced the transfer of babies and their mothers to the Nelson Mandela Children’s Hospital and Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital respectively.
tgt: Letona la Bophelo bo Botle, Ngaka Aaron Motsoaledi, o se a entse tsebiso ya hore masea le bomma ona sepetleleng sena ba tla fetisetswa Sepetlele sa Bana sa Nelson Mandela le Sepetlele sa Dithuto sa Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg ka tatelano.

src: This gives the provincial health department an opportunity to scrub down and decontaminate the environment, and also address the structural issues, without any disturbance.
tgt: Sena se fa lefapha la bophelo bo botle la profense monyetla wa ho hlwekisa tikoloho, esita le ho rarolla ditaba tsa sebopeho sa sepetlele, ntle le tshitiso ya letho.

src: Decisions.
tgt: Diqeto.

src: Stimulus packageCabinet deliberated and approved the proposed stimulus package which proposes measures to reignite our economy from a number of related portfolios.
tgt: Mokgekgetho wa diqholotsiKabinete e tshohlile yaba ya ananela mokgekgetho wa diqholotsi o sisintsweng, o sisinyang mehato ya ho tsosolosa moruo wa rona ho tswa ditshebetsong tse ngatanyana tse amanang le wona.

src: A media briefing led by President Cyril Ramaphosa will held on Friday 21 September to present this package.
tgt: Seboka sa ditaba se etelletsweng pele ke Moporesidente Ramaphosa se tla tshwarwa ka Labohlano mohla la 21 Loetse ho teka mokgekgetho ona.

src: VISA related reformsCabinet also received a joint report from the Ministers of Home Affairs and Tourism respectively, on a number of visa-related reforms which will make it easier for tourists, business people and academia to come to South Africa.
tgt: Ditlhabollo tse amanang le VISAKabinete e boetse ya amohela tlaleho ya kopanelo e tswang ho Matona a Merero ya Lehae le Bohahlaudi ka tatelano, mabapi le ditlhabollo tse ngatanyana tse amanang le visa tse tla nolofaletsa bahahlaudi, bahwebi le barutehi ho tla Aforika Borwa.

src: The reforms include amendments to the regulations applying to foreign minors travelling to South Africa, which will be gazetted in October.
tgt: Ditlhabollo tsena di akga dihlomathiso melawaneng e sebetsang ho melata ya bana e etelang Aforika Borwa, tse tla phatlalatswa kaseteng ya mmuso ka Mphalane.

src: Negotiations on visa waivers and relaxation of visa requirements for certain countries are also being finalised.
tgt: Ditherisano tsa ho nyahlatswa ha ditlhoko tsa di-visa le ho nyehliswa ha ditlhoko tsa di-visa bakeng sa dinaha tse itseng, le tsona di a phethelwa.

src: Further details will be announced this week.
tgt: Dintlha tse tomanyana di tla tsebiswa bekeng ena.

src: Bills.
tgt: Dibili.

src: Cabinet approved the following Bills for publication for public comment:.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Dibili tse latelang bakeng sa ho phatlalatswa hore setjhaba se tshwaele ka tsona:.

src: Employment Equity Amendment Bill of 2017.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya 2017 ya Tekano Mesebetsing.

src: The amendments seek to strengthen the compliance mechanisms and will allow for the setting up of employment equity sector-specific numerical targets.
tgt: Dihlomathiso tsena di habile ho matlafatsa mekgwa ya boikamahanyo mme di tla dumella ho ralwa ha dipeelo tsa lenane le badilweng tsa tekano mesebetsing ya makala a totobaditsweng.

src: The Minister of Labour, in consultation with the sector’s stakeholders, will be able to set employment equity sector-specific numerical targets.
tgt: Letona la tsa Bosebetsi, ka pontshano le ba amehang lekaleng, ba tla kgona ho rala dipeelo tsa lenane le badilweng tsa tekano mesebetsing ya makala a totobaditsweng.

src: Financial Sector Laws Amendment Bill of 2018: The amendments seek to strengthen the curatorship provisions for banks, including mutual and cooperative banks, and certain non-banks.
tgt: Sehlomathiso sa Bili ya 2018 ya Melao ya Lekala la tsa Ditjhelete: Dihlomathiso tsena di habile ho matlafatsa ditlhoko tsa poloko ya matlotlo bakeng sa dibanka, ho akga le dibanka tsa kopanelo le tsa dikoporasi, le tse ding tse itseng tseo e seng dibanka.

src: The changes will ensure that should these financial institutions experience difficulties, they can be assisted in a way that protects vulnerable depositors with minimal disruptions to the financial system and broader economy.
tgt: Diphetoho di tla netefatsa hore ha ho ka etsahala hore ditheo tsena tsa ditjhelete di be le mathata, di ka thuswa ka mokgwa o tshireletsang beng ba tjhelete ba tlokotsing ka hore ho se ke ha eba teng ditshita tse kgolo tsamaisong ya tsa ditjhelete le moruo ka bobatsi.

src: Upcoming Events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse Tlang.

src: Heritage Day The 2018 National Heritage Day celebration under the theme: “The Year of Nelson Mandela: Advancing transformation of South Africa’s heritage landscape”, takes place at the Riverview Stadium in Kokstad, KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Keteko ya Letsatsi la Bojalefa la 2018 katlasa mookotaba o reng: “Selemo sa Nelson Mandela: Ho ntshetsa pele phetoho lepatlelong la bojalefa ba Aforika Borwa”, e tshwarelwa Lebaleng la Dipapadi la Riverview Kokstad, KwaZulu-Natal.

src: This is part of the month-long programme of activities which are addressing issues of transformation, promotion and preservation of South Africa’s rich and diverse heritage, national identity, nation-building and social cohesion.
tgt: Ena ke karolo ya lenaneo le le lelele la kgwedi kaofela la diketsahalo tse rarollang dintho tse amanang le phetoho, phahamiso le paballo ya mohlahlwe wa bojalefa le manoni a Aforika Borwa.

src: The Heritage Day celebration is in honour of Adam Kok and the Griqua community for their courage, determination and fortitude in resisting colonial occupation.
tgt: Keteko ena ya Letsatsi la Bojalefa e etsetswa ho tlotla Adam Kok le ditjhaba tsa Makgerikwa ka sebete, boikitlaetso le matla a bona ka ho hanana le boipehi ba bokoloniale.

src: Cabinet calls on the public to celebrate their unity in diversity as we work together to build a country where all its people care for and respect one another.
tgt: Kabinete e etsa kgoeletso ho setjhaba hore se keteke kopano ya sona ka mohlahlwe wa sona, jwalo ka ha re sebetsa mmoho ho aha naha eo batho bohle ba yona ba hlomphanang ba bile ba tsotellana.

src: United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).
tgt: Seboka Kakaretso sa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UNGA).

src: In contributing towards the centenary of former President Nelson Mandela, the UNGA will on 24 September 2018 hold a high-level plenary meeting on global peace known as the Nelson Mandela Peace Summit, in honour of the centenary of the birth of Madiba.
tgt: Ho kenyeng letsoho mabapi le dilemo tse lekgolo tsa tswalo ya Moporesidente wa mehleng Nelson Mandela, ka la 24 Loetse 2018 UNGA e tla tshwara kopano ya boemo bo hodimo mabapi le kgotso ya lefatshe lohle e tsejwang ka hore ke Seboka sa Kgotso sa Nelson Mandela, e le ho tlotla dilemo tse lekgolo tsa tswalo ya Madiba.

src: The plenary is scheduled to adopt a political declaration negotiated by UNGA Member States.
tgt: Kopano ena e reretswe ho ananela tsebiso ya selekane sa sepolotiki e duletsweng majwana ke Dinaha tseo e leng Ditho tsa UNGSena se etsahala kamora dipuisano tsa Baemedi ba Moshwelella mokgatlong wa UN ba Aforika Borwa le Ireland, ba sebetsang e le bahlophisetsi, hammoho le mebuso e mmedi ena ka dikateng tsa tsebiso ena ya selekane.

src: President Ramaphosa is also expected to participate in the UN High-Level Meeting on TB on 26 September 2018.
tgt: Moporesidente Ramaphosa o boetse o lebelletswe ho ba le seabo Kopanong ya UN ya Boemo bo Hodimo mabapi le bohloko ba Lefuba (TB) mohla la 26 Loetse 2018.

src: TB is a major disease in Africa and some of the world’s high TB burden countries are on the continent.
tgt: TB ke bohloko bo ka sehloohong Aforika mme tse ding tsa dinaha tse thefutsweng ke TB ka ho fetisisa di khontinenteng ena.

src: Messages.
tgt: Melaetsa.

src: CondolencesCabinet sends its condolences to the families that lost their loved ones in a bus crash that occurred on the N1-25 near Tobias in the Waterberg Municipality District in Limpopo.
tgt: MatshedisoKabinete e fetisetsa matshediso a yona ho malapa a lahlehetsweng ke baratuwa ba ona ho swahlamaneng ha bese ho etsahetseng mmileng wa N1-25 haufi le Tobias, Masepaleng wa Setereke sa Waterberg Limpopo.

src: Cabinet also wishes those injured a speedy recovery.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e lakaletsa bao ba lemetseng hore ba fole ka potlako.

src: CongratulationsCabinet congratulates the Minister of Small Business Development, Ms Lindiwe Zulu, for being admitted to the highest level of the Order of Rio Branco (Ordem de Rio Branco), and the Grand Cross from the Government of Brazil.
tgt: DithoholetsoKabinete e thoholetsa Letona la Dikgwebo tse Nyenyane, Mofumahadi Lindiwe Zulu, ka hore a amohelwe boemong bo hodimodimo ba Tlotlo ya Rio Branco (Ordem de Rio Branco), le Grand Cross ho tswa Mmusong wa Brazil.

src: This is in recognition for the Minister’s continuous efforts to enhance bilateral relations between Brazil and South Africa.
tgt: Sena se entswe ka lebaka la matsapa a Letona a ntseng a tswelapele a ho ntlafatsa dikamano tsa dinaha tse pedi dipakeng tsa Brazil le Aforika Borwa.

src: This honorific order of Brazil is granted to those who have distinguished themselves in acts of meritorious service and civic virtues.
tgt: Tlotlo ena ya Brazil e fuwa bao ba ipabotseng ka diketso tsa tshebeletso e tswileng matsoho esita le makgetha a setjhaba.

src: Minister Zulu was the South African Ambassador to Brazil between 2004 and 2008.AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: Letona Zulu e ne e le Leqosa la Aforika Borwa Brazil dipakeng tsa 2004 le 2008.DithonyoDithonyo kaofela di lokela ho netefatswa ka mangolo a thuto le tumello e amehang.

src: Board of Rand Water:a. Adv Faith Matshidiso Hashatse (Chairperson)b. Ms Massacha Khulekelwe Glynnis Mbonambi (Deputy Chairperson)c. Mr LL Makibinyaned.
tgt: Boto ya Rand Water:a. Moadvokheiti Faith Matshidiso Hashatse (Modulasetulo)b. Mofumahadi Massacha Khulekelwe Glynnis Mbonambi (Motlatsi wa Modulasetulo)c. Monghadi LL Makibinyaned.

src: Mr Ahmed Mohammed Pandorf.
tgt: Monghadi Ahmed Mohammed Pandorf.

src: Ms Mahlatse Martha Kabig.
tgt: Mofumahadi Mahlatse Martha Kabig.

src: Ms Mankone Ntsabah.
tgt: Mofumahadi Mankone Ntsabah.

src: Ms Nomsa Georgina Mbilenii.
tgt: Mofumahadi Nomsa Georgina Mbilenii.

src: Mr Protas Thamsanqa Philij.
tgt: Monghadi Protas Thamsanqa Philij.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 10 October 2018 at Tuynhuys in Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e kopane ka Laboraro, 10 Mphalane 2018 Tuynhuys, ho la Motse Kapa.

src: Cabinet welcomes the practical interventions such as the commitment to buy local products, a more aggressive approach to increasing exports, interventions in agricultural value chains and support for small and medium enterprises.
tgt: Dintlha tsa Hajwale Letsholo la moruo le tsetelo Kabinete e amohela diketso tsa tshebetso tse jwalo ka boitlamo ba ho reka dihlahiswa tse entsweng kahare ho naha, katamelo e matla ho feta ya ho eketsa dihlahiswa tse rekiswang kantle ho naha, mesebetsi kgwebong ya temo le tshehetso bakeng sa dikgwebo tse nyane le tse mahareng.

src: These announcements came out of the recent two-day Job Summit, which was convened under the National Economic Development and Labour Council.2 The outcome of the Job Summit follows the announcement of the Economic Stimulus and Recovery Plan, which seeks to restore economic growth and create much-needed jobs.
tgt: Diphatlalatso tsena di hlahile Kopanong ya Mesebetsi ya matsatsi a mabedi e sa tswa tshwarwa, e tshwerweng tlasa Khansele ya Naha ya Ntshetsopele ya Moruo le Mesebetsi.2 Sephetho sa Kopano ya Mesebetsi se latela phatlalatso ya Morero wa Tsosoloso le Ntjhafatso ya Moruo, e rerileng ho tsosolosa kgolo ya moruo ya ho theha mesebetsi e hlokehang e le kannete.

src: The new Mining Charter – which was finalised in consultation with the mining industry, labour, affected communities and other stakeholders – clarifies the imperatives of growth, sustainability and transformation.
tgt: Tumellano e Ntjha ya Merafo – e phethetsweng ka tshebedisanommoho le indasteri ya merafo, kgwebo le ditjhaba tse amehileng le baamehi ba bang – e hlakisa dintlha tsa bohlokwa tsa kgolo, phehello le phetoho.3 Kabinete e kopa baamehi bohle ho sebetsana le Tumellano ya Merafo e le ho phethela le ho theha botsitso kgwebong ya merafo.

src: Cabinet calls on all stakeholders to engage with the Mining Charter so as to finalise and create stability in the mining sector.
tgt: Ofisi ya Merero ya Lehae ya Kokstad le phano ya mangolo a beng ba matlo Kabinete hammoho le Mopresidente Cyril Ramaphosa ba lebohisa Lefapha la Merero ya Lehae bakeng sa ho bula ofisi ya Kokstad ho la KwaZulu-Natal.

src: Kokstad Home Affairs office and handover of title deeds.
tgt: Mopresidente o butse ofisi ya Merero ya Lehae jwalo ka karolo ya lenaneo la mmuso la ho atolosa kgato ya dibaka tsa phano ya ditshebeletso ya Merero ya Lehae ho kgotsofatsa ditlhoko tsa baahi bakeng sa dikarete tsa boitsebiso (di-Smart ID) le ditokomane tse ding.2 Ho feta moo, Mopresidente Ramaphosa o fane ka mangolo a beng ba matlo a 443 ho bajalefa ba Projeke ya Franklin Housing.

src: The President opened the Home Affairs office as part of government’s programme to expand the footprint of Home Affairs service-delivery points to meet citizens’ demands for Smart ID cards and other documents.
tgt: Ena ke karolo ya lenaneo la puseletso la ho netefatsa hore bajalefa ba fumana melemo e felletseng ya ho ba le ntlo mme ba kgona ho fihlella mmaraka wa semmuso wa matlo.3 Kabinete e boetse e nka monyetla ona ho kgothaletsa baahi ka matla hore ba late di-ID tsa bona hang ha ba fumana tsebiso ya ho di lata.

src: This is part of the restoration programme to ensure beneficiaries experience the full benefits of owning a house and are able to access the formal property market.
tgt: Tumellano ya phethelo mabapi le sepeketeramo Kabinete e amohela tumellano ya phethelo e fihletsweng tabeng e kenyelletsang Memo ya ho etsa Kopo bakeng sa kabo ya sepeketeramo sa tlhoko e phahameng.

src: Cabinet also takes this opportunity to strongly encourage citizens to collect their IDs as soon as they receive a notification of collection.
tgt: Sena se fana ka botsitso ba pholisi lekaleng ka theknoloji ya tlhahisoleseding le dikgokahano (ICT).2 Tumellano ena ya phethelo e tsamaellana le pitso ya Mopresidente Ramophosa ya ho qala tshebetso ya kabo ya dilaesense tsa seyalemoya tsa sepeketeramo sa tlhoko e phahameng.4 E le ho kenya letsoho ka tsela tse eketsehileng ho tshebetso ya Tokomane ya Tataiso ya Pholisi e Kopantsweng ya Naha ya ICT, baamehi ba nang le kgahleho ba ka fana ka ditlatsetso tse ngotsweng ho fihlela la 8 Pudungwana 2018 ho pholisi e sisintsweng le tjhebo ya yona ho ba boholong.

src: In further contributing to the implementation of the National Integrated ICT Policy White Paper, interested parties have until 8 November 2018 to provide written inputs on the proposed policy and policy direction to the authority.
tgt: Balefi ba lekgetho bao eseng ba nakwana ba kgethang ho faela diforomo tsa bona ka eFiling ba ka etsa jwalo ho fihlela la 31 Pherekgong 20.2 Pokeletso e nepahetseng e sebetsang hantle e netefatsa matla a nahana a busang tjhelete ya yona, mme dinehelano tse etswang ka nako le ka nepo di netefatsa hore balefi ba lekgetho ba latela molao wa lekgetho.

src: Cabinet welcomes South Africa’s first small-scale cooperatives in the fishing sector, namely the Port Nolloth and Hondeklipbaai cooperatives in the Northern Cape, which were launched by the Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Mr Senzeni Zokwana.
tgt: Ditefo tsa digrante tsa setjhaba Kabinete e tlalehetswe ke Komiti ya Mafapha a Kopaneng: Digrante tsa Setjhaba, eo modulasetulo wa yona e leng Letona Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma.

src: The fishing rights give dignity to local fishermen, who have been fishing illegally, in that they are now protected for the first time.3 The two small-scale fishing communities who will be benefiting from this policy have received basic training on cooperatives and have been assisted to register cooperatives for the purpose of applying for 15-year fishing rights.
tgt: Bajalefa bohle ba kontane ba lefuwang ke CPS ba fetiseditswe mme CPS e se e tsebisitswe ka phediso ya konteraka ho tloha ka la 30 Loetse 20.3 Kabinete e leboha mosebetsi o motle wa botsamaisi o neng o etelletswe pele ke Komiti ya Mafapha a Kopaneng e tsheheditswe ke Sehlopha sa Mosebetsi wa Botekgeniki sa Balaodikakaretso.

src: As of the 1st October 2018, more than 10 million beneficiaries were paid using either of these platforms - the South African Post Office (SAPO)/Postbank Grinrod Bank as well as merchants such as Boxer, Shoprite, and Pick ’n Pay.
tgt: Boipelaetso ba Westbury Kabinete e amohela tshebetso ya Letona la Sepolesa Bheki Cele ho la Westbury, eo e leng karolo ya moralo o pharalletseng wa ho lwantsha bothata ba dithethefatsi le dintwa tse amanang le maqulwana sebakeng seo.2 Tshebetso ena e kenyelletsa ho romelwa ha Sehlopha sa Tshebetso e Radilweng sa Thibelo ya Botlokotsebe (TRT - Maberete) le boteng bo eketsehileng ba sepolesa.

src: Government has successfully migrated social-grant payments from Cash Paymaster Services (CPS) as instructed by the Constitutional Court Judgement.
tgt: Sa bohlokwa ke hore, ho boetse ho tla ba le dipatlisiso mabapi le manyofonyofo a etsahalang kahare ho Seteishene sa Sepolesa sa Westbury.3 Kabinete e bitsa setjhaba sa Westbury le ditjhaba tsohle hore di sebetse le sepolesa ho netefatsa hore re fatolla diteketso tsa botlokotsebe, dithethefatsi le maqulwana dibakeng tse fapaneng tse ba dulang ho tsona.

src: All cash beneficiaries effected by CPS have been migrated and CPS has been notified of the termination of the contract as of 30 September 2018.
tgt: Botlokotsebe.1 Kabinete e lebohisa ditheo tsa molao ka ho etsa dipatlisiso tse matla tsa makala a fapaneng tse amanang le diketsahalo tsa dimolong, mabenkeleng le dimoskeng tse lebisitseng ho ho tshwarwa ha babelaellwa ba Di ne di kenyelletsa Sehlopha sa Toka, Thibelo ya Botlokotsebe le Tshireletso.

src: It further extends its appreciation to the work of the officials from SAPO, South African Social Security Agency and, the departments of Social Development Telecommunications and Postal Services Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation National Treasury South African Police Service and GCICabinet thanks all the social-grant beneficiaries for their cooperation during this transition.
tgt: Ho lebelletswe hore babelaellwa bohle ba tla shebana le diqoso tse kenyelletsang polao, teko ya polao le ho tlola Molao wa Diqhomane.2 Kabinete e netefalletsa maAforika Borwa hore ho lwantshwa botlokotsebe ho bohlokwa haholo le hore mmuso o tla tswelapele ho nka mehato e hlokehang ho netefatsa hore ho ba le tikoloho e bolokehileng hape e sireletsehileng bakeng sa baahi bohle ba Aforika Borwa.

src: Cabinet commends the law-enforcement agencies in carrying out an intensive multi-disciplinary investigation relating to incidents at shopping malls, retail stores and mosques which has resulted in the arrest of nineteen suspects.
tgt: Kabinete e lebohisa sehlopha sa bafuputsi ba Yunivesithi ya Wits se entseng phetolo e atlehileng ya nalane ho tlosa sebete ho tswa ho Mme ya nang le tshwaetso ya HIV ho ya ho ngwana wa hae ya senang HISehlopha sa dingaka se ne se kenyelletsa Moprofesara Jean Botha, Ngaka Francesca Conradie, Ngaka Harriet Etheredge, Ngaka June Fabian le Moprofesara Caroline Tiemessen.

src: Cabinet reassures South Africans that fighting crime is a top priority and that government will continue to take necessary steps to ensure a safe and secure environment for all inhabitants of South Africa.
tgt: E boetse e bile mampodi wa naha le wa matjhaba bakeng sa poloko ya tikoloho bakeng sa lefatshe le tswellang le ka arolelanwang le ho natefelwa ke bohle.

src: Cabinet welcomes the name change of Grahamstown, in the Eastern Cape, to Makhanda, in honour of Xhosa prophet, philosopher and military man who fought against colonialism.
tgt: Mmuso o se o tshepisitse tshehetso ya ona, moo ho hlokehang, mme Kabinete e tlotla basebetsi ba maAforika Borwa ba thuso ba nkileng karolo mesebetsing ya thuso Sehlekehlekeng sa Indonesia sa Sulawesi, se otluweng ke ho reketla ha lefatshe le tsunami.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 24 October 2018 at Tuynhuys in Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e kopane ka Laboraro, 24 Mphalane 2018 ho la Tuynhuys, Motse Kapa.

src: Cabinet welcomes the maiden MTBPS by Finance Minister Tito Mboweni, which is based on the strong conviction that South Africa can be renewed.
tgt: Polelo ya Pholisi ya Tekanyetso ya Nako e Bohareng (MTBPS)1.1 Kabinete e amohela MTBPS ya pele ka Letona la Ditjhelete Tito Mboweni, e thehilweng hodima tumelo e matla ya hore Afrika Borwa e ka ntjhafatswa.2 MTBPS ya 2018 e totobatsa dikgetho tsa thata tsa moruo le lekgetho tse tjametseng mmuso nakong ya dilemo tse tharo tse tlang.

src: The 2018 MTBPS highlights the difficult economic and fiscal choices confronting government over the next three years.
tgt: Kgolo ya moruo bakeng sa 2018 e fetoletswe tlase ho tloha ho 1.5% ho ya ho 0.7%, mme tikoloho ya lefatshe e dula e ntse e le thata bakeng sa meruo ya mebaraka e thuthuwang.

src: Economic growth for 2018 has been revised down from 1.5% to 0.7%, and the global environment remains challenging for emerging market economies.
tgt: MTBPS ya 2018 e qala tshebetso ya morero wa Mopresidente wa tsosoloso ya kgolo ya moruo le puseletso, tse tla tshehetswa ke botsitso ba tsa lekgetho le ditjhelete.3 Mmuso o dula o itlametse botsitso ba tsa lekgetho, empa ho bile le phokotseho esale ho tloha ka puo ya Ditekanyetso ya 2018 ka Hlakola selemong sena.

src: Government remains committed to stabilizing and bringing down debt.
tgt: Mmuso o ikitlaelletsa ho tlisa botsitso le ho fokotsa mekoloto.

src: Against the backdrop of a difficult economic and fiscal environment, the proposed division of revenue continues to prioritise large social spending programmes that support basic education, health, social welfare, water, sanitation and electricity services.
tgt: Papisong le tikoloho e phephetsang ya moruo le tsa lekgetho, karolo e sisingwang ya lekeno e tswelapele ho beha sehlohlolong mananeo a tshebediso e hodimo ya tjhelete a tshehetsang ditshebeletso tsa thuto ya motheo, bophelo bo botle, boiketlo ba setjhaba, metsi, tlhwekiso le motlakase.

src: Cabinet welcomes the outcomes of the Presidential Health Summit which aim to address the various challenges facing the public health system.
tgt: Kopano ya Mopresidente ya Bophelo bo Botle Kabinete e amohela diphetho tsa Kopano ya Mopresidente ya Bophelo bo Botle tse reretsweng ho sebetsana le diphephetso tse fapaneng tseo sistimi ya setjhaba ya bophelo bo botle e tobaneng le tsona.

src: The outcomes will strengthen the preparations for the implementation of the National Health Insurance.
tgt: Diphetho di tla matlafatsa ditukisetso tsa ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha Inshorense ya Naha ya Bophelo bo Botle.

src: Cabinet welcomes the consistent implementation of land reform and restitution programmes that redresses the past injustices and help to grow the economy.
tgt: Phetolo ya lefatshe Kabinete e amohela ho kenngwa tshebetsong ho tsitsitseng ha mananeo a phetolo le pusetso ya lefatshe a lokisang tlhokeho ya toka ya nako e fetileng le ho thusa ho hodisa moruo.2 Mopresidente Cyril Ramaphosa o etelletse pele mokete wa pusetso ya lefatshe, moo dihektere tse 4 586 tsa lefatshe di fuweng setjhaba sa KwaMkhwanazi ho la Empangeni, KwaZulu-Natal.3 Setjhaba sa KwaMkhwanazi se boetse se tla fumana dikapana tsa kamora phallo le tshehetso tse tla ba thusa ho fihlella tshebediso e hodimodimo ya leruo la lefatshe leo.

src: President Cyril Ramaphosa led a land restitution ceremony, where over 4 586 hectares of land were handed to the community of KwaMkhwanazi in Empangeni, KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Sena se tlosa ditjhaba ho tloha ho hoba dihwai tsa malapa a bona hore ebe dihwai tsa kgwebo le beng ba dikgwebo mekgahlelong e fapaneng ya matsete a lefatshe la bona.4 Mmuso o ikemiseditse ho tshehetsa boteng ba dikgwebo tse thuthuhang tsa temo, ho akgang diprojeke tse 262 tse amanang le phetolo ya lefatshe ho fa batjha le basadi molemo diporofenseng tsohle.

src: The KwaMkhwanazi community will also receive post-settlement packages and support that will assist them to maximise the potential wealth of the land.
tgt: Tshenyo ya disebediswa tsa setjhaba Kabinete e hlahisitse ngongoreho mabapi le tshenyo ya disebediswa tsa dipalangwang.

src: This shifts communities from subsistence to commercial participants and owners of businesses across the value chains of the assets on their land.
tgt: Sena se nyotobetsa boitlamo ba mmuso ba ho isa ditshebeletso ho ditjhaba tse neng di sotlehileng nakong ya kgale.

src: Government is committed to supporting the sustainability of emerging agricultural enterprises, which includes 262 land reform-related projects to benefit youth and women across all provinces.
tgt: Leha batho ba ka se kgotsofale ka tsela e kgolo, ha baa lokela ho senya thepa ya setjhaba.

src: This undermines government's commitment to take services to historically disadvantaged communities.
tgt: Tshenyo ena e hlokisa batho ba sotlehileng ditshebeletso tseo ba di hlokang e le kannete.2 Kabinete e kopa ditho tsa setjhaba hore di be sedi mme di sebetse mmoho le ditheo tsa molao hore ba ikarabellang diketsong tsena ba tshwarwe.

src: Cabinet calls on members of the public to be vigilant and work with law enforcement agencies to bring those responsible to account.
tgt: Tshebetso ya ho thonya Molaodi wa Botjhotjhisi ba Naha (NDPP)5.1 Kabinete e amohetse tsela e ntjha ya ho thonya NDPMopresidente Ramaphosa o thontse Sehlopha sa Keletso ho thonya batho ba tshwanelehang le ho tshwara dikopano tsa dipotso tsa mosebetsi le bona ho bona haeba ba tshwaneleha ho ka palama setulo sa Hlooho ya Bolaodi ba Botjhotjhisi ba Naha.

src: Cabinet further noted that the Justice, Crime Prevention and Security Cluster will deal with this matter accordingly.
tgt: Sehlopha seo se kopane lekgetlo la pele bekeng ena mme ho lebelletswe hore se tla fana ka lenane le lekgutshwane la mabitso a batho ba tshwanelehang ho Mopresidente pele ho la 7 Tshitwe Kahlolo ya Lekgotla la Molaotheo Kabinete e sekasekile Kahlolo ya Lekgotla la Molaotheo e mabapi le tshebediso, temo le ho ba le matekwane ke motho e moholo ha hae bakeng sa tshebediso ya hae le kamo ya sena.

src: Cabinet welcomed the new approach of appointing the NDPPresident Ramaphosa appointed the Advisory Panel to identify and conduct interviews with individuals worthy of consideration to occupy the position of the Head of the National Prosecuting Authority.
tgt: Ditho tsa setjhaba di koptjwa ho ithuta kahlolo ena kaha tshebediso ya matekwane sebakeng sa setjhaba e thibetswe.

src: Constitutional Court Judgement.1 Cabinet deliberated on the Constitutional Court Judgement on the use, cultivation and possession of cannabis by an adult person in private for his/her personal consumption and its impact.
tgt: Mme ho feta moo, kahlolo ena ha e ya kenya thekiso ya matekwane molaong.2 Kabinete e ananela hore kahlolo eo e itsheheditse ka melao e meng e kannang ya sebediswa mabapi le ho sebediswa, ho tshwara le ho lema matekwane.

src: Cabinet is taking advice on the matter.
tgt: Kabinete e ntse e batla keletso tabeng ena.

src: School Safety Summit.
tgt: Kopano ya Polokeho Dikolong.1 Kabinete e amohela Kopano ya Polokeho Dikolong e sa tswa tshwarwa tlasa boetapele ba Letona la Thuto ya Motheo Angie Motshekga.

src: Cabinet welcomes the recently held School Safety Summit hosted under the leadership of Basic Education Minister Angie Motshekga.
tgt: Kopano e kopantse baamehi ba thuto le ba ditaba tsa kantle hore ba fumane ditharollo ditabeng tsa tshireletso tseo dikolo di tobaneng le tsona, le ho fumana tsela ya ho ba le dikolo tse bolokehileng ho feta.2 Sena se latela diketsahalo tsa dikgoka dikolong tse itseng, ho kenyelletswa le lefu le sehlooho la titjhere e dilemo di 24, Monghadi Gadimang Daniel Mokolobate, ya hlabilweng ka thipa ke moithuti Sekolong sa Sekhondari sa Ramotshere ho la Zeerust, Leboya Bophirima.3 Baamehi bohle ba dumellane hore dikgoka ka kakaretso, le dikolong ka ho qolleha, ha di a amoheleha mme ho hlokeha tshebedisanommoho e eketsehileng ho netefatsa hore dikolo eba dibaka tse bolokehileng bakeng sa baithuti hammoho le matitjhere.

src: The summit brought together education and external stakeholders to find solutions to safety issues facing the country’s schools as well as to pave the way forward for safer environments in schools.
tgt: Dihlahlobo tsa Matriki Kabinete e lakalletsa baithuti bohle, haholo baithuti ba Kereiti ya 12, mahlohonolo nakong ena.

src: This follows incidents of violence at some schools, including the tragic death of the 24-year-old teacher, Mr Gadimang Daniel Mokolobate, who was fatally stabbed by a learner at the Ramotshere Secondary School in Zeerust, North West.
tgt: Ka lekgetlo la pele, selemong sena lefapha le boetse le tla tsamaisa tlhahlobo ka Puo ya Matsoho ya Aforika Borwa boemong ba Puo ya Lapeng bakeng sa baithuti ba 58 ba sa kgoneng ho utlwa dikolong tse Ditlhahlobo tsena di tla nka dibeke tse hlano le halofo mme ho tla qetwa ho ngolwa ka la 28 Pudungwana.2 Baithuti naheng ka bophara ba boetse ba tla tekena boitlamo ba boikgethelo ho itlamela ho netefatsa seriti sa ditlhahlobo ka ho se nke karolo diketsong dife kapa dife tse mpe.

src: The benefit of the additional designation will, amongst others, allow for further development of the ecotourism and promotion of access to sustainably managed resources for small-scale fisheries.
tgt: Ho latela Seratswana sa 9 sa tumellano, baamehi ba hloka ho hlahisa, ho lokisa le ho kenya tshebetsong NAP jwalo ka karolo e bohareng ya moralo wa ho lwantsha tlhaho ya mahwatata le ho thibela dikamo tsa komello.

src: The NAP seeks to contribute towards the conservation and sustainable use of our land and other natural resources.
tgt: Bili ena e labalabela ho matlafatsa kgokahano ya sistimi ya tlhokomelo ya bana le tshireletso ka tshebedisanommoho ya mafapha le makala.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the Children’s Amendment Bill in the Government Gazette for public comments.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela tsebiso ya Bili ya Tokiso ya Ditshebeletso tsa Poso ho Palamente.

src: The Bill seeks to strengthen coordination of the child-care and protection system through interdepartmental and intersectoral collaboration.
tgt: Bili e kenya tshebetsong Molawana o sisintsweng wa Pholisi e Kopaneng ya Naha ya ICT o ammohetsweng ke Kabinete ka Lwetse 2016.Diphetho tse rerilweng di tla etsa hore ho be le Ofisi ya Ditshebeletso tsa Poso ya Aforika Borwa e hlodisanang, e sebetsang hape e tshwarelletseng e fanang ka/e tsamaisang ditshebeletso tsohle le phihlello hammoho le phetoho ya lekala la diposo.

src: The amendments respond to the North Gauteng High Court Judgement of November 2017, wherein the Department of Social Development was ordered to prepare and introduce the necessary amendments to the Children’s Act, 2005 (Act 38 of 2005) in respect to the legal solution towards the management of the foster-care system.
tgt: Bili e boetse e fana hape le ka matla a ho fana ka diaterese tsa bodulo ho ditjhaba tsa mahaeng le tse dulang metseng ya marena.

src: Cabinet approved the introduction of the Postal Services Amendment Bill to Parliament.
tgt: Bili e se e fetile mokgahlelo wa tshekatsheko ke setjhaba.

src: The Bill gives effect to the National Integrated ICT Policy White Paper that was approved by Cabinet in September 2016.The intended outcomes are to have a competitive, viable and sustainable South African Post Office that provides/facilitates universal services and access as well as the transformation of the postal sector.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse Tlang Kopano ya Matsete ya Matjhaba ya Aforika BorwaMopresidente Ramaphosa ka Labohlano, 26 Mphalane 2018, o tla tsamaisa Kopano ya Matsete ya pele ya Aforika Borwa e tla tshwarelwa Sandton Convention Centre ho la Johannesburg.

src: South African International Investment ConferencePresident Ramaphosa will on Friday, 26 October 2018, preside over South Africa’s inaugural Investment Conference at the Sandton Convention Centre in Johannesburg.
tgt: Kopano ya Sehlopha sa Dinaha tse Mashome a Mabedi (G20) Mopresidente Ramaphosa o memilwe ke Tjhanselara ya Federale ya Jeremane, Ngaka Angela Merkel, ho nka karolo ho Kopano ya Matsete ya G20 – Kgwebo ya Jeremane le Tumellano le Dinaha tsa (CwA), le Kopano ya Kgwebo, tseo bobedi di tla tshwarelwa ho la Berlin, Jeremane ka la 30 Mphalane 2018.Kopano ya Matsete ya G20 e tla kopanya kgwebo ya Jeremane le Dinaha tsa CwA hore ba utulle menyetla ya tsetelo tlasa moralo wa G20 wa Selekane le Aforika.

src: This is part of a combination of efforts to attract investments and grow our economy.
tgt: Batsetedi ba Jeremane ba tla hlahisa diprojeke tsa bohlokwa tse di ntseng di tswelapele Dinaheng tsa CwA le ho batla menyetla e meng kontinenteng.

src: Additionally, the four investment envoys who were appointed by the President will report back to the conference on progress made.
tgt: Mopresidente o tla ya kopanong ka boemo ba Modulasetulo-mmoho wa Sehlopha sa Aforika sa Keletso sa G. Kopano ya G20 e mabapi le CwA e tla shebane le ditsela tseo ka tsona G20, dinaha tsa Aforika le ditsi tsa ntshetsopele di ka sebetsang mmoho ho phahamisa tsetelo ya poraefete le bonkakarolo ba moruo dinaheng tsa Aforika.

src: Group of Twenty (G20) SummitPresident Ramaphosa has been invited by the Federal Chancellor of Germany, Dr Angela Merkel, to participate in the G20 Investment Summit – German Business and the Compact with Africa (CwA) Countries, and a Business Roundtable, both of which will be held in Berlin, Germany on 30 October 2018.The G20 Investment Summit will bring together German business and CwA Countries to explore investment opportunities under the framework of the G20 Partnership with Africa.
tgt: Kopano e boetse e tla etsa hape le mosebetsi wa boitokiso lekaleng lena bakeng sa Kopano ya G20 e tla tshwarwa ho la Buenos Aires, Argentina.

src: German investors will present flagship projects currently undertaken in the CwA Countries and explore further opportunities on the continent.
tgt: Beke ya Tsepamiso ya Imbizo ya Naha Ditho tsa Phethahatso di tla nka karolo lenaneong la GCIS la Beke ya borobong ya Tsepamiso ya Imbizo ya Naha ya tsamaiso ya bohlano ya demokrasi, e tla qala ka la 12 ho isa la 25 Pudungwana 2018.

src: The G20 Conference on the CwA will focus on ways in which the G20, African countries and development institutions can cooperate to promote private investment and economic participation in African states.
tgt: Beke ya Tsepamiso ya Imbizo e tla fana ka monyetla wa hore ditho tsa Phethahatso ya Naha, hammoho le baetapele ba mmuso ba porofense le ba lehae ho tshware dikopano tsa setjhaba le di-Izimbizo naheng ka bophara, nakong ena, ho bontshahatsa ho kenngwa tshebetso ke mmuso ha Moralo wa Thero wa Nako e Bohareng wa 2014-2019 le ho arabela ditaba tse hlahiswang ke baahi, tse amang polokeho, kgolo le ntshetsopele ya ditjhaba.

src: The meeting will also undertake preparatory work in this field for the G20 Summit in Buenos Aires, Argentina.
tgt: Dibeke tsena tse pedi tsa dipontsho di etsahala hara diketekelo tsa dilemokgolo tsa bahale ba ntwa ya kgethollo e leng Mama Albertina Sisulu le Tata Nelson Mandela, bao bobedi ba neng ba dumela ka matla ho dipuisano le dikopano tsa kgafetsa le ditjhaba tseo ba di sebeletsang.

src: National Imbizo Focus WeekMembers of the Executive will participate in the GCIS’s 9th National Imbizo Focus Week of the fifth democratic administration, which will take place from 12 to 25 November 2018.
tgt: MelaetsaDitebohiso Kabinete e lebohisa Letona la Bophelo bo Botle, Ngaka Aaron Motsoaledi, ya fumaneng dikgau tse pedi tsa bohlokwa tsa Kochon, moketeng wa dikgau o neng o tshwaretswe The Hague, ho la Netherlands.

src: The two weeks of activism takes place against the backdrop of celebrations of the centenaries of Struggle icons Mama Albertina Sisulu and Tata Nelson Mandela, both of whom epitomised the value of regular consultation and interaction with the communities they served.
tgt: Durban ho la KwaZulu-Natal e boetse e ananetswe jwalo ka Motseteropo o Tswang pele wa Ketelo Aforika mme wa hape le sehlooho sa bohlokwa sa Boemakepe bo Tswang pele ba Dikepe tsa Maeto ho la Aforika.

src: Cabinet congratulates the Minister of Health, Dr Aaron Motsoaledi, who received two prestigious Kochon prizes, at an award ceremony held at The Hague, The Netherlands.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela ho bapalwa ha filimi ya ka naheng e bitswang Nommer 37 ya moetsi wa difilimi Joshua Bradley ho la Amerika ka la 2 Pudungwana 2018.

src: The first prize is in the Minister’s individual capacity for his role and political leadership in the fight against tuberculosis (TB) globally.
tgt: Filimi ena e buwang ka botlokotsebe e thehetsweng sebakeng sa Cape Flats e tsheheditswe ka ditjhelete ke Lefapha la Kgwebo le Indasteri ka morero wa lona wa Kgokelo ya Baetsi ba Difilimi ba Thuthuhang ba Batsho ba Aforika Borwa.

src: The second prize, which the Minister will share with the Right Honourable Nick Hebert, Member of Parliament (MP) in the United Kingdom, will be in their capacity as co-chairs of the Global TB Caucus of MPs from all over the world.
tgt: Sena se tla kenya letsoho ho hoheleng tsetelo e tswang kantle e otlolohileng ho indasteri ya difilimi ya Aforika Borwa.

src: The Kochon Prize is awarded annually to individuals and/or organisations that have made a significant contribution to combating TB either in their countries or globally.
tgt: Matshediso Kabinete hammoho le Mopresidente Ramaphosa ba fetisitse tlhomoho le matshediso:19.1 bakeng sa ho feta ha batho ba fetang 27, kotsing ya makoloi a mangata mmileng wa N1 Leboya ho la Limpopo.

src: Cabinet welcomes the World Travel Awards 2018 which voted South Africa as Africa’s Leading Destination.
tgt: Basebedisi ba mebila ba kgothaletswa ho ba sedi mebileng ya rona le ho netefatsa hore ba latela melao ya tsela ka dinako tsohle.2 bakeng sa ho feta ha molwanedi wa tokoloho, Mama Agnes Msimang.

src: Durban in KwaZulu-Natal was also recognised as Africa’s Leading City Destination and scooped the prestigious title of Africa’s Leading Cruise Port.
tgt: Mama Msimang ene e le molwanedi ya itlammeng wa ditaba tsa bong hape e le Motlatsi wa Mehleng wa Mopresidente wa Mokgatlo wa Basadi wa African National Congress (ANCWL).

src: Cape Town, in the Western Cape landed the title of Africa’s Leading Festival and Event Destination.
tgt: E ne e le e mong wa basadi ba bangata ba ileng ba etella pele ditjhaba Aforika Borwa ho pota kgahlano le puso ya kgethollo.

src: The crime thriller set in the Cape Flats was funded by the Department of Trade and Industry through its South African Emerging Black Filmmakers Incentive scheme.
tgt: Tshebeletso ya lepato e tla qala ka 08:00 kerekeng ya Our Lady of Cedars Catholic Church e Woodmead, Johannesburg.3 bakeng sa ho feta ha molwanedi wa tokoloho le moamohedi wa Kgau ya Naha ya Mendi bakeng sa Sebete ka Silifere, Monghadi Eric “Stalin” Mtshali.4 bakeng sa ho feta ha mohale wa ANC Moss Chikane.

src: at the passing of Struggle icon, Mama Agnes Msimang.
tgt: Boto ya SENTECH SOC LIMITED:a. Mofumahatsana Maureen Makole Manyama (molaodi eo eseng wa phethahatso) leb.

src: Mama Msimang was a committed gender activist and former Deputy President of the African National Congress (ANC) Women’s League.
tgt: Mofumahatsana Precious Nompumelelo Sibiya (molaodi eo eseng wa phethahatso).

src: She was amongst countless women who mobilised their communities across South Africa against the apartheid system.
tgt: Ho thongwa-botjha ha Mofumahatsana Gugulethu Brightness Nokukhanya (Poppy) Khoza jwalo ka Molaodi: Difofane tsa Setjhaba wa Boto ya Aforika Borwa ya Setheo sa Difofane tsa Setjhaba.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 7 November 2018 at Tuynhuys in Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e kopane ka Laboraro, 7 Pudungwana 2018, Tuynhuys e Motse Kapa.

src: Presidential Gender-Based Violence and Femicide Summit Cabinet welcomes the successful deliberations of the Presidential Gender Based Violence and Femicide Summit held on 01 and 02 November.
tgt: Dintlha tsa Ha jwale Seboka sa Boporesidente se Kgahlano le Dikgola le Dipolao tsa Basadi Kabinete e amohela katleho ya dipuisano tsa Seboka sa boMoporesidente se Kgahlano le Dikgoka tsa bong le Dipolao tsa Basadi se tshwerweng ka la 01 le 02 Pudungwana 2018.

src: The Summit has confirmed the urgency of forging consensus on dealing with the crisis of gender-based violence, discrimination against women and gender disparities.
tgt: Seboka se netefaditse potlako ya ho theha tumellano ka ho shebana le qaka ya dikgoka tsa bong, kgethollo e kgahlano le basadi le diphapano tsa bong.

src: Government has agreed to conduct a review of national plans to end gender-based violence and the development of a National Action Plan on gender-based violence.
tgt: Mmuso o tjhaetse monwana ho hlahlobisa meralo ya naha ya hofedisa dikgoka tsa bong le ntshetsopele ya Moralo wa Tshebetso wa Naha wa ho lwantsha dikgoka tsa bong.

src: It remains committed to work with all stakeholders to ensure that we dramatically reduce levels of gender-based violence – and ultimately eradicate it.
tgt: O tswella ho itlama ho sebetsa le bohle ba nang le seabo ho netefatsa hore re fedisa maemo a dikgoka tsa bong ka sekgahla – mme qetellong re di fedise ka botlalo.

src: Cabinet calls on all South Africans to work together to fundamentally change attitudes, practices and institutions to end violence against women.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAfrika Borwa ho sebedisana mmoho ho fetola motheo wa maitshwaro, ditlwaelo le ditheho ho fedisa dikgoka tse kgahlano le basadi.

src: Cabinet welcomes the successful Investment Conference that took place in October in Sandton, Johannesburg.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela katleho ya Seboka sa Letsete se ileng sa nka sebaka ka Mphalane mane Sandton, Johannesburg.

src: The Investment Conference enabled South Africa to garner in access of R290 billion in investment commitments across different sectors of the economy.
tgt: Seboka sena sa Letsete se entse hore Afrika Borwa e kgone ho bokella ditshepiso tsa boitlamo ba ho tsetella R290 bilione mekgahlelong e fapaneng ya moruo.

src: This adds to the pledges of over R400 billion that were received during the investment drive by the special envoys and from various countries during state visits.
tgt: Sena ke hodima ditshepiso tsa boitlamo ba ho tsetela tjhelete e fetang R400 bilione tse ileng tsa fumanwa nakong ya letsholo la letsete ka baemedi ba ikgethileng le ho tswa dinaheng tse fapaneng nakong ya maeto a mmuso.

src: The Conference was attended by more than 1 000 delegates, drawn from more than 35 countries.
tgt: Ho ne ho le barumuwa ba fetang 1 000 ba neng ba le teng Sebokeng sena, ho tswa dinaheng tse Meya le maikutlo e ne e le ya lethabo mme le naha ya bontshahatsa menyetla ya letsete le boiteko ba maano a thusang ho theha tikoloho e dumellang letsete.

src: The spirit and mood was upbeat and the country showcased new opportunities for investment and policy-initiatives that are helping to create an investment-friendly environment.
tgt: Kabinete e lebohisa sehlopha se sebeditseng Sebokeng sena mme e thabetse ho fumantshwa dipehelo tsa ka mehla ka ho phethahatsa boitlamo bo entsweng.

src: As South Africa and the rest of Africa continues to move on a higher trajectory towards growing the economy of the continent, Cabinet also welcomes the inaugural Africa Investment Forum, currently taking place up until the 9th November, in Johannesburg.
tgt: Jwalo ka ha Afrika Borwa le Afrika ka kakaretso di tswela ho phahamisa moruo wa kontinente, Kabinete e boela e amohela tlhomamiso ya Foramo ya Letsete ya Africa, le ntseng le nka sebaka ho fihlela ka la 09 Pudungwana 2018, Johannesburg.

src: The Africa Investment Forum was convened by the African Development Bank.
tgt: Foramo ya Letsete ya Afrika e tshwerwe ke Banka ya Ntshetsopele ya Afrika.

src: It aims to build on current successes by bringing together public and private sector investors to chart a new growth path for the entire African Continent.
tgt: E ikemiseditse ho aha katleho ka ho tlisa mmoho batsetedi ba makala a mmuso le a poraefete ho rala tsela e ntjha ya kgolo molemong wa Kontinente ya Afrika yohle.

src: The recently held G20 Africa Conference further boosts our growth prospects through the various commitments that promote private investment and economic participation in African states as part of the Compact with Africa Initiative.
tgt: Seboka sa G20 sa Afrika se neng se tshwerwe ha mmamorao tjena se tswella ho matlafatsa kgonahalo ya kgolo ka boitlamo bo fapaneng bo phahamisang letsete la poraefete le ho ba le seabo morung wa dinaha tsa Afrika jwalo ka karolo ya Mokgatlo wa Tumellano le Boiteko ba Afrika.

src: The Compact with Africa Initiative is co-chaired by South Africa and Germany through the Africa Advisory Group.
tgt: Mokgatlo wa Tumellano le Boiteko ba Afrika e dulwasetulong ka kopanelo ke Afrika Borwa le Jeremane ka Sehlopha sa Dikeletso sa Afrika.

src: Cabinet also welcomed the recently launched R50 million Phuthaditjhaba Industrial Park in the Free State which will promote industrialization and increase local job creation and growth in that province.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya boela e amohela ho bulwa ha Paka ya Indasteri ya Phuthaditjhaba e boleng ba R50 milione Foreistata e tla phahamisa tshebetso ya diindasteri le ho theha mesebetsi ya lehae le kgolo porofenseng.
