tgt: Ngaka Keith Ivor Jacobsk.

src: Inge Maree Vieiram.
tgt: Inge Maree Vieiram.

src: Dr Prittish Dalao.
tgt: Ngaka Prittish Dalao.

src: Ulandi Exnerp.
tgt: Ulandi Exnerp.

src: Ms Florence Rabadaq.
tgt: Mme Florence Rabadaq.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 21 November 2018 at Tuynhuys in Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e kopane ka Laboraro, 21 Pudungwana 2018, Tuynhuys e Motse Kapa.

src: Cabinet welcomes the successful inaugural Africa Investment Forum held from 7 to 9 November 2018 at the Sandton Convention Centre in Gauteng.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela tlhomamiso e atlehileng ya Seboka sa Letsete sa Afrika se ileng sa tshwarwa ho tloha ka la 7 ho isa ho la 9 Pudungwana 2018 mane Setsing sa Dipuisano sa Sandton, Gauteng.

src: African governments and businesses, international financial institutions and other development partners focused on making Africa the next global frontier in investment.
tgt: Mmeso le dikgwebo tsa Afrika, ditheho tsa ditjhelete tsa matjhabeng le balekane ba bang ba ntshetsopele ba tsipameng ho etsa Afrika moetapele ya ka sehloohong lefatsheng ho tsa botsetedi.

src: At the close of the conference 45 deals, worth US$32 billion, were concluded to benefit the continent.
tgt: Phethelong ya seboka ditumellano tse 45, tsa boleng ba US$32 bilione, di ile tsa phethelwa molemong wa kontinente.

src: Of that, South Africa will benefit from US$6.8 billion in investment.
tgt: Tjheleteng eo, Afrika Borwa e tla e fumantshwa ke US$6.8 bilione ya botsetedi.

src: African Union (AU) Summit.
tgt: Seboka sa Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tsa Afrika (AU).

src: Cabinet is encouraged by deliberations at the AU Summit held in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia on 17 and 18 November 2018, where President Cyril Ramaphosa participated.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaditswe ke dipuisano tse bileng Sebokeng sa AU mane Addis Ababa, Ethiopia ka la 17 le 18 Pudungwana 2018, moo Moporesidente Cyril Ramaphosa a ileng a ba le seabo.

src: The Extraordinary Session deliberated on the ongoing reform processes which are intended to establish an effective, efficient and re-energized AU that is capable of achieving continental priorities and goals set out in Agenda 2063, which is a strategic framework for the socio-economic transformation of Africa over the next 50 years.
tgt: Mokgahlelo ona o Ikgethileng o ile wa buisana ka ditsamaiso tsa tlhabollo tse ikemiseditseng ho theha AU e sebetsang, e hlophisitsweng le ho matlafatswa botjha, e kgonang ho fihlella maikemisetso a kontinente le dipheo tse hlahellang ho Ajenda 2063, eo e leng leano la mokgwatshebetso la ho fetola moruo wa setjhaba wa Afrika dilemong tse 50 tse tlang.

src: The reform of the AU is an ongoing process, with some of its recommendations already implemented, particularly in relation to the commitment to have member states of the AU assume greater ownership of financing the organisation.
tgt: Ntjhafatso ya AU ke tshebetso e tswelangpele, ke tse ding tsa ditshitshinyo tse se ntseng di phethisitswe, haholoholo tse amanang le boitlamo ba hore dinaha tsa ditho tsa AU di be le taolo e kgolo ya ho nehela mokgatlo ka tjhelete.

src: More countries continue to sign the African Continental Free Trade Agreement to ensure the Continent realises the continent-wide free-trade agreement.
tgt: Boholo ba dinaha di tswella ho tekena Tumellano ya Bohwebi bo Senang Ditshitiso Kontinenteng ya Afrika ho netefatsa hore Kontinente e lokolla tumellano ya bohwebi bo senang ditshitiso kontinenteng ka bophara.

src: Strategic Partnership with the European Union (EU).
tgt: Selekane sa Lewa la tshebetso le Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tsa Yuropa (EU).

src: Cabinet is pleased with the positive outcome of the 7th South Africa – EU Summit held on 15 November in Belgium.
tgt: Kabinete e thabetse sephetho sa Seboka sa EU – sa bo7 sa Afrika Borwa se ileng sa tshwarwa ka la 15 Pudungwana 2018 mane Belgium.

src: The outcomes and commitments made at the summit build on our unprecedented drive to place economic growth and job creation at the centre of South Africa’s national agenda.
tgt: Diphetho le boitlamo bo ileng ba etswa sebokeng seo bo tlatseletsa tshebetso e sa tlwalehang ya ho beha kgolo ya moruo le ho theha mesebetsi bohareng ba ajenda ya naha ya Afrika Borwa.

src: South Africa is the only African country and one of the 10 countries globally that has a Strategic Partnership with the EThe EU is South Africa’s largest trading partner and largest foreign investor as a bloc, representing 73.7% of total Foreign Direct Investment stocks in the country.
tgt: Afrika Borwa ke yona feela naha ya Afrika le e nngwe ho dinaha tse 10 tsa matjhabeng tse nang le Selekane sa Lewa la tshebetso le EEU ke molekane wa kgwebisano le motsetedi wa naheng tse ding e moholoholo wa Afrika Borwa jwalo ka mokgatlo wa dinaha, e emetse 73.7% ya kakaretso ya dihb stoko tsa Tsetelo e Tobileng Naheng e nngwe naheng.

src: President Ramaphosa this week hosted the President of the Federal Republic of Germany, Mr Frank-Walter Steinmeier, on a State Visit to South Africa.
tgt: Bekeng ena Moporesidente Ramaphosa o ile a amohela Mopresidente wa Rephaboliki ya Federale ya Germany, Monghadi Frank-Walter Steinmeier, Leetong la Semmuso mona Afrika Borwa.

src: Germany is one of the largest foreign investors in South Africa, with more than 600 German companies having subsidiaries or production in the country, sustaining about 100 000 jobs.
tgt: Germany ke e nngwe ya batsetedi ba matjhabeng ba baholoholo mona Afrika Borwa, ka dikhamphani tse fetang 600 tsa Germany tse laolwang ke dikhamphani tse ding kapa tsa tlhahiso ka hara naha, tse nyehelana ka mesebetsi e ka bang 100 000.

src: This State Visit resulted in the signing of trade and investment agreements between the two countries, and afforded both leaders an opportunity to discuss multilateral issues and cooperate closely as non-permanent members of the United Nations (UN) Security Council for a two-year term from 2019 to Land reform.
tgt: Leeto lena la Semmuso le ile la phethela ka ho tekena ditumellano tsa kgwebisano le botsetedi dipakeng tsa naha tsena tse pedi, le ho nehela baetapele ka bobedi monyetla wa ho buisana ka dintlha tsa ditumellano tsa naha le tshebedisano ka botlalo jwalo ka ditho tsa nakwana tsa Lekgotla la Tshireletso la Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tsa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) ka nako ya dilemo tse pedi ho tloha ka 2019 ho isa Kabobotjha ya Mobu.

src: Cabinet noted that Parliament’s Joint Constitutional Review Committee adopted its report that is in favour of amending Section 25 of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse hore Komiti ya Kopanelo ya Tlhahlobo ya Molaotheo ya Palamenteng e ananetse pehelo e tshihetsang ho fetola Mokgahlelo wa 25 wa Molaotheo wa Rephaboliki ya Afrika Borwa wa 1996.

src: The amendment will make it possible for the State to expropriate land without compensation in the public interest.
tgt: Phetolo ena e tla etsa hore Mmuso o kgone ho phethahatsa kamoho ya mobu ntle le ditlhapiso molemong wa setjhaba.

src: The committee’s report is expected to be tabled in the National Assembly for debate.
tgt: Pehelo ena ya komiti e lebetswe ho hlahiswa ka pela Seboka sa Naha hore ho ngangisanwe ka yona.

src: A public consultation process saw numerous organisations making submissions on the Bill and public hearings were held in all nine provinces.
tgt: Tsamaiso ya dipuisano tsa setjhaba e bone mekgatlo e mengata e nyehelana ka dikgothaletso tsa Bili mme le dipitso tsa setjhaba di ile tsa tshwarwa diporofenseng tse robong kaofela.

src: The Constitution has so far been amended 17 times through a consultative and inclusive process.
tgt: Ho fihlela ha jwale, Molatheo o se o fetotswe makgetlo a 17 ka tsamaiso ya ho thonya maikutlo a baahi le ho kenyeletsa mehopolo ya bohle.

src: Government remains committed to a responsible land reform approach that is in the best interests of everyone.
tgt: Mmuso o tswella ho itlama ka mokgwa wa kabobotjha ya mobu o nang le boikarabelo molemong wa bohle.

src: Cabinet affirms that government respects the rule of law and will, at all times, act in accordance with the Constitution.
tgt: Kabinete e tiisa hore mmuso o hlompha molao le phethatsa molao, ka dinako tsohle, le ho sebetsa o ipapisitse le Molaotheo.

src: Constitutional Court judgement.
tgt: Kahlolo ya Lekgotla la Molaotheo.

src: Cabinet welcomes the Constitutional Court judgment which ruled that the Minerals and Petroleum Resources Development Act, 2002 (Act 28 of 2002) which governs the awarding of mining rights, must be read concurrently with the Interim Protection of Informal Land Rights Act, 1996 (Act 31 of 1996), which protects vulnerable land rights.
tgt: Kabinete e amohela kahlolo ya Lekgotla la Molaotheo e phethetseng ka hore Molao wa Ntshetsopele ya Dihlahiswa tsa Petoroliamo le Dirashwa, wa 2002 (Molao wa 28 wa 2002) o laolang ho nehelana ka ditokelo tsa dimaene, o tlameha o balwe mmoho le Molao wa Tshireletso ya Ditokelo tsa Mobu tse seng Molaong, wa 1996 (Molao wa 31 wa 1996), o sireletsang ditokelo tsa baahi ba mobu o senang tshireletso ya molao.

src: The victory of the Lesetlheng community in North West signals a start to the recognition of land rights of which South Africa’s historically oppressed people had been deprived for generations.
tgt: Katleho ya setjhaba sa Lesetlheng mane Bokone Bophirama e bontsha qalo ya ho lemoha ditokelo tsa mobu tsa batho ba Afrika Borwa ba neng ba hateletswe nakong e fetileng tseo ba neng ba di tingwe ka melokoloko.

src: Where mining impacts on settlements, families and communities, people directly affected by mining must consent to any changes affecting their land rights.
tgt: Moo merafo e amang bodulo, malapa le ditjhaba, bathong ba angwang ke merafo ka kotloloho ba tlameha ho nehelana ka tumello ho diphetho di fe kapa di fe tse ka amang ditokelo tsa bona tsa mobu.

src: Cabinet welcomes and congratulates the government departments and entities that continues to consistently receive clean- audit outcomes.
tgt: Sephetho sa Bohlakisi Kabinete e amohela le ho lebohisa mafapha le dikgwebo tsa mmuso tse tswellang ho fumana sephetho se hlakileng sa bohlakisi.

src: This comes after the release by the Auditor General (AG) Kimi Makwetu of the Public Finance Management Audit Report of the 2017/18 financial year.
tgt: Sena se tla ka mora sephetho sa Pehelo ya Bohlakisi ba Tsamaiso ya Ditjhelete tsa Setjhaba ya Kantoro ya Mohlakisi Kakaretso (AG) Kimi Makwetu, ya selemo sa ditjhelete sa 2017/18.

src: Cabinet is however concerned with the report that shows an overall deterioration in the audit results of some national and provincial government departments and their entities.
tgt: Empa Kabinete o ngongoriswa ke pehelo e bontshang mpefalo ka kakaretso sephethong sa bohlakisi ba mafapha a mang a mmuso wa naha le a porofense le dikgwebo tsa mmuso.

src: The signing into law of the Public Audit Amendment Bill by President Ramaphosa, which will strengthen the work of the Office of the AG, will assist in holding accountable those that continue to have disregard for the governance framework.
tgt: Ho tekenwa ha molao wa Bili ya Phetolo ya Bohlakisi ba Ditjhelete tsa Setjhaba ke Moporesidente Ramaphosa, ho tla matlafatsa mosebetsi wa Kantoro ya AG, ho tla thusa ka boikarabellong ha batho ba tswellang ho iphapanyetsa leano la tshebetso ya puso.

src: Cabinet encourages all departments and entities to work on remedial interventions on all the issues flagged by the AG and to monitor progress regularly to address issues before the next audit cycle.
tgt: Kabinete e kgothaletsa mafapha le dikgwebo tsohle ho sebedisana le ho fumana bonamodi ba dintlha tsohle tse tshwailweng ke AG le ho hlahloba tshebetso kgafetsa le ho lokisa dintlha tseo pele ho nako ya bohlakisi hape.

src: Safety and Security.
tgt: Polokeho le Tshiriletseho.

src: Cabinet pledges support to the National Safer Festive Season Campaign that was launched by Police Minister Bheki Cele under the theme “Operation Quiet Storm”.
tgt: Kabinete e itlamme ho tshihetsa Letsholo la Naha la Polokeho Nakong ya Matsatsi a Phomolo le ileng la thakgolwa ke Letona la Seponesa Bheki Cele ka tlasa mookotaba wa “Operation Quiet Storm”.

src: The campaign aims to make South Africa a safer place as we approach the year-end holiday season.
tgt: Letsholo lena le ikemiseditse ho etsa Afrika Borwa tulo e bolokehileng ha e le mona re atumetse nako ya matsatsi a phomolo a mafelo a selemo.

src: The South African Police Service will conduct nationwide operations in every town, village and township until the end of January 2019.They will focus on visible policing, whilst conducting special crime awareness and prevention operations.
tgt: Tshebeletso ya Sepolesa sa Afrika Borwa (SAPS) e tla tshwara ditshebeletso toropong, motseng le lekeisheneng le leng le le leng ho fihlela mafelong a Pherekgong 2019.

src: Cabinet appeals to all people in South Africa to continue cooperating with the police in keeping our communities safe.
tgt: Ba tla tsepama letsholong la ho bonahatsa maponesa, ha ka lehlakoreng le leng ba ntse ba ntse ba sebedisana le masolo a tlhokomediso le thibelo ya ditlolo tsa molao tse ikgethileng.

src: Parents and guardians are also advised to be extra vigilant in caring for their children during the upcoming festive season.
tgt: Batswadi le bahlokomedi ba eletswa hore ba be kelahloko ha ho tla ho tlhokomelo ya bana ba bona nakong ya matsatsi a phomolo.

src: Cabinet also pledges support to the 2018 Festive Season Road Safety campaign, launched by the Minister of Transport, Dr Blade Nzimande, in Limpopo at the weekend.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e itlama ho tshihetsa Letsholo la Naha la Polokeho la Nako ya Matsatsi a Phomolo, le thakgotsweng ke Letona la Dipalangwang, Ngaka Blade Nzimande, Limpopo mafelong a beke.

src: The launch coincided with the annual two-day Road Safety Summit and the UN’s World Day of Remembrance for victims of road crashes.
tgt: Phatlalatso ena e tsamaisana le Seboka sa matsatsi a mabedi sa Polokeho Mebileng le Letsatsi la Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tsa Matjhaba a Kopaneng la ho Hopola Mahlatsipa a dikotsi tsa mebileng.

src: It is in the best interests of our well-being that we all play a part in ensuring a safer festive season by driving responsibly and obeying the rules of the road.
tgt: Ke molemong wa tshireletseho ya maphelo a rona hore re bapale karolo ho netefatseng hore nako ya matsatsi a phomolo re tshireletsehile ka ho kganna ka maikarabelo le ho ikobela melao ya tsela.

src: Maputo-Catembe Bridge.
tgt: Borokgo ba Maputo-Catembe.

src: Cabinet congratulates the South African engineers involved in the historic development of the longest suspension bridge in Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e lebohisa dienjenere tsa Afrika Borwa tse bileng le seabo ntshetsopeleng ena e entseng nalane ya borokgo ba fanyeho bo bolelele ka ho fetisisa Afrika.

src: The Maputo-Catembe Bridge was built by the China Road and Bridge Corporation and connects Maputo in Mozambique and KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Borokgo ba Maputo-Catembe bo ile ba ahwa ke China Road and Bridge Corporation e le ho kopantsha Maputo Mozambique le KwaZulu-Natal.

src: President of Mozambique, Mr Filipe Nyusi, inaugurated the three-kilometre-long Maputo-Catembe Bridge, which was built over four years at a cost of US$785 million.
tgt: Moporesidente wa Mozambique, Monghadi Filipe Nyusi, o butse Borokgo ba Maputo-Catembe bo bolelele ba dikilomitara tse tharo, bo ileng ba ahwa ka nako ya dilemo tse nne ka ditjeho tsa US$785 milione.

src: This development will stimulate trade and tourism between Mozambique and South Africa with travel time between Maputo to Kosi Bay in KwaZulu-Natal’s East Coast border post drastically reduced from six hours to 90 minutes.
tgt: Ntshetsopele ena e tla kgothaletsa kgwebisano le bohahlaudi dipakeng tsa Mozambique le Afrika Borwa ka nako e fokotsehileng haholo ho tloha dihoreng tse tsheletseng ho ya ho metsotso e 90 e dipakeng tsa Maputo le moedi wa Kosi Bay o Lebopong le Botjhabela la KwaZulu.

src: Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Kabinete Beke ya Tsebiso ya Bobehaditaba ka Lenaneo la Tshebetso ya Mmuso.

src: Cabinet was apprised on the progress reports on the priority outcomes for the period starting 1 April 2018 to 30 September 2018.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya tsebiswa ka dipehelo tsa tshebetso ka diphetho tse ka sehloohong nakong e qalang ka la 1 Mmesa 2018 ho ya ho 30 Loetse 2018.

src: Departments working within the clusters to implement the 14 priority outcomes continue to achieve their respective deliverables.
tgt: Mafapha a sebetsang ka hara mekgahlelo ya ho kenya diphetho tse sehloohong tse 14 a tswelapele ho fihlela ditshebeletso tsa ona tse ikgethileng.

src: These outcomes are derived from the 2014-2019 Medium Term Strategic Framework and from the National Development Plan’s Vision 2030.
tgt: Diphetho tsena di tswa ho Moralo wa Lewa la Nako e Bohareng (MTSF) wa 2014-2019 le ho tswa ho Ponelope ya 2030 ya Morero wa Ntshetsopele ya Naha (NDP).

src: Cabinet has approved the action required to deal with the challenges affecting implementation.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse mosebetsi o hlokehang ho tobana le diphephetso tse hahlamelang phethahatso.

src: The reports are published on the DPME website (WEBTOKEN).
tgt: Dipehelo di phatladitswe wepsaeteng ya Lefapha la Merero, Bodisa le Tlhatlhobo ya Tshebetso (DPME) (WEBTOKEN).

src: Automotive Production and Development Programme (APDP).
tgt: Leano la Tlhahiso le Ntshetsopele ya Dipalangwang (APDP).

src: Cabinet approved the extension of the APDP from 2021 to 2035 with amendments to support the South African Automotive Masterplan (SAAM).
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana katoloso ya APDP ho tloha ka 2021 ho ya ho 2035 ka diphetoho tse tla Leano le Hlokolosi la Dipalangwang la Afrika Borwa (SAAM).

src: The SAAM focuses on six areas: Local market optimisation Regional market development Localisation Infrastructure development Industry transformation, and Technology and associated skills development.
tgt: SAAM e tsepame ho mekgahlelo e tsheletseng e leng Ntshetsopele ya dimaraka tsa lebatoweng Dihlahiswa tsa selehae Ntshetsopele ya meralo ya motheo Phetolo ya Diindasteri, le Thekelonoji le ntshetsopele ya bokgoni bo amehang.

src: The amendments seek amongst others to encourage higher levels of local value addition to create more opportunities for additional employment.
tgt: Diphetoho tsena ho tse ding di tla kgothaletsa maemo a phahameng a nang le boleng ba selehae ho theha menyetla e meng e tla eketsa mesebetsi.

src: Monitoring and evaluation of the programme and related industry trends are further enhanced to ensure progress towards the SAAM vision and objectives.
tgt: Hlahlobo le tekolo ya leano le mekgwa e tla atoloswa ho ya pele ho netefatsa tswelopele ho ya ponelopele ya SAAM le maikemisetso a lona.

src: .The Minister of Trade and Industry, Dr Rob Davies, will brief the media on these amendments on Friday, 23 November 2018.Bills.
tgt: Letona la Kgwebisano le Diindasteri (dti), Ngaka Rob Davies, o tla buisana le ba bo raditaba ka diphetoho tsena ka Labohlano, la 23 Pudungwana 2018.Dibili.

src: Cabinet approved for the Public Audit Excess Fee Bill of 2018 to be introduced in Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana ntlha ya hore Bili ya Bohlakisi ba Ditjeo tse Fetang Ditekanyetso ya 2018 e tla phatlalatswa Palamenteng.

src: The Bill supports changes to the regulation of fees for Auditor General functions in the Public Audit Amendment Act, assented to by the President and promulgated earlier this week.
tgt: Bili e tla nehela Kantoro ya Mohlakisi wa Kakaretso matla a ho nka mehato ho netefatsa hore ditahlehelo tsa ditjhelete tse hlahelang Mmuso, haeba ho kgonahala, di a busetswa le ho hlahisa tsohle tse belaelwang tse bakang tshebediso e bohlaswa ya ditjhelete hore di fuputswe.

src: The Public Audit Excess Fee Bill proposes that audit fees in excess of 1% of expenditure of municipalities and certain other public institutions payable to the Auditor-General, be treated as a direct charge against the National Revenue Fund.
tgt: Bili e ikemiseditse ho matlafatsa tshebetso ya Kantoro ya Mohlakisi Kakaretso ho phethahatsa mosebetsi wa bohlakisi ba matjhabeng le ho hlakisa, le ho ikamahantsha le ditlhophiso tsa taolo ya maemo a matle a tshebetso.

src: 100 #WomenOfFortitudeFollowing a period of nominations, the 100 #WomenOfFortitude will be unveiled at the Union Buildings in Pretoria on 22 November 2018.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse Tlang Letsholo la 100 # WomenOfFortitudeKa mora nako ya ho thunya, 100 # WomenOfFortitude e tla phahlalatswa mane Union Buildings, Pretoria ka la 22 Pudungwana 2018.

src: The Inter-Ministerial Committee on the Nelson Mandela Centenary and Centenary of AlbertinaSisulu announced on the 11 October 2018 the #WomenOfFortitude campaign as one of the Mama Sisulu Centenary activities.
tgt: Komiti ya Matona ka Puso ya Kopanelo ya Mengwahakgolo wa Nelson Mandela le Albertina Sisulu e ile ya tsebahatsa letsholo la #WomenOfFortitude ka la 11 Mphalane 2018 jwalo ka le leng la diketsahahalo tsa Mongwahakgolo wa Mama Sisulu.

src: The #WomenOfFortitude campaign is a movement of 100 women to drive the conversation of how women today can sustain the legacy of Mama Sisulu.
tgt: Letsholo la #WomenOfFortitude ke mokgatlo wa basadi ba 100 la ho tsamaisa dipuisano ka hore basadi ba ka kgona ho tswella ka mesebetsi ya mohale enwa, Mama Sisulu le kajeno lena.

src: 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence (GBV)The Department of Women is coordinating and consolidating government's calendar of events for the 16 Days of Activism against GBV Campaign from 25 November to 10 December 2018.
tgt: Matsatsi a 16 a Boitseko bo kgahlano le Dikgoka tsa Bong (GBV)Lefapha la Basadi le hokela le tiiseletsa alakamani ya diketsahalo ya Letsholo la Matsatsi a 16 a Boitseko bo kgahlano le GBV ho tloha ka la 25 Pudungwana ho isa ho la 10 Tshitwe 2018.

src: Members of the National Executive as well as provincial and local government leaders will undertake portfolio/sector-specific events throughout the country through community-engagement initiatives.
tgt: Ditho tsa Tsamaiso ya Kakaretso ya Mmuso wa Naha ha mmoho le baetapele ba mmuso wa porofense le wa selehae ba tla ba le seabo diketsahalong tsa potefolio kapa lekaleng la naha ka bophara ka boiteko ba ho buisana le setjhaba.

src: Detailed government programmes can be accessed from WEBTOKEN Cabinet urges all South Africans to use this platform and participate in a government event nearest to them.
tgt: Mananeo a mmuso ka botlalo a ka fumaneha ho WEBTOKEN Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAfrika Borwa ohle ho sebedisa polatefomo ena ho ba le seabo diketsahalong tsena tsa mmuso tse haufinyana le bona.

src: Civil society and other women's organisations are encouraged to populate their calendars of events for the period.
tgt: Setjhaba le mekgatlo ya basadi e kgothaletswa ho ba le seabo diketsahalong tsena nakong ena.

src: All South Africans are urged to work together to heed the call to #HearMeToo, by listening to the plight of women, and taking action to end the scourge of all forms of violence against women.
tgt: MaAfrika Borwa ohle a kgothaletswa ho sebetsa mmoho le ho mamela pitso ya #HearMeToo, ka ho mamela sello sa basadi, le ho etsa ho hong ho fedisa tlhekefetso ya mekgwa yohle le dikgoka tse kgahlano le basadi.

src: Congratulations.
tgt: Ditebohiso.

src: Cabinet congratulates all local sporting heroes who are flying the South African flag high.
tgt: Kabinete e lebohisa bahale bohle ba selehae ba dipapadi ba phahamisetsang folakga ya Afrika Borwa hodimo.

src: The achievements of those who excelled in their respective sporting fields, was acknowledged at the recent 2018 Sports Award ceremony.
tgt: Katleho ya ba itlhommeng pele mekgahlelong ya dipapadi, ile ya bontshahatswa ka ho ba putsa moketeng wa Dikgao tsa Dipapadi tsa 2018.

src: South Africa’s Caster Semenya bagged double gold by winning the coveted Sports Star of the Year award along with the Sportswoman of the Year Award.
tgt: Caster Semenya wa Afrika Borwa o hapile Dikgau tse pedi tsa Kgauta ka ho hloha kgau ya Naledi ya Dipapadi ya Selemo ha mmoho le ya Mosadi wa Dipapa wa Selemo.

src: South African swimming sensation Chad le Clos won the Sportsman of the Year Award.
tgt: Sesesi se hlwahlwa Chad le Clos se hlotse Kgau ya Monna wa Dipapadi wa Selemo.

src: Ndodomzi Ntutu won the Sportsman of the Year with Disability Award.
tgt: Ndodomzi Ntutu o hlotse Kgau ya Monna wa Dipapadi wa Selemo ya batho ba holofetseng.

src: Anrune Liebenberg won the Sportswoman of the Year with Disability Award.
tgt: Anrune Liebenberg o hlotse Kgau ya Mosadi wa Selemo ya batho ba holofetseng.

src: Banyana Banyana won their match against Nigeria at the 2018 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON).
tgt: Banyana Banyana ba hlotse papadi ya pulo kgahlano le Nigeria Ditlhodisanong tsa Mohope wa Dinaha tsa Afrika (AFCON) wa 2018.

src: Bafana Bafana drew 1-1 in the AFCON qualifier match with Nigeria.
tgt: Bafana Bafana ba bapetse 1-1 kgahlano le Nigeria hore ba kgone ho bapala dipapading tsa AFCOSehlopha sa Rekebi sa Afrika Borwa se theoheleditswe ka dipapadi tsa sona mme re se lakaletsa mahlohonolo papading e tlang e kgahlano le Wales ka la 24 Pudungwana 2018.

src: The South African Rugby team is commended for their performances and we wish them well for their upcoming match against Wales on 24 November 2018.Cabinet calls on South Africans to continue to rally behind the country’s sports women and men.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAfrika Borwa hore ba tswelle ho tshihetsa basadi le banna ba dipapadi naheng.

src: Cabinet also congratulates:.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e lebohisa:.

src: Science and Technology Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi-Ngubane, who has been nominated to serve in the World Economic Forum Council on the Fourth Industrial Revolution, which consists of government, civil society and academics.
tgt: Letona la Saense le Thekenoloji Mmamoloko Kubayi-Ngubane, a ileng a thongwa ho Lekgotla la Seboka sa Moruo ho tsa Phetolo ya Diindasteri ya Bone, e kenyeleditseng mmuso, setjhaba le barutehi.

src: This will help countries globally to respond and take advantage of opportunities presented by the Fourth Industrial Revolution.
tgt: Sena se tla thusa dinaha lefatsheng ho arabela le ho sebedisa menyetla e hlahisitsweng ke Phethoho ya Diindasteri ya Bone.

src: Finance Minister Tito Mboweni on his appointment to the Board of Trustees of the AU Peace Fund, which will finance mediation and preventative diplomacy activities, institutional capacity requirements, and peace support operations in Africa.
tgt: Letona la Ditjhelete Tito Mboweni ho kgethweng ha hae e le Setho sa Lekgotla la Batshepuwa ba Letlwele la Kgotso la Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tsa Afrika (AU), le tla thusang ka bonamodi ba ditjhelete le ho thibela diketso tsa thibelo tsa ditshebeletso tsa bodiplomate, ditlhokeho tsa ditheo, le ditshebeletso tsa tshehetso tsa kgotso Afrika.

src: As a member of the Board of Trustees, Minister Mboweni will contribute towards the strategic coherence and enhanced governance, financial and administrative oversight of the Peace Fund.
tgt: Jwaloka setho sa Lekgotla la Batshepuwa, Letona Mboweni o tla tswelapele ho nehelana pusong e nang le nyalano le e atolositsweng, bolekodi ba tsamaiso le ditjhelete tsa Letlwele la Kgotso.

src: The appointment of the trustees of the AU’s Peace Fund is a key step in the implementation of the financing of the AU’s agenda, which is part of the ongoing institutional reform process.
tgt: Ho thongwa ha batshepuwa ba Letlwele la Kgotso la AU ho bohlokwa haholo tseleng ya ho sebedisa ditjhelete ajendeng ya AU, hoo e leng karolo ya tshebetso e ntjhafalang ya ditheo tse ntseng di tswella ho sebetsa.

src: Higher Education and Training Minister Naledi Pandor, who will be conferred with the French National Order of the Legion of Honour Award on Friday, 30 November 2018.
tgt: Letona la Lefapha la Thuto le Thupello tse Phahameng, Letona Naledi Pandor, o tla tlotlwa ka tlotla ya Kgau ya Tlotla ya Odara ya Naha ya Fora ya Bahale ka Labohlano, 30 Pudungwana 2018.

src: The award is in recognition of her lifelong remarkable achievements and efforts in nurturing and furthering the cooperation between France and South Africa in the field of Science and Technology.
tgt: Kgau ena e ananela dikatleho tsa hae tse hlwahlwa ka nako e telele le boiteko ba ho tataisa le ho ntshetsapele tshebedisano mmoho dipakeng tsa Fora le Afrika Borwa lekaleng la Saense le Thekenoloji.

src: The ceremony will be held in at the residence of the French Ambassador to South Africa in Pretoria.
tgt: Mokete ona o tla tshwarelwa bodulong ba Lenqosa la Fora le Afrika Borwa mane Pretoria.

src: AppointmentsAll appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant clearance.
tgt: Dithonyo Dithonyo kaofela di lokela ho netefatswa ka mangolo a thuto le tumello e amehang.

src: Provincial heads of the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation:.
tgt: Dihlooho tsa Diporofense tsa Bolaodi ba Dipatlisiso tsa Ditlolo tsa Molao tse ka Sehloohong (Hawks):.

src: Free State: Brigadier Kubandran Moodley and.
tgt: Foreistata: Brigadier Kubandran Moodley le Leboya Bophimira: Majoro wa Mokgenerale Dumisani Patrick Mbotho.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 5 December 2018 at Tuynhuys in Cape TownIssues in the environment.
tgt: Kabinete e kopane ka Laboraro, 5 Tshitwe 2018, Tuynhuys e Motse Kapa.

src: Economic growthCabinet welcomes the 2.2% growth in the South African economy during the third quarter, which is helping move the country out of a technical recession.
tgt: golo ya moruoKabinete e amohela 2.2% ya kgolo moruong wa Afrika Borwa nakong ya kotara ya boraro, e thusang ho ntsha naha putlamong ya moruo ka tatelano dikotareng tse pedi.

src: The growth figures were driven by increases in the agricultural sector (6.5%), financial sector (2.3%) manufacturing sector (7.5%) and wholesale and retail trade sales (3.2%).
tgt: Dipalo tsa kgolo di ile tsa susumetswa ke keketseho e lekaleng la temothuo (6.5%), lekala la ditjhelete (2.3%), lekala la tlhahiso (7.5%) ha mmoho le thekiso e kgolo le thekiso ya bohwebi (3.2%).

src: The growth figures signal a rebound in the economy and together with initiatives from the Jobs Summit and South African Investment Conference, will continue to improve.
tgt: Dipalo tsa kgolo di bontsha nyoloho ya moruo ha mmoho le dikgwebo tse hlahileng ho tswa Kopano ya Mesebetsi le Seboka sa Letsete sa Afrika Borwa, di tla tswella ho ntlafala.

src: Cabinet also joins South Africans in welcoming this month’s drop in the fuel price which comes as a relief, especially as we move into a holiday period.
tgt: Kabinete e boela e amohela ho theoha ha ditjeo tsa mafura kgweding ena mme sena se imolla haholo, haholoholo jwang ha e le mona re ya nakong ya matsatsi a phomolo.

src: All sectors of society are urged to build on the positive momentum during the third quarter to help place the South African economy on a new growth trajectory.
tgt: Ho ipiletswa ho makala ohle a setjhaba hore a ahelle hodima kgatelopele ena e matla nakong ya kotara ya boraro ho thusa ho kenya moruo wa Afrika Borwa tseleng e ntjha ya kgolo.

src: National Minimum Wage (NMW)Cabinet also welcomes the signing of the NMW Bill into law by President Cyril Ramaphosa.
tgt: Bonnyane ba Moputso wa Naha (NMW)Kabinete e boela e amohela ho tekenwa ha Bili ya Bonnyane ba Moputso wa Naha hore e fetolelwe molao ke Mopresidente Cyril Ramaphosa.

src: The Bill sets a historic precedent in the protection of low-earning workers and reduction of inequality in society.
tgt: Bili e bapatsa mohlala o motle mabapi le ho tshireletsa basebetsi ba kgolang meputso e tlase le ho fokotsa tlhokeho ya tekatekano setjhabeng.

src: The first NMW will raise the earnings of an estimated six million South African low-earning workers.
tgt: Bonnyane ba Moputso wa Naha ba pele bo tlo phahamisa meputso ya basebetsi ba maAfrika Borwa ba ka bang milione tse tsheletseng ba kgolang meputso e tlase.

src: There will be a phase-in period for farm workers, forestry workers and domestic workers.
tgt: Ho tla ba le nako ya ho kenyeletsa basebetsi ba mapolasing, basebetsi ba meru le basebetsi ba malapeng.

src: Whilst this NMW will not end income inequality, Cabinet believes it will go a long way to breaking the back of rising inequality and persistent poverty.
tgt: Le ha Bonnyane ba Moputso wa Naha bo se na ho fedisa tlhokeho ya tekatekano ya makeno, Kabinete e dumela hore e tla fihlela tse ngata ha ho tla ho tsa bophahamo ba tlhokeho ya tekatekano le bofuma bo tsitlalletseng.

src: Toyota Wessels Institute for Manufacturing Studies (TWIMS)Cabinet welcomes the launch of the newly established R56-million TWIMThe institute will boost South Africa’s manufacturing sector, develop world-class capabilities and drive African industrialisation.
tgt: Institjhuti yaToyota Wessels ya Dithuto tsa Tlhahiso (TWIMS)Kabinete e amohela ho thakgolwa ha TWIMS e ntjha ya boleng ba R56 milione.

src: It will also accelerate the building of a manufacturing culture that the country needs to drive its domestic demands and create more WEBTOKEN is an independent and not-for-profit initiative established through grant funding from the Toyota South Africa Education Trust.
tgt: Institjhuti e tla matlafatsa lekala la tlhahiso la Afrika Borwa, e ntshetsepele bokgoni ba maemo a lefatsheng le ho tsamaisa ho thehwa ha diindastri Afrika.

src: It has been established in partnership with the University of Pretoria’s Gordon Institute of Business Science to deliver a Master of Business Administration degree specialising in manufacturing.
tgt: E tla boela e potlakisa kaho ya setso sa diindasteri e leng seo naha e se hlokang ho tsamaisa ditlhoko tsa yona tsa ka hara naha le ho theha mesebetsi e meng e mengata.

src: Social EconomyCabinet notes the successful Symposium on the Social Economy held by government in partnership with the International Labour Organisation (ILO) and the Government of Flanders on Friday, 30 November 2018.
tgt: Ke setheo se ikemetseng se sa etseng phaello se thehilweng ka dithuso tsa ditjhelete ke Traste ya Thuto ya Toyato e Afrika Borwa.

src: The symposium was led by the Economic Development Department and supported by the Department of Small Business Development.
tgt: E thihilwe ka bolekane le Institjhuti ya Dithuto tsa Kgwebo ya Gordon ya Yunivesithi ya Pretoria ho nyehelana ka dikgarata ya Masters ya Tsamaiso ya Kgwebo (MBA) e shebaneng le tsa tlhahiso.

src: The Social Economy comprises enterprises and initiatives directed at achieving social-policy objectives such as creating jobs, mainstreaming excluded groups, and bringing goods and services to rural communities.
tgt: Merero ya Mekgatlho ya Setjhaba o kenyeletsa dikgwebo le ditheo tse tsepameng ho fihlella maikemisetso a maano a setjhaba a jwalo ka ho theha mesebetsi, dikgwebo tse kgolo tse sa kenyeletswang, le ho tlisa dihlahiswa le ditshebeletso ho baahi ba mahaheng.

src: It has the potential of supporting economic inclusion and creating thousands of additional jobs.
tgt: Se na le bokgoni ba ho tshehetsa moruo o kenyeletsang bohle le ho theha mesebetsi ya tlatsetso.

src: The symposium brought together social entrepreneurs, policymakers, researchers and non-governmental organisations, and will help in the development of a Green Paper on the Social Economy during Voter registrationIn preparation for the 2019 elections, Cabinet calls on South Africans to exercise their right as responsible citizens by ensuring they have a green bar-coded ID book, smart ID card or temporary identity certificate and are registered to vote in their districts.
tgt: Seboka sena se kopantshitse borakgwebo, baradi ba maano, bafuphutsi le mekgatlo e seng ya mmuso, mme e tla thusa ntshetsopeleng ya Sengolwa sa Dikeletso sa Merero ya Mekgatlho ya Setjhaba ka Ngodiso ya MokgethiHo lokisetsa dikgetho tsa 2019, Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAfrika Borwa ho sebedisa tokelo ya bona jwalo ka baahi ka ho netefatsa hore ba na le tokomane ya Boitsebiso e tala e nang le bakhoutu, Karete ya Boitsebiso kapa ditokomane tsa boitsebiso tsa nakwana mme ba ngodisitswe ho kgetha diterekeng tsa bona.

src: The Independent Electoral Commission will hold a voter-registration weekend on 26 and 27 January 2019 and South Africans are encouraged to use the opportunity to register to vote or verify their registration status.
tgt: Komishene e Ikemetseng ya Dikgetho e tla ba le mafelo a beke a ngodiso ya bakgethi ka la 26 le 27 Pherekgong 2019 mme maAfrika Borwa a kgothaletswa ho sebedisa monyetla ona ho ingodisa ho kgetha kapa ho hlahloba maemo a bona a boingodiso.

src: Cabinet appeals to those who have applied for Smart IDs to collect their documents at their respective Department of Home Affairs (DHA) branches.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho ba kentseng kopo ya Ditokomane tsa Dikarete tsa Boitsebiso ho ya lata ditokomane tsa bona Makaleng a Lefapha la Merero ya Lehae (DHA).

src: National Director of Public Prosecutions (NDPP)Cabinet applauds President Ramaphosa’s appointment of Advocate Shamila Batohi as the new NDPThis follows the President’s consideration of five nominees shortlisted by an advisory panel.
tgt: Molaodi wa Naha wa Botjhotjhisi ba Setjhaba (NDPP)Kabinete e theoletsa Mopresidente Ramaphosa ka ho thonya Moadvokheiti Shamila Batohi jwalo ka Molaodi wa Naha wa Botjhotjhisi ba Setjhaba.

src: The appointment brings stability to the leadership of the National Prosecuting Authority and emboldens the country’s fight against crime and corruption.
tgt: Sena se tla ka mora hore Mopresidente a thuise lenane la bathonngowa ba bahlano ba ile ba thongwa ke phanele ya baeletsi.

src: Cabinet extends its appreciation to Energy Minister Jeff Radebe and the panel for their contribution to this historic process of appointment.
tgt: Thonyo ena e tlisa botsitso ketapeleng ya Baloadi ba Naha ya Botjhotjhisi ba Setjhaba le ho kgothaletsa naha twantshong e kgahlano le tlolo ya molao le bobodu.

src: Limpopo health professionalsCabinet strongly condemns attacks on doctors in hospitals around Limpopo.
tgt: Kabinete e atolosa kananelo ya yona ho Letona la Matla, Jeff Radebe le phanele ka seabo sa bona tsamaisong ya thonyo ena e bohlokwa.

src: Health professionals and health facilities serve communities, especially vulnerable members who facilities to get assistance.
tgt: Basebetsi ba Bophelo bo Botle ba LimpopoKabinete e tshwela ka mathe ditlhaselo tsa dingaka dipetleleng tse Limpopo.

src: The Minister of Health, Dr Aaron Motsoaledi, is leading a multidisciplinary task team – comprising police intelligence agents, detective services, public order policing, private security authorities and DHA officials – to review the security systems at public healthcare facilities.
tgt: Basebetsi ba Bophelo bo Botle le ditsha tse nehelang ka ditshebeletso tsena di sebeletsa setjhaba, haholoholo ditho tsa setjhaba tse kotsing e kgolo tse yang ho ya fumantshwa thuso ditsheng tsena.

src: Cabinet calls on the community to work with law-enforcement agencies to ensure that perpetrators of this heinous crimes are arrested and convicted.
tgt: Ho hlasela ba pholosang maphelo a batho ke tlolo ya molao mme sena se keke sa dumellwa.

src: Road users are urged to adhere to the traffic rules, and not to drive recklessly and negligently, especially under the influence.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho setjhaba hore se sebedisane le baemedi ba tsa taolo ya molao ho netefatsa hore baetsi ba ketso tsena tse soto tsa tlolo ya molao ba ya kwalla le ho fumanwa ba le molato.

src: Pedestrians are also urged to remain cautious on the road.
tgt: Matsatsi a phomolo a bolokehileng Kabinete e ipiletsa ho maAfrika Borwa ohle ho dula a bolokehile nakong ya matsatsi a phomolo a Tshitwe.

src: The Justice, Crime Prevention and Security (JCPS) Cluster has intensified anti-crime and safety operations countrywide.
tgt: Basebedisi ba ditsela ba kopuwa hore ba ikamahantshe le melao ya tsela, ba se kganne bohlaswa kapa ntle le kelahloko, haholoholo ba le tlasa tahi.

src: The DHA’s has increased its capacity in ports of entry to ensure it is able to respond to the expected increase of travellers over the festive period.
tgt: Ho boela ho ipiletswa ho ditaso hore le tsona di dule di le hlwahlwa tseleng.

src: It also plans to extend operating hours at busy ports of entry, covering pre-festive season movements, the festive season period and the re-opening of schools.
tgt: Sehlopha sa Toka, Thibelo ya Tlolo ya Molao le Tshireletso (JCPS) se tiisitse matsholo a kgahlano le tlolo ya molao le polokeho naheng ka bophara.

src: Fifth anniversary of the passing of MadibaCabinet joins South Africans in commemorating the fifth anniversary of the passing of our first democratically elected President Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela, who passed on 5 December 2013.
tgt: Sehopotso sa bohlano sa ho hlokahala ha Madiba Kabinete ha mmoho le maAfrika Borwa e keteka sehopotso sa bohlano sa ho hlokahala ha mopresidente wa rona wa pele ya kgethilweng tlasa demokrasi Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela, ya ileng a hlokahala ka la 5 Tshitwe 2013.

src: President Ramaphosa declared 2018 as the Year marking Mandela’s centenary.
tgt: Mopresidente Ramaphosa o phatlaladitse 2018 e le Selemo se tshwayang mongwahakgolo wa Mandela.

src: His legacy has been celebrated throughout the year by South Africans in their various formations, the most recent being the Global Citizens Mandela 100 Festival held over the past weekend.
tgt: Lefa la hae le ile la ketekwa selemong sena kaofela ke maAfrika Borwa mekgahlelong ya bona e fapaneng, keteko ya ha mmamorao tjena ke ya mokete wa Global Citizen Festival Mandela 100 o ileng wa tshwarwa mafelong a beke a fetileng.

src: Cabinet calls on all to stay true to Madiba’s ideals, including his unwavering commitment to justice, equality and non-racialism.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho bohle ho dula ba ipapisitse le mehopolo ya Madiba, ho kenyeletsa boitlamo bo sa qeqeng ho tsa toka, tekatekano le tlhokeho ya kgethollo ya morabe.

src: Global Citizen Festival Mandela 100Cabinet thanks all participants of the Global Citizen Festival Mandela 100 held in Johannesburg on Sunday, 2 December 2018.
tgt: Global Citizen Festival Mandela 100Kabinete e leboha bohle ba bileng le seabo Moketeng wa Global Citizen Festival Mandela 100 o neng o tshwaretswe Johannesburg ka Sontaha, ka la 2 Tshitwe 2018.

src: The festival formed part of the national commemorative events to celebrate the centenary of Tata Nelson Mandela and was transmitted in over 180 countries.
tgt: Mokete ona e bile karolo ya diketsahalo tsa keteko ya mongwahakgolo wa Ntate Nelson Mandela mme o bapetse diraleng tsa kgaso tsa dinaha tse ding tse fetang 180.

src: It brought together thousands of global citizens, activists, world leaders, musicians and influencers to advance the Sustainable Development Goals of the United Nations (UN) in honour of Mandela’s memory.
tgt: O tla kopantse diketekete tsa baahi ba lefatsheng, baitseki, baetapela ba lefatshe, dibini le ba nang le kgahlamelo ho potlakisa Maikemisetso a Ntshetsopele ya Mokoka ya Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) a ho tlotla sehopotso sa Mandela.

src: Cabinet extends its sympathy to all those who were violated by criminal elements that preyed on them whilst leaving the stadium.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisetsa matshediso a yona ho bohle ba ileng ba hlekefetswa ka dikgoka nakong eo ba neng ba tsamaya lebaleng la dipapadi.

src: It strongly condemns these criminal acts and calls on law-enforcement agencies to bring offenders to book.
tgt: E tshwela ka mathe diketso tsena tsa tlolo ya molao mme ipiletsa ho baemedi ba tsa taolo ya molao ho tlisa batludi bana ba molao molaong.

src: World AIDS DaySouth Africa marked World AIDS Day on 1 December under the theme: “Cheka Impilo.
tgt: Letsatsi la AIDS la LefatsheAfrika Borwa e tshwaile Letsatsi la AIDS la Lefatshe ka la 1 Tshitwe ka tlasa mookotaba wa: “Cheka Impilo.

src: Know Your Status.” Cabinet appreciates government’s multidimensional HIV and AIDS programme that has taken decisive steps to bring an end to the epidemic.
tgt: Know Your Status.” Kabinete e ananela lenaneo la mmuso la mekgahlelo e fapaneng ya HIV le AIDS le nkileng qeto e tsepameng ya ho fedisa koduo ena.

src: The programme has realised an additional uptake of two million people to the antiretroviral treatment programme.
tgt: Lenaneo lena le se le ekeditse ka palo ya batho ba dimilione tse pedi ba lenaneong la ho fumantshwa pheko ya meriana ya ARV.

src: South Africa has more than 4,2 million people on treatment, making it one of the world’s biggest treatment programmes.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e na le batho ba fetang 4,2 milione ba nkang pheko ya meriana ena, mme sena se etsa lenaneo lena e be le leng la mananeo a pheko a maholo ka ho fetisisa lefatsheng.

src: The HIV and AIDS campaign continues to make inroads towards changing behaviour, medical treatment and social de-stigmatisation.
tgt: Letsholo la HIV le AIDS le tswella ho lebisa tshebetso phetolong maitshwaro, pheko ya meriana le ho fedisa sekgobo hara setjhaba.

src: Cabinet is steadfast in its call on South Africans to get tested so they can know their HIV status, which will help them make informed decisions on preventative measures, treatment, care and support.
tgt: Kabinete e tiisitse pitsong ya yona ho maAfrika Borwa hore a lo etsa diteko tsa madi mabapi le maemo a bona a HIV, eleng se tla thusa ho etsa diqeto tse nang le tlhahisoleseding e nepahetseng ka mekgwa ya ho thibela tshwaetso, ho mka pheko ya meriana, ho itlhokomelo le ho thola tshehetso.

src: UN International Day of Persons with DisabilitiesSouth Africa joined the global community in observing the annual UN International Day of Persons with Disabilities on Monday, 3 December.
tgt: Letsatsi la Matjhaba la Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tsa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) la Batho ba Holofetseng Afrika Borwa ha mmoho le baahi ba matjhabeng e ile ya ana keteko ya selemo le selemo ya Letsatsi la Matjhaba la Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tsa Matjhaba a Kopaneng la Batho ba Holofetseng ka Mantaha, wa la 3 Tshitwe.

src: Government remains committed to the inclusion and protection of persons with disabilities through dedicated programmes and interventions to ensure access to equal opportunities, as enshrined in the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996.Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Mmuso o ntse o tswella ho itlama ka ho kenyeletsa le ho tshireletsa batho ba holofetseng ka ho sebedisa mananeo le bonamodi ho netefatsa hore ba fumantshwa menyetla e lekanang le ya ba bang, jwalo ka ho tobekeditswe ka hara Molaotheo wa Rephaboliki ya Afrika Borwa wa 1996.

src: Nkomazi Special Economic Zone (SEZ)Cabinet ratified a decision of the Minister of Trade and Industry, Dr Rob Davies, to designate the SEZ and to grant a SEZ Licence to the Mpumalanga Provincial Government’s Department of Economic Development and Tourism.
tgt: Sebaka sa Moruo o Ikgethileng sa Nkomazi (SEZ) Kabinete e tjhaetse monwanana qeto ya Letona la Kgwebisano le Indasteri, Ngaka Rob Davies, ho hlwaya Sebaka sa Moruo o Ikgethileng sa Nkomazi le ho nehelana ka laesense ya Sebaka sa Moruo o Ikgethileng sa Nkomazi ho Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Moruo le Bohahlaudi la Mmuso wa Porofense ya Mpumalanga.

src: The Nkomazi SEZ will be positioned as an “Agro-Processing Hub” using green energy.
tgt: Sebaka sa Moruo o Ikgethileng sa Nkomazi se tla sebetsa jwalo ka “Setsi sa Tlhahiso ya Dihlahiswa tsa Temothuo, Meru le Botshwasi ba Ditlhapi” ka tshebediso ya matla a mehlodi ya tlhaho.

src: It will be supported by mixed services such as warehousing and logistics.
tgt: Se tla tshehetswa ke ditshebeletso tse jwalo ka polokeho e kgolo le tlhophiso ya moralo le disebediswa.

src: This forms part of is the Maputo Development Corridor project, which is a major trade corridor which connects Gauteng, Limpopo and Mpumalanga with Maputo in Mozambique.
tgt: Sena e ba karolo ya leano la Phaseitjhe ya Kgwebisano ya Ntshetsopele ya Maputo, eo e leng phaseitjhe e kgolo ya kgwebisano e kopantshang Gauteng, Limpopo le Mpumalanga le Maputo e Mozambique.

src: It comprises, among other things, roads, ports and WEBTOKEN will contribute towards accelerating growth, attract foreign and domestic direct investment, expand the manufacturing sector and create employment in the region.
tgt: E kenyeletsa, ho tse ding tsa dintho, ditsela, maemakepe le diporo tsa terene.

src: Cabinet has approved the signing of the rollover Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) with the United Kingdom (UK) once the last outstanding technical issues are resolved and the internal administrative issues are finalised.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse ho tekenwa ha Tumellano ya Bolekane ba Moruo ya katoloso ya sekoloto (EPA) le Dinaha tsa Yuropa ka Kopanelo (UK) hang ha mathata a tshebetso a ntseng a saletse morao a se a lokisitswe mme le tsamaiso ya ka hare e se e phethetswe.

src: Cabinet also approved the submission in Parliament for ratification, the Agreement establishing the EPA between Southern African Customs Union and Mozambique and the UCabinet approved the publication of the streamlined White Paper on Home Affairs for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e boetse e ananetse ho tjhaelwa ka monwanana ha phehiso ena Palamenteng, Tumellano ya ho theha Tumellano ya Bolekane ba Moruo ya katoloso ya sekoloto dipakeng tsa Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tse Borwa ba Afrika wa Lekgetho la Direkwantle le Mozambique le Dinaha tsa Yuropa ka Kopanelo.

src: The White Paper argues that for South Africa to fully realise the potential of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, the DHA must play a critical enabling role in citizen empowerment, inclusive development, efficient government and national security.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse phatlalatso ya ho phatlalatsa Tokomane ya Tataiso ya Lefapha la Merero ya Lehae mabapi le ho thola maikutlo a setjhaba.

src: It is also based on the DHA having sole mandate for the management of official identity and status, international migration, and asylum seekers and refugees.
tgt: Tokomane ya Tataiso e ngangisa hore Afrika Borwa hore e ntshe bokgoni ba yona ka Phetolo ya Bone ya Indasteri, Lefapha la Merero ya Lehae le tlameha ho bapala karolo e bohlokwa haholo mabapi le ho matlafatsa baahi, ntshetsopele e kenyeletsang bohle, mmuso o sebetsang le tshireletso ya setjhaba.

src: The White Paper proposes measures to reduce the fraudulent bank transactions and realise savings due to increased inefficiencies.
tgt: E boela e itshetlehile ho thomo ya mantlha ya Lefapha la Merero ya Lehae ya taolo ya boitsebiso le maemo a semmuso, phallo ya matjhaba, bakopi ba tshireletso le baphaphathehi.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO) Copyright Treaty (WCT) of 1996 to Parliament for accession.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse hore phehiso ya Tumellano ya Ditokelo tsa Kgatiso (WCT) ya Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Ditokelo tsa Thepa ya Bonono (WIPO) ya 1996 e phahamise maemo Palamenteng.

src: This is a multilateral agreement and a special agreement under the Berne Convention that deals with the protection of the work and rights of their authors in the digital environment.
tgt: Ena ke tumellano ya mmeso ya dinaha tse fapaneng e boelang e le tumellano e ikgethileng ka tlasa Seboka sa Berne se shebaneng le tshireletso ya mosebetsi le ditokelo tsa bangodi tikolohong ya dijithale.

src: Acceding to the WCT also benefits the South African creative industry, specifically authors of literary and artistic works.
tgt: Ho phahamisa Tumellano ya Ditokelo tsa Kgatiso ho tla boela ho tswela molemo indasteri ya bonono ya Afrika Borwa, haholoholo bangodi ba dingolwa le mesebetsi ya bonono.

src: The WCT is in the best interest of South Africa as it ensures that the country’s copyright law will keep pace with technological change.
tgt: Tumellano ya Ditokelo tsa Kgatiso e molemong wa Afrika Borwa ka ha e netefatsa hore molao wa ditokelo tsa kgatiso o tla latelwa o ipapisitse le diphetoho tsa thekenoloij.

src: This will afford important protection against piracy for rights holders in the areas of computer programmes and databases.
tgt: Sena se tla nehelana ka tshireletso e bohlokwa kgahlano le boshudu ba dikgatiso ho beng ba ditokelo tsa kgatiso Makaleng a mananeo a dikhomphyutha le dipolokelo tsa dintlha.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the WIPO Performances and Phonograms Treaty of 1996, to Parliament for accession.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse hore phehiso ya Tumellano ya Ketsahatso le Difonokgamo ya Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Ditokelo tsa Thepa ya Bonono ya 1996 e phahamiswe maemo Palamenteng.

src: This is a multilateral agreement which deals with the rights of performers and producers of phonograms, specifically in the digital environment.
tgt: Ena ke tumellano ya mmeso ya dinaha tse fapaneng e shebaneng le ditumellano tsa ditokelo tsa baetsahatsi le bahlahisi ba difonokgamo, haholoholo tikolohong ya dijithale.

src: This treaty will protect people or organisations that add substantial creative, technical or organisational skill in the process of bringing work to the public and enhance revenue to benefit them.
tgt: Tumellano ena e tla tshireletsa batho kapa mekgatlo e tlatseletsang kgolo ya bonono, tsebo le bokgoni ba tshebetso tsamaisong ya ho tlisa mosebetsi setjhabeng le ho atolosa lekeno molemong wa bona.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the Beijing Treaty to Parliament for accession.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse hore phehiso ya Tumellano ya Beijing e phahamiswe maemo Palamenteng.

src: This is a multilateral agreement, which regulates copyright for audio-visual performances and expands the audio-visual performers’ rights.
tgt: Ena ke tumellano ya mmeso ya dinaha tse fapaneng, e laolang ditokelo tsa kgatiso tsa ketsahatso ya kutlo-le-pono le ho atalosa ditokelo tsa baetsahatsi ba kutlo-le-pono.

src: It recognises audio-visual performers’ intellectual property right in their audio-visual work and creates economic benefit for them.
tgt: E ananela tokelo ya thepa ya bonono ya baetsahatsi ba kutlo-le-pono mosebetsing wa bona wa kutlo-le-pono le ho ba etsetsa melemo ya moruo.

src: It also provides audio-visual performers with moral rights in respect of their work and recognises audio-visual performers’ rights in the digital environment.
tgt: E nehela baetsahatsi ba kutlo-le-pono ka ditokelo tsa maitshwaro a matle mabapi le mosebetsi wa bona le ho ananela ditokelo tsa baetsahatsi ba kutlo-le-pono tikolohong ya dijithale.

src: Cabinet approved for the establishment of an Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) to lead the African Peer Review Mechanism (APRM) second generation periodic review.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse ho thehwa ha Komiti ya Matona ka Kopanelo (IMC) ho etelapele hlahlobo ya nako ya moloko wa bobedi wa Mekgwa ya ho Hlahloba Balekane ba Afrika (APRM).

src: It will be conducted after the 2019 General Elections.
tgt: Hlahlobo e tla etswa ka mora Dikgetho tsa Kakaretso tsa 2019.

src: The IMC will be supported by the approved establishment of the APRM National Governing Council.
tgt: Komiti ya Matona ka Kopanelo e tla tshehetswa ke ho thehwa ha Lekgotla la Mmuso wa Naha wa Mekgwa ya ho Hlahloba Balekane ba Afrika.

src: This APRM review process provides member states a space for national dialogue on governance and socio-economic indicators and an opportunity to build consensus on the way forward.
tgt: Tsamaiso ya hlahlobo ya Hlahloba Balekane ba Afrika e nehela dinaha tsa ditho sebaka sa ho tshwara dipuisano ka matshwao a tshebetso a puso Merero ya Mekgatlho ya Setjhaba le monyetla wa ho theha tumellano ka tsela ya ho ya pele.

src: Cabinet approved for South Africa to sign the Convention to establish, under international law, an intergovernmental organisation called the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) Observatory, which will be responsible for the construction and operational phases of the global SKA radio telescope project, to be located in South Africa and Australia.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse hore Afrika Borwa e tekene tokomane ya Seboka sa ho theha, tlasa molao wa matjhaba, mokgatlo wa mmeso ka kopanelo o bitswang Obseferatori ya Dipontsho tsa Sekwere sa Kilomithara (SKA), eo e tla ikarabellang ho aha le mekgahlelong ya tshebetso ya leano la radiyo ya theleskoupo SKA, se tla fumaneha Afrika Borwa le Australia.

src: The signing of the convention will be crucial in providing the global partnership with the appropriate governance mechanisms, which will ensure successful delivery of the project.
tgt: Ho tekenwa ha tumellano ho tla ba bohlokwa ho neheleng balekane ba matjhabeng ka mekgwa ya puso e tshwanetseng, e tla netefatsa katleho ya ho phethisa leano lena.

src: South Africa will also be able to leverage foreign inward investment, as well as skills and infrastructure development benefits associated with the SKA project.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e tla boela e kgona ho sebedisa ditjhelete ya kadimo ho eketsa botsetedi ba ka hare ho naha, ha mmoho le bokgoni le melemo ya ditheo tsa ntshetsopele tse amanang le leano la SKKabinete e ananetse phethahatso ya Moralo wa Naha wa Sebaka se le Seng sa Ditshebeletso tsa Moedi wa Boemakepe (OSBP).

src: Cabinet approved the One-Stop Border Post (OSBP) National Framework for implementation.
tgt: Sena re nehelana ka tataiso ho potlakiseng ho thehwa ha Dibaka tse leng ding tsa Ditshebeletso tsa Moedi wa Boemakepe dipakeng tsa Afrika Borwa le dinaha tsa yona tsa boahisane.

src: The OSBP will enhance trade facilitation without compromising national security or revenue collection through the efficient movement of goods, persons and services between South Africa and the adjoining states of Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia, Mozambique and Zimbabwe.
tgt: Sebaka sa Ditshebeletso tsa Moedi wa Boemakepe se tla atolosa taolo ya kgwebisano ntle le ho beha tshireletso kapa pokello ya lekeno la naha ka mosing ka tsamaiso ya dihlahiswa e hantle, batho le ditshebeletso dipakeng tsa Afrika Borwa le dinaha tse arolelanang meedi tsa Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia, Mozambique le Zimbabwe.

src: It will also result in the region realising a faster border clearance and limited duplication of border agency interventions, which in turn improves trade competitiveness and movement of person by cutting down on cost and time.
tgt: Sena se tla boela se baka hore lebatowa le nehelane ka bohlakisi ba meeding bo potlakileng le ho fokotsa phetapheto ya bonamodi ba baemedi ba meeding, mme sena se tla ntlafatsa tlhodisano ya kgwebisano le taolo ya maeto a batho ka ho fokotsa ditjeo le nako.

src: Cabinet approved that the National Treasury and Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) will coordinate South Africa’s preparation for the national risk assessment and upcoming mutual evaluation process which commences in mid-April 2019.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse hore Lefapha la Ditjhelete la Naha le Setsha sa Bohlwela sa Ditjhelete (FIC) di tla hokela boitukisetso ba Afrika Borwa mabapi le tsamaiso ya hlahlobo ya dikotsi tsa naha le tekolo ka bobedi tse tlang tse tla qala mahareng a Mmesa ka 2019.Tekolo ka bobedi ke tsamaiso ya ho hlahloba balekane e etswang ke ditsebi tsa matjhaba ho tswa ho dinaha tsa ditho tsa lekgotla la puso ka kopanelo, ke Lekala la Tshebetso ya Tshebediso ya Ditjhelete, ho hlahloba tshebetso e hantle ya lekgotla le kgahlano le kadimano ya ditjhelete (AML) le ho thibela mokgwatshebetso ya thuso ya ditjhelete ho tsa boferekanyi (CFT) mona Afrika Borwa.

src: The mutual evaluation is a peer-review process conducted by international experts from other member countries of the intergovernmental body, the Financial Action Task Force, to assess the effectiveness of the anti-money laundering (AML) and combating of terrorist financing (CFT) system in South Africa.
tgt: Diphetho tsa tsamaiso di tla thusa ho matlafatsa seriti sa mokgwatshebetso wa ditjhelete tsa Afrika Borwa ka ho hlwaya mekgwa e tla nkuwa ho lokisa bofokodi bo teng mokgwatshebetsong wa lekgotla le kgahlano le kadimano ya ditjhelete kapa thuso ya ditjhelete ho tsa boferekanyi.

src: The outcomes of the process will assist in strengthening the integrity of the South African financial system by identifying steps to be taken to address any weaknesses in our AML/CFT system.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ditshitshinyo tse hlahisitsweng ke Lefapha la Merero, Bodisa le Tlhatlhobo ya Tshebetso (DPME) ho Lefapha la Thuo ya Motheo (DBE).

src: The recommendations flow from the Impact evaluation of the Early Grade Reading Study after two years of interventions.
tgt: Ditshitshinyo di tswa ho Tekolo ya sekgahla sa Diphuphutso tsa Ho Bala ha bana ba Dihlopheng tse Tlase ka mora bonamodi ba dilemo tse pedi.

src: The DBE initiated the Early Grade Reading Study in collaboration with various universities.
tgt: DBE le ile la qala Diphuphutso tsa Ho Bala ha Bana ba Dihlopheng tse Tlase ka kopanelo le diyunivesithi tse mmalwa.

src: This is a large-scale educational impact evaluation which aims to build evidence about what works to improve the teaching and learning of early grade reading in African languages in the country.
tgt: Ena ke tekolo ya thuto ya sekgahla se seholo e ikemiseditseng ho aha bopaki ka hore ke eng se sebetsang mabapi le ho ntlafatsa ho ruta le ho ithuta ho bala dihlopheng tse tlase ka maleme a dipuo tsa bathobatsho tsa ka naheng.

src: The Report will be posted on the DPME website.
tgt: Pehelo e tla phatlalatswa wepsaeteng ya DPMKabinete e ananetse Moralo wa Leano la Dimusiamo tsa Naha.

src: Cabinet approved the Policy Framework on National Museums.
tgt: Maikemisetso ke ho ntlafatsa taolo le ditshebetso tsa dimusiamo ho ya ka phumaneho, kabobotjha, tekatekano, kaho le kopano ya setjhaba.

src: The aim is to transform the management and operations of museums in terms of access, redress, equity, nation-building and social cohesion.
tgt: Leano le sisinya ho kopantshwa ha dimusiamo dibopehong tsa taolo tse ntjha le ho fihlella poloko ya ditjeo ka ho fokotsa palo ya makgotla.

src: The policy proposes the clustering of museums into new management structures to achieve economies of scale by reducing the number of WEBTOKEN also provides for the grading of all the museums according to qualities, scope and significance to enable equitable funding allocations.
tgt: E boela e nehelana ka ho tshwaya dimusiamo ho ya ka boleng ba tsona, tshebetso, le bohlokwa ho dumella hore matlole a nehelanwe ka tekatekano.

src: Cabinet approved the National Guide for the Appointment of Persons to Boards and Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) of State-owned and State-controlled Institutions.
tgt: 25.Kabinete e ananetse Mosupatsela wa Naha wa Ho Thonya Batho ba Makgotla le Bahlanka ba Baholo ba Phethahatso (di-CEO) le Diinstitjhuti tsa Mmuso le tse Laolwang ke Mmuso.

src: The guide provides national principles and good-practice guidelines to promote uniformity in the appointment of persons.
tgt: Mosupatsela o nehelana ka tataiso ya melao le maitshwaro a matle a kgothaletsang mokgwa o tshwanang wa ho thonya batho.

src: It responds to the Presidential Review Committee on State-owned Entities to promote transparency, accountability and good governance practices in all organs of state.
tgt: E arabela Komiti ya Hlahlobo ya Kantoro ya Moporesidente ka Dikgwebo tsa Mmuso mabapi le hore ho kgothaletswe botshepehi, boikarabelo le maitshwaro a puso e ntle makaleng ohle a mmuso.

src: Cabinet approved the 6th progress report by the Inter-Ministerial Task Team on North West.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse pehelo ya bo6 ya kgatelopele ya Leboya Bophirima ho tswa ho Sehlopha sa Tshebetso ya Matona ka Kopanelo.

src: Cabinet is pleased that visible progress has been made in stabilising the provincial departments in North West and the provision of basic services has been prioritised.
tgt: Kabinete e thabetse kgatelopele e bonahalang e entsweng ho tsitsisa mafapha a porofense ya Leboya Bophirima le nehelo ya ditshebeletso tsa mantlha e potlakisitswe.

src: The intervention has cleared over 90% of the accruals to suppliers enabling the improved supply of medicine and equipment.
tgt: Bonamodi bo fetsisitse 90% ya ho eketseha ha tswalla ya dipatele tsa ba nehelanang ka ditshebeletso mme sena se kgonne ho ntlafaditse phano ya meriana le disebediswa tse ding.

src: Four of the five operating theatres at Mafikeng hospital have been returned to functionality.
tgt: Tse nne ho tse hlano tsa diphaphosi tsa diopereishene tsa Sepetlele sa Mafikeng di se di sebetsa hape.

src: A number of the funded vacant posts in the respective departments have been filled.
tgt: Boholo ba dikgeo tsa mesebetsi di tlatsitswe ka hoo mafapha a amehang a se a kgona ho sebetsa.

src: A process to address the backlog infrastructure maintenance has been put in place and the law enforcement agencies continue to make progress in bringing those who were involved in corruption to account.
tgt: Tshebetso e tobaneng le tlhokomelo ya meaho e se ntse e qadile mme baemedi ba tsa taolo ya molao ba tla tswella ho netefatsa hore ba tshwara ba ikarabellang ho diketso tsa bobodu.

src: Working with the North West leadership the appointed Administrators continue to make progress in setting in place good governance processes.
tgt: Ka tshebedisano mmoho le ketapele ya Leboya Bophirima Batsamaisi ba tla tswella ho fihlela kgatelopele ho kenyeng tshebetso ya puso e ntle.

src: The NCOP visited the North West in October and have tabled their report endorsing the National government intervention in the Province.
tgt: Lekgotla la Naha la Diporofense le ile la etela Leboya Bophirima ka Mphalane mme la nehelana ka pehelo ya lona e tshehetsang hore mmuso wa Naha o namole Porofenseng eo.

src: Cabinet approved the hosting of the following events:The Fourth Annual Meetings of the New Development Bank (NDB), during the first quarter of 2019.
tgt: Kabinete e ile ya boela ya ananela ho tshwarwa ha diketsahalo tse latelang:Dikopano tsa bone tsa selemo le selemo tsa Banka e Ntjha ya Ntshetsopele (NDB), nakong ya kotara ya pele ya 2019.

src: The NDB was established by the Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa (BRICS) bloc to mobilise resources to support infrastructure and sustainable development projects in BRICS countries, and other emerging markets and developing countries.
tgt: Banka e Ntjha ya Ntshetsopele e thihilwe ke sehlopha sa Brazil, Russia, India, China le Afrika Borwa (dinaha tsa BRICS) ho sebedisa disebediswa tse tla tshehetsa meaho le mananeo a ntshetsopele ya mokoka dinaheng tsa BRICS, le dimaraka tse ding tse thuthuhang le dinaha tse moruo o thuthuhang.

src: The 17th Ordinary Session of the African Ministerial Conference on the Environment (AMCEN) in June/July 2019.
tgt: Mokgahlelo wa Mehla wa Seboka sa bo7 sa Matona a Afrika a tsa Tikoloho (AMCEN) ka Phuptjane/Phupu ka 2019.

src: AMCEN is a permanent forum where African Ministers of the Environment deliberate and decide on environmental issues of relevance to the Continent.
tgt: Mokgahlelo wa Mehla wa Seboka sa bo7 sa Matona a Afrika a tsa Tikoloho ke foramo ya moshelella moo Matona a Afrika a tsa Tikoloho a buisanang le ho nka diqeto ka ditaba tsa tikoloho le seabo sa tsona Kontinenteng.

src: South Africa assumes its chairship from 2019 to 2021.Bills.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e tla qala ho ba modulasetulo ho tloha ka 2019 ho isa ho 2021.

src: Cabinet approved publication of the Revised Expropriation Bill for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse phatlalatso ya Bili ya Boeletsa Kamoho e le ho thonya maikutlo a setjhaba.

src: The revised bill adds a section that provides explicit circumstances under which land expropriation in the public interest may be without compensation.
tgt: Bili ya boeletso e tlatseletsa mokgahlelong o nehelanang ka maemo a totobetseng ao tlasa ona kamoho ya mobu e ka phethiswa ntle le ditlhapiso molemong wa setjhaba.

src: The section strengthen the earlier Expropriation Bill that was withdrawn from the parliament process.
tgt: Mokgahlelo o matlafatsa Bili ya Kamoho ya pele e ileng ya holwa tsamaisong ya palamente.

src: The Bill will assist in accelerating the land reform programme whilst within the framework of the constitutional principles.
tgt: Bili e tla thusa ho potlakisa kabobotjha ya mobu ka hara moralo wa melawana ya molaotheo.

src: Cabinet approved for the publication of the Conduct of Financial Institutions Bill of 2018 for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e amohetse phatlalatso ya Bili ya Boitshwaro ba Diinstitjhuti tsa Ditjhelete ya 2018 e le ho thonya maikutlo a setjhaba.

src: This forms part of government’s reform of the financial sector regulation towards a Twin Peaks model and follows the enactment of the Financial Sector Regulation Act, 2017 (Act 9 of 2017) which, amongst others, aims to ensure better market conduct and the treatment of customers in the financial sector.
tgt: Sena ke karolo ya mmuso ya ho rala botjha taolo ya lekala la ditjhelete ho ya ho mokgwa o taolo ya ditjhelete o bitswang Twin Peaks le ho latela Molao wa Lekala la Taolo ya Ditjhelete, wa 2017 (Molao wa 9 wa 2017) oo, ho tse ding, o ikemeseditseng ho netefatsa hore maemo a maraka le tshwaro ya bareki di ya ntlafala lekaleng la ditjhelete.

src: Market conduct regulation aims to prevent and manage when prevention is not successful, the poor outcomes that arise from financial institutions conducting their business in ways that are unfair to customers or undermines the integrity of financial markets and confidence in the financial system.
tgt: Taolo ya tsamaiso ya maraka e ikemiseditse ho thibela le ho laola ha thibelo e sa atlehe, diphetho tse mpe tse ka phahamang ho tswa ho diinstitjhuti tsa ditjhelete tsamaisong ya kgwebo ya tsona ka mekgwa e seng hantle ho bareki kapa e nyedisang serithi sa dimaraka tsa ditjhelete le tshepo ya mokgwatshebetso ya ditjhelete.

src: The Bill will strengthen customer protection by putting in place a single comprehensive market conduct law.
tgt: Bili e tla matlafatsa tshireletso ya moreki ka ho beha molao o le mong o akaretsang tsamaiso ya maraka tsohle.

src: This will result in the consistent application of customer-protection principles across the financial sector.
tgt: Sena se tla baka tshebetso e tshwanang ya tshireletso ya melawana ya moreki lekaleng la ditjhelete ka bophara.

src: It provides for a single, activity-based approach to licensing all financial institutions, and ensuring full regulatory coverage and supervision.
tgt: E nehelana ka mokgwa o le mong, o ikamahantshang le tshebetso ho isa ho nehelaneng ka dilaesense ho diinstitjhuti tsohle tsa ditjhelete, le ho netefatsa ho kenyeletsa taolo le bolebedi.

src: This will allow the newly established Financial Sector Conduct Authority to better meet its mandate of protecting financial customers by ensuring fair treatment.
tgt: Sena se dumella hore Bolaodi ba Boitshwaro ba Lekala la Ditjhelete bo sa tswa thehwa bo kgone ho ikamahantsha le thomo ya yona ya ho tshireletsa bareki ba ditjhelete ka ho netefatsa tshwaro e tshwanang.

src: The Bill, which will apply to all financial institutions, also supports transformation of the financial sector through implementation of the Financial Sector Code issued under the Broad-Based Black Economic Empowerment Act, 2003 (Act 53 of 2003) by requiring that policies be introduced to comply with the code and also supervising implementation of those policies.
tgt: Bili eo e tla sebediswa diinstitjhuti tsohle tsa ditjhelete, e tla boela e tshehetsa ntlafatso ya lekala la ditjhelete ka ho kenya Molao wa Lekala la Ditjhelete o ntshitsweng tlasa Molao wa Matlafatso ya Batho ba Batsho Moruong ka Kotloloho, wa 2003 (Molao wa 53 wa 2003) ka ho kopa hore maano a kenyeletswe ho ikamahantsha le molao ha mmoho le ho lebella kenyo tshebetsong ya maano ao.

src: Cabinet approved for the introduction of the Financial Matters Amendment Bill of 2018 in Parliament.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse tsebahatsa Bili ya Sehlomathiso sa Merero ya tsa Ditjhelete Palamenteng.

src: The amendments relate to the:a) Insolvency Act of 1963, to strengthen the regulation of over-the-counter derivative market, in line with G20 commitmentsb) Military Pensions Act of 1976, to address discriminatory provisionsc) Banks Act of 1990, to allow for qualifying state-owned companies to apply for banking licencesd) Government Employment Pension Law of 1996, to change the clean break principle in the case of divorce, ensuring that members’ pension pay outs to former spouses on divorce are not converted to a debt obligation ande) Auditing Profssion Act of 2005, to address challenges and limitations that the Independent Regulatory Board for Auditors faces in discharging its regulatory and oversight responsibilities.
tgt: Diphetoho di amanana le tse latelang:a) Molao wa Putlamo ya Kgwebo wa 1963, ho matlafatsa taolo ya dikonteraka tseo ho utlwanweng ka tsona, ho ya ka boitlamo ba G20b) Molao wa Dipenshene tsa Masole wa 1976, ho rarolla karolo ya kgethollo le ho netefatsa bosiyo ba tshekamelo ya bong, e le ho amohela mefuta e fapaneng ya dikamanoc) Molao wa Dibanka wa 1990, ho dumella dikhamphane tseo e leng tsa mmuso tse tshwanelehileng ho etsa kopo ya dilaesense tsa dibanka, haeba ba Phethahatso ba ananela d) Molao wa Dipenshene tsa Basebetsi ba Mmuso wa 1996, ho fetola mokgwa wa ditefo tlhalanong, ho netefatswe hore ditefo tsa penshene ya ditho ho balekane ba mehleng ha di fetolwe ho ba sekoloto le e) Molao wa Porofeshene ya Bohlahlobi ba Dibuka wa 2005, ho rarolla diphephetso le dithibelo tseo Boto e Ikemetseng ya Taolo ya Bahlahlobi ba Dibuka e tobaneng le tsona ha e etsa mesebetsi ya yona ya taolo le tekolo.

src: Upcoming events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse Tlang.

src: National Minimum Wage (NMW) announcementPresident Ramaphosa will announce the NMW at an event to be held at Kliptown in Soweto on Friday, 7 December 2018.
tgt: Tsebahatso ya Bonnyane ba Moputso wa Naha (NMW)Moporesidenete Ramaphosa o tla tsebahatsa Bonnyane ba Moputso wa Naha moketeng o tla tshwarelwa Kliptown Soweto ka Labohlano, la 7 Tshitwe 2018.

src: The NMW will immediately benefit more than six million workers and help address the level of inequality and poverty in South Africa.
tgt: Bonnyane ba Moputso wa Naha bo tla bo sentse bo tswela molemo basebetsi ba fetang Dimilione tse tsheletseng le ho thusa ho lokisa boemo ba tlhokeho ya tekatekano le bofuma Afrika Borwa.

src: This landmark proclamation will extend our social net to the most vulnerable people.
tgt: Phatlalatso ena ya seemahale sena e tla atolosa moputso wa setjhaba le ho batho ba kotsing haholo.

src: International Anti-Corruption DayIn commemoration of the UN’s International Anti-Corruption Day on Sunday, 9 December 2018, Cabinet reaffirms the country’s fight against corruption in both the private and public sectors.
tgt: Letsatsi le Kgahlano le Bobodu la Matjhaba Ka keteko ya Letsatsi le Kgahlano le Bobodu la Matjhaba la Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tsa Matjhaba ka Kopanelo (UN) ka Sontaha, 9 Tshitwe 2018, Kabinete e hatella twantsho ya Naha kgahlano le bobodu Makaleng a poraefete le a mmuso bobedi.

src: The JCPS Cluster has prioritised the fight against this scourge in line with government’s zero-tolerance stance towards corruption.
tgt: Sehlopha sa Toka, Thibelo ya Tlolo ya Molao le Tshireletso (JCPS) se potlakisitse ntwa e kgahlano le sewa sena ka ho ikamahantsha le boemo ba mmuso bo kgahlano le bobodu ho hang.

src: Corruption is a societal problem that must be fought by everyone as it hinders socio-economic development and increases poverty by diverting resources away from where they are most needed.
tgt: Bobodu ke bothata ba setjhaba mme botlameha hore bo lwantshwe ke bohle ka ha bo thibela ntshetsopele ya moruo le ho eketsa bofuma ka ho tlosa disebediswa moo di hlokehang ka ho fetisisa.

src: International Human Rights DaySouth Africa will join the international community in observing International Human Rights Day on Monday, 10 December 2018.
tgt: Letsatsi la Ditokelo tsa Botho la Matjhaba Afrika Borwa e tla keteka le setjhaba sa matjhabeng ha ho hopolwa Letsatsi la Ditokelo tsa Botho la Matjhaba ka Mantaha, 10 Tshitwe 2018.

src: The day marks the anniversary of the UN General Assembly's adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948.
tgt: Letsatsi lena le tshwaya sehopotso sa ho ananelwa ha Boitlamo ba Lefatshe ba Ditokelo tsa Botho ka 1948 ke Seboka sa Kakaretso sa Mokgatlo wa Dinaha tsa Matjhaba ka Kopanelo (UN).

src: Government continues to ensure that all South Africans enjoy all human rights such as the rights to life, equality and human dignity.
tgt: Mmuso o tswella ho netefatsa hore maAfrika Borwa ohle a natefelwa ke ditokelo tsa botho tse jwalo ka ditokelo tsa bophelo, tetekano le seriti sa botho.

src: Every citizen has a responsibility to ensure that human rights and dignity in our nation is protected.
tgt: Moahi e mong le e mong o na le boikarabelo ba ho netefatsa hore ditokelo le seriti tsa botho di tshireletsehile naheng ya rona.

src: Global Commission on the Future of WorkThe report from the Global Commission on the Future of Work will be launched on 22 January 2019.
tgt: Komishene ya Lefatshe ya Bokamoso ba Mesebetsi Pehelo e tswang ho Komishine ya Lefatshe ya Bokamoso ba Mesebetsi e tla phatlalatswa ka la 22 Pherekgong 2019.

src: It was established by the ILO in 2017 to assess the rapid transformation taking place in the global economy and world of work, and identify the key challenges and recommendations.
tgt: E thehilwe ke Mokgatlo wa Basebetsi wa Matjhaba (ILO) ka 2017 ho hlahloba ntlafatso e etsahalang moruong wa lefatshe le mokgahlelong wa mesebetsi, le ho hlwaya diphephetso tse ka sehloohong le ditshitshinyo.

src: This High-Level Global Commission is co-chaired by President Ramaphosa together with Prime Minister Stefan Löfven of the Kingdom of Sweden.
tgt: Komishene ya Boemo-Bo-Kahodimo ya Lefatsheng e dulasetulo ka kopanelo ke Moporesidente Ramaphosa ha mmoho le Tonakgolo Stefan Löfven wa Borena ba Sweden.

src: Messages.
tgt: Melaetsa.

src: CondolencesCabinet joins President Ramaphosa in expressing sadness at the passing of Struggle stalwart and former High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, Mr Mendi Msimang, on Monday, 3 December 2018, following a long illness.
tgt: MatshedisoKabinete ha mmoho le Moporesidente Ramaphosa e fetisetsa matshediso a yona ka ho hlokahala ha Molwanedi wa Tokoloho le Mokomishenara ya Moholo wa mehleng naheng ya Yuropa ka Kopanelo, Monghadi Mendi Msimang, ka Mantaha, ka la 3 Tshitwe 2018, ka mora ho kula ka nako e telele.

src: Cabinet extends condolences to the family, friends, comrades and associates of Mr Msimang.
tgt: Kabinete e fetisetsa matshediso ho ba lelapa, metswalle, makhomorete le ba amanang le Monghadi Msimang.

src: Mr Msimang has been accorded a Special Official Funeral category 1 which entails elements of military ceremonial honour in line with the policy on State and Provincial official funerals.
tgt: Monghadi Msimang o tla bolokwa ho ya ka mokgahlelo wa 1 wa Lepato la Semmuso le Ikgethileng le tla kenyeletsa dikarolo tsa tshebeletso ya tlotla ya sesole e ikamahantshang le leano la mapato a semmuso a Naha le a Porofense.

src: Congratulations.1 Cabinet congratulates Banyana on reaching the final of the 2018 Africa Women’s Cup of Nations.
tgt: Ditebohiso.1 Kabinete e lebohisa Banyana Banyana ka ho fihlela mokgahlelo wa ho qetela wa Mohope wa Dinaha tsa Afrika wa Basadi wa 2018.

src: By doing so they have automatically qualified for next year’s FIFA Women’s World Cup in France.2 Cabinet commends Dr Lindiwe Sidali, who made history by becoming the first African female cardiothoracic surgeon in the country.
tgt: Ka ho etsa jwalo ba tla be ba sentse ba fetela ho Mohope wa Lefatshe selemo se tlang wa FIFA wa Basadi mane Fora.

src: Cabinet met on Wednesday, 13 February 2019 at Tuynhuys in Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e kopane ka Laboraro, la 13 Hlakola 2019, Tuynhuys Motse Kapa.
