src: The implementation of the NBF is guided by the adopted National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (2015-2025).
tgt: Ho sebediswa ha NBF ena ho tataiswa ke Leano le amohetsweng la Naha la Dintho tse Fapafapanneng tse Phelang le Moralo wa Tshebetso (wa dilemo tsa 2015-2025).

src: South Africa is a signatory to the United Nations’ Convention on Biological Diversity, which promotes the conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components, and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources.
tgt: Afrika Borwa ke setho se jarang boikarabelo sa Seboka sa Dinaha tse Kopaneng tsa Lefatshe se malebana le tlhokomelo ya Dintho tse Fapafapaneng tse Phelang, e ntshetsang pele paballo ya bophelo ba dintho tse fapafapaneng tse phelang, tshebediso e nang le mokoka ya dikarolo tsa tsona, le kabelano e hlokang leeme, hape e nang le tekatekano ya ditholwana tse fumanehang mehloding ya diphatsa tsa lefutso.

src: Draft National Spatial Development Framework (NSDF).
tgt: Moralo wa Tokomane ya Moralo wa Naha wa Ntshetsopele ya Dibaka tsa Bodulo (NSDF).

src: Cabinet approved the draft NSDF for implementation.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse moralo wa NSDF bakeng sa ho sebediswa.

src: It was prepared in terms of the Spatial Planning and Land Use Management Act, 2013 (Act 16 of 2013) and approved for public consultation in 2019.
tgt: E ile ya etswa ho ikamahantswe le Molao wa Moralo wa Dibaka tsa Bodulo le Taolo ya Tshebediso ya Mobu, molao wa 2013 (Molao wa 16 wa selemo sa 2013), mme ya ananelwa bakeng sa ditherisano tsa setjhaba ka selemo sa 2019.

src: Inputs were obtained from various stakeholders, including professional bodies, all spheres of government, SOEs and members of the public.
tgt: Diphehiso di ile tsa amohelwa ho tswa ho bankakarolo ba fapafapaneng, ho kenyeletswa le mekgatlo ya ditsebi, didikadikwe tsohle tsa mmuso, di-SOE le ditho tsa setjhaba.

src: The framework seeks to deal with the eradication of the colonial and apartheid spatial legacies in an orderly and coordinated manner.
tgt: Moralo ona o batla ho sebetsana le ho fediswa ha maano a kabo ya dibaka tsa bodulo a mebuso ya bokoloniale le ya kgethollo ka mokgwa o makgethe le o hokahantsweng hantle.

src: It provides a long-term spatially focused developmental approach towards planning and a land use management system.
tgt: O lokisetsa katamelo ya nako e telele e tsepamisitseng maikutlo ntshetsopeleng ya dibaka tsa bodulo, e tla fihlella moralong le tshebetsong ya taolo ya tshebediso ya mobu.

src: The document will be accessible through the website of the Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development (WEBTOKEN).
tgt: Tokomane ena e tla fumaneha webosaeteng ya Lefapha la Temo, Diphetoho tsa Mobu le Ntshetsopele ya Dibaka tsa Mahae (WEBTOKEN).

src: Official Identity Management Policy.
tgt: Leano la Taolo ya Boitsebiso ba Semolao.

src: Cabinet approved the Official Identity Management Policy, following an extensive public consultation in 2021.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Leano la Taolo ya Boitsebiso ba Semolao, ka morao ho ditherisano tsa setjhaba tse ileng tsa tshwarwa ka selemo sa 2021.

src: This policy will replace the current Identification Act, 1997 (Act 68 of 1997), which establishes the National Population Register (NPR) and also specify its scope in the mandatory records that are captured on it.
tgt: Leano lena le suthisa Molao wa jwale wa Boitsebiso wa selemo sa 1997 (Molao wa 68 wa selemo sa 1997), o thehang Rejistara ya Naha ya Setjhaba (NPR), o boetseng hape o totobatsa tema ya yona direkotong tse tlamehang ho ngolwa ho yona.

src: This Act is not aligned to the constitutional principles of equality, non-discrimination and human dignity.
tgt: Molao ona ha o a amahanngwa le metheo ya molaotheo ya tekatekano, ho se kgetholle le seriti sa botho.

src: The adopted policy proposes a single digital NPR of all people – irrespective of citizenship and sex status – who live and have lived in the country.
tgt: Leano lena le amohetsweng le sisinya hore ho be le NPR e le nngwe ya digithale bakeng sa batho bohle – ho sa natsehe boemo ba boahi le ba bong – ba phelang kapa ba phetseng Afrika Borwa.

src: It also provides for a biometric National Identity System (NIS) that will enable a single view of a person.
tgt: Hape le lokisetsa hore ho be le Sistimi ya Naha ya Boitsebiso (NIS) e sebedisang kgatiso ya menwana, e tla thusa hore ho bonahale motho a le mong ka nako.

src: The NIS will also be able to interface with other government and private sector identity systems.
tgt: NIS ena e tla boela e kgona ho hokelana le disistimi tse ding tsa boitsebiso tsa mmuso le tsa poraefete.

src: The policy will also ensure the protection of the rights of members of the Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Intersex, Queer and Asexual community.
tgt: Leano lena le tla boela le netefatsa tshireletso ya ditokelo tsa ditho tsa setjhaba sa LGBTIQTokomane ya Ntlhakemo ya Mmuso Malebana le Manyalo Afrika Borwa.

src: White Paper on Marriages in South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse Tokomane ya Ntlhakemo ya Mmuso malebana le Manyalo Afrika Borwa bakeng sa tshebediso.

src: The White Paper responds to many court judgements that have found some elements of the current marriage legislation to be unconstitutional.
tgt: Tokomane ena ya Ntlhakemo e arabela dikahlolo tse ngata tse entsweng ke makgotla a dinyewe tse ileng tsa fumana dikarolo tse itseng tsa melao ya jwale ya manyalo di sa ikamahanye le molaotheo wa naha.

src: It has aligned all marriages to be concluded in accordance with the principles of equality, non-discrimination and human dignity as provided for in the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996.
tgt: E amahantse manyalo ohle hore a tle a phethahatswe ho ikamahantswe le metheo ya tekatekano, ho se kgetholle le seriti sa botho, jwalo ka ha ho hlakisitswe Molaong wa Motheo wa Rephaboliki ya Afrika Borwa wa selemo sa 1996.

src: The approved White Paper will allow South Africans and residents of all sexual orientations, religious and cultural persuasions to conclude legal unions in line with the constitutional principles.
tgt: Tokomane ena e ananetsweng ya Ntlhakemo ya Mmuso e tla dumella Maafrika Borwa ohle le badudi ba ditshekamelo tsohle tsa bong, ditumelo le ditso tsohle ho kena manyalong a molaong ho ikamahantswe le metheo ya molaotheo.

src: The White Paper outlines some of the unions that are excluded such as child marriages and those done in the absence of the other party.
tgt: Ntlhakemo ena ya Mmuso e fana ka lenane la dikopano tse ding tse sa amohelehang tse kang manyalo a bana le tse ding tse phethwang motho wa bobedi a amehang a le siyo.

src: One-Stop Border Post (OSBP) Policy.
tgt: Leano la ho Thibela Tiehiso Madibohong (OSBP).

src: Cabinet approved the OSBP and its implementation strategy.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse OSBP mmoho le leano la yona ya tshebediso.

src: The policy seeks to harmonise the movement of people and goods between South Africa’s land ports of entry and its neighbouring countries.
tgt: Leano lena le batla ho tlosa mekgwa ya tshebetso e sitisang ho tsamaya ha batho le tsamaiso ya thepa pakeng tsa madiboho a Afrika Borwa le dinaha tsa boahisani.

src: It gives effect to the One-Stop Border Framework that was adopted by Cabinet in 2018.
tgt: E kenya tshebetsong Moralo wa ho Thibela Tiehiso Madibohong o neng o dumelwe ke Kabinete ka selemo sa 2018.

src: The application of the policy will alleviate current congestions at our land ports of entry for cross-border travellers and traders.
tgt: Tshebediso ya leano lena e tla fokotsa tshubuhlellano ya jwale madibohong a rona bakeng la baeti ba tshelang meedi le bahwebi.

src: These interventions are also key in the country’s efforts in driving the AfCFTA agreement.
tgt: Mehato ena e boetse e le ya bohlokwa matsapeng a naha a ho sebedisa ka katleho tumellano ya AfCFTHa leano lena le se le amahantswe le melao e amehang mmoho le dintlafatso tsa metheo ya tshebetso ya moruo, re dumela hore tshebetso ya ho fetiswa ha thepa, dikoloi le batho e tla etswa ka mokgwa o hlokang makukuno le o potlakileng.

src: Interim hosting of the Presidential Climate Commission.
tgt: Ho Tshwarwa ha Nakwana ha Khomishene ya Mopresidente ya Boemo ba Lehodimo.

src: Cabinet approved the transitional hosting of the Presidential Climate Commission by the National Economic Development and Labour Council (Nedlac).
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho tshwarwa ha Khomishene ya Mopresidente ya Boemo ba Lehodimo ke Lekgotla la Naha la Ntshetsopele ya Moruo le Basebetsi (Nedlac), e le mosebetsi oo Nedlac e o filweng ha nakwana.

src: Nedlac will host the commission with its secretariat for two years or shorter to enable the promulgation of the Climate Change Act.
tgt: Nedlac e tla tshwara khomishene ka ofisi ya yona ya dinako tsohle nakong ya dilemo tse pedi kapa ka tlase, e le ho dumella ho pasiswa ha Molao wa Diphetoho tsa Boemo ba Lehodimo.

src: The period will also afford the commission – in collaboration with the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment – to finalise the feasibility study and business case for the future establishment of the commission as determined by the Climate Change Bill.
tgt: Nako ena e tla boetse e thusa khomishene – ka tshebetsommoho le Lefapha la Meru, Botshwasi le Tikoloho – ho phetha diphuputso tsa kgonahalo le tokomane e fupereng mabaka a projekte ena malebana le ho thewa ha ka moso ha khomishene ho latela ditshisinyo tsa Bili ya Diphetoho tsa Boemo ba Lehodimo.

src: Draft White Paper on National Rail Policy.
tgt: Tokomane ya Moralo wa Ntlhakemo ya Mmuso Malebana le Leano la Naha la Ditshebeletso tsa Diterene.

src: Cabinet approved the draft White Paper on National Rail Policy.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse tokomane ya moralo wa Ntlhakemo ya Mmuso malebana le Leano la Naha la Ditshebeletso tsa Diterene.

src: The policy will guide in creating an efficient transport system that will be able to compete locally and internationally.
tgt: Leano lena le tla tataisa ho thewa ha tshebetso e sebetsang hantle ya dipalangwang e tla kgona ho emelana le tlhodisano ka hare ho naha esita le matjhabeng.

src: The policy proposes focused interventions that will promote investments in both the feight and passenger services.
tgt: Leano lena le sisinya mehato e tsepamisang maikutlo e tla kgothaletsa ho jalwa ha matsete ditshebeletsong tsa ho thothwa ha thepa le tsa bapalami.

src: It will also improve rural access and increase mobility to promote economic growth.
tgt: E tla boetse e ntlafatsa ho fihlelleha ha dibaka tsa mahaeng, e be e eketse bokgoni ba ho tsamaya molemong wa ho ntshetsa pele kgolo ya moruo.

src: It will also contribute substantially towards reducing the country’s emissions as it proposes rail genetic technologies in upgrading the rail stock.
tgt: E tla boetse e ba le seabo se seholo phokotsong ya tlhahiso ya naha ya dikgase tse tshilafatsang sepakapaka jwalo ka ha e sisinya ditheknoloji tse ikgethang tsa ditshebeletso tsa diterene ha ho ntlafatswa disebediswa tsa ditshebeletso tsa diterene.

src: The policy will be made public once the Department of Transport has published it in the Government Gazette.
tgt: Leano lena le tla hlahella setjhabeng hang ha Lefapha la Dipalangwang le se le le phatlaladitse Lesedinyanneng la Mmuso.

src: Independent Municipal Demarcation Authority (IMDA) Bill of 2022.
tgt: Bili Bili ya Lekgotla le Ikemetseng la Meedi ya Bommasepala (IMDA) ya Selemo sa 2022.

src: Cabinet approved the submission of the IMDA Bill of 2022 to Parliament for further processing.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho romelwa Palamenteng ha Bili ya IMDA ya selemo sa 2022 bakeng sa ho ntshetswa pele.

src: The Bill was published for public comment in June 2020 and subsequent engagements on the comments received from the public.
tgt: Bili ena e ile ya phatlaletswa ditshwaelo tsa setjhaba ka kgwedi ya Phuptjane selemong sa 2020, mme dipuisano tse ileng tsa latela tsa ho tshohla ditshwaelo di ile tsa amohelwa ho tswa setjhabeng.

src: The Bill provides the governance regime of the IMDIts proposals include clarifying the terms of the Board members and that they are to serve on a part-time basis, except for the Chairperson who may serve on a full-time basis.
tgt: Bili ena e fana ka melawana ya tsamaiso ya IMDDitshisinyo tsa yona di kenyeletsa ho hlakiswa ha dipehelo tsa ditho tsa Boto le hore ditho di tshwanela ho sebetsa mosebetsi wa nakwana, kantle ho Modulasetulo yena ya ka sebetsang ka dinako tsohle.

src: It also guides the IMDA on the process towards the delimiting of boundaries.
tgt: E boetse e tataisa IMDA tshebetsong e lebisang ho theweng ha meedi.

src: Upcoming event.
tgt: Ketsahalo e Tlang.

src: Visit to the Middle East.
tgt: Ketelo ya Botjhabela bo Mahareng.

src: President Ramaphosa will lead a delegation of Ministers to the World Expo Dubai in the United Arab Emirates on Monday, 28 March 2022.
tgt: Mopresidente Ramaphosa o tla etella pele boemedi ba Matona ho ya sebokeng sa World Expo Dubai se tla tshwarelwa United Arab Emirates ka Mantaha wa 28 Tlhakubele 2022.

src: South Africa is participating at the expo with a pavilion showcasing the country’s rich heritage and investment opportunities.
tgt: Afrika Borwa, e ilo emelwa ke letshwelehadi, e tla ba le seabo dipontshong tsena ka ho bapatsa mafa a nonneng a naha le menyetla ya matsete.

src: Messages.
tgt: Melaetsa.

src: CongratulationsCabinet extended its congratulations and well-wishes to the:the South African women’s cricket team, for flying the national flag high at the Women’s Cricket World Cup in New Zealand.
tgt: DithoholetsoKabinete e thoholeditse le ho lakaletsa katleho: sehlopha sa Afrika Borwa sa kirikete ya basadi, ka ho tumisa Afrika Borwa dipapading tsa Mohope wa Lefatshe wa Kirikete ya Basadi tse tshwaretsweng New Zealand.

src: They defeated current World Champions England in their third match and have managed to win four matches in the tournament so far.
tgt: Sehlopha sena se ile sa hlola England, eo e leng Mmampodi wa jwale wa Lefatshe, papading ya sona ya boraro, hape, ho fihlela jwale, se kgonne ho hapa tlholo dipapading tse nne tlhodisanong ena.

src: CondolencesCabinet joined President Ramaphosa in extending condolences to the government and people of the Republic of Zambia following the passing of former President Rupiah Bwezani Banda (85).Cabinet expressed condolences to the family and friends of:Mr Michael Spicer (68), the former Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Business Leadership South Africa, who played a significant role in forging a stronger relationship between business and WEBTOKEN Luzuko Koti (47), the former Director of Communication and Marketing at the Nelson Mandela Foundation and Business Manager of Channel Africa.
tgt: MatshedisoKabinete e ikamahantse le Mopresidente Ramaphosa ho fetisa matshediso a yang mmusong le bathong ba Rephaboliki ya Zambia ka morao ho lefu la Mopresidente wa bona wa mehleng Rupiah Bwezani Banda (ya dilemo di 85).

src: Mr Sheik Abdul Gamiet Gabier (86), Life President of the Muslim Judicial Council South Africa, who was a renowned scholar, community activist and a pioneer of the Al-Azhar Institute of Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e tshedisitse malapa le metswalle ya: Ntate Michael Spicer (ya dilemo di 68), Mohlanka ya ka Sehloohong wa mehleng wa Lekgotla la Phethahatso (CEO), wa Business Leadership South Africa, ya bileng le tema e matla mosebetsing wa ho theha dikamano tse matla pakeng tsa sedikadikwe sa kgwebo le mmuso.

src: Fourth South Africa Investment Conference (SAIC).
tgt: Ditaba tse Itlhommeng PeleSeboka sa Bone sa Botsetedi sa Afrika Borwa (SAIC).

src: Cabinet welcomed the successful conclusion of the fourth SAIC held at the Sandton Convention Centre, Johannesburg on Thursday, 24 March 2022, which saw domestic and international investors pledging new investments in our country.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho phethelwa ka katleho ha seboka sa bone sa SAIC se neng se tshwaretswe Sandton Convention Centre, Johannesburg ka Labone la la 24 Tlhakubele 2022, seo ho sona batsetedi ba kwano le ba matjhaba ba itlammeng ho tsetela naheng ya rona.

src: Our country received 80 new investment pledges totalling R332 billion.
tgt: Naha ya rona e fumane maitlamo a 80 a matjha a matsete a ballwang dibiliyoneng tse R332.

src: This takes the total investments pledged to R.14 trillion, which not only represents 95 percent of our investment target but also places us firmly on the path to exceed our R.2 trillion investment target over five years.
tgt: Sena se beha matsete kaofela ao ho itlanngweng ka ona ho ditriliyone tse R.14, mme palo ena ke dipersente tse 95 tsa matsete ao re a pheelletseng e boelang e re behe boemong bo botle ba ho feta matsete ao re a pheelletseng a ballwang ho ditriliyone tse R.2 dilemong tse hlano tse tlang.

src: These investment commitments affirm our country’s status as an investment destination of choice.
tgt: Boinehelo bona matseteng bo tiisa maemo a naha ya rona jwaloka e tshepelwang matsete.

src: So far, R316 billion of the commitments have been invested in 46 projects that have been completed and a further 57 projects that are still under construction.
tgt: Ho fihlela jwale, maitlamo a ballwang dibiliyoneng tse R316 a tsetetswe diprojekeng tse 46 tse seng di phethetswe, le diprojekeng tse ding tse 57 tse ntseng di tswela pele.

src: Cabinet notes the successes of past pledges as reported at the Conference, covering among others new production capacityin sectors as diverse as automobiles, food production, pharmaceuticals and digital centres.
tgt: Kabinete e elellwa dikatleho tsa maitlamo a pele jwalokaha a tlalehilwe Sebokeng, tse kenyeletsang hara tse ding mothamo o motjha wa tlhahiso makaleng a fapaneng a kang a makoloi, tlhahiso ya dijo, tlhahiso ya meriana le ditsi tsa dijithale.

src: Cabinet called on all sectors of society to support these critical interventions as we work together to reverse our unemployment rate, which climbed to percent, according to the Quarterly Labour Force Survey results released recently by Statistics South Africa.
tgt: Kabinete e ipileditse makaleng ohle setjhabeng ho tshehetsa maiteko ana a bohlokwa ha re sebetsa mmoho ho lwantsha tlhokeho ya mesebetsi, e seng e finyelletse dipersenteng tse 35.3, ho ya ka diphetho tsa Dipatlisiso tsa Kotara ka nngwe tsa Basebetsi tse sa tswa ntshwa ke ba Dipalopalo Afrika Borwa.

src: Lifting of the National State of Disaster Cabinet also welcomed the lifting of the National State of Disaster announced by President Cyril Ramaphosa on Monday, 4 April 2022.
tgt: Ho fediswa ha Boemo ba Naha ba Dikoduwa Kabinete e boetse e ananetse ho fediswa ha Boemo ba Naha ba Dikoduwa ho tsebahaditsweng ke Presidente Cyril Ramaphosa ka Mantaha wa la 04 Mmesa 2022.

src: This milestone was made possible by the resilience of people in South African who complied with all Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) safety protocols designed by government to save lives and livelihoods.
tgt: Ketsahalo ena ya bohlokwa e kgonahaditswe ke mamello ya batho ba Afrika Borwa ba ileng ba hlompha melao yohle ya polokeho ya Lefu la vaerase ya Corona (COVID-19) e behilweng ke mmuso molemong wa ho boloka maphelo le mekgwa ya ho iphedisa.

src: The pandemic will henceforth be managed in terms of the National Health Act, 2003 (Act 61 of 2003).
tgt: Ho tloha jwale sewa sena se tla laolwa ho latela Molao wa Naha wa Bophelo bo Botle wa 2003 (Molao wa 61 wa 2003).

src: The draft health regulations that will inform the National Health Act of 2003 are open for public comment until 16 April 2022.
tgt: Setjhaba se ka ntsha maikutlo a sona ka melawana e sisintsweng ya bophelo bo botle e tla ba karolo ya Molao wa Naha wa Bophelo bo Botle wa 2003 ho fihlela la 16 Mmesa 2022.

src: Cabinet reminded all people in the country to continue taking the necessary preventative measures to safeguard ourselves and others against COVID-19 infections.
tgt: Kabinete e hopoditse batho bohle naheng ho tswela pele ka ho hlompha mehato ya bohlokwa ya tshireletso ho ipoloka ka bobona le ba bang kgahlano le ho tshwaetswa ke COVID-19.

src: This includes regularly washing our hands with water and soap or using a 70% alcohol-based sanitiser, wearing a mask that covers both the nose and mouth when indoors, keeping a safe social distance of at least one metre, opening windows for ventilation and vaccinating.
tgt: Sena se kenyeletsa ho hlapa matsoho kgafetsa ka metsi le sesepa kapa o sebedisa sehlwekisi se nang le dipersente tse 70 tsa alcohol, ho rwala semonkwana se kwahelang nko le molomo ha o le katlung, ho se atamelane le batho ba bang ka bonnyane mitara, ho bula difenstere hotle moya o kene le ho enta.

src: COVID-19 vaccinations are effective in preventing serious illness, hospitalisation and even death.
tgt: Ente ya COVID-19 e sebetsa hantle ho thibela ho kula haholo, ho robatswa sepetlele le lefu.

src: Protect yourself and your loved ones by visiting your nearest vaccination site to get vaccinated for free, even without an appointment.
tgt: Itshireletse le ba lelapa la hao ka ho etela sebaka sa ho enta se haufinyane o ente mahala, hobane ha ho sa hlokeha hore o bolele hore o a tla.

src: Migration to digital broadcasting.
tgt: Ho Fallela Kgasong ya Dijithale.

src: The deferment on the Analogue Switch-off Date from 31 March to 30 June 2022 provides sufficient time to government to complete the installation of set-top boxes (STBs) for households that have registered timeously and are entitled to receive them before the analogue switch-off.
tgt: Ho emiswa ha ho kwala ho hasa ka mokgwa wa Analogue wa jwale ho neng ho lebelletswe ho ba ka la 31 Tlhakubele empa ho se ho tla ba ka la 30 Phupjane 2022 ho fana ka nako e lekaneng ya hore mmuso o phethele ho kenngwa ha di-set-top box (di-STB) malapeng a ingodisitseng ka nako a nang le tokelo ya ho di fumana pele ho tingwa mokgwa wa kgaso wa analogue.

src: The Department of Communications and Digital Technologies will ensure that all the 507 251 households that registered by 31 October 2021 are connected no later than 30 June 2022.
tgt: Lefapha la Dikgokahano le Teknoloji ya Dijithale le tla netefatsa hore malapa ohle a 507 251 a ingodisitseng ho fihlella la 31 Mphalane 2021 a a hokelwa ho eso fete la 30 Phupjane 2022.

src: The 260 868 households that registered between 31 October 2021 and 10 March 2022 will be connected to their STBs by 30 September 2022.
tgt: Malapa a 260 868 a ingodisitseng ho tloha ho la 31 Mphalane 2021 ho ya ho la 10 Tlhakubele 2022 a tla hokelwa ho di-STB ho e so fete la la 30 Loetse 2022.

src: Cabinet is confident that the completion of this process will support the process of digital migration and the subsequent release of the high frequency spectrum.
tgt: Kabinete e na le tshepo ya ho re ho phethelwa ha motjha ona ho tla tshehetsa motjha wa ho fallela kgasong ya dijithale le ho ntshwa ha ‘high frequency spectrum.’4.

src: Fighting crime and corruption Cabinet congratulated the country’s new National Commissioner of Police, General Sehlahle Fannie Masemola, following his recent appointment by President Ramaphosa.
tgt: Twantsho ya bosenyi le bobodu Kabinete e thoholeditse Khomeshenara e ntjha ya Mapolesa ya Naha, Mokgenerale Sehlahle Fannie Masemola, kamora hore a kgethwe ke Presidente Ramaphosa.

src: General Masemola has an outstanding record of achievements in policing across South Africa.
tgt: Mokgenerale Masemola o ipabotse mosebetsing wa hae sepoleseng Afrika Borwa ka bophara.

src: Cabinet welcomed the preservation orders granted to the Asset Forfeiture Unit of the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) by the Gauteng High Court against those involved in ‘financing’ the purchase of Optimum Coal Mine for R.1-billion in 2016 by the Gupta-owned Tegeta Exploration and Resources company.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ditaelo tsa paballo tse nehilweng Yuniti e Hapang Thepa ya Bolaodi ba naha ba Botjhutjhisi (NPA) tse ntshitsweng ke Lekgotla le Phahameng la Dinyewe kgahlano le ba bileng le seabo ho thuseng ka ditjhelete thekong ya Morafo wa Mashala wa Optimum ka dibiliyone tse R.1 ka 2016 ke khampani ya ba ha Gupta ya Tegeta Exploration and Resources.

src: The rulings, which demonstrate the effective coordinated approach of the NPA and the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation of the South African Police Service, send a strong message about the growing capacity of government to deal with State Capture and ensure accountability for those involved – and to seize, recover and return stolen money.
tgt: Diqeto tsena tse bontshang tshebetso e hlophisehileng ka bokgabane ya NPA le Bolaodi ba Diphuputso tsa Bosenyi bo ka Sehloohong ba Tshebeletso ya Mapolesa ya Afrika Borwa di romela molaetsa o matla ka bokgoni bo matlafalang ba mmuso ba ho sebetsana le ho Hatjwa ha Mmuso le ho netefatsa ho nka boikarabelo ha ba amehang – le ho hapa, ho fumana le ho kgutlisa ditjhelete tse utswitsweng.

src: In holding those involved in corruption accountable, Cabinet also welcomed the judgement by the Palm Ridge Specialised Commercial Crimes Court in Gauteng against a former Eskom financial controller for defrauding the power utility of R35 million by loading fake invoices for coal transport and the initiatives to recover the stolen monies.
tgt: Maitekong a ho jarisa ba molato boikarabelo, Kabinete e boetse ya ananela kahlolo ya Lekgotla la Dinyewe tse Ikgethang tsa Bobodu ba Ditjhelete la Palm Ridge Gauteng kgahlano le molaodi wa Ditjhelete, Eskom diketsong tsa manyofonyofo a dimiliyone tse R35 ha a ne a kenya ditlankana tseo eseng tsa nnete tsa ditshebeletso tsa ho tsamaiswa ha mashala le maiteko a ho kgutlisa ditjhelete tseo.

src: As an important milestone in our nation’s fight against corruption, Cabinet welcomed the handover of the fourth part of the Judicial Commission of Inquiry into State Capture Report.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho ntshuwa ha karolo ya bone ya Tlaleho ya ho Hatjwa ha Mmuso ya Khomeshene ya Boahlodi ya Dipatlisiso, e le ketsahalo ya bohlokwa haholo ntweng kgahlano le bobodu.

src: President Ramaphosa will present to Parliament interventions to implement the commission’s recommendations when he submits the full report by 30 June 2022.
tgt: Presidente Ramaphosa o tla tekela palamente ditsela tsa ho kenya tshebetsong dikgothaletso tsa khomeshene ha a nehelana ka tlaleho e felletseng pele ho feta la la 30 Phupjane Seboka sa Mokgatlo wa Boraro se Ikgethang sa Mokgatlo o Borwa ba Afrika wa Ntshetsopele (SADC).

src: Southern African Development Community (SADC) Extraordinary Organ Troika Summit.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse diphetho tsa Seboka sa Boraro se Ikgethang sa SADC se neng se tshwerwe Pretoria ka Mantaha wa la 4 le Labobedi la la 5 Mmesa 2022.

src: Cabinet welcomed the outcomes of SADC Extraordinary Organ Troika Summit held in Pretoria on Monday, 4 and Tuesday, 5 April 2022.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e ne e tshwere seboka jwalokaha e le Modulasetulo wa Mokgatlo wa SADC wa Tshebedisano Dipolotiking, Tshireletsong le Tshireletsehong.

src: The country’s tenure runs from August 2021 to August 2022.
tgt: Naha ena e tshwere marapo ho tloha ka Phato 2021 ho ya ho Phato 2022.

src: The summit received, among others, the SADC Mission in Mozambique (SAMIM) progress report.
tgt: Hara tse ding seboka se ananetse tlaleho ya kgatelopele ya lebotho la SADC la ho tliswa ha kgotso Mozambique (SAMIM).

src: The SAMIM was deployed to support Mozambique to combat terrorism and acts of violent extremism.
tgt: SAMIM e rometswe ho ya tshehetsa naha ya Mozambique ho lwantsha boferekanyi le diketso tsa dikgoka tsa bongangele.

src: Economy Cabinet welcomed credit rating agency Moody’s upgrade of its outlook on South Africa to stable from negative and the decision to affirm South Africa’s long-term foreign and local currency debt ratings at ‘Ba2’.
tgt: Moruo Kabinete e ananetse ho ntlafatswa ha maemo a Afrika Borwa ke mokgatlo o lekolang bokgoni ba dinaha ba ho lefa melato ya tsona e leng Moody’s, ho ya maemong a tsitsitseng ho tloha ho a mabe, mmoho le qeto ya ho netefatsa hore Afrika Borwa e tla kgona ho lefa melato e leshwang ka ditjhelete tsa dinaha tse ding le tjhelete ya naha ena ka nako eo ho dumellanweng ka yona, mme sena sa beha Afrika Borwa boemong ba ‘Ba.’ Ntlafatso e tiisa mosebetsi wa mmuso wa ho tsoseletsa botsitso ditjheleteng tsa naha tsa setjhaba, e leng botsitso bo tshehetswang ke pokello ya lekgetho e hodimo ho feta kamoo ho lebelletsweng.

src: The upgrade affirms the work of government to restore sustainability to the country’s public finances, which is supported by better-than-expected revenue collection.
tgt: Diphetho tsa kuno tsa ho tloha ka Mmesa 2021 ho ya ho Tlhakubele 2022, di bontshitse Tshebeletso ya Pokello ya Lekgetho Afrika Borwa e bokelletse ditriliyone tse fetang Ena ke keketseho ya dipersente tse 25 ha ho bapiswa le ngwahola le ya dipersente tse 15 ha ho bapiswa le ngwahola pele ho sewa sa COVID-19.

src: Government is using the additional revenue to accelerate debt stabilisation and address urgent social needs, promote job creation through the Presidential Youth Employment Initiative, and support the public health sector.
tgt: Mmuso o sebedisa kuno ena ya tlatsetso ho potlakisa ho leshwa ha melato ya naha le mererong ya thekolohelo, ho kgothaletsa ho thehwa ha mesebetsi ka Maiteko a Khiro ya Batjha a boemo ba ofisi ya Presidente, le ho tshehetsa lekala la bophelo bo botle la setjhaba.

src: Freedom Month.
tgt: Kgwedi ya Tokoloho.

src: South Africa this year celebrates Freedom Month in April with renewed hope for a better tomorrow, having endured two sombre years under the global COVID-19 pandemic.
tgt: Selemong sena Afrika Borwa e keteka Kgwedi ya Tokoloho ka Mmesa ka tjheseho tshepong ya bokamoso bo betere, kamora ho mamella dilemo tse pedi tsa masisapelo tsa sewa sa COVID-19.

src: The annual Freedom Day will be commemorated on Wednesday, 27 April 2022.
tgt: Letsatsi la Tokoloho la selemo le selemo le tla ketekwa ka Laboraro la la 27 Mmesa 2022.

src: Freedom Month commemorates and salutes all those whose sacrifices made it possible for us to enjoy the human rights and freedoms contained in our world-acclaimed Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996.
tgt: Ka Kgwedi ya Tokoloho ho hopolwa le ho hlompha ba ileng ba intsha sehlabelo mme ka hona ra kgona ho ba le ditokelo tsa botho le ditokoloho tse Molaong wa rona wa Motheo wa Rephaboliki ya Afrika Borwa wa 1996 o hlontjhwang haholo lefatsheng.

src: Cabinet called on all South Africans to work together as we continue our struggle to overcome the impact of COVID-19.
tgt: Kabinete e ipileditse ho Maafrika Borwa ohle ho sebetsa mmoho ntweng kgahlano le sewa sa COVID-19.

src: We all need to do our part to restore our economy, through the Economic Reconstruction and Recovery Plan, and grow more businesses to be able to create more jobs.
tgt: Bohle re lokela ho kenya letsoho tsoseletsong ya moruo wa rona, ka Moralo wa Kahobotjha le Tsoseletso ya Moruo, re thehe dikgwebo tse ding hotle re kgone ho theha mesebetsi e meng.

src: Holy Month of Ramadan Cabinet wished South Africa’s Muslim community a blessed Holy Month of Ramadan.
tgt: Kgwedi e Halalelang ya Ramadan Kabinete e lakaleditse setjhaba sa Mamoseleme Afrika Borwa mahlohonolo Kgweding ya bona e Halalelang ya Ramadan.

src: Ramadan is annually marked around the world with prayer, fasting and acts of charity.
tgt: Ramadan e ketekwa selemo le selemo lefatsheng ka bophara ka ho rapela, ho ila dijo le ho phallela ba hlokang.

src: The Muslim community is an integral part of our national diversity and of our national character.
tgt: Setjhaba sa Mamoseleme ke karolo ya bohlokwa ya naha ya rona.

src: Cabinet decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Kabinete.

src: Draft National Integrated Small Enterprise Development (NISED) Masterplan.
tgt: Moralo wa Leano le Leholo la Naha le Momahaneng la Ntshetsopele ya Dikgwebo tse Nyenyane (NISED) Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana phatlalatso ya Leano le leholo la NISED hotle setjhaba se ntshe maikutlo ka lona.

src: Cabinet approved the publication of the draft NISED Masterplan for public comment.
tgt: Leano la Sethathong le Momahaneng la Bohwebi le Dikgwebo tse Nyenyane le ile la tjhaelwa monwana ka 2005.

src: The initial Integrated Strategy for Entrepreneurship and Small Enterprises was adopted in 2005.
tgt: Leano lena la NISED ya morao di kenya tshebetsong Tokomane ya Tataiso ya 1995 ya Leano la Naha la Ntshetsopele le Phahamiso ya Dikgwebo tse Nyenyane Afrika Borwa.

src: The strategy and the subsequent NISED give effect to the 1995 White Paper on National Strategy for the Development and Promotion of Small Business in South Africa.
tgt: Ha e se e ananetswe, NISED e tla nka sebaka sa Leano la jwale le momahaneng la Bohwebi le Dikgwebo tse Nyenyane.

src: It will provide a coordination framework for all key ecosystem role players in small enterprise development.
tgt: E tla fana ka moralotshebetso bakeng sa bohle ba amehang marangranng a ntshetsopele ya dikgwebo tse nyenyane.

src: It guides the coordinating mechanism that will guide all programmes that support small enterprises.
tgt: E tataisa mokgwa wa bohokahanyi o tla tataisa mananeo ohle a tshehetsang dikgwebo tse nyenyane.

src: This strategy seeks to increase the participation of small enterprises in the formal economy, eliminate red tape and promote the ease of doing business, particularly for small entrepreneurs.
tgt: Sepheo sa leano lena ke ho eketsa seabo sa dikgwebo tse nyenyane lekaleng la moruo le molaong, ho tlosa melao e mengata e bakang tieho le ho phahamisa pebofatso ya ho hweba, haholoholo bakeng sa bahwebi ba banyenyane.

src: The NISED is the product of a wide consultation with the relevant departments in the national, provincial and local spheres of government, business, labour, academics and various relevant institutions.
tgt: NISED e hlahile kamora hore ho be le dipuisano tse matla le mafapha a amehang a mmuso boemong ba naha, provense le lehae, dikgwebo, basebetsi, dirutehi le ditheo tse fapaneng tse loketseng.

src: Incorporation of the Small Enterprise Finance Agency (SEFA) and Cooperative Banks Development Agency (CBDA) into the Small Enterprise Development Agency (SEDA).
tgt: Ho Kopanngwa ha Mokgatlo o Thusang Dikgwebo tse Nyenyane ka Ditjhelete (SEFA) le Mokgatlo wa Ntshetsopele ya Dibanka tsa Koporasi (CBDA) ho ba Mokgatlo wa Ntshetsopele ya Dikgwebo tse Nyenyane (SEDA).

src: Cabinet approved the 20 months extension period for the merging of the two entities, the SEFA and CBDA, into the SEDThe merger was initially set to be effective from 1 April 2022.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse keketso ya dikgwedi tse 20 bakeng sa ho kopanya ditheo tse pedi e leng SEFA le CBDA, hore e be SEDSethathong ho kopanngwa ha mekgatlo e ne e lokela ho kena tshebetsong ho tloha ho la 01 Mmesa 2022.

src: This was after Cabinet approved the mergers to ensure government provides a single entity that will support its work in supporting small to medium enterprises and cooperatives.
tgt: Sena se etsahetse kamora hore Kabinete e tjhaele monwana ho kopanngwa ha mekgatlo ho netefatsa hore mmuso o na le setheo se le seng se tla tshehetsa mosebetsi wa ona wa ho tshehetsa dikgwebo tse nyenyane le tse mahareng le dikoporasi.

src: The approved extension will enable the Department of Small Business Development to finalise the legislative review to provide a proper legislated and policy environment that allows the formation of the single entity – SEDA single and well-resourced entity will provide a more streamlined support to small to medium enterprises and cooperatives.
tgt: Katoloso ya nako e tjhaetsweng monwana e tla thusa Lefapha la Ntshetsopele ya Dikgwebo tse Nyenyane ho phethela tekolo ya molao molemong wa ho tlisa maemo a matle ka molao, a leano a dumellang ho thehwa ha setheo se le seng e leng SEDSetheo se le seng se ntlafetseng se tla fana ka tshehetso e tsitsitseng dikgwebong tse nyenyane le tse mahareng le dikoporasing.

src: Cabinet also approved the appointment of the interim Boards of Directors for the SEFA and SEDRegulations relating to the Protection, Promotion, Development and Management of Indigenous Knowledge (IK regulations) Cabinet approved the publication of IK regulations for public comment.
tgt: Kabinete e boetse e tjhaetse monwana ho kgethwa ha Diboto tsa nakwana tsa Balaodi tsa SEFA le SEDMelawana e Amanang le Tshireletso, Phahamiso, Ntshetsopele le Tsamaiso ya Tsebo ya Batala (IK) Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana phatlalatso ya melawana ya Tsebo ya Batala (IK) hore setjhaba se ntshe maikutlo ka yona.

src: The IK regulations will give effect to the implementation of the IK Act, 2019 (Act 6 of 2019).
tgt: Melawana ena e tla lebisa ho kenngweng tshebetsong ha Molao wa Tsebo ya Batala wa 2019 (Molao wa bo 6 wa 2019).

src: The Act provides for the protection, promotion, development and management of indigenous knowledge.
tgt: Molao ona o kgonahatsa tshireletso, phahamiso, ntshetsopele le tsamaiso ya tsebo ya ditsela tsa bophelo tsa boholoholo.

src: It provides for the establishment of national IK systems management of rights of IK of communities.
tgt: O kgonahatsa tshibollo ya mekgwatshebetso ya naha ya Tsebo ya Batala taolo ya ditokelo tsa ditjhabana tsa Tsebo ya Batala.

src: It also provides for the establishment of an advisory panel recognition of prior learnings facilitation and coordination of IThe proposed regulations deal with, amongst others, the setting up of the Advisory Panel accreditation processes registration of competencies of IK practitioners how to access or use IK and the safekeeping of registers of IThe regulations also provide for dispute-resolution mechanisms.
tgt: O boetse o kgonahatsa tshibollo ya moifo wa boeletsi hlompho ya thuto ya batala pebofatso le tsitsiso ya tsebo ya batala.

src: The regulations will be gazetted and can also be accessed through the Department of Science and Innovation website: WEBTOKEThey will also be available in all official languages.
tgt: Hara tse ding, melawana eo e sisintsweng e shebane le ho thehwa ha Moifo wa Boeletsi metjha ya kananelo ya semmuso ya boemo ba botsebi ngodiso ya bokgoni ba basebetsi ka Tsebo ya Ditsela tsa Bophelo tsa Batala kamoo ho ka fihlellwang kapa ho ka sebediswang Tsebo ya Batala mmoho le paballo ya direjistara tsa Tsebo ya Batala.

src: United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2020-2025 Cabinet approved South Africa’s UNSDCF 2020-2025 for implementation.
tgt: Moralo wa Tshebedisano wa Ntshetsopele ya Moshwelella wa Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UNSDCF) 2020-2025 Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana hore ho kenngwe tshebetsong UNSDCF 2020-2025 ya Afrika Borwa.

src: The framework provides an accountability partnership between government, the broader society and the UN’s country office in South Africa.
tgt: Moralotshebetso ona o etsa hore ho be le tshebedisano e nang le boikarabelo pakeng tsa mmuso, setjhaba ka kakaretso le ofisi ya Matjhaba a Kopaneng e Afrika Borwa.

src: The UNSDCF outlines four broad strategic priority pillars to cover (1) inclusive , justice and sustainable growth (2) human capital and social transformation (3) effective, efficient and transformative governance and (4) climate resilience and sustainably managed natural resources.
tgt: UNSDCF e na le ditshiya tse nne tse batsi le tsa bohlokwa tse shebaneng le (1) toka e kenyeletsang bohle le kgolo ya ho ya ho ile (2) bohlokwa ba motho mosebetsing le diphetoho setjhabeng (3) puso e atlehang, e sebetsang hantle le e tlisang diphetoho le (4) bokgoni ba ho emelana le mathata a tlelaemete le matlotlo a tlhaho a laolehang ho ya ho ile.

src: These strategic pillars are interlinked with the country’s National Development Plan: Vision 2030 and the Medium Term Strategic Framework, and also with the UN Sustainable Development Goals driven through the UN country’s office in South Africa.
tgt: Ditshiya tsena tsa bohlokwa di amane le Moralo wa Naha wa Ntshetsopele: Maikemisetso a 2030 le Moralotshebetso wa Bohlokwa wa Nako e Mahareng, mmoho le Dipheo tsa Matjhaba a Kopaneng tsa Ntshetsopele ya Moshwelella tse phethahatswang ka ofisi ya mokgatlo ona e Afrika Borwa.

src: The implementation will be done through a joint resource mobilisation strategy.
tgt: Ho kenngwa tshebetsong ha tsona ho tla phethahatswa ka leano la disebediswa tse kopanetsweng.

src: National intervention in the Mangaung Metropolitan and Enoch Mgijima Local municipalities.
tgt: Ho kenella ha Mmuso wa naha Masepaleng e Moholo wa Mangaung le Masepaleng wa Lehae wa Enoch Mgijima.

src: Cabinet approved the intervention in terms of Section 139(7) of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996, read together with Section 150 of the Municipal Finance Management Act, 2003 (Act 56 of 2003), in the Mangaung Metropolitan and Enoch Mgijima Local municipalities.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana ho kenella ha mmuso ho ya ka Karolo ya 139(7) ya Molao wa Motheo wa Rephaboliki ya Afrika Borwa wa 1996, o balwang mmoho le Karolo ya 150 ya Molao wa Tsamaiso ya Ditjhelete tsa Bomasepala wa 2003 (Molao 56 wa 2003), Masepaleng e Moholo wa Mangaung le wa Lehae wa Enoch Mgijima.

src: Both municipalities have been experiencing significant financial and service delivery failures for a prolonged period.
tgt: Bomasepala bana ka bobedi esale ba na le mathata a maholo a ditjhelete ba hloleha le ho fana ka ditshebeletso ka nako e telele.

src: The Free State Provincial Executive placed the Mangaung Metropolitan Municipality under a mandatory intervention in terms of Section 139(5)
tgt: Mmuso wa Provense ya Freistata o ile wa kenella ka molao Masepaleng e Moholo wa Mangaung ho ya ka Karolo ya 139(5)

src: and
tgt: le

src: of the Constitution in December 2019.
tgt: ya Molao wa Motheo ka Tshitwe 2019.

src: A mandatory financial recovery plan was subsequently imposed on the municipality in 2020.
tgt: Ho qetelletse ho kenngwa tshebetsong leano la ho kgutliswa ha ditjhelete le tlamang masepaleng ka 2020.

src: After failing for more than two years to implement the financial recovery plan during the provincial intervention, the Metro has now been placed under a national intervention in terms of Section 139(7) of the Constitution.
tgt: Kamora hore masepala e moholo o hlolehe ka dilemo tse fetang tse pedi ho Kenya leano lena tshebetsong ha mmuso wa provense o kenelletse, mmuso wa naha o qetelletse o kenella Masepaleng ho latela Karolo ya 139(7) ya Molao wa Motheo.

src: The Enoch Mgijima Local Municipality was also placed under mandatory intervention by the Eastern Cape Provincial Executive in terms of Section 139(5)
tgt: Masepala wa Lehae wa Enoch Mgijima le ona o ile wa thuswa ke Mmuso wa Provense wa Kapa Botjhabela ho ya ka Karolo ya 139(5)

src: of the Constitution in 2018.
tgt: ya Molao wa Motheo wa Afrika Borwa ka 2018.

src: However, after the municipality failed to make progress in improving its financial and service delivery performance, Cabinet decided to place it under a national intervention.
tgt: Leha ho le jwalo kamora hore masepala o hlolehe ho bontsha kgatelopele ntlafatsong ya ditjhelete tsa ona le phanong ya ditshebeletso, Kabinete e ile ya nka qeto ya ho o beha tlasa thuso ya mmuso wa naha.

src: The invocation of a national intervention in terms of Section 139(7) of the Constitution implies that in both municipalities, national government will now act in the stead of the Provincial Executive.
tgt: Boipiletso ba hore mmuso wa naha o kenelle ho latela Karolo ya 139(7) ya Molao wa Motheo bo bolela hore ho bomasepala ka bobedi mmuso wa naha o tla ba le boikarabelo bakeng sa mebuso ya Diprovense.

src: This type of intervention is mandatory and follows the same procedure as Section 139(5) of the Constitution, except that national government will now directly assume responsibility for these interventions.
tgt: Ho kenella hona ho a tlama ka molao mme ho latela motjha o tshwanang le wa Karolo ya 139(5) ya Molao wa Motheo, ntle feela le hore mmuso wa naha jwale o tla nka boikarabelo ka ho otloloha ha o thusa bomasepala.

src: To give effect to the assumption of responsibility, National Cabinet Representatives (NCR) will shortly be deployed to both municipalities.
tgt: Ha ho kenngwa tshebetsong ho nkuwa ha boikarabelo, ho tla romelwa Baemedi ba Kabinete ba Naha (NCR) ho bomasepala ka bobedi.

src: The Minister of Finance will delegate powers to the NCR and will also be supported by a multidisciplinary team of experts.
tgt: Letona la Ditjhelete le tla neha baemedi ba NCR matla mme ba tla boela ba tshehetswe ke sehlopha sa ditsebi tse fapaneng.

src: No decision has yet been taken to dissolve the municipal council in terms of Section 139(5) of the Constitution.
tgt: Ha ho eso nkwe qeto ya ho qhala makgotla a bomasepala ho latela Karolo ya 139(5) ya Molao wa Motheo.

src: The national intervention will take effect upon formal gazetting in the Government Gazette, however, the current Section 139(5) intervention will remain in effect until this date.
tgt: Ho kenella ha mmuso wa naha ho tla kena tshebetsong ha ho se ho phatlaladitswe Koranteng ya Mmuso, leha ho le jwalo ho kenella tlasa Karolo ya 139(5) ho tla nne ho sebetse ho fihlela tsatsi leo.

src: The Section 139(1) intervention into the Enoch Mgijima Local Municipality will also be replaced by a Section 139 (5)
tgt: Karolo ya 139(1) ya ho kenella Masepaleng wa Lehae wa Enoch Mgijima e tla nkelwa sebaka ke Karolo ya 139 (5)

src: intervention, which will also cover the failure of the municipality to fulfil its executive obligations.
tgt: le , eo tlasa yona ho tla rarollwa ho hloleha ha masepala ho phetha mesebetsi ya ona.

src: The Minister in The Presidency, Mr Mondli Gungubele will – together with the Minister of Finance, Mr Enoch Godongwana and the Minister of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs, Dr Nkosazana Dlamini Zuma – hold a media briefieng next week to outline the national intervention.
tgt: Letona Ofising ya Presidente, Monghadi Mondli Gungubele mmoho le Letona la Ditjhelete, Monghadi Enoch Godongwana le Letona la Puso ya Kopanelo le Ditaba tsa Setso, Ngaka Nkosazana Dlamini Zuma, ba tla ba le seboka le boraditaba bekeng e tlang molemong wa ho hlakisa leano la ho kenella ha mmuso wa naha ho bomasepala.

src: Upcoming event.
tgt: Ketsahalo e Latelang.

src: District Development Model (DDM) Presidential Imbizo.
tgt: Imbizo ya Presidente ya Mokgwa wa Ntshetsopele wa Ditereke (DDM).

src: President Ramaphosa will hold a DDM Presidential Imbizo at the Petrus Molemela Sports Complex in Mangaung, Free State on Friday, 8 and Saturday, 9 April 2022.
tgt: Presidente Ramaphosa o tla epa Imbizo ya DDM Lebaleng la Dipapadi la Petrus Molemela, Mangaung, Freistata ka Labohlano la la 08 le ka Moqebelo wa la 09 Mmesa 2022.

src: The Imbizo, convened under the theme: “Leave no one behind”, will assess the level of service delivery in the province, track progress on the DDM, and oversee key interventions and plans.
tgt: Imbizo ena e hlophisitsweng tlasa mookotaba: “Ha ho ya siuwang morao”, e tla lekola boemo ba phano ya ditshebeletso provenseng, e lekole kgatelopele ya DDM, e boele e laole mekgwa ya ho thusa le merero e ka sehloohong.

src: The DDM Presidential Imbizo is an important public participation platform as its gives citizens a voice and the President the opportunity to listen to the people and respond to their concerns.
tgt: Imbizo ya Presidente ya DDM ke mokgwa wa bohlokwa o dumellang setjhaba ho ba le seabo le o nehang baahi monyetla wa ho ntsha maikutlo a sona, o boele o nehe Presidente monyetla wa ho mamela batho le ho arabela dillo tsa bona.

src: South Africans can follow and participate in discussions on social media under the hashtag #PresidentialImbizo.
tgt: Maafrika Borwa a ka latela le ho ba le seabo dipuisanong tsena diwebsaeteng tsa ho etsa setswalle tlasa lepetjo la #PresidentialImbizo.

src: CongradulationsCabinet extended its congratulations and well-wishes to: Mr Nkosinathi Maphumulo, better known as DJ Black Coffee, who recently won his first Grammy in the category of “Best Dance/Electronic Album” for his album Subconsciously, at the 64th Grammy Awards ceremony held in Las Vegas, United States.
tgt: MahlohonoloKabinete e lebohisitse le ho lebisa ditakalletso tse ntle ho: Monghadi Nkosinathi Maphumulo, ya tsejwang ka la DJ Black Coffee, ya sa tswa hapa kgau ya hae ya pele ya Grammy mokgahlelong wa “Best Dance/Electronic Album” bakeng sa albamo ya hae e bitswang Subconsciously, moketeng wa bo- 64 wa Dikgau tsa di-Grammy o neng o tshwaretswe Las Vegas naheng ya Amerika.

src: Appointment All appointments are subject to the verification of qualifications and the relevant WEBTOKEN Mpumelelo Tyikwe as Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director of the South African Special Risk Insurance Association.
tgt: Khiro Ho tlameha hore ho netefatswe mangolo a thuteho a ba hirwang mme ho netefatswe hore ha ba eso ka ba tlola molao.

src: Cabinet expressed condolences to all people who have lost their loved ones in the recent devastating floods that hit several parts of our country, particularly KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Taolo ya Dikoduwa Kamora Dikgohola Kabinete e lebisitse matshediso bathong bohle ba lahlehetsweng ke beng ka bona dikgoholeng tsa morao tse mpe tse ileng tsa hlasela dibaka tse ngata tsa naha ya rona, haholoholo KwaZulu-Natal.

src: The declaration of a National State of Disaster and socio-economic relief interventions recently announced by President Cyril Ramaphosa, sought to ensure an effective and coordinated response across all spheres of government, through the National Disaster Management Centre.
tgt: Sepheo ka tsebahatso ya Maemo a Dikoduwa a Naha le dithuso tsa boiphediso tse sa tswa tsebahatswa ke Presidente Cyril Ramaphosa e ne e le ho netefatsa karabelo e atlehileng le e hlophisehileng makaleng ohle a mmuso, ka Setsi sa Taolo ya Naha ya Dikoduwa.

src: The R1 billion made available by the government is being used to support relief and recovery efforts, restore basic services and provide humanitarian assistance in the form of food, water, shelter, sanitation and clothing.
tgt: Biliyone ya diranta eo mmuso o e ntshitseng e sebedisetswa ho tshehetsa maiteko a dithuso le ho iphumana, ho kgutlisa ditshebeletso tsa motheo le ho phallela ba hlokang ka ho ba thusa ka dijo, metsi, botshabelo, tsa bohlweki le diaparo.

src: The process to rebuild affected areas has already started as the people of our country unite in their determination to assist those who have lost their homes and possessions.
tgt: Motjha wa ho aha botjha dibaka tse amehileng o se o qadile mme le batho ba naha ya rona ba kopane ka maikemisetso a ho thusa ba lahlehetsweng ke bodulo le thepa ya bona.

src: Update on the Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) Cabinet noted with concern the recent spike in COVID-19 infections in some parts of the country and urged all people to take precautionary measures to protect themselves against the deadly virus, especially during winter.
tgt: Tlhahisoleseding ka Lefu laCoronavirus (COVID-19) Kabinete e kgathatsehile ka ho eketseha ha morao tjena ha ditshwaetso tsa COVID-19 dikarolong tse ding tsa naha mme e ipileditse ho bohle ho nka mehato ya ho itshireletsa kgahlano le vaerase ena e kotsi, haholoholo mariha tjena.

src: The virus is still a constant threat and vaccination remains the most effective weapon to protect ourselves.
tgt: Vaerase ena e ntse e le kotsi mme ho enta e ntse e le sebetsa se bohlokwa haholo seo re ka itshireletsang ka sona.

src: The cabinet is pleased that more people continue to choose vaccination as their first line of defence against COVID-19 after recent statistics showed that we have reached the milestone of over 50 per cent of adult vaccinations in five provinces.
tgt: Kabinete e thabiswa ke hore batho ba bangata ba ntse ba kgetha ho enta e le tshireletso ya bona ya pele kgahlano le COVID-19 kamora hore dipalopalo tsa morao di bontshe hore batho ba baholo ba fetang dipersente tse mashome a mahlano ba se ba entile diprovenseng tse hlano.

src: Cabinet calls on those who have not yet been vaccinated to do so to protect themselves and their loved ones.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho ba so ente ho enta molemong wa ho itshireletsa le beng ka bona.

src: We should also all continue to adhere to all COVID-19 prevention protocols, including the wearing of a mask that covers both the nose and mouth, washing hands with water and soap, or using a 70% alcohol-based hand sanitiser, and keeping a safe social distance of at least one metre.
tgt: Bohle re lokela ho tswela pele le ho ikamahanya le melao ya ho itshireletsa ho COVID-19, e kenyeletsang ho rwala semonkwana se kwahelang nko le molomo, ho hlapa matsoho ka metsi le sesepa, kapa ho sebedisa sehlwekisi se nang le alcohol e ballwang dipersenteng tse 70, le ho arohana le ba bang ka bonnyane mitara.

src: Social Relief of Distress (SRD) Grant Cabinet encouraged citizens receiving the R350 SRD Grant to reapply, following the introduction of new regulations governing applications and eligibility for the grant.
tgt: Thuso e Imollang Nakong ya Mathata (SRD) Kabinete e kgothaleditse baahi ba fumanang R350 ya SRDGrant ho etsa dikopo hape, kamora hore ho kenngwe tshebetsong melawana e metjha e laolang dikopo le ho lokela ha batho ho fumana dithuso.

src: Applications can be lodged on the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) website: WEBTOKEN The application system opened on 23 April 2022 and is a fully digital process to enable quick turnaround times.
tgt: Dikopo di ka etswa websaeteng ya Setheo sa Dithuso tsa Setjhaba sa Afrika Borwa (SASSA) e leng:WEBTOKEN wa dikopo o butswe ka la 23 Mmesa 2022 mme o etswa inthaneteng molemong wa ho potlakisa katleho ya ona.

src: The relief grant is an important safety net for needy families who would otherwise be devastated by the scourge of poverty and unemployment.
tgt: Thuso ena ya ho imolla e bohlokwa haholo malapeng a hlokang le a ka sulafallwang ke maphelo ka lebaka la bofuma le ho hloka mesebetsi.

src: Government is committed to providing social assistance to the most vulnerable so that they can meet their basic needs.
tgt: Mmuso o ikemiseditse ho fana ka dithuso tsa setjhaba hoba hlokang haholo ba kgone ho fumana tseo ba di hlokang tsa motheo.

src: Safety and security Cabinet continues to condemn the senseless killing of women and has welcomed the swift response by law-enforcement officers in arresting suspects in connection with the death of Ms Hillary Gardee (28), of Kamagugu in Mpumalanga.
tgt: Kabinete e tswella le ho nyatsa ho bolawa ka sehloho ha basadi mme e ananetse karabelo e potlakileng ya mapolesa ha a tshwara babelaellwa polaong ya Mofumahatsana Hillary Gardee (28), waKamaguguMpumalanga.

src: Cabinet further condemned the killing of six people in Khayelitsha, Cape Town.
tgt: Kabinete e boetse e nyatsitse ho bolawa ha batho ba tsheletseng Khayelitsha, Motsekapa.

src: These senseless murders are a reminder that we must do more as a society to end violence and gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF).
tgt: Dipolao tsena tse sehloho di re hopotsa hore re lokela ho sebetsa ka matla re le setjhaba ho fedisa dikgoka le dikgoka tsa bong le polao ya basadi (GBVF).

src: Cabinet urged all people in the country to work with the government in the fight against crime and GBVTogether we can ensure that our communities and streets are safer for all people, including the elderly, women and children.
tgt: Kabinete e ipileditse ho bohle naheng ena ho sebetsa mmoho le mmuso ntweng kgahlano le bosenyi le GBVMmoho re ka netefatsa hore metse le diterata tsa rona di bolokehile bakeng sa batho bohle, ho kenyeletsa maqheku, basadi le bana.

src: Economy.
tgt: Moruo.

src: Cabinet welcomed the official opening of Corobrik’s Kwastina brick manufacturing factory at Driefontein in Gauteng by President Ramaphosa on Wednesday, 4 May 2022.
tgt: Kabinete e ananetse ho bulwa semmuso ha feme ya ho etsa ditene ya Kwastina ya Corobrik, Driefontein,Gauteng ke Presidente Ramaphosa ka Laboraro la la 4 Motsheanong 2022.

src: The state-of-the-art factory forms part of an R800 million investment, which goes hand in hand with a further R200 million earmarked to expand Corobrik’s concrete operations in KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Feme ena ya maemo a phahameng haholo ke karolo ya matsete a diranta tse dimiliyone tse 800, a tsamayang mmoho le diranta tse ding tse dimiliyone tse 200 tse behetsweng ho atolosa feme ya Corobrik ya konkreiti KwaZulu-Natal.

src: Corobrik is one of several local businesses that have responded to President Ramaphosa’s call on South African and international enterprises to invest in this economy.
tgt: Corobrik ke e nngwe ya dikgwebo tsa mona tse ileng tsa utlwa boipiletso ba Presidente Ramaphosa ba hore dikgwebo tsa Afrika Borwa le tsa matjhaba di tsetele moruong wa naha ena.

src: Cabinet noted that the fledgling hydrogen economy has been given a boost with the launch of a hydrogen-powered truck by Anglo American.
tgt: Kabinete e elelletswe hore moruo o fokolang wahydrogen o matlafaditswe kamora ho thakgolwa ha lori e sebedisang hydrogen ke Anglo American.

src: The truck – which was converted from diesel to hydrogen, and is powered in part by lithium-ion batteries – is a world first.
tgt: Lori ena e neng e sebedisa diesel mme ya fetolelwa tshebedisong ya hydrogen le e sebedisang le dibetri tsa lithium-ion keya pele lefatsheng.

src: The hydrogen economy has been identified as a strategic priority for our country’s green economy, and to drive economic growth and employment.
tgt: Moruo wahydrogen o hlwauwe e le lewa le pele moruong wa naha ya rona o lwantshang tshenyo ya tikoloho, mme moruo ona o tla ntshetsa pele kgolo moruong o thuse le ho thehweng ha mesebetsi.

src: Cabinet also welcomed a further investment into our economy by an Irish food company, The Kerry Group, which has opened a new R650-million plant in Hammarsdale, KwaZulu-Natal aimed at producing sustainable food for the continent.
tgt: Kabinetee boetse e ananetse matsete a mang moruong wa rona ka khampani ya dijo ya Ireland, The Kerry Group, e butseng feme ya diranta tse dimiliyone tse 650, Hammarsdale,KwaZulu-Natal, eo sepheo ka yona e leng ho hlahisa dijo ho ya ho ile kontinenteng.

src: The plant is unique as it boasts numerous sustainability features including low energy usage equipment, solar power generation to reduce consumption from the local grid, waste heat capture, and efficient water capture, reuse and reduction.
tgt: Feme ena ke e ikgethang hobane e na le dikarolo tsa moshwelella tse kenyeletsang disebediswa tsa eneji e nyenyane, tlhahiso ya matla a letsatsi ho fokotsa tshebediso ya motlakase wa keriti ya naha ena, mokgwa wa paballo ya eneji, le wa paballo ya metsi, tshebediso ya ona hape le mokgwa wa ho fokotsa tshebediso ya ona.

src: The Kerry Group has had a presence in South Africa since 2011, and their further investment is a sign that South Africa remains an investment destination of choice.
tgt: The Kerry Group e fihlile Afrika Borwa ka 2011, mme matsete a yona amang ke letshwao la hore Afrika Borwa e ntse e ratelwa matsete.

src: These investments follow in the footsteps of the launch of the locally manufactured Isuzu D-Max bakkie in Gqeberha in the Eastern Cape last month.
tgt: Matsete ana a tla kamora ho thakgolwa ha vene ena ya Isuzu D-Max e hlahisitsweng naheng, Gqeberha, Kapa Botjhabela kgweding e fetileng.

src: The new generation D-MAX crowns Isuzu’s commitment to South Africa and is one of the successes achieved under the Automotive Production Development Programme (APDP).
tgt: Koloi ena ya D-MAX ya mehleng ena e bontsha boinehelo ba Isuzu naheng ena mmeke e nngwe ya dikatleho tse fihletsweng tlasa Lenaneo la Ntshetsopele ya Tlhahiso ya Makoloi (APDP).

src: The APDP is a production incentive scheme for the motor industry aimed at promoting production volumes in the specified motor vehicle industry, promoting added value in the automotive component industry thus creating employment across the automotive value chain.
tgt: APDP ke mokgwatshebetso wa kgothatso wa tlhahiso bakeng sa indasteri ya makoloi oo sepheo ka ona e leng ho phahamisa tlhahiso indastering e boletsweng ya makoloi, ho phahamisa bolengindastering mme ka tsela ena ho thehwe mesebetsi makaleng ohle a amanang le tlhahiso ya makoloi.

src: Approximately R2,8 billion will be generated in local content production value through the lifecycle of the APDThe investment will secure more than 1 000 direct jobs at the plant and indirectly employ 24 000 people, contributing significantly to community upliftment in the region.
tgt: Kediranta tse dibiliyone tse batlang di eba 2,8 tse tla etswa ka tlhahiso ya mona nakong ya tshebetso ya APDMatsete a tla thusa ho theha mesebetsi e fetang 1000 ka palo ka kotloloho femeng, le e meng ya tlatsetso e hirang batho ba 24 000, mme sena se tla kenya letsoho matlafatsong ya baahi lebatoweng.

src: The Investing in African Mining Indaba 2022 held at the Cape Town International Convention Centre from 9 to 12 May 2022, is one of the biggest platforms for engagement and collaboration between all stakeholders in the mining industry.
tgt: Investing in African Mining Indaba 2022 e neng e tshwaretswe Cape Town International Convention Centreho tloha ka la 9 ho ya ho la 12 Motsheanong 2022, ke le leng la mapatlelo a maholo a ho bontshana le tshebedisano pakeng tsa ba amehang indastering ya merafo.

src: The theme of the event was: “Evolution of African Mining: Investing in the Energy Transition, ESG, and the Economies”.
tgt: Mookotaba wa ketsahalo ena e ne e le: “Ntshetsopele ho tsa Merafo Afrika: Matsete Diphetohong ho tsa Eneji, ESG, leMeruo”.

src: Cabinet is confident that the Mining Indaba will assist in showcasing and promoting South Africa as an investment destination of choice.
tgt: Kabinete e na le tshepo ya hore Seboka sa tsa Merafo se tla thusa ho pepesa le ho phahamisa Afrika Borwa jwaloka naha e ka kgahlang batsetedi.

src: South Africa welcomes investments into our country and is committed to creating favourable conditions for inclusive growth and transformation of the economy.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e amohela matsete naheng ya rona mme e inehetse ho theheng maemo a loketseng kgolo e kenyeletsang bohle le diphetoho moruong.

src: Cabinet also welcomed President Ramaphosa’s recent interactions with President Joe Biden of the United States, President Emmanuel Macron of France and President Hakainde Hichilema of Zambia on different platforms.
tgt: Dikamano le Dinaha tsa Matjhaba le tsa Mabatowa Kabinete e boetse e ananetse ditherisano tsa morao tjena tsa Presidente Ramaphosa le Presidente Joe Biden wa Amerika, Presidente Emmanuel Macron wa France le Presidente Hakainde Hichilema wa Zambia mapatlelong a fapaneng.

src: These engagements allowed the President to strengthen bilateral relations and cooperation between South Africa and partner states on key regional and international issues, including finding a peaceful solution to the conflict in Ukraine.
tgt: Dipuisano tsena di nehile Presidente monyetla wa ho tiisa maqhama le tshebedisano pakeng tsa Afrika Borwa le dinaha tse ding ditabeng tsa bohlokwa boemong ba mabatowa le matjhaba, ho kenyeletsa ho fumana tharollo ya kgotso ntweng ya Ukraine.

src: Cabinet Decisions.
tgt: Diqeto tsa Kabinete.

src: Budget Votes.
tgt: Dipuo tsa Ditekanyetso tsa Ditjhelete.

src: Cabinet calls on all citizens to follow the various Budget Votes by national government departments and The Presidency so that they can hold the government to account.
tgt: Kabinete e ipiletsa ho baahi bohle ho mamela Dipuo tsa Ditekanyetso tsa Ditjhelete tsa mafapha a naha a mmuso le puo ya lefapha la Bopresidente molemong wa hore ba behe mmuso leihlo.

src: During Budget Votes, all departments give a detailed account of their plans and priorities for the year.
tgt: Ha ho tekwa Dipuo tsa Ditekanyetso, mafapha ohle a fana ka dintlha tse felletseng tsa merero le tsa bohlokwa tseo a ikemiseditseng ho di phetha selemong.

src: Budget Votes seek to ensure that public funds are spent efficiently in meeting the needs of the public.
tgt: Sepheo ka Dipuo tsa Ditekanyetso ke ho netefatsa hore ditjhelete tsa setjhaba di sebediswa hantle ho thusa setjhaba ka tseo di se hlokang.

src: They also provide the ideal platform for Ministers to further unpack the work of government, including successes and challenges.
tgt: Dipuo tsa ditekanyetso di boetse ke monyetla wa hore Matona a hlalose haholwanyane ka mosebetsi wa mmuso, ho kenyeletsa dikatleho le diphephetso tseo o tobanang le tsona.

src: Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Rollout Strategy Cabinet approved the LPG Rollout Strategy for implementation, which was published for public consultation in March 2022.
tgt: Lewa la Qalo ya Tshebediso ya Kgase ya Mafura (LPG) Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana Lewa la Qalo ya Tshebediso ya LPG, le phatlaladitsweng hore setjhaba se ntshe maikutlo ka lona ka Tlhakubele 2022.

src: The strategy seeks to expand the LPG industry in the country.
tgt: Sepheo ka lewa ke ho atolosa indasteri ya kgase ya mafura naheng.

src: LPG will contribute meaningfully to the diversification of sources of energy.
tgt: LPG e tla ba le seabo se molemo phapanong ya mehlodi ya eneji.

src: The strategy will amongst other interventions, regulate the pricing in the value chain and support the manufacturing of LPG cylinders in the country.
tgt: Hara tse ding lewa le tla laola theko makaleng a fapaneng a tlhahiso le ho tshehetsa tlhahiso ya meqomo ya LPG naheng ena.

src: It will also educate the public about the benefits of using LPG as an alternative form of energy.
tgt: Le tla boela le rute setjhaba ka melemo ya ho sebedisa LPG jwaloka mofuta o mong wa eneji.

src: It will be accessible after it has been published by the Department of Mineral Resources and Energy on WEBTOKENational Strategic Framework on Disability Rights Awareness-Raising Campaigns for Persons with Disabilities Cabinet approved the National Strategic Framework on Disability Rights Awareness-Raising Campaigns for Persons with Disabilities.
tgt: Le tla fumaneha kamora hore le phatlalatswe ke Lefapha la Diminerale le Eneji WEBTOKEMoralotshebetso wa Batho ba sa Itekanelang wa Lewa wa Naha o Mabapi le Matsholo a ho Hlokomedisa ka Ditokelo tsa ba sa Itekanelang.

src: The framework seeks to guide both private and public sectors in ensuring the rights of persons with disabilities are protected, as enshrined in the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa of 1996.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana Moralotshebetso wa Batho ba sa Itekanelang wa Lewa wa Naha o mabapi le Matsholo a ho Hlokomedisa ka Ditokelo tsa ba sa Itekanelang.

src: The framework provides a toolkit that will assist in the removal of discriminatory barriers in decision-making, especially those related to persons with disabilities.
tgt: Moralotshebetso o nehelana kadisebediswa tse tla thusa ho tlosa kgethollo e thibelang ho nkuwa ha diqeto, haholoholo tse amanang le batho basa itekanelang.

src: It also conscientise persons with disabilities to know their rights as protected by the Constitution.
tgt: O boetse o lemosa batho ba sa itekanelang hore ba tsebe ditokelo tsa bona jwalokaha di sireleditswe ke Molao wa Motheo.

src: The framework also provides training, media reporting and awareness-raising within society on the rights of persons with disabilities.
tgt: Moralotshebetso o boetse o fana ka thupelo, o hlokomedise mehloding ya ditaba le setjhabeng ka ditokelo tsa batho basa itekanelang.

src: It gives effect to the White Paper on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.
tgt: O thusa ho kenngweng tshebetsong ha Tokomane ya Tataiso ya Ditokelo tsa Batho ba sa Itekanelang.

src: South Africa is a signatory to the United Nations (UN) Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities and the UN Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (African Disability Rights Protocol).
tgt: Afrika Borwa e saenne Tumellano ya Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) ya Ditokelo tsa Batho basa Itekanelang mmoho le Tokomaneya Matjhaba a Kopaneng (UN) yaLekgotla la Tumellano la Ditokelo tsa Botho le Batho Afrika e mabapi le Ditokelo tsa Batho ba sa Itekanelang (e leng Tokomane ya Tumellano ya Ditokelo tsa basa Itekanelang Afrika).

src: The framework was consulted with all relevant stakeholders, including the National Economic Development and Labour Council.
tgt: Ho bontshanwe le bohle ba amehang, ho kenyeletsa Ntshetsopele ya Moruo ya Naha le Lekgotlala Basebetsi.

src: Land Administration and Land Tenure in Communal Areas Summit.
tgt: Seboka sa Lefatshe Metseng ya Mahae sa Tsamaiso ya Lefatshe le Tokelo ya Lefatshe.

src: Cabinet approved the hosting of the Land Administration and Land Tenure in Communal Areas Summit on Friday, 27 and Saturday, 28 May 2022 in Gauteng.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana ho tshwarwa ha Seboka saMetse ya Mahae sa Tsamaiso ya Lefatshe le Tokelo ya Lefatshe ka Labohlano la la 27 le ka Moqebelo wa la 28 Motsheanong 2022, Gauteng.

src: Cabinet adopted the Position Paper on Land Administration and Land Tenure in Communal Land Areas in March 2021.
tgt: Kabinete e tjhaetse monwana Tlaleho ya Maikutlo ka Seboka saMetseng ya Mahae sa Tsamaiso ya Lefatshe le Tokelo ya Lefatshe ka Tlhakubele 2021.

src: It directed that further consultation be undertaken will all relevant stakeholders.
tgt: Kabinete e laetse hore ho be le dipontshano tse ding lebohle ba amehang.

src: The summit will be the culmination of the work that was done in the past year, which solicited inputs from various stakeholders.
tgt: Seboka ke sehlohlolo sa mosebetsi o entsweng ngwahola, o ileng wa nonya maikutlo a ba fapaneng ba amehang.

src: Upcoming Events.
tgt: Diketsahalo tse Tlang.

src: Fifth Global Conference on the Eradication of Child Labour South Africa will host the Fifth Global Conference on the Eradication of Child Labour at the Durban International Convention Centre in KwaZulu-Natal from Sunday, 15 to Friday, 20 May 2022.
tgt: Afrika Borwa e tla tshwara Seboka sa Bohlano sa Lefatshe sa Phediso ya Mosebetsi wa Bana, Durban International Convention Centre, KwaZulu-Natal ho tloha ka Sontaha sa la 15 ho ya ho Labohlano la la 20 Motsheanong 2022.

src: It is the first time the International Labour Organisation (ILO) hosts this conference in Africa.
tgt: Ke lekgetlo la pele Mokgatlo wa Lefatshe wa Basebetsi (ILO) o tshwarela seboka sena Afrika.

src: Heads of state, 120 ministers, tripartite constituents of 187 member countries of the ILO, UN agencies, academic institutions, civil society organisations, non-governmental organisations, media and civil society are expected to attend the conference.
tgt: Baetapele ba Dinaha, matona a 120, baemedi ba dikarolo tse tharo tsa dinaha tse 187 tseo e leng ditho tsa ILO, makgotla a Mokgatlo wa Matjhaba, ditheo tsa thuto e phahameng, mekgatlo ya baahi, mekgatlo eo eseng ya mmuso le mehlodi ya ditaba ba lebelletswe ho ba sebokeng sena.

src: The event will also allow South Africa to bring to the fore the country’s Constitution as it protects the rights of children.
tgt: Seboka se tla boela se nehe Afrika Borwa monyetla wa ho beha ka pele Molao wa Motheo wa naha jwalokaha o sireletsa ditokelo tsa bana.

src: The country will engage with different countries that are ahead of us in eliminating child labour and learn from them.
tgt: Naha e tla bontshana le dinaha tse ding tse itlhommeng pele phedisong ya mosebetsi wa bana mme e ithute ho tsona.

src: President Ramaphosa will hold a DDM Presidential Imbizo in Mpumalanga on Friday, 20 May 2022 under the theme: “Leave no one behind”.
tgt: Imbizo ya Presidente ya Mokgwa wa Ntshetsopele ya Ditereke (DDM) Presidente Ramaphosa o tla ba le Imbizo ya Mokgwa wa Ntshetsopele ya Ditereke Mpumalanga ka Labohlano la la 20 Motsheanong 2022 tlasa mookotaba: “Ha re siye motho morao”.

src: As an important public participation platform, the Imbizo allows the President to directly engage various stakeholders – especially rural communities – and to listen to their issues and challenges with the aim to address them.
tgt: Jwaloka mokgwa wa bohlokwa wa ho ba le seabo ha setjhaba, Imbizo e fa Presidente monyetla wa ho buisana le ba amehang ba fapaneng ka ho otloloha – haholoholo batho ba metseng ya mahae – le ho mamela mathata a bona ka sepheo sa ho buisana le bona ka ona.

src: The DDM Presidential Imbizo aims to unlock blockages to integrated service delivery and promote public participation in line with the DDSouth Africans can follow and participate in discussions on social media under the hashtag #PresidentialImbizo.
tgt: Sepheo ka Imbizo ya Presidente ya Mokgwa wa Ntshetsopele ya Ditereke ke ho lwantsha tse sitisang phumantsho e momahaneng ya ditshebeletso le ho kgothaletsa seabo sa baahi ho ikamahantswe le Mokgwa wa Ntshetsopele ya Ditereke.

src: Africa Month The commemoration of the annual Africa Month and Africa Day on Wednesday, 25 May is being celebrated under the theme: “The Year of Nutrition: Strengthening resilience in nutrition and food security on the African continent”.
tgt: Maafrika Borwa a ka latela le ho ba leseabo dipuisanong kaho kena diwebsaeteng tsa ho etsa setswalle tlasa #PresidentialImbizo.

src: As part of the long-term vision set out in Agenda 2063 (which is Africa's development blueprint to achieve inclusive and sustainable socio-economic development over 50 years), the theme focuses on the potential of the people of Africa with an emphasis on women, adolescents and children.
tgt: Ho ketekwa ha selemo le selemo ha Kgwedi ya Afrika le Letsatsi la Afrika ka Laboraro lala 25 Motsheanong ho tla ba le mookotaba oo e leng: “Selemo sa Phepo e Nepahetseng: Matlafatso ya Phepo e Nepahetseng le ya dijo tse lekaneng bohle kontinenteng ya Afrika”.

src: This is key for development as it leads to improved lives for individuals, higher earnings and improved incomes for countries.
tgt: Jwaloka karolo ya ponelopele ya nako e telele e ho Agenda 2063 (eo e leng leano la ntshetsopele la Afrika la ho fihlella ntshetsopele ya tsa bophelo e kenyeletsang bohle le ya moshwelella ya dilemo tse fetang tse mashome a mahlano), mookotaba ona o tsepame bokgoning ba batho ba Afrika mme ho tsepamisitswe maikutlo haholo basading, batjheng le baneng.

src: A notable highlight in Africa Month celebrations is Africa Communications Week, which will be held at Constitutional Hill in Johannesburg from 23 to 27 May 2022.
tgt: Ntlha e ka sehloohong meketeng ya Kgwedi ya Afrika ke Beke ya Dikgokahano ya Afrika, e tla ketekwa Constitutional Hill, Johannesburg ho tloha ka la 23 ho ya ho la 27 Motsheanong 2022.

src: Africa Month is an opportunity to promote African unity and deeper regional integration, and to recommit Africa to a common destiny.
tgt: Kgwedi ya Afrika ke monyetla wa ho phahamisa kopano ya Afrika le momahano e tebileng ya lebatowa, le ho inehela botjha ha Afrika bokamosong bo le bong.

src: Cabinet reminds everyone that our national interests are intrinsically linked to Africa’s stability, unity and prosperity.
tgt: Kabinete e hopotsa bohle hore ditabatabelo tsa rona tsa naha di amana haholo le botsitso, kopano le tswelopele ya Afrika.

src: Messages.
tgt: Melaetsa.

src: Condolences Cabinet expressed condolences to the family and friends of: Ms Phindile Xaba (53), who had a long and illustrious career in the media industry, both in South Africa and abroad.
tgt: MatshedisoKabinete e lebisitse matshediso malapeng le metswalleng ya bana: • MmePhindile Xaba(53),ya sebeditseng nako e telele le ka bokgabane indastering ya ditaba, Afrika Borwa le mose.

src: Ambassador Silumko Sokupa (74), who served the State Security Agency in various capacities over his long and illustrious career in the Public WEBTOKEN Francis Wilson (83), an acclaimed economist and founder of the Southern Africa Labour and Development Research Unit.
tgt: O sebeleditse ntlafalo ya naha ena ka boitelo.• LenqosaSilumkoSokupa(74),ya sebeleditseng Lekgotla la Tshireletseho ya Mmuso maemong a fapaneng, nako e telele a sebetsa ka bokgabane Tshebeletsong ya Mmuso.

src: Dr Kesavan Naidoo as Deputy Director-General (DDG): Institutional Development at the Department of Cooperative Governance (DCoG).
tgt: • Profesa Francis Wilson(83), setsebi sa moruo se ipabotseng, le mothehi wa Lekala la Diphuputso la tsa Basebetsi le Ntshetsopele Lebatoweng le Borwa ba Afrika.

src: Mr Siphosihle Emmanuel Hlomuka as DDG: Local Government Support and Interventions Management at the DCoMr Risimati Patrick Mathye as DDG: Water and Sanitation Services Management at the Department of Water and Sanitation (DWS).
tgt: Ngaka Kesavan Naidoo jwaloka Motlatsa-Molaodi-Kakaretso (DDG): Ntshetsopele ya Makgabane Ditheong, Lefapheng la Puso ya Kopanelo (DCoG).

src: Mr Collin Xolani Zwane as DDG: Regulation, Compliance and Enforcement at the DWMr Melanchton Makobe as DDG: SOC Governance Assurance and Performance at the Department of Public Enterprises.
tgt: Monghadi Siphosihle Emmanuel Hlomukajwaloka DDG: Botsamaisi ba Tshehetso le Dithuso Mebusong ya Lehae,DCoMonghadi Risimati Patrick Mathyejwaloka DDG: Botsamaisi ba Ditshebeletso tsa Metsi le Bohlweki (DWS).

src: Mr Bhekuyise Mathews Khenisa as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Housing Development Agency (HDA).
tgt: MonghadiCollin Xolani Zwane jwaloka DDG: Taolo, Tumellano le Phethahatso,DWMonghadiMelanchton Makobe jwaloka DDG:Ditshebeletso tsa Molao le Peholeihlo ya Tshebetso Pusong, Dikgwebong tsa Mmuso,Lefapheng la Dikgwebo tsa Mmuso.

src: Recovery and rebuilding efforts after the floods Cabinet expressed its praise and appreciation to all people and organisations involved in recovery and rebuilding efforts following the recent devastating floods in some parts of the country, especially in KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Boiphumano le Maiteko a Kahobotjha Kamora Dikgohola Kabinete e rorisitse le ho ananela mosebetsi wa batho le mekgatlo yohle e kentseng letsoho maitekong a hore batho ba iphumane, le kahongbotjha kamora dikgohola tse mpe dikarolong tse ding tsa naha, haholoholo KwaZulu-Natal.

src: It thanked all non-governmental organisations, faith-based organisations, communities, business people and relief organisations that have provided food, clothes, blankets, dignity packs and school uniforms to vulnerable families to meet their basic needs.
tgt: E lebohile mekgatlo yohle eo eseng ya mmuso, ya ditumelo, baahi, beng ba dikgwebo le mekgatlo e thusang e faneng ka dijo, diaparo, dikobo, dipakana tse sebediswang ke bomme ha ba le matsatsing le diaparo tsa sekolo malapeng a tlokotsing a sa kgoneng ho iphumanela tsa motheo tseo a di hlokang.

src: The National Disaster Management Centre continues to coordinate all spheres of government in its efforts to provide humanitarian relief to all affected households.
tgt: Setsi Sa Taolo ya Dikoduwa se ntse se tswela pele le ho kopanya makala ohle a mmuso maitekong a sona a ho fana ka thuso ya diphallelo malapeng ohle a amehileng.

src: Sheltering services are being provided to over 7 000 people in the four worst affected districts in KwaZulu-Natal.
tgt: Batho ba fetang 7 000 ka palo ba fuwa botshabelo diterekeng tse nne tse amehileng haholo KwaZulu-Natal.

src: Work has started on building temporary residences for affected families on state-owned land parcels that have been identified in KwaZulu-Natal for possible resettlement.
tgt: O qadile mosebetsi wa ho fumantsha malapa a amehileng bodulo ba nakwana ditsheng tseo e leng tsa mmuso tse hlwauweng KwaZulu-Natal tse ka sebedisetswang ho ahela batho.

src: Cabinet affirmed government’s commitment to managing the flood relief funds prudently and transparently.
tgt: Kabinete e tiisitse boinehelo ba mmuso ba ho laola matlole a dithuso tsa kamora dikgohola ka hloko le ka ho se pate letho.

src: The Auditor-General of South Africa is providing an additional monitoring service and the reprioritisation of funds is in line with the government’s budgeting system.
